articles.title: The changing burden of disease in Türkiye, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Türkiye has had improvements in population health over the past three decades, driven by the Health Transformation Programme launched in 2003, which expanded primary care through the family medicine system and, through the General Health Insurance Scheme, extended population coverage to near-universal levels. However, recent shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the catastrophic February 2023 earthquakes, have caused temporary reverses in health gains.
METHODS: We used Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 estimates for Türkiye, produced using the standard GBD methods applied to all 204 countries and territories, to describe age-standardised trends from 1990 to 2023 in life expectancy, healthy life expectancy (HALE), mortality, years of life lost, years lived with disability, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and risk-attributable burden, by sex, age, and cause. Estimates are reported as means of 250 draws with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). The effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and of the February 2023 earthquakes are described by examining the annual series across 2019-23 and, for the earthquakes, the burden assigned to the GBD cause exposure to forces of nature in 2023.
FINDINGS: Between 1990 and 2023, Türkiye's life expectancy increased from 68·1 years to 76·1 years (male: 65·2 years to 73·9 years; female: 71·2 years to 78·3 years), and HALE from 58·7 years to 65·1 years. The COVID-19 pandemic caused a 2·0-year decline in life expectancy, whereas the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes resulted in over 53 000 deaths. Age-standardised all-cause mortality declined by 34·9% from 1040·3 (95% UI 1022·4-1061·6) per 100 000 in 1990 to 677·3 (634·3-731·6) in 2023, with reductions of 36·5% in non-communicable diseases (NCDs) from 836·5 (808·4-861·7) in 1990 to 530·8 (488·4-580·8), 64·6% in communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional diseases from 151·5 (135·5-167·0) in 1990 to 53·7 (43·5-63·9), but an increase of 77·5% in injuries from 52·3 (41·1-64·8) in 1990 to 92·8 (85·8-100·8) in 2023 due to the earthquakes. The top three causes of mortality in 2023 were ischaemic heart disease with an age-standardised mortality rate of 123·7 per 100 000 (95% UI 99·7-150·5), exposure to forces of nature (the February 2023 earthquakes) 65·2 (59·3-71·6), and stroke 57·0 (43·4-71·4). The leading age-standardised risk factors contributing to deaths in 2023 were high blood pressure with a rate of 137·4 per 100 000 (104·0-173·9), high BMI (86·9 [45·3-125·6]), and high fasting plasma glucose (85·8 [74·0-100·6]). Although our findings show a reduction in smoking-attributable burden, smoking remains the leading DALYs age-standardised risk factor for men in 2023 at 3928 per 100 000 (3098-4669). Among women, high BMI emerged as the leading risk factor of age-standardised DALYs at 2548 per 100 000 (1141-3719). Diabetes rose to become the third leading cause of health loss in 2023, and metabolic risks (ie, high BMI, high blood pressure, and high fasting plasma glucose) were the three leading risk factors for DALYs in 2023.
INTERPRETATION: Türkiye has achieved sustained health gains but faces rising NCDs, dietary, and behavioural risks that need to be monitored and addressed through multisectoral efforts. Strengthening prevention and early detection while leveraging digital health infrastructure is essential for Türkiye to build a strong health system.
FUNDING: Gates Foundation.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield of genetic testing in heart transplant recipients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: A single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy genetic testing is recommended for patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) but is inconsistently applied once a patient has reached end-stage disease and undergone heart transplantation. Whether a transplant program can systematically test its existing NICM cohort and what completion rate is achievable when testing is operationalized in the clinic rather than offered ad hoc is not well characterized.
METHODS: We studied all 73 adults followed in the Southern Alberta Transplant Program after transplantation for NICM: dilated (DCM), non-dilated left ventricular (NDLVC), restrictive, or hypertrophic (HCM). Cardiomyopathy genetic testing was offered as a program-wide initiative and performed in adulthood using clinically validated multigene panels. Variants were classified by ACMG/AMP criteria; pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants interpreted as explanatory for the recipient's cardiomyopathy were counted as diagnostic. Single heterozygous P/LP variants in autosomal recessive genes were interpreted as carrier findings and not counted toward yield. Yields are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); the childhood- versus adult-transplant comparison was tested with Fisher's exact test.
RESULTS: Of 71 eligible patients, 27 (38.0%) had a genetic-testing result before the 12-month operational window; of the 44 offered testing during the window, 37 completed it (84.1%), raising cohort testing coverage to 90.1% (64/71). A diagnostic pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant was identified in 28 of 64 tested patients (43.8%; 95% CI 32.3%-55.9%); a sensitivity analysis restricted to the 36 patients tested with the comprehensive Invitae 121-gene panel yielded an indistinguishable 38.9% (14/36; 95% CI 24.8%-55.1%), with no evidence that variation in panel breadth materially biased the overall estimate. Two additional patients carried a single heterozygous P/LP variant in an autosomal recessive gene (carrier findings, not counted). Yield was higher in patients transplanted in childhood (10/14, 71.4%) than in adulthood (18/50, 36.0%; Fisher's exact P = 0.031). TTN was the most frequent gene (7 P/LP), followed by LMNA, PKP2, and MYH7 (3 each).
CONCLUSIONS: A 12-month program-wide initiative raised cardiomyopathy genetic testing coverage in an existing NICM heart transplant cohort from 38% to 90% by embedding testing in routine transplant clinic visits. The diagnostic yield among tested patients (43.8%) was consistent with published estimates and similar when restricted to the most comprehensive panel, with markedly higher yield in patients transplanted in childhood. These findings provide a reproducible operational template for transplant programs seeking to close the implementation gap in cardiomyopathy genetic evaluation and to enable cascade testing of at-risk relatives.

articles.title: Regional and national burden and aetiologies of non-COVID lower respiratory infections in Latin America and the Caribbean, 1990-2023: a secondary analysis of the global burden of disease study 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income regions. Reliable, up-to-date burden estimates are needed to inform public health strategies in Latin America and the Caribbean, where prevention and management strategies remain heterogeneous. We aimed to characterise temporal and geographical patterns in LRTI mortality, incidence, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and aetiology across the region from 1990 to 2023.
METHODS: We analysed secondary, modelled estimates of mortality, incidence, and DALYs attributable to LRTIs in Latin America and the Caribbean from 1990 to 2023, extracted from the GBD 2023 Results Tool and produced following the standardised GBD protocol coordinated by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME).
FINDINGS: In Latin America and the Caribbean, LRTI mortality declined in most countries between 1990 and 2023, with the steepest reductions among children younger than five years (e.g., Brazil ARC -6·16, 95% UI -6·61 to -5·71). All-age mortality rose in some countries, but age-standardised rates showed that these increases reflected population ageing rather than rising age-specific risk. Following a sustained pre-pandemic decline, incidence showed and overall upward direction in the post-pandemic period across age groups, although the magnitude and statistical relevance of these changes varied by age and country, with the largest increase observed among children in Suriname (ARC +8·84, 95% UI +2·80 to +14·95). Streptococcus pneumoniae remained the leading cause of LRTI mortality in 2023 (7·68 per 100,000, 95% UI 7·11-8·24; ARC -2·70, 95% UI -2·96 to -2·45).
INTERPRETATION: LRTIs remain a major cause of death in the region, with substantial progress among children but persistent burden among older adults, driven by population ageing, and evidence of a post-pandemic increase in incidence. There is a great importance of combining clinical interventions with broader public health strategies addressing vaccination coverage, antimicrobial-resistance surveillance, nutrition, housing, and access to primary care, particularly in populations that have experienced less favourable trends.
FUNDING: Wellcome Trust (303666/Z/23/Z); UK International Development (301542-403); the Gates Foundation (INV-063472) and Universidad de La Sabana (MED-289-2020).

articles.title: Pediatric Sleep Disorders: Early Identification and Management Strategies.
articles.abstract: This review highlights pediatric sleep disorders that can be identified early and treated effectively, emphasizing their impact on child health and quality of life. Key conditions discussed include obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), restless legs syndrome (RLS), sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE), and narcolepsy. This article discusses epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentations, diagnostic approaches, complications and evidence-based treatments for each disorder. OSA is associated with neurocgnitive abd cardiovascular consequences, while RLS is strongly linked to low iron stores (ferritin). SHE requires prompt recognition to reduce seizure burden, and narcolepsy often presents atypically in children, causing diagnostic delays and significant psychosocial impact..

articles.title: Employing Implementation Science to Move from Paper to Practice.
articles.abstract: Implementation Science studies evidence practice gap separating innovation from clinical practice and designs interventions to close this gap. Process, determinant and evaluation frameworks provide a systematic way to ensure Implementation Science efforts are planned in a comprehensive and standardized format maintaining core components of the intervention but allowing for context-specific adaptations necessary for sustainment. Logic models provide a blueprint to allow for the operationalization of these models and frameworks. Otherwise, I would add one more sentence. Evaluation is a critical piece of all implementation science work from pre- to post-implementation and can be accomplished through evaluation frameworks. Future efforts are needed to close evidence to practice gaps that exist in the field of allergy-immunology, including crucial technological advancements proven to improve health outcomes.

articles.title: Emerging Drugs.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic development in Sjögren's disease has accelerated after decades of largely negative clinical trials. Improved patient selection, refined outcome measures, and targeted modulation of key immune pathways have produced positive late-stage studies and the prospect of disease-modifying treatment. This article examines emerging B-cell-directed therapies, neonatal Fc receptor inhibitors, costimulatory blockade, intracellular signaling inhibitors, immune-restorative approaches, repurposed therapies, and cellular treatments. It also considers lessons from contemporary trials, including phenotype-based enrollment, multidimensional endpoints, and organ-specific responses, and discusses how these advances may enable increasingly precise therapeutic selection.

articles.title: Systemic Lupus and Other Autoimmune Disorders During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Rheumatologic conditions occur in reproductive aged women, requiring a multidisciplinary approach to care. Patients require coordinated care with obstetrics, maternal fetal medicine, and rheumatology. Many drugs used for the care of rheumatologic conditions are safe in pregnancy, but detailed review should occur, ideally preconception, so the patient can be on the safest regimen while maintaining disease control. Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies particularly pose unique risks of neonatal lupus syndrome, including cardiac manifestations. Medical management is unique to each disease and includes ultrasounds and antenatal testing to optimize both maternal and fetal well-being and minimize perinatal risks.

articles.title: Burn Management in Disasters.
articles.abstract: Burn disasters are uncommon but uniquely resource-intensive mass casualty events, requiring prolonged multidisciplinary care that can rapidly exhaust the limited number of verified burn centers and beds. This article reviews the epidemiology and injury patterns of burn disasters, burn-specific triage and transport principles, and system-level planning built on regional burn networks. It examines the American Burn Association's role in center verification, regional response plans, and national burn bed capacity monitoring, alongside federal support mechanisms. Acute resuscitation, damage-control operative strategies, temporary wound coverage, workforce augmentation, and pediatric considerations are addressed, together with ethical decision-making, long-term recovery, and emerging technologies.

articles.title: Care of Special Populations in Disasters.
articles.abstract: Disasters and mass casualty incidents disproportionately harm elderly, pediatric, and pregnant patients, yet most triage algorithms and preparedness plans are built around the healthy adult. This review examines the physiologic, anatomic, and social characteristics that make each population vulnerable, drawing on experience from Hurricane Katrina and contemporary armed conflict. For older adults, frailty, rather than chronologic age, drives outcomes, and polypharmacy complicates resuscitation. Children require age-adjusted triage, weight-based dosing, and protection from family separation. Pregnant patients require simultaneous maternal and fetal assessment, as the physiologic adaptations of pregnancy mask hemorrhage. Systems-level preparedness remains the strongest determinant of outcome.

articles.title: Phase resolved functional lung (PREFUL) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) detects perfusion deficits in pediatric lung transplant recipients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a radiation-free technique that detects regional ventilation and perfusion abnormalities and has shown promise for identifying chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) in adult lung transplant (LTx) recipients. Its utility in pediatric LTx has not been investigated. We evaluated the feasibility of PREFUL MRI in pediatric LTx recipients and its association with pulmonary function.
METHODS: In this single-center cross-sectional study, pediatric LTx recipients and healthy controls underwent contrast-free PREFUL MRI at 1.5 T to quantify regional ventilation and perfusion defects. Spirometry and nitrogen multiple-breath washout were performed to determine forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁) and lung clearance index (LCI). Group differences were assessed using the rank-sum test, and associations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation.
RESULTS: Twenty-two of 24 eligible pediatric LTx recipients (feasibility 92%; median age 13.6 years [range 6-17]; median time since LTx 3.9 years [range 0.6-16.3]) and 11 healthy controls (median age 10.7 years [range 6-15]) completed the study. Perfusion defect extent was significantly greater in pediatric LTx recipients than in controls (p = 0.001), whereas ventilation defects did not differ (p = 0.359). No participant met spirometric criteria for CLAD. FEV₁ %predicted, but not FEV₁ % of baseline, correlated inversely with perfusion defect extent (ρ = -0.487, p = 0.022). No correlations were observed between LCI and MRI-derived ventilation or perfusion parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: PREFUL MRI is feasible in pediatric LTx recipients and detects regional perfusion abnormalities despite stable spirometry. It may provide a sensitive, radiation-free imaging biomarker for monitoring the pediatric lung allograft.

articles.title: Kidney-Alone Transplantation With siRNA Therapy in Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) is a rare genetic disease causing severe hyperoxaluria, kidney stones, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive kidney failure (KF) followed by systemic oxalosis. Expert guidelines traditionally recommended liver-kidney transplantation (LKTx) for patients with vitamin B6-unresponsive PH1 and KF, with 1-year mortality of 5% to 15%. Small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) therapies targeting hepatic oxalate production have shifted the treatment landscape. Eighteen patients on siRNA therapy with successful kidney-alone transplantion (KATx) have been reported.
METHODS: A multicenter, international, retrospective case series from 11 countries included patients with: (1) confirmed PH1 diagnosis; (2) KATx as definitive kidney replacement therapy; and (3) concurrent lumasiran and/or nedosiran treatment beyond the induction phase before and/or after transplantion.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight patients were analyzed: at transplantion, 27 received lumasiran, 6 received nedosiran, and 1 received both; 60.5% carried a priori vitamin B6-responsive variants. All 25 AGXT alleles identified were pathogenic or likely pathogenic, including 3 not previously reported in PH1 and 1 requiring haplotype-level resolution. Median pretransplant plasma oxalate was 59 μmol/l (interquartile range [IQR], 30; range, 5-100). Donors were deceased in 57.9%; 39.5% of recipients were pediatric. Median follow-up was 25 months (range, 2-60). Peritransplant or posttransplant dialysis was used in 60.5%. Four patients diagnosed after KATx were included; 3 were successfully treated with lumasiran. One-year graft survival was 95%; patient survival was 100%.
CONCLUSION: This international series supports KATx as standard of care for carefully selected patients with PH1 with assured long-term siRNA therapy and expert follow-up. Practical recommendations, including a peritransplant checklist emphasizing expert-centered care and vigilance for emerging complications, are provided.

articles.title: Oropouche virus disease across Latin America during the 2023-2025 epidemic: a multi-country case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023-2025 epidemic of Oropouche virus (OROV) disease across Latin America raised public health concerns due to its expansion into previously unaffected regions, alongside reports of increased clinical severity and vertical transmission.
METHODS: We conducted a multi-country case series to characterise the clinical presentation, disease course, outcomes, and virological features of OROV disease during the 2023-2025 epidemic. Analyses were descriptive.
FINDINGS: We describe 2716 OROV disease cases reported between January 31st, 2024, and November 4th, 2025, across ten states in Brazil, Panama, and Peru. Median age was 38 years (IQR 25-51); 1379/2716 (51%) were female. Most common symptoms were fever (89%), headache (88%), and myalgia (59%), followed by retro-orbital pain (47%). One-fourth of participants reported symptoms' duration beyond one week. Most cases were mild (2542/2716; 94%), although severe manifestations and one death occurred. Haemorrhagic manifestations were reported in 41/2716 (2%), and 7/2716 (<1%) developed severe disease temporally associated with OROV infection. Among 108 pregnant women, 15 (14%) had adverse pregnancy outcomes, including abortions, preterm births, stillbirths, and symptomatic newborns; no congenital malformations were observed. Older age, comorbidities, warning signs, and laboratory abnormalities were more frequently observed among participants with complications. Prolonged RNA detection beyond seven days was observed in serum and urine.
INTERPRETATION: Although most OROV disease cases were mild, severe disease and adverse pregnancy outcomes occur and may be under-recognised. These findings support the need for improved clinical recognition, risk stratification, and diagnostics, particularly for high-risk groups, and highlight priorities for surveillance and future research.
FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Children Undergoing Major Non-Cardiac Surgery: Protocol for a Multicentre Study (POAKIDS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with increased mortality and adverse long-term outcomes. Postoperative AKI is a common and recognised complication after surgery in adults. In children, AKI following paediatric cardiac surgery has been extensively studied. However, the incidence and characteristics of postoperative AKI after non-cardiac surgery in children remain poorly defined, with existing evidence largely derived from retrospective and single-centre studies.
METHODS: POAKIDS is an international, multicentre, prospective observational study including hospitalised children aged 0-16 years undergoing major non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Postoperative AKI will be defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO). The primary outcome is the incidence of postoperative AKI. Secondary objectives include evaluation of established and novel urinary biomarkers as predictors of postoperative AKI and exploration of perioperative potential predictors of renal injury. The maximal follow-up is seven postoperative days. Sample size is based on the incidence estimate, with a planned inclusion of 2000 patients. Data will be analysed using descriptive statistics, agreement analyses, and exploratory regression models.
DISCUSSION: This study aims to provide robust prospective data on the incidence of postoperative AKI in children undergoing major non-cardiac surgery and to improve understanding of perioperative renal injury in this population. By combining standardised AKI definitions with systematic biomarker assessment, the results are expected to inform future preventive strategies and guide the design of interventional studies targeting postoperative renal injury in paediatric perioperative care.

articles.title: Digital Twin Models for Cancer.
articles.abstract: The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials. In precision oncology, MDTs can simulate disease progression and therapeutic responses, allowing treatment regimens to be tested virtually before administration and thereby supporting personalized treatment decisions. In virtual clinical trials, MDTs can enhance randomized trials through the PROCOVA™ methodology, provide synthetic control arms for single-arm studies, and support the identification of optimal dosing regimens in early-phase trials. However, MDTs also face challenges related to computational complexity, generalizability across diverse populations, AI-related model validation and regulatory compliance, and underdeveloped ethical frameworks for continuous-learning systems. Despite these challenges, MDTs hold considerable potential to reshape cancer care, optimize individualized therapies, and accelerate oncology drug development.

articles.title: 47, XYY Syndrome (Jacobs Syndrome): Real-World Data From Patient Associations Suggest an Integrated Multidisciplinary Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 47, XYY syndrome (Jacobs syndrome) is a sex chromosome aneuploidy with an estimated prevalence of approximately 1:1000 live male births. Despite its frequency, 47, XYY syndrome remains largely underdiagnosed, with often late identification and the absence of structured and uniform care pathways.
OBJECTIVES: Here, we aimed to integrate the most recent scientific evidence with real-world descriptive data collected from two patient associations in Italy and Spain, in order to identify key clinical organizational challenges and propose an integrated model for multidisciplinary management.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data obtained through structured questionnaires disseminated by two national patient associations were analyzed. The analysis was descriptive and comparative, integrating questionnaire-derived information with evidence from the published literature.
RESULTS: The data suggest that 47, XYY syndrome is a multisystem condition that requires coordinated longitudinal monitoring.
CONCLUSION: Patient-reported opinions advocate for the development of an integrated multidisciplinary clinical pathway to enhance the continuity of care, equity of access to services, and endocrinological surveillance.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Bipolar Disorder.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Pediatric (bipolar disorder) BD carries substantial morbidity, including prolonged symptom burden, high rates of suicide attempts and substance use, and psychosocial impairment. Accurate diagnosis requires careful longitudinal assessment, as presentations in youth often differ from adults, with more rapid cycling, mixed features, and irritability over classic euphoric mania. Early diagnosis and treatment are critical to reduce potential impairment and to support early recovery of youth with BD. The purpose of this article is to discuss the use of antipsychotics in the treatment of pediatric BD.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Pediatric Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Trauma-Related Disorders.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Childhood trauma is associated with a broad spectrum of psychiatric symptoms beyond core posttraumatic stress disorder criteria, including emotional dysregulation, aggression, sleep disturbance, and behavioral instability that impair functioning and safety. The pediatric evidence base is limited to case reports and small observational studies, with no randomized controlled trials. Adult data show modest and inconsistent benefits with notable adverse effects. Antipsychotics should be embedded within trauma-informed care, applied in a time-limited, symptom-specific manner, and closely monitored for metabolic, neurologic, and potential neurodevelopmental effects. Their role remains narrow and adjunctive, with psychotherapy, diagnostic precision, and risk minimization as primary priorities.

articles.title: Clozapine in Children and Adolescents: Indications, Efficacy, and Safety.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic but it remains underutilized. This review synthesizes evidence for clozapine use in children and adolescents, including additional indications such as suicidality, aggression, autism, and catatonia. Children have differences in pharmacokinetics, dosing, and side effect profiles. Although side effects can include agranulocytosis, myocarditis, and metabolic effects, regular laboratory and vital sign monitoring and adjunctive treatments can mitigate these risks. Persistent barriers often delay initiation, but increased education and systems-level changes can reduce barriers to clozapine use. Recent regulatory changes and emerging evidence support earlier and more widespread use of clozapine in appropriately selected pediatric populations.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Adolescents with Substance Use and Substance Use Disorders.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Antipsychotic medications are frequently prescribed off label in adolescents, particularly to manage agitation, behavioral dysregulation, and sleep disturbances, often in the context of substance use. However, their use is not consistently supported by a strong evidence base and carries meaningful risks, including metabolic, neurologic, and long-term health consequences. This article examines the clinical complexity of adolescents with substance use and co-occurring psychiatric symptoms, highlighting the risk of diagnostic ambiguity during acute intoxication or withdrawal. We provide a practical, developmentally informed framework to guide clinicians in the thoughtful, time-limited, and indication-specific use of antipsychotics in this population.

articles.title: Psychosis in medically ill Children and Adolescents.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Psychosis in children and adolescents caused by medical illnesses/conditions is rare. Visual hallucinations, confusion, and change of baseline mentation support this diagnosis. Certain physical examination findings also suggest a secondary etiology of psychosis. Specific laboratory, imaging, and other tests are then utilized. Numerous medical etiologies have been identified to cause psychosis in children and adolescents, specifically delirium, inborn errors of metabolism, genetic syndromes, encephalitides, other systemic infections, space occupying lesions, seizures, trauma, and endocrine and nutritional disorders. Treatment is mainly extrapolated from the delirium literature, and there are conflicting data showing the utility of antipsychotic use for secondary psychosis.

articles.title: Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder and Atypical Antipsychotics.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD) was introduced to classify children with impairing, chronic irritability and outbursts. Approaching treatment starts with evidence-informed assessment including using standardized rating scales to support diagnostic decision making and track symptom response. DMDD has no Food and Drug Administration-approved medications and few randomized clinical trials demonstrating efficacy. It is recommended to start with treating co-occurring disorders, often attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and then to treat residual symptoms. Atypical antipsychotics have evidence of efficacy in treating irritability and reactive aggression and come with adverse effects, including metabolic side effects. Therefore, benefit versus risk analysis of atypical antipsychotics is needed.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Children and Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Antipsychotic medications may be effective for the management of irritability, aggression, and other mental health disorders in youth with autism spectrum disorder and other neurodevelopmental disorders including intellectual disability. While these medications may significantly improve safety outcomes and quality of life, autistic youth may be at greater risk of overprescribing, side effects, and insufficient monitoring. Best practice includes clarifying target symptoms/behaviors, using lowest effective doses, ensuring first-line behavioral and environmental interventions, collaboratively working with parents/guardians and other care team members, utilizing creative strategies to follow gold-standard monitoring guidelines, and deprescribing when able.

articles.title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder and Disruptive Behavior Disorders.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Disruptive behavior disorders (DBDs; oppositional defiant disorders, and conduct disorders) frequently co-occur with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and can be commonly associated with aggression, a major driver of clinical presentation and service utilization. Despite no US Food and Drug Administration -approved medications for DBDs in this population, antipsychotics, specifically second-generation agents, are used in clinical practice for this purpose. Evidence supports behavioral interventions as a first-line treatment of DBDs. In youth with comorbid ADHD, optimized stimulant and non-stimulant treatments of ADHD are indicated. Among antipsychotics, risperidone has the strongest evidence for reducing aggression, particularly as adjunctive therapy to stimulant medications.

articles.title: Preparation of Mouse Primary Microglia Cultures for α-Synuclein Propagation.
articles.abstract: Hyperstimulation of microglia affects the regulation of α-synuclein (α-syn) spreading in the brain. Isolation and purification of primary microglia from animal brains will be a useful tool for investigating the pathological α-synuclein propagation in vitro. In this chapter, we describe a general operational procedure that involves culturing mixed neuroglial cells from the cerebral cortex and hippocampus of neonatal mice and obtaining primary microglia through mechanical oscillation. The primary cells are suitable for establishing microglial activation induced by α-synuclein preformed fibrils (α-syn PFFs). Conditioned medium produced by these microglial cells to further culture neuronal cells recapitulates the transmission of amyloid α-syn to neurons. This protocol may provide an effective ex vivo model for studying microglia-related neuroinflammation in amyloid α-syn cell-to-cell transmission.

articles.title: Preparation of Rat Primary Cortical Astrocyte Culture.
articles.abstract: Astrocytes and neurons originate from common neural stem cells, with astrocytes playing essential roles in neuronal survival. By forming the blood-brain barrier, astrocytes create a specialized metabolic environment that supports neuronal function. Traditionally, astrocytes have been classified as neurotoxic or neuroprotective subtypes based on gene expression and phenotypes, but their diversity across brain regions and functions renders this binary categorization insufficient. Increasing evidence also highlights astrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles as protective mediators against neuronal injury and degeneration. Understanding astrocytic functions is therefore critical for elucidating the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases, and diverse co-culture and organoid models have been developed for this purpose. Primary astrocyte cultures, which are thought to retain characteristics of the in vivo environment, remain a robust and versatile system. In this chapter, we describe a fundamental protocol for isolating and culturing astrocytes from neonatal rat brains. This method is an isolation and culture method that takes advantage of the difference in adhesiveness between astrocytes and other brain cells, which allows the generation of large cell populations, making it particularly suitable for biochemical analyses and for isolating scarce materials such as extracellular vesicles and microRNAs.

articles.title: Curative Therapy for Rhabdomyosarcoma: A Model Disease for Multidisciplinary Sarcoma Care.
articles.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is an aggressive soft tissue sarcoma affecting children and adolescents. Treatment involves a multidisciplinary approach, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. This review focuses on newly diagnosed RMS and discusses the role of surgery in RMS evaluation and treatment, highlighting the importance of achieving local control. We also discuss chemotherapy and radiation therapy, as well as ongoing controversies and novel strategies under investigation, including targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and novel biomarkers. Efforts are ongoing to improve outcomes for patients with RMS, particularly those with high-risk disease.

articles.title: Pediatric Musculoskeletal Emergencies: A Primer for Practicing Radiologists.
articles.abstract: Acute musculoskeletal conditions are a frequent cause of pediatric emergency imaging. In children, skeletal immaturity and open physes influence injury patterns, predisposing to unique fracture types. Incomplete ossification and growth plate anatomy may obscure or mimic pathology, complicating interpretation. Beyond trauma, musculoskeletal infections are also common reasons for pediatric emergency visits. Radiographs remain the first-line imaging modality, while ultrasound, CT, and MR imaging are important problem solving modalities. Clear understanding of age-related patterns of musculoskeletal injury and infection, normal anatomic variants, and imaging pitfalls allows accurate assessment of various acute musculoskeletal conditions in the pediatric population.

articles.title: Abdominopelvic Imaging Emergency in Children: A Comprehensive Update and Review.
articles.abstract: Abdominopelvic emergencies are one of the most common causes of pediatric emergency department visits, frequently resulting in urgent surgical management. Because conditions such as midgut, volvulus and torsion are time-sensitive, accurate and timely diagnosis is essential and imaging evaluation plays a crucial role. Following abdominal radiograph, ultrasound remains the preferred next imaging modality in most conditions to avoid radiation, even more so with the introduction of contrast-enhanced ultrasound. Advancements in computed tomography and MRI continue to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient safety. This article provides an up-to-date review of current imaging protocols and imaging characteristics of pediatric abdominopelvic emergency conditions.

articles.title: Pediatric Thoracic Imaging Emergency: Practical Approach for Daily Practice.
articles.abstract: Imaging of thoracic emergencies in children is crucial for early diagnosis, guiding treatment, and avoiding severe complications. Radiography, ultrasound, and computed tomography are the most common modalities in emergency imaging. Radiologists should be familiar with the appropriate choice of imaging modality and the radiologic characteristics of serious conditions that can present acutely in the pediatric emergency room. This article discusses a practical overview of the major pediatric thoracic emergencies, including pulmonary infections, airway abnormalities, neoplasms, air leaks, traumatic injuries, and foreign bodies. An up-to-date review of key imaging findings is provided, with emphasis on features that are unique to children.

articles.title: Neonatal Imaging Emergencies: Essential Considerations for General Radiologists.
articles.abstract: Neonatal emergencies comprise a diverse group of congenital and acquired conditions that require prompt diagnosis and intervention to minimize morbidity and mortality. Imaging plays a critical role in the evaluation of these disorders, with radiography remaining the cornerstone of initial assessment in the neonatal intensive care unit. Familiarity with the imaging appearances of emergent neonatal conditions is essential for radiologists. This article reviews the key imaging findings of neonatal emergencies, which can be categorized into pulmonary, cardiomediastinal, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, diaphragmatic, and catheter-related emergencies.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Emergency Radiology: Where Do We Stand Now?
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in pediatric emergency radiology, where timely and accurate image interpretation is critical. Current evidence highlights its strongest role in detection and localization tasks across neuroimaging, thoracic, abdominopelvic, and musculoskeletal studies. AI also shows promise for classification, severity assessment, and workflow prioritization, improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in some settings. However, existing research is limited by retrospective designs, small datasets, insufficient external validation, and poor transferability of adult-trained models. Pediatric-specific models, multicenter validation, prospective studies, and thoughtful clinical integration are needed before wider adoption beyond assistive use in routine pediatric emergency imaging practice today.

articles.title: Pediatric Dermatologic Conditions.
articles.abstract: Pediatric skin conditions of the lower extremity present a diagnostic and management challenge, and this article offers the practitioner a systematic framework. It opens with practical guidance on performing cutaneous procedures in children-engaging the parent, minimizing pain and anxiety through topical anesthesia and distraction, and setting postoperative limits for optimal scar outcomes. It then surveys environmentally induced disorders, bites and stings, genodermatoses including the palmoplantar keratodermas, and bacterial, viral, and fungal infections. Eczematous conditions, psoriasis, nevi, pediatric melanoma, and nail disorders are each reviewed with attention to lower extremity presentation, common misdiagnoses, and current management strategies.

articles.title: Pediatric Foot and Ankle Infection and Osteomyelitis.
articles.abstract: This article reviews pediatric foot and ankle infections and osteomyelitis, emphasizing how a child's developing vasculature, growth plates, and periosteum predispose to rapid hematogenous spread and unique complications like growth arrest. It covers epidemiology, age-specific and risk-specific patterns, and a classification spanning superficial soft-tissue infection, deep infection, septic arthritis, and acute/subacute/chronic osteomyelitis. Staphylococcus aureus (including methicillin-resistant S aureus) and Kingella kingae are highlighted as key pathogens. Diagnostic strategy combines inflammatory markers, cultures, and MRI, while management centers on targeted antibiotics with early transition to oral therapy and timely surgical debridement. Four illustrative case studies and emerging diagnostic/therapeutic trends round out the discussion.

articles.title: The Newborn Examination and Pediatric Foot Development.
articles.abstract: Neonatal foot and ankle pathology is underemphasized in most medical training, leaving podiatrists increasingly called upon to assess newborns. This article sets out a systematic approach: a detailed prenatal, maternal, perinatal, and developmental history, followed by examination extending from head, neck, upper extremities, thorax, and spine to hips and knees. It then reviews common lower extremity conditions-hallux nail disorders, curly toe, digiti quinti varus, focal gigantism, brachymetatarsia, syndactyly, polydactyly, hallux varus and valgus, metatarsus adductus, talipes equinovarus, and calcaneus deformities-stressing early serial casting where indicated and delaying most surgical correction until skeletal maturation.

articles.title: Sleeper Growth Plate Modulation for the Treatment of Mechanical Axis Deviation: A Review Article.
articles.abstract: This article aims to review the use of sleeper growth plates (SGPs) in the management of mechanical axis deviation in pediatric patients. Growth modulation using staples or the 8 plate have offered effective treatment options, but overcorrection and rebound remain prevalent issues. The SGP offers a potential solution involving metaphyseal screw removal only from the 8 plate construct. This potentially facilitates simple reapplication of the metaphyseal screw to resume growth modulation if deformity recurs. Using the available literature, this article reviews the history, indications, technique, and potential complications associated with SGP use.

articles.title: Association of Parenting Styles and Parental Involvement with the Mental Health of Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize quantitative evidence on associations among parenting styles, parental involvement, and mental health outcomes among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Extension for Scoping Reviews (ScR) guidelines. Literature published between January 1993 and May 2025 was searched across four databases (PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library). Search terms included Medical Subject Headings (MeSH), title/abstract (ti/ab), and text words (tw). This review included only original quantitative studies examining relationships among parenting styles, parental involvement, mental health outcomes, and glycemic control in adolescents aged 10-19 years with Type 1 diabetes. Qualitative studies, mixed-methods studies, and review articles were excluded.
RESULTS: Out of 486 identified studies, 10 met the inclusion criteria, seven focusing on parent-child dyads and three on adolescents only. Across the included studies, supportive and collaborative parenting was consistently linked to fewer depressive symptoms, higher quality of life (QOL), greater self-efficacy, better adherence, and improved HbA1c levels. Conversely, controlling, overinvolved, or uninvolved parenting tended to be associated with increased depressive symptoms, lower QOL, and poorer glycemic control.
CONCLUSIONS: Parenting styles and parental involvement appear to be important factors associated with both psychological adjustment and glycemic control among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes. Although this review did not test a specific theoretical model, the findings can be interpreted through the lens of self-determination theory, underscoring the importance of autonomy support. Future research requires greater conceptual clarity and international standardization of autonomy support measures.

articles.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors in the Pediatric Population.
articles.abstract: Pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PPitNETs) are rare but present significant clinical challenges in children. Their diverse presentations necessitate comprehensive endocrinologic and radiographic evaluation. They are most commonly prolactin-secreting or adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting. A genetic mutation can be present, particularly in young patients with aggressive disease. Management is multidisciplinary. Medical therapy is first-line treatment of prolactinomas, and surgery is first-line treatment of most other PPitNETs, with reasonable remission rates when performed in experienced centers. Long-term outcomes are favorable, although hypopituitarism and lifelong hormone replacement remain important concerns. Ongoing surveillance is essential to ensure detect recurrence, and monitor treatment-related complications.

articles.title: Criterion-related validity, classification accuracy, and misclassification patterns of the International Fitness Scale in adolescents from a rural Mediterranean region of Spain: The EHDLA study.
articles.abstract: Self-reported fitness instruments provide a scalable surveillance solution when objective testing is impractical, yet the nature of perception-accuracy discordance in adolescents is not well understood. This study examined criterion-related validity, classification accuracy, convergent construct validity against the Spanish Perceived Physical Literacy Instrument (S-PPLI), and misclassification patterning of the International Fitness Scale (IFIS) in a community sample of adolescents from the Valle de Ricote (Region of Murcia, Spain). Cross-sectional data from 1017 Spanish adolescents (471 boys, 546 girls; median age 14 years) from the Eating Healthy and Daily Life Activities (EHDLA) study were analyzed. IFIS overall correlated with the Assessing the Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA-Fit) composite (Spearman rho [ρ] = 0.369; partial ρ = 0.377, p < 0.001), with flexibility showing the strongest domain-specific validity (Spearman ρ = 0.635; partial ρ = 0.592, p < 0.001). Using the full five-level IFIS score, the area under the curve (AUC) for identifying the lowest fitness tertile was 0.66 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.63-0.69). At the primary screening cut-off (IFIS ≤ 3), sensitivity was 0.68, specificity was 0.59, and negative predictive value was 0.80, while a stricter threshold (IFIS ≤ 2) increased specificity (0.94) at the cost of sensitivity (0.16). Convergent validity with S-PPLI was supported (partial ρ = 0.56, p < 0.001). Misclassification profiling identified 18.5% of participants as underestimators and 17.6% as overestimators; underestimation was associated with shorter sleep, while concordant-low membership was associated with higher body mass index (BMI), lower activity, and more sedentary time. In conclusion, IFIS showed weak-to-modest criterion-related validity and limited discriminative accuracy. Therefore, IFIS may serve as a low-burden adjunct to objective testing for population-level prioritization, but its performance relative to other brief instruments or low-burden measures, including BMI, remains untested. Discordance between perceived and objective fitness was common (36.1%) and co-occurred with lifestyle and adiposity characteristics, supporting consideration of perception-accuracy profiling in school-based and public health surveillance. Findings pertain to a single rural region and require replication in urban, regional, and socioeconomically diverse samples before broader generalization.

articles.title: Pediatric intensive care resources in Ibero-Latin America: SPREAD PED Ibero-Latin America, a multinational, multicentre, cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) are a cornerstone of child survival, yet their structure, staffing, and adherence to evidence-based protocols vary widely across regions. Comprehensive and contemporary data from Ibero-Latin America are lacking. We aimed to characterize the organization, human resources, and implementation of standardized care practices in PICUs across this region.
METHODS: We conducted an international, multicentre, cross-sectional study including all PICUs admitting patients during a five-day period (Sept 2024) across 21 countries in Latin America, Spain, and Portugal. Unit-level data were obtained through a standardized electronic survey describing hospital characteristics, workforce distribution, monitoring capabilities, and clinical protocols. The primary objective was to characterize the distribution of structural and organizational features of participating PICUs across the región; secondary outcomes examined multidisciplinary coverage and adherence to standardized care practices.
FINDINGS: Among 339 PICUs (70.6% public; 61.4% university-affiliated), nearly half had fewer than ten beds. Median physician-to-patient ratio was 1:5-6 by day and 1:8-10 overnight. Nursing ratios varied widely, most favourable in the Iberian region (≈1:1-2) and least in the Andean block (≈1:3-4), underscoring inequities in bedside care capacity. Only 68% of units had dedicated physiotherapists, with far lower coverage from nutritionists, psychologists, or pharmacists. Basic monitoring and ventilation were nearly universal (>95%), yet advanced technologies-cardiac output, near-infrared spectroscopy, renal replacement therapy-were available in fewer than 40% of centers. Structured protocols for sepsis, mechanical ventilation, sedation, or antimicrobial stewardship were reported in only 56% of PICUs, with adherence highest in the Iberian and lowest in the Andean and Caribbean regions.
INTERPRETATION: This multinational, multicentre assessment provides the first comprehensive and contemporary map of pediatric critical care capacity across Ibero-Latin America, revealing major disparities in infrastructure, human resources, and protocol implementation. Strengthening human capital, multidisciplinary training, and regionally adapted strategies is essential to achieve equitable, high-quality critical care for children across the region.
FUNDING: This work was supported by institutional funding from the Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo (FAPESP; Grant No. 2017/21052-0), provided to the Latin American Sepsis Institute (ILAS) to support the conduct of the study, including research assistant and statistical support.

articles.title: Gender bias in stereotypes of autism: Assessing the non-prototypicality of autistic women within the autistic group.
articles.abstract: Autistic women face specific challenges and feel they do not fit the autistic prototype. This paper examines the gendered nature of stereotypes towards autistic individuals as a possible underlying mechanism, owing to the apparent incompatibility between stereotypes on autistic individuals and stereotypes on women. In four studies, stereotypes about autistic individuals were analysed through a gendered (Studies 1 and 2) or intersectional lens (Studies 3 and 4). The first two studies used a trait nomination task (Study 1) or ecological traits (Study 2). Contrary to expectations, in these studies, stereotypes towards autistic individuals were represented by traits that are more predominantly perceived as feminine. However, more detailed analysis suggests that this varies according to facets of social evaluation. To deepen these results, two other studies focused on perceptions within the intersectional space. Study 3 underlined that core characteristics associated with autistic individuals are perceived as more representative of autistic men than of autistic women. Finally, a fourth study suggests that autistic women are being perceived differently than the average of autistic individuals and autistic men. These findings suggest that core facets of the stereotypes of autism are more masculine, suggesting a non-prototypicality of autistic women within the autistic community.

articles.title: Youth Correlates of Genetic Liability to Substance Use Disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Substance use disorders (SUDs) are moderately to highly heritable and develop in stages that typically begin in adolescence or young adulthood. The predominant use of cross-sectional adult samples to study SUDs and their genetic liability leaves it unclear whether their correlates may plausibly reflect predispositional risk and/or arise as a consequence of exposure.
METHODS: We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of polygenic scores (PGSs) for SUDs (i.e., problematic alcohol use, tobacco use disorder, cannabis use disorder [CUD], opioid use disorder [OUD], and a general addiction risk factor) in children ages 8 to 13 years (n European ancestry = 5556; n African American ancestry = 1584) enrolled in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study. Up to 1697 phenotypes were examined across several domains, including mental health, substance use, physical health, cognition, and screen media.
RESULTS: The PheWAS yielded 309 significant associations with the SUD PGS, particularly among mental health, sleep, screen time, and caffeine consumption phenotypes. Most associations remained significant in substance-naïve participants. The CUD PGS had the largest number of associations and was particularly associated with externalizing behavior in both genetic ancestry subsamples. OUD PGS associations were enriched for cognitive and neighborhood environmental phenotypes. Neuroimaging phenotypes (e.g., resting-state functional connectivity) partially accounted for associations between the SUD PGS and screen time phenotypes.
CONCLUSIONS: Genetic liability to SUDs is expressed during childhood as potentially modifiable risk factors that could be targeted to attenuate its expression in adolescence and adulthood.

articles.title: Usability of Turbuhaler devices for children aged 5 to 11 years with asthma: A STep-wise Anti-inflammatory Reliever Therapy Children's Asthma Research substudy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dry powder inhalers (DPIs) are an effective delivery system for asthma medications in children, yet global practice relies on the use of metered-dose inhalers, which have a greater environmental impact. A key issue relevant to implementation in clinical practice is whether children can master the technique and inspiratory flow required to use DPIs.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the ability of children aged 5 to 11 years with asthma to use the Turbuhaler DPI.
METHODS: Satisfactory Turbuhaler performance was assessed as part of the STep-wise Anti-inflammatory Reliever Therapy Children's Asthma Research study. This was assessed in the following 2 parts: an inspiratory flow rate assessment and the ability to perform all key steps using a dummy Turbuhaler DPI. The data from the first 100 children enrolled across 2 sites were used for this substudy.
RESULTS: Of the 100 participants, only 1 had unsatisfactory inspiratory flow assessment at their first visit. All other participants achieved satisfactory performance for both inspiratory flow and the Turbuhaler technique. All mandatory steps of the dummy Turbuhaler technique were achieved by 13% of participants on their very first attempt; however, this increased substantially across subsequent attempts and visits. Satisfactory inspiratory flow rates were achieved by 93% of children on their very first attempt.
CONCLUSIONS: With repeated training, almost all children aged 5 to 11 years can correctly use a Turbuhaler DPI device and achieve satisfactory inspiratory flow when clinically stable. It is important that children have their DPI technique checked and corrected at each asthma review following initial training.

articles.title: Depressive symptoms are associated with poor asthma control in adults and adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinically significant depressive symptoms are common among those with asthma, yet their impact on asthma outcomes is not well defined.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between depressive symptoms and asthma outcomes.
METHODS: In this pooled cross-sectional analysis of 741 participants aged ≥15 years from 3 multicenter studies, we examined whether depressive symptoms (assessed with validated surveys) were associated with asthma control, symptoms, quality of life, lung function, and exacerbations. Associations between clinically significant depressive symptoms and asthma-related outcomes were analyzed using analysis of covariance, adjusted for age, sex, race, body mass index, education level, and the parent study to account for potential confounding and between-study differences.
RESULTS: Clinically significant depressive symptoms were present in a substantial proportion of participants (n = 483; 65.2%) and were associated with worse asthma control, with higher odds of poorly controlled asthma (odds ratio, 1.98; 95% CI, 1.45-2.71; P < .001). Among participants with depressive symptoms, 68.1% (n = 329) had poorly controlled asthma, compared with 50.2% (n = 130) without depressive symptoms. Symptom burden was greater in those with depressive symptoms (0.727 vs 0.768; P < .001). Asthma-specific quality of life scores were lower in those with depressive symptoms (4.85 vs 5.35; P < .001). Health-related quality of life was also lower in those with depressive symptoms (63.62 vs 73.34; P < .001). Depressive symptoms were not associated with spirometric measures or exacerbation frequency.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinically significant depressive symptoms in adults with uncontrolled asthma are associated with worse perceived disease burden and quality of life but not with objective measures of lung function or exacerbation risk.

articles.title: Using serum eosinophil-derived neurotoxin to differentiate asthma from other allergic diseases in children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allergic diseases, including asthma, are increasingly prevalent among pediatric populations. Diagnostic measures are limited and often nonspecific, due to overlapping symptoms and inaccessibility to pulmonary function tests.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate serum eosinophil-derived neurotoxin (EDN) and blood eosinophil count (BEC) for differentiating asthma from other allergic diseases.
METHODS: We enrolled pediatric participants (1 to 17 years old) with asthma (n = 74), other allergic conditions (n = 35), or neither (healthy participants, n = 32). BEC, blood neutrophil count, and EDN concentrations were measured and compared among 3 groups. The potential contribution of each biomarker to asthma and allergy diagnoses was analyzed based on machine learning classifier models.
RESULTS: The asthma group had significantly higher overall levels of serum EDN than the allergic and healthy groups (median 55.5 vs 40.7 vs 30.1 μg/L, respectively; P < .001). The asthma group had significantly higher BEC than the healthy group (median 0.29 × 109 cells/L vs 0.16 × 109 cells/L; P = .002), whereas the elevation against the allergic group (median 0.20 × 109 cells/L) was not statistically significant. No healthy participants exhibited elevated EDN, but some showed elevated BEC. Most patients with asthma also had other allergic conditions, such as food allergy or atopic dermatitis. In multifeature classifier models including blood biomarkers, clinical attributes, and demographic factors, the addition of BEC or EDN similarly improved overall model accuracy when differentiating asthma from other allergic conditions and healthy state.
CONCLUSIONS: BEC and EDN elevations were both frequently observed in patients with various allergic diseases. EDN may aid the asthma diagnosis among patients with allergy, with more studies warranted.

articles.title: Holding it together: how mothers' work becomes knowledge in childhood spinal cord injury.
articles.journal: Int J Qual Stud Health Well-being
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Parents of children with spinal cord injury navigate support and care across services and everyday life, yet their experiences remain underexplored. This study examined mothers' experiences across these contexts as work and as a source of experiential knowledge.
METHODS: The qualitative study incorporated participatory elements and included five interviews, one workshop, and two follow-up sessions with five mothers. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Four themes were developed: (1) Facing services that do not connect; (2) Carrying what services leave disconnected; (3) Walking a tightrope in uneven relationships; and (4) Making connection and belonging possible in everyday life. Gaps between services became visible as ongoing work carried into family life. Through this work, mothers developed experiential knowledge of what it takes for support and care to function around the child.
CONCLUSIONS: This knowledge comes from a position across services and everyday life that no single service or professional role can occupy. Coordination responsibilities must be clearly assigned within services, and mothers' experiential knowledge should inform how these responsibilities are fulfilled. Involvement in research, practice, and policy should enable mothers to contribute on their own terms, without adding to their workload, and address unequal relationships with services and professionals.

articles.title: Youth perspectives on tuberculosis prevention in South Africa: A qualitative study in faith-based organisations.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading public health challenge in South Africa, with high rates of co-infection with HIV. Faith-based organisations (FBOs) have untapped potential to support TB prevention, particularly by engaging youth who are often overlooked. This study explored youth perspectives on TB prevention and FBOs' roles in advancing youth-led, culturally grounded health promotion strategies in Johannesburg, South Africa. A qualitative, exploratory study was conducted using five focus group discussions with youth aged 18-30 years from Christian, Muslim, and Rastafarian faith communities. The study was guided by principles of Community-Based Participatory Research and Human-Centered Design, applying the 'Define' and 'Develop' phases of the Double Diamond model. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Participants demonstrated a blend of biomedical knowledge and persistent TB myths. Youth identified FBOs as trusted yet underutilised platforms and proposed strategies including music, storytelling, drama, peer-led health clubs, and digital campaigns. They expressed readiness to lead within faith institutions but noted barriers, including resistance from traditional hierarchies and limited resources. Youth in faith communities possess the creativity, insight, and commitment to transform TB prevention efforts. Strengthening partnerships between youth and FBOs, and investing in participatory, faith-aligned health promotion models, could yield more equitable and sustainable public health outcomes in high-burden settings.

articles.title: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization.
articles.abstract: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development. After birth, rapid microbial colonization occurs in the intestine and lungs. Through signaling molecules including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, and bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs), coupled with vagal nerve and mucosal immune pathways, the microbiota maintains intestinal and pulmonary immune homeostasis, preserves blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and modulates microglial activation, thereby regulating neurogenesis, synaptic pruning, and brain functional programming. Early-life dysbiosis is commonly associated with preterm birth, cesarean delivery, infection, and antibiotic exposure. In human observational studies, it accompanies disrupted organ homeostasis and neuroinflammatory signatures, and is linked to an increased long-term risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disability; in neonatal animal models, it aggravates hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and encephalopathy of prematurity. Because dysbiosis frequently co-occurs with prematurity, infection, and other confounders, these associations do not by themselves establish causality. This review summarizes early-life colonization patterns of intestinal and pulmonary microbiota and their underlying neuroimmune mechanisms, analyzes the impacts of dysbiosis on neuroimmunity and related diseases, and proposes intervention strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for neonatal health protection and neurodevelopmental disorder prevention.

articles.title: All-cause mortality among persons with and without diagnosed diabetes in Greenland: a nationwide register-based cohort study.
articles.abstract: Mortality has historically been about twice as high in people with diabetes as in those without, although this gap has narrowed in high-income countries. Whether this pattern also applies in Greenland is unknown. We estimated age- and sex-specific mortality rates and mortality rate ratios by diabetes status in Greenland. In this nationwide register-based cohort study, we included all persons with a registered civil address in Greenland from 2017 to 2023 and used Poisson regression to estimate mortality per 1,000 person-years, mortality rate ratios by diabetes status and sex, and the annual change in mortality. Of 87,652 residents, 2,670 had diagnosed diabetes. During the study period, 3,639 persons died, 388 of whom had diabetes. Age-specific mortality rates were slightly higher among persons with diabetes than among persons without diabetes at most ages in both sexes. However, the differences were not statistically significant. The largest rate ratios were seen at younger ages (death before 50 years). Mortality declined over calendar time in the general population (7% per year in women, 5% in men) but remained unchanged in persons with diabetes. Mortality in Greenland did not differ by diabetes status, which may reflect adequate access to and quality of diabetes care, survivorship bias, or competing risks.

articles.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation for pediatric Clostridioides difficile infection: efficacy, challenges, and the path to next-generation microbiome therapies.
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is an increasing cause of morbidity in children, with recurrent disease posing substantial therapeutic challenges. Antibiotic therapy remains the cornerstone of initial management; however, up to 30% of children experience recurrence, and those with underlying comorbidities face recurrence rates as high as 65%. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has demonstrated superior efficacy over antibiotics for recurrent CDI (rCDI) in adults and has emerged as the most effective available intervention for pediatric rCDI. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on FMT efficacy, microbiome changes, and safety in children with CDI. Data from large multicenter cohort studies demonstrate cure rates exceeding 80%, with comparable efficacy observed in high-risk subpopulations, including those with inflammatory bowel disease and immunocompromising conditions. Critical research gaps remain, including the absence of randomized controlled trials and limited long-term safety data in children. Despite demonstrated effectiveness, significant barriers limit FMT accessibility for children. The COVID-19 pandemic has substantially impacted availability, and current regulatory changes have further restricted access. The lack of FDA-approved live biotherapeutic products approved for CDI in children creates additional challenges. We critically examine the emerging pipeline of next-generation microbiome-based therapies and identify the steps required to ensure children with recurrent CDI have access to safe, effective, and approved treatments.

articles.title: Changes in full vaccination coverage and in the gap between poor and non-poor households among children aged 12-23 months in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2013-14 to 2023-24: a comparison of two Demographic and Health surveys.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunisation coverage in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is far below global targets, and poorer children are less often vaccinated. Expanded outreach since 2013-14 could have narrowed this gap; COVID-19, outbreaks and conflict could have widened it.
OBJECTIVES: To estimate full vaccination, BCG and DPT3 coverage in 2013-14 and 2023-24, the change in the poor-non-poor gap in full vaccination (primary outcome), and its provincial variation.
METHODS: Repeated cross-sectional analysis of the 2013-14 and 2023-24 Demographic and Health Surveys (3,443 and 4,208 children aged 12-23 months). Poor: poorest 40% by household wealth index. Weighted linear probability models with a poor-by-survey interaction estimated the change in the percentage-point gap; a provincial interaction model assessed heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Full vaccination fell from 45.3% (95% CI 42.1-48.5) to 21.0% (18.5-23.4), BCG from 83.4% to 69.2%, and DPT3 from 60.6% to 46.3%; children with no DPT dose rose from 18.9% to 33.5%. Coverage fell in every province and wealth group. The full-vaccination gap was 16.0 points in 2013-14 and 12.4 in 2023-24 (change +3.6; 95% CI - 2.8 to +10.1; inconclusive). In secondary analyses, poor children's relative coverage fell more (ratio of ratios 0.77; 0.59-0.99), BCG, DPT3 and measles gaps widened by 7.8-11.7 points and changes differed across provinces (p = 0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Fewer than one in four children was fully vaccinated in 2023-24. Routine and catch-up immunisation must recover in all wealth groups and provinces, prioritising the poorest children.

articles.title: Metabolic profiling of brain and cerebrospinal fluid in cerebral malaria.
articles.abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM), a severe neurological complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection, is a common cause of pediatric mortality and long-term cognitive impairment in endemic regions. The mechanisms driving CM-associated coma and neuropathology are not fully understood. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of brain tissue from experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) mouse models and brain autopsy tissue and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from children with CM and non-malarial coma (NMC). ECM brain samples exhibited significant metabolic alterations, including differences in energy metabolism and amino acids and elevated pipecolic and lactic acids. In contrast, CM and NMC brain metabolomes showed limited differences. CSF metabolomes from cohorts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Malawi showed elevated glyceric acid in CM compared with NMC. Together, these findings highlight metabolic perturbations in CM across species and sample types and identify glyceric acid as a potential CSF biomarker.

articles.title: Risk of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension Following Anemia in Young Adults: A Retrospective Cohort TriNetX Database Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Anemia has been associated with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) in small studies, but whether severity modulates IIH risk remains unclear. This study evaluated the hazard of incident IIH after mild, moderate, and severe anemia in young adults.
METHODS: Using the TriNetX Research Network (111) health care organizations), adults aged 18-50 years with persistent anemia (≥2 hemoglobin values) were stratified as mild (11.0-12.9 g/dL), moderate (8.0-10.9 g/dL), or severe (<8.0 g/dL) and matched 1:1 to controls (Hb ≥ 13.0 g/dL) by propensity score matching on demographics, body mass index, comorbidities, and socioeconomic factors. The primary outcome was incident IIH; Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) at 6 months, 1 year, and 3 years. Sensitivity analyses applied the World Health Organization (WHO) women's mild threshold and compared patients with vs without iron supplementation.
RESULTS: After matching, 1,240,670 mild anemia patients (mean age 29.0 ± 8.7 years, 83.4% female), 666,515 moderate (29.7 ± 8.1, 86.3% female), and 114,785 severe (31.0 ± 8.9, 75.4% female) were compared with equal-sized control cohorts. Hazard of incident IIH was elevated at every severity and time interval. At 6 months, HRs were 1.45 (95% CI 1.29-1.63), 1.61 (1.39-1.86), and 2.53 (1.82-3.52) for mild, moderate, and severe anemia. At 1 year, HRs were 1.35 (1.22-1.49), 1.33 (1.17-1.51), and 1.94 (1.46-2.58). At 3 years, HRs were 1.17 (1.08-1.26), 1.15 (1.04-1.27), and 1.40 (1.11-1.76); all estimates remained significantly elevated, although CIs overlapped across severity bands. The WHO women's threshold sensitivity yielded concordant, modestly stronger estimates (6 months: HR 1.99 [1.73-2.30]; 3 years: 1.43 [1.31-1.58]). Iron supplementation was associated with reduced IIH hazard (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.93; n = 340,660 per group).
DISCUSSION: Anemia is associated with elevated hazard of incident IIH in young adults across all severity bands. Point estimates were higher with greater anemia severity and at earlier follow-up, but CIs overlapped across severity bands, so a severity gradient could not be established. Iron supplementation was associated with reduced hazard. Findings are limited by observational design, administrative case identification, and low absolute incidence; anemia represents a potentially modifiable factor warranting evaluation in patients with papilledema.

articles.title: The Combined Effect of Migraine and Smoking on Premature Stroke and All-Cause Mortality in Parous Women: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Migraine and smoking are established stroke risk factors. We examined the individual and combined effects of migraine and smoking on risk of premature stroke (age 60 years or younger) and all-cause mortality in women and evaluated additive interaction.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based cohort study using nationwide Danish health registries (1996-2022). Women aged 15-60 years giving birth during 1996-2022 were identified through the Danish Medical Birth Registry and categorized as having migraine, smoking, both exposures, or neither (reference). Participants were followed until stroke, death, emigration, 61st birthday, or December 31, 2022. Outcomes were ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and all-cause mortality. Absolute risks (ARs), adjusted hazard ratios (HRs), and relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) were estimated.
RESULTS: Among 1,677,707 women (median age 29-32 years across exposure groups), the 20-year AR of premature ischemic stroke was 0.8% in the reference cohort (n = 1,389,361), 1.3% with migraine (n = 65,422), 1.5% with smoking (n = 214,277), and 2.8% with both exposures (n = 8,647). ARs of premature hemorrhagic stroke were 0.3%, 0.5%, 0.6%, and 0.9%. All-cause mortality ARs were 1.0%, 1.2%, 2.3%, and 3.4%. Compared with the reference cohort, adjusted HRs for premature ischemic stroke were 1.85 (95% CI 1.66-2.05) for migraine, 2.10 (95% CI 1.99-2.20) for smoking, and 3.61 (95% CI 3.03-4.31) for both exposures. HRs for premature hemorrhagic stroke were 1.46 (95% CI 1.23-1.74), 2.02 (95% CI 1.87-2.18), and 2.60 (95% CI 1.91-3.54). For all-cause mortality, HRs were 1.08 (95% CI 0.96-1.22), 2.44 (95% CI 2.34-2.54), and 3.30 (95% CI 2.80-3.88). The 20-year RERI was 0.67 (95% CI 0.22-1.13) for ischemic stroke, 0.11 (95% CI -0.59-0.82) for hemorrhagic stroke, and 0.78 (95% CI 0.34-1.22) for mortality.
DISCUSSION: Migraine and smoking were associated with elevated risk of premature stroke, and mortality risk was increased among women who smoked regardless of migraine status. Additive interaction indicated excess risk of ischemic stroke and all-cause mortality among women with migraine who smoked. These findings support targeted cessation strategies to reduce premature vascular events and mortality.

articles.title: Validation of the BASED Score as a Prognostic Biomarker for Refractory Epilepsy Following Treatment of Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
