BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Refractory epilepsy is common among children with a history of infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS), yet no validated prognostic biomarkers exist to guide early risk stratification. The Burden of Amplitudes and Epileptiform Discharges (BASED) score is an interictal EEG rating scale for children with IESS, with scores of 4 or 5 suggesting epileptic encephalopathy. The objective of this study was to determine whether a post-treatment BASED score of 4/5 is a prognostic biomarker for refractory epilepsy after IESS treatment.
METHODS: This retrospective validation study of children with IESS was conducted at a Level 4 pediatric epilepsy center. Children with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) were excluded. Three blinded reviewers assigned 2021 BASED scores to full-length post-treatment EEGs. Refractory epilepsy was defined as persistent seizures despite treatment with at least 2 antiseizure medications or completion of epilepsy surgery. Prespecified performance benchmarks for BASED 4/5 as a rule-in test required ≥80% specificity and a positive likelihood ratio of ≥4.
RESULTS: The cohort included 123 children (42.3% female), with a median first treatment age of 8.0 months (IQR 5.9-10.3) and follow-up duration after first treatment of 58.8 months (IQR 42.2-80.7). Only 11.4% had a favorable etiology. EEGs (median 19 hours) were completed at a median of 47 days (32-72) after starting treatment. The inter-rater agreement for epileptic encephalopathy was excellent (κfree = 0.78). Half (52%) of the children had refractory epilepsy. BASED 4/5 demonstrated high specificity (88.1%, 95% CI 77.1-95.1) for refractory epilepsy, with a positive likelihood ratio of 4.4 (2.1-9.1). The sensitivity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 51.6% (38.7-64.3), 82.5% (69.3-90.8), and 62.7% (56.1-68.7), respectively. An exploratory composite indicator comprising BASED 4/5, persistent epileptic spasms, and/or epileptic spasms relapse demonstrated higher sensitivity (79.7%, 67.8-88.7) with modestly reduced specificity (81.4%, 69.1-90.3).
DISCUSSION: Study limitations include the single-center design, exclusion of children with TSC, variable EEG timing, and shorter follow-up in some children. Nevertheless, in this independent validation cohort, a post-treatment BASED 4/5 demonstrated favorable prognostic performance consistent with its proposed use as a rule-in test for refractory epilepsy. These findings support a post-treatment BASED score of 4/5 as a prognostic biomarker for refractory epilepsy after IESS treatment.

articles.title: Adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health services in Asia-Pacific settings: a systematic scoping review.
articles.abstract: In the Asia-Pacific region, adolescents face significant impacts from unintended pregnancy and are disproportionately affected by the growing HIV epidemic. Despite decades of policy commitments, adolescents have high unmet need for sexual and reproductive health services. The World Health Organization's 2015 global standards for quality adolescent health services provide a framework, but evidence of their implementation in the region remains limited. This systematic scoping review mapped approaches to adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health service delivery in Asia-Pacific low- and middle-income countries and factors influencing implementation. On 6 January 2026, three databases (Medline, Embase and Scopus) were searched for peer-reviewed literature published between January 2019 and December 2025. In line with scoping review methodology, methodological quality was not assessed. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning nine South and Southeast Asian countries; none were from Pacific Island countries. The most evidence was available for Standards 1, 3 and 5. Where studies reported on equity and non-discrimination (Standard 6), and providers' competencies (Standard 4), they described shortfalls, although evidence on competencies was mixed. Few studies reported on community support, data and quality improvement, or adolescents' participation (Standards 2, 7 and 8), reflecting limited available evidence. These findings underscore priorities for investment in adolescent health. More comprehensive, adolescent-centred sexual and reproductive health services and action on stigma are needed, with adolescent engagement and co-leadership central to this shift. Self-care may complement formal health systems, although evidence of its effectiveness in the region remains limited.

articles.title: The impact of a co-designed PrEP referral directory on PrEP continuation among migrant female sex workers in Kisii County, Kenya.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Kenya, female sex workers (FSWs) are disproportionately burdened with HIV compared with the general population. Low continuation of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among FSWs, driven by temporary or permanent migration from safe spaces, heightens their risk of HIV acquisition and transmission, as many do not know where to access PrEP in new locations. We evaluated the impact of a PrEP referral directory in enhancing PrEP continuation among young migrant FSWs.
METHODS: We adopted a pre-post study design, with PrEP continuation as the primary outcome. Health facilities offering PrEP in common migration destinations were mapped. FSWs aged 18-24 years were randomly selected from a safe space register, enrolled, and provided with a co-designed PrEP referral directory listing PrEP-offering facilities. Participants were encouraged to call, or text prior to migrating to facilitate early linkage to services. Phone-based follow-up interviews and facility records were used to assess continuation, comparing pre- and post-intervention periods.
RESULTS: We enrolled 299 participants: mean age was 22 years; 12 out of 299 had no formal education, 163 out of 299 had primary education and 239 out of 299 were single. Migration was the main barrier to continuation (48.1%), with 28.4% migrating twice and 23.7% three times monthly. Post-intervention, 68.2% obtained PrEP refills at linked facilities, with 96.0% citing the directory as the main facilitator. PrEP continuation increased from 17.6% pre-intervention to 41.3% post-intervention (P < 0.001). Monthly continuation rose significantly: 11% versus 40% (OR 5.1, 95% CI: 2.47-11.89) in Month 1; 20% versus 38% (OR 2.5, 95% CI: 1.36-4.96) in Month 2; 22% versus 43% (OR 2.4, 95% CI: 1.38-4.49) in Month 3; 19% versus 47% in Month 4 (OR 3.9, 95% CI: 2.04-8.11); 17% versus 43% in Month 5 (OR 3.9, 95% CI: 1.98-8.41); and 17% versus 37% in Month 6 (OR 2.8, 95% CI: 1.48-5.55). All comparisons were statistically significant (P < 0.001 for Months 1, 4 and 5; P = 0.002 for Month 2, P = 0.0013 for Month 3 and P = 0.0008 for Month 6).
CONCLUSION: The PrEP referral directory significantly improved PrEP continuation among migrating FSWs. Integrating such mobility-responsive tools into PrEP programming could strengthen PrEP continuation among mobile key populations.

articles.title: Evaluation of collateral circulation in symptomatic Moyamoya disease using artificial intelligence-assisted whole-brain computed tomography perfusion-derived dynamic four-dimensional computed tomography angiography.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical value of artificial intelligence-assisted dynamic four-dimensional computed tomography angiography (4D-CTA) reconstructed from whole-brain computed tomography perfusion (CTP) source data for assessing collateral circulation in symptomatic Moyamoya disease (MMD).
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 36 patients with digital subtraction angiography (DSA)-confirmed symptomatic MMD who underwent CTP and single-phase CTA (sCTA). Three datasets were derived: group A, conventional sCTA; group B, CTP-derived arterial-phase images; and group C, artificial intelligence-postprocessed 4D-CTA using the Shukun AI algorithm. Image quality was assessed in the arterial phase using objective parameters [CT attenuation, image noise, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR)] and subjective scores. The diagnostic performance of 4D-CTA was evaluated against DSA for modified Suzuki staging (mSS) and collateral circulation assessment.
RESULTS: Group C showed significantly higher CT attenuation value of the vessel, SNR, CNR, and subjective scores, and significantly lower standard deviation of the vessel and standard deviation of the brain parenchyma than groups A and B (all P < 0.05; most P < 0.001). The 4D-CTA showed excellent agreement with DSA in mSS grading (P < 0.001) and a strong positive correlation (P < 0.001). For collateral circulation grading, good agreement (P < 0.001) and moderate positive correlation (P < 0.001) were observed.
CONCLUSION: Artificial intelligence-assisted 4D-CTA reconstructed from whole-brain CTP enables comprehensive multiphase vascular visualization without additional radiation exposure. It facilitates rapid, reliable, noninvasive evaluation of collateral circulation in symptomatic MMD, offering diagnostic accuracy comparable with DSA with promising potential for routine clinical application.

articles.title: Frequency-Specific Thalamocortical Network Dynamics During Focal Seizures in Humans.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The thalamus is an emerging neuromodulation target in drug-resistant focal epilepsy because of its frequent ictal involvement. However, frequency-specific and directional thalamocortical dynamics remain poorly understood. We sought to characterize thalamocortical network dynamics across seizure evolution using stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed SEEG recordings from patients with pediatric-onset drug-resistant focal epilepsy with simultaneous cortical and thalamic sampling focusing on the anterior nucleus (AN) and centromedian nucleus (CM). We applied visual analysis with quantitative measures of spectral power, imaginary coherence, and spectral Granger causality across slow (1-12 Hz), β (13-30 Hz), and γ (30-70 Hz) bands to quantify thalamocortical and cortico-cortical interactions from seizure onset to termination. Random forest models were trained to classify seizure state using thalamic EEG features as an exploratory analysis.
RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 19 patients (median age, 16.9 years; 31.6% female), with 66 focal seizures analyzed. Thalamic ictal activity was present at seizure onset in 81% of sampled thalamic contacts and became nearly universal by seizure termination. Both the thalamus and seizure onset zone showed increased spectral power during seizures, with prominent slow-band augmentation at seizure termination in the thalamus. Similarly, thalamocortical imaginary coherence increased during seizures, with the largest changes near seizure termination in the slow band (AN-SOZ: 11% [IQR, 2 to 20], rank-biserial correlations (rrb) = 0.84; CM-SOZ: 12% [IQR, 3 to 23], rrb = 0.84) and β band (AN-SOZ: 5% [IQR, 0 to 12], rrb = 0.74; CM-SOZ: 8% [IQR, 2 to 15], rrb = 0.86). Directed connectivity analyses demonstrated bidirectional thalamocortical interactions, with large slow-frequency thalamus-to-SOZ outflow near seizure termination from both AN and CM, exceeding propagation-zone-to-SOZ cortico-cortical flow (both p < 0.01). Seizure state was classified using thalamic EEG features, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.825 for AN and 0.839 for CM.
DISCUSSION: Human focal seizures engage frequency-specific and bidirectional thalamocortical interactions that evolve from onset to termination. These findings support the thalamus as a source of clinically relevant seizure-state information and may inform thalamic biomarker development for neuromodulation in drug-resistant epilepsy.

articles.title: Influenza vaccination coverage and associated factors, including asthma diagnosis, in Korea: analysis of the Korea national health and nutrition examination survey (2014-2021).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate influenza vaccination coverage and associated factors in the South Korean population, focusing on individuals with asthma across age groups.
METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted using Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (2014-2021) for 43,191 individuals (aged ≥6 years). Vaccination rates and predictors were examined in the general population and those with asthma across four age cohorts (6-13, 14-18, 19-64, and ≥ 65 years) using survey-weighted logistic regression.
RESULTS: Vaccination coverage was consistently higher among individuals with asthma than those without: 68.2% vs. 62.8% (ages 6-13), 36.8% vs. 27.1% (ages 14-18), 28.5% vs. 27.0% (ages 19-39), 48.2% vs. 32.1% (ages 40-64), and 85.3% vs. 82.5% (ages ≥65). Female sex and chronic comorbidities positively correlated with vaccination. Increasing age was linked to lower coverage in youth but higher coverage in adults. Notably, asthma history independently predicted vaccination in age groups with lower baseline coverage.
CONCLUSIONS: Although individuals with asthma showed higher coverage, vaccination rates remained suboptimal, particularly among adolescents and working-age adults. Proactive age-tailored vaccination strategies are needed.

articles.title: Leucine exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes in maple syrup urine disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic, longitudinal, and treatment-related evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurodevelopmental impairment remains a major long-term complication of maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). Although leucine is a principal neurotoxic metabolite, studies have characterized exposure using clinically distinct measures, including diagnostic or acute peak concentrations and longitudinal indices of metabolic control. We therefore evaluated these exposure patterns separately and examined neurodevelopmental outcomes in the context of early diagnosis and liver transplantation.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to July 26, 2026. A total of 203 records were identified through database searching (63 PubMed/MEDLINE, 58 Scopus, and 82 Web of Science); 46 unique studies were included after deduplication, screening, full-text assessment, and supplementary reference-list searching. Leucine exposure was classified as diagnostic/peak or long-term/mean exposure. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to studies with sufficiently comparable populations, exposure definitions, outcomes, and effect measures. Correlations between long-term/mean leucine and IQ were transformed to Fisher's z, pooled using inverse-variance random-effects weighting with the DerSimonian-Laird estimator of between-study variance, and back-transformed to Pearson's r. Heterogeneous outcomes were synthesized narratively. Methodological quality and risk of bias were appraised with JBI tools appropriate to study design.
RESULTS: Four studies (total N = 61) contributed to the long-term/mean leucine-IQ meta-analysis. Higher long-term/mean leucine exposure was associated with lower IQ (pooled r = -0.40, 95% CI -0.66 to -0.05; I2 = 39%; tau2 = 0.056). The 95% prediction interval was -0.77 to 0.17. Leave-one-out analyses identified the small le Roux study as influential; its exclusion yielded r = -0.52 (95% CI -0.70 to -0.27; I2 = 0%). Diagnostic/peak leucine showed a less consistent relationship with later neurodevelopment and was not combined in a single pool. The approximately 200 μmol/L value reported in longitudinal evidence is best interpreted as a study-level treatment-associated target in young children, not a universal neurotoxicity threshold. Newborn screening and early diagnosis were generally associated with more favorable clinical and neurological outcomes. Liver transplantation consistently improved metabolic stability, whereas neurocognitive improvement was variable.
CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal leucine exposure appears more consistently associated with neurodevelopmental outcome in MSUD than a single concentration measured at diagnosis or during an acute episode. The findings support early diagnosis and sustained metabolic control while cautioning against interpreting any single leucine value as a universal neurotoxicity threshold. Liver transplantation provides robust metabolic stabilization but may not reverse established cognitive impairment.

articles.title: Validity and reliability of the Turkish version of the modified Yale food addiction scale for children 2.0 among adolescents in Istanbul, Türkiye.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study adapted and validated the Turkish Modified Yale Food Addiction Scale for Children 2.0 (mYFAS-C 2.0) in adolescents aged 13-17 years.
METHODS: Following World Health Organization guidelines, 532 adolescents (267 non-clinical, 265 clinical) in Istanbul, Türkiye completed the mYFAS-C 2.0, Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire Short Form, and Perceived Stress Scale. Construct validity and three-week test-retest reliability (n = 91) were evaluated.
RESULTS: Exploratory factor analysis supported a single-factor structure (46.11% variance). Confirmatory factor analysis showed good fit (χ2/df = 4.19, comparative fit index = 0.93, Tucker-Lewis index = 0.91, standardized root mean square residual = 0.04, root mean square error of approximation = 0.08; loadings: 0.58-0.74). Cronbach's α (0.90) and intraclass correlation coefficient (0.99) demonstrated high reliability. Total scores correlated with eating pathology (r = 0.68) and perceived stress (r = 0.32) (p < 0.01). Clinical participants scored higher than non-clinical controls (28.24 ± 11.16 vs. 20.37 ± 5.95, p < 0.01), peaking in adolescents with obesity (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: The Turkish mYFAS-C 2.0 is a valid, reliable instrument for assessing addictive-like eating behaviors among Turkish adolescents aged 13-17 years.

articles.title: Anxiety and depressive disorders among children and young people following a cancer diagnosis in England: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychiatric conditions are important survivorship outcomes among children and young people (CYP) diagnosed with cancer. However, many population-based studies have examined hospital contacts only, and estimates of absolute risk can be biased when competing mortality is not accounted for. We estimated absolute risks and relative hazards of clinically recorded anxiety and related disorders, depressive disorders, and first-time psychotropic prescribing.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based matched retrospective cohort study across 1474 general practices in England using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum primary care records linked to Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care and mortality records. CYP diagnosed with malignant cancer or any central nervous system tumour at ages 0-24 years between Jan 1, 2000, and Dec 31, 2022, were matched by age, recorded sex, and general practice to up to 20 comparators without cancer at the index date. Primary outcomes were first recorded anxiety and related disorders and depressive disorders; secondary outcomes were first-time psychotropic prescribing. Individuals with pre-index records of the respective outcome were excluded from that outcome analysis. Follow-up ended at outcome occurrence, death, practice deregistration, last data collection, or Dec 31, 2022. We estimated cumulative incidence using the Aalen-Johansen estimator and ethnicity-adjusted cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs) using matched-set stratified Cox models.
FINDINGS: There were 9145 CYP with cancer and 178709 comparators. Adjusted cause-specific HRs were 1.74 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.61-1.88) for anxiety and related disorders, 1.16 (1.06-1.26) for depressive disorders, 1.27 (1.20-1.35) for antidepressant prescribing, 2.21 (2.05-2.38) for antipsychotic prescribing, and 2.69 (2.53-2.86) for anxiolytic prescribing. At 15 years, cumulative incidence was 14.1% (95% CI 13.0-15.3) versus 12.8% (12.5-13.1) for anxiety and related disorders, and 12.8% (11.6-14.0) versus 14.1% (13.8-14.5) for depressive disorders. Excess hazards were greatest in the early years after diagnosis.
INTERPRETATION: CYP diagnosed with cancer had higher hazards of clinically recorded anxiety and related disorders, depressive disorders, and first-time psychotropic prescribing. These findings support proactive mental health monitoring and timely referral pathways within cancer and survivorship care, particularly early after diagnosis. Further research should evaluate whether timely assessment and tailored psychosocial support improve outcomes.
FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research Manchester Biomedical Research Centre and Greater Manchester Patient Safety Research Collaboration.

articles.title: Addressing loneliness and social isolation in at-risk groups during COVID-19 and beyond: a qualitative study in Switzerland.
articles.abstract: When Switzerland implemented public health measures against COVID-19, certain populations were particularly at risk of loneliness and social isolation, e.g., adolescents and young adults, older people, and migrants. This retrospective qualitative study aimed to explore stakeholders' experiences and perspectives on addressing loneliness and social isolation among these at-risk populations, with particular attention to the contextual, protective, and barrier factors shaping these experiences. It included 36 participants across six focus groups who provided social support to at-risk groups during COVID-19 in both the German- and French-speaking parts of Switzerland. The data were analysed using applied thematic analysis. Three overarching themes were developed: (1) communication and design of public health measures, (2) seizing and adapting existing resources, and (3) establishing a culture of social relationships. According to a socio-ecological framework for loneliness and social isolation during COVID-19, this study shows the interplay between the organisational and institutional levels to which participants belonged and different levels of the social system. Stakeholders perceived that their provision of social support was connected to individual initiatives, pre-existing interpersonal relationships and community support networks. Further, poor policy communication and a lack of acknowledgement of at-risk groups' social needs impacted the ability to address loneliness and social isolation. Stakeholders described opportunities to maintain social support within pandemic restrictions, noting that Swiss public health measures provided some room to meet social needs. Their accounts suggest that future preparedness should consider social relationships alongside infection prevention, pointing to specific approaches that require further safety evaluation and ethical assessment.

articles.title: Preliminary convergent validity and group discrimination of a serious game for assessing attention in children and adolescents with and without clinician-established ADHD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmentally inappropriate inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity. Diagnosis requires a comprehensive, multi-informant clinical assessment; performance on a single attention task is neither necessary nor sufficient. This cross-sectional study examined the preliminary convergent validity, reliability, and group discrimination of Attention Robots, a serious game designed to assess attention-related performance.
METHODS: Participants were 117 children and adolescents aged 6-18 years: 47 with a clinician-established ADHD diagnosis and 70 community comparison participants without a recorded ADHD diagnosis. Attention Robots scores were examined alongside CARAS-R and CogniFit measures using correlations, age- and sex-adjusted group comparisons, split-half reliability, and exploratory ROC analyses.
RESULTS: Attention Robots scores were associated with CARAS-R inhibitory-control and several CogniFit measures. After adjustment for age and sex and correction for multiple comparisons, participants with ADHD showed lower Attention Robots concentration and working-speed scores than community comparison participants, whereas error percentage did not differ between groups. Among the CogniFit outcomes, only visual perception remained significantly different between groups after Holm correction. The game-only ROC model showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.61; sensitivity = 0.28; specificity = 0.80). A model that also included sex yielded an AUC of 0.73, with sensitivity of 0.57 and specificity of 0.76; however, the higher AUC cannot be attributed to the game because sex was unevenly distributed between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Attention Robots may provide complementary information about attention-related performance, but the present two-gate, single-site findings do not support stand-alone screening or diagnosis. Independent validation with consistently verified, sex-balanced, clinically heterogeneous samples is required.

articles.title: Clinical and microbiological pattern of invasive pneumococcal disease in adults admitted to a tertiary care hospital in Oman: a 10-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a major cause of invasive bacterial disease and a major contributor to morbidity and mortality worldwide. Pediatric pneumococcal conjugate vaccine programs have markedly reduced the burden of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) globally; however, there is a paucity of data on the clinical spectrum, antimicrobial susceptibility, vaccine uptake, and outcomes of IPD in adults from the Arabian Peninsula.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study at Sultan Qaboos University Hospital, a tertiary referral center in Muscat, Oman. Adult patients (aged ≥18 years) admitted with culture-confirmed IPD-defined as the isolation of S. pneumoniae from a normally sterile site-between January 2012 and January 2022 were included. Demographic, clinical, microbiological, vaccination, and outcome data were extracted from electronic medical records. Antimicrobial susceptibility was interpreted using the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute criteria.
RESULTS: Sixty-six adults with IPD were identified (median age, 60.5 years [interquartile range, 40-72.8]; 56.1% female). At least one indication for pneumococcal vaccination was present in 93.9% of patients; however, only 39.4% had received any pneumococcal vaccine before admission. Bacteremic pneumonia was the most frequent clinical syndrome (57.6%), followed by bacteremia of unknown source (22.7%) and meningitis (10.6%). All isolates tested were susceptible to ceftriaxone (49/49) and meropenem (25/25), 96.6% to cefotaxime (28/29), and 87.5% of nonmeningitis isolates to penicillin (49/56). The 30-day and 90-day all-cause mortality rates were 24.2% and 30.3%, respectively; 25.8% required intensive care unit admission. Mortality was highest in cases of bacteremic pneumonia (39.5% at 90 days).
CONCLUSION: Adult IPD in Oman is associated with substantial mortality despite high beta-lactam susceptibility and despite most patients being eligible for vaccination. The persistent vaccine gap supports the urgent expansion of adult pneumococcal immunization programs in Oman and the wider Gulf region.

articles.title: Complete Blood Count-Derived Inflammatory Markers in Treatment-Naive Patients With First-Episode Psychosis and First Manic Episode: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Evidence supporting the role of immune-inflammatory mechanisms in psychiatric disorders is increasing. This study compared complete blood count-derived haematological and inflammatory markers in treatment-naive patients with first-episode psychosis (FEP) or a first manic episode (FMEs) and healthy controls (HCs).
METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 74 treatment-naive patients and 91 HC. The primary analysis compared patients with HC, while secondary analyses compared the FEP and FME groups. Selected parameters showing significant between-group differences were further evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and body mass index (BMI).
RESULTS: Patients had higher white blood cell (WBC), neutrophil and platelet counts, plateletcrit, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), derived NLR (dNLR) and neutrophil-to-monocyte ratio (NMR), together with lower platelet distribution width (PDW) and mean platelet volume-to-platelet ratio (MPR). No significant differences in inflammatory markers were found between the FEP and FME groups. WBC and neutrophil counts showed the highest, although moderate, discriminative performance. In adjusted regression models, WBC count, neutrophil count, SII, SIRI and AISI were significantly associated with patient status. However, SII, SIRI and AISI provided no significant incremental explanatory value beyond neutrophil count.
CONCLUSION: Peripheral immune-inflammatory activation may already be evident in the early stages of treatment-naive FEP and FME. The absence of significant differences in inflammatory markers between the FEP and FME groups limits their potential utility as diagnosis-specific biomarkers.

articles.title: Stress-induced alterations in neurodevelopment in iPSC-Derived i n vitro model systems.
articles.abstract: Psychological stress is common in women during pregnancy and after childbirth, showing a prevalence of up to 15.6% in pregnant women in developing countries. Clinical and pre-clinical studies have implicated their role in negatively affecting pregnancy outcomes and have been linked to adverse child outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, specifically the signatures associated with their effect on human fetal development. Thereby, impairing our further understanding of the effects of therapeutics used to treat these disorders in expecting mothers. This study proposes the use of human iPSC-derived embryoid bodies (EBs) and forebrain-specific organoids as complementary human developmental models to investigate the effects of exposure to prenatal stress (mediated by glucocorticoids) across distinct stages, in vitro. Our findings suggested that excessive glucocorticoids altered early lineage specification in an exposure-dependent manner. This was evidenced by a brief increase in pluripotent and neural progenitor populations, with mild alterations in proliferative dynamics without a net change in proliferative capacity. Changes in lineage-associated markers were observed in ectodermal and meso-endodermal layers of EBs. Particularly, focusing on neurogenesis (forebrain-specific organoids) to understand the impact of stress on neurodevelopment, we saw concentration-dependent changes in progenitor maintenance and neuronal- glial differentiation. Furthermore, the activation of inflammatory and oxidative stress responses can be implicated as signalling mechanisms responsible for the differences observed. Together, these results suggest that glucocorticoid signalling linked to prenatal stress can alter developmental trajectories by modifying cellular states rather than directly altering proliferation or survival during early development.

articles.title: Recreational opportunities and mentorship at Play Marin enhance health and well-being for adolescents in Marin City, CA.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Finding evidence-based interventions and community supported solutions to the mental health crisis among youth is imperative. We aimed to understand the impact of Play Marin (PM, a community-based organization) on overall well-being using data collected from current and former students and community members.
METHODS: The research methodology consisted of a mixed methods approach: interviews were conducted with students of PM, family members and coaches in the Spring of 2024. Quantitatively, the survey data were compared between former students of PM and the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS), collected in 2024.
RESULTS: Qualitatively revealed results that individuals associated with PM experienced recreational opportunities and mentorship, better mental and physical health, and increased feelings of belonging. Quantitative results suggested participants had better mental health, less screentime, competed on more sports teams, slept more on school nights, vaped less, and felt closer to other students at school (p < 0.05) as compared to the YRBSS.
CONCLUSIONS: The current mental health crisis may be alleviated with increased recreational opportunities and mentorship for adolescents and young adults through community engagement and positive interactions. Exposure to mentors with lived experiences help adolescents gain necessary tools and resources to make better health decisions than the YRBSS.

articles.title: Phototherapy Irradiance Exposure in Near-Term Infants Treated for Indirect Hyperbilirubinemia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate phototherapy irradiance in near-term infants with indirect hyperbilirubinemia and compare it with American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) intensive phototherapy thresholds.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a prospective observational study conducted at level III and level IV neonatal intensive care units within a single health system. Neonates born at ≥35 weeks' gestation with indirect hyperbilirubinemia requiring overhead phototherapy were enrolled, and irradiance was measured with a single calibrated light meter at the infant's trunk beneath the light source. Clinical and treatment data, including gestational age, birth weight, bilirubin concentrations, irradiance levels, number of phototherapy devices, phototherapy duration, and phototherapy-associated adverse effects, were collected.
RESULTS: Seventy infants were enrolled. The median gestational age was 38.0 weeks, and the median birth weight was 3135 g. The median irradiance was 60.8 μW/cm2/nm (IQR, 43.0-71.1; range, 19.1-106.0), approximately 2-fold the AAP minimum threshold for intensive phototherapy. Intensive irradiance (≥30 μW/cm2/nm) was achieved in 94.3% of infants. Hyperthermia occurred in 6 infants (8.6%), rash occurred in 4 infants (5.7%), and diarrhea occurred in 1 infant (1.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary neonatal intensive care unit practice, phototherapy irradiance is frequently and substantially above the AAP-recommended minimum thresholds, with a median dose approximately twice the guideline minimum. These findings highlight variability in phototherapy dosing and may inform quality improvement efforts to optimize irradiance delivery. Further studies should evaluate efficacy and long-term safety of high irradiance exposure.

articles.title: Upper Eyelid Lipofilling for Improving Ocular Comfort in Facial Palsy: A 12-Year Experience in 350 Patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The eyelid implantable weight is the most commonly used remedy for the correction of lagophthalmos. However, this approach has several limitations (migration, extrusion, poor esthetics, infection, astigmatism). It targets the restoration of eyelid closure, which is not the correct goal. The main goal should be to improve blinking, as it plays a crucial role in ocular surface protection and overall function. This objective can be achieved much more effectively through eyelid lipofilling. Lipofilling provides a more physiological restoration of blinking and enhances functional and esthetic outcomes compared with traditional eyelid weight implantation.
METHODS: Between 2012 and 2025, 432 upper eyelid lipofillings were performed in 350 patients, including 206 treated with the original technique and 144 with the modified technique. Of these, 318 patients had adequate follow-up and were included in the clinical outcome analysis.
RESULTS: All patients reported immediate improvement of corneal comfort. The need for artificial tears significantly decreased. The immediate improvements were partially reduced 2 months after surgery due to the initial resorption of the grafted fat, after which they remained stable. In 62 cases, a second lipofilling procedure was necessary. In 10 cases, a third lipofilling procedure was necessary.
CONCLUSIONS: Lipofilling of the upper eyelid sulcus has demonstrated a strong ability to reduce symptoms and improve corneal comfort in a large number of patients. The esthetic outcome is significantly superior compared with the application of a traditional eyelid weight.

articles.title: Association of the cerebroplacental ratio with small fetal size and adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia is frequently complicated by fetal growth compromise. The cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) shows promise for identifying fetuses at risk, but its diagnostic performance specifically in preeclamptic pregnancies remains unclear.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of 236 women with singleton preeclamptic pregnancies (January 2020-December 2023). Inclusion criteria: ISSHP-defined preeclampsia, gestational age 28-40 weeks at Doppler examination, and complete UA-PI and MCA-PI data within two weeks before delivery. The primary outcome was antenatal identification of small fetal size (estimated fetal weight <10th percentile). Multivariable logistic regression with prespecified covariates was used to assess independent associations. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis determined optimal cutoffs; bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples) corrected for optimism. DeLong test compared AUCs.
RESULTS: CPR demonstrated moderate-to-good diagnostic accuracy for small fetal size (AUC 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.92; optimism-corrected AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.79-0.91), higher than UA-PI (AUC 0.76, p = 0.018) and MCA-PI alone (AUC 0.75, p = 0.015). The exploratory optimal cutoff was 1.08 (sensitivity 66.0% [95% CI 55.8-75.2%], specificity 80.3%[95% CI 73.0-86.3%]). Abnormal CPR was independently associated with composite adverse outcomes (aOR 3.5, 95% CI 1.8-7.0, adjusting for baseline confounders; aOR 2.4, 95% CI 1.2-4.8, after additional adjustment for birth weight percentile and gestational age at delivery), including emergency cesarean for fetal distress (42.2% vs. 18.5%), 5-minute Apgar <7 (18.9% vs. 5.5%), and NICU admission (48.9% vs. 21.2%). CPR showed higher discrimination in early-onset versus late-onset preeclampsia (AUC 0.87 vs. 0.76), although this difference was attenuated after gestational-age adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In preeclamptic pregnancies, reduced CPR is independently associated with small fetal size and adverse perinatal outcomes, with numerically higher discrimination in early-onset disease, attenuated after gestational-age adjustment. These findings support CPR as a potential adjunctive tool for contemporaneous risk stratification in preeclampsia, particularly early-onset disease, pending prospective validation with serial measurements.

articles.title: Cross-protective immune responses to pneumococcal serotype 6A following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: India bears a pneumococcal disease burden, with serogroup 6 contributing to invasive pneumococcal disease, acute otitis media, and nasopharyngeal carriage. Serotype 6B is included in several pneumococcal conjugate vaccines, with evidence suggesting cross-protection against serotype 6A. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated serotype 6A-specific immune responses following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines. Databases were searched for studies reporting IgG geometric mean concentrations, proportions achieving IgG ≥ 0.35 µg/mL, and opsonophagocytic activity titers. Forty-three studies met inclusion criteria; eight contributed quantitative data. Overall, 6B-containing vaccines elicited measurable cross-reactive IgG and functional responses against serotype 6A. Booster-containing 3 + 1 schedules showed numerically higher responses than 3 + 0 schedules, with pooled IgG GMCs of 1.63 vs. 0.59 µg/mL, proportions achieving IgG ≥ 0.35 µg/mL of 92.78% vs. 65.38%, and OPA GMTs of 984.6 vs. 169.2, respectively. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251134118). These findings support 6B-mediated cross-reactive immunogenicity, particularly following booster dosing in vaccinated children.

articles.title: From Vein to Vaccine: Monocentric Analysis of Monocyte Apheresis and Dendritic Cell Vaccine Manufacturing Procedures in the Pediatric Setting.
articles.abstract: Focused use of dendritic cell (DC) vaccination strategies is under investigation to address the therapeutic gap that persists for difficult-to-treat malignancies. In vulnerable pediatric populations, DC immunotherapy can be added to standard-of-care treatments to strengthen anti-tumor immunity without increasing toxicity. Based on this rationale, our center initiated the ADDICT-pedGLIO clinical trial, investigating Wilms' tumor protein (WT1)-directed DC vaccination as supplementary treatment for pediatric diffuse midline gliomas and high-grade gliomas. Although monocyte apheresis and subsequent DC vaccine manufacturing have been reported to be feasible in pediatric populations, publicly available data describing the practical aspects of pediatric CD14+ monocyte apheresis and their implications for subsequent DC production remain limited. This limits the evidence base available to inform standardized, risk-stratified approaches to pediatric monocyte collection. Data were collected from 10 children with pediatric high-grade glioma or diffuse midline glioma in the ADDICT-pedGLIO trial and 22 adults who underwent apheresis and WT1 mRNA-electroporated DC vaccine production. Patient characteristics, apheresis parameters, yields, and DC phenotypes were compared between cohorts and correlated with CD14+ monocyte yield, DC viability, and adverse events. Blood volume, flow rate, processed blood volume, and baseline monocyte count correlated positively with CD14+ yield and collection efficiency, while repeated blood volume processing increased adverse events and reduced efficiency. When these findings are considered during pediatric CD14+ monocyte apheresis planning, larger total blood volumes may be processed to maximize yield and the number of therapeutic vaccines. We recommend a minimum peripheral monocyte count of 240/μL before apheresis, routine use of central venous catheters, and close electrolyte monitoring in children. Translating adult experience to the pediatric setting, this prospective monocentric clinical trial provides a reference framework for safe, successful monocyte apheresis and subsequent therapeutic DC vaccine production. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04911621.

articles.title: Apixaban reduces hepatic decompensation in patients with cirrhosis (ApiHep): A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evolving data suggest that anticoagulation is safe in cirrhosis and may improve decompensation-free survival in select patients. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of the direct oral anticoagulant apixaban in patients with cirrhosis.
METHODS: In this open-label randomized controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment, adult patients (18-60y) with cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B7-C10) without splenoportal axis thrombosis were randomized (1:1) to receive apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) along with standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone for 12 months. The primary outcome was the comparison of the proportion of patients with hepatic decompensation at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included frequency of liver-related events, overall and liver-related mortality, and adverse events (AEs).
RESULTS: One hundred thirty-four patients (mean age 43.4±9.5 y; Child-Pugh B/C:115/19) were randomized (67 Apixaban+SMT and 67 SMT). Patients receiving apixaban experienced significantly lower rates of hepatic decompensation compared with SMT (33.1% vs. 54.3%; absolute risk reduction 21.2% [95% CI: 4.5%-38.2%]; p=0.013). Although rates of ascites (6.4% vs. 17.4%), HE (21.2% vs. 36.0%), and variceal bleeding (7.5% vs. 14.6%) were lower among patients receiving Apixaban+SMT as compared with SMT alone, the differences were not statistically significant. No significant between-group differences in all-cause and liver-related mortality at 1 year were noted. There were no significant between-group differences in AEs (55.2% vs. 53.7%), any bleeding (41.8% vs. 46.3%), and major bleeding (9.0% vs. 11.9%) events.
CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban significantly reduced hepatic decompensation events without increasing hemorrhagic episodes in Child-Pugh B7-C10 cirrhosis (CTRI/2023/09/058018).

articles.title: Exploring RSV prevention among pregnant people and healthcare professionals in Aotearoa, New Zealand.
articles.abstract: In Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), RSV causes severe disease in infants, particularly Māori and Pacific infants, and is a high burden on the health system. Although an antenatal RSV vaccine and long-acting monoclonal antibodies are available internationally to prevent disease, they are not yet available in NZ. This study aims to explore the knowledge and perceptions of pregnant people and health care providers regarding RSV preventative options, and strategies for supporting a potential future immunization rollout in NZ. In this mixed-methods study, a cross-sectional survey of health care professionals (HCPs) across NZ and qualitative interviews with recently/pregnant Māori, Pacific, or ethnic minority migrants were conducted. A directed content analytic approach was used for analysis. Most HCPs (79.5%; 159/200) thought there was a high need for universal antenatal RSV vaccination, and 73.5% (147/200) ranked antenatal vaccination as their preferred prevention strategy over either targeted or universal infant monoclonal antibody. However, pharmacists comprised 63% of respondents. Interviewed caregivers (n = 13) would prefer to be offered whichever option had the longest duration of protection. If effectiveness and length of protection were similar, most preferred the antenatal vaccine so their infant was not injected to avoid discomfort or potential side effects their infant may experience. Recommendation from trusted HCPs, access to clear information from credible sources, and accessible and trusted administration settings are critical to supporting immunization acceptance. These insights can inform future implementation of a comprehensive rollout of an equitable preventative immunization program, reducing the risk of severe infant RSV disease.

articles.title: Long-Term Postpartum Dyspareunia and Sexual Dysfunction After Childbirth.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Postpartum sexual dysfunction is common, but long-term outcomes beyond the early puerperium remain insufficiently integrated into routine postpartum and gynecologic care.
OBJECTIVE: The objective was to systematically review dyspareunia and sexual dysfunction beyond 6 months postpartum, including associated factors and rehabilitation interventions.
STUDY DESIGN: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and CENTRAL from inception to January 31, 2026. Eligible primary studies included postpartum women with at least 1 relevant sexual outcome assessed at or beyond 6 months after childbirth. Prevalence and associated-factor findings were synthesized descriptively. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to randomized rehabilitation trials reporting validated sexual-function outcomes at eligible postpartum time points with extractable numerical data.
RESULTS: Twenty-two eligible reports representing 21 unique studies or cohorts were included; 2 randomized rehabilitation studies contributed to quantitative synthesis. Dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remained clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum, with incomplete recovery persisting in a substantial subset of women. Persistent morbidity was most consistently associated with severe perineal trauma, including obstetric anal sphincter injury; associations with operative delivery were less consistent. Breastfeeding-related symptoms, depressive symptoms, pelvic floor morbidity, and genital or body image concerns were also reported. The pooled rehabilitation estimate favored intervention but was imprecise and highly heterogeneous (standardized mean difference: 1.19; 95% CI, -0.18 to 2.57; I²=91.7%), with very-low-certainty evidence.
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remain clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum and warrant proactive assessment within routine postpartum and gynecologic follow-up, with multidisciplinary management and referral for pelvic floor rehabilitation or urogynecologic evaluation when indicated.

articles.title: Association between continuum of care in maternal health services and neonatal mortality in 23 sub-Saharan African countries: the moderating role of government health expenditure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal mortality remains high in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Continuum of care (CoC) throughout antenatal (ANC), childbirth, and postnatal care can improve survival, yet completion in SSA remains low. Variation in government health expenditure (GHE) may influence neonatal outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: We examined the association between CoC completion and neonatal mortality and assessed whether this association differed by GHE level in SSA.
METHODS: We analysed Demographic and Health Surveys (2016-2022) from 23 SSA countries among neonates born to women aged 15-49 years with a recent live birth. We used multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression models to assess CoC completion and neonatal mortality associations, including interaction terms between CoC completion and GHE level, followed by stratified analyses by GHE level. Results are reported as adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Among 87,947 neonates, neonatal mortality was 22.5 per 1,000 live births. CoC completion declined across stages: 56.4% (95% CI: 55.6-57.2) for ANC, 45.8% (95% CI: 44.9-46.7) for ANC plus childbirth stage, and 37.4% (95% CI: 36.6-38.2) for full CoC. Completion of ANC, ANC plus childbirth stage, and full CoC was associated with lower odds of neonatal mortality, with AORs of 0.77 (95% CI: 0.69-0.87), 0.75 (95% CI: 0.66-0.86) and 0.61 (95% CI: 0.53-0.70), respectively. In high-GHE countries, AORs were 0.67 (95% CI: 0.56-0.79), 0.59 (95% CI: 0.49-0.70), and 0.53 (95% CI: 0.44-0.64) across CoC stages, respectively, whereas no significant associations were observed in low-GHE countries.
CONCLUSION: Strengthening CoC and health-system resources may support neonatal survival, particularly in high-GHE countries.

articles.title: All About the Meds: Contraception, Infertility, and Immunosuppression in Reproductive-aged Female Transplant Recipients.
articles.abstract: The number of reproductive-aged solid organ transplant recipients continues to rise, underscoring the need for comprehensive reproductive health counseling that spans throughout the transplant continuum. Fertility is often impaired in end-stage organ disease but often resumes within months after transplantation, which may cause unintended pregnancy during a period of heightened maternal, fetal, and allograft vulnerability. This review synthesizes the evidence and expert consensus from the American Society of Transplantation Women's Health Community of Practice Controversies Conference on contraception, infertility, and immunosuppression in reproductive-aged female transplant recipients. Recommendations are largely US-based, although reference to international variability is noted, where relevant. We outline contraceptive options with attention to efficacy and safety in transplant recipients. Data on infertility and assisted reproductive technologies in solid organ transplant recipients remain limited, although emerging evidence supports the feasibility and safety of ovulation induction, in vitro fertilization, and single-embryo transfer with careful monitoring for complications such as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Immunosuppressive regimens require individualized adjustment before, during, and after pregnancy: calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids, and azathioprine are generally considered safe, whereas mycophenolate is strictly contraindicated due to teratogenicity; the safety of mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors and belatacept remains incompletely defined. Lactation is supported with most immunosuppressants, although caution is warranted with mycophenolate and mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors. Ultimately, preconception counseling, shared decision-making, and coordination amongst transplant, maternal-fetal medicine, and reproductive endocrinology specialists are essential to optimize outcomes for recipients, grafts, and infants. Closing persistent knowledge gaps and enhancing access to reproductive care should remain a research and policy priority in transplant medicine.

articles.title: Treatment outcomes and safety of oral β-blockers and sirolimus in children with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe outcomes and safety of oral β-blockers and sirolimus in children with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children with KHE receiving oral β-blockers or sirolimus at Beijing Children's Hospital from January 2016 to April 2026. Lesion regression at fixed time points, treatment duration, treatment discontinuation, recurrence, and safety were assessed.
RESULTS: Thirteen patients received β-blockers and 11 sirolimus, including three with prior therapy. Baseline lesion measurements did not differ significantly, but the β-blocker group was younger [median 4.0 (IQR, 3.0-4.0) vs. 19.0 (10.5-29.5) months; p < 0.001] and had lower frequencies of pain (23.1% vs. 72.7%; p = 0.038) and hyperhidrosis (0% vs. 54.5%; p = 0.003). Cumulative lesion-regression thresholds did not differ significantly through 9 months. At 9 months, >25%, >50%, and >75% regression occurred in 76.9%, 46.2%, and 23.1% with β-blockers versus 100.0%, 72.7%, and 18.2% with sirolimus, respectively. Treatment was discontinued in 9/13 and 3/11 patients (median durations, 40.0 and 18.0 months, respectively). No recurrence was observed after cessation. Safety events were reversible and manageable.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, both treatments were associated with improvement, but baseline imbalances limit direct comparison. β-blocker responses in predominantly younger, less symptomatic patients require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Dosing Evaluation for Sedation in Neonates Undergoing Therapeutic Hypothermia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recently, dexmedetomidine has replaced opioids for sedation in neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). The study objectives were to describe dosing patterns, evaluate compliance, and compare effectiveness and safety between the original (pre-implementation) and revised (post-implementation) in-house dexmedetomidine dosing guidelines.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study that included neonates with HIE admitted to a level IV NICU for therapeutic hypothermia comparing two dexmedetomidine dosing regimens: (1) pre-implementation: starting dose of 0.05 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.05 μg/kg/h every 6 h as needed, and (2) post-implementation: 0.2 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.1 μg/kg/h every 30-60 min as needed.
RESULTS: A total of 106 neonates were included: 50 in the pre-implementation group and 56 in the post-implementation group. Compliance to post-implementation formulary recommendations was 69.6% for initial doses, 62.5% for dose increases, and 44.6% for dose decreases. An increased odds of opioid exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 7.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.59-51.5, p = 0.02) and greater proportion of bradycardia (21.4% vs. 4%, p = 0.03) were observed in the post-implementation group. No significant differences in effectiveness end points or hypotension were observed between groups (p ≥ 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Compliance with formulary-recommended dexmedetomidine dosing was variable and dose decreases were common in the post-implementation group. The post-implementation dosing approach was not associated with improved effectiveness outcomes (sedation) but was associated with greater opioid exposure and more bradycardia, supporting the need for further prospective evaluation to determine the optimal dexmedetomidine dosing in neonates undergoing HIE.

articles.title: Levels of Psychological Detachment in Nurses: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Psychological detachment among nurses, a critical component of professional recovery, plays a vital role in stabilizing the nursing workforce and expanding clinical human resources. This review aims to assess the level of psychological detachment among nurses and evaluate the impact of data collection periods (during and outside the COVID-19 pandemic), gender, and department. Computerized searches were conducted across 10 databases: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Medline, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed. The search period spanned from the inception of each database to January 7, 2026. A random-effects model was used to pool the total mean scores for psychological detachment, and subgroup analyses were conducted to explore sources of heterogeneity among studies. A total of 34 studies involving 20 517 nursing staff from six countries were included in the meta-analysis. Results showed that the overall mean score for nurses' psychological detachment was 2.68 (95% CI: 2.53, 2.82), indicating a low-to-moderate level. Subgroup analyses revealed relatively higher total mean psychological detachment scores among male nurses and during the COVID-19 pandemic, while paediatric nurses exhibited lower levels compared to other departments. Future efforts should prioritize the development of targeted clinical management systems to systematically enhance psychological detachment levels across diverse nursing populations. Trial Registration: This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261304558).

articles.title: Building Systems Capacity in Paediatric Nutrition: A Descriptive Case Study of a Statewide Network and Feeding Team Model for Children and Youth With Special Health Care Needs.
articles.abstract: The Washington State Nutrition Network, a long-standing collaboration between the Washington State Department of Health (DOH), and the University of Washington's Institute on Human Development and Disability (IHDD), focuses on children and youth with special health care needs (CYSHCN). Established in 1987 following a survey administered by the CYSHCN programme and disseminated to neuromuscular centres as part of a statewide Title V Maternal and Child Health (MCH) needs assessment in 1985, the programme is designed to strengthen the capacity of Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDNs) to meet the complex nutrition and feeding challenges of CYSHCN. The Network demonstrates how a systems-based practice can address statewide access to care for complex paediatric feeding and nutrition by applying systems thinking methodologies, such as leveraging cross-sector relationships, building and distributing workforce capacity, strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration and promoting equitable access, all by continuously evaluating and adjusting the Network's activities. This descriptive case study describes the Nutrition Network's evolution over four decades and by highlighting its impact on workforce capacity, interdisciplinary collaboration and equitable access to care for CYSHCN. Key elements of this established model may serve as a foundation to inform replication of a systems-based approach to improve access and care coordination for children and youth with chronic and complex nutrition and feeding needs nationwide.

articles.title: Oropouche Fever Outbreak, Havana, Cuba, June-September 2024.
articles.abstract: Oropouche fever emerged nationwide in Cuba in 2024. We investigated the outbreak in Havana; of 549 suspected cases, 189 (34.4%) were confirmed. No cases were severe. Incidence was 8.9/100,000 population and was highest in adults 27-59 years of age (10.2/100,000 population). Three infants tested positive. Dengue cocirculation challenged surveillance.

articles.title: Monkeypox Virus Seroprevalence among Adults Assessed at Roadside Wellness Centers along Major Transportation Corridor, Kenya, 2025.
articles.abstract: Since 2024, Kenya has confirmed >1,000 cases of monkeypox virus (MPXV) infection. We conducted a cross-sectional serosurvey at 8 clinics along a transportation corridor in Kenya to quantify unrecognized MPXV transmission. From September 29-October 28, 2025, adults >18 years completed a questionnaire and provided blood samples tested with a serologic assay that distinguishes likely MPXV infection from orthopoxvirus vaccination. We used a modified Poisson regression to assess associations with likely MPXV infection. We compared participants with serologic evidence of MPXV infection to those self-reporting prior confirmed mpox cases. Of 2,896 participants, 332 (11.5%) were seropositive, including 82 (2.8%) classified as likely MPXV infection. Four participants reported prior confirmed MPXV cases, yielding a 21:1 ratio of participants with serologic evidence of MPXV infection to self-reported confirmed cases. Despite some evidence of undetected transmission, most participants lacked serologic evidence of prior orthopoxvirus exposure, indicating a large susceptible population and supporting additional vaccination and ongoing serosurveillance.

articles.title: Association of adverse perinatal outcomes of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy with maternal serum bile acid profiles.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is associated with increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, yet current monitoring lacks predictive accuracy. This study aimed to explore alterations in serum bile acid profiles and their relationship with adverse perinatal outcomes in ICP.
METHODS: This study enrolled 149 pregnant women, including 77 normal pregnant women and 72 cases with ICP, subdivided into ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes and those without according to the perinatal outcomes. Serum concentrations of 15 bile acids were quantified using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry and compared among the three groups.
RESULTS: ICP patients exhibited significantly lower gestational age at delivery, Apgar scores, and birth weight, alongside higher rates of cesarean delivery, low birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit admission, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and preterm birth (all p < 0.05). Twelve bile acids were significantly elevated in ICP (all p < 0.01); notably, taurolithocholic acid elevation was exclusive to the ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes. Glycocholic acid (GCA), glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA), taurocholic acid (TCA), taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA), tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA), and total bile acid levels positively correlated with adverse perinatal outcomes (all p < 0.05). The combined indicator of these six indicators demonstrated superior predictive efficacy for adverse perinatal outcomes with an area under the curve of 0.836, sensitivity of 73.0%, and specificity of 82.9%.
CONCLUSIONS: Distinct serum bile acid metabolic signatures characterize ICP patients with adverse perinatal outcomes. Elevated levels of total bile acids and conjugated bile acids, including GCA, GCDCA, TCA, TCDCA, and TUDCA, were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes and might serve as candidate biomarkers for risk prediction. The multi-bile acid combined indicator demonstrated superior exploratory predictive performance over individual markers, offering a potential tool for identifying high-risk ICP patients, which requires prospective external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Management of Infants Born to Mothers with Q Fever During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: We conducted a systematic review of published literature from 1953-2021 for cases of infants born to mothers who had Q fever during pregnancy. We describe clinical management characteristics and neonatal outcomes for 11 case reports. No live-born infant had confirmed C. burnetii infection. Placental infection was identified in 4 cases; all infants tested negative. Uncommon adverse obstetric outcomes included preterm birth and low birthweight. There were no cases of transmission through breastmilk. Infection-control precautions ranged from standard to airborne. Evidence indicated that vertical transmission to the fetus or live-born infant is rare. Maternal illness and fetal loss appear related to placental infection. Separation of mother and infant or avoidance of breastfeeding are not supported. Management should prioritize placental handling precautions and structured infant follow-up. No published clinical consensus guidelines exist for management of infants born to mothers with Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) during pregnancy. Global collaboration and evidence gathering can inform evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: A neonatal prediction model for lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheters depth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a robust and generalizable prediction model for PICC depth in neonates undergoing lower-extremity catheterization, with the aim of improving the first-attempt success rate of catheter tip positioning and reducing PICC-related complications.
METHODS: A total of 240 neonates who successfully underwent lower-extremity PICC placement in the neonatal intensive care unit of a maternal and child health hospital were enrolled as study subjects. Variable selection was performed using stepwise regression based on the Akaike information criterion, followed by development of a multiple linear regression model. Internal validation was performed using the random split sample method (8:2). Model performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, coefficient of determination (R2), and Pearson's correlation coefficient.
RESULTS: The final model included two simple and objective variables: body weight on the day of catheterization and puncture site. The prediction equation was established as follows: insertion depth (cm) = 17.3 + body weight at catheterization (kg) × 2.3 - adjustment value for the puncture site (2.7 for small saphenous vein, 4.5 for popliteal vein, 5.1 for popliteal great saphenous vein, and 10.3 for femoral vein, respectively; reference: ankle great saphenous vein). Internal validation showed that the model achieved an R2 of 0.8789, RMSE of 1.0754, MAE of 0.8157, and Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.9375 between the predicted and observed values. Residual diagnostics indicated good predictive accuracy and stability.
CONCLUSIONS: The prediction model for neonatal lower extremity PICC insertion depth based on body weight at the catheterization and puncture sites demonstrated good fit and reliable predictive performance. It can assist in individualizing and precisely determining the catheter insertion depth in clinical practice, thereby reducing repeated adjustments and complications.

articles.title: Changing characteristics, treatment patterns, and risk among children and young people with a first recorded common mental disorder symptom or diagnosis in primary care in England (2001-23): a retrospective, population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Presentations to primary care by children and young people (CYP) for common mental disorders (anxiety and depression) have risen steeply in the past two decades. In this study, we aimed to describe changes in the case mix of CYP with an incident record of a common mental disorder, treatment patterns after the incident record, and whether these trends were accompanied by secular changes in the demographics of those presenting, their treatment patterns, and whether the clinical risk profile of those presenting changed between 2001 and 2023 in England.
METHODS: In this retrospective, population-based cohort study, we used anonymised primary care health records data from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum (2001-23). We identified children and adolescents (aged 10-18 years) registered with English general practices with linked hospital admission and mortality records. We estimated trends in incidence of common mental disorders (using both symptom and diagnosis codes) in primary care and, among CYP with an incident record of a common mental disorder, changes in demographic and comorbidity profiles, referrals to Child And Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), and antidepressant prescribing. We compared CYP with incident common mental disorders to matched controls on hospital admission for self-harm, alcohol misuse, and drug misuse, and tested for change in these associations using common mental disorder-by-calendar-year interactions. People with lived experience were not involved in the design or conduct of this study.
FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2001, and Dec 31, 2023, 6 220 923 CYP were registered with CPRD-Aurum practices. 379 802 CYP had a first recorded common mental disorder symptom or diagnosis. 250 315 (65·9%) of 379 802 CYP were girls and 129 353 (34·1%) were boys, with a mean age of 15·2 years (range 10-18; SD 2·1), 304 544 (80·2%) were White, and 35 082 (19·2%) were from minoritised ethnic groups. From 2001, the incidence of common mental disorders increased by four times from 57 per 10 000 person-years to 240 in 2019, followed by a decrease to 163 in 2023. The age of CYP with an incident record of a common mental disorder became younger (mean age 15·5 years [SD 2·1] to 15·0 [SD 2·1]), the proportion of White CYP became increasingly overrepresented relative to the general population, and the prevalence of psychiatric or neurodevelopmental comorbidities almost tripled (5·1% in 2001, 13·8% in 2023). After an incident common mental disorder, CAMHS referrals increased from 6·8 to 17·8 per 100 person-years (rate ratio [RR] 2·64 [95% CI 2·48 to 2·79]); antidepressant prescribing halved (38·8 to 17·9 per 100 person-years; RR 0·46 [0·45-0·48]), while prescriptions per treated CYP increased from 4·1 to 6·2 (RR 1·50, 1·48- 1·52). Between 2001 and 2019, the association between common mental disorders and adverse outcomes in the 2 years after the index date remained broadly stable over time (ratio of hazard ratios [HRs] per calendar year 1·01 [95% CI 1·00-1·02] for hospital admission for self-harm; 1·00 [0·99-1·01] for alcohol misuse; 1·01 [0·99-1·02] for drug misuse).
INTERPRETATION: The increase in recorded common mental disorders among CYP was not accompanied by declining clinical risk as would be expected if young people were increasingly being recorded at lower levels of severity, whether through readier presentation to primary care, greater clinical recognition, or more liberal recording. These findings highlight the need for greater consistency, better recording of psychometric measures, and transparency in care pathways.
FUNDING: NIHR, Wellcome Trust, Place2Be.

articles.title: The importance of RSV vaccination for at-risk adults aged 18-59: An expert opinion with an Italian perspective.
articles.abstract: This expert opinion reviews the burden of RSV in at-risk adults aged 18-59 years and summarizes available evidence to provide expert considerations that may inform prevention strategies. Adults with comorbidities or immunocompromise frequently experience severe RSV infection, with annual and seasonal rates of 37.6 per 1000 persons/year and 28.4 per 1000 persons/season, respectively. Clinical presentation ranges from being asymptomatic through to acute respiratory distress, with 6.5-32.8% at-risk adults requiring hospitalization for RSV disease. Three preventative vaccines (RSVpreF, mRNA-1345, RSVPreF3) are currently approved in Europe for adults ≥18 years and in the United States for adults ≥60 years and 18-59 years at increased risk. The panel supports RSV vaccination in adults 18-59 years with severe forms of immunocompromise, respiratory disease, cardiovascular disease, neurological/neuromuscular disease, or renal disease. Higher vaccination rates in this population can be achieved by enhancing awareness, empowering health-care professionals, developing consistent policies, and improving access.

articles.title: Gitelman syndrome complicated by pregnancy: clinical management and maternal-fetal outcomes - a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gitelman syndrome (GS), an autosomal recessive tubulopathy caused by SLC12A3 mutations, presents with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypocalciuria and hypomagnesemia. Pregnancy can exacerbate these imbalances, increasing maternal-fetal risks, yet standardized management remains lacking. This review summarizes complications, management strategies, and outcomes to guide evidence-based care.
METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CNKI were searched from inception to December 31, 2025, using 'Gitelman Syndrome' AND ('pregnancy' OR 'gestation'). Two reviewers independently performed literature screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. Core data were analyzed descriptively, categorical variables as frequencies (%), continuous as mean ± SD or median (range).
RESULTS: Fifty-six studies (96 pregnancies, 81 women) from 19 countries were included. Among pregnancies with available outcome data, reported maternal complications included gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (11.5%), oligohydramnios (9.4%), and preeclampsia/hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets (HELLP) syndrome (3.1%); fetal/neonatal complications included preterm birth (16.7%), growth restriction (5.2%), and death (4.2%). Preconception diagnosis showed lower GDM (6.3% vs 18.4%) and fetal/neonatal death (0% vs 8.2%); these comparisons were descriptive and exploratory only. Oral potassium and magnesium were the main treatments. Potassium-sparing diuretics were used in 16 pregnancies (18 exposures); no malformations were reported, but safety is unestablished. Vaginal delivery occurred in 51.2% and Cesarean in 48.8%.
CONCLUSIONS: Preconception counseling and multidisciplinary care with close electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation may benefit GS-complicated pregnancies, but evidence is limited by case-report data, publication bias, and heterogeneity. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed to clarify risk factors and guide clinical management.

articles.title: Exploring the behavioural and social drivers of routine childhood immunisation in rural Vanuatu: qualitative community insights.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine childhood immunisation coverage in Vanuatu remains suboptimal, with substantial regional disparities. While supply-side constraints are well recognised barriers to vaccine uptake in the Pacific, other contributing factors remain less understood.
OBJECTIVE(S): This study sought to explore the behavioural and social drivers of routine childhood immunisation in rural Vanuatu, generating critical evidence to inform future immunisation programming.
METHODS: We conducted an exploratory qualitative study using the World Health Organisation's Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with participants from two rural villages in Tafea Province, between May and June 2024. Participants included caregivers, community influencers, healthcare workers, and immunisation program managers. Data were analysed using framework analysis, guided by the BeSD domains. Fourteen participants completed interviews.
RESULTS: Caregivers indicated strong support for routine immunisation and motivation to vaccinate; however, vaccination efforts were shaped by multiple social and behavioural factors. Community-specific beliefs, gender dynamics, and the influence of community and religious leaders affected decision-making and prioritisation, while social networks were a source of both support and misinformation. Trusted relationships with healthcare workers and the quality of communication further influenced caregiver experiences. These factors converged with practical access barriers to create complex constraints on immunisation uptake.
CONCLUSIONS: Improving routine immunisation uptake in rural Vanuatu will require coordinated, multi-level efforts that simultaneously address health system constraints and the social and behavioural dynamics shaping vaccination. Priority strategies include strengthening outreach reliability, improving healthcare worker communication, and engaging community leaders, male caregivers, and social networks to support informed vaccination decisions.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics and Initial Bolus Dosing of Furosemide in Children on ECMO.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is an established technology that provides life-saving mechanical support for critically ill children. In these children, fluid overload is commonly treated with furosemide; however, optimal dosing of furosemide is unknown in children supported with ECMO because ECMO may alter furosemide exposure. In this work, human blood-primed ex vivo experiments quantified red blood cell partitioning and extraction of furosemide by the ECMO circuit. Furosemide partitioned into red blood cells but was not extracted by ECMO circuits. These data then parameterized a pediatric physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of furosemide in children with and without ECMO. Next, plasma furosemide concentrations from 10 critically ill children supported by ECMO were used to evaluate PBPK model performance, with the optimized model achieving average fold error and absolute average fold error of 1.02 and 1.67, respectively. The optimized PBPK model also predicted that ECMO increases apparent volume of distribution by a median of > 30% in neonates and infants. Finally, population PBPK simulations with the optimized PBPK model provided initial bolus doses that most rapidly achieve steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations with and without ECMO. These calibrated initial bolus doses achieved steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations > 3 h faster than continuous infusions without an initial bolus dose, and this improvement was most pronounced in neonates and infants on ECMO. Overall, this work supports comparatively larger initial bolus doses for neonates and infants on ECMO, and provides calibrated initial bolus doses based on plasma exposure for critically ill children.

articles.title: Sexual, Pharmaceutical, and Lifestyle Variables in a Cohort of Pregnant Western Australian Women, and Their Association With Detection of Vaginal Microorganisms and Preterm Birth.
articles.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.abstract:
