BACKGROUND: The vaginal microbiome is shaped by factors such as sexual behaviour, smoking, and feminine hygiene practices. Although these associations are well documented in non-pregnant women, less is known in pregnancy, particularly in Australia, despite links between the vaginal microbiome and complications like preterm birth (PTB).
AIM: To document sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle variables in pregnant Australian women and examine their associations with vaginal microorganisms and, secondarily, PTB risk.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Mid-pregnancy (12-23 weeks' gestation) vaginal swabs from 936 women in the Predict1000 study were analysed for key microorganisms using qPCR. Participants completed a recruitment survey on medication use, urinary/vaginal infections, smoking, alcohol use, sexual practices, and vaginal douching. Associations between these factors, PTB (spontaneous and indicated), and specific microorganisms were assessed using Chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Mann-Whitney tests.
RESULTS: Thirteen percent of women reported smoking during pregnancy. Over half reported vaginal intercourse 1-2 times per week, although one quarter reported none. Thirty-two percent engaged in other sexual activities, most commonly oral sex (25%), followed by use of sex toys (11%). Vaginal douching was uncommon (3%). Sexual behaviour and douching were not associated with PTB risk. Smoking was associated with increased rates of non-optimal microbes, an association that persisted after correction for multiple comparisons. Associations between reduced frequency of vaginal intercourse (< 2 times/week) and lower prevalence of non-optimal vaginal microbes, and between douching and higher detection of Gardnerella vaginalis and Ureaplasma parvum, were also observed but did not remain significant after correction.
CONCLUSION: Sexual, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle factors influenced the vaginal microbiota in pregnancy, but none were associated with PTB risk.

articles.title: Pain Pathophysiology and Assessment in Pediatric Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Pain is pervasive and affects upwards of 59% of critically ill children. Consequences of severe pain include worsened health related quality of life and longer lengths of stay. Evaluating pain in non-verbal critically ill children is a unique challenge due to difficulties with communication and the wide variety of developmental stages. The purpose of our review is to examine the underlying pathophysiology of pain, the current landscape in pain assessment of non-verbal critically ill children and pain assessment tools for non-verbal critically ill children. We performed literature searches from April 25, 2023 to November 20, 2025; we performed literature searches using PubMed and EMBASE with a combination of keywords that included "pain", "pathophysiology", "pediatric", "comfort-behavioral", "FLACC", "P-CPOT", "ventilated", "PICU". The pathophysiology of pain starts with inflammatory reactions at the site of injury, which are transmitted via the dorsal horn to the ascending spinothalamic tract and converge onto the brain using two separate pathways. There are three behavioral pain scales that have been validated in both ventilated and non-ventilated critically ill children: the faces, legs, activity, crying, and consolability scale; the COMFORT-Behavior scale; and the pediatric critical care pain observation tool. While pain assessments are regularly performed in PICUs worldwide, there still exist sites in which validated scales are not used, or no scales are used to evaluate pain. Pain is frequent among critically ill children, and its prompt identification can be challenging. Understanding the pathophysiology of pain and the barriers that clinicians face in identifying pain, particularly in non-verbal critically ill children, will improve the care of these patients.

articles.title: No impact of gluten-free diet on glycemia, growth, or quality of life in asymptomatic celiac disease with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Evidence is limited on longitudinal health outcomes with a gluten-free diet (GFD) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and asymptomatic celiac disease (CD) identified by screening.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of the GFD on glycemic management, anthropometrics, gastrointestinal symptoms, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and nutritional intakes in patients with T1D and screen-detected CD.
METHODS: Celiac Disease and Diabetes Longitudinal Follow-up and Evaluation Study (CD-LiFE) was a prospective follow-up study (NCT03122093) whereby 62 participants aged 8-45 years (77% adult, 23% pediatric) with T1D and screen-detected CD were evaluated annually over a 2-year study period.
RESULTS: 51.6% of participants were GFD-adherent (daily gluten intake < 10 mg) at study baseline. After 2 years, rates of GFD adherence increased (72.7%) with only 15.2% transitioning to a gluten-containing diet (GCD). No differences were seen in mean HbA1c levels between individuals on a GFD and GCD (Δ = 0.1%; 95% CI: -0.6 to 0.4; P = .613, weight (Δ = 0.2 kg/m2; 95% CI: -2.3 to 2.8; P = .848) or BMI among adults (Δ = -1.1 kg/m2; 95% CI: -0.4 to 0.6; P = .149) nor BMI Z scores among pediatric participants (Δ = 0.91; 95% CI: -0.34 to 2.16; P = .136), number of acute GI symptoms (IRR = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.6 to 1.5; P = .810) nor longitudinal differences in HRQoL with respect to generic (Δ = -0.4; 95% CI: -4.0 to 3.3; P = .840) nor diabetes-specific HRQoL (Δ = 1.5; 95% CI: -2.9 to 5.9; P = .505).
CONCLUSION: This 2-year follow-up study demonstrates adherence to a GFD does not impact glycemic control, anthropometrics, GI symptom development, or HRQoL in adult and pediatric patients with T1D and screen-detected CD.

articles.title: Apolipoprotein ε4-allele as predictor of outcome in radiotherapy-treated childhood brain tumor survivors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) is a polymorphic gene with three main alleles; the ε4-allele is a risk factor for distinct diseases, particularly for Alzheimer's disease. Radiotherapy-treated childhood brain tumor (BT) survivors face an increased risk of developing late-effects, especially cognitive impairment. Despite the similar treatment modality, the outcome varies considerably. Thus, we investigated the influence of ε4-allele on outcome in these survivors.
METHODS: A Finnish national cohort of radiotherapy-treated childhood BT survivors was investigated in a cross-sectional setting (median follow-up of 20 years). Survivors participated in the follow-up visit including neuropsychological and physical examinations, brain magnetic resonance imaging, and laboratory tests. BT and treatment-related information were collected from the patient files. APOE polymorphism was examined, and the results were compared to a previous study on the Finnish population. We also compared the late-effects between ε4-carriers and non-carriers.
RESULTS: Among 58 survivors [median age of 27 (range, 16-43) years], the observed frequencies of APOE genotypes were 78% (N = 45) for ε3ε3, 14% (N = 8) for ε3ε4, 7% (N = 4) for ε2ε3, and 2% (N = 1) for ε2ε4. The presence of ε4-allele was associated with poorer semantic, immediate, and delayed auditory memory. Since all ε4-carriers had ventriculoperitoneal shunt, we compared their results to those of non-carriers with ventriculoperitoneal shunt, which revealed that ε4-carriers had worse immediate and delayed auditory memory. E4-carriers exhibit higher total cholesterol and triglyceride levels than non-carriers.
CONCLUSIONS: APOE ε4-allele may impact the cognitive outcome and cholesterol levels in the radiotherapy-treated childhood BT survivors. E4-carrier survivors may especially benefit from healthy life-style interventions.

articles.title: Return to sports after pediatric brain tumors: Time to move beyond survival.
articles.abstract: Brain tumors are the second most common malignancy in children and adolescents and the leading cause of cancer-related death in this population. While survival rates have improved, survivors are at risk of neurocognitive, motor, and psychosocial sequelae due to both tumor location and treatments used. Participation in sport is increasingly recognized as beneficial for functional recovery, cardiorespiratory fitness, and overall well-being in children and adolescents treated for brain tumors. However, return to play (RTP) may pose some challenges, particularly in the presence of neurosurgical devices, cranial radiotherapy, or residual neurological deficits. This narrative clinical review summarizes current evidence on the risks of sport-related injuries in pediatric brain tumor patients and survivors, highlighting factors influencing vulnerability, including treatment history and specific sport characteristics. We propose a risk-based framework for RTP evaluation emphasizing individualized coordinated assessment by pediatric oncologists, neurosurgeons, and sports medicine specialists. Protective strategies are discussed, although evidence for concussion prevention remains limited. A safe RTP should be enhanced by the here-proposed structured evaluation, balancing safety with the physical, cognitive, and psychosocial benefits of active participation. This framework aims to support clinicians and families in facilitating safe and effective reintegration of pediatric brain tumor survivors into both recreational and competitive sports.

articles.title: Fifteen years of pediatric neuro-oncology trials: Insights from ClinicalTrials.gov to optimize future design.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in children. Despite therapeutic advances, outcomes remain poor, and trial conduct is challenged by disease rarity, limited accrual pools, and complex multimodal regimens. Premature trial termination compounds these challenges, wasting resources and delaying progress. A comprehensive evaluation of the US pediatric neuro-oncology trial landscape and determinants of early discontinuation has not been performed.
METHODS: We queried ClinicalTrials.gov for US-based interventional pediatric neuro-oncology trials initiated between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2024. Trials were categorized by design features, tumor type, sponsor, and consortium involvement. Temporal trends, trial duration, and reasons for discontinuation were analyzed. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed factors associated with trial completion among trials initiated between 2010 and 2019.
RESULTS: Of 819 identified trials, 243 met inclusion criteria. Most trials were early phase (phase 1/1-2, 69.5%) and focused on recurrent/progressive disease (68.3%), with targeted therapy (53.9%) and immunotherapy (26.3%) most common. Trial opening declined significantly over time (Poisson regression, P < .001), although the proportion of closed trials remained stable (χ² P = .97). Mean time to accrual was 4.8 ± 1.2 years, with modest improvement after 2018. Among 52 (21.4%) prematurely closed trials, poor accrual was the leading reason (50%), followed by funding issues (19.2%). Multivariable analysis identified greater site numbers decreasing the risk of premature discontinuation (hazard ratio = 0.55; 95% CI, 0.35-0.83).
CONCLUSIONS: Multisite reach is a key determinant of trial persistence. Strategies to optimize accrual and reduce early termination should prioritize interinstitutional networks and trial platform site networks.

articles.title: Clinical and molecular divergences in diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered: A comparative study of survival outcomes in 1498 adults and children.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered (DMG), is a highly lethal brain tumor that predominantly affects children but is increasingly diagnosed in adults. This study aims to compare the clinical features, molecular profiles, and survival outcomes between these groups.
METHODS: PubMed and EMBASE searches (June 2021) identified 82 studies with 1498 patients (34.7% adults). Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves where necessary. Cox regression analyses were used to compare the overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) between adults and children, with subgroup analyses for age effects on OS.
RESULTS: Adults demonstrated longer median OS than children (16.2 vs 11.4 months, P < .05) and longer PFS (9.17 vs 7.2 months, P < .05). Brainstem involvement was significantly less common in adults than in children (22.6% vs 78.7%). Among patients with brainstem tumors, adults had longer OS, whereas survival was similar between age groups in non-brainstem tumors. Molecular data were limited, available in only 14.2%-37.1% of cases. Adults had higher rates of PPM1D (37.0% vs 12.6%), FGFR1 (17.1% vs 5.6%), and NF1 (35.1% vs 12.3%) mutations and lower rates of ACVR1 mutations (5.0% vs 24.1%). FGFR1, NF1, and TP53 mutations were prognostic in both age groups.
CONCLUSION: Adults with DMG have longer OS compared to children, with the survival advantage confined to brainstem tumors and not observed in non-brainstem tumors. Whether this reflects intrinsic biological differences or tumor location remains uncertain. Prospective studies with comprehensive molecular profiling are needed to better define differences in DMG biology across the age groups.

articles.title: Divided oral versus single-dose intravenous etoposide for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with comorbidity: lower early hematologic toxicity with preserved 2-week response.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Etoposide is a backbone of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) treatment. But most adults suffering from HLH have comorbidity that limits the use of intravenous etoposide.
OBJECTIVE: We conducted a retrospective study to compare the efficacy and safety of divided oral versus single-dose intravenous etoposide within the DEP regimen (liposomal doxorubicin, etoposide, methylprednisolone) in HLH.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of 57 patients (28 oral, 29 intravenous), including 13 patients under 18 years (six oral, seven intravenous). Week-2 overall response was the efficacy endpoint. The safety endpoint was any grade III-IV hematologic event at the worst grade recorded within 14 days after treatment.
RESULTS: Patients with comorbidity were enrolled in both groups: 24/28 (85.7%) in the oral and 20/29 (69.0%) in the IV group. Week-2 overall response was 96.4% vs 89.7%, respectively. Grade III-IV hematologic events occurred in 5/28 (17.9%) oral and 16/29 (55.2%) IV group (p = 0.006). This association persisted after adjustment for lymphoma-associated HLH, age, performance status, comorbidity, LDH, AST, platelet and creatinine (odds ratios 0.13 to 0.19; all p ≤ 0.008). In the 44 patients with comorbidity, grade III-IV hematologic events were far less frequent (16.7% vs 65.0%; odds ratio 0.11; 95% confidence interval 0.03 to 0.44; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared to single-dose etoposide, divided oral dosing was associated with fewer grade III-IV hematologic events in comorbid HLH. However, if true absorption is much lower than 50% in critically ill patients, the apparent reduction in hematologic toxicity would in part reflect the lower dose administered rather than the route of administration. Further randomized pharmacokinetic studies are warranted.

articles.title: Intensity-controlled Raster Scanning Carbon Ion Radiation Therapy With a Heavy-ion Gantry: Clinical Experience at Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center.
articles.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Carbon ions have biophysical advantages over photons, including a finite range, increased relative biological effectiveness, and lowered oxygen dependence. Maximum treatment flexibility is attainable with rotational beam delivery. We report our clinical experience using the carbon-ion gantry at the Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center with intensity-controlled raster scanning capability, focusing on treatment toxicity.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 1622 patients treated using the carbon-ion gantry between 2012 and 2026 were evaluated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Toxicity analysis was conducted using Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events v5.0.
RESULTS: The median age preradiation therapy was 59 years (range, 18-91). Most patients had locally advanced tumors (21.8% T4; 11.2% T3) without regional lymph node metastases (45.4% N0). The most common treatment indications were sacrococcygeal tumors (n = 331; 20.4%), followed by tumors of the paranasal sinuses (n = 166; 10.2%) and the spine (n = 121; 7.5%). A total of 486 patients (30.0%) received carbon-ion reirradiation, the most frequent carbon-ion gantry treatment indication viewed across all patients. The most common particle therapy beam-angle number was 2 (range, 1-7). The use of more than 2 beam angles was particularly frequent in tumors of the skull base (45.8%) and the thoracic region (40.0%). High-grade (III and IV) acute and late toxicity rates were 2.4% and 4.2% in primary treatment. Mean numbers of acute and late grade I and II toxicity events per patient were 2.2 (95% confidence interval, 2.0-2.4) and 2.0 (95% confidence interval, 1.7-2.4), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Carbon-ion radiation therapy using a heavy-ion gantry resulted in favorable toxicity rates in specific indications. Further interdisciplinary research demonstrating the clinical benefit of carbon-ion radiation therapy is required. This study provides more evidence supporting particle therapy facilities and may serve as a foundation for prospective clinical trials.

articles.title: Current practice in paediatric occupational therapy in Australia: A descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Australian paediatric occupational therapy has seen significant changes in the last 15 years, yet there have been no published studies in that time that explore current practice. This study aimed to examine and create a profile of current practices of Australian paediatric occupational therapists regarding application of theories and models, goal setting, assessment, intervention, professional development, and use of evidence.
METHODS: In this descriptive study, a purpose-designed online survey was distributed via social media, occupational therapy organisations, and researcher contacts. The survey was open between March and September 2023. The survey was approximately 25 minutes long and included fixed choice and open-ended questions. Descriptive and content analysis were conducted.
CONSUMER AND COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT: An advisory group of paediatric occupational therapists was involved in survey design and testing.
RESULTS: One-hundred and fifty-six surveys were fully completed. Participants predominantly worked in private practice (56.41%) and utilised National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS)/Early Childhood Intervention funding (71.15%). The most common diagnosis seen was autism spectrum disorder (84.62%). The most common theory used was developmental theory (80.00%). The most frequently used model was the Person, Environment, Occupation model (66.67%). The goal setting tool most used was the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (81.15%). The most frequently used assessment was Sensory Profile 2 (71.23%). Participants identified that they most commonly focussed on fine motor training (77.93%), parent/caregiver education (69.66%), and goal directed training (68.28%) for intervention. Less than half (41.67%) reported being 'somewhat satisfied' with their access to professional development, but the majority reported being supported by their workplace in using evidence-based practice (90.38%).
CONCLUSION: Changes in current paediatric occupational therapy practice were identified, which were reflective of the change to funding via the NDIS and evidence supporting top-down interventions. An emphasis on measuring at the level of impairment remains a barrier to supporting and evaluating occupational performance and participation outcomes.

articles.title: Measles resurgence in Bangladesh in 2026: national surveillance trends, cumulative divisional burden, and historical vaccination context.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bangladesh experienced a major measles resurgence in 2026. We reassessed early outbreak indicators while distinguishing daily notifications, cumulative burden and historical vaccination measures.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive analysis of Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) bulletins dated 2-30 April 2026, reporting cumulative totals from 15 March. We reconstructed cumulative division-level counts from the 22 April bulletin and calculated population-standardized notification rates using the 2022 census. Official national measles-containing vaccine coverage for 2019, 2023 and 2024 provided historical context.
RESULTS: By 30 April, DGHS reported 37,131 suspected and 5028 confirmed cases, with 227 suspected and 49 confirmed deaths. On 22 April, cumulative division-level totals were 27,164 suspected and 3934 confirmed cases. Dhaka recorded 2634 confirmed cases, or 5.957 per 100,000 population. Official national MCV1 and MCV2 coverage in 2024 was 86.1% and 80.7%, respectively. Earlier childhood MR1 division-level measurements were not contemporaneous with the outbreak and were not used for correlation testing.
CONCLUSIONS: The early outbreak showed substantial reported burden and geographic heterogeneity. Accurate interpretation requires matching reporting windows, strengthening age- and vaccination-status surveillance and avoiding causal inferences from historical aggregate coverage.

articles.title: AI-assisted evidence map prioritising TB research signals from the Union World Conference on Lung Health 2025 against End TB 2035 priorities.
articles.abstract: Progress to end the global tuberculosis (TB) epidemic remains off track despite current efforts. Conferences generate emerging evidence to help achieve End TB 2035 targets, but these signals are rarely assessed for their alignment with End TB targets and for adoption readiness. Therefore, we aimed to identify and prioritize TB research from the Union World Conference on Lung Health (WCLH) 2025 against End TB 2035 targets, using an adoption readiness framework. We conducted an AI-assisted, human-verified synthesis of conference presentations. Speech recognition and three large language models supported transcription, structured extraction, verification, evidence classification, scoring and target mapping. Adoption readiness of research findings was assessed across development stage, affordability, scalability, implementation feasibility, financing, health-system compatibility and equity. Of 247 presentations included, 13 were classified as Tier 1, 128 as Tier 2 and 106 as Tier 3. Diagnostics and treatment showed the highest adoption potential (shortened regimens, pooled molecular testing and computer-aided radiography). Prevention had moderately strong evidence but lower adoption potential. Vaccines and prevention strategies carried the highest potential population impact but the lowest readiness, remaining uncertain to be ready before the mid-2030s. Major research gaps persisted for pregnancy, children, extrapulmonary TB, and in resource-limited settings. Despite meaningful scientific progress, current evidence was neither sufficiently mature nor equitably deployable to place the 2035 targets within reach. Greater investment, implementation evidence, health-system capacity and political action are required to translate innovation into global impact. AI-assisted, human-verified synthesis can rapidly organise emerging evidence, but its outputs are hypothesis-generating and require independent validation.

articles.title: Genetic Counseling When One Partner Carries a CF-Causing Variant and the Other Has the Intronic IVS8-5T Variant.
articles.abstract: Complex genetic counseling situations can arise when whole-gene sequencing is used as part of reproductive genetic carrier screening or newborn screening for cystic fibrosis (CF). One of the most common scenarios is when one reproductive partner carries a CF-causing variant such as c.1521-1523del (or p.F508del) and the other partner carries the c.1210-12T[5] (or IVS8-5T) variant. Questions arise as to what information to provide about the likely outcome if the fetus or newborn has both variants in trans, as well as implications for future pregnancies and other family members. In this paper, we consider an approach to genetic counseling based on knowledge of CFTR biology and available clinical data.

articles.title: Implementation of the Toronto guidelines for childhood cancer staging: experience from 65 population-based cancer registries participating in the BENCHISTA project.
articles.journal: ESMO Real World Data Digit Oncol
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population-based cancer registries (PBCRs) are central to measuring childhood cancer outcomes and informing global health policy. The International Benchmarking of Childhood Cancer Survival by Stage (BENCHISTA) project stimulated participating PBCRs to assign stage at diagnosis according to the international Toronto Stage Guidelines (TGs). This study aims to provide a quantitative assessment of operational findings and structural barriers limiting routine TGs implementation within PBCRs participating in the first phase of BENCHISTA.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Seventy-three PBCRs participating in the first phase of BENCHISTA were invited to complete a semistructured survey assessing operational practices, data collection capacity, and structural and operational barriers to routine implementation of the TGs and associated non-stage-prognostic (NSP) variables across six solid childhood tumours. Sixty-five PBCRs from 23 countries provided valid and complete answers.
RESULTS: Before BENCHISTA, 85% PBCRs reported no routine collection of TGs. Following participation, 51% indicated that they would continue staging all childhood cancers. The principal barriers to TGs assignment were workload (38%), lack of linkage with clinical sources (32%), and time required for data retrieval (29%). Molecular NSP variables-particularly rhabdomyosarcoma fusion markers and medulloblastoma subgroups-were the most difficult to capture due to inconsistent pathology reporting and limited registry access to molecular data. Fewer than half had systematic collection of treatment and recurrence data.
CONCLUSIONS: This multinational survey provides a quantitative assessment of barriers limiting routine TGs implementation in PBCRs. Sustaining consistent data collection will require targeted investment in workforce capacity, improved interoperability between clinical and registry systems, and standardisation of clinical, molecular, and pathology reporting frameworks.

articles.title: Calpeptin attenuates LPS-induced ventriculomegaly in neonatal mice.
articles.abstract: Acute inflammatory insults in the developing brain can produce ventriculomegaly, but underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We tested whether preventive calpeptin treatment modified the phenotype induced by intraventricular lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in neonatal mice. Ventricular-volume analysis included vehicle (12 pups/4 litters), LPS (8 pups/3 litters), and LPS + calpeptin (10 pups/2 litters). Calpeptin reduced mean ventricular volume by 72% relative to LPS (2.48 versus 8.92 mm3); the difference persisted in a mixed-effects model with litter as a random intercept (-0.61 log10 mm3, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.20, p = 0.004). Survival analysis included vehicle (13 pups/4 litters), LPS (26 pups/5 litters), and LPS + calpeptin (12 pups/2 litters). Observed endpoint survival was 10/12 with calpeptin versus 10/26 with LPS, but the litter-level comparison was not significant, and pronounced between-litter heterogeneity and only two calpeptin litters preclude a definitive treatment-effect inference; survival remains exploratory. Cortical DiI vascular labeling and VE-cadherin immunofluorescence were obtained from one litter per group and are descriptive, not measures of blood-brain barrier permeability. In cultured primary brain microvascular endothelial cells, LPS increased permeability and the approximately 95/130 kDa VE-cadherin-immunoreactive band ratio. Calpeptin and TLR4 inhibition reduced the band-ratio increase but did not significantly attenuate permeability relative to LPS. Calpeptin is not protease- or isoform-selective, and target engagement was not measured. Thus, the findings suggest a contribution from calpeptin-sensitive protease activity without identifying the responsible protease, confirming cleavage of the lower band, or demonstrating endothelial barrier protection in vivo.

articles.title: Predicting severity and long-term respiratory health in pediatric adenovirus pneumonia: A retrospective cohort study integrating risk modeling and atopic status.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To identify risk factors for severe adenovirus pneumonia (SAP) in children, develop and validate a predictive nomogram, and investigate the impact of atopy on both acute severity and long-term pulmonary sequelae.
METHODS: The retrospective cohort study involved 416 children diagnosed with adenovirus pneumonia at Shandong Provincial Hospital between January 2019 and February 2025. Patients were stratified into SAP and non-SAP groups based on disease progression. Independent predictors were identified using multivariate logistic regression to construct a nomogram, validated by 1,000 Bootstrap resamples. 89 survivors of SAP were followed up longitudinally to compare pulmonary function and respiratory complications between patients with and without atopic predisposition.
RESULTS: In this study, 189 enrolled children (45.43%) progressed to SAP. Multivariate analysis revealed that atopic predisposition (odds ratio [OR] = 1.933, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.102-3.392), pulse oxygen saturation< 95% (OR = 4.963, 95% CI: 2.702-9.117), serum amyloid A (OR = 1.002, 95% CI: 1.000-1.004), hypoalbuminemia (OR = 0.914, 95% CI: 0.888-0.941), and clinical pulmonary infection score ≥ 1 (score 1: OR = 3.899, 95% CI: 1.533-9.915; score 2: OR = 15.825, 95% CI: 6.663-37.587) were independent predictors of SAP. The constructed nomogram demonstrated robust discrimination (area under the curve = 0.854, 95% CI: 0.818-0.890) and excellent calibration (Spiegelhalter Z-test p = 0.941). In the follow-up cohort, atopic predisposition was associated with adverse long-term outcomes: it was present in 69.23% (18/26)of children who developed bronchial asthma and 100% (10/10) of those diagnosed with bronchiolitis obliterans respectively.
CONCLUSION: This study developed a reliable risk prediction model integrating clinical, laboratory, and imaging markers to facilitate early identification of children at high risk for SAP. Atopic predisposition is associated with acute disease severity and may increase the risk of long-term pulmonary impairment (particularly bronchiolitis obliterans and asthma) , highlighting host-virus interplay rather than viral infection alone. These findings support systematic long-term pulmonary function monitoring and personalized respiratory rehabilitation strategies for children post-adenovirus infection to optimize respiratory health.

articles.title: Patient- and family-reported satisfaction in child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care: An exploratory descriptive survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe and compare patient- and family-reported satisfaction with child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care in a Japanese inpatient unit.
METHODS: Patients aged 8-15 years discharged from a single Japanese inpatient unit and their families completed an anonymous web questionnaire with separate patient and family versions. Overall satisfaction was rated on a 10-point scale, and respondents who reported interaction rated the usefulness of five professional groups. Because responses were unlinked, 10 probable patient-family pairs identified from submission times were used in sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Invitations were handed to 61 patients and their families at discharge; 52 family members (85.2%) and 26 patients (42.6%) responded. Family members reported higher satisfaction than patients (mean 8.14 [SD 1.83] vs. 6.27 [SD 2.15]; medians 8 vs. 7; mean difference 1.87, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-2.86), and the lower 95% CI limit was at least 0.73 in all sensitivity analyses addressing dependence between the groups. The maximum score was given by 25.5% of family members and 3.8% of patients. Among respondents who rated each professional group, a higher proportion of family members than patients rated child and adolescent psychiatrists (98.1% vs. 69.2%) and nurses (92.3% vs. 73.1%) as useful, whereas proportions for psychiatric social workers, clinical psychologists, and teachers were similar or higher among patients. These profession-specific comparisons were descriptive only.
CONCLUSION: Patients rated inpatient care less favorably than family members. Family reports should complement, not replace, patients' own evaluations, and future multicenter studies should use matched patient-family dyads.

articles.title: Changes in the Number of Patients With Drug Overdose due to Deliberate Self-Harm Transported to the Hospital Emergency Department During the Past 12 Years.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Recently, over-the-counter (OTC) drug overdoses have increased. This study aimed to clarify the clinical characteristics and temporal trends of acute drug overdose and explore effective countermeasures in emergency medical settings.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients admitted to our hospital for acute drug overdose due to deliberate self-harm between January 2012 and December 2023. Data collected from medical records included sex, age, ingested substances, implementation of advanced interventions, and outcomes. Cases were categorized as prescription drugs only or OTC drugs present. Comparisons were made before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Severe cases were defined as those requiring advanced interventions; psychiatric care history was assessed in severe cases.
RESULTS: Of the 1676 included patients (mean age 37.8 years), 74.4% used only prescription drugs, 15.0% used only OTC drugs and 5.1% used both. OTC drug-involved cases increased significantly from 15.7% before to 29.7% after the COVID-19 pandemic (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients aged 10-29 years also increased significantly (p < 0.001), as did their OTC drug use (p < 0.001). Severe cases accounted for 8.2% (n = 137) and 12 deaths (0.7%). The proportion of severe cases did not differ significantly between groups. Among the severe cases, psychiatric care history was more frequent in the prescription-only group (90.9%) compared to the OTC-involved group (54.5%).
CONCLUSION: Since 2019, a marked increase in OTC drug overdoses among younger individuals has been observed. Emergency departments should play a key role in initiating multidisciplinary, community-based support systems to prevent recurrence.

articles.title: Testing Failure Mode and Effect Analysis: A Descriptive Empirical Study in Paediatric and Adolescent Hospital Care.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Patient safety incidents may have serious consequences for hospitalised paediatric patients. It is estimated that half of all incidents in paediatric care could be prevented. Proactive risk management methods aim to identify, assess and mitigate potential risks before they result in harm to patients.
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To test and introduce the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis method in various processes in paediatric and adolescent department with action research methodology.
METHOD: Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) produces a risk priority number (RPN), calculated by multiplying the values of occurrence, severity and detectability. In this study, FMEA was tested by professionals working in the department with the support of a team leader. A cyclical action research process was used, including the phases of planning, acting, analysis and drawing conclusions. The study was conducted between February and September 2024, conducting one action research cycle.
RESULTS: Multidisciplinary teams (team sizes varied from 3 to 6) from a paediatric department tested the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis method and assessed 8 processes, identifying 59 failure modes (average of 6.75 per process). The RPN range was from 2 to 36. A total of 52 corrective actions were developed targeting high-risk failure modes. Actions ranged from simple (e.g., information sharing) to complex (e.g., equipment changes). FMEA enabled the teams to proactively prioritise and address risks.
CONCLUSION: The Failure Mode and Effect Analysis is a suitable method for assessing various processes in a paediatric hospital. Action research was an appropriate method to support the testing of FMEA and to introduce a proactive risk management method to study participants.

articles.title: Antibiotic utilization patterns, direct antibiotic acquisition costs, and hospital transfer outcomes in a pediatric emergency care unit: a retrospective study from Northeastern Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibiotic prescribing in pediatric emergency care represents an important clinical and economic challenge, particularly for antimicrobial stewardship and resource allocation. Evidence from pediatric emergency settings in low- and middle-income countries remains limited.
APPROACH: This retrospective study evaluated antibiotic prescribing patterns, direct antibiotic acquisition costs, and hospital-transfer status in a pediatric emergency care unit in Northeastern Brazil from 2019 to 2021. The full prescription dataset was used for descriptive analyses and cumulative acquisition cost estimation, whereas complete-case subsets were used for antibiotic unit-cost comparisons and hospital-transfer analyses. Direct costs were estimated using institutional acquisition prices. Statistical analyses included group comparisons, principal component analysis (PCA), and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA).
RESULTS: The descriptive sample comprised 10,489 antibiotic prescription records, with 324 treatment episodes included in the unit-cost analysis and 302 in the hospital-transfer analysis. The estimated minimum cumulative direct antibiotic acquisition cost for the overall prescription dataset was USD 13,044.67, with benzathine benzylpenicillin, ceftriaxone, amoxicillin, and azithromycin accounting for the highest cumulative costs. Antibiotic unit costs differed significantly across diagnostic groups (p = 0.022). Among treatment episodes included in the unit-cost analysis, 78.1% of antibiotics were classified as Access and 21.9% as Watch according to the World Health Organization (WHO) Access, Watch, and Reserve (AWaRe) classification, with no Reserve antibiotics identified. Exploratory PCA and HCA showed differences in therapeutic profiles across diagnostic groups. Higher antibiotic unit costs were observed among transferred episodes, although only seven episodes involved transfer, limiting the interpretation of this exploratory comparison.
CONCLUSIONS: Antibiotic utilization and direct antibiotic acquisition costs varied across pediatric diagnoses, highlighting opportunities for antimicrobial stewardship and pharmaceutical resource optimization in pediatric emergency care.

articles.title: Introduction of respiratory virus point-of-care testing at multi-site front-door admission wards.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, rapid point-of-care testing (POCT) multiplex polymerase chain reaction assays for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and influenza A/B viruses were introduced at four front-door admission sites.
AIM: To provide timely diagnosis of respiratory infections, help inform clinical decision-making, and potentially support patient flow and reduce the risk of hospital-acquired infections. This study also investigated the impact on laboratory testing demand as a proxy for workload, and the propriety of POCT use by ward staff.
METHODS: Respiratory samples tested by the laboratory or by POCT between January 2022 and June 2024 were analysed retrospectively to assess testing demand, rate of positivity, turnaround time (TAT), and staff competency in the use of POCT.
RESULTS: Of the 42,073 respiratory samples received, 54% (N=22,664) were tested by the virology laboratory and 46% (N=19,409) by POCT. Among adults, 44% of influenza-A-positive samples and 63% of SARS-CoV-2-positive samples were from patients aged ≥65 years. Among children, 69% of influenza-A-positive samples and 72% of SARS-CoV-2-positive samples were from patients aged 0-4 years. Only 4.3% of POCT results were invalid, suggesting acceptable operational performance in routine use. The time to result was significantly shorter for POCT compared with laboratory testing for influenza A/B (approximately 20 min vs 1319 min; P<0.05) and SARS-CoV-2 (approximately 20 min vs 418 min; P<0.05), reflecting more rapid availability of results for clinical decision-making.
CONCLUSION: Introduction of rapid POCT at front-door admission was associated with a reduction in laboratory testing volume and shorter analytical TAT, which may support timely clinical management.

articles.title: Series of six cases of tinea capitis caused by Microsporum audouinii with atypical parasitism.
articles.abstract: Microsporum audouinii typically causes ectothrix tinea capitis. We describe six pediatric cases with endothrix parasitism and positive Wood's lamp fluorescence. Cultures identified Microsporum audouinii, with additional MALDI-TOF confirmation in a subset. These findings suggest possible variation in hair invasion. Fluorescence reflects infection-associated fluorophores rather than arthroconidial location alone; its coexistence with endothrix parasitism is a plausible interpretation requiring further investigation. Microscopy should be interpreted alongside culture and species identification.

articles.title: Association Between Dietary Zinc Intake and Hay Fever in US Children and Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hay fever is an increasingly common allergic disease worldwide. As an essential trace element, zinc is vital for immune homeostasis, and diet plays an important role in allergic diseases. We examined the relationship between dietary zinc intake and hay fever in US children and adolescents.
METHODS: We conducted cross-sectional analysis of children and adolescents participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline, threshold effects, and subgroup analyses were used to evaluate the association between dietary zinc and hay fever.
RESULTS: Of 26,447 children and adolescents, 2800 (10.6%) had hay fever. In the fully adjusted model, higher dietary zinc intake was associated with lower odds of hay fever: each 100 μg/kg/day increase corresponded to a 5% reduction (OR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.97). Compared with the lowest quartile (Q1, ≤ 141 μg/kg/day), adjusted ORs were 0.84 (95% CI 0.74-0.95), 0.72 (95% CI 0.62-0.83), and 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76) for Q2 (142-247 μg/kg/day), Q3 (248-423 μg/kg/day), and Q4 (≥ 424 μg/kg/day), respectively. The dose-response relationship was L-shaped (nonlinearity, p < 0.001): below the threshold of 273.4 μg/kg/day, each 100 μg/kg/day increase in zinc intake was associated with a 25.3% reduction in the odds of hay fever (OR 0.747, 95% CI 0.666-0.837), whereas above this threshold no significant association was observed.
CONCLUSION: The association between dietary zinc intake and hay fever is L-shaped, with an inflection point of roughly 273.4 μg/kg/day.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 4.

articles.title: Correlation between post-pyeloplasty diuretic scintigraphic and ultrasonographic parameters in children.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The best surveillance method, timing and frequency to outline resolution of obstruction in children after pyeloplasty are not yet defined.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the correlation between post-operative diuretic scintigraphic and ultrasonographic parameters in children who underwent pyeloplasty.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a single arm prospective cohort study, 83 children who underwent open Anderson-Hynes pyeloplasty from June 2023 to May 2024, were included. Those who had bilateral pyeloplasty or pyeloplasty in a solitary or anomalous kidney were excluded. Six months after surgery, follow-up ultrasonography and diuretic scintigraphy were performed.
RESULTS: Successful pyeloplasty was noted in 81 patients (97.59 %), while the remaining 2 patients (2.41 %) who had failed pyeloplasty were managed by redo pyeloplasty. Pre and post-operative ultrasonographic and scintigraphic parameters were evaluated in all patients. Post-operative cortical transit time (CTT) showed significant correlation with post-operative anteroposterior diameter (APD), parenchymal thickness, calyceal dilation, calyx-to-parenchyma ratio, cortex-to-pelvis ratio and T-half (T½). Post-operative T½ also showed significant correlation with post-operative APD, parenchymal thickness, calyx-to-parenchyma ratio and cortex-to-pelvis ratio. On the other hand, post-operative CTT showed insignificant correlation with APD change, while post-operative T½ showed insignificant correlation with APD change and post-operative calyceal dilation.
CONCLUSIONS: Post-operative ultrasonographic parameters, apart from APD change and post-operative calyceal dilation, may correlate with post-operative diuretic scintigraphic parameters in children who underwent pyeloplasty.

articles.title: Associations of screen time, physical activity and neuromuscular fitness with brain structure in adolescents.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the associations of total screen time, smart device use, physical activity, and neuromuscular fitness with brain gray matter volumes in adolescence.
METHODS: Brain gray matter volumes were assessed using magnetic resonance imaging in 44 healthy adolescents (25 females and 19 males) aged 16-19 years. Physical activity and sedentary behavior questionnaires were used to assess screen time, including smart device use, and physical activity, including organized sports in sports clubs. Neuromuscular fitness was assessed using a score combining results of a 50-m shuttle-run test and a standing long jump test.
RESULTS: Screen time and smart device use were negatively associated with medial temporal lobe volumes but positively associated with supplementary motor cortex and dorsal lateral prefrontal cortex volumes. Screen time was also positively related to left cuneus volume. Total physical activity was positively associated with right inferior occipital gyrus volume, but the association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Neuromuscular fitness was positively associated with parietal lobe volumes but negatively associated with right hippocampus and left posterior cingulate gyrus volumes, but these associations were no longer statistically significant after correction for multiple testing.
CONCLUSION: Longer screen time was related to lower medial temporal lobe volumes and larger frontal lobe volumes, whereas higher physical activity and better neuromuscular fitness were associated with larger volumes in the parietal and occipital regions. These findings highlight the complex relationships of screen time and physical activity with brain gray matter volumes in adolescence.

articles.title: Patient-specific heart rate modulates developmental electrophysiology in transcriptomic-guided in silico models of pediatric human atrial cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract: Cardiac electrophysiology adapts throughout pediatric development, driven by factors including age-associated ion channel expression changes and decreasing heart rate. Our prior transcriptomic-guided simulations of human atrial cardiomyocytes predicted developmental-associated changes in electrophysiology biomarkers at a fixed pacing rate, leaving the contribution of age- and patient-specific heart rate unresolved. In this study, we incorporated intrinsic heart rate into gene expression-guided computational models to predict the interaction between developmental maturation and pacing rate to shape atrial electrophysiology. Virtual patient-specific populations of atrial cardiomyocytes were generated from the right atrial cardiomyocyte gene expression data from 117 patients, spanning neonates to young adults. We simulated each population at pacing rates corresponding to each patient's intrinsic ECG-based heart rate and at fixed rates corresponding to the patient cohort minimum, median, and maximum. We also simulated each population at the patient's intrinsic heart rate in the presence of isoproterenol. Action potential and calcium transient biomarkers were quantified, and partial least squares regression assessed key biomarker dependencies. For intrinsic-rate pacing conditions, action potential duration at 50% and 90% repolarization increased with age, whereas early repolarization shortened; maximum upstroke velocity increased, resting membrane potential became more negative, and alternans prevalence decreased. Developmental differences persisted during fixed-rate pacing conditions, indicating that differences were not explained solely by the faster heart rates of younger patients. Notably, intrinsic-rate simulations exhibited stronger age associations for upstroke velocity and alternans than fixed-rate simulations. Further, isoproterenol induced age-dependent responses, with most notably opposite directional changes in action potential duration. Sensitivity analyses indicated that electrophysiological phenotypes arose from interactions among ionic conductances, calcium handling, age, and heart rate. Collectively, we find that pediatric atrial electrophysiology reflects both intrinsic developmental remodeling and rate-dependent modulation.

articles.title: Recent positive psychosocial experiences are linked to SARS-CoV-2 IgG immune memory in adults exposed to adverse childhood experiences.
articles.abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with altered immune function in adulthood including elevated susceptibility to viral infection, chronic inflammation, and poorer COVID-19 disease outcomes. Meanwhile, protective experiences have been associated with better immune profiles, although few studies have examined this in the context of high ACEs. In a community-based sample of middle-aged (35-59y) adults with high average 10-item ACE scores (mean(SD) = 4.2(2.9)) and who self-reported at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose or one COVID-19 illness (N = 72), we tested whether early life ACEs and current protective and compensatory experiences (C-PACEs) in adulthood were associated with reduced anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike protein subunit 1 receptor binding domain (S1-RBD) IgG antibody levels. In covariate-adjusted analyses, higher childhood ACE scores were associated with lower levels of log2-transformed anti-S1-RBD IgG antibodies (β = -0.17 ± 0.06 per ACE event, p = 0.005). Analyses examining adult C-PACE scores documented an elevation in anti-S1-RBD IgG (β = 0.09 ± 0.03 per C-PACE point, p = 0.001). Follow-up analyses did not detect moderation of the effect of ACEs by C-PACEs (interactive term β = 0.17, p = 0.296). In an exploratory mediation analysis, the estimated indirect effect through C-PACEs was not statistically supported (β = -0.07, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.167, 0.004], p = 0.113). These results suggest that SARS-CoV-2 IgG immune memory may be linked to protective experiences in adulthood, which are inversely correlated with childhood ACEs.

articles.title: Dense Granule Protein DG9 of Cryptosporidium parvum Interacts With DG10 at the Dense Band.
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidium parvum, a protozoan parasite, causes life-threatening diarrhea in young children and immunocompromised individuals. During host cell invasion and intracellular proliferation, C. parvum secretes rhoptry, dense granule (DG), and small granule (SG) proteins into the parasite-host interface. These secreted proteins facilitate the biogenesis of the parasitophorous vacuole (PV) enclosing the parasite and the feeder organelle and electron-dense band (DB) at the parasite-host interface. Nevertheless, the molecular compositions of these organelles are poorly defined. Here, we characterized the subcellular localization and functional role of cgd1_470, a highly polymorphic protein associated with host adaptation in the parasite. Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated endogenous tagging, we revealed that cgd1_470 is a novel DG protein, designated DG9. DG9 is secreted to the parasite-host interface during invasion and localizes to the DB after the PV formation. Deleting the dg9 gene did not significantly alter the in vitro growth or in vivo pathogenicity of a virulent C. parvum strain. Proteomic screening identified several putative DG9-interacting partners, including DG10 (cgd7_4280) and SG5 (cgd1_640), both of which display a similar interfacial localization. We validated the physical interaction between DG9 and DG10 using coimmunoprecipitation and colocalization analyses. Taken together, these findings suggest that DG9 and DG10 are interacting components of the DB at the parasite-host interface.

articles.title: Role of Selected Myokines and Mineral Metabolism in Spinal Muscular Atrophy: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Despite substantial progress in understanding spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), the roles of several biological factors in its pathophysiology remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the current evidence on the role of selected myokines, namely myostatin, follistatin, IL-6 (Interleukin-6), and IGF-1 (Insulin-like growth factor 1), as well as the minerals, copper, zinc, calcium, iron, and magnesium, in the pathogenesis and treatment of SMA. A PROSPERO-registered systematic review included 25 studies. Risk-of-bias assessment using validated tools revealed heterogeneity in methodological quality. The findings suggested that reduced levels of myostatin were associated with disease subtype, functional status, but not with age or 30 months of nusinersen treatment. Follistatin demonstrated protective effects on the neuromuscular system in preclinical models, whereas clinical evidence was inconclusive, with no consistent associations with SMA subtype, age, or body weight. Altered IL-6 levels in blood samples from both children and adults were linked to neuroinflammatory processes and disease activity, suggesting its potential as a biomarker of treatment response. Exogenous IGF-1 attenuated muscle atrophy and improved motor function in preclinical models. Disturbances in mineral homeostasis were related to skeletal and metabolic dysfunction. Studies revealed reduced bone mineral density, magnesium and iron deficiencies, a relationship between copper metabolism and adverse body composition, and the potential neuroprotective role of zinc. Growing evidence suggests that "myokine-mineral crosstalk" may bridge neuromuscular integrity with bone remodeling and calcium-phosphate metabolism in SMA. Overall, these findings provide broader insights into the biological mechanisms underlying SMA pathophysiology and disease monitoring while emphasizing the need for a multidisciplinary research approach.

articles.title: Localization mechanisms and function of postsynaptic Kv7 (KCNQ) channels and their reduction in KCNQ2 epileptic encephalopathy.
articles.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.abstract: Kv7 channels composed of Kv7.2 and Kv7.3 subunits are enriched in neuronal axons where their hyperpolarizing potassium current suppresses repetitive and burst firing of action potentials. Mutations in their genes, KCNQ2 and KCNQ3, cause neonatal epilepsy, underscoring their critical role in regulating neuronal excitability. In this study, we provide evidence that Kv7 channels are present at and near the postsynaptic density within dendritic spines of hippocampal neurons, where their current decreases calcium influx through NMDA receptors. This spine localization is promoted by heteromerization of Kv7.2 and Kv7.3 and their binding to AnkyrinG-190, which is the only AnkyrinG isoform present in dendritic spines. Lastly, spine localization of Kv7 channels and their ability to suppress NMDA receptor activity are markedly reduced by select variants of KCNQ2 that cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). These findings reveal a subcellular population of Kv7 channels that can dampen excitatory synaptic transmission and implicate their dysregulation in KCNQ2-associated DEE.

articles.title: Chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment attenuates auditory fear conditioning in adult male rats.
articles.abstract: Noncompetitive-777-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms, supporting the NMDA receptor hypofunction hypothesis. Neonatal NMDA receptor blockade with MK-801 is widely used to model neurodevelopmental aspects of schizophrenia; however, its impact on cue-specific fear learning remains incompletely characterized. Male Sprague-Dawley pups received subcutaneous injections of MK-801 (0.4 mg/kg) or saline twice daily from postnatal day 7-20. In adulthood, rats underwent auditory fear conditioning (five tone-shock pairings), 4 days of extinction (45 tone-alone trials/session), a retrieval test, and a remote retrieval test. Across acquisition and all test sessions, MK-801-treated rats showed consistently lower freezing than controls. These findings suggest that chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment disrupts acquisition or expression of cue-shock associations, or both. Given the small sample size and the potential contribution of altered locomotion or shock reactivity, future work should incorporate locomotor and sensory controls.

articles.title: Prediction of severe neonatal morbidity using maternal, fetal, social, and delivery factors.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate prediction models for severe neonatal morbidity (SNM) at admission for delivery and at delivery while evaluating the incremental contribution of maternal, fetal, social, intrapartum, and immediate post-delivery factors.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of singleton deliveries ≥32 weeks' gestation at two tertiary hospitals (2019-2023). SNM was defined using a composite of severe neonatal diagnoses and procedures. The cohort was randomly divided into training (70 %) and testing (30 %) cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression models were developed iteratively to predict SNM at admission for delivery and at delivery. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), compared using the DeLong test, and overall accuracy using Brier scores.
RESULTS: Among 53,872 singleton deliveries, 3,775 newborns (7.0 %) experienced SNM. Maternal factors alone demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC 0.721, 95 % CI 0.704-0.738); adding fetal and social factors produced a modest increase (AUC 0.738, 95 % CI 0.721-0.755; difference 0.017, 95 % CI 0.005-0.029; p=0.0051). Gestational age was the strongest predictor; others included major structural anomalies, polyhydramnios, abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers, hypertensive disorders, and substance use disorder. Adding intrapartum factors and newborn sex increased the AUC to 0.776 (95 % CI 0.761-0.791); birthweight relative to gestational age added minimal improvement (AUC 0.780, 95 % CI 0.765-0.795).
CONCLUSIONS: SNM can be predicted with moderate accuracy using routinely available clinical information. Fetal and social factors modestly improved discrimination, and intrapartum information further improved it, supporting staged neonatal risk assessment during the delivery hospitalization.

articles.title: Integrated Vector, Canine, and Human Evidence Reveal a Stable Dog-Maintained Cycle of Leishmania Infantum in a Historically Endemic Area From Spain.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Leishmaniosis, caused by Leishmania infantum, is a major zoonotic vector-borne disease in southern Europe. Dogs act as the primary domestic reservoir of the parasite. However, there is growing evidence that transmission cycles involving wild lagomorphs may contribute to both epidemic and endemic human cases in certain settings. Nevertheless, the ecological and epidemiological mechanisms sustaining long-term endemic transmission in stable foci remain poorly understood. This study used an integrated One Health approach combining vector, canine, and human data to investigate transmission dynamics in a long-established endemic area with low human case incidence.
METHODS: An eco-epidemiological study was conducted in Crevillente Municipality in southeast Spain, between 2021 and 2022. Sand flies were collected using CDC light traps and analysed to determine species composition, Leishmania infection by real-time PCR, parasite identification, and blood meal sources. Dogs were tested for anti-Leishmania antibodies using ELISA. Human blood donors were assessed for Leishmania infection by PCR and for anti-Leishmania antibodies and antibodies against Phlebotomus perniciosus saliva as markers of parasite and vector exposure, respectively.
RESULTS: A total of 11,375 sand flies were collected, predominantly Sergentomyia minuta and Phlebotomus perniciosus, and displayed marked seasonal and spatial variation. High Leishmania infection rates were detected in confirmed vector species, with L. infantum identified in most samples. Blood meal analysis revealed that the primary feeding sources were dogs and humans, while rabbits and hares were detected but infrequently. Canine seroprevalence was high (43%) and associated with rural exposure. In humans, infection markers were low (3% PCR, 4% serology), despite high exposure to sand fly bites (38% seroprevalence for anti-saliva antibodies).
CONCLUSIONS: The study characterizes a Mediterranean endemic focus with intense circulation of L. infantum in vectors and dogs, widespread human exposure to sand flies, but low levels of asymptomatic human infection and no reported clinical disease during the decade preceding the study. The findings support a predominantly domestic transmission, with dogs representing the main identified reservoir host and lagomorph-derived blood meals being relatively infrequent. The potential contribution of lagomorphs to local parasite circulation warrants further investigation. The detection of Leishmania DNA in non-confirmed vector species, including sequences consistent with the L. donovani/L. infantum complex, further highlights the need for continued surveillance of Leishmania diversity and transmission dynamics.

articles.title: Altitude and disease persistence in childhood immune thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract: Yin and colleagues reported childhood immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) lasting at least three months in 8.8% of children hospitalized in Xining and 27.3% in Ningbo. In Ningbo, 79 of 88 children achieved complete response within the first seven days, while only 64 recovered before three months. At least 15 of the 24 children with prolonged disease must therefore have achieved early complete response. Linking their platelet counts to intervening treatment would clarify how long those responses lasted. Because each altitude was represented by one hospital, referral practices and opportunities to detect secondary immune disease may also contribute to the observed difference. Parental consanguinity, family histories of immunodeficiency or autoimmunity, immunoglobulin levels before intravenous immunoglobulin, and diagnoses emerging during follow-up merit systematic documentation. Our clinical impression of more frequent persistence in Van than in Adana raises this question in Türkiye. Published series from Van, Adana, and Istanbul used different definitions of disease duration, limiting geographic comparisons. At three months, a child's platelet trajectory and the appearance of another cytopenia or lymphoproliferation can guide reassessment of presumed primary ITP. Prospective comparisons across residential altitudes should document bleeding, rescue treatment, sustained platelet recovery off therapy, and the timing and basis of any subsequent diagnosis.

articles.title: Giving patients a voice: a pilot study of patient-reported outcomes in the Australian cystic fibrosis registry.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop, implement, and evaluate a patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) module within the Australian Cystic Fibrosis Data Registry (ACFDR) to enable routine collection of health-related quality of life (HRQoL) data and support clinical care and quality improvement for people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF).
METHODS: This project used a multi-phase mixed methods design to develop, implement, and evaluate a PROMs module within the ACFDR. Study 1 involved co-design with pwCF, caregivers, and clinicians; Study 2 developed and piloted a REDCap-based PROMs module using the tools identified through co-design with pwCF and caregivers; and Study 3 evaluated implementation through a clinician survey.
RESULTS: Participants supported the integration of PROMs into the ACFDR and identified the CFQ-R and AWESCORE as the preferred HRQoL instruments. Priorities for implementation included electronic PROM administration, routine collection of PROM data, and clear reporting of outcomes using these validated measures. During the pilot, 197 (18.7%) of 1,052 invited participants completed the questionnaires. Adults reported generally high HRQoL, except for vitality, health perceptions, and treatment burden. Clinicians supported PROMs collection in the ACFDR, but highlighted challenges including survey fatigue, low response rates, time constraints, and concerns about data quality and representativeness.
CONCLUSION: Integration of PROMs into the ACFDR is feasible and provides valuable insights into the HRQoL of Australians with CF. Future efforts should focus on improving participation and response rates, as well as enhancing data reporting, to maximise the value of PROMs for quality improvement, benchmarking, and patient-centred care.

articles.title: Evaluation of clinical, immunological, genetic characteristics and follow-up results of patients presenting with common variable immunodeficiency phenotype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) is an antibody deficiency characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, recurrent infections and non-infectious clinical features. Patients presenting with heterogeneous clinical findings lead to delayed diagnosis, various complications, and organ damage.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the clinical, immunological, genetic features of CVID cases diagnosed in our clinic over a 20-year period.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 51 patients diagnosed with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) according to ESID criteria and followed at the Department of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology, Ankara University Faculty of Medicine, between 2002 and 2022.
RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 11.08 years (range: 4-27.91), with a median diagnostic delay of 4.79 years (range: 1-22.91). The most common clinical manifestation was sinopulmonary infections (96%). The most frequent non-infectious clinical manifestation was lymphoproliferation (41.1%). Splenomegaly was significantly more common in patients with autoimmune disease (53.3%). Patients with bronchiectasis had significantly lower proportions of class-switched memory B cells (p = 0.020). CD4+ naive T-cell counts were significantly lower in patients with malignancy compared to those without malignancy (p = 0.006). Genetic analysis performed in 40 patients revealed pathogenic variants in 35%, most frequently involving TACI, followed by ICOS and NFKB2. Following immunoglobulin replacement therapy, infection-related hospitalization rates markedly decreased (from 71.4% to 9.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: CVID patients can present with a wide variety of clinical features. Early diagnosis and treatment can improve quality of life. Identification of genetic defects will enhance understanding of immunopathogenesis opening new avenues for targeted therapies.

articles.title: Hepatocellular Tumors in Patients With Ornithine Transcarbamylase Deficiency Include Focal Nodular Hyperplasia, Hepatocellular Adenoma, and Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency (OTCD) is the most common urea cycle disorder and can cause potentially life-threatening hyperammonemia. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and hepatocellular adenoma (HCA) have been reported in OTCD, usually in adults. Non-neoplastic histologic findings include non-specific glycogenosis, steatosis, and fibrosis.
DESIGN: A retrospective pathology database search between 2000 and 2024 was performed to identify patients with a clinical history of OTCD. Electronic medical records were reviewed for clinical, laboratory, genetic, and imaging findings. Available native liver specimens underwent histologic review, with additional studies performed in select cases.
RESULTS: We identified 11 patients with OTCD. All patients were diagnosed biochemically; pathogenic OTC mutations were detected in all 8 tested patients. Three patients had hepatocellular lesions. One patient with Li-Fraumeni syndrome developed focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) at age 6 and conventional HCC at age 10, when OTCD was also diagnosed. RNA sequencing revealed biased allelic expression toward the mutant OTC allele in the FNH (100% mutant), HCC (94% mutant), and background liver (87% mutant). Two additional pediatric patients had incidental HCAs identified on explant examination at 9 and 17 years of age. The remaining 8 patients (72%) had no focal hepatic lesions. Glycogenosis was the most common histologic finding (10/11, 91%). Only 1 patient had significant steatosis (grade 2) or fibrosis (stage 1).
CONCLUSION: Hepatocellular tumors in OTCD included HCC, HCA, and FNH in pediatric patients. Glycogenosis was the predominant non-neoplastic histologic finding. These findings expand the spectrum of hepatic lesions and non-neoplastic liver pathology reported in OTCD.

articles.title: Effect of critical illness and mechanical ventilation on energy and substrate metabolism in patients with liver cirrhosis: an indirect calorimeter-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Energy and substrate metabolism are altered in liver cirrhosis and may worsen with critical illness. Indirect calorimetry provides accurate metabolic assessment. This study compared resting energy expenditure (REE), respiratory quotient (RQ), and substrate oxidation among healthy controls, non-critically ill, and critically ill cirrhosis patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This prospective observational study included 63 healthy controls (Group I; age 32.5 years; 46% male), 68 non-critically ill cirrhosis patients (Group II; age 47.5 years; 85.3% male; MELD 15), and 70 critically ill ventilated cirrhosis patients (Group III; age 49.7 years; 75.7% male; MELD 29). Valid indirect calorimetry (Quark RMR) measurements were available for all 63 controls and for 66 and 68 patients in Groups II and III, respectively. Metabolic state was classified using the measured-to-predicted REE ratio (Harris-Benedict): hypometabolic (< 0.9), normometabolic (0.9-1.1), and hypermetabolic (> 1.1). Compared with Group I, RQ declined across Groups II and III (0.86, 0.80, 0.74; p=0.003), carbohydrate oxidation decreased (60.3%, 30.3%, 13.3%; p<0.001), and fat oxidation increased (27%, 59.8%, 72.7%; p<0.001), indicating progressive starvation, while REE remained comparable (1446, 1485, 1415 kcal/day; p=0.32). Hypometabolism was more prevalent in Group III than Groups I and II (45.6% vs. 22.2% and 30.3%; p=0.015). Group III had higher pro-inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP) and non-esterified fatty acid levels. Across Child-Pugh classes A, B, and C, RQ decreased (0.86, 0.79, 0.75) and fat oxidation increased (36.3%, 69%, 73%), with minimal changes in REE.
CONCLUSION: Liver cirrhosis is characterized by a progressive starvation phenotype without a significant increase in absolute energy expenditure. Critically ill patients with cirrhosis showed further reduction in carbohydrate utilization, without a significant increase in energy expenditure. These findings suggest that altered substrate utilization may be the predominant metabolic abnormality in cirrhosis, particularly during critical illness.

articles.title: Metabolomic signature of adiposity in preschool children: findings from the CORALS cohort.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity is increasingly recognized as a condition characterized by excess adiposity and early metabolic dysregulation. However, evidence on metabolomic alterations during the preschool years remains limited. This study aimed to characterize circulating metabolomic profiles associated with body mass index (BMI) and examine their relationships with body composition. This cross-sectional analysis included 1200 children aged 3-6 years from the Childhood Obesity Risk Assessment Longitudinal Study (CORALS), of whom 1110 had complete covariate data. Circulating metabolic biomarkers were quantified in EDTA plasma using proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) spectroscopy. Associations between BMI z-score (zBMI) and metabolites were assessed using multivariable linear regression with Bonferroni correction. Adjusted Spearman correlations were used to assess the relationships between metabolites and the z-scores for fat mass index (zFMI), fat-free mass index (zFFMI), and the waist-to-height ratio (zWtHR). Higher zBMI was associated with higher levels of branched-chain and aromatic amino acids, alanine and glycoprotein acetyls, and with lower levels of citrate and β-hydroxybutyrate. Children with a higher zBMI also had higher very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) concentrations and lower high-density lipoprotein (HDL) concentrations and particle size. These metabolic differences showed consistent patterns across body composition indicators, particularly zFMI. These findings indicate that metabolic differences associated with higher BMI are detectable during the preschool years and involve multiple metabolic pathways. Body composition analyses suggest that individual metabolic features may relate differently to fat mass, fat-free mass, and central adiposity. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine their temporal and clinical relevance.

articles.title: Central line-associated bloodstream infection in preterm infants with umbilical venous catheters versus peripherally inserted catheters.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) is a serious complication in preterm infants. Umbilical venous catheters (UVCs) are commonly used, but whether CLABSI risk differs from peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) remains unclear. We compared CLABSI incidence between UVCs and PICCs placed within 72 h after birth.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included preterm infants with gestational age <30 weeks and birth weight <1000 g admitted to Amsterdam UMC (2016-2024) who received a UVC or PICC. CLABSI episodes within the first seven catheter days were analyzed. Kaplan-Meier and logistic regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Among 545 infants (UVC 64%, PICC 36%), 63 CLABSI events occurred. CLABSI incidence was higher with UVC than PICC (14.6% vs 6.1%). UVC use was associated with increased odds of CLABSI (adjusted OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.54-5.93; p = 0.001). CLABSI-free dwell time was shorter in the UVC group (p < 0.01). Subgroup analyses suggested a stronger association in infants ≥26 weeks' gestation.
CONCLUSION: UVC use was associated with higher CLABSI incidence and shorter CLABSI-free dwell time than PICC use during the first seven catheter days. Primary PICC placement may therefore warrant consideration, particularly in infants born at ≥26 weeks' gestation.
IMPACT: UVC use was associated with higher CLABSI incidence and shorter CLABSI-free dwell time than PICC use during the first seven catheter days. This study provides direct comparative evidence on early CLABSI risk between UVCs and PICCs. Restricting catheter placement to the first 72 h and using an identical seven-day risk window improved comparability between catheter types. Differences in catheter timing, dwell time, and risk windows may explain inconsistent findings in previous studies. Primary PICC placement may reduce early CLABSI risk compared with UVC placement, although differences by gestational age warrant further study.

articles.title: The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth and cognition in middle childhood.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth, and cognition in childhood is unknown. This study aimed to characterize associations between (i) regional brain growth from birth to 6-8 years and socio-environmental factors; and (ii) regional brain growth and cognitive outcomes in middle childhood.
METHODS: One hundred and thirty-seven 6-8-year-old children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neonatal and paediatric brain MRI and a full-scale IQ assessment. Data on household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation, and early cognitively stimulating home environment were collected. Regional brain growth (extracerebral CSF, ventricles, cortical grey matter, white matter, deep grey matter, cerebellum, brainstem) from the neonatal period to 6-8 years was assessed using Gaussian process regression.
RESULTS: Low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth (B, 95% CI -1.14, -1.88 to -0.396; pFWE = 0.044) and extracerebral CSF expansion (-1.55, -2.51 to -0.585; pFWE = 0.042). Higher cortical grey matter (3.89, 1.12-6.65; pFWE = 0.038) and brainstem (3.24, 0.894-5.58; pFWE = 0.038) growth were associated with better full-scale IQ. Brainstem (p = 0.014), but not cortical grey matter (p = 0.177), remained significant after adjustment for socio-environmental factors.
CONCLUSIONS: Support for financially vulnerable families may promote brain growth. Brainstem growth is a brain correlate of childhood cognition independent of the effects of socio-environmental factors.
IMPACT: One hundred and thirty-seven children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neuroimaging at birth and at 6-8 years and a full-scale IQ assessment at 6-8 years. Household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation and early home environment data were collected. After adjustment for other socio-environmental factors and group, low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth and extracerebral CSF expansion. Higher cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with higher full-scale IQ in middle childhood. Household poverty was linked to reduced brain growth, while cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with cognitive abilities in childhood.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatrics.
articles.journal: Curr Probl Pediatr Adolesc Health Care
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is already part of pediatric practice, particularly for triage, early detection, documentation, and point-of-care decision support.
