Some currently available tools perform at an expert level, including bone age estimation and fracture detection. Ambient documentation is easing a persistent burden, and language models effectively draft notes and messages. However, the evidence for the technology in pediatrics lags behind adult medicine. Of the 876 AI and machine learning (ML) enabled devices currently authorized by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), only 149 carry labeling for patients younger than 18 years, and only 19% of those report validation in children. This review article examines where AI already exists in, or is approaching, everyday pediatric use. In each domain, the discussion pairs the strength of the technology with its present limitations. Notably, strong test set statistics do not always translate into better outcomes, and few pediatric tools have been validated externally or prospectively. The reasons for that gap are examined in depth: pediatric datasets are smaller and less representative, which leaves them more prone to bias, and a child's consent binds their data for longer than an adult's. In general, the argument is neither for swift adoption nor for resistance. Instead, it is for holding the technology to a high standard, which means keeping a human in the loop and training clinicians to be exacting judges of the currently available tools.

articles.title: Retention Across Developmental Stages: Insights from a Longitudinal Birth Cohort.
articles.abstract: Sustained participant retention is critical to the validity of longitudinal pediatric cohort studies yet remains an operational challenge-particularly in resource-limited settings. We evaluated retention patterns and contributing factors in the Urban Environment and Childhood Asthma (URECA) birth cohort, a multisite study that followed 609 children (49.0% female; 51.0% male) from birth through late adolescence (up to age 17) across four U.S. cities. Overall, 382 (62.7%) of participants completed final assessments at the last planned study visit. Attrition was highest during the first year of life and declined thereafter. Younger maternal age at delivery (<18 years (48% vs 64% for ≥ 18 years) and failure to complete an early-life home visit (44% vs 67% for completed) were significantly associated with lower retention, whereas most other maternal sociodemographic and psychosocial characteristics were not. Adolescent participant factors, including school enrollment, residential stability, anxiety, and depression, were similarly not associated with retention. High retention was sustained through adolescence and during COVID-19-related disruptions, alongside continuity in core study staff, strong and enduring participant-study relationships, flexible communication strategies, participant-centered engagement, and practices designed to reduce logistical barriers. These findings suggest that long-term retention in urban pediatric cohorts is associated with early engagement and the reported/perceived trust and reciprocal relationships over time. Relationship-centered, adaptive, and barrier-reducing approaches may be particularly relevant to supporting sustained participation across developmental transitions and external disruptions.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Insulin Dosing in Gestational Diabetes: A Simulation Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Gestational diabetes (GDM) is a major contributor to maternal and neonatal morbidity, healthcare costs and a growing healthcare burden for clinicians. Artificial intelligence (AI) applications are increasingly used in healthcare, but data are lacking on their use in GDM management.
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate the proof of concept of utilizing a large language model (LLM) clinical decision support tool (CDST) in GDM care we conducted a study with an objective to compare ChatGPT management of insulin dependent GDM to clinician management. Our primary hypothesis was that ChatGPT would suggest starting insulin at a higher dose than the clinicians. Our secondary hypothesis was that clinician-prescribed doses would converge with the initially recommended ChatGPT dose by the first visit occurring more than 2 weeks after insulin initiation.
STUDY DESIGN: In a retrospective cohort of patients with insulin-dependent GDM, we compared a model using ChatGPT as a simulated CDST to traditional clinician-prescribed insulin. Gestational age (GA), weight, and glucose values were entered into ChatGPT with a request to create an initial insulin regimen, and subsequent log values were entered with a request to alter the regimen as appropriate. The primary outcome was total daily insulin dose (TDD) and the exposure was regimen source (ChatGPT vs clinician). We compared TDD at the initial visit and the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation.
RESULTS: A total of 60 patients were included. The initial clinician TDD of insulin was 13.3 units lower than the ChatGPT recommendation (95% CI: 7.7-18.9, p < 0.001). At the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation, clinicians increased their prescribed TDD by an average of 11.1 units (95%CI: 7.4-14.4, p< 0.001). At this subsequent time point clinician prescribed TDD was similar to the initial ChatGPT prescription (mean: [ChatGPT-CP]: 2.2 units (95%CI: -3.2-7.7), p=0.42), and concurrent visit (mean [ChatGPT-CP]: 1.6 units (95%CI: -0.2-3.4), p=0.08).
CONCLUSION: Clinicians initiate insulin at lower doses than recommended by ChatGPT. However, 2-3 weeks after insulin initiation, recommended doses were similar. These findings suggest the feasibility of prospective studies assessing the use of an AI-CDST in GDM management. This approach may complement clinicians as a co-management tool and expand access to earlier medical intervention, particularly in areas with limited access to high-risk obstetricians.

articles.title: Early-Life Farm Exposure and Food Allergy.
articles.abstract: Food allergy has increased substantially, increasing interest in environmental exposures that may promote immune tolerance. The "farm effect," in which children raised in traditional farming environments have lower rates of allergic disease, may also extend to food allergy. This review summarizes epidemiologic and mechanistic evidence linking prenatal and early-life farm exposures with food allergy and related atopic outcomes. Protective associations likely reflect combined exposures to livestock, farm dust, environmental microbes, diet, and farm milk during critical developmental windows. Proposed mechanisms include altered gut microbiome maturation, microbial metabolites, reduced epithelial inflammation, innate immune programming, and enhanced regulatory T-cell responses. However, direct evidence for clinically confirmed food allergy remains limited compared with evidence for asthma and allergic sensitization. Future studies should identify specific microbial, metabolic, and immune pathways that mediate protection and determine whether safe, defined surrogates of farm exposure can be translated into food allergy prevention strategies.

articles.title: 2026 updated recommendations of the Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology for biologic therapy in moderate-to-severe psoriasis: Management of special populations, comorbidities, and treatment-related risks-Part 2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology regularly updates its recommendations for the management of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. The expanding availability of biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments, together with emerging evidence on their efficacy and safety, requires updated guidance for special populations, patients with comorbidities, and treatment-related risk management. This document provides evidence-informed recommendations to support individualized therapeutic decision-making.
METHODS: Recommendations were developed using the nominal group technique, supported by a scoping review of the literature. Two coordinators appointed a panel of GPS experts and defined the clinical questions and topics requiring revision. With the assistance of an information specialist, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 2025. Evidence was selected from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and high-quality real-world studies. Relevant national and international clinical practice guidelines and consensus documents were also reviewed. Previous recommendations were revised, and new recommendations were developed, evaluated by the expert panel, and refined through successive review rounds.
RESULTS: Updated recommendations address biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments for moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Management considerations include older adults, pediatric patients, pregnancy, breastfeeding, conception planning, poor treatment adherence, multiple treatment failures, and psoriasis affecting special anatomical sites. Recommendations also address treatment selection in patients with obesity, metabolic syndrome, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, depression, malignancy, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, neurologic disorders, lupus, and other autoimmune diseases. Treatment-related risk management encompasses pretreatment assessment, laboratory and clinical monitoring, vaccination, infection and latent tuberculosis screening, neurotoxicity, perioperative management, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation. Multidisciplinary care is emphasized throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: These updated recommendations provide an evidence-informed framework for individualized systemic treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis in special populations and patients with comorbidities. Treatment selection should integrate disease characteristics, comorbidities, patient preferences, available evidence, and treatment-specific safety considerations. Ongoing risk assessment, appropriate monitoring, and multidisciplinary collaboration are essential components of long-term psoriasis management.

articles.title: Using placental biomarkers to guide delivery in late preterm preeclampsia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In women with late preterm preeclampsia without severe features, the optimal timing of delivery remains uncertain. Earlier delivery may reduce progression to severe maternal disease, whereas expectant management may limit neonatal morbidity related to late preterm birth. Because conventional clinical criteria have limited ability to predict short-term deterioration, angiogenic biomarkers may provide additional risk stratification. A randomized clinical trial showed that biomarker-guided timing of delivery reduced progression to preeclampsia with severe features; however, its effectiveness in routine clinical practice has not been established.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether angiogenic biomarker-guided timing of delivery, when implemented in routine clinical practice, was associated with lower progression to preeclampsia with severe features and to compare short-term neonatal outcomes between study periods.
STUDY DESIGN: Before-after cohort study at the two principal recruiting centers of the previous trial, including singleton pregnancies with preeclampsia without severe features between 34+0 and 36+6 weeks. Women managed expectantly from 2014 to 2017 were compared with women managed according to angiogenic biomarkers from 2022 to 2025. Delivery was recommended for an abnormal angiogenic profile, defined according to the center-specific protocol as PlGF <60 pg/mL in Center 1 or an sFlt-1/PlGF ratio >110 in Center 2. The primary maternal outcome was progression to preeclampsia with severe features. The coprimary neonatal outcome was composite neonatal morbidity, including respiratory distress, hypoglycemia, jaundice, 5-minute Apgar score <7, umbilical arterial pH <7.00, or neonatal admission. Confounding was addressed with propensity-score weighting and multivariable regression.
RESULTS: Progression to preeclampsia with severe features decreased from 52.1% to 19.6%, an observed unadjusted absolute difference of 32.5 percentage points (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.22; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.13-0.38). Composite neonatal morbidity decreased from 57.0% to 45.6% (aOR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30-0.81); this difference was driven by fewer neonatal admissions, whereas neonatal morbidity excluding admission was nearly identical between periods (35.2% vs 35.6%). Gestational age at delivery did not differ significantly between the biomarker-guided and standard-care periods (36.7 vs 36.6 weeks; adjusted mean difference, 0.09 weeks; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.28).
CONCLUSION: Angiogenic biomarker-guided delivery timing was associated with lower progression to preeclampsia with severe features, without earlier delivery at the cohort level. No between-period difference was observed in short-term neonatal morbidity excluding neonatal admission; because the study was not designed or powered to establish neonatal noninferiority, clinically important differences in neonatal morbidity could not be excluded. By supporting earlier delivery in women with an abnormal biomarker profile and continued surveillance in those with a reassuring profile, angiogenic testing may help individualize delivery-timing decisions in late preterm preeclampsia without severe features.

articles.title: Chromosomal Amplification in Pediatric Tumors: Implications and Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract: Pediatric tumors often exhibit relatively low coding mutation burdens, and recurrent chromosomal amplifications are observed in specific tumor entities. These amplifications may contribute to influence tumor initiation, progression, and treatment response. For instance, amplification of the MYCN oncogene is a well-established marker of high-risk neuroblastoma and is associated with aggressive disease and poor outcomes. Advances in genomics and molecular biology have identified numerous chromosomal amplification events in pediatric tumors and provided insights into their underlying mechanisms. In this review, we first examine the molecular mechanisms driving chromosomal amplification. We then discuss the roles of chromosomal amplifications in pediatric tumorigenesis and summarize therapeutic approaches, including targeted inhibition, combination strategies, and experimental approaches to promote oncoprotein degradation. Throughout, we distinguish promising therapeutic concepts and preclinical findings from strategies with demonstrated clinical benefit. Further Integration of mechanistic studies, functional validation and biomarker-guided clinical trails may help advance precision therapy for pediatric tumors.

articles.title: MALDI-TOF MS and FT-IR spectroscopy for typing vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium: Comparison with PFGE in a hospital outbreak collection.
articles.abstract: Rapid and reliable strain typing is essential for investigating hospital outbreaks of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm). We evaluated MALDI-TOF MS and Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy as rapid typing approaches, and compared the resulting strain classifications with those obtained by pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE). Twenty-two VREfm isolates collected during a hospital outbreak investigation (November 2016-February 2017) were analyzed by MALDI-TOF MS and FT-IR spectroscopy; PFGE was performed for 18 isolates. Comparative analysis included 16 isolates with complete and interpretable results for all three methods. Concordance and discriminatory power were assessed using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Simpson's Index of Diversity (SID). MALDI-TOF MS identified six types among 21 classifiable isolates, FT-IR identified five clusters, and PFGE identified five major pulsotypes, with the predominant pulsotype A divided into closely related subtypes A1 and A2. In the 16-isolate comparative dataset, MALDI-TOF MS reproduced the PFGE subtype classification (ARI = 1.000; SID = 0.683), whereas FT-IR, using a dataset-specific cut-off of 0.154, grouped A1 and A2 together (ARI = 0.692; SID = 0.533). When A1 and A2 were considered variants of the same major pulsotype, FT-IR showed complete concordance with PFGE within this subset (ARI = 1.000). Epidemiological reconstruction supported a predominant Onco-Hematology cluster and a separate epidemiologically linked Neonatal cluster. MALDI-TOF MS reflected finer PFGE subtype-level differentiation, whereas FT-IR corresponded to the broader major-pulsotype structure. Both methods may have potential as preliminary typing approaches in VREfm outbreak investigations, but their results require epidemiological interpretation, while WGS remains preferable when high-resolution assessment of genomic relatedness is required.

articles.title: The role of parent-child relationship quality in socioeconomic inequalities in unintentional injuries and alcohol poisonings among adolescents: A Danish cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Low socioeconomic position is associated with unintentional injury in adolescents. We examined whether parent-child relationship quality mediates the association between low parental socioeconomic position (SEP), unintentional injuries, and alcohol poisonings.
METHODS: The Danish National Youth Cohort 2014 (15-19 years old) was linked to nationwide registers (n = 65,851). Outcomes were unintentional injuries and alcohol poisonings. Logistic regression assessed associations between parental SEP, parent-child relationship quality, and outcomes. Mediation analysis assessed if relationship quality accounted for socioeconomic differences in risk of harm.
RESULTS: Lower SEP associated with higher risk of unintentional injury and alcohol poisonings and dose-dependent associations were observed between lower SEP and lower parent-child relationship quality. For instance, the odds ratios (95% confidence interval) of low parental interest were 1.13 (95% CI 1.04,1.22), 1.40 (1.29,1.52), and 1.92 (1.64,2.24) for medium, short, and elementary education, respectively, compared with long education. Low relationship quality was in turn associated with higher odds of unintentional injury and alcohol poisoning. No statistically significant effect operated through the parent-child relationship pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings highlight the potential importance of socioeconomic hardship in shaping parent-child relationships and injury risk however more research is needed to elucidate underlying causal mechanisms.

articles.title: Social Media, Skin Appearance, and Adolescent Psychosexual Health: A Dermatologic Perspective.
articles.abstract: Adolescence is a period of intensive biologic and psychosocial development during which physical appearance becomes especially important for self-esteem, peer relationships, and identity formation. Social media increases the exposure of adolescents to idealized representations of appearance, including skin without acne, erythema, pigmentation, or scarring. This may be especially relevant for young people with visible dermatoses whose actual appearance differs from the digitally modified representations. This contribution discusses associations between social media use, body image, skin appearance, and adolescent psychosexual health, especially to acne, atopic dermatitis, and psoriasis. It considers the potential roles of social comparison, internalization of attractiveness standards, sexualization of appearance, and stress related to the evaluation of one's skin. Clinical implications are also addressed, including attempts to conceal lesions, unrealistic expectations of dermatological treatment and skin care, and the possibility of substantial appearance-related distress. Available evidence does not justify attributing these outcomes exclusively to social media; however, it supports taking the digital environment into account when assessing adolescents with visible skin diseases.

articles.title: Beauty Algorithms and AI Filters in Adolescent Body Image Disturbance: Dermatologic and Psychologic Consequences.
articles.abstract: Adolescence is a period of increased vulnerability to changes in body image, while visible skin features, including acne, pigmentation, and scarring, may have substantial social and psychologic significance. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based beauty filters enable simultaneous modification of skin texture and complexion and facial proportions, creating a digital representation that may differ substantially from actual appearance. This study examines the potential dermatologic and psychologic consequences of AI beauty filters in adolescents, with particular attention to discrepancies between actual and digitally modified appearance. The roles of social comparison, internalization of appearance ideals, self-objectification, and self-discrepancy in shaping body image are discussed. Current evidence suggests associations between appearance-focused social media activity, photo editing, and appearance dissatisfaction; however, evidence specifically concerning AI beauty filters remains limited and heterogeneous, with a substantial proportion of available studies involving adults. From a dermatologic perspective, AI filters may influence perceptions of acne, pigmentation, scarring, and skin texture and may shape expectations involving dermatologic treatment and aesthetic procedures. Additional longitudinal research of the adolescent population is needed to examine the relationships between repeated exposure to filtered representations of appearance, psychologic factors, and objectivel assessed skin status.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes of Long-Acting Beta-Agonist Add-On Therapy to Inhaled Corticosteroids in Preschool Children with Asthma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) add-on therapy to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in preschool children with asthma remains uncertain. Although ICS+LABA is an established step-up strategy, data in children younger than 6 years are limited.
RESEARCH QUESTION: In children ≤6 years with asthma, how were morbidity outcomes associated with ICS+LABA therapy compared with ICS alone, before and after LABA initiation?
STUDY DESIGN: and Methods: This retrospective comparative effectiveness study used the TriNetX research network, a multicenter electronic health record database. Children aged ≤6 years with asthma treated with ICS+LABA were compared with propensity-matched children treated with ICS alone (n≈12,100 per cohort). To account for treatment timing and the age-related effects on asthma severity and incidence, analyses were conducted using two index definitions: asthma diagnosis with LABA initiation within 12 months, and the time of LABA initiation itself. Outcomes included systemic corticosteroid exposure, bronchodilator use, ED visits/hospitalizations, pneumonia, fractures, and gastroenteritis.
RESULTS: When indexed at asthma diagnosis, ICS+LABA was associated with higher hazards of systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.32-1.43), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.36-1.46), and pneumonia (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.28-1.52) compared to ICS alone. When reindexed to LABA initiation, these associations were attenuated, but not eliminated: systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.09-1.18), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.13-1.21), and pneumonia (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.22). Direct comparison of the ICS+LABA cohort across index definitions showed lower rates of asthma-related outcomes after LABA initiation. Findings were similar in unmatched analyses, and in sensitivity analyses by younger age, later follow-up, Bayesian analysis and LABA type.
INTERPRETATION: In young children selected for ICS+LABA escalation, excess morbidity was greatest compared to ICS alone before LABA initiation and attenuated after LABA initiation. These findings may provide real-world evidence for ICS+LABA effectiveness in a selected group of preschool children with uncontrolled asthma and the basis for future prospective studies.

articles.title: Documenting Psychosocial Needs at the End of Life: Implementation of an Interdisciplinary Huddle to Foster Communication in Pediatric Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: - Psychosocial support is a core component of pediatric oncology palliative care (PPC), yet structured approaches for documenting and communicating psychosocial information across interdisciplinary teams remain inconsistent in pediatric cancer.
OBJECTIVE: - To describe the content documented within a structured interdisciplinary psychosocial huddle note and summarize lessons learned from its implementation within a hospital-based pediatric palliative care program for children with cancer.
METHODS: - This single-site retrospective decedent study included patients at a large pediatric cancer center with at least one documented end-of-life psychosocial huddle note between October 2023 and October 2025. The first huddle note for each patient was reviewed for documentation across nine psychosocial domains. Demographic, clinical, temporal, and interdisciplinary participation data were collected. For patients with multiple notes, changes in documentation over time were assessed.
RESULTS: - Forty-six patients with malignancy met inclusion criteria. The most frequently documented domains were social/spiritual support (84.8%), family/caregiver support (82.6%), and anticipatory grief (76.1%). Emotional distress (45.7%) and goals of care/decision-making (43.5%) were documented in nearly half. Notes reflected broad interdisciplinary participation, particularly from social work, child life, and spiritual care. Documentation patterns varied across demographic and clinical subgroups. Among 14 patients with multiple notes, all demonstrated changes in at least one psychosocial domain over time.
CONCLUSIONS: - Structured psychosocial huddle notes facilitated interdisciplinary communication and documentation of supportive care needs and revealed variability in documentation of decision-making processes. Standardized longitudinal documentation may strengthen communication, continuity, and goal-concordant end-of-life care in PPC for children with cancer.

articles.title: Treatment of vitiligo with narrowband ultraviolet B phototherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitiligo is an acquired immune depigmenting disorder. Narrowband 311 nm ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy is an important component of the standard treatment. Many questions arise about its safe use. The aim of the study was to clarify the use of NB-UVB in the management of vitiligo.
METHODS: A comprehensive review was coordinated by the French Society of Photodermatology, French vitiligo experts and the Centre of Evidence of the French Society of Dermatology to ascertain the efficacy and safety of NB-UVB used for vitiligo to draw up consensus guidelines.
RESULTS: The consulted experts defined NB-UVB phototherapy as a cornerstone treatment of vitiligo. They ensure its safety by establishing a dose protocol regarding treatment duration and subsequent monitoring. Given that most studies show that NB-UVB is not associated with an increased incidence of skin cancers, there is no ceiling on the maximum number of sessions allowed in adults with dark Fitzpatrick skin phototypes. In children and fair-skinned patients, additional data on the maximum number of sessions are needed before a recommendation can be made, even if the risk of cutaneous malignancy seems reduced in the population with vitiligo. For increased efficacy, NB-UVB combined with topical agents (calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids and ruxolitinib) and oral corticosteroids should be considered in localized vitiligo and active disease, respectively. A combination of NB-UVB with oral Janus kinase inhibitors seems promising.
CONCLUSION: There are now guidelines available to French dermatologists and practitioners for treating vitiligo with NB-UVB phototherapy.

articles.title: On the value of extending propranolol treatment for more than 6 months for infantile hemangioma: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infantile hemangiomas (IH) occur in approximately 4.5% of children, of whom 10% require treatment. The French and European guidelines recommend propranolol treatment for a minimum of 6 months; however, observational studies indicate that treatment is often extended beyond this duration in clinical practice.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the clinical relevance of continuing propranolol beyond 6 months.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study at Nancy Hospital, including infants treated with propranolol for ≥6 months between 2014 and April 2025. Patients were divided into a 6-month treatment group (6M group) and a prolonged treatment group (PT group, >6 months). IH regression was assessed by two blinded evaluators, with complete or near-complete regression defined as ≥80% reduction in IH volume.
RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included: 42 in the 6M group and 26 in the PT group (mean duration 9.7 ± 2.4 months). Deep or mixed IH were more frequent in the PT group (73% vs 43%). Complete or near-complete regression was observed in 34 patients (81%) in the 6M group and 20 patients (77%) in the PT group (p = 0.69). Severe adverse events were rare; one severe case of hypoglycemia occurred in the PT group. The relapse and re-treatment rates were not significantly different.
CONCLUSION: Extending propranolol beyond 6 months did not significantly improve IH regression, even in deeper lesions. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective design, small sample size, heterogeneous photographic assessment, and difficulty distinguishing treatment effects from natural involution. Prospective studies with larger cohorts are needed to identify IH subtypes that might benefit from longer therapy.

articles.title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Prenatal atrazine exposure and offspring neurodevelopment: Sex-specific effects, neurochemical pathways, and risk assessment using the TRAEC strategy.
articles.abstract: Atrazine (ATR) is a widely used herbicide detected in various environmental media, raising concerns about its potential neurodevelopmental toxicity. To systematically evaluate this risk, we employed the Targeted Risk Assessment of Environmental Chemicals (TRAEC) framework. However, epidemiological evidence regarding ATR exposure during pregnancy and its impact on offspring neurodevelopment remains limited. Here, we conducted a cohort study of 579 mother‑child pairs with urinary ATR determination in early and late pregnancy and neurodevelopmental assessments at 1-year-old using the Gesell Developmental Scale. Sex-dependent neurodevelopmental effects were identified, characterized by greater vulnerability in adaptive performance among girls and in gross motor among boys. Furthermore, we established a mouse model and exhibited sex‑dependent neurobehavioral deficits in offspring, including male motor impairment and female cognitive dysfunction. Histological and transcriptomic analyses further revealed region‑ and sex‑specific hippocampal neuronal alterations, with dopaminergic neuron loss in the DG region of males and GABAergic neuron elevation in the CA1 region of females. The primary neural stem cell cultures derived from E14.5 fetal mice demonstrated that ATR exposure impaired neurosphere formation and shifted neuronal subtype specification away from the dopaminergic lineage toward glutamatergic and GABAergic fates. By systematically integrating published studies and our results, the TRAEC‑based assessment for ATR yielded a composite evidence score of 8.69, classifying ATR as a high-risk developmental neurotoxicant. Overall, our study establishes a comprehensive framework for evaluating the neurodevelopmental toxicity of ATR exposure during pregnancy, elucidates the sex‑ and region‑specific neuronal mechanisms, and provides robust evidence for the high‑risk classification of ATR as a developmental neurotoxicant.

articles.title: Gestational co-exposure to PM2.5 and heat impaired cardiac development in offspring.
articles.abstract: Air pollution and extreme heat frequently co-occur, yet their combined effects on cardiac development following gestational exposure remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects and potential mechanisms of gestational co-exposure to PM2.5 and heat. Pregnant mice were exposed to filtered air, PM2.5 (10 μg/m3), heat (39 ℃), or both for 2 h/day from embryonic day 6.5 (E6.5) to E18.5, and offspring hearts were evaluated on postnatal day 1 (P1). Gestational co-exposure increased ventricular wall thickness and impaired systolic function, accompanied by inflammatory cell infiltration, oxidative damage, and mitochondrial ultrastructural changes. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that co-exposure altered pathways related to energy metabolism, including inositol phosphate metabolism and pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis. Further analysis of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) revealed that myo-inositol levels and Ucp2 expression were reduced after co-exposure. These changes are noteworthy because myo-inositol has been linked to congenital heart defect risk, while UCP2 contributes to neonatal cardiomyocyte metabolism. Experimental validation further showed that co-exposure decreased ATP content, downregulated cardiac development-related genes, and increased the protein expression of DRP1 and FIS1. Collectively, these findings suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to impaired cardiac development following gestational co-exposure, with reductions in myo-inositol levels and UCP2 expression potentially involved in this process. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic insights into the developmental cardiotoxicity of combined environmental exposures.

articles.title: Measuring school wellbeing in neurodivergent children: Exploring the suitability of a self-report measure with primary school children with Down syndrome.
articles.abstract: The current study examines the suitability of a self-report measure of school wellbeing for primary school-aged children with Down syndrome. The sample comprised 48 children with Down syndrome aged between 6 and 10.75 years (M = 8.4 years, SD = 1), of whom 43 had both parent-reported school wellbeing and teacher-reported classroom behaviour measures. Children and parents completed parallel versions of the How I Feel About My School (HIFAMS; Allen et al., 2018) measure of school wellbeing; classroom teachers completed the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (Goodman, 2001) and the Brief Early Skills and Support Index (Hughes et al., 2015). Properties of the child-reported HIFMAS were broadly similar to those for neurotypical children. Notably, however, both parent-reported school wellbeing and teacher-reported classroom behaviour showed limited association with child-reported school wellbeing, highlighting the need for further research to evaluate this measure's sensitivity to variation in the school experiences of children with Down Syndrome.

articles.title: MEK inhibitors in the management of NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas in children: experience from a reference center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is characterized by hyperactivation of the RAS pathway. MEKi, which inhibit downstream targets, have been shown to be effective in the treatment of symptomatic, unresectable plexiform neurofibromas (PN). We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-center study in the NF1 reference center of Marseille. Seven patients with NF1 treated with MEKi (MEK inhibitor), mainly selumetinib, were included. Pre-treatment evaluations, clinical presentation, treatment duration, and clinical and radiological efficacy and safety outcomes were collected.
RESULTS: The mean age at NF1 diagnosis was 3.5 years. PN most commonly manifested as pain (85.7%), signs of spinal cord compression (28.6%) were observed, presenting with gait disturbances, neurogenic pain, and/or radiological evidence of spinal cord involvement, respiratory disease (14.3%), and abdominal mass syndrome (14.3%). The mean delay before MEKi initiation was 6.4 years. Selumetinib was administered to all patients (five first-line, two after trametinib). All patients who initially reported pain experienced clinical pain relief by the first month, and in four, tumor bulk decreased palpably. On imaging, treatment with selumetinib resulted in tumor reduction in two patients and disease stabilization in five. Side effects were mostly cutaneous, gastrointestinal, and muscular. Mean follow-up on selumetinib was 18 months (8-24).
CONCLUSION: Selumetinib was effective clinically and radiologically with an overall acceptable safety profile. However, longer-term prospective studies are needed to confirm sustained response, establish therapeutic indications, and optimize management of complex NF1 cases.

articles.title: ﻿Long-Term Efficacy and Tolerability of a Dermocosmetic Regimen in Mild-to-Moderate Facial and Truncal Acne: A 6-Month Clinical Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acne remains the most common inflammatory skin condition globally, with an increasing prevalence among adolescents and adults. Expert recommendations and clinical research indicate that dermocosmetic products can play an important role in the management of acne. The objective of this open-label, non randomized, single-center study conducted in Brazil was to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of an anti-acne dermocosmetic regimen combining a foaming cleansing gel, a multi-targeted cream, and a sunscreen for 6 months in subjects with mild-to-moderate acne on the face and trunk (chest and back).
METHODS: The investigation included 51 subjects (32 females and 19 males; mean age: 24 years). Subjects washed their face and trunk with the foaming cleansing gel and applied the dermocosmetic cream twice daily to the face and trunk, along with sunscreen at least once daily. The study included multi-zones (face and trunk) assessments, evaluation of clinical efficacy (inflammatory and non inflammatory lesions, acne-induced erythema [AIE], acne-induced hyperpigmentation [AIH]), objective skin barrier measurements, quality of life and stigmatization analysis, assessment of cutaneous tolerability, evaluation of cosmeticity/satisfaction with the cleanser and cream, and photography before/after treatment.
RESULTS: Multi-zone analysis of the combination dermocosmetic regimen demonstrated that the treatment led to improvement of acne on the face and trunk. The dermocosmetic regimen was linked to reductions in the number of inflammatory and non inflammatory acne lesions on the face and trunk. The AIE and AIH were statistically significantly improved on the back after 6 months. The regimen did not disrupt the skin barrier integrity. The stigmatization and skin discomforts associated with acne were significantly reduced. The subjects reported overall satisfaction regarding the efficacy and cosmetic properties of the regimen.
CONCLUSIONS: The use of a specific anti-acne dermocosmetic regimen was associated with improvement of mild-to-moderate facial and truncal acne.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06463925.

articles.title: Improving Assessment Practices With Autistic Girls: Views and Experiences of Psychologists in the Republic of Ireland.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The role of sex and gender warrants careful consideration in autism identification. Studies focusing on prevalence rates consistently report higher numbers of autistic boys compared to autistic girls, and there is increasing awareness autistic girls may be under-identified within the general population. Different reasons have been cited, including issues with assessment practices and behavioural differences between autistic girls and autistic boys.
METHODS: In attempting to understand and improve assessment practices with autistic girls, 91 psychologists working in publicly funded services in the Republic of Ireland involved in autism assessments with children completed a survey focused on their autism assessment experiences, with an emphasis on autistic girls. Survey questions were designed to gather quantitative and qualitative data, with descriptive statistics and content analysis used to provide an overview of participants' responses.
RESULTS: Psychologists reported gender-related differences in autism assessments, highlighting diverse expressions of autistic differences and different referral reasons. Specific gender-based assessment practices were noted, resulting in lengthier assessments with autistic girls. Most psychologists engaged in 'upgrading' (autism identified in cases where presentations are less clear and/or where individuals do not meet thresholds on standard diagnostic tools (Rogers et al., 2016), with nearly half reporting that it happens more frequently with autistic girls compared to autistic boys.
CONCLUSION: Further research is needed to explore the role of clinical judgement in autism assessment and identification, as well as parental and autistic girls' experiences of assessments. From a practice-based perspective universities offering psychology professional training need to develop curricula of learning in autism assessment and identification to include experiences of autistic females.

articles.title: Strengthening Rural Prevention Networks Through Government-University-Community Partnerships: Evidence from a Demonstration of a Community-Based System of Family Support for Preventing Child Welfare System Involvement.
articles.abstract: This study examines a five-year primary prevention demonstration project designed to reduce child maltreatment and family separation in an eight-county rural Midwestern U.S. region through a government-university-community partnership. By introducing four community-led capacity building strategies across the region, The Family Strong Community Collaborative sought to strengthen local family support systems and prevent the unnecessary use of foster care when child safety was not an immediate concern. Reflective inquiry revealed key organizational drivers and contextual factors for forming partnerships that provide a conceptual framework for future work. Evidence revealed that implementation drivers promoted successful collaboration and contributed to changes in the local prevention service network. Specifically, social network analyses of the local prevention service provider network revealed steady growth over time and emergence of new core members, suggesting increased capacity for coordinated service access and support. Findings suggest that systematic cross-sector collaboration supported by organizational, competency, and leadership drivers, can strengthen collaborative infrastructure and support the development of interconnected community prevention networks. While preliminary and noncausal, these findings offer a promising model for collaborative rural prevention networks and highlight strategies for building strong government-university-community partnerships that support long-term system improvement.

articles.title: Quick Parenting Assessment (QPA) Screening Tool: Helping Health Care Providers Identify Parenting Needs and Prevent Child Abuse.
articles.abstract: Harsh parenting (e.g., spanking, yelling) can negatively affect children's physical and mental health and development. The Quick Parenting Assessment (QPA) is a brief screening tool designed to facilitate provider-parent discussions about, and identification of, harsh parenting behaviors. The QPA assesses prior month use (yes/no) of seven types of child discipline behaviors: five punitive (spanking, yelling, threatening, shaming, and time-out) and two positive (redirecting and setting expectations). This study assessed the QPA's psychometric properties and clinically meaningful scoring. Participants were female primary caregivers (N = 333) recruited from WIC clinics in the greater New Orleans, Louisiana area, with an index child mean age of 8 years (SD = 1.3). Validity, reliability, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were conducted. Construct validity was assessed using parenting measures including the Attitudes Toward Spanking scale (ATS), use of spanking, and the Parenting and Family Adjustment Scale (PAFAS), which included both coercive and positive parenting practices. Criterion validity was assessed using child behavior measures including the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) and the Child Adjustment and Parent Efficacy Scale (CAPES). ROC analyses used a CBCL score > 60, an accepted cutoff for identifying clinical risk. The QPA showed acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.71) and modest test-retest reliability (r = 0.67). Strong construct validity was demonstrated with higher QPA scores correlated with higher use of spanking (r =  .53, p <  .001), coercive parenting (r = 0.50, p <  .001), and support for spanking (r = 0.43, p <  .001), and less use of positive parenting strategies (r =  - 0.41, p <  .001). Criterion validity was also supported as higher QPA scores were correlated with more child behavioral problems (r = 0.20 to 0.27, all ps <  .01). QPA item-level correlations with parenting and child measures were strongest and most highly significant for spanking, yelling, and threatening. ROC analyses indicated that a QPA (two-caregiver version) score greater than 4 yielded sensitivity of .60, and a QPA (single-caregiver version) score greater than 3 yielded sensitivity of .70. Sensitivity improved (.88-.89) when flags were based on these cutoff scores or endorsement of any one of these items: spanking, yelling, and threatening. These findings both affirm and expand knowledge of the QPA's psychometric strengths and provide more nuanced guidance for child health and family service professionals using this screening tool for both primary and secondary prevention of child abuse, thereby improving child health outcomes.

articles.title: Risk factors and clinical phenotype stratification of secondary and drug-resistant epilepsy in children with gray matter heterotopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gray matter heterotopia (GMH) is a congenital brain malformation caused by abnormal neuronal migration, and children with GMH are at risk of secondary epilepsy and drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). We aim to investigate risk factors for secondary and DRE in children with GMH for early risk identification and management.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled children with GMH diagnosed using magnetic resonance imaging at Chongqing Medical University Children's Hospital (from Sept 2012 to Sept 2025). Kaplan-Meier analysis, Firth-corrected Cox regression, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox (LASSO-Cox) analysis  were used to identify risk factors for secondary epilepsy. Firth-LASSO logistic regression was used to assess risk factors of DRE. K-mode clustering was used to define phenotypic subgroups based on pre-epilepsy baseline variables.
RESULTS: A total of 219 children with GMH were enrolled in this study. Periventricular nodular heterotopia was the most common type of GMH (82.19%). The main clinical manifestations included epileptic seizures (43.38%), intellectual disability (ID) (38.81%), and global developmental delay (GDD) (33.33%). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that ID (P < 0.001), GDD (P < 0.001), multiple brain abnormalities, and patent foramen ovale (PFO) (P = 0.006) were linked to shorter seizure-free survival. Multivariate Firth-corrected Cox regression identified ID [hazard ratio (HR) = 2.606, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) = 1.375-4.864, P = 0.003], GDD (HR = 3.068, 95% CI 1.625-5.912, P < 0.001), lissencephaly-pachygyria spectrum (HR = 1.835, 95% CI 1.046-3.139, P = 0.035), and PFO (HR = 4.002, 95% CI 1.659-8.433, P = 0.003) as being statistically associated with secondary epilepsy. Exploratory mediation analysis demonstrated that multiple structural abnormalities were significantly associated with both ID and epilepsy. Furthermore, subcortical band heterotopia [odds ratio (OR) = 6.229, 95% CI 1.596-25.797, P = 0.008] and moderate-to-severe ID (OR = 6.114, 95% CI 2.136-20.855, P < 0.001) were statistically associated with secondary DRE. Cluster analysis stratified patients into high-risk (n = 78) and low-risk (n = 141) subgroups. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance revealed significant differences in characteristics between the two groups (F = 40.494, R2 = 0.157, P = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Developmental impairment, lissencephaly-pachygyria spectrum, and SBH were associated with higher risks of epilepsy and DRE. In addition, an exploratory phenotype stratification into high and low risk of secondary epilepsy based on clinical and imaging features is proposed. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings and advance precision care for children with GMH.

articles.title: Clinical, Genetic, MR Spectroscopy characteristics and Response to Flunarizine in Episodic Ataxia Type 2: The Sheffield Ataxia Cohort.
articles.abstract: Episodic ataxia type 2 (EA2) is an autosomal-dominant calcium channelopathy caused by pathogenic mutations in the CACNA1A gene, characterized by episodic cerebellar symptoms and marked phenotypic heterogeneity. Data on real-world clinical features and treatment responses, particularly in the era of major genetic advances, remain limited. This is a retrospective observational single-centre case series of 58 individuals from 38 families with genetically confirmed EA2. Clinical, demographic, genetic, and treatment data were extracted from medical records using a standardized Excel-based data collection tool. Symptom patterns with associated neurological features, genetic characteristics, and treatment responses were analyzed descriptively. Paired MRI imaging including MR spectroscopy (MRS) of the cerebellum at baseline and follow up data, and medication efficacy were assessed using patient-reported benefit, and statistical analysis was performed using Wilcoxon signed rank test and Exact binomial testing respectively. The mean age at diagnosis was 35.2 ± 21.5 years, and a positive family history was identified in 48 patients (82.70%). The most frequent clinical manifestations were gait instability (87.93%), dysarthria (39.66%), headache (58.62%) and isolated dizziness (48.28%). Episodic symptoms predominated, with 33 patients (56.89%) experiencing discrete attacks. Amongst those with episodic symptoms, weekly attacks were the most common (42.4%), while 17 patients (29.31%) exhibited a non-episodic course with persistent symptoms. Interictal oculomotor abnormalities, including nystagmus, were noted in some individuals. Paired longitudinal MRS analyses for both vermis (W = 118.0, p = 0.67) and hemisphere (W = 122.0, p = 0.39) revealed no significant change over time. Flunarizine showed the highest rate of therapeutic benefit, with 76.5% of treated patients reporting improvement (p = 0.04), whereas other treatments demonstrated variable but non-significant effects. This study highlights the clinical heterogeneity and neuroimaging (MRS) insight of EA2 underscoring the predominance of episodic manifestations, while also recognizing a subset with non-episodic symptoms. Flunarizine appears to be an effective, accessible therapeutic option for reducing attack frequency and duration in EA2, though further studies are required to compare efficacy with alternative therapeutic options such as acetazolamide.

articles.title: Phenotype-guided multiplex molecular profiling in children with food-associated anaphylaxis of unknown trigger.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Identifying the culprit allergen remains challenging in some children with food-associated anaphylaxis despite comprehensive routine evaluation. This study evaluated the clinical contribution of phenotype-guided interpretation of multiplex molecular allergen profiling in children whose reactions remained unexplained after conventional assessment. This retrospective study included children aged 1-18 years evaluated at a national tertiary pediatric allergy center between January 2020 and January 2026. ALEX2 profiles were interpreted alongside exposure history, reaction phenotype, cofactors, conventional allergy investigations, and clinical follow-up. Diagnostic certainty was categorized as confirmed, probable, possible, or unresolved. Among 1640 food-associated anaphylactic episodes, 53 episodes in 33 children remained unexplained after routine evaluation. ALEX2 testing was performed in 30 children, representing 49 episodes. Overall, 26/30 children (86.7%) received a molecularly supported clinical classification: 7 confirmed, 10 probable, and 9 possible; four remained unresolved. Seven classifications were challenge-confirmed, including six nsLTP-associated phenotypes confirmed by supervised food-exercise challenge and one poppy seed allergy confirmed by oral food challenge. The most frequent phenotype was nsLTP-associated food allergy (11/30, 36.7%), accounting for 22 episodes. Other classifications included oral mite anaphylaxis, shrimp allergy, Alternaria-associated food allergy, wheat-dependent exercise-induced anaphylaxis, serum albumin-associated food allergy, and profilin-associated food allergy.
CONCLUSION: Phenotype-guided interpretation of multiplex molecular allergen profiles supported clinically meaningful classification in most children with unexplained food-associated anaphylaxis. Molecular diagnostics should be used to generate clinically testable hypotheses and guide targeted confirmation rather than to establish causality from sensitization alone.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Conventional allergy testing may fail to identify the trigger in a small subset of children with food-associated anaphylaxis. • Multiplex molecular testing can detect sensitizations not captured by routine diagnostic evaluation.
WHAT IS NEW: • Phenotype-guided molecular profiling identified clinically relevant patterns, particularly nsLTP and oral mite anaphylaxis, in children with previously unexplained food-associated anaphylaxis. • Challenge-confirmed cases demonstrate that molecular findings are most informative when interpreted alongside clinical phenotype and cofactors.

articles.title: The Association Between Parent-Reported ADHD-Related Symptoms and English Word Reading in Syrian Refugee Children.
articles.abstract: The purpose of the present study was to examine child-level and family-level factors associated with English word reading in a sample of 133 Syrian refugee children aged 6-13 years resettled in Canada, 35% of whom had resided in refugee camps before resettlement. Using multilevel modeling to account for children nested within families, we examined whether parent-reported ADHD-related symptoms were associated with English word reading after accounting for age, nonverbal reasoning, receptive vocabulary, and phonological awareness, and whether time spent in refugee camps was associated with word reading at the family level. Parent-reported ADHD-related symptoms were assessed using the Hyperactivity/Inattention subscale of the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), a behavioral screening instrument rather than a diagnostic assessment of ADHD. Findings indicated that older age and stronger phonological awareness were associated with higher English word reading scores, while parent-reported ADHD-related symptom scores were associated with lower word reading performance after accounting for the other predictors. In contrast, time spent in refugee camps was not significantly associated with English word reading. These findings highlight the importance of considering attentional and behavioral functioning alongside established cognitive and linguistic correlates when examining English literacy development among Syrian refugee children following resettlement.

articles.title: Maternal and paternal adverse childhood experiences and parent-child disconnectedness in later life.
articles.abstract: Childhood is a sensitive life stage during which significant adversity can set in motion chains of disadvantage in social relationships across the life course. Thus, older parents' adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) may shape the quality of their relationships with adult children. Although rates of disconnectedness tend to be higher for fathers, prior research primarily focused on mothers, overlooking potential gender differences. Using data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE; N = 38,900), we run logistic regressions to examine how both mothers' and fathers' ACEs (physical abuse, emotional neglect, parental absence, poverty, and peer isolation) relate to parent-child disconnectedness, defined as having no contact with at least one child. Each of the five parental ACEs is associated with a higher likelihood of parent-child disconnectedness in later life, with cumulative effects across ACEs. Patterns are highly similar for mothers and fathers, suggesting that the mechanisms linking parental ACEs to adult intergenerational relationship quality are largely gender neutral. Our findings highlight how early adversity reverberates across generations, shaping the parent-child bond well into later life in similar ways for mothers and fathers. This underscores the need for policies that protect children from ACEs and mitigate their long-term consequences.

articles.title: Evolution of bilirubin detection: analytical strategies, sensing platforms, and translational opportunities.
articles.abstract: Liver diseases, including fatty liver disease, viral hepatitis, cirrhosis, and cholestatic disorders, leading to hyperbilirubinemia contribute substantially to the global burden of morbidity and mortality. It is also a major clinical concern in neonates, with neonatal jaundice occurring in approximately 60% of term and 80% of preterm newborns during the first week after birth. Over the past decades, bilirubin detection has evolved from conventional laboratory-based methods to advanced sensing technologies designed for rapid, sensitive, and decentralized analysis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of bilirubin sensing, with emphasis on well-established electrochemical and optical sensing to integrated paper-based, smartphone-assisted, and wearable sensor technologies. Recent advances in functional materials, miniaturized sensors, digital analysis, and integrated sensing platforms have expanded the potential for portable bilirubin testing across diverse diagnostic and monitoring settings. These advances hold promise for applications in point-of-care (POC) testing, resource-limited settings, and neonatal care units, where timely and accessible bilirubin assessment is essential for informed clinical decision-making. Established bilirubin-sensing techniques and emerging technologies are critically evaluated to highlight novel approaches, compare analytical performance, and assess translational potential. Alternative sample matrices, which offer considerable potential for diverse applications, are also evaluated to distinguish exploratory demonstrations from clinically validated applications. Furthermore, matrix effects, sensor drift, storage stability, reproducibility, and variations across devices and fabrication batches are critically examined in relation to their implications for measurement reliability and clinical applicability. By integrating advances in sensing mechanisms, functional materials, and device architectures, the discussion provides a foundation for understanding bilirubin-sensing principles, critically evaluating reported approaches, and addressing existing challenges, while offering insights into sensor design and technology selection and identifying key priorities for developing reliable, accessible, and clinically translatable bilirubin-sensing platforms.

articles.title: Theory of mind, autism-like traits, executive functions, and structural brain MRI findings in children with neurofibromatosis type 1.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aimed to examine social-cognitive difficulties in children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) by jointly investigating theory of mind (ToM), executive functions, and autism-like traits and to explore whether children with NF1 show structural differences in brain regions commonly implicated in social cognition and executive functioning. In this two-center cross-sectional study, 41 children aged 8-18 years were included, comprising 21 children with NF1 and 20 age- and sex-matched typically developing children. Participants underwent behavioral assessment, including parent-reported autism-like traits, everyday executive functioning, and direct measures of ToM. Structural brain MRI data were analyzed using automated volumetric and cortical thickness measures, focusing on these regions. Children with NF1 showed higher autism-like traits, lower everyday executive functioning in play and social routines, and poorer performance on an advanced ToM task. The NF1 group also had larger global brain volume reflecting widespread white matter expansion; lower cortical gray matter proportion and thickness in frontal, temporal, parietal, cingulate, and limbic regions; and larger subcortical structures including the amygdala, hippocampus, and thalamus. Exploratory within-group brain-behavior correlations were few and selective, none survived multiple-comparison correction, and none involved autism-like traits.
CONCLUSION: Children with NF1 display a multidimensional profile of social-cognitive difficulties together with structural differences indicating an imbalance between cortical and subcortical regions typically involved in social cognition. These structural differences offer a possible neurobiological substrate for the social-cognitive difficulties observed in NF1. Whether they account for these difficulties remains to be tested in samples powered to examine brain-behavior associations directly.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) frequently show executive dysfunction, autism-like traits, and theory of mind (ToM) difficulties. • These domains have rarely been examined jointly, or alongside brain structure, in the same children.
WHAT IS NEW: • Autism-like traits, everyday executive difficulties, and poorer ToM co-occurred in children with NF1. • The same children showed reduced cortical thickness and proportion with enlarged subcortical structures in regions implicated in social cognition, a candidate substrate for future brain-behavior studies.

articles.title: T​he use of biosynthetic mesh in complex abdominal wall reconstruction - a single‑center experience.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Abdominal wall reconstruction in patients presenting with enteric fistulas and mesh infection is challenging. Synthetic mesh should be avoided in contaminated fields and to be used in selected cases. Alternative strategies include primary fascial closure with or without component separation, biologic mesh, and resorbable biosynthetic mesh. Our study aims to evaluate the use of long-term absorbable mesh in a single-stage procedure, focusing on postoperative complications and hernia recurrence rates.
METHODS: A retrospective single-arm study was conducted following Institutional Review Board approval. All incisional hernia repairs using bio-absorbable Poly-4-Hydroxybutyrate mesh were performed at our medical center between January 2017 and March 2025 were included. Adult and pediatric patients with Ventral Hernia Working Group (VHWG) grade III and IV wounds were eligible.
RESULTS: Thirty-four patients met the inclusion criteria. The mean age was 58.7 ± 17.1 years, and the mean body mass index was 30.4 ± 7.6 kg/m². Comorbidity burden was high: 52.9% had a Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and 35.3% had an ASA score ≥ 3. Most patients (82.3%) presented with infected mesh. Mean operative time was 188.5 ± 75 min, and bowel resection was required in 18 cases. Postoperative wound infection occurred in 10 patients. Follow‑up data were available for 28 of the 34 patients with median follow-up duration of 20.5 months. A single death occurred, hernia recurrence was observed in four cases (16%), all managed with reoperation. Quality-of-life assessments demonstrated a clear postoperative improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: In this high-risk, contaminated and infected cohort, P4HB mesh demonstrated acceptable recurrence and complication rates. Its long-term resorbable properties provides a feasible alternative to use in incisional hernia repair with infected meshes.

articles.title: Symptom burden and support needs of children with cancer at home: A creative qualitative study during treatment and end of life.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Children with cancer experience distressing symptoms at home, but research on their experiences and needs is scarce. To inform the development of a new home-based symptom app, we aimed to gain insight into the symptoms, symptom bother, and experiences and needs of children and their families during treatment and end of life.
METHODS: A qualitative study design was applied. We conducted 11 generative interviews supported with LEGO® as engaging method to help participants visualize and talk about their experiences. Participants were five children (≥ 8 years) and ten parents of children (≥ 0 years) undergoing cancer treatment or receiving palliative care. End-of-life symptom experiences and needs were explored in a focus group with seven bereaved parents. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the data of interviews and focus group separately.
RESULTS: Participants reported a wide range of symptoms. The most bothersome physical and psychological symptoms reported in the interviews were nausea and feeling scared or worried. Bereaved parents identified nausea, fatigue, pain, and behavioral changes as the most bothersome symptoms during the last phase of life. Children and parents faced uncertainty in determining the cause and severity of symptoms, as well as how to manage them at home. They emphasized the need for clear guidance on when to seek medical support. Over time, children and parents became experts in managing symptoms. Bereaved parents highlighted the intense symptom burden in their child's final weeks and stressed the importance of swift and effective communication with healthcare professionals. Despite facing severe symptoms and the approaching end of life, families remained focused on making the most of each moment.
CONCLUSIONS: Families require clear guidance on recognizing and managing symptoms at home across the entire care continuum. Especially in the last phase of life, rapid communication between parents and healthcare professionals is crucial to alleviate distress and maximize comfort.

articles.title: Outpatient Referral After Adolescent Sexual Health Emergency Department Visits Improves Follow-Up.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate which methods of outpatient referral during pediatric emergency department (ED) visits for sexual health are associated with increased follow-up among adolescents otherwise at risk of being lost to care.
METHODS: A single-institution retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients 14-20 years-old who underwent testing for any sexually transmitted infection during ED visits between 1/1/2018 and 12/31/2018 and were discharged home, excluding pregnant patients or those presenting following sexual assault. The primary outcome was any follow-up within 6 months of the index ED visit. The primary independent variable was referral at discharge. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations.
RESULTS: Among 1,152 patients (median age 17 years; 76% female), 73% received a referral, and 36.5% were seen in follow-up within 6 months of the index visit. Referrals specifying time frame for follow-up were associated with increased follow-up (odds ratio [OR] 5.9, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.2-8.4), whereas "as needed" referrals were not. In multivariable modeling, attending a follow-up visit was associated with referral (adjusted OR [AOR] 3.6, 95% CI 2.5-5.2), female sex (2.74, 95% CI: 1.90-3.95), and prior preventive care (4.42, 95% CI: 3.36-5.81). Although associated with having follow-up visits, referrals were not associated with contraception initiation or decreased return to the ED within 6 months of the index visit.
DISCUSSION: Referral to outpatient care was associated with increased follow-up among adolescents with sexual health needs, particularly when referrals specified a follow-up time frame. Pediatric EDs should standardize discharge processes to include specific and consistent outpatient referrals.

articles.title: Suppurative Mediastinal Tuberculous Lymphadenopathy Leading to Airway Compression in Children: Report of two cases.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lymphobronchial tuberculosis (TB) is the most common manifestation of intrathoracic TB in children and frequently causes airway compression, particularly in young infants. Although anti-TB therapy and corticosteroids remain the cornerstone of management, severe airway obstruction may require surgical intervention. We report two paediatric cases of drug-resistant pulmonary TB with progressive airway compression caused by suppurative mediastinal lymphadenopathy requiring thoracotomy and surgical decompression.
CASE PRESENTATIONS: A 4-month-old HIV-exposed infant and a 10-month-old HIV-negative infant with drug-resistant TB developed severe compression of the bronchus intermedius and left main bronchus despite anti-TB therapy and corticosteroids. CT scans demonstrated extensive mediastinal lymphadenopathy with central necrosis/liquefaction, while bronchoscopy confirmed progressive airway obstruction. In Case 1, serial CT volumetric assessment demonstrated an increase in mediastinal lymph node volume from 8.3 cm³ to 19.3 cm³, correlating with worsening airway compression. Both children underwent right thoracotomy, during which large subcarinal and right paratracheal nodal abscesses containing copious pus were drained. Intraoperative bronchoscopy showed immediate improvement in airway patency, and histology demonstrated necrotising granulomatous inflammation.
CONCLUSION: These cases demonstrate progression of mediastinal tuberculous lymphadenitis to suppurative abscess formation with life-threatening airway compression. CT was essential in identifying abscess-like lymph nodes, while volumetric assessment objectively documented disease progression and supported surgical decision-making. Surgical decompression resulted in rapid airway improvement. These are the first reported cases using CT volumetric assessment of mediastinal lymph nodes to monitor progression of airway compression. Further studies are needed to determine the role of volumetric imaging in guiding intervention in children with severe mediastinal TB.

articles.title: The Varying Benefits of Two Years Automated Insulin Delivery System Use on Continuous Glucose Monitoring Profiles in Children and Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems are recommended for youths with type 1 diabetes, but real-world longitudinal data remains limited despite increasing use. This study evaluates the effect of 2 years of AID use on continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) profiles and body mass index (BMI) development.
METHODS: Data from individuals with type 1 diabetes aged <18 years, diabetes duration >3 months, and AID use of >3 months from the Diabetes Prospective Follow-up (DPV) Registry between 2019 and 2025 were analyzed. CGM and HbA1c were required at the last documented time in range (TIR) (±90 days; follow-up) and 2 years earlier (±90 days; baseline). Changes were investigated using adjusted regression models with repeated measurements.
FINDINGS: Data from 2486 participants (baseline: median age: 11.9 years, diabetes duration: 5.0 years, 53% male) were analyzed over ∼23 months. The largest gains occurred in time in tight range (TiTR) (42.4% [95% confidence interval: 41.0-43.7] to 50.1% [48.8-51.4]; P < 0.001) and coefficient of variation (CV) (32.9 [32.0-33.7] to 29.5 [28.7-30.2]; P < 0.001). HbA1c (7.3% [7.2-7.3] to 7.2 [7.1-7.2]; P < 0.001), TIR (64.5% [63.9-65.1] to 66.7% [66.1-67.3]; P < 0.001), and mean sensor glucose (SG) (161.0 mg/dL [158.4-163.5] to 155.5 mg/dL [153.1-157.9]; P = 0.001) improved statistically, but below clinical relevance thresholds. Time below range (TBR) < 70 mg/dL increased (2.7% [2.6-2.9] to 3.2% [3.1-3.4]; P < 0.001), TBR < 54 mg/dL remained stable (1.7%-1.8%; P = 0.516), and severe hypoglycemia decreased (6.4-4.5/100 patient-years; P < 0.001). No changes were seen in children <6 years. In youth 6 to <12 and 12 to <18 years, TiTR and CV improved most, while TBR increased. BMI-standard deviation score (SDS) increased (0.57 [0.53-0.61] to 0.67 [0.63-0.72]; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: After 2 years of AID use, TiTR and CV showed clinically relevant improvements, while TBR < 70 mg/dL increased with stable TBR < 54 mg/dL and severe hypoglycemia decreased. Changes in TIR, SG, and HbA1c were statistically significant but small, yet noteworthy, as glycemia usually deteriorates during adolescence. The increase in BMI-SDS needs to be further investigated.

articles.title: Pediatric Acute Myeloid Leukemia Treatment Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study on Prognostic Factors and Survival in a Low- to Middle-Income Country.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) outcomes remain substantially lower in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where treatment-related mortality (TRM), treatment abandonment, and limited access to risk-adapted therapy and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remain important challenges. We evaluated contemporary outcomes and factors influencing survival in children with AML treated at a tertiary center in Pakistan.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients aged <18 years diagnosed with AML between 2011 and 2023. Patients in main AML cohort were compared between an early era (2011-2016) and a later era (2017-2023), following institutional availability of HSCT. Overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS), and relapse-free survival (RFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Cumulative incidences of relapse and TRM were estimated using competing-risk analysis. Acute myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome (AML-DS) and Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) were analyzed separately.
RESULTS: Among 143 patients in the main AML cohort, 114 (80%) initiated therapy and 69 (60%) achieved complete remission. Induction mortality was 16%, while TRM occurred in 27% of treated patients, predominantly due to sepsis. Three-year OS, EFS, and RFS were 35%, 17%, and 38%, respectively. Survival did not differ significantly between the early and later eras (3-year OS, 37% vs. 32%, p=0.70; EFS, 20% vs. 15%, p=0.35). The 3-year cumulative incidences of relapse and TRM were 51% and 26%, respectively, with no significant differences between eras. Thirty patients relapsed; 12 received salvage therapy, of whom nine achieved a second remission. Treatment abandonment occurred throughout the treatment course, including in 16% before therapy initiation. Intermediate- and high-risk disease and higher presenting white blood cell count were associated with increased mortality on multivariable analysis. Twelve patients underwent HSCT, all in the later era. Three-year OS was 78% in AML-DS and 75% in APL.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric AML outcomes remained limited by the combined effects of TRM, relapse, and treatment abandonment. Institutional availability of HSCT in the later era was not associated with improved population-level survival, although the small number of transplanted patients precludes conclusions regarding HSCT effectiveness. Strengthening supportive care, molecular risk stratification, treatment continuity, and timely access to salvage therapy and HSCT may improve outcomes in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Predictors of Severe Anaphylaxis in Infants and Toddlers: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anaphylaxis in infants and toddlers is increasingly recognized, yet knowledge on its clinical characteristics and predictors of severe disease remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the demographic, clinical, and immunological characteristics of anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months and to identify factors associated with severe anaphylaxis.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 68 children aged 0-36 months diagnosed with anaphylaxis at a tertiary pediatric allergy center. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, and outcome data were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with severe anaphylaxis.
RESULTS: The median age at presentation was 13.0 months (interquartile range [IQR], 7.0-23.0), and 58.8% of patients were male. Food was the leading trigger (80.9%), with tree nuts, hen's egg, and cow's milk being the most common allergens. Skin involvement was the predominant manifestation (94.1%), followed by respiratory and gastrointestinal involvement (both 57.4%). Respiratory involvement was more frequent in females, whereas gastrointestinal manifestations predominated in males. Non-atopic children had significantly higher rates of severe anaphylaxis, cardiovascular involvement, and multisystem reactions than atopic children. Non-food triggers were associated with a more severe clinical course. In univariate analysis, atopy was associated with lower odds of severe anaphylaxis, whereas drug-induced reactions had higher odds of severe disease than food-induced reactions. Neither atopy nor trigger category remained independently associated with severity after multivariable adjustment. All patients received intramuscular epinephrine under protocolized emergency care, and no biphasic reactions or fatalities occurred.
CONCLUSION: Anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months has distinct clinical characteristics. Although food remained the predominant trigger, non-food triggers and the absence of atopy were associated with a more severe clinical phenotype. However, no baseline atopic or trigger-related factor independently predicted severe anaphylaxis after multivariable adjustment, highlighting the challenges of risk stratification in this age group.

articles.title: Hippotherapy for the social communication of children with ASD: An exploratory randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
