INTRODUCTION: Hippotherapy has emerged as a promising complementary approach, offering rich sensorimotor and social experiences that may enhance communication outcomes in children with ASD. However, despite growing interest in equine-assisted interventions, there is a scarcity of robust randomized clinical trials examining structured speech-language programs focused on social communication within hippotherapy settings. This study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of the Step-by-Step in Communication program (a standardized speech-language intervention used in hippotherapy) in improving communicative and linguistic skills in children with ASD.
METHODS: Randomized clinical trial with 49 children aged 2 to 6 years diagnosed with ASD. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups: G1 (one session per week for 24 weeks) and G2 (two sessions per week for 12 weeks), both totaling 24 sessions. The intervention followed the Step-by-Step in Communication program. Outcomes were assessed using the Behavioral Observation Protocol (PROC) and the Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist (ATEC).
RESULTS: Both groups' language skills improved significantly intragroup, as measured by PROC, and reduced significantly three ATEC domains, whereas no significant changes were observed in the Health/Physical/Behavior domain. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for baseline scores, revealed no significant differences between groups and their intervention conditions.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that hippotherapy may be an effective complementary intervention for improving language and autism-related outcomes in children with ASD. Different weekly intervention frequencies with the same total number of sessions did not appear to influence final outcomes; hence, the program may be implemented with different weekly schedules without compromising its effectiveness.

articles.title: Age-Specific Self-Care, Psychosocial, and Coping Competencies in Children with Type 1 Diabetes: Development of a Competency Framework from Diabetes Camp Experiences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The progressive acquisition of self-care and coping competencies is essential for children and adolescents living with type 1 diabetes (T1D), as these skills support increasing autonomy in diabetes management. However, limited data are available regarding the ages at which these competencies are typically acquired. This study aimed to determine the ages at which key self-care and coping competencies are acquired among children and adolescents with T1D.
METHODS: We analyzed data from competency evaluations conducted in 943 patients aged 7-17.9 years during diabetes summer camp in France in 2021. A broad range of self-care and coping competencies was assessed in patients treated with either multiple daily injections (MDI) or insulin pump therapy. Age groups were defined as 7-8, 9-10, 11-12, 13-14, and 15-17 years. Descriptive statistics were used to determine the proportion of patients acquiring each competency by age group, and treatment modalities were compared using univariate analyses.
RESULTS: Among the 114 self-care competencies classified into 14 domains, 94.1% were acquired by patients treated with MDI and 96.5% by those using insulin pump therapy by the age of 17.9 years. We established a detailed reference list of the ages at which at least 75% of patients had acquired each competency and developed a corresponding competency evaluation tool. Several competencies were acquired at younger ages in patients using insulin pump therapy than in those treated with MDI.
CONCLUSIONS: The age-specific reference list developed in this study may help healthcare professionals design and adapt therapeutic education programs to support the progressive development of autonomy in children and adolescents with T1D.

articles.title: Prenatal Genetics and Investigational in Utero Gene Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease: Clinical, Ethical, and Justice Considerations.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a monogenic hemoglobinopathy with inequities in morbidity and care within and between countries. Prenatal somatic gene therapy is proposed but remains preclinical for SCD. This critical narrative review examines how such an intervention would interact with existing disparities and evaluates it in terms of autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. SCD differs from conditions for which fetal intervention is established: fetal hemoglobin is protective, clinical manifestations generally arise after its postnatal decline, and newborn screening permits early preventive care. A prenatal intervention must therefore demonstrate a material advantage over timely postnatal management while exposing neither the pregnant person nor fetus to disproportionate procedural or product risk. Intended somatic treatment is not equivalent to heritable genome editing or embryo selection, although off-target effects, mosaicism and unintended germline exposure require explicit investigation. There is currently no evidence that prenatal somatic gene therapy is cost-effective or would overcome access barriers. Its reliance on fetal medicine, molecular, and manufacturing infrastructure could initially widen disparities. Clinical translation would be ethically defensible only after disease-specific comparative evidence, independent oversight, non-directive consent, lifelong follow-up and a credible equitable-access plan. Strengthening newborn screening and proven care remains the immediate justice priority.

articles.title: Montelukast sodium in preventing oxygen requirements at day 28 in preterm infants: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: BackgroundEvaluating the efficacy and safety of oral montelukast in preventing oxygen requirement at day 28 of birth in preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit through a randomized trial with open-label treatment administration and blinded outcome assessment.MethodsTarget Population: 92 preterm infants admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Units of four hospitals.
INTERVENTION: Daily oral administration of 1 mg/kg montelukast.
PRIMARY OUTCOME: Incidence of Oxygen requirement on days 14 and 28 of life.ResultsReduction in Oxygen requirement: Significantly lower in the intervention group (31.7%) compared to the control group (55%). Lung Disease Severity: Pulmonary Severity Score was significantly lower in the montelukast group on days 14 and 28. Safety Profile: No serious drug-related adverse effects were reported.
SECONDARY OUTCOMES: No statistically significant differences were observed regarding mortality or length of hospital stay between the two groups.ConclusionPreventive administration of montelukast in high-risk preterm infants appears to be safe and effective in reducing the incidence of oxygen requirement at day 28/discharge.

articles.title: The Clinical and Neuro-Informed Benefits of Utilizing a Grief-Focused Camp for Supporting Childhood Bereavement.
articles.abstract: Grief-focused camps offer clinical and neuro-informed benefits for grieving children. This conceptual article highlights both design and implementation of a bereavement camp, exploring how structured, experiential, and expressive activities engage developing neural networks involved in emotion regulation, attachment, and stress response. Drawing on the Dual-Processing Model of Grief and the Window of Tolerance, the camp model emphasizes relational safety, peer normalization, and multisensory engagement to promote adaptive coping and support the grieving processes. Rotating small-group sessions, large-group activities, and ending with guardian-inclusive activities provides repeated corrective emotional experiences supporting neuroplasticity and resilience. The design intentionally balances opportunities for processing loss with restorative, play-based experiences fostering emotional growth and co-regulation. Clinical implications for counselors include program and staff structures and supervision, grounded in neuro-informed principles. By applying a neuroscience lens to grief-focused camp design, this model demonstrates potential to enhance coping, emotional development, and long-term adaptive functioning in bereaved children.

articles.title: Rhabdomyolysis in Ugandan children with severe malaria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rhabdomyolysis is a serious clinical syndrome characterized by skeletal muscle injury, release of creatine kinase (CK) and increased risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). Few studies have examined rhabdomyolysis in severe pediatric malaria.
METHODS: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study. We examined the association of rhabdomyolysis with mortality (Cox proportional hazards models, complete case analysis and multiple imputation by chained equations). We also examined putative mediators of rhabdomyolysis-associated mortality.
RESULTS: Of 600 patients in the cohort (median age 2 years, 44% female), 512 (85%) had at least one CK measurement. The median CK was 120 U/L (IQR 44-490) and 73/512 patients (14%) had rhabdomyolysis (CK>1000 U/L). There were 44 deaths in the cohort (case fatality rate 7.3%). Rhabdomyolysis was associated with an unadjusted 2.5-fold increased hazard of mortality (95%CI 1.1-6.1, p=0.038). This estimate remained statistically significant after adjustment for age and sex and after multiple imputation for missing CK values. The odds of AKI (OR 2.0, 95%CI 1.2-3.6, p=0.0085) and hyperkalemia (OR 2.7, 95%CI 1.3-5.5, p=0.0049) were higher among patients with rhabdomyolysis. AKI and hyperkalemia attenuated the effect of rhabdomyolysis in multivariable models. We estimated that the proportion of rhabdomyolysis-associated mortality risk mediated by AKI and hyperkalemia was 23% (95% UI 12-41%) and 18% (95% UI 12-29%), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Rhabdomyolysis is common in children with severe malaria and is associated with elevated mortality. Rhabdomyolysis may be a marker of disease severity or may contribute to the pathogenesis of fatal malaria (e.g., via AKI and hyperkalemia).

articles.title: Clinical, metabolic and transcriptomic effects of congenital DLK1 deficiency in women who had central precocious puberty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loss-of-function mutations in Delta-like Noncanonical Notch Ligand 1 (DLK1), a maternally imprinted gene at chromosome 14q32.2, are rare causes of central precocious puberty (CPP) associated with metabolic dysfunction in both sexes.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the clinical, metabolic and transcriptomic consequences of congenital DLK1 absence in women who had CPP in their childhood.
METHODS: Peripheral blood from eight women from three distinct families who carried DLK1 deletions and exhibited undetectable circulating DLK1 serum levels were evaluated. 3T3-L1 cell differentiation into adipocytes was induced using DLK1-deficient serum from these women. In addition, mitochondrial function, cellular metabolism (Seahorse XL Analyzer), and whole blood transcriptomic profiling (RNAseq) were evaluated.
RESULTS: Women with congenital DLK1 deficiency had increased visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue on abdominal computed tomography. DLK1-deficient serum promoted greater adipogenesis of 3T3-L1 cells compared with control subjects serum. Flow cytometry revealed increased mitochondrial mass and oxidative stress in leukocytes in the patients. In addition, their leukocytes had decreased oxygen consumption and increased extracellular acidification. Whole blood transcriptomic profiling identified upregulation of several genes involved in neutrophil activation and inflammatory signaling, including obesity-associated genes (OLFM4 and LCN2).
CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrated distinct metabolic profiles in women with congenital DLK1 deficiency. The absence of DLK1 leads to increased adiposity, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and upregulation of genes involved in immune-related pathways, particularly neutrophil activation.

articles.title: Managing environmental enteropathy among Egyptian infants and children with growth faltering.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental enteropathy (EE) is an acquired subclinical inflammation of the small bowel mucosa, leading to reduced nutrient absorption and increased intestinal permeability. There are currently no universally accepted protocols for the diagnosis and treatment of EE.
OBJECTIVE: The primary aim of this clinical trial was to assess the prevalence of EE among children with faltering growth (FG). Determination of the dietary requirements in pediatric FG with EE and highlighting the histopathologic changes in the small intestine in such conditions were the secondary objectives.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The current study recruited 200 patients (their age range was 6-58 months) diagnosed as GF at the Pediatric Clinical Nutrition Clinic, Children`s Hospital, Faculty of Medicine, Ain Shams University (Cairo, Egypt), during the period from April 2022 till June 2023. The first phase of the study was a cross sectional interventional one where all patients underwent nutritional rehabilitation using diet regimen including polymeric milk formula. Patients whose weight z score was still below - 2 SD for age and sex after 12 weeks were considered as non-responders and were enrolled in the second phase, when esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and mucosal biopsies were done. In the latter phase, patients with EE received nutritional rehabilitation regimen using peptide-based milk formula with assessment of anthropometric measurements after 8 weeks of follow up.
RESULTS: Out of the studied cases, 170 were responders, and 30 were non-responders, 24 of the non-responders underwent EGD with biopsies and all were diagnosed as EE with prevalence of 12% among the studied patients with GF as the least possible prevalence. Total histology scores of the EE fell between those of the controls and celiac disease reference samples with cut off values > 3 and ≤ 14 for EE, ≤ 3 for controls and > 14 for celiac disease. There was a significant increase in weight and height z scores among patients of EE on peptide-based formula compared to polymeric formula.
CONCLUSION: EE isn`t uncommon and should be suspected when provision of catch-up nutrients can`t correct FG. Peptide-based formula has a possible beneficial effect on growth of patients with EE.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The clinical trial was registered at Protocol Registration and Results System with number NCT06497907 (12/07/2024).

articles.title: Communicating dermatologic drug safety: a comparative evaluation of United States and United Kingdom pharmacovigilance systems using dapsone as a model medication.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postmarketing pharmacovigilance systems are essential for identifying adverse drug reactions (ADRs) that may not be recognized during premarketing clinical trials. Although the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS) and the United Kingdom Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) Yellow Card Scheme share the common objective of medication safety surveillance, little is known about how these systems differ in organizing and communicating postmarketing safety information to clinicians. This study compared the clinician-facing organization, accessibility, and communication of postmarketing safety information between the FDA AEMS Public Dashboard and the MHRA Yellow Card Interactive Drug Analysis Profile (iDAP) using dapsone as a representative dermatologic medication.
METHODS: A cross-sectional comparative pharmacovigilance study was conducted using publicly available FDA AEMS and MHRA Yellow Card data extracted on June 29, 2026. Descriptive analyses characterized adverse-event reports, patient demographics, clinical outcomes, MedDRA Preferred Terms, and System Organ Class distributions. The two pharmacovigilance platforms were qualitatively compared using a predefined framework assessing data accessibility, organization, clinical usability, and research utility.
RESULTS: The FDA AEMS identified 4,793 reports associated with dapsone-containing products, including 3,686 (76.9%) classified as serious and 280 (5.8%) reporting death. The MHRA Yellow Card Scheme identified 699 reports comprising 1,701 adverse reactions, including 559 (80.0%) serious reports and 25 (3.6%) fatal outcomes. Both systems demonstrated overlapping patterns of reported adverse reactions. Despite similar pharmacovigilance outputs, substantial differences were observed in the communication of safety information. The FDA emphasized downloadable datasets, customizable searches, and case-level transparency to facilitate secondary pharmacovigilance analyses, whereas the MHRA prioritized standardized, drug-specific summaries, hierarchical MedDRA organization, integrated visualizations, and contextual guidance to support rapid clinical interpretation.
CONCLUSIONS: The FDA AEMS and MHRA Yellow Card Scheme identify similar postmarketing safety profiles for dapsone while employing distinct approaches to communicating pharmacovigilance information. These complementary strengths suggest that future clinician-facing pharmacovigilance platforms should integrate the analytical flexibility of the FDA with the standardized, medication-specific communication strategies of the MHRA to improve the translation of postmarketing safety data into dermatology practice while preserving scientific transparency.

articles.title: Predictors of anemia among children 6-59 months of age in Tanzania: a multilevel analysis of TDHS-MIS 2022.
articles.abstract: Anemia remains a major public health problem among children in developing countries, including Tanzania, despite ongoing nutritional and health interventions. This study aimed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with anemia in children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania. The study used data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS), a nationally representative cross-sectional survey conducted between February and July of 2022. Multilevel logistic regression was performed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with childhood anemia. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. A total of 4334 children aged 6-59 months were included in the analysis. The overall prevalence of anemia among children aged 6-59 months was 59.9% (95% CI: 58.48-61.39). Of these, 1.9%, 32.4%, and 25.6% had severe, moderate, and mild anemia, respectively. In the final multilevel model, children aged 6-23 months (AOR = 2.48; 95% CI: 2.01-3.07), those who were fourth or fifth born (AOR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.25-2.52), those having recent diarrhea (AOR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.11-2.21), those with stunting (AOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.08-1.59), and those with positive malaria test results (AOR = 4.87; 95% CI: 3.06-7.75) had significantly higher odds of anemia. Maternal age of 15-24 years (AOR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05-2.27), maternal anemia (AOR = 1.74; 95% CI: 1.44-2.10), and lack of health insurance (AOR = 1.67; 95% CI: 1.09-2.55) were also associated with increased odds of childhood anemia, whereas maternal overweight was associated with lower odds of anemia (AOR = 0.75; 95% CI: 0.59-0.96). Significant geographical disparities in childhood anemia were also observed across zones. Conclusion: Anemia affects approximately six out of ten children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania, indicating that it remains a public health concern in the country. Both individual- and community-level factors contribute to childhood anemia. Integrated interventions targeting child nutrition, malaria and diarrheal disease prevention, maternal anemia, and geographically tailored strategies are needed to reduce the burden of childhood anemia in Tanzania. What is known: • Anemia is a persistent public health problem among children under five years of age in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, with several individual-level risk factors (nutritional status, infections, and maternal characteristics) previously documented. What is new: • Using nationally representative data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS) and a multilevel logistic regression model, this study found that childhood anemia remains highly prevalent. • In addition to confirming established child-related predictors (younger child age, higher birth order, diarrhea, stunting, malaria infection, younger maternal age, and maternal anemia), this study demonstrated the independent influence of household factors (lack of health insurance) and community-level geographic disparities on childhood anemia.

articles.title: Extravascular Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators in Children: Real World Evidence.
articles.abstract: The extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV-ICD) is a novel substernal ICD with limited reports in children and adolescents. Single-centre review of EV-ICDs in children <18-years. Clinical, peri-procedural, and electrocardiographic data reviewed, including device performance in routine exercise stress testing. Median follow-up 10.9 (IQR 7.5 - 12.5) months. Between April 2025-April 2026, 15 EV-ICDs were successfully implanted by a single cardiothoracic surgeon: median age 13.8-years, IQR 10.2-16.4; 11 (73%) male; weight 52 kg, IQR 38.2-64.1; BSA 1.6 m2, IQR 1.2-1.8. Smallest child was 4-years, 17.3 kg (BSA 0.7 m2). Indications were primary (n = 10) and secondary (n = 5) prevention. Underlying diagnoses included cardiomyopathy (n = 9), channelopathy (n = 3). One child had a previous sternotomy and another severe chest-wall deformity. Median anaesthetic time was 148 min (IQR 130-161), surgical time 68 min (59-88), fluoroscopy time 2.6 min (2.2-3.8). Median 3 (IQR 2-4) day hospitalisation. Two children experienced early complications. In one child, defibrillator threshold testing terminated ventricular fibrillation (VF) into ventricular tachycardia (VT) requiring CPR and a decision to use external cardioversion. The child fully recovered. One adolescent experienced profound bradycardia and syncope early post anaesthesia. R-wave amplitude at implant (5mV, IQR 4.2 - 6.7), discharge (5, IQR 2.8 - 8.1) and latest follow-up (5.8, IQR 3.2 - 13.7) was stable. Device sensing during routine exercise stress testing has been appropriate. There has been one successful appropriate high voltage therapy and no inappropriate high voltage therapy. This is the largest single-centre series internationally, demonstrating reliable paediatric EV-ICD implantation and short-term device performance. Ongoing paediatric surveillance is necessary.

articles.title: Early childhood outcomes in survivors of congenital chylothorax: a single-centre retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Congenital chylothorax is a rare neonatal condition and the most common cause of pleural effusion in neonates. Although neonatal morbidity and mortality have been described, outcomes beyond the neonatal period remain incompletely characterised. This study aimed to describe respiratory, developmental, and feeding outcomes during early childhood after congenital chylothorax. We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study including infants with congenital chylothorax managed at Lille University Hospital between 2011 and 2023. Cases were identified through an electronic database search and confirmed by individual medical record review. Follow-up data between 1 and 3 years of age included growth, respiratory symptoms and healthcare use, chylothorax recurrence, developmental outcomes, and feeding difficulties. Among 260 medical records screened, 34 infants with congenital chylothorax were included. Four died during the neonatal period. Follow-up data were available for 26 of the 30 survivors (87%) at a median age of 2.0 years [1.5-2.0]. Chylothorax recurred in one child (4%). Seventeen children (65%) received inhaled respiratory medications, 11 (42%) had respiratory symptoms, and 14 (54%) required hospital readmission. Developmental delay was identified in six children (23%) and feeding difficulties in four (15%). Nine children (35%) had no respiratory, neurodevelopmental, or feeding problems identified during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Chylothorax recurrence was uncommon during early childhood, whereas respiratory medication use and hospital readmissions were frequent. Developmental and feeding difficulties were also documented in a subset of survivors. Although these outcomes cannot be attributed solely to congenital chylothorax, the findings highlight the importance of structured multidisciplinary follow-up.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Congenital chylothorax is a rare neonatal condition associated with substantial neonatal morbidity and variable outcomes. • Data beyond the neonatal period remain limited and are derived mainly from small cohorts, with respiratory and neurodevelopmental outcomes incompletely characterised.
WHAT IS NEW: • Chylothorax recurrence was uncommon during early childhood, whereas respiratory symptoms and healthcare use remained frequent. • Developmental and feeding difficulties affected a subset of survivors, while 35% had no respiratory, neurodevelopmental, or feeding problems identified during follow-up.

articles.title: Fulminant Early-Onset Sepsis Caused by Multidrug-Resistant Aeromonas hydrophila in a Preterm Neonate: A Case Report and Therapeutic Challenge.
articles.abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila is a rare but virulent pathogen in neonates, historically associated with aquatic environments. However, the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains presenting as early-onset sepsis (EOS) poses a severe diagnostic and therapeutic dilemma. We report a fatal case of a preterm neonate (33 weeks gestation) who developed fulminant septic shock at 20 hours of life. Despite the initiation of broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam), the clinical course rapidly progressed to pulmonary hemorrhage and death at 26 hours of life. Blood cultures subsequently confirmed Aeromonas hydrophila septicemia with high-level resistance to carbapenems (Meropenem MIC > 16 μg/mL) and piperacillin-tazobactam (MIC > 128 μg/mL). This case highlights the growing threat of nonfermenting MDR gram-negative organisms in EOS and underscores the limitations of standard empiric regimens against atypical pathogens.

articles.title: Surgical treatment of extratemporal epilepsy in children: seizure outcomes, complications and patterns of relapse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extratemporal resections are increasingly performed in children with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but contemporary pediatric-only cohorts are scarce and reported seizure freedom has been modest. We examined seizure outcome, complications, and patterns of seizure recurrence in a national, population-based cohort.
METHODS: We reviewed all children (<19 years at surgery) who underwent unilobar extratemporal resection for DRE at Helsinki University Hospital, Finland's national center for pediatric epilepsy surgery, between 2003 and 2024. Seizure outcome was classified by the Engel scale at last follow-up. Freedom from seizure recurrence after the first resection was estimated with the Kaplan-Meier method, and predictors of recurrence were assessed by Cox regression.
RESULTS: Of 105 children (median follow-up 3.9 years, IQR 2.1-8.4), focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) was the most common etiology (69.5%). Engel class 1 was achieved in 58.1% overall (81.8% for long-term epilepsy-associated tumors, 65.0% for FCD type 2, 50.0% for tuberous sclerosis complex, and 35.5% for FCD type 1), and in 65.5% of children operated on from 2012 onward compared with 48.9% before 2012. Surgical complications occurred in 3.8% (permanent in 1.9%). Among children with recurrence, 55.6% recurred within 6 months, and 25.9% recurred late (≥2 years). In multivariable analysis, malformations of cortical development (HR 4.4; 95% CI 1.7-11.8), acute (HR 5.5; 95% CI 2.6-11.7) and early (HR 3.3; 95% CI 1.6-7.0) postoperative seizures, and preoperative SPECT (HR 3.0; 95% CI 1.5-6.0) were associated with recurrence, and preoperative 3T MRI with a lower risk (HR 0.3; 95% CI 0.2-0.7), whereas surgical era was not.
CONCLUSIONS: Unilobar extratemporal resection rendered most children seizure-free with few permanent deficits. Recurrence was mostly early, but a quarter of recurrences occurred after 2 years. Preoperative 3T MRI was associated with a lower risk of recurrence independently of surgical era, suggesting that improved lesion detection, rather than calendar era itself, underlies the improvement.

articles.title: Hepatic Macrophages Depletion by Clodronate Liposomes Alleviates RRV-Induced Biliary Injury via Targeting the Notch3/PPAR Signalling Pathway.
articles.abstract: Biliary atresia is a rare obliterative cholangiopathy in neonates, and hepatic macrophages participate in biliary atresia pathogenesis. The study aimed to reveal the regulatory mechanism of macrophages in the progression of biliary atresia. Hepatic macrophages were co-cultured with vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Delta like canonical notch ligand 4 (DLL4) and neurogenic locus notch homologue 3 (Notch3) were quantified in rhesus rotavirus (RRV)-treated cells following anti-DLL4 antibody REGN1035. In RRV-challenged mice, Notch3 was activated by Ade-NICD3, while macrophages were depleted by clodronate liposomes (Clo-Lip) to compare intervention effects on RRV-induced biliary injury, hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), Notch3, CD68 and CD163. Notch3 knockout mice were used to verify the effect of Notch3 on RRV-induced injury. Transcriptome sequencing screened Notch3-related differentially expressed genes, and downstream pathway regulation was further verified. Macrophages upregulated DLL4, while REGN1035 treatment inhibited DLL4 and Notch3 expression. In RRV-infected mice, Clo-Lip-mediated macrophage depletion alleviated biliary injury, repressed Notch3 signalling and downregulated HIF-1α, CD68 and CD163. In RRV mice with NICD3 overexpression, macrophage depletion alleviated Notch3 activation-triggered biliary lesions, inhibited inflammation and downregulated HIF-1α, CD68 and CD163. Transcriptomic analysis identified 715 upregulated and 585 downregulated genes, confirming the peroxisome proliferators-activated receptor (PPAR) signalling pathway as a downstream pathway of Notch3. Compared with RRV-infected wild-type mice, Notch3 knockout alleviated RRV-induced biliary injury and abnormal macrophage polarization, downregulated HIF-1α and CYP7A1, but upregulated PPARα. This protective effect was abolished by the PPARα inhibitor GW6471. Macrophage depletion ameliorates RRV-induced biliary injury via regulating the Notch3/PPAR signalling pathway.

articles.title: Cost effectiveness of exome and chromosomal microarray analysis in cases of severe central nervous system structural anomalies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The central nervous system (CNS) is affected in 9% of fetal malformations but accounts for as much as one-third of all pregnancy terminations due to fetal anomaly. When applying chromosomal microarray (CMA) to the diagnosis of fetal CNS anomalies, the estimated diagnostic yield remains low. Recent study demonstrated that, in fetuses with major CNS anomalies, exome sequencing (ES) had an additional diagnostic yield of 44% over the 10% provided by CMA. We aimed to determine the cost effectiveness of the added value of ES in major CNS structural anomalies.
METHODS: We modeled costs, utility, and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) for CMA versus CMA + ES in prenatal testing. Two strategies were compared using the Markovian process decision analysis model: (1) CMA only, abnormal result culminating in termination of pregnancy (TOP); (2) ES after a negative CMA, where for positive result a TOP is conducted. The outcomes included health quality of life after TOP or having a disabled child, the costs of the CMA test, the ES test, and the health expenses of a disabled child. The time horizon of the model was 20 years. Sensitivity analysis including probabilistic sensitivity analysis of all parameters was conducted.
RESULTS: In the base-case model, the total expected cost per pregnancy was $US 91 059 for the CMA-alone strategy (driven largely by the expected long-term cost of raising a child with an undiagnosed disability) and $US 3101 for the CMA + ES strategy. The QALYs with a time horizon of 20 years were 11.84 and 13.84 for CMA and CMA + ES strategies, respectively, so CMA + ES dominated CMA alone (higher QALY value and cost saving). Sensitivity analysis revealed that the results were robust, and CMA + ES dominated the CMA with cost savings for all sensitivity analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: We suggest that ES has the potential to be cost effective and should be considered as a first-tier test in the prenatal diagnosis of major CNS anomalies. The substantial increase in diagnostic yield offered by ES not only provides valuable information for the current pregnancy but also holds significant relevance for future pregnancies. These findings are pivotal in facilitating timely and evidence-based decision-making.

articles.title: Clinical presentation of Van Praagh Type A4 truncus arteriosus with interrupted aortic arch in an adolescent.
articles.abstract: We describe a 14-year-old boy (weight 32 kg, height 148 cm), who was brought to a tertiary care facility in North India, with complaints of progressive exertional dyspnoea, palpitations, and chest pain with a recent episode of moderate haemoptysis. Imaging findings include Chest PA-view demonstrated cardiomegaly with abnormal great vessel contour, prominent superior mediastinal shadow, and increased bilateral pulmonary vascular markings, suggestive of a single large arterial outflow tract. Similarly, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a large outlet ventricular septal defect (VSD) with a dilated single arterial trunk overriding the defect. Cardiac CT angiography confirmed a large outlet VSD and an interrupted aortic arch, with no continuity between the ascending and descending aorta. The right and left pulmonary arteries, descending aorta, and left subclavian artery arose directly from the truncal vessel, while a separate ascending aorta bifurcated into the right brachiocephalic and left common carotid arteries. This particular case brings a remarkably unusual paediatric presentation with Van Praagh Type A4 truncus arteriosus with interrupted aortic arch and emphasises the effects of late diagnosis. Due to the patient's severe pulmonary arterial hypertension, palliative care was the only option for treatment, and definitive surgical repair was not feasible.

articles.title: Cerebral redistribution in late-onset fetal growth restriction: relation between abnormalities of individual Doppler components and adverse outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cerebral redistribution consists of the preferential redirection of the arterial and well-oxygenated blood flow to the fetal brain and is commonly associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR) secondary to placental insufficiency. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with late-onset FGR and cerebral redistribution, examining whether outcomes differed according to the normality or abnormality of the individual Doppler components that determine a reduction in the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR).
METHODS: This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted across four tertiary maternity units in Italy (University of Parma, Parma; Fondazione Policlinico Universitario 'A. Gemelli' IRCCS, Rome; IRCCS Materno Infantile Burlo Garofolo, Trieste; and University of Brescia, Brescia), including non-anomalous singleton pregnancies complicated by late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution (defined as CPR < 5th percentile according to the Fetal Medicine Foundation reference charts). The study included cases collected at the four participating units between January 2019 and December 2024. Cases were categorized according to umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler data (Group 1: normal UA-pulsatility index (PI) (≤ 95th percentile for gestational age) and MCA-PI (≥ 5th percentile); Group 2: abnormal UA-PI (> 95th percentile) and normal MCA-PI; Group 3: normal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI (< 5th percentile); and Group 4: abnormal UA-PI and MCA-PI), and perinatal outcomes were compared and evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: In total, 352 cases were included, of which 117 (33.2%) were assigned to Group 1, 84 (23.9%) to Group 2, 85 (24.1%) to Group 3 and 66 (18.8%) to Group 4. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, Group 4 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (odds ratio (OR), 2.07 (95% CI, 1.08-3.96); P = 0.03), birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01), neonatal hypoglycemia (OR, 3.34 (95% CI, 1.46-7.67); P < 0.01), neonatal intensive care unit admission (OR, 2.33 (95% CI, 1.24-4.37); P = 0.01) and composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO) (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01) compared with Group 1. Furthermore, Group 2 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (OR, 2.06 (95% CI, 1.12-3.79); P = 0.02) and birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.92 (95% CI, 1.07-3.46); P = 0.03) and Group 3 showed greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.79 (95% CI, 1.01-3.26); P = 0.02) and CAPO (OR, 1.88 (95% CI, 1.05-3.38); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. However, in the multivariable logistic regression analysis only Group 4 was associated with greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (adjusted OR, 2.11 (95% CI, 1.11-4.00); P = 0.02) and neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted OR, 2.68 (95% CI, 1.10-6.50); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, abnormal UA and MCA Doppler parameters were also associated with perinatal complications. However, none of the associations were confirmed after adjustment for gestational age at delivery and birth weight in the multivariable models.
CONCLUSIONS: In cases of late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution, isolated abnormalities of the UA-PI or MCA-PI could not identify fetuses at increased risk of perinatal complications. However, the coexistence of both abnormal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI, indicating the highest extent of cerebral redistribution, was independently associated with perinatal complications including neonatal hypoglycemia and birth weight < 3rd percentile. In such cases, birth weight was also independently associated with perinatal complications. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: Quality of Life During Oral Peanut Immunotherapy in the OPIA Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) findings have varied between peanut oral immunotherapy (OIT) trials. The objective of this study was to compare changes in the HRQoL between the OIT and standard (control) treatment groups during the OPIA peanut OIT double-blind randomised controlled trial and at long-term follow-up.
METHODS: OPIA was a single-centre, 3-arm, double-blind placebo-controlled trial of peanut OIT in children aged 10-16 years. Standardised questionnaires (FAQLQ, FAIM, FAQLQ-Parent Burden, PSS) and bespoke surveys were administered at 0, 6, 12 and 13.5 months, with 3-year follow-up. Changes in scores at different time points were analysed descriptively and using 2-tailed T tests. A GEE model investigated the interaction between change in HRQoL score, treatment (OIT vs. standard care) and time. 3 year follow-up surveys were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative analysis.
RESULTS: Sixty-five subjects were randomised and 61 participants completed the study. There was no evidence of difference in HRQoL score changes between the OIT and standard treatment groups from baseline to 12 months or 13.5 months. Furthermore, achieving OPIA's primary efficacy endpoint (tolerance of ≥ 1000 mg of peanut protein (cumulative dose 1449 mg) at month 13.5 double blind placebo-controlled food challenge was not associated with a more favourable change in FAQLQ from baseline to end of study. Changes in global FAQLQ-Parent proxy (FAQLQ-PF) scores from baseline to 12 months were less favourable for carers of children who had experienced treatment-related serious adverse events compared to those without such events (mean change 0.10 vs. -0.97, 0.0063).
CONCLUSIONS: OIT did not confer a HRQoL benefit over standard care in this cohort, based upon the tools used to assess HRQoL. Treatment-related serious adverse effects negatively impacted FAQLQ-Parent proxy scores.

articles.title: Family Factors in Sibling Sexual Abuse: A Comparative Study With Interfamilial and Peer Child Sexual Abuse.
articles.abstract: Sibling sexual abuse (SSA) cases were compared with two other types of child sexual abuse (CSA): sexual abuse by an adult family member and sexual abuse by a peer to identify differences in individual, family, abuse, and actor characteristics. In addition, differences in parental responses upon disclosure were examined given the importance of parental support for long-term trauma processing of children. Data from 131 client records from a children's mental health center were used, with 43 to 44 records per type of CSA. Results suggested some specific individual and family characteristics associated with SSA, including a larger family size, delayed disclosure, parental reluctance to place accountability with the sibling who has harmed, more ongoing contact between the harmed child and the sibling who has harmed, and the co-occurrence of child maltreatment. A limitation is that clinical records reflect a self-selective sample of families who voluntarily reached out for professional help, limiting the generalizability of findings to sibling sexual abuse cases that typically remain undisclosed. However, this may simultaneously enhance the relevance of our findings for professionals supporting families that have experienced SSA. The findings underscore the need for systemic interventions that take into account the emotional bonds between siblings, parent-child relationships, and the complex family dynamics that are associated with the abuse.

articles.title: Detailed Memory and the Self: Examining the Development of the Self-Referential Effect in Autism.
articles.abstract: The self-referential effect (SRE), better memory for self-related information, strengthens with age and includes certain source details. In autism, altered self-referential processing may reduce the SRE, though findings remain mixed. Further, the effect of self-referencing on source details is understudied in autism. We studied 37 (10 female) autistic and 64 (35 female) nonautistic children between the ages of 7 and 17 years using a self- vs. other-referential encoding paradigm and a recognition task. Both groups showed stronger memory for self-encoded words, but nonautistic children had higher average SRE. The SRE emerged for inherent (referent type) but not peripheral (word location) source memory in both groups. In nonautistic children, the SRE increased with age. Findings suggest self-referential encoding can support memory and social learning in both autistic and nonautistic children.

articles.title: Maternal Substance Use During Pregnancy and Congenital Syphilis Among Hospitalized Neonates.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: US congenital syphilis (CS) cases have increased 10-fold in the past decade, exceeding 3700 cases in 2022. This study evaluated the association between maternal substance use during pregnancy and CS among hospitalized neonates by region and year.
METHODS: We analyzed hospitalized neonates (postnatal age ≤28 days) in the Kids' Inpatient Database from 2016, 2019, and 2022. We identified CS using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes and categorized maternal substance use as no substance use, single substance use, or polysubstance use. Using survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression, we tested effect modification by region and year.
RESULTS: Among 4 531 346 hospitalized neonates, 217 220 (weighted prevalence = 2.5%) had maternal substance use during pregnancy. CS prevalence among substance-exposed neonates increased 467% from 2.5 to 14.5 per 1000 neonates between 2016 and 2022, compared with 0.2 to 0.8 per 1000 neonates among unexposed neonates. After adjusting for demographic charateristics, health insurance status, median household income, housing insecurity, year, and region, single substance use and polysubstance use were associated with higher odds of CS (single substance use: adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 9.68; 95% CI, 8.88-10.55; and polysubstance use: AOR = 17.18; 95% CI, 15.21-19.40). We observed a significant effect modification: the association was much stronger in the West region of the United States (interaction OR = 4.80; 95% CI, 3.10-7.44) than in the Northeast, and the polysubstance use association was significantly elevated in 2022 relative to 2016 (interaction OR = 3.10; 95% CI, 1.81-5.30).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal substance use was strongly associated with CS. These findings underscore the need to address structural barriers to prenatal care through the expansion and integration of syphilis screening within substance use treatment and harm-reduction contexts, especially in regions with a high burden of CS.

articles.title: Admission systemic inflammatory response index and prognostic nutritional index in children with diabetic ketoacidosis-associated acute kidney injury: an exploratory retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Early identification of acute kidney injury (AKI) in children with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is important to enable timely management, but conventional markers based on serum creatinine may delay detection. The Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI) and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) have been associated with adverse outcomes in various clinical settings, but their association with DKA-associated AKI in children has not been investigated. This retrospective study included 122 children with type 1 diabetes mellitus complicated by DKA. SIRI and PNI were calculated from admission blood samples. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection, and multivariable logistic regression was performed. A nomogram was constructed and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. AKI occurred in 36 children (29.5%). Spearman correlation analysis showed that SIRI was positively correlated with creatinine, uric acid, and BUN, and negatively correlated with pH and bicarbonate, while PNI showed only weak correlations with these variables. In the fully adjusted model, admission PNI, likely reflecting hemoconcentration, remained independently associated with AKI (OR 1.132, 95% CI 1.051-1.243, P = 0.003), whereas SIRI showed a positive but non-significant association (OR 1.066, 95% CI 0.981-1.166, P = 0.143). PNI remained significant after adjustment for hydration-related variables and when post-rehydration PNI was used. In an exploratory analysis, the combined SIRI-PNI model achieved an AUC of 0.845 (95% CI 0.765-0.925), which was higher than that of SIRI alone (0.752) and PNI alone (0.746) (DeLong test, both P < 0.05). The nomogram showed acceptable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow χ2 = 3.617, P = 0.890) and potential net clinical benefit. Conclusion: Admission PNI, likely reflecting hemoconcentration and disease severity rather than nutritional immune reserve, was associated with AKI in children with DKA In an exploratory analysis, the combination of SIRI and PNI provided moderate discriminative ability , supporting further evaluation of these routinely available indices for early risk assessment.

articles.title: Paired independent child-parent symptom reporting using the Turkish SSPedi and mini-SSPedi: psychometric evaluation and discordance patterns in pediatric oncology.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The Symptom Screening in Pediatrics Tool (SSPedi; ages 8-18) and mini-SSPedi (ages 4-7) are validated pediatric oncology symptom-screening instruments. Turkish versions are available, but paired independent child self-report and parent proxy-report within the same assessment have not been systematically evaluated in Türkiye. This study assessed the psychometric properties of paired SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting and characterized child-parent discordance. In this prospective observational study, conducted from January to December 2025 at Istanbul University pediatric hematology-oncology inpatient and outpatient clinics, child-parent dyads aged 4-18 receiving cancer treatment or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation were enrolled. Children completed SSPedi or mini-SSPedi independently, followed by an independent parent proxy-report on the same items. This approach differs from consensus-based co-SSPedi, which produces a single joint score through structured child-parent discussion. Psychometric evaluation included internal consistency, test-retest reliability, known-groups validity, convergent validity, and responsiveness. Convergent validity was examined using ChIMES, PeNAT, and FPS-R. Among 131 dyads, child self-report showed high internal consistency (α = 0.884-0.956; overall α = 0.922), as did parent proxy-report (α = 0.852-0.911). Combined child-parent scores correlated significantly with ChIMES (ρ = 0.268), PeNAT (ρ = 0.263), and FPS-R (ρ = 0.270). Known-groups validity and responsiveness were supported. Discordance varied systematically by symptom domain and developmental age: parents more often overestimated emotional distress, whereas children rated internal physical symptoms as more bothersome. Several individual correlations were marginally below the prespecified r ≥ 0.25 threshold. Future studies should determine whether consensus-based co-SSPedi provides additional clinical value beyond paired independent reporting in routine practice.
CONCLUSION: Paired independent SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting demonstrated acceptable-to-strong psychometric properties and supports simultaneous child-parent symptom assessment in Turkish pediatric oncology.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Child self-report is the preferred approach for assessing subjective symptoms in pediatric oncology, but parent proxy-reports are often needed and may differ from children's perceptions.
WHAT IS NEW: • Paired independent Turkish SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting demonstrated high internal consistency, acceptable convergent validity, and supported known-groups validity and responsiveness, and revealed systematic child-parent discordance, with parents rating emotional symptoms higher and children reporting greater burden from internal physical symptoms.

articles.title: Long-term (≥ 10-year) outcomes after laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To the best of our knowledge, no previous dedicated study has evaluated laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision (LCCE) in a cohort in which all patients had at least 10 years of follow-up. We therefore evaluated long-term outcomes after LCCE in this population.
METHODS: This retrospective two-center cohort study included all 47 consecutive eligible children who underwent LCCE between June 2009 and September 2016. All patients had at least 10 years of confirmed follow-up. The standardized technique included cyst excision with tailored intrapancreatic dissection, intraoperative endoscopy of the common channel and/or intrahepatic ducts, and mucosa-to-mucosa Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy (HJ). The primary endpoint was late biliary event-free survival; overall late event-free survival including intestinal events was a secondary endpoint.
RESULTS: Ten patients (21.3%) had at least 15 years of follow-up. Median follow-up was 12.85 years (IQR 10.89-14.64; range 10.00-17.26). Early and first-year complications occurred in 8 (17.0%) and 4 patients (8.5%), respectively. Two patients (4.3%) developed qualifying late biliary events: one developed cholangitis at 1.02 years and was treated medically, and the other developed an intrahepatic stone at 5.14 years and underwent redo reconstruction. Late biliary event-free survival was 95.7% at both 10 and 15 years. One additional patient underwent surgery for adhesive intestinal obstruction at 13.79 years, resulting in an overall late event-free survival of 90.4% at 15 years. No late pancreatitis, clinically relevant remnant duct pathology, internal hernia, or biliary malignancy occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Standardized LCCE was associated with durable long-term biliary outcomes. However, late biliary and intestinal complications remained possible, supporting continued surveillance into adulthood.

articles.title: Neurosurgical outcome in infants with low-grade glioma - systematic review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Low-grade gliomas (LGGs) in infants pose significant clinical challenges due to their biologically distinct behavior and frequent location in surgically complex regions. While resection remains the preferred initial treatment, its feasibility is frequently limited by age-specific clinical and tumor-related factors. This review explores the role of tumor resection in infants and its association with survival, disease progression, and neurological outcome.
METHODS: A systematic literature search identified studies published within the last decade reporting surgical outcomes in infants with LGGs. Retrospective and prospective cohort studies and relevant case reports were included. Methodological quality was assessed, and relevant data were extracted and analyzed.
RESULTS: Complete resection was less commonly achieved in infants (20.1% vs. 30.9% in total), who demonstrate higher rates of tumor progression and more frequently require multimodal treatment strategies. Resectability was influenced by tumor location, growth pattern, and patient age. Although infants appear to experience lower overall survival rates and greater need for adjuvant, non-surgical therapies, a greater extent of resection is consistently associated with improved survival outcomes, reduced rates of reoperation, and decreased reliance on additional therapeutic modalities.
CONCLUSION: In infants with LGG, the maximal safe extent of resection should be pursued where anatomically feasible. However, particularly for midline tumors, where extensive resection is often not possible, comprehensive assessment of tumor biology and further investigation of non-surgical treatment options are essential to optimize therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Tangeretin improves Neuro-2a cell survival after oxygen-glucose deprivation via phosphorylation of Akt.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI) results from insufficient cerebral blood flow and hypoxia and can cause severe damage to the neonatal brain, leading to long term neurological disabilities. In this study, we hypothesized that tangeretin would improve cell survival by modulating mitochondrial potential in Neuro-2a (N2a) cells after oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) via Akt phosphorylation.
METHODS: N2a cells underwent 3 hours of OGD to mimic HIBI in vitro. Cells were treated with Tangeretin +/- MK2206 (an Akt inhibitor) or vehicle immediately after OGD. Cell survival was quantified by alamarBlue, propidium iodide, and TUNEL assays. Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) was determined by JC-1 fluorescence. Protein expression was evaluated using western blotting.
RESULTS: Treatment with tangeretin significantly improved N2a cell survival after OGD, which was reversed with co-treatment with MK2206. Specifically, tangeretin improved apoptotic DNA fragmentation in cells as measured by TUNEL assay, which was also attenuated by MK2206. OGD significantly increased the percentage mitochondrial depolarization and reactive oxygen species in N2a cells compared with normoxic groups. Tangeretin treatment significantly diminished this effect.
CONCLUSION: Tangeretin provided neuroprotection against OGD in N2a cells by enhancing cell survival, maintaining mitochondrial membrane potential and suppressing apoptosis. Tangeretin deserves further exploration for its neuroprotective effects against HIBI.
IMPACT: In Neuro-2a cells injured by oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD), tangeretin enhances cell survival. Tangeretin-associated cell survival is mediated in part by reduced DNA fragmentation. Tangeretin preserves mitochondrial membrane potential after OGD. The neuroprotective effects of tangeretin are at least partially mediated by Akt phosphorylation. Tangeretin deserves further evaluation for its neuroprotective effects after hypoxic-ischemic brain injury.

articles.title: Comparing 70 kV and 120 kV photon-counting CT protocols for pediatric cardiac imaging in children weighing 10-30 kg: Radiation dose and image quality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scanning at 70 kV on photon-counting CT (PCCT) reduces radiation dose by 50% compared to 120 kV in infants under 10 kg without loss of diagnostic quality. Whether scanning at a lower kV is of benefit in larger children, in whom greater attenuation increases image noise, has not been determined.
METHODS: We retrospectively compared ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT examinations in children weighing 10-30 kg acquired at 70 kV (n = 79) or 120 kV (n = 80), both at a CARE keV IQ level of 25. We measured signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery and compared radiation dose. Two pediatric cardiac radiologists rated image quality in five vascular structures on a 5-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: Groups were similar in age and size. Neither CNR nor SNR differed significantly. Median Likert scores were at least 4 for four of five structures in both groups. Median CTDIvol was 0.49 vs 0.63 mGy (P < 0.001), and effective dose 0.65 vs 0.75 mSv (P < 0.001) for 70 vs 120 kV.
CONCLUSION: In children weighing 10-30 kg, 70 kV ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT was associated with lower radiation dose than 120 kV, with no significant difference in CNR and median reader scores in the diagnostic range. A 120 kV protocol remains appropriate when metal-artifact reduction or advanced spectral reconstructions are needed.

articles.title: Taiwanese Dermatological Association consensus for the management of atopic dermatitis: A 2024 update.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions and intense itching. AD commonly arises in children, in some of whom the condition may persist into adulthood; and a significant proportion of patients experience adult-onset disease as well. Although the prevalence of AD in Taiwan has risen over the past decades, recent therapeutic advances have contributed greatly to disease management. The Taiwanese Dermatological Association (TDA) has therefore developed an evidence-based consensus for the management of AD in Taiwan, and established a consensus committee to provide regular updates. This paper presents the 2024 update, for which a literature search was conducted to include relevant papers published between January 2020- March 2023. Supplementary searches targeted to approvals of new AD medications were subsequently conducted, and information was updated to August 2026. The consensus committee included 17 dermatology experts, and a modified Delphi method was used to evaluate the recommendations, with an approval threshold of ≥ 75%. A total of 21 new recommendations were added, 4 recommendations were revised, and the treatment algorithm was updated. Special considerations for pregnant, lactating, pediatric, and geriatric patients, as well as patients with active infections or undergoing vaccination, were included. This update incorporates the latest evidence and approved therapies, and may help to enhance treatment outcomes for AD patients in Taiwan.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of antiseizure medication dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States: A retrospective claims-based cohort study, 2004-2021.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe trends and identify factors associated with antiseizure medications (ASMs) dispensing among pregnant persons in the United States.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective claims-based cohort study within AMerican PREGNANcy Mother-Child CohorT (AM-PREGNANT). We identified pregnant persons aged 15-45 years continuously enrolled from 12 months before the last menstrual period (LMP) through pregnancy end, with ≥1 ASM dispensing from 2004 to 2021. Annual prevalence of ASM dispensing was estimated by pregnancy start year. Within a first-ever ASM dispensing cohort, we examined dispensing patterns across pregnancy time windows, ASM-related indications and changes in dispensing during pregnancy. We also assessed factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP among those initiating ASM therapy before pregnancy.
RESULTS: The cohort included 337 449 pregnant persons. Annual ASM dispensing prevalence remained stable (10%-13%). Among those with first-ever ASM dispensing (n = 115 896), 56% had dispensing before pregnancy, of whom 65% had no dispensing during pregnancy. The most common starting ASMs were clonazepam (28%), topiramate (25%) and gabapentin (20%). Dispensing patterns varied by indication: epilepsy was characterized by lamotrigine, levetiracetam and topiramate, generally dispensed for >60 days, whereas psychiatric and pain indications showed more variable patterns, typically with <30 days of dispensing. Factors associated with ASM dispensing at LMP included pre-specified indications, comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing; among these, epilepsy/seizure had the strongest association (aOR 2.14; 95% CI 1.78-2.59).
CONCLUSIONS: ASM dispensing varied by indication, with most pre-pregnancy dispensing not continuing during pregnancy. Epilepsy/seizure was most strongly associated with dispensing at LMP, with additional associations observed for comorbidities and pre-conception medication dispensing.

articles.title: Protein intake scaling and muscle status in children with Spinal Muscular Atrophy: implications for protein prescription.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Protein requirements in children with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) are uncertain, and conventional protein targets expressed per kilogram of body weight may be difficult to interpret because fat-free mass is disproportionately reduced. We examined whether protein intake expressed relative to body weight, fat-free mass (FFM), or energy was associated with muscle status and whether these associations differed by SMA phenotype or disease-modifying therapy (DMT) exposure.
METHODS: This longitudinal observational analysis included 248 assessments from 114 children aged 24-159 months with SMA types 1 and 2. Protein intake was derived from dietitian-reviewed 3-day food records. Arm muscle area (AMA) z score was the primary outcome and fat-free mass index (FFMI) the secondary outcome. Generalised estimating equations accounted for repeated assessments and clinical covariates. Within-person, consecutive-visit, sensitivity, interaction, and paired pre/post-DMT analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Protein intake per kilogram of body weight was not associated with AMA (β = -0.001; 95% CI -0.204 to 0.202; P = 0.99), with no interaction by SMA type or treated status. Protein per kilogram of FFM was associated with concurrent AMA (β = 0.189; 95% CI 0.066 to 0.312; q = 0.018), but this association was not robust longitudinally and was absent after adjustment for dietary energy relative to measured resting energy expenditure, although the original model fitted in the same 226 assessments still showed the association (β = 0.182; 95% CI 0.032 to 0.332). Only 3 of 245 assessments were below the age-specific population reference intake (PRI) for healthy children, whereas 75.5% were at least twice that value; this does not establish protein adequacy in SMA. In 27 paired assessments surrounding DMT initiation, body-weight-normalised protein intake decreased without significant changes in AMA or FFMI.
CONCLUSION: In children with SMA whose protein intake was predominantly at or above the general-population PRI, higher protein intake was not associated with better muscle status, and no phenotype- or DMT-specific protein target was identified. FFM-normalised protein was not supported as a prescription target. Nutritional management should emphasise protein adequacy, energy balance, body composition, growth, and longitudinal response rather than routine protein escalation.

articles.title: Predictors of Clinician Success, Quality, and Resilience in Outpatient Pediatric Palliative Care.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Many inpatient PPC programs are growing into the outpatient setting, heeding the call of national organizations to offer pediatric palliative care (PPC) across the care continuum. In this context, expanding PPC programs face high volumes with limited resources.
OBJECTIVES: To improve sustainability, we aimed to assess associations between outpatient pediatric palliative care (OPPC) clinic operationalization and clinician perception of programmatic success, quality of care and team resilience.
METHODS: In a national cross-sectional study, 48 freestanding children's hospitals with established inpatient PPC programs were surveyed about their OPPC program's success, quality of care, and team resilience in Spring 2021; participants were asked to base responses on pre- March 2020 experiences.
RESULTS: Of the 28 programs with OPPC, 89% (25/28) responded to items on programmatic success, quality of care, and team resilience. Most reported that OPPC program design and workflow allowed for high-quality care (76%). Half felt their design and workflow were successful (52%) and promoted team resilience (48%). Across different clinical care models, OPPC programs with a dedicated clinic space reported increased programmatic success. Use of a free-standing clinic model was significantly associated with increased perception of success and high-quality care compared to floating and embedded clinic models. Perception that OPPC design and workflow promoted team resilience was associated with perception of high-quality care.
CONCLUSION: OPPC program design and workflow impacts clinician perception of success, provision of high-quality care, and team resilience. Quality metrics specific to OPPC models are needed to guide programs in successful expansion of PPC into the outpatient clinic setting.

articles.title: Perceived Clinical Utility of a Routine Family Experience Feedback Loop in Pediatric Palliative Care.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Home is typically the preferred setting of care for children living with serious illness, yet children and families frequently experience unmet needs in the home. Pediatric palliative care (PPC) teams provide longitudinal support for these children and families but have limited insight into families' day-to-day experiences and needs while at home. Routinely collecting family-reported data about care experiences in the home and sharing these data with PPC teams may enable more timely, responsive, and family-centered care.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the perceived clinical utility of sharing routinely collected, digitally enabled, family-reported data between families and PPC teams.
METHODS: We used a modified experience-based co-design approach to evaluate acceptability, perceived feasibility, and perceived clinical actionability through 1) individual interviews with family participants, (2) "clinical action check-in" meetings with outpatient PPC clinicians, and (3) co-design sessions with PPC and hospice clinicians. We used a content analytic approach to identify codes, categories, and themes.
RESULTS: Twenty-four parents of children with serious illness and 11 PPC and hospice clinicians participated in this project. Sharing routinely collected care experience data was perceived as: (1) acceptable or valuable, although comfort and willingness varied for families, (2) feasible with attention to timing, frequency, recipients, and implementation, and (3) clinically actionable along a spectrum.
CONCLUSION: A routinely collected, digitally enabled feedback loop between home and hospital is perceived by families and clinicians as holding promise for helping teams identify unmet needs and tailor care. Facilitating routine, bidirectional communication between families and teams may improve alignment between the care provided and families' needs at home.

articles.title: ACCOMPANI: A Psychosocial Nurse Intervention for African American Families in Pediatric Oncology.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: African American parents of children with cancer face magnified existential crisis, defined as emotional distress related to the child's illness and intensified by disconnected and discordant health care interactions and economic worries. Nurses providing direct care are positioned to elicit parents' psychosocial needs and facilitate psychosocial care but have identified barriers to intervention.
OBJECTIVES: To co-develop components of a nurse-targeted intervention, ACCOMPANI, African American Childhood Cancer Multiprong Psychosocial Nurse Intervention through thought partner engagement.
METHODS: We conducted a deductive-inductive thematic qualitative study involving seven thought partners who participated in six-remote focus groups and supplemental individual interviews (n=5). Thought partners included African American parents of children with cancer (n=2), pediatric oncology nurses (n=2), pediatric oncology social worker (n=1), an African American community partner (n=1), and an African American disparity scholar (n=1). Thought partners were presented with a raw intervention prototype and provided iterative feedback on intervention components and delivery.
RESULTS: Thought partners endorsed ACCOMPANI's three targeted domains (attitude, knowledge, and skills) and contributed to developing the intervention components and delivery characteristics. Three themes shaped revisions: (1) cultural relevance, emphasizing avoidance of monolithic assumptions and centering lived experiences; (2) participant engagement, highlighting brief, modular, and flexible learning; and (3) interactive learning, using digital storytelling, web-based modules, and realistic animated simulations. Feedback led to a four-session intervention to be delivered digitally over four consecutive weeks.
CONCLUSION: ACCOMPANI, the first nurse-targeted intervention for African American families with childhood cancer, aims to facilitate psychosocial care. Findings will inform future refinement and pilot testing.
FUNDING: This work was conducted with the support from 2023 Pedals for Pediatrics (Dana-Farber Cancer Institute) as well as 2023 K12TR004381 award through Harvard Catalyst | The Harvard Clinical and Translational Science Center (National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, National Institutes of Health). The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of Harvard Catalyst, Harvard University and its affiliated academic healthcare centers, or the National Institutes of Health.

articles.title: Multiomics Approach to Regionally Profile Zinc-Driven Host-Gut Microbiome Interactions in the Intestinal Tract.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Zinc (Zn) deficiency (ZnD) is a major risk factor for metabolic and inflammatory diseases associated with gut microbial alterations, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, and inflammatory bowel disease. Despite its importance, there are no established dietary recommendations for Zn supplementation in individuals with these conditions, except in cases of severe diarrhea in children. This gap stems from inconsistent outcomes in Zn supplementation trials, suggesting an incomplete understanding of Zn-mediated spatial regulation within the host-microbiome interface.
METHODS: Here, we employed a multi-omics approach to investigate Zn-driven host-gut microbial interactions along the intestinal tract of mice fed Zn-adequate (ZnA) or ZnD diets.
RESULTS: Radiotracing and metallomics analyses revealed region-specific Zn gradients across intestinal tissues and demonstrated reduced mucosal Zn levels in conventionalized compared with germ-free mice, highlighting an influence of microbial colonization on mucosal Zn availability. Transcriptomic analyses identified shared interferon-dominant immune activation in both the small intestine (SI) and the colon under ZnD conditions, accompanied by region-specific epithelial remodeling programs. In the SI, ZnD suppressed apical surface gene networks while inducing Paneth cell-associated antimicrobial responses. In contrast, ZnD colon exhibited suppression of apical junction and extracellular matrix (ECM) structural gene programs. Metagenomic profiling revealed reduced microbial diversity in the SI under ZnD, while the colon displayed enrichment of glycan-degrading taxa, including Hungatella hathewayi and Bacteroides ovatus, along with Clostridioides difficile, a glycan-responsive pathogen that benefits from microbial glycan degradation. Integrated host-microbe correlation and network analyses in the colon identified coordinated associations between ECM/cytoskeletal gene expression and glycosaminoglycan (GAG)-utilizing bacterial taxa. Functional annotation demonstrated enrichment of GAG-catabolic enzymes under ZnD conditions, with the strongest homology mapping to B. ovatus and H. hathewayi, and qPCR confirmed increased tissue-associated abundance of bacterial GAG-utilizing gene sequences alongside reduced host ECM gene expression.
CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Zn deficiency induces region-specific host epithelial and microbial adaptations, revealing a coordinated ECM-GAG-microbe axis in the colon and distinct epithelial remodeling programs along the intestinal tract.

articles.title: Prevalence of von Willebrand disease among adolescents and young women with heavy menstrual bleeding in hospital-based settings: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) affects up to 40% of adolescent and reproductive-age females and is a leading cause of complications such as severe anemia, iron deficiency and hospitalization. In adolescents and young women, it is commonly linked to anovulatory cycles and underlying inherited bleeding disorders, with von Willebrand disease (VWD) being the most prevalent but frequently underdiagnosed. This systematic review explores the prevalence of VWD among adolescents and young women aged ≤25 years assessed for HMB within hospital-based settings and evaluates diagnostic setting gradients.
METHODS: This review included six databases - PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, and ProQuest that were searched electronically using relevant keywords and MeSH terms. After the search, the articles were transferred to Rayyan software for further screening. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Prevalence Critical Appraisal Tool. Data extraction was performed, and the findings were presented narratively.
RESULTS: Among 1,709 young women with heavy menstrual bleeding across 16 studies, 199 were found to have von Willebrand disease, yielding an overall occurrence rate of 11.64%. Subgroup analysis by clinical referral setting revealed a distinct diagnostic gradient: Specialized Hematology and Hemophilia Treatment Centres (HTCs) demonstrated the highest prevalence at 16.78% (77/459), followed by Inpatient / Acute Emergency Admissions at 10.20% (25/245), General Tertiary Referral Hospital Settings at 10.20% (65/637), and Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) / Multidisciplinary Outpatient HMB Clinics at 8.70% (32/368).
CONCLUSION: von Willebrand disease is a highly significant underlying cause of heavy menstrual bleeding in young women, affecting 11.64% of patients presenting to hospital-based settings, including nearly 1 in 11 patients (8.70%) evaluated in specialized Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) clinics. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing rather than universal screening, specifically for patients who present to hospital-based settings and PAG clinics.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024563010.

articles.title: Working memory and BMIz in preschool children: an indirect association involving insufficient healthy food intake.
articles.abstract: Executive function and health behaviors may be relevant to obesity in preschool children, a critical period for obesity prevention, but their associations remain unclear. Our cross-sectional study investigated these associations in 1,557 preschool children from Wuhan, China. The primary adiposity outcome was body mass index z-score (BMIz). Executive function was assessed using seven tasks, from which standardized task scores were averaged to derive working memory and inhibitory control composite scores. Dietary intake was assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire. The insufficient healthy food intake and excessive unhealthy food intake scores were summed to derive an overall dietary risk score. Linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for kindergarten showed that working memory composite score was inversely associated with BMIz. This association was not observed in inhibitory control composite score. Both insufficient healthy food intake score and overall dietary risk score were positively associated with BMIz. The indirect association analysis indicated that insufficient healthy food intake accounted for 4.94% of the total association between working memory composite score and BMIz. These findings indicate an inverse association between working memory and BMIz in preschool children and suggest a potential indirect association through insufficient healthy food intake. Given the cross-sectional design, prospective studies are needed to clarify the temporal ordering and directionality of these associations.

articles.title: Training the Next Generation: How Are We Preparing Pediatric Residents in Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Care?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatricians are expected to provide sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care to adolescents assigned female at birth (AFAB), yet there is variability in the degree of clinical training pediatric residents receive. This study assesses training opportunities and comfort level of pediatric residents providing SRH care to AFAB adolescents.
METHODS: Third-year pediatric residents and their program directors completed a survey assessing resident training and comfort with SRH clinical skills, and perceived importance of topics. Descriptive statistics summarized participant demographics, and χ² or Fisher exact tests assessed associations between experiences and training settings.
RESULTS: Among 111 pediatric residents at 11 residency programs, 99.1% felt it was important to obtain training in SRH. The majority (65.8%) planned to provide SRH services in future practice. Common barriers to addressing SRH needs included insufficient training and lack of comfort of pediatric attendings. All program directors felt it was important to expand opportunities in SRH clinical skills.
