Conclusions Pediatric residents find value in providing SRH care and most plan to do so after graduation yet may not receive sufficient training. Multiple barriers interfere with provision of SRH care. Standardization of curricula and clinical experiences may increase resident comfort and improve quality of care provided to AFAB youth.

articles.title: Adverse and Positive Childhood Experiences among US Bereaved Youth (2022-2024).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe associations of adverse and positive childhood experiences (ACEs and PCEs) and social demographic characteristics with exposure to parent or guardian death among a nationally representative sample of US youth (6-17 years).
METHODS: We pooled cross-sectional data from the 2022-2024 National Survey of Children's Health (N=101,617). We estimated stepwise Poisson and Negative Binomial regression models testing the association of parent or guardian death with ACEs and PCEs accumulation in both the full sample and racial and ethnic stratified subsamples.
RESULTS: Approximately 4% of youth experienced parent or guardian death and were disproportionately non-Hispanic Black, Native American/Other Race, or from low-income households. Bereaved youth were more likely to be exposed to all ACEs and less likely to be exposed to the majority of PCEs relative to their non-bereaved counterparts. Youth exposed to parent or guardian death exhibited significantly more ACEs (β = 0.40, IRR = 1.49, SE = 0.03), yet a similar number of PCEs (β = -0.02, IRR = 0.98, SE = 0.01), relative to their non-bereaved peers. The association between parent and guardian death and ACEs was no longer significant among non-Hispanic Black (β = 0.15, IRR = 1.16, SE = 0.08) and Native American/Other Race (β = 0.12, IRR = 1.12, SE = 0.11) youth relative to other racial and ethnic groups.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore the elevated and unequal exposure of adversity among youth exposed to parent and guardian death. Implications for targeted pediatric supports that address heightened adversities and inequities within this population are discussed.

articles.title: Caregiver Perspectives on Health-Related Social Needs Disclosure and Perceived Risk of Child Protective Services Involvement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Health-related social needs (HRSN) screening is frequently implemented in pediatric health care settings. Caregivers may be reluctant to disclose HRSN due to fear of Child Protective Services (CPS) involvement, limiting the effectiveness of these efforts. Our primary objectives were (1) to explore caregiver perspectives regarding HRSN disclosure and perceived risk of CPS involvement, and (2) to identify factors that could alleviate concerns regarding inappropriate CPS involvement and improve caregivers' comfort in disclosing HRSN.
METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with caregivers of pediatric inpatients at an academic quaternary care children's hospital. Caregivers were eligible if they were offered a standardized HRSN screener (Linking Families to Support- LiFTS) during their child's hospitalization. Purposive sampling was used to ensure representation across caregiver sociodemographic characteristics. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed by two independent coders using thematic content analysis guided by an adapted health equity implementation framework. Interviews were conducted until thematic saturation was achieved.
RESULTS: We interviewed 25 caregivers who were predominantly Medicaid-insured (60%). Most (64%) disclosed 1+ HRSN. We identified five themes: (1): Balancing benefits of support with perceived risks of HRSN disclosure; (2) potential CPS involvement and fear of family separation; (3) factors and experiences that heighten perceived risks of HRSN disclosure; (4) distinguishing social needs from neglect; (5) trauma-informed practices could facilitate HRSN disclosure.
CONCLUSION: Caregivers valued HRSN screening but described fear of CPS involvement as a barrier to disclosure. Trauma-informed approaches that normalize help-seeking behaviors, emphasize transparency, and distinguish poverty-related need from neglect may improve caregiver engagement with HRSN screening.

articles.title: One-Year Survival After Hybrid Stage 1 Single Ventricle Palliation - The Impact of Institutional Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hybrid stage 1 palliation (HS1P), an alternative to the Norwood procedure for hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), is often reserved for high-risk patients. We aimed to evaluate the survival of HS1P through one year when used as standard palliation strategy for HLHS and similar lesions and to assess changes in survival over time.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of all infants who underwent HS1P for single ventricle palliation. A structured protocol for patient management was developed between 2009 and 2017, with all components implemented by June 2017. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on timing of HS1P: Era 1 (January 2002 - May 2017), and Era 2 (June 2017 - December 2024). The primary outcome was survival through one year.
RESULTS: A total of 281 infants underwent HS1P, 221 in Era 1 and 60 in Era 2. Median age at HS1P was 6 days for both groups. Balloon atrial septostomy at the time of HS1P was significantly more common in Era 2 (43% vs 4% in Era 1), as was use of smaller bands (p <0.001 for both). One-year survival was significantly higher in Era 2 compared to Era 1 (83% vs 65%, p=0.01), and this benefit persisted in multivariable analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study of HS1P used as standard palliation, contemporary survival was excellent with significant improvements in outcomes in more recent years. Further study is needed to understand longer-term outcomes and the interplay of patient risk factors, to help guide best practices.

articles.title: Presenting Complaints for Children in US Emergency Departments: An Analysis of a Nationally Representative Sample.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the presenting complaints for children in the emergency department (ED), both overall and within subgroups of age, acuity and pediatric ED status, and to evaluate changes in complaint patterns over time.
STUDY DESIGN: We performed a serial, cross-sectional study using the 2014-2022 National Hospital Ambulatory Medical Care Survey, including ED encounters for children (<18 years). Our variable of interest was patient complaint, evaluated as (a) the chief complaint and (b) all reported complaints. We described the distribution of patient complaints using the Pediatric Emergency Reason for Visit Clusters (PERC) rubric and examined distributions across subgroups. We evaluated changes in complaints over time using survey-weighted logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of the 277,624,292 ED encounters, the most common chief complaints were fever (37,330,480; 13.4%), extremity injury or pain (30,546,932; 11.0%), cough (22,479,119; 8.1%), abdominal pain (16,867,178; 6.1%), and rash (14,181,775; 5.1%). Fever predominated from infancy through early childhood, whereas extremity injury or pain and abdominal pain became more prominent with increasing age; psychiatric/behavioral complaints emerged notably in adolescence. Fever was most common among immediate and urgent visits, psychiatric/behavioral concerns among emergent visits, extremity injury or pain among semi-urgent visits, and rash among nonurgent visits. Complaint patterns were similar between pediatric and general EDs. Overall findings were similar when considering all reported complaints.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the distribution of complaints was similar over time and between pediatric and general EDs, there were differences based on age and acuity. These findings provide a national characterization of patient complaints that inform pediatric readiness and resource planning.

articles.title: Association of allergic conjunctivitis severity with meibomian gland abnormalities in children: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate associations of allergic conjunctivitis (AC) severity with meibomian gland structure and function and tear film stability in children.
DESIGN: Single-center, cross-sectional study.
PARTICIPANTS: The primary analysis included 144 children: 32 healthy controls and 112 patients with active AC classified as mild (n = 42), moderate (n = 39), or severe (n = 31). Supplementary analyses included 141 adults.
METHODS: Participants underwent standardized ocular surface examinations and noncontact meibography. AC severity was classified according to ocular surface signs. Multivariable linear regression evaluated severity-related associations after adjustment for age, sex, and disease duration.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Total meibomian gland loss (MGL), fluorescein breakup time (FBUT), gland morphology scores, and meibum quality and expressibility scores.
RESULTS: Median total MGL was 9.00%, 20.50%, 31.00%, and 36.00% in the control, mild, moderate, and severe groups, respectively. Corresponding median FBUT values were 9.50, 4.00, 3.00, and 2.00 seconds (both overall P < .001). Meibum expressibility and gland morphology scores differed across groups (both P < .001), whereas meibum quality grade did not (P = .447). After adjustment, each one-category increase in AC severity was associated with 7.54 percentage points higher total MGL (95% CI, 3.17-11.92). Each increase was also associated with 0.72 seconds shorter FBUT (β = -0.72; 95% CI, -0.95 to -0.50; both P < .001). Similar associations were observed in adults.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater AC severity was associated with greater MGL and reduced tear film stability in children. Meibum quality grade, however, did not differ significantly across groups. These findings support including meibomian gland and tear film assessments in the clinical evaluation of pediatric AC. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between AC severity and gland abnormalities.

articles.title: Human cytomegalovirus infection impairs axon formation by inducing inhibitory GSK-3β Ser9 phosphorylation and suppressing ATP synthesis.
articles.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a globally prevalent pathogen known to significantly impact neural development in embryos and young children. Despite its well-established association with neurological disorders, the precise mechanisms through which HCMV infection induces these diseases remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we show that HCMV infection impairs neural cell differentiation by perturbing adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production during the neurogenesis. HCMV infection disrupts the neural differentiation of stem cells derived from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHEDs) and the human neuroblastoma cell line (SH-SY5Ys), alternating the expression of neural cell markers and impairing axon formation. Moreover, under neurogenic inductive conditions, HCMV infection in SHEDs and SH-SY5Ys increases Ser9 phosphorylation levels of GSK-3β, which suppresses GSK-3β kinase activity. This inhibition of GSK-3β activity reduces mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP synthesis, disrupting energy support for neural differentiation. This study reveals a molecular cascade connecting HCMV infection to defective neural differentiation through crosstalk between GSK-3β phosphorylation and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, offering a potential therapeutic target for congenital HCMV infection.

articles.title: Development and In Vitro Evaluation of [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE for Targeted Alpha Therapy of Neuroblastoma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: High-risk neuroblastoma remains a leading cause of pediatric cancer mortality. Radioligand therapy targeting somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2) with the β-emitter [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE) is under clinical investigation. Alpha-emitters such as actinium-225 (²²⁵Ac) cause more potent, localized DNA damage owing to higher linear energy transfer and shorter path length. We aimed to establish a robust labeling protocol for [²²⁵Ac]Ac-DOTATATE (²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE) for preclinical use and to compare its in vitro cytotoxicity with ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE in neuroblastoma cell lines.
METHODS: ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE was synthesized using 5 µg DOTATATE per MBq ²²⁵Ac, and ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE at 60 MBq/nmol in 25 mM sodium ascorbate/50 mM sodium acetate (pH 5). SSTR2-mediated binding of ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE to IMR-32, SK-N-AS and BON cells was measured in real time (LigandTracer). Cytotoxicity was assessed by CellTiter-Glo® viability assay and DNA double-strand breaks by γH2AX immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE was obtained with >95% radiochemical purity and remained stable for at least 48 h. ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE bound specifically to SSTR2-positive IMR-32 cells, with low binding to SSTR2-low BON and minimal binding to SSTR2-negative SK-N-AS cells. The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC₅₀) was 0.0049 kBq/mL for ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE and 5.4 kBq/mL for ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE, an approximately 1000-fold lower activity concentration required for alpha as compared with beta emitter. γH2AX analysis indicated a trend toward greater DNA damage with ²²⁵Ac-DOTATATE. These findings support further development of SSTR2-targeted alpha therapy for high-risk neuroblastoma.

articles.title: Nonverbal reasoning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy: associations with gross motor function, MRI, and EEG findings.
articles.abstract: To examine the association between gross motor function level and Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (CPM) performance in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy (CP), compare CPM performance with typically developing participants, and explore associations with MRI and EEG findings. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 40 participants with CP and 20 comparison participants aged 10-17 years. CPM totals were converted to center-derived age-referenced scores; the upper available normative age band was applied above age 11.5 years. Gross motor function was classified with the GMFCS. Clinically indicated MRI and EEG findings were categorized using prespecified systems. Median CPM score was 72 (IQR 64-81) in the CP group and 98 (IQR 92-104) in the comparison group (adjusted difference -26.4, 95% CI -31.2 to -21.6). GMFCS level was inversely associated with CPM score (Spearman rho = -.78, 95% CI -.85 to -.68). Predominant white matter injury was associated with lower CPM scores. The adjusted association with epileptiform EEG abnormalities was inconclusive. CPM performance was associated with GMFCS level and MRI pattern, but the cross-sectional findings do not establish causality. Gross motor classification must not substitute for accessible neuropsychological assessment.

articles.title: Intraoperative serum sodium variation and postoperative complications: a single-center prospective cohort study in pediatric cardiac surgeries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess intraoperative serum sodium variation in children undergoing low- to moderate-risk cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and examine its association with a composite postoperative outcome.
METHODS: A total of 214 children were evaluated. Intraoperative serum sodium variation was defined as the difference between the highest and lowest observed concentrations. Its association with the composite outcome - defined as neurological, renal, cardiac, or pulmonary complications and/or death - was assessed using univariate and multivariable analyses. Mortality was additionally evaluated in exploratory unadjusted analyses.
RESULTS: Eighty-three children (38.8%) experienced the composite postoperative outcome. Median (interquartile range) intraoperative serum sodium variation was greater in patients with the composite outcome than in those without it (15.0 [10.2-20.0] vs. 8.0 [[5.0-12.0] mmol/L, p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, variation was also greater among non-survivors than survivors (24.0 [20.0-26.5] vs. 10.0 [6.0-15.0] mmol/L, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, sodium variation remained independently associated with the composite outcome (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.06-1.19), together with CPB duration, peak intraoperative arterial lactate level, and body weight.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater intraoperative serum sodium variation was independently associated with a higher probability of the composite postoperative outcome in children undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Exploratory unadjusted analysis also demonstrated greater sodium variation among non-survivors; however, the limited number of deaths precluded adjusted mortality analysis.

articles.title: Coping with developmental coordination disorder: A comparative study of adults and parents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD/Dyspraxia) is a common, yet under-recognised lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterised by motor coordination difficulties affecting daily functioning and psychosocial wellbeing. Coping plays an important role in wellbeing, yet little is known about how adults with DCD manage ongoing challenges or how their coping compares with that of parents of individuals with DCD.
METHODS: One hundred and fourteen participants (90 adults with DCD; 24 parents who raised a child with DCD for at least 16 years) completed an online survey assessing coping, acceptance, optimism, resilience, condition perceptions and life satisfaction. Group differences were examined using MANCOVA and t-tests.
RESULTS: Parents reported greater use of adaptive coping, particularly acceptance, and planning, alongside higher optimism, resilience, and life satisfaction. Adults with DCD relied more on maladaptive coping, notably mental disengagement, which was associated with poorer wellbeing. Acceptance-based coping was a protective factor in both groups. Social support and humour showed no clear association with wellbeing. Greater motor coordination difficulties were associated with increased disengagement and reduced humour use.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with DCD and parents show distinct coping and wellbeing profiles. Findings highlight the need for tailored interventions that promote adaptive coping and acceptance in adults with DCD overall.

articles.title: Longitudinal pulmonary function in children with sickle cell disease after acute chest syndrome: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute chest syndrome (ACS) is one of the most severe complications of sickle cell disease (SCD) and may contribute to long-term pulmonary morbidity. However, its impact on pulmonary function evolution in children remains insufficiently documented.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between ACS and longitudinal changes in pulmonary function parameters in pediatric patients with SCD.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective monocentric study at Reims University Hospital including children with SCD who underwent pulmonary function testing between 2017 and 2025. Patients with a history of ACS were compared with those without ACS. Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁), FEV₁/FVC ratio, and carbon monoxide transfer coefficient (KCO) were analyzed at baseline and after two years of follow-up. Within-group longitudinal analyses were performed. A sensitivity analysis excluding patients with asthma was also conducted.
RESULTS: No significant differences were observed in baseline FEV₁ or at two-year follow-up between ACS and non-ACS groups (p = 0.44 and p = 0.40, respectively). In contrast, the FEV₁/FVC ratio was significantly lower in the ACS group both at baseline and at two years (p = 0.01 and p = 0.03, respectively). Baseline KCO values were higher in patients with ACS (p = 0.01), but no significant difference persisted at follow-up (p = 0.07). Sensitivity analyses excluding patients with asthma yielded similar findings.
CONCLUSION: ACS was not associated with a decline in FEV₁ but was consistently associated with lower FEV₁/FVC ratios, suggesting early airflow limitation. These findings support systematic pulmonary function monitoring in children with SCD, particularly following ACS episodes, to enable early detection of respiratory involvement.

articles.title: The social production of silence and vulnerability after child sexual abuse: A qualitative study of young women from the Romanian child protection system.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child sexual abuse (CSA) is often embedded in broader contexts of cumulative victimization, while opportunities for disclosure and protection are shaped by familial, relational, and institutional conditions. These processes remain insufficiently understood among young people with histories of placement in child protection systems.
OBJECTIVE: This study explored young women's retrospective accounts of CSA and how they understood the conditions shaping silence, vulnerability, disclosure, and recovery in the context of their histories of placement in the Romanian child protection system.
PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Seven women aged 19-27 participated in semi-structured telephone interviews. The interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed in Romanian using a hybrid inductive and theoretically informed thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Participants situated CSA within broader experiences of physical and emotional abuse, neglect, family violence, parental alcohol misuse, and the absence of protective adults. They described silence as shaped by threats, fear, shame, self-blame, dependency, the normalization of violence, uncertainty about institutional responses, and experiences of invalidation. Their accounts presented vulnerability as relationally and structurally conditioned, including through limited or uneven access to protection and support. Trusted adults, educators, psychologists, supportive partners, and educational opportunities were described by participants as supportive resources in relation to disclosure, emotional well-being, autonomy, and the reinterpretation of traumatic experiences.
CONCLUSIONS: Participants' retrospective accounts suggest that silence and vulnerability following CSA cannot be understood solely as individual responses to trauma. They were experienced as shaped by relationships of dependency, normalized violence, responses to disclosure, and access to protective and supportive resources within and beyond the child protection system.

articles.title: Navitoclax and Venetoclax with Chemotherapy for Relapsed/Refractory ALL in Children and Young Adults.
articles.abstract: Despite improving survival rates, a significant number of children, adolescents and young adults (CAYA) with relapsed/refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia (r/r ALL) still die from disease. This calls for new drugs combination to reinduce complete remissions (CR) and enable consolidation. B-cell lymphoma (BCL) family proteins have a key role in regulating the blast apoptotic response to chemotherapy-induced cell damage and the combination of the BCL-2 and BCL-XL/BCL-2 inhibitors (venetoclax [VEN] and navitoclax [NAV], respectively) with chemotherapy could revert the resistance observed in r/r ALL. We retrospectively collected data of NAV/VEN, combined with chemotherapy, in 30 CAYA with advanced, R/R, either B-ALL (n=17) or T-ALL (n=13), treated under compassionate use, in 5 European centers. NAV and VEN (median number of cycles 1, range 1-3) were administered over 28 days. The most common toxicity was hematologic: overall, 93% of the patients developed grade 3-4 neutropenia, 83% grade 3-4 anemia and 83% grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia. No fatal adverse event was recorded. The overall response rate (CR/CRi/PR) was 71% for the B-ALL (12/17 patients) and 50% (6/12) for the T-ALL cohort, allowing, respectively, 11 and 4 patients to receive further consolidation. Six B-ALL patients and 2 T-ALL patients are alive and maintain response, with a median follow-up of 25 (0,6 - 38) and 8 months (0.5-47), respectively. All patients who did not receive consolidation ultimately relapsed and died. Our experience underlines the strong potential of NAV/VEN plus conventional chemotherapy to reinduce complete remission in heavily pretreated and refractory CAYA with either B- or T-ALL.

articles.title: Assessing quality of life during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injuries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess quality of life (QOL) outcomes during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injury (BPBI) and to identify factors linked to poorer outcomes. Additionally, the authors aimed to determine the construct validity of the Impact of a Brachial Plexus Injury Questionnaire (Mancuso scale) for use in the birth injury population.
METHODS: This study utilized a cross-sectional, within-subject comparative survey design to assess the QOL outcomes of adolescents and adults with BPBI. Participants older than 13 years of age and with a history of BPBI were identified using the United Brachial Plexus Network Facebook group. QOL was assessed using the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale-Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) in adults, Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) in adolescents, and a brachial plexus injury-specific tool (Mancuso scale). To determine construct validity, scores from each Mancuso subscale were compared to the participants' overall WHOQOL-BREF scores.
RESULTS: Adults (n = 59) who completed the WHOQOL-BREF had a mean overall score of 63.1 ± 22.2 (0- to 100-point scale). The scores of the Mancuso scale with regard to the symptoms, limitations, and emotion subscales were 45.8 ± 29.5, 35.2 ± 17.3, and 43.6 ± 25.3, respectively. These findings contrasted with the published values from subjects who had sustained a traumatic brachial plexus injury whose scores were 66 ± 18.7, 48.2 ± 22.3, and 39.5 ± 21.2, respectively. For adolescents (n = 4), the overall score on PedsQL was 63.7 ± 21.3. Adolescent scores on the Mancuso scale were 31.7 ± 26.9, 29.8 ± 20.7, and 39.7 ± 18.8, respectively. In adults, severe functional limitation and limited access to care were associated with poorer QOL (p < 0.05), whereas surgical history and occupational therapy attendance did not. Higher scores on the Mancuso subscales correlated with lower quality of life scores on the WHOQOL-BREF. Adolescent data analysis revealed similar, nonsignificant results.
CONCLUSIONS: BPBI plays a role in long-term QOL, notably by the severity of functional limitation and access to care. The Mancuso scale shows promising construct validity in the adult BPBI population, but a larger sample of adolescents is needed.

articles.title: Safety and effectiveness of surgery for medically refractory insular epilepsy in children: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Insular epilepsy is an increasingly diagnosed cause of pediatric drug-refractory focal epilepsy. However, adoption of surgical treatments-resective or ablative-has been limited due to concerns about neurological risks. This systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis aimed to identify predictors of seizure freedom and neurological deficits following surgery in children with insular epilepsy.
METHODS: A systematic search of 4 databases up to August 2024 was undertaken to identify studies reporting postsurgical outcomes in patients aged under 18 years with insular epilepsy. Studies with follow-up under 12 months were excluded. Quality assessment was performed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Education (GRADE) framework, and risk of bias was evaluated using Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Published institutional results from 11 patients were included within the analysis. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify predictors of seizure freedom and neurological complications.
RESULTS: Of 154 identified studies, 12 retrospective studies reporting on 97 patients met the inclusion criteria. The median follow-up duration was 37 months. At last follow up, 57% of patients were seizure free, defined as Engel class I or International League Against Epilepsy class 1 and 2. Patients who underwent preoperative stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) had significantly lower odds of seizure recurrence (OR 0.25, CI 0.06-0.95, p = 0.047). Procedure type (resection vs ablation; OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.13-3.27, p = 0.606), age at surgery (OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.94-1.18, p = 0.392), and surgical extent (insular only versus insular "plus" surgery; OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.17-3.59, p = 0.777) were not significant predictors of seizure freedom. Postoperative permanent neurological deficits occurred in 11% of children, with motor deficits being the most common. Younger age at surgery was associated with greater odds of motor deficit (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.78-0.99, p = 0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first and largest systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to report the outcomes of insular epilepsy surgery in a purely pediatric cohort. Both ablative and resective approaches are feasible, with over half of patients achieving seizure freedom and over two-thirds of neurological deficits being transient.

articles.title: Inferring population-level physiologically based model parameters for sleep in infancy and young childhood.
articles.abstract: The sleep patterns of infants and young children differ from adult sleep patterns, with longer duration and multiple bouts per 24 hours. There is also considerable heterogeneity in infant sleep, both between individuals and within individuals across development. While mathematical models have been used to understand the mechanisms that regulate adult sleep, the development of sleep from infancy through early childhood has remained largely unexplored. Here we used an established mathematical model for adult sleep regulation to investigate how the underlying mechanisms of sleep mature from ages 1 month to 5 years, and identify a basis for inter-individual differences at each age. Using a Bayesian approach to estimate joint distributions of model parameters at different ages, we found that: (i) decreases in the rate of accumulation of sleep homeostatic pressure captured the reduction in sleep duration across development; while (ii) increases in the time scale of the sleep homeostatic drive captured the consolidation of sleep into fewer sleep bouts per day across development. In terms of inter-individual differences, we found larger spread in the parameters within the earlier stages of infancy (<1 year). The center and boundaries of the joint distributions evolved with age through the parameter space, converging towards previously described adult parameter values. A bifurcation analysis of the homeostatic time scale parameter revealed that progressive consolidation of sleep occurs through abrupt loss of bouts one at a time, punctuated by narrow intervals of non-entrained (>24-h) cycles. These results establish plausible, population-level trajectories in physiological parameters underpinning maturation of sleep regulation through infancy and early childhood.

articles.title: Changes in posture and balance in children with cerebral palsy assessed using DIERS formetric 4D and clinical scales: An exploratory single-group pre-post observational study.
articles.abstract: Spinopelvic alignment contributes to postural control and balance in children with cerebral palsy. This study aimed to evaluate baseline-to-follow-up changes in DIERS Formetric 4D parameters and explore their associations with changes in clinical measures of balance and trunk control. This exploratory, single-group pre-post observational study included 56 children with cerebral palsy aged 5 to 18 years and classified at Gross Motor Function Classification System levels I to III. Participants received individualized rehabilitation as part of routine care. DIERS parameters and Pediatric Balance Scale, Trunk Control Measurement Scale, and Trunk Impairment Scale scores were assessed at baseline and follow-up. Change was calculated as follow-up minus baseline. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure was applied within defined analysis families. The mean age was 9.86 ± 4.37 years, and 48.2% of participants were female. All 10 clinical total and subscale scores improved significantly after correction. Among 40 DIERS parameters, coronal imbalance, pelvic obliquity, apical deviation root mean square, and apical deviation amplitude changed significantly after correction. Of 400 Spearman correlations between DIERS and clinical change scores, 15 had unadjusted P values below .05, but none remained significant after correction. Selected DIERS parameters and clinical measures changed significantly between baseline and follow-up; however, changes in DIERS parameters were not significantly associated with clinical changes after multiple-testing correction. DIERS Formetric 4D may provide supplementary objective information on spinopelvic alignment but should not replace validated clinical assessments. The clinical relevance of longitudinal changes requires confirmation in controlled prospective studies.

articles.title: Prenatal clinical features and clinical outcomes of fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome: A single-center case series of 22 patients.
articles.abstract: This study analyzes 22 fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome in Eastern China to investigate the prenatal clinical features and postnatal outcomes. We conducted a retrospective study of 22 fetuses diagnosed with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion (312-855 kilobase) via chromosomal microarray analysis among 2607 prenatal cases from January 2022 to September 2024. Parental origin, ultrasound findings, and postnatal outcomes were evaluated. The 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion prevalence was 0.84% (22/2607). Prenatal ultrasound anomalies were observed in 54.5% (12/22), primarily mild cardiac findings (tricuspid regurgitation), choroid plexus cysts, and thickened nuchal translucency. Parental testing (13 cases) revealed 6 paternal, 6 maternal, and 1 de novo case. Postnatal follow-up of 18 live births (mean 14.7 months) showed normal development in most cases (17/18), with 1 child exhibiting delayed language development. Four pregnancies (18.2%) were terminated despite genetic counseling. Our study underscores that the 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion exhibits incomplete penetrance and variable prenatal phenotypes, complicating outcome prediction. Long-term pediatric follow-up is essential, and early reassurance should be avoided even in cases with normal prenatal findings or favorable short-term outcomes.

articles.title: The effect of physical exercise on sleep quality in Chinese middle school students: A cross-sectional study on the mediating role of positive and negative emotions.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to explore the effect of physical exercise (PE1) on sleep quality (SQ) among Chinese middle school students and to further analyze the mediating roles of positive and negative emotions (NE). A total of 1056 middle school students (aged 11-15 years, M = 13.28, SD = 1.08; 516 males, 540 females) from 6 middle schools in Sichuan Province, China, voluntarily participated in this cross-sectional survey. The Physical Activity Rating Scale, Positive and Negative Affect Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index were used in this study. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0. Mediation analyses (model 4) were conducted with the PROCESS 3.5 macro, and the significance of indirect effects was tested using a bias-corrected nonparametric percentile bootstrap method with 5000 resamples, generating 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The total effect of PE1 on SQ was not significant (P > .05). After controlling for positive and NE, the direct effect of PE1 on SQ was also non-significant (P > .05). However, both positive emotions (indirect effect = 0.032, 95% CI [0.015, 0.051]) and NE (indirect effect = 0.037, 95% CI [0.012, 0.064]) played significant mediating roles in the relationship between PE1 and SQ. These findings suggest that PE1 improves SQ in middle school students primarily by enhancing positive emotions and reducing NE, rather than through a direct effect.

articles.title: Associations of personalized prenatal care with delivery and perinatal outcomes in women with high-risk pregnancies.
articles.abstract: This study examines whether the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with delivery and perinatal outcomes among women with high-risk pregnancies in a retrospective observational cohort. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 100 women with high-risk pregnancies who delivered between January 2020 and December 2023. Participants were classified according to documented receipt of personalized prenatal care or routine prenatal care. Propensity scores were estimated using maternal age, gravidity, parity, pre pregnancy or early-pregnancy body mass index, gestational age at registration, gestational diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, thyroid dysfunction, uterine scar, and history of adverse pregnancy outcomes. One-to-one nearest-neighbor matching without replacement was performed using a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score. All 100 women were retained after matching. Outcomes were analyzed using unadjusted independent-group comparisons (50 women per group). Vaginal delivery was more frequent in the personalized-care group than in the routine-care group (62.0% vs 40.0%), corresponding to an absolute difference of +22.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], +2.4- + 39.3) and an odds ratio (OR) of 2.45 (95% CI, 1.10-5.47; P = .028). Cesarean delivery occurred in 28.0% and 48.0% of women, respectively, corresponding to an absolute difference of -20.0 percentage points (95% CI, -37.1-- 1.0) and an OR of 0.42 (95% CI, 0.18-0.97). Preterm birth occurred in 10.0% versus 26.0% of women (absolute difference, -16.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -30.7- - 0.8; OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.10-0.97; P = .037). One and 5-minute Apgar scores were higher in the personalized-care group (P = .026 and P = .006, respectively). The composite adverse perinatal outcome, defined as the occurrence of at least one of preterm birth, low birth weight, neonatal asphyxia, or neonatal intensive care unit admission, occurred in 16.0% versus 36.0% of women (absolute difference, -20.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -35.8- - 2.8; OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.13-0.88; P = .023). In this study, the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with differences in delivery patterns, selected neonatal outcomes, nursing-compliance measures, and end-of-care psychological scores. The findings represent associations rather than causal effects and should be interpreted in light of the small sample size, residual confounding, and limited statistical power for several individual outcomes.

articles.title: Global burden of HBV/HCV-related liver diseases, 1990-2021, and projections to 2050: A global burden of disease study 2021.
articles.abstract: Despite the availability of measures to control hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related diseases, achieving elimination remains a substantial challenge. Effective action demands accurate assessment of the present and anticipation of the future. We utilized data from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2021 to estimate the global burden of HBV- and HCV-related diseases for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. We defined HBV/HCV-related liver disease to include chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, and cirrhosis attributable to chronic HBV or HCV. The burden was assessed using the age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR), stratified by region, age, sex, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI). GBD estimates were reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs); 1990 to 2021 percentage changes were calculated from point estimates. Forecasting analysis was conducted using the GBD 2021 forecast framework, supplemented by Das Gupta decomposition analysis. From 1990 to 2021, the global ASMRs of HBV- and HCV-related cirrhosis declined by 41.51% and 31.47%, respectively, while liver cancer-related ASMR showed divergent changes (HBV: -16.40%; HCV: +2.35%). ASDRs also declined across both cirrhosis and liver cancer (HBV: -42.07%, -22.34%; HCV: -29.34%, -8.24%). Regionally, the highest ASMRs for chronic hepatitis B and C including cirrhosis in 2021 were observed in Eastern Sub-Saharan Africa (14.51 per 1,00,000) and Central Sub-Saharan Africa (13.92 per 1,00,000), respectively. The burden of both viruses was generally higher in men. Age-specific mortality rates were highest in older age groups across HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases. By the late 2030s, the mortality burden of chronic hepatitis C is projected to surpass that of chronic hepatitis B, amid a slowing annual decline in the ASMR of chronic hepatitis C (-1.21% to -0.24%). Although the overall burden of HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases may decrease or stabilize, sustained progress hinges on equitable access to vaccination, optimized antiviral therapies, and a renewed global focus on HCV as its relative impact grows. Achieving meaningful reductions across SDI contexts will require not only scientific advances but also strategic efforts to improve affordability and distribution, supported by the political will to implement change.

articles.title: Nonlinear relationship between AST/ALT levels and MASLD: A secondary cross-sectional study in healthy Japanese individuals.
articles.abstract: Fatty liver disease is a prevalent condition worldwide, particularly in developed countries. Previous studies have examined the relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and both metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and alcohol-associated liver disease. However, there is a scarcity of research focusing specifically on the association between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD. The objective of this study is to investigate the relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD in healthy Japanese individuals. This study was a cross-sectional analysis involving 15,464 participants, comprising 7034 men and 8430 women, aged between 18 and 79 years. Data for this secondary analysis were obtained from the Dryad Digital Repository. A medical professional utilized ultrasound imaging to assess the presence of fatty liver disease and administered a questionnaire to gather information about lifestyle factors, including smoking history, alcohol consumption, and exercise habits. Hematological indicators were evaluated at Murakami Memorial Hospital from 2004 to 2015. By adjusting for sex, age, body mass index, waist circumference, regular exercise, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total cholesterol, triglycerides, HbA1c (%), alcohol consumption, smoking status, fasting plasma glucose, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, body weight, gamma-glutamyl transferase, and triglycerides, we identified a nonlinear relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD. This relationship exhibited a significant notable threshold at an AST/ALT ratio of 0.95, with odds ratio values of 0.03 (0.02, 0.05) when the ratio was <0.95, and 0.32 (0.22, 0.46) when the ratio was greater than or equal to 0.95. Furthermore, in subgroup analyses, we observed that the relationship between AST/ALT levels and fatty liver varied across different subgroups based on gender, alcohol consumption, and smoking status, with the exception of exercise. There is a nonlinear relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD, with a more pronounced negative correlation observed when the ratio is <0.95. These findings suggest that the AST/ALT ratio may provide supportive information for risk stratification in MASLD, particularly when interpreted in conjunction with sex and lifestyle factors. However, prospective validation of the 0.95 threshold in diverse populations is warranted before any clinical application.

articles.title: Relationship between baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels and the incidence of maternal fever after epidural labor analgesia: A cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels and the incidence of maternal fever after epidural labor analgesia. Blood samples were collected from the median cubital vein, and serum IL-6 concentrations were measured using up-converting phosphor technology. Based on the IL-6 concentration results, parturients were categorized into 2 groups: the normal baseline IL-6 group and the elevated baseline IL-6 group. Demographic and clinical data including maternal age, gestational week, height, weight, body mass index, basal body temperature, intra-labor temperature, number of cervical examinations, duration of the first and second stages of labor, neonatal 1-minute and 5-minute Apgar scores, cesarean section rate, instrumental delivery rate, neonatal transfer, and mechanical ventilation were recorded. The overall incidence of intrapartum fever was higher in the elevated IL-6 group, and mean maternal temperature was also higher at 3 and 9 hours after analgesia (P < .05). No significant differences were observed in other indices (P > .05). Elevated baseline IL-6 was associated with a higher unadjusted incidence of intrapartum fever among women receiving epidural labor analgesia.

articles.title: The trends and hotspots of research on polycystic ovary syndrome in adolescents over the past three decades: A bibliometric analysis from 1995 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women, with increasing research attention directed toward adolescent populations. However, no comprehensive bibliometric analysis has systematically mapped the research landscape in this subspecialty. This study aimed to evaluate global research trends and hotspots in adolescent PCOS over the past 3 decades using bibliometric methods.
METHODS: Publications on adolescent PCOS from 1995 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer and Citespace were employed for data analysis and visualization, while key bibliometric indicators were computed and presented in tabular form.
RESULTS: A total of 1070 publications were included. Research output steadily increased over time, with the United States (n = 384, 35.89%), Turkey (n = 105, 9.81%), and India (n = 82, 7.66%) being the most productive countries. The most prominent institutions included the University of Pittsburgh, the University of Barcelona, and Monash University. Ibanez, Lourdes (n = 34) was the most prolific author, while the Journal of Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology (n = 84) and the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism (highest citations, n = 6921) were the leading publication platforms. Core research areas encompassed mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment, metabolism, and clinical outcomes. Keyword burst detection identified "diagnosis" (strength = 14.12) and "luteinizing hormone" (strength = 13.6) as the most intense hotspots. Notably, "quality of life" (2020-2024) and "depression" (2015-2024) emerged as the most recent and ongoing research frontiers.
CONCLUSION: This first bibliometric analysis of adolescent PCOS reveals growing global interest and active international collaborations in this field. Future research is expected to focus on refining diagnostic approaches and improving long-term quality of life for adolescent PCOS.

articles.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.
METHODS: The data are derived from the Web of Science Core Collection and the PubMed database, covering relevant literature on asthma during pregnancy. The time range is from 2008 to 2024. The search strategy combined asthma-related terms ("asthma" OR "bronchial asthma") with pregnancy-related terms ("pregnancy" OR "gestation" OR "gestational"). After screening, 4088 eligible publications were included in the bibliometric analysis. A separate search of PubMed identified 28 clinical trials for the supplementary analysis of clinical research progress. Bibliometric analyses and visualization were performed using the bibliometrix R package (developed by Massimo Aria and Corrado Cuccurullo, Department of Economics and Statistics, University of Naples Federico II [with an academic spin-off, K-Synth Srl, associated with its dissemination]), CiteSpace (developed by Chaomei Chen, College of Computing and Informatics, Drexel University), and VOSviewer (developed by Nees Jan van Eck and Ludo Waltman, Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Leiden University).
RESULTS: This study comprised 4088 publications focusing on asthma during pregnancy. Annual publication counts demonstrated a gradual increase with intermittent fluctuations. The United States dominated both in publication output and international collaboration. Litonjua AA, Bisgaard H, and Weiss ST demonstrated high centrality and citation influence among authors. The core contributing journals included Pediatric Allergy and Immunology and Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. Major research focuses encompassed mechanistic exploration, influencing factors, and fetal and child health. Research hotspots were primarily concentrated on "air pollution," "birth cohort," "pregnancy complications," and "maternal diet." In recent years, emerging research frontiers have included "inflammation," "impact," "gut microbiota," "climate change," and "survivors." Clinical trial analysis highlighted nutritional interventions (particularly vitamin D) and precision management using biomarkers like fractional exhaled nitric oxide as current research priorities.
CONCLUSION: This work examined the evolving trends and trajectories within pregnancy asthma research, offering a systematic roadmap for subsequent studies. The article highlighted the main contributors, research hotspots, emerging frontier topics, and key directions for future research. This study can serve as a crucial reference for researchers in this field and relevant stakeholders.

articles.title: JUVENILE IDIOPATHIC ARTHRITIS IN CHILDREN WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES: IMPACT OF CURRENT MEDICAL TREATMENT OPTIONS ON ANTHROPOMETRY AND METABOLIC CONTROL.
articles.abstract: Children with both type 1 diabetes (T1D) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) face increased disease complexity due to overlapping autoimmune and inflammatory processes. This study aimed to assess anthropometric, metabolic, and cardiovascular risk factors compared to children with T1D alone. Data from the Diabetes Patient Follow-up (DPV) registry (1995-2023) were analyzed, comparing 489 children with T1D and JIA to 67,462 children with T1D only. Children with T1D and JIA used diabetes technologies (insulin pumps, CGM, AID systems) more frequently with similar HbA1c levels. Between 2014-2019 and 2020-2023, HbA1c levels significantly improved in the JIA group, while BMI and height approached the T1D only group. Despite increased disease burden, children with T1D and JIA achieve glycemic control comparable to those with T1D alone. Nonetheless, elevated cardiometabolic risks highlight the need for tailored, interdisciplinary care strategies.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of photon radiotherapy versus proton beam therapy for pediatric Ewing sarcoma: Tsukuba Review Project-Ewing sarcoma 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in multimodal treatment strategies and chemotherapy have led to improved outcomes for patients with Ewing sarcoma (EWS). Proton beam therapy (PBT) has increasingly been utilized in pediatric oncology to minimize late toxicities associated with conventional treatments; however, studies addressing the use of PBT in EWS remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a meta-analysis to compare the efficacy of photon radiotherapy (RT) and PBT in pediatric EWS. We analyzed English-language articles published between 1990 and 2022. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and local control (LC).
RESULTS: A total of 38 studies from 36 articles (8 reporting PBT and 30 reporting photon RT) were included in the meta-analysis. PBT showed better 5-year OS and 4- and 3-year LC rates compared to photon RT, while a higher proportion of male patients and a higher rate of concurrent surgery were associated with better OS at selected time points. In a post hoc exploratory analysis restricted to studies published since 2015, only PBT was associated with improved 5-year OS.
DISCUSSION: The observed differences across the entire study period may be attributed to improvements in treatment protocols, including interval-compressed chemotherapy, and recent advancements in supportive care and radiation technology, which could have influenced outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: PBT appears to provide treatment outcomes that are comparable to those of photon RT in pediatric EWS. Further studies are needed to assess long-term outcomes and the treatment-related toxicities of PBT.

articles.title: The global macroeconomic burden of idiopathic epilepsy: estimates for 2021 and projections to 2050.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic epilepsy imposes substantial health and economic burdens worldwide, yet evidence on welfare-based macroeconomic losses attributable specifically to idiopathic epilepsy remains limited. This study estimated the global, regional, and national welfare burden of idiopathic epilepsy across 190 countries and territories in 2021 and projected this burden to 2050.
METHODS: Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and healthy life expectancy were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021; gross domestic product (GDP) and GDP per capita from the World Bank's World Development Indicators database; and country-, sex-, and age-specific population estimates and medium-variant projections from the United Nations World Population Prospects 2024. VLW was estimated using the value of a statistical life and the value of a statistical life year and expressed in purchasing power parity-adjusted constant 2021 international dollars. Age- and sex-specific DALY rates were projected to 2050 using exponential smoothing state-space models and combined with the corresponding population projections.
RESULTS: In 2021, the global undiscounted VLW attributable to idiopathic epilepsy was Int$1,138.013 billion, equivalent to 0.737% of global GDP. By 2050, it was projected to reach Int$1,287.730 billion, equivalent to 0.834% of the 2021 global GDP benchmark and 13.156% above the 2021 level. Absolute VLW was concentrated in high-income and populous regions, particularly the United States, China, and India, whereas the relative burden was greatest in low-SDI regions and Sub-Saharan Africa. Higher VLW was observed among adolescents, young and middle-aged adults, and males.
CONCLUSIONS: Idiopathic epilepsy causes substantial and growing global welfare losses with marked inequalities. Strengthening prevention, diagnosis, affordable antiseizure medication access, primary care integration, and anti-stigma interventions is essential, especially in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Intrarater reliability of expert electroencephalographic interpretation of 100 full-length recordings.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The value of electroencephalography (EEG) relies on accurate and reliable interpretation. Prior research has demonstrated imperfect interrater reliability, but intrarater reliability remains poorly characterized. We performed a "noise audit" primarily to measure intrarater variability in EEG interpretation by epileptologists.
METHODS: Experts independently rated the same 100 full-length EEGs on two separate occasions ≥60 days apart, unaware the EEGs were the same. EEGs were recorded from adult (56%) and pediatric patients in outpatient (78%) and non-critical care inpatient settings. There were 20 studies in each of five categories: normal, focal epileptiform (FE), generalized epileptiform (GE), focal nonepileptiform (FNE), and generalized nonepileptiform (GNE) abnormalities. EEGs were presented using our online platform (EEGHub) without clinical information except for age and sex. Experts rated each recording and indicated their level of confidence (LOC) for each EEG and overall. We analyzed percent as well as chance-corrected intra- and interrater agreement.
RESULTS: Fourteen experts (mean of 19 years EEG reading experience, range = 4-52 years) were included in the study. Percent self-agreement was 96% for GE, 90% for FE, 88% for FNE, and 87% for GNE abnormalities; 90% for any epileptiform abnormality; and 82% for any nonepileptiform abnormality. Self-agreement was strongly correlated with interrater agreement (mean κML), which was almost perfect for GE (.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .87-.94) and FE (.82, 95% CI = .77-.87) and substantial for GNE (.75, 95% CI = .69-.81) and FNE (.74, 95% CI = .68-.80) abnormalities. LOC correlated with self-agreement on the presence of nonepileptiform but not epileptiform abnormalities.
SIGNIFICANCE: We found generally strong within-expert agreement in EEG interpretation, especially in the identification of epileptiform abnormalities. Nevertheless, the number of flipped decisions was high enough to be clinically consequential. This undesired variability ("occasion noise") may be addressed by interventions to (1) decrease this noise directly and (2) reduce case ambiguity with longer recordings and better EEG data whenever feasible.

articles.title: Paediatric complex regional pain syndrome type 1 in Italy: a national survey of diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Complex regional pain syndrome type 1 (CRPS-1) is a rare but potentially disabling condition, with limited paediatric-specific evidence to guide clinical management. This study aimed to describe diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to paediatric CRPS-1 among Italian centres providing paediatric rheumatology care. A cross-sectional electronic survey was distributed to 34 Italian centres providing paediatric rheumatology care. The questionnaire explored referral patterns, diagnosis, management strategies, availability of formal management protocols, disease burden, and follow-up procedures. Data were analysed descriptively. Twenty-three of 34 centres participated (67.6%). In most centres (17/23, 73.9%), the majority of patients were referred without a prior diagnostic suspicion of CRPS-1, and paediatric rheumatologists most frequently established the diagnosis. In 9/23 centres (39.1%), CRPS-1 was diagnosed more than 3 months after symptom onset in the majority of patients. Multidisciplinary care was widely adopted, with physiotherapy and psychological support routinely incorporated into clinical care in 22/23 (95.7%) and 21/23 (91.3%) centres, respectively. Initial management most commonly combined pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions (14/21, 66.7%). Pharmacological strategies were heterogeneous, with only 2/23 centres (8.7%) having a formal protocol. More than 90% of centres (21/23) rated the impact of CRPS-1 on patients and their families as severe or very severe.
CONCLUSION: This national survey shows substantial convergence in the core principles of multidisciplinary paediatric CRPS-1 management despite the absence of specific guidelines. Future collaborative research should strengthen the paediatric evidence base to support more robust clinical recommendations, while improving awareness among primary care paediatricians and other frontline clinicians should remain a priority to facilitate earlier recognition and timely referral.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Paediatric CRPS-1 is uncommon and potentially disabling, with limited paediatric-specific evidence to guide diagnosis and treatment. • Multidisciplinary rehabilitation and psychological support are key components of treatment, whereas pharmacological management remains poorly standardised.
WHAT IS NEW: • This first Italian multicentre survey shows substantial agreement on the core principles of multidisciplinary care, despite heterogeneity in pharmacological treatment and the limited availability of formal management protocols. • Delayed recognition remains a relevant challenge: in nearly 40% of participating centres, CRPS-1 was diagnosed more than three months after symptom onset in the majority of patients.

articles.title: Clinical analysis of rare chylous mesenteric cyst in children.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chylous Mesenteric Cysts (CMCs) are rare intra-abdominal masses in children, and definitive preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. This study reviews the diagnosis and management of CMCs at a single institution, with particular attention to clinical characteristics and the effectiveness of laparoscopic surgery. A retrospective analysis was performed on the records of all patients diagnosed with CMCs and treated with laparoscopic surgery at our institution between January 2020 and May 2026. Clinical manifestations, preoperative imaging data, surgical techniques, postoperative complications, and patient outcomes were evaluated. The study cohort included three girls and five boys. The median age was 4.2 years (range, 0.1 to 9.0 years), and the median weight was 14.5 kg (range, 4.9 to 32.5 kg). Abdominal pain and vomiting were the most common symptoms, occurring in 62.5% of cases. Four patients experienced cyst-related complications: three developed intestinal volvulus, and one presented with intestinal volvulus accompanied by intestinal obstruction. Sole cyst excision was conducted in two cases, while en bloc resection of the cyst with bowel was performed in six cases. Laparoscopic surgery was completed successfully in seven patients; one case required conversion to open surgery. The mean operative time was 103 ± 31 min. Pathological examination identified lymphatic malformation containing chylous fluid in all patients, findings consistent with mesenteric chylous cyst. No peritoneal infection, anastomotic leakage, or cyst recurrence was observed during short and medium term follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Chylous mesenteric cysts are most often definitively diagnosed during surgery. Once confirmed, prompt removal is recommended to prevent complications. Laparoscopic cyst excision or cyst excision with bowel resection appears to be a feasible approach for pediatric patients with uncomplicated chylous mesenteric cysts.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • CMCs are rare, benign lymphatic malformations of the small-bowel mesentery in children that can result in severe complications such as intestinal volvulus and obstruction. Definitive pre-operative diagnosis of CMC is challenging, with most cases confirmed during surgery. • Surgical resection is the standard treatment. Open surgery has long been mainstream, while laparoscopy is increasingly applied.
WHAT IS NEW: • Transumbilical single-port laparoscopy appears feasible in selected paediatric patients with uncomplicated CMC. Extensive or poorly demarcated lesions may require conversion to open surgery. • Definitive preoperative diagnosis was uncommon in this small cohort and in the limited literature reviewed. The transumbilical approach may offer a cosmetically favourable incision and facilitate specimen extraction. Complete resection was followed by favourable short and medium term outcomes in this series; however, the small sample size and absence of a comparator group preclude firm conclusions.

articles.title: SH3TC2-Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4 C: an Italian multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4 C (CMT4C), caused by biallelic variants in SH3TC2, is the most common autosomal recessive demyelinating neuropathy. Italian multicentre data with detailed genotype-phenotype characterisation are lacking. Yet knowledge of the natural history is urgently needed as SH3TC2 gene replacement therapy approaches clinical trials following a successful Pre-Investigational New Drug meeting with the FDA in November 2024.
METHODS: We screened 684 patients with genetically unresolved CMT using a combination of exome analysis and a multigene next-generation sequencing panel and identified nine (from five Italian neurology centres) with biallelic SH3TC2 variants. All patients underwent standardised neurological examination, nerve conduction studies, and assessment using the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Examination Score version 2 (CMTESv2). Variant pathogenicity was assessed according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) criteria incorporating REVEL (Rare Exome Variant Ensemble Learner) and CADD (Combined Annotation-Dependent Depletion) scores.
RESULTS: Nine patients (5 males, 4 females; age 3.5-66 years) were studied. Twelve distinct SH3TC2 variants were identified, including four not previously reported: p.Glu794* (likely pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP guidelines), p.Gly18Ser (variant of unknown significance, VUS), p.Ala526Thr (VUS), and p.Thr1098Ile (VUS). Scoliosis was present in 6/9 patients (66.7%), foot deformities in 7/9 (77.8%), and sensorineural hearing loss in 2/9 (22.2%). Genotype-phenotype analysis revealed marked intra-class variability, including a 59-year-old with homozygous frameshift variants and near-normal function (CMTESv2 total score of 3). One patient was diagnosed presymptomatically at age 3.5 years through cascade genetic testing prompted by comorbid features of Angelman syndrome. All seven symptomatic patients showed motor nerve conduction velocities below 35 m/s. Novel variants p.Gly18Ser and p.Ala526Thr are of uncertain significance and require functional validation: p.Ala526Thr lies immediately adjacent to the functionally characterised pathogenic residue Arg529, whereas p.Gly18Ser lies 16 residues from the myristoylation site at Gly2, within a segment of very low predicted model confidence.
CONCLUSIONS: This Italian multicentre cohort expands the SH3TC2 mutational spectrum highlighting the marked phenotypic variability of CMT4C, and the possibility of presymptomatic identification through multigene NGS panels. Our data contribute to the evidence base required for the design of forthcoming gene therapy clinical trials.

articles.title: A diagnostic model for central precocious puberty in girls based on ultrasonic bone age and clinical indicators.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central precocious puberty is a common pediatric endocrine disorder in girls. The diagnostic gold standard, the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test, is invasive, limiting its widespread use. Ultrasound-based bone age assessment is radiation-free, but its diagnostic value within an integrated model remains unvalidated.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a diagnostic model integrating ultrasound bone age advancement (ΔBA_OA) with clinical and biochemical markers for the differential diagnosis of central precocious puberty in girls.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 269 girls initially diagnosed with precocious puberty were enrolled. Based on GnRH stimulation test results, they were divided into central precocious puberty (n=66) and non-central precocious puberty (n=203) groups. Clinical data, pelvic ultrasound parameters, hormone levels, and ultrasound bone age parameters were collected. Independent predictors were identified using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: ΔBA_OA (odds ratio (OR)=61.05), basal luteinizing hormone (LH) (OR=8.76), and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) (OR=1.02) were independent predictors (all P<0.001). Standardized coefficients confirmed comparable contributions from ΔBA_OA (β=0.675) and LH (β=0.637). The model demonstrated good apparent discriminative ability (AUC=0.972, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.950-0.993). Bootstrap internal validation with 200 resampling iterations yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.968 (95% CI: 0.953-0.992), with a calibration slope of 0.906 and intercept of -0.015, indicating minimal overfitting and satisfactory calibration. The calibration curve showed good agreement (mean absolute error (MAE)=0.016), and DCA indicated positive net benefit. Discrimination remained high across subgroups (AUC 0.959-0.994), though subgroup estimates were exploratory and based on limited event numbers.
CONCLUSION: The proposed model incorporating ultrasound bone age parameter ΔBA_OA with clinical and biochemical markers showed preliminary evidence of apparent discriminative ability. The model is intended as an auxiliary screening tool that may help reduce unnecessary GnRH stimulation testing, but this requires prospective validation. External validation in multicenter, large-sample studies is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Percutaneous Electrical Nerve Field Stimulation: Revitalizing the Management of Neurogastrointestinal Motility Disorders.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Neurogastrointestinal motility disorders and disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are difficult to treat, particularly with pharmacotherapy alone. This review examines percutaneous electrical nerve field stimulation (PENFS) as a non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, addressing its potential mechanistic rationale, clinical evidence, patient selection, practical implementation, and future directions of research.
RECENT FINDINGS: PENFS appears to act through several pathways: limbic modulation via the central nucleus of the amygdala, altered vagal afferent signaling at the nucleus tractus solitarius, and effects on an enteric nervous system that continues to mature through adolescence. Randomized sham-controlled trials and a multicenter registry show improvement in pain, nausea, and disability alongside a favorable safety profile. Auricular allodynia and impaired cardiac vagal efficiency are emerging as markers of treatment response. PENFS is a safe, effective, non-pharmacologic option across the DGBI spectrum. Formal dose- and duration-response work, adult trials, and long-term durability data remain the principal gaps, though work is ongoing.

articles.title: Lung ultrasound in congenital heart disease: from physiology to precision medicine.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects approximately 8 per 1000 births worldwide. Approximately 25% are classified as critical congenital heart disease (CCHD), requiring early diagnosis and neonatal intervention. Management of these patients is complex, dynamic and multiparametric. Respiratory complications are common during the hospitalization of patients with CHD. Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a valuable bedside tool to accurately assess lung aeration, particularly in critically ill patients in whom conventional imaging techniques may be difficult to obtain, impractical, or challenging to interpret. Although growing evidence supports the use of LUS throughout the perioperative and postoperative period, its application remains insufficiently characterized. LUS is evolving beyond its traditional role as a diagnostic imaging modality toward a dynamic bedside monitoring tool, with the potential to guide and optimize respiratory management before, during, and after cardiac surgery.
CONCLUSION: This review aims to summarize the current evidence regarding the use of LUS in this population and to highlight its potential role in the assessment and management of preoperative and postoperative respiratory complications.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Lung ultrasound (LUS) is a bedside, radiation-free imaging technique that provides real-time information on pulmonary aeration, interstitial edema, pleural effusion, atelectasis, and pneumothorax in children with congenital heart disease (CHD). • Pulmonary abnormalities in CHD are closely related to the underlying hemodynamic physiology and may change dynamically throughout the preoperative, perioperative, and postoperative periods. However, the clinical application of LUS in this population remains heterogeneous and is not yet routinely integrated into CHD management.
WHAT IS NEW: • This review summarizes the current evidence on LUS in CHD from a pathophysiological perspective, linking ultrasound findings to the underlying cardiac physiology and highlighting potential pitfalls in their interpretation. • LUS may contribute to a precision-medicine approach in children with CHD by integrating bedside pulmonary phenotyping with clinical and echocardiographic assessment, while identifying key areas where prospective studies are needed to establish standardized protocols and determine whether LUS-guided management improves clinically relevant outcomes.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and lipid parameters in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: systematic review & meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Although inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may lead to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, evidence regarding cardiovascular and lipid parameters in childhood is limited. We compared vascular markers, blood pressure and lipid levels between patients with pediatric or childhood-onset IBD and controls. This study was performed according to the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A search of major databases (MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library) was conducted from inception until April 24, 2025 (CRD420251039588). The study quality was evaluated using the modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; statistical analysis was conducted using R software. Reactive hyperemia index (RHI) was lower in three studies, involving 109 participants (MD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.48 to - 0.02; p = 0.03). No statistically significant difference in carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) was detected based on six studies. Primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling across ten studies, was also not statistically significant (MD 0.84 mmHg, 95% CI - 0.67 to 2.35; p = 0.28). The exclusion of one influential study resulted in a small difference in SBP (MD 1.89 mmHg, 95% CI 1.17 to 2.61). Primary analyses detected no statistically significant differences in diastolic blood pressure or lipid levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower RHI suggests possible early endothelial dysfunction, but the evidence is preliminary. No difference was observed in cIMT, DBP and lipid levels between the two groups. Future prospective cohort studies should investigate the longitudinal changes in these parameters, in order to elucidate whether early alterations lead, in the long-term, to increased cardiovascular morbidity in adulthood.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by persistent gastrointestinal inflammation and immune activation. • IBD may lead to an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease. However, limited data exist regarding cardiovascular parameters on pediatric IBD patients.
WHAT IS NEW: • Lower Reactive Hyperemia Index (RHI) suggests possible endothelial dysfunction; carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) and lipid levels remain inconclusive. • No statistically significant difference in cIMT was detected between participants with IBD and controls; primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling was not statistically significant; a small increase appeared only after exclusion of one study.

articles.title: DiaMEETes: A Collective Narrative and Play-Based Group Intervention for Children Aged 8-10 Living With Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Children aged 8-10 living with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) may experience emotional distress, isolation, and difficulties adjusting to diabetes management. While collective narrative practice groups have been adapted successfully for older children with T1D, a developmentally appropriate intervention for younger children was needed. This paper describes DiaMEETes, a multidisciplinary group intervention combining collective narrative practices, play, and peer support. DiaMEETes was co-developed with young people with lived experience of T1D and delivered within a paediatric psychology service. Activities aimed to externalise diabetes, strengthen identity beyond illness, foster peer connection, and build hope. Thirty children aged 8-11 attended between 2021 and 2025. Quantitative and qualitative feedback was collected from children and parents/carers and analysed using thematic analysis. Seventy-two percent of attendees rated the group 10/10 and 89% would recommend it to others. Five themes were identified: connection and shared experiences, enjoyment of activities, finding hope and strength, valuing peer trainers, and ideas for future groups. Parents reported increased confidence, pride, and acceptance in their children. DiaMEETes highlights the value of developmentally tailored collective narrative interventions within paediatric diabetes services.

articles.title: Age-Related Tibetan-Han Differences in Continuity of Care Among Insured Populations in High-Altitude Western China: Retrospective Longitudinal Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuity of Care (CoC) is an important dimension of health system performance and health equity, reflecting whether individuals can maintain stable and coordinated care relationships over time, rather than merely gaining access to services. Although ethnic differences in CoC have been documented, most existing studies have examined average group differences and have paid limited attention to whether such differences vary across the life course. Claims-based analyses can provide a population-level approach to monitoring CoC and identifying age-specific equity gaps in routine health service use.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine whether Tibetan-Han differences in CoC vary by age among insured populations in high-altitude western China and to assess whether these age-related patterns differ across outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease care settings.
METHODS: We used deidentified health insurance claims data from 3 major cities in high-altitude western China between January 1, 2021, and December 1, 2024. After data cleaning, we constructed a person-year dataset and restricted analyses to individuals with at least 3 annual health care encounters, yielding 850,469 person-years. The Bice-Boxerman CoC index was the primary outcome. Fixed-effects models with year and insurance-region fixed effects included ethnicity, age, age squared, and their interaction terms, adjusting for covariates derived from the Andersen behavioral model. SEs were clustered at the individual level. Subgroup analyses were conducted for outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease samples.
RESULTS: Mean CoC in the overall sample was 0.52 (SD 0.33). A significant nonlinear interaction between ethnicity and age was observed. Fixed-effects models showed a positive Tibetan coefficient (β=0.0582, P<.001), a negative ethnicity × age interaction (β=-0.0035, P<.001), and a significant ethnicity × age² interaction (P<.001).
