Outpatient results were similar. Inpatient analyses showed an overall disadvantage for Tibetans (β=-0.0795, P<.001) and a different age pattern. No significant age interaction was found in the chronic disease sample, whereas significant age heterogeneity remained in the nonchronic disease sample. Age-group analyses showed the largest Tibetan advantage at ages 20 to 25 and significantly lower continuity in most groups aged 35 to 75.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethnic differences in CoC were age-dependent and nonlinear rather than constant across age groups. Because the study covers 4 calendar years, these age-related associations may also reflect birth-cohort differences and should not be interpreted as within-person aging effects. Policies should pay greater attention to continuity barriers faced by middle-aged and older Tibetan populations.

articles.title: Local Treatment for Perineal and Perianal Rhabdomyosarcoma: Clinical Practice Guidelines and Consensus Statement From the Children's Oncology Group, European Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma Study Group, the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe, and the International Soft Tissue Sarcoma Consortium.
articles.abstract: Local control of rhabdomyosarcoma in the perianal and perineal region (PRMS) is challenging due to the unfavorable tumor location, the often advanced stage of disease, the prevalence of alveolar histology with PAX3/FOXO1 fusion, and frequent regional lymph node (LN) involvement at presentation. Distant metastases are present at diagnosis in up to 49% of patients. Given the high risk of recurrence, the prognosis of patients with PRMS treated with multimodal treatment is poor, with a reported 5-year overall survival (OS) rate of 39%-52%. Due to the rarity of PRMS along with variations in treatment protocols over time and across different cooperative groups, we have developed consensus local treatment guidelines. This guideline is based on a comprehensive literature review and expert opinion and is endorsed by the International Soft-Tissue Sarcoma Consortium (INSTRuCT). It integrates insights from three leading pediatric oncology cooperative groups: the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe (CWS; since December 2024 part of European pediatric Soft-tissue sarcoma Study Group [EpSSG]), Children's Oncology Group (COG), and EpSSG. This document addresses surgical therapy options, including biopsy, nodal staging, and various resection modalities, as well as options for radiotherapy, such as intensity-modulated radiation therapy, proton beam therapy, and brachytherapy.

articles.title: Age-Stratified Sirolimus Trough Concentrations in Pediatric Vascular Malformations: A Real-World Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus is increasingly being used off-label to treat pediatric vascular malformations. In this study, the age-stratified drug exposure, pharmacokinetic variability, and long-term treatment characteristics of sirolimus were evaluated in a real-world pediatric population.
METHODS: In this study, 144 patients (younger than 19 years) with vascular malformations who were treated with sirolimus at a single center (July 2018 and March 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. A total of 2054 therapeutic drug monitoring measurements were obtained. The patients were stratified into 6 age groups (1 month and younger to 12-18 years). The outcomes included trough concentration, interindividual variability (coefficient of variation), target range attainment, treatment duration, and MRI-based response.
RESULTS: The median follow-up was 18.3 months (range, 0.3-74.1 months). Neonates (1 month and younger) showed the highest interindividual variability (coefficient of variation = 61.6%), with lower variability observed in adolescents (40.0%, P < 0.001). Overall, 73.4% of the trough concentrations were within the target range (4-10 ng/mL), and the mean duration within the therapeutic range per patient was 70.9%. Supratherapeutic levels (>15 ng/mL) were most frequent in neonates (6.6%). Prolonged therapy (≥24 months) was observed in 31.9% of patients, with a median duration of 35.1 months. Among the 44 patients who underwent follow-up MRI, 84.1% showed disease improvement or stability.
CONCLUSIONS: Sustained long-term treatment continuity suggests that sirolimus was generally tolerated across pediatric age groups, although direct toxicity data were not systematically captured in this study. Younger patients exhibited greater pharmacokinetic variability, necessitating closer monitoring and cautious dose adjustment. Prospective PK-PD studies incorporating standardized clinical outcomes are needed to define optimal trough targets and individualized dosing strategies.

articles.title: Indocyanine Green Assists in Identification of Solid Tumor Pulmonary Metastases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The presence of pulmonary metastases reduces overall survival in patients with certain solid tumors; therefore, surgical clearance is crucial to cure for some types. This multi-institutional prospective study sought to determine the utility and diagnostic accuracy of indocyanine green (ICG) for delineating pulmonary metastases in diverse pediatric, adolescent, and young adult solid cancers.
PROCEDURE: Thirteen member institutions of the Pediatric Surgical Oncology Research Collaborative administered preoperative ICG to patients undergoing pulmonary metastasectomy for primary or recurrent solid tumor malignancy (2019-2023). Surgeons reported their perspective on ICG utility for pulmonary metastasectomy following each operation. The diagnostic accuracy of ICG fluorescence to identify a pathologically confirmed tumor-containing specimen was determined.
RESULTS: Of 829 specimens resected during 134 pulmonary metastasectomies (30.6% hepatic, 47.0% osteosarcoma, 17.2% non-osteosarcoma-type sarcomas ["other sarcomas"], 5.2% other non-hepatic and non-sarcoma tumor types ["other tumor types"]). Surgeons reported ICG as helpful in 77.6% of procedures. In 11.9% of cases, ICG identified viable metastases not visualized on preoperative imaging. Adjusted diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI]) for metastases from all tumor types was 80.7% (77.9%-83.3%) and 82.5% (78.9%-85.8%), respectively. By primary tumor histology, adjusted accuracy and sensitivity (95% CI) were 83.2% (74.4%-89.9%), 46.7% (28.3%-65.7%) for metastases from other sarcomas, 80.6% (75.3%-85.2%), 95.6% (91.8%-98.0%) for hepatic tumors, 80.6% (76.6%-84.2%), 77.1% (71.4%-82.2%) for osteosarcoma, and 72.7% (49.8%-89.3%), 60.0% (26.2%-87.8%) for other tumor types.
CONCLUSIONS: During pulmonary metastasectomy, adjusted diagnostic accuracy of ICG was 80.7%, and, importantly, 11.9% of metastasectomies contained viable tumors identified by ICG but not by preoperative imaging.

articles.title: Return to School and Readmission Risk After Pain-Related Hospitalizations in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pain is the primary cause of inpatient admissions in sickle cell disease (SCD) and readmission is common. For school-aged youth, successful transition from the hospital necessitates school reentry. This study assessed rates of school return following a pain-related admission and the relationship between school return and readmission.
METHODS: Sixteen youth (7-17 years) admitted for SCD-related pain and caregivers completed daily surveys about school attendance and pain severity for 10 consecutive school days after discharge. Descriptive, independent samples t-test, and chi-square analyses were used to assess differences in pain, school attendance, and readmission.
RESULTS: On average, participants (age M = 13.75; 69% female; 75% HbSS) attended 6.13 out of 10 school days, with 25% returning the next school day after discharge and 13% attending all 10 days. Almost all (94%) reported ongoing pain throughout the monitoring period. Most youth (63%) exhibited variable school attendance after initial school return. Those with variable attendance attended fewer school days (M = 4.40, SD = 2.46) compared to "consistent school attenders" (M = 9, SD = 0.89), p < 0.001, and reported higher daily pain (MVariableAttenders = 3.78, SDVariableAttenders = 1.68; MConsistentAttenders = 1.47, SDConsistentAttenders = 0.81), p = 0.007. Half of "variable school attenders" were readmitted, compared to none of the consistent attenders, χ2 (df = 1) = 4.36, p = 0.037.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that school reentry after a pain-related hospitalization is difficult for many patients and essential to consider in discharge planning. Youth continue reporting pain following discharge, with some experiencing variable school attendance and readmission for pain. Promoting school attendance should be a core component of comprehensive SCD management plans, with implications for pain management and healthcare utilization.

articles.title: Race-Neutral Spirometry Equations and Functional Classification of Latin American Children and Adolescents: A Multinational Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Race-neutral Global Lung Function Initiative (GLI)-Global spirometry equations are increasingly adopted, but their impact on the functional classification of children in Latin America has been examined only in single-country studies, leaving the region without multinational data.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of different spirometry reference equations on functional classification in Latin American children and adolescents, to characterize the physiological and demographic determinants associated with reclassification relative to GLI-Global, and to relate the reclassification of obstruction to bronchodilator responsiveness.
METHODS: Retrospective, cross-sectional study of spirometry in participants younger than 20 years at four Latin American sites (2009-2025). One test per individual was analyzed. Z-scores and functional patterns (normal, obstructive, non-specific, mixed; ATS/ERS 2022) were derived for Martínez-Briseño (a regional reference equation), NHANES-Hispanic, Knudson, GLI-2012 (Caucasian), and GLI-Global equations. Agreement (kappa) and logistic and multinomial models characterized reclassification relative to GLI-Global.
RESULTS: Among 13,171 children (median age 10.2 years; 56.4% male), GLI-Global classified 74.6% as normal versus 61.4% (Martínez-Briseño) and 64.4% (NHANES-Hispanic) in those ≥8 years, with the non-specific and mixed categories becoming uncommon. Relative to the regional equations, GLI-Global assigned higher FEV1 and FVC z-scores (by ∼0.95 SD versus Martínez-Briseño and ∼0.65 SD versus NHANES-Hispanic) while leaving the FEV1/FVC z-score little changed. Agreement with GLI-Global was 84.3% for Martínez-Briseño (kappa 0.65) and 88.7% for NHANES-Hispanic (0.75); GLI-2012 (Caucasian) agreed in 96.6%, although non-specific results still shifted to normal. GLI-Global reclassified about one in six tests-mostly low-FVC patterns moving to normal-with a net shift toward normal of + 7 to + 15 percentage points across sites. Among 11,621 children with post-bronchodilator testing, GLI-Global identified more bronchodilator-responsive children than Martínez-Briseño (24.1% versus 19.8%) but identified fewer with any abnormal finding (37.6% versus 42.3%; difference -4.7 percentage points, 95% CI - 5.4 to - 4.1); about one in eight bronchodilator-responsive obstructive children was relabeled as normal.
CONCLUSIONS: Relative to the equations in regional use, GLI-Global mainly relabels low-FVC patterns as normal in these referred children-a change in classification, not resolved disease. It identified more bronchodilator-responsive children but identified fewer children with any abnormal finding, and a larger share of responders had a baseline read as normal.

articles.title: Task-specific Humeral Head Translation Is Associated With Neuromuscular Recruitment Deficits in Multidirectional Shoulder Instability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidirectional shoulder instability is a common clinical challenge, particularly in adolescents and young adult females. It can impact daily function and athletic performance. However, evidence regarding the relationship between humeral head translation and muscle recruitment patterns in this population remains unclear.
QUESTIONS/PURPOSES: This study aimed to (1) compare humeral head translation between patients with multidirectional instability and controls, as well as among clinical subgroups characterized by anterior, inferior, and posterior instability; (2) examine shoulder muscle activity across groups, including variations within clinical subgroups; and (3) investigate the relationship between humeral head translation and muscle activation levels during three standardized isometric tasks.
METHODS: From an initial screening of 37 patients and 35 controls, 19% (7) of patients and 14% (5) of controls were excluded based on predefined criteria (shoulder pain < 3 months, prior shoulder surgery, or adhesive capsulitis), leaving 30 eligible participants with multidirectional instability (25 female, mean ± SD age 24 ± 1 years) and 30 control participants (23 female, age 25 ± 4 years) who successfully completed all testing without data loss. To address our three study questions, the methodology was structured as follows: first, ultrasonography was used to calculate humeral head translation via changes in acromiohumeral and glenohumeral distances. Based on clinical relevance and patient perception thresholds, a difference of ≥ 1.4 mm in humeral head translation was defined as the minimal detectable change (MDC). Second, surface electromyography recorded muscle activities (biceps long head, infraspinatus, middle deltoid, serratus anterior, upper trapezius, and lower trapezius) across groups and clinical subgroups during three isometric tasks, including (1) isometric shoulder flexion, (2) isometric horizontal adduction, and (3) extension while holding weight. For extension while holding weight, participants lifted a standardized dumbbell (5 kg for participants with BMI ≥ 21 kg/m2 and 4 kg for those with a BMI of < 21 kg/m2). All data on muscle activity are reported as percentages of maximum voluntary isometric contraction rather than absolute values, with 20% representing the MDC. Participants were further stratified into subgroups based on predominant instability patterns, and comparative analyses were conducted to evaluate differences in humeral translation and muscle activities across these specific groups. Third, the relationship between humeral head translation and muscle activation levels was investigated using Pearson correlation coefficients, interpreted as weak for r < 0.30, moderate for r = 0.30 to 0.50, and strong for r > 0.50.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with multidirectional instability demonstrated greater humeral head translation across all tasks, exceeding the MDC threshold in controls versus patients for anterior translation (mean ± SD 0.4 ± 0.3 mm versus 2.6 ± 1.1 mm, mean difference 2.2 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.8 to 2.6]; p < 0.001), posterior translation (0.4 ± 0.2 mm versus 2.2 ± 1.2 mm, mean difference 1.8 [95% CI 1.3 to 2.2]; p < 0.001), and inferior translation (0.3 ± 0.2 mm versus 3.0 ± 1.8 mm, mean difference 2.8 [95% CI 2.1 to 3.4]; p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis showed that patients with a predominant direction of instability experienced the greatest translation during corresponding specific tasks (mean difference 1.5 to 2.4 mm [95% CI 0.2 to 4.1]; p < 0.02). We found no clinically important difference between controls and patients in terms of infraspinatus activity during horizontal adduction (23% ± 11% versus 15% ± 6%, mean difference 8% [95% CI 2% to 13%]; p = 0.001). Similarly, no clinically important difference was observed in upper trapezius activity during weighted extension (32% ± 19% versus 17% ± 13%, mean difference 14% [95% CI 4% to 22%]; p = 0.001), nor in middle deltoid activity during weighted extension (11% ± 6% versus 7% ± 4%, mean difference 3% [95% CI 1% to 6%]; p = 0.009). Only the reduction in biceps long head during flexion in controls versus patients (64% ± 38% versus 36% ± 12%, mean difference 29% [95% CI 14% to 44%]; p < 0.001) exceeded the MDC threshold. Correlations between translation and muscle activity occurred during specific tasks, showing moderate positive associations with serratus anterior (r = 0.38; p = 0.04) and lower trapezius activity (r = 0.40; p = 0.03) during flexion and a strong positive association with middle deltoid activity during horizontal adduction (r = 0.59; p = 0.001), whereas no correlations were found during weighted extension.
CONCLUSION: Patients with multidirectional instability exhibit task-specific increases in humeral head translation exceeding the MDC, driven by distinct neuromuscular deficits. Subgroup analyses show that patients experience the greatest translation during tasks corresponding to their predominant direction of instability. Future studies should evaluate the longitudinal efficacy of rehabilitation protocols in modifying abnormal translation patterns and improving clinical outcomes across different subgroups.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: From a foundational science perspective, our findings indicate that traditional, generalized shoulder strengthening is insufficient for multidirectional instability. Instead, rehabilitation should utilize direction-specific interventions tailored to each patient's predominant instability pattern, targeting underperforming muscles to mitigate abnormal joint translation and restore dynamic glenohumeral stability.

articles.title: Multimodality Care and Survival in Adolescents and Young Adults With Metastatic Non-Rhabdomyosarcoma Soft Tissue Sarcoma in California.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 20% of adolescents and young adults (AYA: ages 15-39) with non-rhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcoma (NRSTS) are diagnosed with metastatic disease, which has a dismal prognosis. Optimal care is critical to improve outcomes, but there is no consensus on the best management approach. We sought to evaluate multimodality care (MMC) and survival among AYAs with metastatic NRSTS.
METHODS: We identified AYAs diagnosed during 2004-2022 with metastatic NRSTS in the California Cancer Registry. We defined MMC as first-line treatment receipt of surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation per the Children's Oncology Group ARST0332 protocol. We used multivariable logistic regression to evaluate associations of sociodemographic and clinical factors with receipt of MMC, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression to examine the impact of MMC on overall survival.
RESULTS: Of the 726 AYAs with metastatic NRSTS, 14% received MMC. A larger proportion of patients 15-25 years old who were treated by pediatric (vs. medical) oncologists received chemotherapy (96% vs. 75%), radiation (53% vs. 34%), and chemoradiation (51% vs. 25%). Older age (>21 years) was associated with decreased odds of receiving MMC. In patients ages 15-25, treatment by a pediatric (vs. medical) oncologist was associated with higher odds of receiving MMC (odds ratio [OR] = 3.4, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.33-8.72). Median overall survival was longer for patients receiving MMC (2.1 vs. 1.1 years), although associations did not remain statistically significant in the multivariable-adjusted model (HR = 0.89, CI = 0.68-1.16). Receiving all care at a specialized cancer center was associated with improved overall survival (HR = 0.63, CI = 0.49-0.81).
CONCLUSION: We found that only 14% of AYAs with metastatic NRSTS received MMC, which was impacted by age at diagnosis and physician specialty. Future research should investigate decision-making in patients with metastatic NRSTS and their providers, and its impact on outcomes.

articles.title: Frequency of On-Scene Goal-Directed Field Interventions for Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in a Regional System of Care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Early on-scene resuscitation improves outcomes from pediatric non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); however, for pediatric patients, the early evacuation strategy remains commonplace. We sought to determine the frequency of goal-directed interventions initiated by paramedics prior to transport for pediatric patients with OHCA in a regional emergency medical services (EMS) system.
METHODS: In this retrospective observational study and cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) and linked electronic patient care reports (ePCR) data for patients aged <15 years treated by EMS for nontraumatic OHCA in Los Angeles (LA) County from January 2021 to December 2022. The primary outcome was the frequency of goal-directed therapies administered on scene prior to transport, which we defined as defibrillation for shockable rhythms and administration of epinephrine and fluid resuscitation for non-shockable rhythms. We also tabulated descriptive statistics regarding arrest characteristics, scene times, frequency of other prehospital treatments, and patient outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 176 eligible pediatric OHCA cases analyzed in CARES, 112 (64%) were male, the median age was 10 months (IQR 3-51), and 162 (92%) had an initial non-shockable rhythm. Of these, 156 patients were successfully linked to electronic patient care report (ePCR) records for analyses of prehospital interventions. Among 143 patients with non-shockable rhythms, EMS administered epinephrine before transport in 58 (41%) and fluids in 12 (8%). Among 13 patients with shockable rhythms, EMS delivered defibrillation before transport in 11 (85%). Bag-valve-mask (BVM) use was documented in 80 (51%) patients, although its timing relative to scene departure could not be determined. Median on-scene time was 10 minutes (IQR 5-18). Ten patients (6%) survived to hospital discharge, including 6 (3%) with a favorable neurologic outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: In this regional EMS system, fewer than half of patients with non-shockable rhythms received a dose of epinephrine and fewer than one in ten received intravenous fluids prior to transport, whereas most patients with shockable rhythms were defibrillated on scene. Further work is needed to identify barriers to timely delivery of on-scene resuscitative interventions.

articles.title: Olfactory Disorders in Children: A Clinical Approach to Aetiologies, Psychophysical Testing and Therapeutics.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Olfaction is a critical physiological function, yet paediatric olfactory dysfunction remains poorly characterized compared to adult populations. This narrative review aims to synthesize current knowledge regarding the aetiology, diagnosis and management of olfactory disorders in children to provide a practical guide for general paediatricians and otolaryngologists.
METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/Medline, Scopus and Embase. A total of 425 peer-reviewed clinical trials, observational studies and guidelines focusing on paediatric olfaction were evaluated and 41 highly relevant articles were included.
RESULTS: The exact prevalence of paediatric olfactory disorders remains unclear, though it is highly underdiagnosed. Unlike adult presentations, paediatric aetiologies are predominantly congenital (accounting for roughly two-thirds of cases, such as Kallmann syndrome), while acquired causes (traumatic brain injury, post-viral) account for one-third. Diagnostic modalities must be age-appropriately tailored; tools like the 'U-Sniff' or 'Smell Wheel' are required for younger children, alongside high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to evaluate olfactory bulb aplasia. Therapies range from surgical correction for conductive losses to targeted olfactory training for sensorineural deficits.
CONCLUSION: Olfactory disorders in children carry potential safety and developmental consequences. Implementing age-adapted testing and systematic clinical pathways is essential for improving diagnosis and patient outcomes in paediatric practice.

articles.title: First Report of Gene Therapy in a Patient With Hemoglobin SC Disease.
articles.abstract: Gene therapy in patients with severe sickle cell disease has been recently approved for commercial use, even in children. Clinical trials leading to approval were limited to patients with hemoglobin SS and Sβ0, due to the severity of disease in these patients. The efficacy of gene therapy in patients with hemoglobin SC disease is unknown. We provide details on treatment and clinical course of the first hemoglobin SC patient treated with gene therapy due to the severity of symptoms and the absence of any viable treatment options that could provide relief from the ravages of the disease.

articles.title: Draft genome sequencing of Burkholderia cenocepacia strain DC660 isolated from a chronically colonized patient with cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract: We have isolated the Burkholderia cenocepacia strain DC660 from a chronically colonized pediatric patient with cystic fibrosis to develop a bacteriophage-mediated decolonization treatment to improve candidacy for lung transplantation. Whole-genome sequencing revealed antimicrobial resistance genes, consistent with the multidrug resistance observed in antimicrobial susceptibility testing, as well as several prophage-associated regions.

articles.title: Pharmacological considerations in opioid use disorder treatment in pregnant and postpartum patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Untreated perinatal opioid use disorder (OUD) is a major contributor to maternal and infant morbidity and mortality, worsened by an often adulterated fentanyl-dominant drug supply. Medication for OUD (MOUD) is standard of care, yet evidence guiding selection, initiation, dosing, pain management, neonatal withdrawal, breastfeeding, and postpartum continuity is evolving.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review with expert opinion synthesizes five years of literature, alongside foundational trials, on MOUD treatment across pregnancy, delivery, and the first postpartum year, prioritizing shared decision-making and trauma-responsive care. Topics include MOUD maternal dose and formulation, fentanyl-era induction, adulterant-complicated withdrawal, peripartum pain management, neonatal considerations, medication-specific breastfeeding, postpartum co-occurring mental health and MOUD access challenges, and long-term child outcomes. A PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov search (2020-2026) supplemented foundational sources.
EXPERT OPINION: Treatment needs to center in trust, non-judgment, and shared decision-making. Extended-release buprenorphine is an emerging preferred option, especially for patients stabilized on buprenorphine, and buprenorphine-naloxone appears to be as good as, if not better than, buprenorphine alone. Withdrawal management must accommodate an increasingly adulterated drug supply, and breastfeeding is generally compatible with MOUD. Like all children, prenatally opioid-exposed children need nurturing care, developmental screening, and early intervention when indicated.

articles.title: Exploring the COSA-t and Other Occupation-Based Assessments in Pediatric Occupational Therapy for Tic Disorders.
articles.abstract: ImportanceThere is a paucity of research describing the occupational therapy assessment process for children with tic disorders (TD) and the priority areas of occupational performance that should be considered during assessment.ObjectiveThis study aimed to (1) explore the content validity of the COSA-t items, as indicated by clinical importance and (2) understand how occupational therapists use the COSA-t and other occupation-based assessments to inform their Comprehensive Behavioral Intervention for Tics (CBIT) practice.DesignCross-sectional, qualitative study.SettingVirtual focus groups (Zoom) and asynchronous surveys.ParticipantsOccupational therapists were recruited through closed, professional networks. All participants were CBIT trained, had experience providing occupational therapy to at least one child with TD, and had training or experience administering the COSA-t or other occupation-based assessments with children with TD.Outcomes and MeasuresParticipants rated the clinical importance of each COSA-t item using a 0 to 10 visual analog scale. Five virtual focus groups explored participants' use of occupation-based assessments with children with TD.ResultsNineteen occupational therapists completed the survey of clinical importance and 18 participated in focus groups (17 female, 1 male, 2-20 years of experience). COSA-t importance ratings ranged from 5.95 to 8.95. Occupation-based assessments were a starting point, revealed the daily impact of tics, provided clinical discernment, and fostered motivation and insight.Conclusions and RelevanceThe occupational therapists found value in administering occupation-based assessments, such as the COSA-t. Therefore, there is a pressing need for further evidence to support the incorporation of self-reported, occupation-based assessments into interventions with children with TD.

articles.title: Asthma Blitz Days: An Innovative Approach to Asthma Management in Schools.
articles.abstract: Asthma is the most prevalent chronic condition among school-aged children in the United States, contributing to emergency department visits, school absences, and diminished well-being. Inadequate asthma control is driven by medication nonadherence, psychosocial stressors, and social determinants of health. School nurses are pivotal in coordinating care, supporting medication management, and fostering asthma-friendly environments. In Pitt County, North Carolina, Asthma Blitz Days were developed as a collaborative, school-based intervention between Pitt County School Health Program and ECU Health (formerly Vidant) Maynard Children's Hospital Pediatric Asthma Program. Targeting Pre-K to 5th grade students with documented asthma, this program assessed symptoms, delivered age-appropriate education using the teach-back method, and improved medication and documentation compliance. School nurse-led, multidisciplinary interventions like Asthma Blitz Days offer a scalable approach to improving asthma control and promoting health equity in school communities.

articles.title: A Phase IB Study to Evaluate the Safety and Feasibility of Nivolumab or Nivolumab With Azacitidine in Patients With Recurrent, Resectable Osteosarcoma: A Report From the National Pediatric Cancer Foundation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Relapse rates following complete surgical resection (CSR) of pulmonary osteosarcoma recurrence remain high. We hypothesized that PD-1 inhibition with nivolumab (Nivo) combined with epigenetic priming using azacitidine (5-Aza) would be safe and augment systemic immune activation in patients with resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse.
METHODS: This Phase I trial sought to establish the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) of perioperative Nivo/5-Aza in patients ≤39 years old with isolated, resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse. Three dose levels (DLs) were studied using a modified 3 + 3 design with dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) assessed from Day 1 of therapy to CSR. Patients received biweekly Nivo 3 mg/kg alone (DL1) or with 5-Aza at 60 or 75 mg/m2/day (DL2 and DL3) in 28-day cycles.
RESULTS: Twenty patients received therapy; 18 were evaluable for DLTs. DL3 exceeded the maximum tolerated dose (Grade 3 vomiting, prolonged Grade 4 neutropenia). Common adverse events included anemia, neutropenia, and nausea. Seventeen patients (85%) reached CSR after neoadjuvant therapy. Median event-free survival (EFS) was 3.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.7-7.7 months), and median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% CI: 10.1-42.6 months). Combination therapy was associated with evidence of systemic immune activation, including increases in IFN-γ, IL-1α, IL-1β, and CCL5.
CONCLUSION: The RP2D was Nivo 3 mg/kg and 5-Aza 60 mg/m2/day on Days 1-5 and 8-9. The combination was feasible and tolerable. EFS was limited in the context of a Phase I trial. These findings provide safety, feasibility, and exploratory immunologic data to inform future immunotherapy trials in osteosarcoma.

articles.title: A Narrative Review of Myths and Misconceptions About Methylphenidate in the Treatment of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Methylphenidate (MPH) has been a cornerstone of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) pharmacotherapy for more than 70 years, with robust evidence supporting its efficacy and tolerability across the patient lifespan. Despite this extensive evidence base, persistent myths and misconceptions among clinicians, patients, and caregivers continue to drive treatment hesitancy, premature discontinuation, and suboptimal prescribing practices. Our objective was to identify and critically appraise prevalent myths surrounding MPH use in ADHD that may adversely influence treatment decisions.
METHODS: Myths were identified based on clinical experience, discussions with prominent ADHD experts, and a literature search for relevant articles and guidelines. Evidence from the literature was reviewed and supplemented with clinical recommendations.
RESULTS: Twelve common misconceptions about MPH were identified. These include misconceptions about interchangeability and dose equivalence between MPH formulations, treatment timing for continuous symptom control, endurance of drug onset- and offset-related side effects, and patient feelings as an indicator of drug effectiveness. Myths that MPH will always cause insomnia, increase anxiety and depression, stunt growth, have similar levels of abuse potential and side effects as other drugs, or worsen behavior in patients with autism spectrum disorder were also identified, as well as a common misconception that MPH is only effective in child and adolescent populations. Evidence gathered from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, pharmacokinetic studies, and clinical practice guidelines provided counterarguments to these concerns.
CONCLUSIONS: MPH remains a well-studied, effective, and generally well-tolerated treatment for ADHD in children, adolescents, and adults. The diversity of available formulations, including novel delivery systems such as delayed-release/extended-release MPH and serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate, allows for individualized treatment matched to patient needs and daily functional demands. Clinicians who understand evidence-based rebuttals to myths about MPH can improve prescribing decisions and patient/family counseling while reducing the burden of misinformation that contributes to the undertreatment of this highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder.

articles.title: Professional judgement in early childhood: predictors of concern, support needs and referrals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of developmental delays is crucial for timely support. This study examined what factors influence professional concern, perceived support needs, and referral decisions.
METHOD: A vignette study was conducted among 401 professionals evaluating a 2.5-year-old girl with mild eating difficulties, supplemented with manipulated variables about the developmental level of the child, the socioeconomic status, and parental concern. Five outcomes were examined using regression analyses: professional concern, perceived support needs for developmental monitoring and diagnostic assessment and referral for developmental monitoring and diagnostic assessment.
RESULTS: Developmental delay was a predictor of professional concern, perceived support needs and referral behaviour. Parental concern predicted professional concern but not support needs or referral decisions. Organisational sector was associated with support needs and referral decisions.
CONCLUSION: These findings underline the need for targeted training of professionals working with young children in developmental screening and taking parental concerns seriously.

articles.title: Cystic fibrosis in China: addressing the cycle of underdiagnosis and treatment inaccessibility.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is substantially underdiagnosed in China, and access to targeted therapy remains limited. Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy has dramatically improved survival internationally, yet none has been approved or entered clinical trials in China. A circular problem contributes to this situation: CF is not included in newborn screening programmes because it has historically been considered extremely rare in East Asian populations. Yet, fewer than 300 patients have been genetically confirmed, in part due to limited diagnostic infrastructure. Epidemiological data based on carrier frequency suggest the true affected population exceeds 17,000 individuals. Patients who receive a molecular diagnosis face additional challenges, including a CFTR variant spectrum that differs from Western populations without established theratyping pathways, and the absence of regulatory submissions for CFTR modulators. Here, we discuss three potential approaches: expanding diagnostic capacity through standardised sweat chloride testing and clinician education, building theratyping infrastructure via patient-derived organoid biobanks, and applying existing rare disease regulatory pathways to facilitate drug approval.

articles.title: Future vaccine priorities in Cambodia: preparedness for emerging infectious diseases.
articles.abstract: Cambodia has achieved substantial progress in immunisation over the past two decades, culminating in one of Southeast Asia's most successful COVID-19 vaccination campaigns. However, the epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing. Climate change, environmental degradation, urbanisation, increasing regional mobility, and intensified human-animal interactions are increasing the risk of emerging infectious diseases, placing Cambodia at the frontline of future epidemic and pandemic threats. Although national vaccine policy has traditionally focused on childhood immunisation, preparedness for emerging infectious diseases requires a broader strategy that integrates pathogen surveillance, genomic monitoring, regulatory readiness, rapid vaccine platforms, and One Health collaboration. Here, we highlight the need for Cambodia to transition from a vaccine delivery agenda toward a broader vaccine preparedness agenda. We propose a national framework centred around surveillance-informed vaccine prioritisation, strengthened laboratory and genomic capacity, resilient vaccine delivery systems, sustainable financing, and regional partnerships. Such an approach could enhance Cambodia's preparedness for pathogens including H5N1, dengue, Japanese encephalitis, rabies, and future Disease X scenarios, while strengthening its contribution to regional health security.

articles.title: Late Effects of 131I-MIBG in Survivors of High-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group LEAHRN Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Meta-iodobenzylguanidine radiolabeled with iodine-131 (131I-MIBG) is used to treat high-risk neuroblastoma (HRNBL). Late toxicities of 131I-MIBG have not been well studied due to limited survival of patients receiving this therapy for relapsed disease.
METHODS: The Children's Oncology Group LEAHRN study evaluated HRNBL survivors diagnosed after 2000 and alive at least 5 years from diagnosis. Clinical history and the prevalence of late effects were summarized for participants treated with 131I-MIBG (cases). Participants who did not receive 131I-MIBG were randomly selected and matched by age at diagnosis and relapse history (controls) in a 1:2 case-control study design. Chi-squared analysis was used to evaluate the association between 131I-MIBG and late toxicities.
RESULTS: Of 375 participants in the LEAHRN analytic cohort, 32 (8.5%) received 131I-MIBG. Differences in the proportion with thyroid toxicity and growth failure were observed but not statistically significant. The proportions of other major organ toxicities were not different between cases and controls, including subsequent malignancy.
DISCUSSION: No statistically significant differences were identified in the burden of late toxicities for HRNBL survivors treated with and without 131I-MIBG. A small sample size likely limited the ability to detect statistically significant differences. Our data provide information for follow-up care of 131I-MIBG-treated survivors and clinical trial design.

articles.title: The Ross procedure: Technical principles, operative strategy, and pitfalls for long-term success.
articles.abstract: The Ross procedure remains an attractive aortic valve replacement strategy for children, adolescents, and selected young adults. Pulmonary autograft replacement provides excellent hemodynamics, freedom from anticoagulation, growth potential in children, and favorable long-term survival in appropriately selected patients. These advantages, however, come at the cost of substantial technical complexity. Small imperfections during autograft harvest, implantation, coronary transfer, or root reconstruction can result in early dysfunction, coronary complications, or late autograft dilatation and failure. The purpose of this review is to summarize a practical and reproducible approach to the Ross procedure with emphasis on operative strategy, technical details, Ross-Konno modifications, autograft stabilization techniques, and avoidance of common pitfalls. Rather than advocating a single technique, we emphasize fundamental principles that permit adaptation to patient anatomy while maintaining the geometric integrity of the left ventricular outflow tract, aortic root, and pulmonary root.

articles.title: Prenatal alcohol exposure and adolescent sleep in clinical pathways: a commentary on Devine et al.
articles.abstract: Devine et al. provide timely evidence that parent-reported adolescent sleep disturbances are associated with prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development cohort, even when most exposure was low to moderate. This commentary argues that the central contribution of the study is not only the replication of a sleep signal after PAE, but the identification of a clinically recognisable phenotype: sleep-wake transition problems, excessive somnolence, and possible sleep breathing symptoms. We highlight three implications: sleep should be treated as a developmental mediator and modifiable target, future studies should triangulate retrospective PAE and parent-reported sleep with objective measures, and prevention messages about alcohol in pregnancy should be paired with non-stigmatising family support. Building clinical pathways from screening to intervention may transform small epidemiologic effects into meaningful benefits for affected adolescents.

articles.title: Early Life Adversity and Adolescent Sleep: A Longitudinal Study Examining Associations Between Dimensions of Early Adversity and Adolescent Sleep Metrics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A dimensional approach was utilized to examine associations between early environmental adversity (deprivation, unpredictability) and adolescent sleep metrics (average and night-to-night variability in bedtime, wake time, and sleep duration). We predict that greater deprivation and unpredictability are uniquely associated with worse adolescent sleep.
METHODS: In this study (N = 337), preschool unpredictability and deprivation were measured via home observation and parent report; adolescent sleep was measured by actigraphy. Multilevel structural equation modeling examined longitudinal associations between early adversity dimensions and adolescent sleep, controlling for sex, adolescent age, maternal education, preschool family income, and adolescent family income.
RESULTS: In independent models, greater deprivation was associated with more sleep duration variability (β = .18 [.01, .34]), greater bedtime variability (β = .30 [.14, .45]), and shorter average sleep duration (β = -.20 [-.35, -.03]); greater unpredictability was associated with shorter average sleep duration (β = -.21 [-.39, -.02]) and greater bedtime variability (β = .23 [.04, .40]). In the combined model, only greater deprivation (β = .26 [.09, .42]) was associated with greater bedtime variability, controlling for unpredictability.
CONCLUSIONS: While deprivation and unpredictability predict sleep independently, only deprivation played a unique role in adolescents' bedtime variability, beyond other aspects of early childhood adversity. Results inform early intervention and prevention efforts to promote healthy adolescent sleep.

articles.title: Ferric derisomaltose for the treatment of iron deficiency with or without anemia in women's health: an expert review.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency (ID) with or without anemia is highly prevalent in women, and is commonly caused by abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB; including heavy menstrual bleeding), increased iron requirements during pregnancy, or postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). ID or iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in women of reproductive age has been associated with a substantial burden on quality of life, impaired physical and cognitive functioning, decreased productivity, and increased healthcare costs. The presence of ID/IDA during pregnancy has also been linked to poorer maternal outcomes and fetal developmental impairments, including an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in neonates. Despite the high prevalence of ID/IDA and negative impact on women's health, these conditions are frequently overlooked and undertreated, in part due to the nonspecific nature of symptoms, such as fatigue. There is an increasing body of evidence for the use of intravenous (IV) iron to treat ID/IDA in women. Although efficacy is largely comparable among IV iron formulations when equivalent doses are used, there are factors that distinguish certain IV iron formulations from others. This review aims to discuss available evidence for the treatment of ID/IDA in women with ferric derisomaltose (FDI; a high-dose IV iron formulation), focusing on AUB, pregnancy, and PPH. Based on existing data, FDI represents a clinically-effective option for iron repletion in these contexts, and a low risk of hypersensitivity reactions and hypophosphatemia. There is scope for further research within the field of ID/IDA in women's health to address unmet needs and evidence gaps across the patient care pathway.

articles.title: Concurrent Oximetry and Transcutaneous Carbon Dioxide Monitoring to Screen for Paediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnoea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) diagnosis requires polysomnography (PSG) which can be difficult to access due to wait times. Concurrent oximetry and transcutaneous carbon dioxide (TcCO2) monitoring is used in our sleep unit to triage patients, but its diagnostic utility has not been formally evaluated. The objective of the study was to assess whether adding TcCO2 to overnight oximetry improves screening accuracy for paediatric OSA when compared to a full PSG scored according to the American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) guidelines.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of 172 consecutive overnight PSGs performed at the Children's Hospital at Westmead. Three independent sleep consultants scored deidentified oximetry traces (Phase 1), then the same traces with concurrent TcCO2 (Phase 2). Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) with 95% Wilson confidence intervals were calculated for the senior clinician's impression against the PSG-based AASM diagnosis. Univariate logistic regression identified individual predictors of OSA.
RESULTS: The diagnosis of OSA within the study cohort was 77.3% (133/172). Oximetry alone yielded sensitivity 0.865 (95% CI 0.796-0.913) and NPV 0.514 (0.359-0.666). Adding TcCO2 without a structured scoring framework reduced sensitivity to 0.629 (0.544-0.706) and NPV to 0.310 (0.214-0.425), with non-overlapping confidence intervals. The strongest predictor of OSA was concurrent carbon dioxide (CO2) retention with oxygen (O2) desaturation (OR 9.83, 95% CI 2.88-33.54). Overall inter-rater agreement was poor (weighted κ = 0.13), which reflects lack of clearly defined diagnostic criteria. Concurrent CO2 and O2 events, CO2 rise above baseline of 5-9 mmHg, and episodic CO2 retention are the strongest identifiable predictors of OSA.
CONCLUSIONS: TcCO2 adds extra information to oximetry traces. However, without an established scoring system, adding CO2 traces reduces sensitivity of diagnosing OSA. Further research needs to be conducted in developing and validating a scoring system to interpret CO2 traces.

articles.title: Surgical and Cosmetic Outcomes After Fronto-Orbital Advancement With Hybrid Fixation for Unilateral Coronal Craniosynostosis: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fronto-orbital advancement (FOA) remains the standard surgical treatment for unilateral coronal craniosynostosis, particularly in patients presenting beyond the age window for endoscopic treatment and in those with significant frontal and orbital deformity. However, postoperative relapse, residual asymmetry, and fixation-related limitations remain important clinical concerns. Fixation strategies aim to provide immediate structural stability while minimizing potential interference with subsequent cranial growth.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate surgical, morphometric, cosmetic, and perioperative outcomes after FOA using a hybrid fixation strategy in patients with nonsyndromic unilateral coronal craniosynostosis.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 14 patients treated between January 2023 and December 2024 at the JSC National Center for Neurosurgery, Astana, Kazakhstan. All patients had CT-confirmed unilateral nonsyndromic coronal craniosynostosis and underwent primary FOA with combined fixation using biodegradable plates in key structural regions and absorbable sutures between individual remodeled bone fragments. Cosmetic outcomes were assessed using the Whitaker classification and clinician-rated Visual Analog Cosmetic Score (VACS), with each patient's VACS calculated as the mean of independent ratings from 10 assessors. Morphometric evaluation combined cephalic index (CI), as a measure of overall cranial width-to-length proportions, with frontal asymmetry index (FAI), orbital assessment, and nasal deviation angle (NDA). Perioperative safety outcomes and follow-up data were also analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean age at surgery was 16.7±12.9 months, and mean follow-up was 16 months (range 12-24). Favorable cosmetic outcomes were achieved in all patients: 92.9% were classified as Whitaker class I and 7.1% as class II, with no class III or IV outcomes or revision surgeries. Median postoperative VACS was 9.5 (range 6-10). FAI categories decreased in 10 of 14 patients (exact sign test, P=0.002; Holm-adjusted P=0.006). CI categories decreased in 6 patients (P=0.031; Holm-adjusted P=0.063), without establishing normalization of cranial shape. NDA categories showed no evidence of a directional change (P=0.625). All 14 patients received intraoperative autologous blood reinfusion and additional allogeneic blood transfusion. Mean total hospital stay was 18.9±3.5 days, including both preoperative and postoperative inpatient care. No major postoperative complications, cerebrospinal fluid leakage, surgical-site infection, relapse, or reoperation were observed.
CONCLUSION: Extended FOA with hybrid fixation was associated with favorable early cosmetic outcomes in this retrospective cohort. These findings describe the combined reconstructive procedure and do not establish the independent contribution of fixation, preservation of physiological cranial growth, or superiority over alternative fixation methods. Larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: A Survey of Clinical Full-Time Equivalents in Academic Infectious Diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: No published definition currently exists for a 1.0 clinical full-time equivalent (cFTE) in academic infectious diseases (ID).
METHODS: The Infectious Diseases Society of America's member-led Academic Advisory Panel, with ECG Management Consultants, developed a cFTE work standards survey with questions on division demographics, inpatient shift commitments and patient volumes, and clinical leadership roles. ECG administered the survey via Cvent from August 2024 to February 2025 and employed descriptive analyses to summarize results.
RESULTS: A total of 155 academic ID divisions (109 adult and 46 pediatric divisions) were invited to participate. The global response rate was 65%, with 51% for adult divisions and 98% for pediatric divisions. Most divisions cover <3 facilities and utilize residents and fellows; advanced practice provider support is less common. The method of defining cFTE varied, with most divisions using time-based metrics like weeks on service; productivity measures were less frequent. Adult divisions reported managing more new patient consults and daily encounters. Over one-quarter of divisions reported uncompensated leadership responsibilities. Constructs for a 1.0 cFTE in academic ID for adult and pediatric divisions were developed based on survey results and reflect approximately 22 inpatient service weeks annually with three 4-hour outpatient clinics when off inpatient service.
CONCLUSIONS: We report the first survey of clinical work standards in academic pediatric and adult ID in the United States. ID leaders can utilize this information as a reference for clinical expectations, estimate work relative value unit generation, minimize un- or underfunded work, and negotiate effort and resources accordingly.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction of cyclosporine nephrotoxicity in pediatric patients using therapeutic drug monitoring and clinical data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cyclosporine A (CsA) nephrotoxicity is a dose-limiting toxicity in pediatric immunosuppression, and early identification of children at risk of CsA-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) remains an unmet clinical need.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In retrospective cohorts of CsA-treated inpatients undergoing therapeutic drug monitoring (352 children; 342 adults), a regularized logistic-regression model was compared with six machine-learning classifiers under five feature-selection schemes, three small-sample strategies were evaluated, and adult-child transferability was assessed on 95 aligned features. A 14-variable model was externally validated in an independent pediatric cohort (n = 257).
RESULTS: Regularized logistic regression achieved the best discrimination in children (hold-out AUC 0.800) and adults (hold-out AUC 0.956), with complex models overfitting. Adult and pediatric risk architectures differed fundamentally, with transfer AUCs near chance (≈0.6). The 14-variable model retained discrimination on external validation (AUC 0.784, 95% CI 0.656-0.912).
CONCLUSIONS: On small clinical datasets, regularization rather than complexity determines predictive performance. We provide an interpretable, TDM-integrated pediatric CsA-AKI model, deployed as an online calculator, supporting early risk stratification in pediatric CsA therapy.

articles.title: Conceptual and psychometric characteristics of instruments used in adults with CHD quality of life research: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improved survival among people with congenital heart disease (CHD) has increased the emphasis on quality of life as a long-term outcome. However, inconsistent distinctions between quality of life, health-related quality of life, health status and functioning complicate the interpretation of this evidence. Examining the conceptual basis and measurement properties of instruments used in contemporary CHD research is therefore necessary to establish which outcomes are being assessed.
AIM: To identify instruments used in studies reporting quality of life outcomes in adults with moderate or severe CHD, classify their intended constructs and summarise reported evidence of validity, reliability and suitability.
METHODS: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched for English-language quantitative and mixed-methods studies published from 2015 in high-income countries. Citation mining identified instrument development and validation literature. Instruments were classified by their primary intended purpose, and reported psychometric evidence and study definitions of quality of life were summarised descriptively.
RESULTS: Sixty-six records published between 2015 and 2026 identified 16 instruments. Five measured overall quality of life, eight assessed health-related quality of life, health status or functioning, and three were disease-specific. Studies using overall quality of life measures more commonly defined the construct, whereas those using short-form health surveys frequently reported quality of life without conceptual clarification. Validation evidence supported some instruments in adult CHD populations, although the suitability of measures developed for paediatric populations remained uncertain.
CONCLUSION: Contemporary CHD research reports conceptually distinct outcomes under the term quality of life, limiting comparability and interpretation. Explicit definitions and instrument selection informed by the intended construct and population are required to strengthen the assessment of patient-reported outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal-fetal considerations of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Recent advances in cystic fibrosis (CF) treatment, particularly the development of CFTR modulators (CFTRm), have transformed disease management and substantially improved survival, health status, and reproductive outcomes in people with CF. In addition to lung symptoms, CF is characterised by pancreatic insufficiency, meconium ileus, and reduced fertility, leading to a shorter life expectancy. CFTRm, e.g. elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor partially restore CFTR function. Together, these treatments have markedly improved survival and quality of life for individuals with CF. As increasing numbers of women with CF conceive while taking CFTRm, understanding maternal-fetal drug exposure has become a clinical priority. Emerging evidence demonstrates that CFTRm cross the placenta and can be detected in cord blood, neonatal plasma, and infant tissues. However, the extent of fetal exposure, tissue accumulation and potential developmental implications remain incompletely understood. Herein, we emphasise the mechanistic and pharmacological evidence underlying fetal exposure to CFTRm . This review synthesises current evidence regarding the transplacental transfer, fetal exposure and developmental implications of CFTRm during pregnancy. We discuss emerging pharmacokinetic data, reported maternal and infant outcomes and key knowledge gaps that remain regarding the safety of in utero CFTRm exposure.

articles.title: Anti-HLA Alloantibody Responses in Living Donor Uterus Transplantation: A Single-center Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Until 1 decade ago, absolute uterine infertility invariably prevented women from bearing their own biological child. A major causative factor is Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome. However, uterus transplantation (UTx) has recently emerged as a successful treatment strategy, with >70 children being born to UTx recipients. This clinical situation represents a unique immunological scenario-namely the combined sensitization risk from solid organ transplantation and exposure to paternal alloantigens of the fetus.
METHODS: Given the rarity of such cases, we assessed HLA sensitization in this context using a microbead-based assay (Luminex) with HLA screening as well as single-antigen beads in 7 UTx patients.
RESULTS: We observed broad, strong IgG alloimmune responses in 3 UTx recipients, directed against both donor and paternal alloantigens. These responses primarily emerged and amplified after graft hysterectomy and withdrawal of immunosuppression, while intermittently also being evidenced before hysterectomy in 1 case. This contrasts with 4 women with transplants remaining in situ and on immunosuppressive treatment, who lack sensitization signs so far.
CONCLUSIONS: These scarce preliminary data already suggest a relevant risk of broad sensitization in this unusual setting. UTx may therefore (1) represent a unique model for studying HLA sensitization under combined physiological and nonphysiological conditions, (2) warrant informing recipients about the risk of HLA alloimmunization, and (3) require further investigation to understand the implications and long-term consequences, demanding the generation of larger datasets.

articles.title: Short-term outcomes and follow-up of NICU graduates in selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal health during the post-discharge period is critical, especially for infants discharged from the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), who are at higher risk of complications and long-term developmental issues. In Sri Lanka, there are limited data on post-NICU follow-up, highlighting the need for research. This study aimed to evaluate the post-discharge follow-up status of neonates admitted to selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted between January 2025 and June 2025 in the NICUs of National Hospital Galle (NHG) and German-Sri Lanka Friendship Hospital for Women (GSLFHW). Neonates admitted within 28 days of birth who were discharged home or transferred to other wards were included; those who died before discharge or were transferred to another NICU or another hospital were excluded. A purposive sampling method was used. Follow-up assessments were conducted one week and one month after discharge. Data were collected using a structured guide on feeding status, feeding issues, medical problems, pharmacological management, follow-up visits, and developmental milestones. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, and descriptive statistics were presented as numbers and percentages.
RESULTS: Respiratory distress was the most common reason for NICU admission (74.4%, n = 96). At discharge, 97.7% were breastfed, and most achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones: cognitive (92.2%, n = 119), motor (96.1%, n = 124), psychosocial (95.3%, n = 123), and communication (93.0%, n = 120). One week post-discharge, 94.4% were breastfed; feeding issues included poor sucking (12.7%, n = 16) and vomiting (6.3%, n = 8). Most infants met developmental milestones. One month post-discharge, 81.8% were breastfed, 10.9% were readmitted for complications, including infections, and the mean weight increased to 3.26 kg. Nearly all (99.1%) achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones by one month.
CONCLUSION: Most neonates showed favorable early post‑discharge status at one week and one month, with high rates of breastfeeding and attainment of age‑expected developmental milestones at these time points. While breastfeeding remained predominant, some experienced feeding difficulties and a small proportion required readmission or died. These findings describe very early outcomes only; continued and longer‑term follow‑up is essential to manage complications and support health outcomes beyond the first month.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Molecular diagnostics and liquid biopsy approaches in diffuse midline glioma: an update and literature review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs), H3 K27-altered, are aggressive childhood central nervous system tumors that remain almost uniformly fatal. Historically diagnosed radiographically as diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), these tumors are now defined by integrated anatomic and molecular criteria encompassing H3 K27-mutant, EZHIP-overexpressing, and EGFR-altered subtypes. Advances in tissue sampling have transformed understanding of their molecular landscape, but their eloquent location, the sampling bias inherent to stereotactic biopsy, and the impracticality of repeated tissue sampling have motivated interest in biofluid-based approaches. Liquid biopsy is being investigated as a complementary modality for molecular characterization, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of progression and resistance.
METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE for articles published through 31 July 2026, supplemented by a ClinicalTrials.gov search performed on the same date. Eligible articles described liquid biopsy methodologies, biomarker substrates, or clinical applications in DMG or DIPG; a separate, explicitly labeled category of enabling or methodologically relevant studies performed on tissue or in other tumor types was retained.
RESULTS: We summarize the WHO CNS5 molecular definition of DMG, the role and limitations of tissue-based diagnosis, the spectrum of liquid biopsy substrates and platforms with study-level performance data, and the incorporation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sampling into interventional DMG trials. We distinguish exploratory biomarker collection from analytically or clinically validated testing, and we address CSF access, safety, selection bias, and turnaround time.
CONCLUSIONS: Liquid biopsy in DMG remains investigational. No application, whether molecular diagnosis, response monitoring, pseudoprogression adjudication, or treatment adaptation, is currently prospectively validated for clinical decision-making. Standardized, prospective, multi-institutional studies with predefined thresholds are required.

articles.title: Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children (≤ 3 years): A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children presents unique challenges related to cranial development, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) disturbances, and subsequent reconstruction. This systematic review evaluated the indications, operative techniques, postoperative complications, and outcomes of conventional decompressive craniectomy and bone-preserving expansile procedures in children aged ≤ 3 years.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for English-language clinical studies involving age-eligible children. Study characteristics, operative details, complications, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Of the 1970 identified records, 46 publications were included, predominantly case reports and small case series. Indications included traumatic brain injury, cerebrovascular events, hemorrhage, and other causes of severe cerebral swelling. Procedures comprised conventional bone-out decompression and various bone-preserving techniques. Hydrocephalus, subdural and extracranial fluid collections, CSF leakage, wound complications, and bone-related morbidity were reported. Conventional decompression introduced subsequent reconstruction requirements and potential bone-resorption complications. Bone-preserving approaches maintained native cranial bone but were not free of CSF-related complications, altered bone fusion, or later reconstructive procedures. Inconsistent outcome definitions, age-specific denominators, and follow-up prevented reliable comparative estimates.
CONCLUSION: Evidence on decompressive surgery in children aged ≤ 3 years remains limited by small, heterogeneous studies and inconsistent outcome reporting. Although both conventional and bone-preserving techniques are feasible, their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. CSF-related complications and reconstructive morbidity warrant particular attention. Standardized complication reporting and long-term assessment of cranial growth and neurodevelopment are essential to guide surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Metaphorical perceptions of caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder regarding the caregiving process.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the metaphorical perceptions of caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) regarding the caregiving process. The study was conducted with 46 participants responsible for the care of children with ASD. Data were collected between March and April 2026 using a metaphor form. The first part of the form included questions regarding sociodemographic characteristics, while the second part included the statement, "Caring for a child with autism spectrum disorder is like … because …" to identify participants' metaphorical perceptions of the caregiving process. Participants produced 46 metaphors, which were analyzed using content analysis and grouped into five themes: love, belonging, and hope; struggle and resilience; patience, acceptance, and adaptation; uncertainty, learning, and discovery; and intensive care and dependency. Regarding emotional valence, 28.3% of the metaphorical expressions were classified as positive, 37.0% as negative, and 34.7% as mixed. The theme of love, belonging, and hope had the highest frequency (28.3%). Descriptive cross-tabulations were also used to present the distribution of metaphor themes according to caregiving support, psychological support, and education about ASD. As no inferential statistical tests were performed, these distributions were interpreted descriptively and were not considered evidence of statistically significant differences, associations, or causal effects. Overall, the findings demonstrate that caregivers' metaphorical perceptions of caring for a child with ASD reflect a multidimensional experience encompassing emotional attachment and hope as well as struggle, adaptation, uncertainty, and dependency.

articles.title: A National Pediatric Primary Care Research Agenda.
articles.abstract: Pediatric primary care (PPC) promotes child wellbeing through health supervision, anticipatory guidance, screening, and intervention. Given an evolving PPC landscape, content experts collaborated with the American Academy of Pediatrics Pediatric Research in Office Settings network in an iterative, multiyear process to create a PPC research agenda to advance child health that reflects professional and family priorities. Using an adapted nominal group technique, we identified research areas of focus based on (1) what PPC clinicians said they frequently encounter in practice; (2) the extent of the problem for families nationally; (3) evidence gaps; and (4) areas in which research could have the highest impact on child health. From 2022 to 2024, we synthesized contributor feedback from 8 key content expert sessions. This process resulted in 6 interconnected domains of highest priority for PPC research: (1) child mental health, (2) obesity, (3) communicating science to support families, (4) pediatric workforce, (5) injury prevention, and (6) adolescent health. We identified cross-cutting themes that warrant research in connection with these 6 prioritized domains. Examples of such themes include removing barriers to access and ensuring quality services for all children; under-resourced communities; care coordination and linkages within and outside PPC; supporting parents/caregivers; and technology and social media, which can serve as tools to enhance practice and can be assets or threats to child wellbeing. This manuscript details a vision for a national, coordinated PPC research agenda to inform investigators' and funders' efforts to advance primary health care and the health of all children based on our results.

articles.title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors.
articles.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

articles.title: The RNA and protein landscapes of mouse brain organoids.
articles.abstract: Organoids are powerful models of brain development and function. Mouse brain organoids reproduce the main steps of neurodevelopment in vivo and differentiate more rapidly than human organoids, making them scalable for screening applications. However, mouse brain organoids remain poorly defined. Here, we showed that the transcriptome and proteome of mouse brain organoids developed for three weeks are close to those of a neonatal mouse brain. Strikingly, organoids recapitulated the majority of alternative splicing and polyadenylation-site events that define neural identity in vivo. Proteomics revealed that most changes in mRNA expression were translated into proteins. Mouse brain organoids differentiated for only three weeks already harbored a complex network of synaptic proteins, including the ionotropic and metabotropic receptors for the neurotransmitters glutamate and GABA. To conclude, our study provides evidence that mouse brain organoids are a rapidly maturing and relevant model of mammalian brain development and function in a neonatal-like environment.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Pregnant Women and Health Care Workers Regarding Antenatal Testing for HIV, Hepatitis B Virus, and Syphilis in Vietnam: Protocol for a Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis remains a preventable cause of fetal loss, neonatal morbidity, and long-term disability. In Vietnam (Viet Nam), although antenatal care coverage is high, gaps persist in the timing, uptake, and completion of screening and follow-up services for these infections.
OBJECTIVE: This study has 2 parallel population-specific objectives. Among women who recently gave birth, we will estimate completion of antenatal testing for HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis and its associated factors with study-defined optimal testing (completion of all 3 tests during the first trimester). Among health care workers (HCWs), we will assess knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices and identify professional factors associated with good practice regarding antenatal screening and MTCT prevention.
METHODS: This multicenter, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2026 in 4 provincial hospitals in northern Vietnam. Women completed an interviewer-administered questionnaire after delivery, once clinically stable and before discharge. Antenatal testing was verified from maternal records, laboratory reports, or electronic records whenever available. HCWs completed a separate anonymous self-administered questionnaire during the same study period. The 2 participant groups were not matched. The primary outcome for women is completion of all 3 antenatal tests during the first trimester (study-defined optimal testing). The primary outcome for HCWs is good practice regarding the prevention of MTCT. The minimum target sample sizes were 601 women and 601 HCWs. Data will be analyzed separately for each group. Descriptive analyses will summarize knowledge, attitudes, and practices indicators and service uptake. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance will be used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcomes.
RESULTS: The protocol received ethics approval on February 9, 2026. The study is funded by Thai Binh University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Hung Yen, Vietnam. Recruitment was conducted from June to September 2026. As of manuscript submission, 601 patients and 601 health care workers had been recruited. Data cleaning is planned for October 2026, followed by statistical analysis from November to December 2026. Dissemination of the first study results is planned for the first quarter of 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: The study will provide hospital-based evidence on completion of antenatal triple screening and provider practices. By prespecifying distinct outcomes for women and HCWs, the study is designed to identify actionable gaps while avoiding causal interpretation of cross-sectional associations.

articles.title: Cost effectiveness of residential care for mental health and substance use disorders: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the cost effectiveness of residential care for mental and substance use disorders.
METHODS: The review follows the PRISMA guidelines with the protocol registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD42021287480). Embase, Medline, CINAHL, PsychINFO, and EconLit databases were searched until 31 March 2025. This review included studies that conducted a full economic evaluation or a return-on-investment (ROI) analysis of residential care or supported housing for mental and/or substance use disorders across all age spectrums. A narrative synthesis was conducted to summarise the findings of the included studies. The 10-point Drummond checklist was used to evaluate study quality.
RESULTS: Total 33 studies were included that consisted of 25 full economic evaluations and seven ROI studies. More than 93% of eligible studies focused on adults, and only two targeted children and adolescents. Most studies showed that residential care for mental or substance use disorders was dominant (i.e., cost-saving and more effective) compared to inpatient care from a healthcare sector perspective. Residential care for substance use disorders was found to be dominant or cost-effective based on a pre-defined threshold compared to outpatient care from a societal perspective.
CONCLUSION: Residential care and supported housing programs offer cost effective services for adults with mental and/or substance use disorders. However, long-term cost effective evidence of such services is required. Future economic evaluations focusing on residential care for children and adolescents, residential care in low- and middle-income countries, or using floating outreach or day programs as comparators are encouraged.

articles.title: Telerehabilitation and teleassessment in rare pediatric neurological disorders: an ERN-RND telerehabilitation working group systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Children and adolescents with rare neurological disorders (RNDs) often require long-term rehabilitation, but specialist access is limited by geography, medical fragility, and travel burden.
