Telerehabilitation and teleassessment may extend care into the home, yet evidence remains fragmented. We evaluated functional outcomes and summarized feasibility, adherence, acceptability, safety, and teleassessment measurement properties.
METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251238931) followed PRISMA and SWiM guidance. PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched through April 20, 2026, supplemented by citation searching. Eligible studies evaluated telerehabilitation or teleassessment in participants aged ≤18 years with Orphanet-classified RNDs and reported child-level functional outcomes. Mixed cohorts required separable data or ≥80% eligible participants. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence using design-appropriate tools.
RESULTS: 2,260 unique records were screened and 71 full texts assessed; 16 studies were included. 13 evaluated telerehabilitation (316 participants: 203 intervention, 113 comparator/control) and 3 evaluated teleassessment (94 participants). Most studies involved neuromuscular disorders, mainly Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy; other conditions included Rett syndrome, Fragile X syndrome, Dravet syndrome, Canavan disease, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and rare pediatric ataxias. Technologies included videoconferencing, apps, wearable sensors, and video-based assessment. Telerehabilitation was associated with improvement or stabilization in selected motor, respiratory, cognitive, communication, and daily functional outcomes, whereas global measures often showed limited short-term change. Feasibility, adherence, and acceptability were generally favorable. No major telerehabilitation-related safety concerns were reported when assessed. Teleassessment showed good reliability or agreement with in-person motor assessment.
DISCUSSION: In selected pediatric RNDs, telerehabilitation and teleassessment demonstrate strong feasibility, high acceptability, and meaningful clinical potential as effective complements to in-person care. These approaches offer valuable opportunities to expand access, enhance continuity of care, and support patient-centered rehabilitation. Larger multicenter studies should evaluate long-term outcomes and equitable implementation.

articles.title: Early Developmental Interventions for Infants Born Very Preterm: A Survey of Australian Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy Practice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To describe clinical practices of Australian physiotherapists and occupational therapists providing early developmental interventions for infants born very preterm (VPT; <32 weeks' gestation) during the first year of life.
METHODS: A national survey was conducted with physiotherapists and occupational therapists who had cared for infants born VPT, under 12 months' corrected age. Clinician demographics and practice characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. Intervention descriptions (guided by the Template for Intervention Description and Replication for Rehabilitation checklist), and perceived barriers and facilitators, were analyzed using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Of 114 responses analyzed (74.6% physiotherapists), representing all Australian states, territories and care sectors, most reported more than 10 years of clinical experience (65.8%), provided care during neonatal hospital admissions (65.8%), and worked within multidisciplinary teams (93.9%). Interventions encompassed multiple interacting components, described using varied terminology. Three categories of barriers and facilitators included: systems and structures, infant and family characteristics, and clinician capabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: Physiotherapists and occupational therapists in Australia provide early developmental interventions across multiple sectors within collaborative practice settings. Variability in terminology and systems-level barriers highlight the need for greater consistency in clinical practice. Standardization of terminology and strengthening clinician capabilities are key priorities for the field.

articles.title: Barriers to Implementing Sleep Interventions for Children With Autism: Malaysian Occupational Therapists' Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Implementing sleep interventions for children with autism spectrum disorder remains challenging. This study identified barriers faced by Malaysian pediatric occupational therapists. A convergent mixed-methods design integrated quantitative survey data from 112 occupational therapists with qualitative data from two focus group discussions (N = 10). Two major barriers emerged: (a) inadequate formal training and knowledge gaps regarding evidence-based sleep management, reported by 76.8% and 67.0% of survey respondents, respectively, leading to reliance on informal practices; and (b) a lack of standardized resources (59.8%) and clinical time constraints, which limited intervention consistency. Malaysian occupational therapists face critical educational, resource, and operational gaps in pediatric sleep practice. Overcoming these barriers requires structured curriculum integration, continuing professional development, standardized clinical toolkits, and multidisciplinary practice frameworks.

articles.title: Development and Initial Psychometric Evaluation of the Family Life Impact Questionnaire.
articles.abstract: Occupation and co-occupation are central to occupational therapy, yet no standardized instrument exists to measure ease of participation in co-occupations for families with a child with sensory integration challenges. This study describes the initial development and psychometric evaluation of data gathered with the Family Life Impact Questionnaire (FLIQ), a parent-report measure assessing perceived ease of family participation. Using Rasch measurement methods, we iteratively evaluated the 43-item FLIQ with a sample of 62 parents of children with sensory integration challenges (n = 25) and typically developing children (n = 37). Analyses supported a two-subscale structure: Social Participation (nine items) and Daily Life Management (25 items), rated on a 4-point scale. Both demonstrated strong reliability (person separation reliability = .88-.95), good item fit, and large between-group effect sizes. FLIQ shows promise as a clinically meaningful, occupation-centered instrument for assessing and monitoring family participation outcomes.

articles.title: Giving Vulnerable Parents a Voice: A Qualitative Synthesis Review of Parent Engagement Experience in Child Maltreatment Prevention Programs.
articles.abstract: Recent child welfare policies in the United States prioritize child maltreatment prevention, making parent engagement in voluntary prevention services crucial to program effectiveness. However, engaging parents in high-risk families remains a significant challenge. This qualitative synthesis review examines parents' perspectives on factors influencing their engagement and identifies parent-recommended strategies to enhance engagement. A systematic search of multiple databases yielded 3,447 studies published between 1980 and 2022. Fifty-three peer-reviewed qualitative and mixed-methods studies published between 1991 and 2022 that explored parent engagement experiences in child maltreatment prevention programs met the inclusion criteria. We assessed study quality using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tool and synthesized qualitative findings using thematic analysis. The qualitative synthesis identified three major domains influencing parent engagement: factors shaping parent engagement, engagement experiences, and parent-recommended strategies. Parents engaged more successfully when programs addressed contextual, internal, and external factors, including socioeconomic adversity, motivation, practical resources, program design, and provider relationships. Positive engagement fostered trust, support, parenting confidence, and stronger family relationships, whereas judgment, cultural mismatch, provider inconsistency, and logistical barriers hindered engagement. Parents recommended culturally responsive and father-inclusive services, flexible program delivery, practical supports, and strong provider-parent partnerships to strengthen engagement. Parent engagement in child maltreatment prevention programs is a dynamic process shaped by interactions among individual, programmatic, and broader contextual factors. Building trusting relationships, reducing structural barriers, and incorporating parents' perspectives into program design and delivery are essential for strengthening engagement and improving the effectiveness of child maltreatment prevention services.

articles.title: Early-Life Overfeeding Drives Lasting Species-Level Shifts of the Gut Microbiome and Exacerbates Allergic Asthma in Mice.
articles.abstract: Early-life overweight is associated with increased asthma risk in children, but the mechanisms linking metabolic status, the gut microbiome and airway disease remain poorly explored. To address this, we used a litter-size reduction model in mice to examine how early-life overfeeding and overweight shape gut microbial development and later allergic asthma severity. Overfed offspring displayed increased body weight, adiposity and altered body proportions from early postnatal life onward, with more pronounced effects in females. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing identified a specific, lasting dysbiosis in the overweight female mice, characterized by reduced alpha diversity and species-level shifts in Lactobacillus, Muribaculum and Bacteroides. Crucially, upon allergic sensitization in adulthood, these animals displayed an exacerbated disease state consistent with an 'obese-asthma' phenotype, marked by heightened airway inflammation, intense eosinophilic and neutrophilic infiltration, higher Type 2 cytokine levels (i.e., IL-4, IL-5) and altered bronchoalveolar immune profiles. These findings suggest that early-life nutritional imbalance establishes an altered immunometabolic trajectory via the gut-lung axis, providing a mechanistic basis for the increased severity observed in obesity-associated asthma.

articles.title: Immediate Postpartum Mental Health and Sleep in Mothers and Fathers with Healthy Newborns.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The postpartum period represents a critical window for parental psychological adjustment, but whether this is the case immediately after birth remains understudied. Furthermore, while many aspects of maternal mental health have been widely investigated in high-risk contexts, less is known about critical factors such as sleep-related vulnerability and attachment-related processes in low-risk situations, how these relate to early mental health in fathers, or how these factors may be associated with neonatal behavior.
METHODS: Thirty-two mother-father-newborn triads, comprising 32 mothers, 32 fathers, and their 32 healthy, full-term newborns, were included in the study. Newborn behavioral functioning was evaluated with the NBAS on Day 2. Mothers completed the EPDS, ECR, and STAI on Day 3. Both parents completed the CES-D, PSS, SCI, and FIRST on Day 3. Correlation, paired-comparison, and exploratory regression analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: Clinically relevant elevations on at least one psychological or sleep-related measure were observed in 59.4% of mothers and 28.1% of fathers. Mothers showed significantly higher depressive symptoms, poorer sleep quality, and greater sleep reactivity than fathers. Among mothers, depressive symptoms were associated with greater sleep reactivity, with trait anxiety showing the strongest association with depressive symptoms. Maternal and paternal depressive symptoms were also positively associated across partners. Newborn behavioral functioning was broadly within expected ranges, and no association between parental psychological or sleep-related measures and NBAS cluster scores survived FDR correction.
DISCUSSION: Psychological and sleep-related vulnerability was detectable in parents during the immediate postpartum period in this low-risk clinical context, with higher levels observed in mothers. Cross-partner concordance was limited to depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that early screening of both parents may be clinically relevant. Sleep reactivity and anxiety were associated with maternal postpartum distress, but their potential predictive value requires confirmation in longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Reversible Xerophthalmia in an Autistic Child With Selective Eating.
articles.abstract: Vitamin A deficiency (VAD) is a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness. Increasingly, severe nutritional deficiencies are recognized in urban settings among children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) due to extreme dietary selectivity. A 9-year-old girl with ASD and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder presented with a 2-month history of bilateral ocular redness and photophobia refractory to topical therapies. Examination revealed a Bitot's spot, conjunctival keratinization and a corneal epithelial defect in the right eye and left inferior conjunctival xerosis. Diagnosed with xerophthalmia secondary to VAD, she also had multiple micronutrient deficiencies and nutritional rickets. Management included intravenous vitamins A and D, oral multivitamins, and electrolyte correction. Within 1 month, ocular changes fully resolved, leaving a superficial right corneal scar. Chronic, treatment-resistant ocular symptoms in children with ASD should prompt suspicion of VAD. Early multidisciplinary intervention and prompt supplementation are vital to prevent permanent blindness.

articles.title: Ten myths about milrinone in pediatric cardiogenic shock.
articles.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a severe and increasingly common condition in children, representing a global health and economic burden. Inodilators (i.e., vasoactive agents with inotropic and vasodilator effects), most commonly dobutamine and milrinone, are the cornerstone of pharmacological treatment for CS in children. Although pediatric guidelines still recommend dobutamine as the first-line inodilator in CS, the use of milrinone has become predominant in this indication. Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase - 3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects and is commonly regarded as offering several theoretical advantages over dobutamine. Based on a critical review of current evidence, we examine here ten myths about milrinone in pediatric CS. The hemodynamic profile of milrinone in CS appears to rely primarily on vasodilation, with limited evidence for clinically meaningful inotropic or lusitropic effects. Current data support a neutral effect on myocardial oxygen consumption and an efficacy in preventing low cardiac output syndrome after pediatric cardiac surgery, while milrinone clearance is reduced in acute kidney injury with unclear clinical significance. However, no consistent evidence demonstrates milrinone's superiority over dobutamine in reducing mortality, length of hospital stay, or tachyarrhythmia, nor its greater efficacy in patients receiving beta-blockers. Its presumed benefits in newborns and in patients with right ventricular failure or pulmonary hypertension remain uncertain and warrant further investigation. What is known: • Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects. • Milrinone has become the preferred inodilator over dobutamine in pediatric cardiogenic shock. What is new: • Milrinone's efficacy appears to stem from vasodilation rather than significant inotropy or lusitropy. • No consistent evidence shows its superiority over dobutamine; further study is warranted.

articles.title: REACH: A multidimensional index for measuring community concordance in US children's hospitals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Equitable access to pediatric healthcare is essential for improving health outcomes and assessing health system accountability. Existing metrics for measuring hospital concordance with surrounding communities are adult-centric or sensitive to hospital catchment area definition.
OBJECTIVE: Through REACH (Representation and Equity in Area-based Child Hospitalizations) index, we aimed to develop a multidimensional, robust, and standardized concordance measure that combines four sociodemographic dimensions, ethnicity, payor, race, and sex, into a composite score that is comparable across hospitals.
METHODS: Using 695,046 inpatient and observation encounters from 48 U.S. children's hospitals in the Pediatric Health Information System (PHIS) for 2023 and 2023 American Community Survey (ACS) five-year estimate, we defined hospital catchment areas and calculated dimension-specific concordance indexes using weighted Chi-square divergence between observed hospitalizations and expected pediatric population. The four indexes were aggregated into a composite REACH score with 95% confidence intervals. Robustness of REACH was assessed using Spearman correlation between unrestricted and two conservative catchment definitions across 48 hospitals.
RESULTS: REACH scores ranged from 0.89 to 0.98. All hospitals demonstrated high (≥0.80) to very high (≥0.90) concordance, with 60% of hospitals scoring ≥0.95. REACH was stable across catchment definitions, with strong correlations (ρ ≥ 0.7); all hospitals stayed in the high-to-very high range. Overall, 87.5% of hospitals retained their concordance category, while six showed modest downward shifts (from very high to high) under the most conservative definition.
CONCLUSION: REACH offers an effective framework to measure community concordance in pediatric hospitals, with potential future applications for benchmarking, quality improvement, and policy development to advance equitable healthcare access.

articles.title: Essential Paediatric Life Support Skills: A Set of Rolling Cart-Based Simulations in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Frequent high occupancy combined with increased rates of nursing turnover in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) has led to a limited ability to perform in-room high-fidelity simulations and an increased need for focused life support training for PICU personnel.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary team of physicians, nurses, respiratory therapists, and undergraduate students implemented various simulations in the PICU August through December 2022. Simulations were conducted via a rolling-cart model to capture the largest audience and included, but were not limited to, chest compressions, defibrillation, bag-mask ventilation, push-pull fluid bolus administration, emergency cart utilization, and intraosseous access.
RESULTS: Twelve simulation sessions were performed. Twenty-four participants supplied feedback, with the majority of responses being overwhelmingly positive. In answer to the question 'The content of the simulation was relevant to my current role in the PICU', over 83% of the respondents said that they 'strongly agree'. 100% of respondents would recommend the simulation they performed to colleagues. Additionally, the participation rate was high, with a median of 10 participants per session. For comparison, the PICU in-room simulations had a median of six participants per session.
DISCUSSION: Conducting rolling cart-based simulations involving life support practices is a well-received method of education and garners high participation from PICU health care workers. This model can be beneficial in times when resources are limited.
RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Maintaining life support competency for staff in the PICU can be well supported by brief, low-fidelity rolling cart-based simulations.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients and general public were not involved in the study. Staff from the paediatric intensive care unit were involved by participating in the bedside simulations.

articles.title: Exploring outcomes and insights from joint agency response investigations for children with learning disabilities who die unexpectedly: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In England, sudden unexpected child deaths are investigated through a joint agency response (JAR). There is wide variation in practice concerning JAR, particularly for children with underlying health conditions, many of whom have learning disability (LD); potentially limiting identification of causes and contributory factors for deaths.
METHODS: All child deaths with LD (including those who died suddenly and unexpectedly), aged 4–17 years, dying between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022 were identified retrospectively by the National Child Mortality Database (NCMD). Data were extracted from NCMD records and information on life-limiting conditions (LLCs) obtained from Hospital Episode Statistics. Unexpected deaths investigated through a JAR were compared with those without for demographics, underlying conditions, causes of death and process of investigations.
RESULTS: There were 738 deaths of children with LD of which 309 (41.8%) were unexpected; 257/309 (83%) had LLCs; 215/309 (69.5%) were subject to JAR. Chromosomal, genetic and congenital anomalies were the most common cause of death accounting for 95/215 (44.2%) JAR cases and 49/94 (52.1%) non-JAR cases. Compliance with JAR processes overall was low. Postmortem examination (PM) took place for 166/215 (77.2%) JAR cases and 21/94 (22.3%) non-JAR cases (p<0.001). A new condition was identified as the cause of death rather than a pre-existing condition as cause of death in 112/215 (52.3%) JAR cases compared with 13/94 (13.8%) non-JAR cases (p<0.001). After adjustment for JAR components, only PM remained associated, with an increase in chance of identifying a new cause of death (72.1% (95% CI 61.6% to 72.7%)). JAR home visits provided little new information relevant to the cause of death.
CONCLUSIONS: Clearer guidance is required on when and how to undertake JAR investigations following sudden deaths of children with LD. Current guidance is largely based on deaths of previously healthy children.

articles.title: Natural environments and sleep during pregnancy: Associations of green and blue spaces with prenatal sleep outcomes in a Canadian cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sleep quality during pregnancy is critical for maternal and child health, yet environmental determinants of prenatal sleep remain understudied. Green and blue spaces have demonstrated positive effects on mental health, which is robustly associated with sleep, but direct impacts of green and blue spaces on sleep among pregnant individuals are unclear. This study examined associations between green and blue spaces and sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment during pregnancy.
METHODS: Data from the pan-Canadian Pregnancy during the Covid-19 Pandemic (PdP, n = 8583) were linked with green (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), tree canopy) and blue space (distance from the nearest water body) data from Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium (CANUE). Sleep outcomes included self-reported sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment. Multiple linear regression models adjusted for age, ethnicity, neighborhood deprivation, socioeconomic status, population density, COVID-19 restriction severity, season, physical activity, and trimester.
RESULTS: Greater tree canopy cover and NDVI were significantly associated with longer sleep duration. Contrary to our hypothesis, greater distance from water bodies was also associated with longer sleep duration and lower sleep disturbance. After additional adjustments, only the associations with sleep duration remained significant. No associations were observed for sleep-related impairment.
CONCLUSIONS: Green spaces, particularly tree canopy, may positively influence prenatal sleep duration, whereas the effects of blue spaces may depend more on the type of interaction with these environments and additional contextual factors. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating environmental factors, particularly tree-rich environment, into maternal health strategies and urban planning to support perinatal well-being.

articles.title: Surrogate decision-making support in pediatric end-of-life care during infancy and early childhood: A case-derived conceptual framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reports on nursing support addressing changes in family functioning during surrogate decision-making in pediatric end-of-life care are limited. This case describes treatment and end-of-life care of an infant with atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (AT/RT).
METHOD: Clinical records and the primary nurse's recollections informed a four-phase account of the clinical course, surrogate decision-making, family situation, and nursing support. Family functioning was retrospectively analyzed using the structural, developmental, and functional dimensions of the Calgary Family Assessment Model.
RESULTS: At admission, the infant had repeated vomiting, minimal spontaneous movement, and an inability to roll over. Treatment included surgery, chemotherapy, autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplantation, and radiotherapy. Despite treatment, the disease progressed, and the infant died at home surrounded by family. The mother's surrogate decision-making evolved with changes in the child's condition, treatment limitations, and the increasing important of family time. She struggled to reconcile hope for continued treatment, treatment burden, and family time. Family roles, relationships, and support systems changed. The nurse helped the mother express her values and wishes and revisit decisions, without pressuring her toward a single conclusion. In parallel, nursing support addressed changes in family roles, caregiving responsibilities, and available support.
CONCLUSION: This case suggests the importance of attending to both surrogate decision-making and changes in family functioning in pediatric end-of-life care during infancy and early childhood. A case-derived conceptual framework illustrates these parallel aspects of nursing support and requires further examination across cases.

articles.title: High-alert medication safety in Pediatric critical care: A multinational analysis of nurses' knowledge and reporting barriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-alert medications are frequently used in pediatric intensive care units and can cause serious harm when used in error. Multinational evidence on pediatric intensive care nurses' knowledge and reporting barriers remains limited.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional multinational study was conducted among 705 pediatric intensive care nurses from Egypt, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Iraq. Data were collected using a sociodemographic and professional form, a 10-item High-Alert Medication Knowledge Questionnaire, and a 23-item Attitudes Toward Medication Errors and Error Reporting Questionnaire. Descriptive, correlation, simple regression, and dummy-coded multiple regression analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27.
RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 5.46 ± 2.69 on the 0-10 scale, corresponding to 54.55% of the maximum possible score. Professional and organizational consequences had the highest mean percentage among attitude domains (59.18%), followed by fear and punitive barriers (50.94%); beliefs about error prevention and safety culture had the lowest percentage (33.45%). Knowledge showed weak correlations with reporting-related attitude domains. Multiple regression showed that knowledge was associated with gender, country, and high-alert medication safety training, whereas total attitude was associated with country and total nursing experience.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric intensive care nurses showed important gaps in high-alert medication safety knowledge, while reporting attitudes reflected persistent organizational and professional barriers. Findings support competency-based education, just-culture reporting systems, feedback mechanisms, and work-system redesign.

articles.title: Changes in pediatric nurses' knowledge of autism spectrum disorder and alternative communication strategies before and immediately after a health education program: a one-group pretest-posttest study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess changes in pediatric nurses' knowledge of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and alternative communication strategies before and immediately after a health education program.
METHODS: A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest study was conducted among pediatric nurses from two teaching hospitals. Participants completed a knowledge questionnaire assessing ASD and alternative communication strategies immediately before and after the program; the questionnaire did not assess observed communication skills or clinical performance.
RESULTS: Baseline knowledge of ASD and alternative communication strategies was limited. Mean ASD knowledge scores increased from 5.92 ± 2.39 at pretest to 12.30 ± 1.38 at immediate posttest. Mean knowledge scores for alternative communication strategies increased from 6.66 ± 3.22 to 12.75 ± 1.39. Both pretest-posttest differences were statistically significant (p < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric nurses demonstrated higher questionnaire-based knowledge scores immediately after the health education program. However, the one-group pretest-posttest design does not establish that the program alone caused these changes or that the knowledge gains were sustained. Questionnaire familiarity, recall, and testing effects may also have contributed to the observed differences.
IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Structured health education may support pediatric nurses' knowledge of ASD and alternative communication strategies. Further evaluation should assess knowledge retention over time and include objective measures of practical communication skills to determine whether knowledge gains translate into clinical competence.

articles.title: Effect of an educational program on pediatric nurses' performance within the critical golden hour following pediatric trauma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Outcomes after pediatric trauma, a leading cause of childhood death and disability, depend substantially on care delivered during the first "golden hour". Nurses are the first to assess injured children, yet evidence shows persistent deficits in their trauma-specific preparation. This study evaluated the effect of a structured educational program on pediatric nurses' knowledge, practice, self-confidence, and attitudes regarding golden-hour trauma care.
DESIGN AND METHODS: A one-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design was used. A convenience sample of 108 nurses in the pediatric emergency department of Beni-Suef University Hospital, Egypt, completed a five-part instrument covering the four outcome domains, received a structured researcher-delivered program on golden-hour pediatric trauma assessment and management, and were reassessed identically. Five pediatric nursing experts confirmed content validity, and internal consistency was acceptable (KR-20 = 0.86 and 0.79 for the dichotomous tools; Cronbach's α = 0.81 and 0.78 for the Likert tools). Paired t-tests and Spearman's correlations were used.
RESULTS: Before the program, 51.9% of nurses were unfamiliar with the golden hour and 88.9% had received no related training. Afterwards, mean knowledge rose from 66.3% to 85.9%, practice from 51.1% to 79.7%, self-confidence from 3.06 to 3.79, and attitudes from 2.48 to 2.76 (all p < .01). Knowledge correlated positively with practice (r = 0.684, p < .01), self-confidence, and attitudes.
CONCLUSIONS: The program was associated with significant improvement across all four domains.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Golden-hour training should be embedded in professional development for pediatric emergency nurses and reinforced with simulation, standardized protocols, and mentorship.

articles.title: Improved sleep and clinical outcomes following a single-session intervention among adolescents with borderline personality disorder features.
articles.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is a serious mental illness that often emerges in adolescence. Although efficacious treatments have been developed, they are often lengthy, expensive, inaccessible, and require specialized training to deliver. Optimizing BPD prevention and early treatment is an important public health priority. Disrupted sleep is closely linked to key BPD features, and prior research has documented a range of sleep problems among BPD samples that appear to worsen symptom course and duration. This intervention trial (NCT04507308) assessed the effects of a single-session sleep-focused treatment on adolescent sleep and BPD-related symptoms. Fifty-seven adolescents (ages 13-18) with 3+ clinically impairing BPD features and at least some self-reported sleep-related difficulties participated with a caregiver. Participants completed baseline surveys, interviews, and 10-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA) protocol to examine BPD symptoms and sleep in daily life. Youth also collected at-home ambulatory electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings before undergoing the treatment informed by the Transdiagnostic Sleep and Circadian Intervention. Post-treatment, youth practiced their new sleep routine for approximately one month before undergoing reassessment (EMA, EEG, surveys). Many indices of sleep quantity and quality improved across both objective (EEG) and subjective assessments (EMA and self- and caregiver-report). Youth reported an earlier clock time at sleep onset and earlier waketime, more sleep, and fewer awakenings in daily life. Every sleep-related questionnaire score improved at post-intervention and was maintained at one-month follow-up. Multiple (though not all) indices of BPD symptoms also improved significantly. Findings suggest sleep may be a promising intervention target for at-risk youth.

articles.title: Early Life Interventions in IgE-mediated Food Allergy Prevention and Management.
articles.abstract: Food allergy has become a major public health concern. Over the past decade, advances in understanding early immune development have transformed approaches to both prevention and treatment of IgE-mediated food allergy. Landmark trials demonstrated that early and sustained introduction of allergenic foods, particularly peanut and egg, significantly reduces the risk of food allergy. This lead to a paradigm shift from allergen avoidance to proactive early introduction. For children who develop food allergy, emerging evidence indicates that early intervention may offer unique advantages, possibly due to heightened immune plasticity. Oral, epicutaneous, and sublingual immunotherapy have shown efficacy in increasing allergen tolerance, with studies suggesting improved outcomes and greater likelihood of remission when initiated in early childhood. Mechanistic studies indicate that these therapies modify allergic immune responses through suppression of effector cells, induction of regulatory pathways, and increased production of protective allergen-specific antibodies. In addition, omalizumab has become the first biologic approved in the United States for food allergy in individuals aged ≥1 year. Despite substantial progress, important knowledge gaps remain. Continued integration of mechanistic discoveries, clinical trials, and real-world evidence will be essential to refine precision approaches that maximize prevention, improve treatment outcomes, and reduce the lifelong burden of food allergy.

articles.title: Vaping-Related Pneumomediastinum in Adolescents: Characterizing Work Up and Management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescent vaping, including nicotine and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) products, carries numerous adverse effects. Case reports, primarily in young adults, describe an association between inhaled substance use and pneumomediastinum, but management of affected adolescents remains unclear. This study sought to characterize this population and identify variations in practice patterns to improve future care.
METHODS: A single center, retrospective descriptive study with 60-day follow-up was conducted. The hospital's radiology database was searched for imaging studies noting "pneumomediastinum" in patients >10 and 18 years from January 2014-May 2025. Patients with pneumomediastinum secondary to another etiology (ex: trauma, recent surgery) were excluded. Those reporting recent inhaled substance use were included.
RESULTS: Forty-one adolescents met inclusion criteria. Median age at symptom onset was 16 years (range 14-18 years). Nicotine and THC vaping were reported in 73.2% and 78.0% of patients, respectively, with >50% using daily. Hospital admission occurred in 68.3% of cases with median length of stay of 2 days (IQR 1, 3). Three patients required intensive care unit admission, one of whom was hypoxic and obtunded at presentation necessitating intubation. Admitted patients underwent more chest radiographs than those discharged from the emergency department (median 2 vs 1, p=0.027). Nineteen patients underwent esophagram, none demonstrating injury. No interventions were required and no patient experienced recurrence during follow up.
CONCLUSION: Management of vaping-related pneumomediastinum in adolescents, notably the use of imaging, varies considerably. Most patients may not require admission or transfer to a specialized pediatric facility unless presenting with hypoxia or respiratory distress.

articles.title: Kawasaki Disease Linked to Age-Dependent Temporal, Seasonal, Temporal Clustering, and Atmospheric Circulation Patterns in San Diego County, 2002-2025.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate age-stratified temporal, seasonal, temporal clustering, and atmospheric circulation patterns of Kawasaki disease (KD) incidence in a large US cohort over a 24-year period in San Diego County and to determine whether these patterns support age-dependent environmental influences.
STUDY DESIGN: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 1,707 children with KD hospitalized at Rady Children's Hospital San Diego (RCHSD) from 2002-2025. Patients were stratified into 6 age groups (<6 months, 6-<15 months, 15-<24 months, 24-<36 months, 36-<60 months, ≥60 months). Temporal and seasonal patterns were evaluated using normalized running means with bootstrap resampling. Temporal clustering used onset dates. Atmospheric circulation patterns during low- and high-incidence years were compared using 700-mb geopotential height anomalies.
RESULTS: ll age groups demonstrated shared interannual variability, including a nadir in February-March 2018 and peaks in late 2016 and spring 2019. Older children showed a twofold increase in incidence until 2010, followed by a plateau, and no age group demonstrated a significant increasing temporal trend thereafter. Seasonal patterns differed by age: infants and young children (<15 months) showed significant variation, with a peak in late January and nadir in late February. Older children (≥36 months) showed more stability, with increased incidence in February-March and decreased incidence in August-October. Temporal clustering identified 56 clusters involving 375 cases (22%), of which 42 (75%) occurred during the November-April high-incidence season. Comparison of geopotential height anomaly composites revealed distinct circulation patterns between low- and high-incidence years.
CONCLUSIONS: Age-dependent temporal and seasonal variation, together with temporal clustering and atmospheric circulation patterns, support a role for environmental influences in KD onset. Shared interannual fluctuations suggest common environmental influences across childhood, whereas age-specific seasonal differences indicate developmental variation in environmental exposures or susceptibility. These data support an age-dependent framework for investigating environmental influences on KD etiology.

articles.title: The burden, temporal patterns, and projected burden of asthma attributable to high BMI among children in China, 1990 - 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Childhood asthma and obesity represent two converging public health crises in China. High body mass index is an established modifiable risk factor for asthma, yet its specific epidemiological burden among Chinese children remains insufficiently characterized.
METHODS: Data on deaths and disability-adjusted life years attributable to high body mass index-related asthma among children aged 0 to 14 years in China from 1990 to 2023 were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study. Average annual percent change was used to assess temporal trends, an age-period-cohort model was applied to disentangle the independent effects of age, period, and birth cohort, and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was employed to project the burden through 2050.
RESULTS: In 2023, high body mass index-related asthma caused 8 deaths and 40,251 disability-adjusted life years among Chinese children, with males bearing a consistently higher burden. From 1990 to 2023, the age-standardized mortality rate declined significantly (average annual percent change: -4.26), while the disability-adjusted life year rate increased (average annual percent change: 1.62). Age-period-cohort analysis revealed declining mortality risk across successive periods and cohorts, whereas the risk of disability-adjusted life years increased markedly in recent birth cohorts (relative risk 1.81 for the 2014 to 2023 cohort). Projections indicate that total disability-adjusted life years will nearly triple to 102,393 by 2050.
CONCLUSION: While mortality from high body mass index-attributable asthma has declined, the morbidity burden is escalating and projected to worsen substantially by 2050. Integrated strategies targeting childhood obesity are urgently needed to mitigate this growing threat.

articles.title: Early Childhood CASPR2 Autoimmunity with Prominent Autonomic Dysfunction: Diagnostic Challenges and Effective Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: CASPR2-associated neurological diseases cover a broad clinical spectrum, with limbic encephalitis and Morvan syndrome representing the most characteristic autoimmune phenotypes. We report the case of a 2-year-old boy who presented with abdominal and generalized pain, refusal to eat or drink, weight loss, loss of mobility, and behavioral changes, including sleep disturbances. Further clinical evaluation revealed pharmacoresistant arterial hypertension and hyperhidrosis. Extensive diagnostic testing excluded infectious and toxic causes. CASPR2 antibodies were detected in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid. Initial therapy with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulins resulted in only minimal clinical improvement. Significant clinical recovery was only achieved after escalation of immunotherapy with plasmapheresis and subsequent B-cell-depleting therapy with rituximab. At the most recent follow-up visit, seven months after the first rituximab infusion, the patient showed complete recovery without residual symptoms. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of CASPR2-associated autoimmunity in early childhood and highlights the importance of early recognition of this rare but treatable disease.

articles.title: Bolus Volume and Mortality in Extremely Low Gestational Age Infants with Shock.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between clinical outcomes and the volume of fluid boluses administered during the first 24 hours of a shock episode in extremely low gestational age newborns (ELGANs) requiring vasoactive support.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included ELGANs (≤28 weeks) at a single Level IV NICU between 2013 and 2021 who received vasoactive medications for shock within the first seven days of life. The primary predictor was total fluid volume (cc/kg) administered in the first 24 hours of shock. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for gestational age, birth weight, 5-minute Apgar score, systemic corticosteroid use, and highest vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS).
RESULTS: Of 97 infants, 26 (27%) died within 14 days of the shock episode. Non-survivors received a higher median bolus volume compared to survivors (40 cc/kg vs. 20 cc/kg, p<0.001). Greater bolus volume was independently associated with increased odds of 14-day mortality (aOR 1.026, 95% CI 1.004-1.048, p=0.019). Each additional 10 cc/kg was associated with an approximately 29% increase in mortality odds. No significant associations were found between bolus volume and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or bronchopulmonary dysplasia after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Greater cumulative fluid bolus volume was independently associated with higher 14-day mortality in ELGANs with shock requiring vasoactive support. Although residual confounding illness severity cannot be excluded, these findings support cautious, individualized use of volume expansion and highlight the need for prospective studies of hemodynamically targeted resuscitation in this population.

articles.title: Departure From Planned 39-Week Delivery for Fetal Congenital Heart Disease: Indications for Earlier Birth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality.
RESULTS: 46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02).
CONCLUSION: Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

articles.title: Healthcare Team Awareness, Knowledge, and Perceptions of Neonatal Delirium: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neonatal delirium is increasingly recognized as an important neuropsychiatric condition in critically ill infants, yet awareness and understanding among healthcare providers remain limited. Underdiagnosis may contribute to prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. This study assessed healthcare team members' awareness, perceptions, and knowledge of neonatal delirium across a large children's hospital and affiliated neonatal care locations.
STUDY DESIGN: A cross‑sectional electronic survey was distributed to multidisciplinary NICU team members within a quaternary academic children's health system and affiliated sites. The survey included demographic items, multiple‑choice questions, Likert‑scale statements, and open‑ended responses. Descriptive statistics summarized quantitative data, and content categorization was applied to open‑ended responses.
RESULTS: A total of 117 respondents completed the survey, representing nursing, advanced practice providers, physicians, respiratory therapists, rehabilitation therapists, and pharmacy. Nearly half of respondents had never heard the term neonatal delirium. Among those familiar with the condition, definitions most commonly referenced agitation, altered consciousness, and sleep-wake disturbance. Ninety percent of respondents agreed that newborn infants can experience delirium, while only 60% indicated that delirium can also occur in preterm infants. Sixty percent indicated that delirium is assessable in infants, and 73% reported previously caring for an infant with suspected delirium. Respondents identified multiple barriers to screening and management, including limited awareness, lack of content expertise, and concerns about medication safety.
CONCLUSIONS: Awareness and understanding of neonatal delirium vary considerably among NICU providers, with notable educational and structural barriers to consistent recognition and management. These findings support the need for foundational education, multidisciplinary training, and continued research to inform development of effective strategies for assessing and managing neonatal delirium in neonatal care settings.

articles.title: Validity and Reliability of the Almli Handedness Assessment (AHA) in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
articles.abstract: Handedness is a key behavioral marker of hemispheric specialization and is closely associated with motor, perceptual, and cognitive development. Although standardized questionnaires such as the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory-Short Form (EHI-Short) provide indirect measures of manual lateralization, observational tools are needed to capture children's functional hand use in everyday activities. This study evaluated the reliability and validity of the Turkish version of the Almli Handedness Assessment (AHA) in 188 children aged 5-12 years, including 81 children with ASD and 107 typically developing (TD) peers. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa, and convergent validity was evaluated through agreement analyses, classification accuracy, and correlations with the EHI-Short. Inter-rater agreement was almost perfect (κ = 0.885, p < .001) and test-retest agreement over a 14-day interval demonstrated excellent stability in the ASD group (κ = 0.870) and perfect agreement in an availability-based TD subsample (n = 50; κ = 1.000). AHA and EHI-Short handedness classifications showed strong categorical agreement (ASD: κ = 0.914; TD: κ = 0.868), and AHA laterality indices were strongly correlated with EHI-Short laterality coefficients (ASD: r = .939; TD: r = .982). Children with ASD showed a higher prevalence of atypical handedness than TD peers, and ASD status remained associated with atypical handedness after adjustment for age and gender. Category-specific estimates for mixed-handedness in the TD group should be interpreted cautiously because no TD children were classified as mixed-handed by the AHA. Overall, the Turkish AHA demonstrated good reliability, with evidence of convergent validity, and agreement with the EHI-Short. These findings should be regarded as preliminary psychometric evidence, and further validation in larger and more diverse samples is warranted.

articles.title: Early Feeding Characteristics from the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Through the First Year of Life and Neurodevelopment at 24 Months in Preterm Infants.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) oral feeding progression and feeding development during the first year of life are associated with neurodevelopment at 24 months corrected age in preterm infants.
STUDY DESIGN: This longitudinal cohort study included 94 preterm infants born at < 37 weeks' gestation in a single level III NICU. NICU feeding progression was operationalized using gestational age-adjusted z-scores for time to full oral feeding. Parent-reported feeding symptoms and feeding skills were assessed during early (1-2 months), mid (4-8 months), and late (10-12 months) infancy. Neurodevelopment was assessed at 24 months corrected age using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-IV). Multivariable linear regression models were used to examine associations between early feeding characteristics and 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes, adjusting for gestational age, infant sex, parent education, and parent race.
RESULTS: Delayed NICU feeding progression showed a trend toward lower motor scores at 24 months (β = -5.12, p = 0.06). Parent-reported feeding symptoms during late infancy were associated with lower motor scores (β = -0.10, p = 0.03) and a similar trend for language score (β = -0.17, p = 0.06). Higher feeding skill proficiency during mid and late infancy was consistently associated with higher motor, language, and cognitive scores (mid infancy: β = 0.19-0.37, p < 0.01; late infancy: β = 0.23-0.38, p < 0.001). The Oral-Motor Coordination, Basic Movement Patterns, and Fundamental Oral-Motor subscales also demonstrated significant positive associations across all neurodevelopmental domains in both mid and late infancy.
CONCLUSION: Feeding characteristics from NICU hospitalization through infancy, including oral feeding progression, feeding symptoms, and feeding skill development, were associated with neurodevelopment at 24 months in preterm infants. These early feeding characteristics may provide clinically accessible measures to inform developmental surveillance and follow-up care.
KEY POINTS: · Delayed NICU oral feeding progression trended toward lower 24-month motor scores in preterm infants.. · More late infancy feeding symptoms were associated with lower 24-month motor scores.. · Higher infant feeding skill proficiency was associated with higher 24-month Bayley-IV scores.. · Early feeding monitoring helps identify preterm infants needing targeted developmental support..

articles.title: Not all food avoidance is the same: a latent profile analysis informed by the Appetite Self-Regulation model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food avoidance is a common problem for some children and negatively affects their dietary quality. The Appetite Self-Regulation (ASR) model proposes that food avoidance phenotypes arise in children due to interactions between bottom-up and top-down processes. However, it is unknown how these factors combine within children to produce distinct food avoidant profiles. This study aimed to better understand different types of food avoidance by identifying food avoidant profiles in middle childhood and examining their neurodevelopmental correlates.
METHODS: Participants were 517 parents of children aged 5-12 years. Latent profile analysis was conducted using multiple ASR domains, including appetitive traits (satiety responsiveness, slowness in eating, food responsiveness, enjoyment of food and food fussiness), temperament traits (fear, shyness, inhibitory control, impulsivity), food avoidance behaviours (food avoidance, texture sensitivity and cognitive rigidity) and liking of low- and high-energy-density foods (vegetable and snack liking). Multinomial logistic regression examined associations between profile membership and neurodevelopmental disorders.
RESULTS: Five profiles were identified, including two food avoidant profiles. Multi-Domain Food Avoidant profile (n = 114, 22%) was characterised by a multi-domain form of avoidance, particularly showing higher levels of fear and shyness, suggesting greater bottom-up emotional reactivity to foods. The Rigid Texture-Sensitive Avoidant profile (n = 66, 13%) showed the highest texture sensitivity and cognitive rigidity, indicating a sensory-driven pathway to food avoidance. The Rigid Texture-Sensitive Avoidant profile was also characterised by the lowest inhibitory control, reflecting reduced top-down regulatory capacity. Children with neurodevelopmental disorders were disproportionately represented in the food avoidant profiles.
CONCLUSIONS: Food avoidance in middle childhood reflects heterogeneous behavioural patterns shaped by different combinations of bottom-up avoidance processes and top-down regulatory control. Identifying distinct avoidant profiles may improve understanding of the processes underlying children's food avoidance and inform more targeted approaches to supporting children with persistent avoidant eating behaviours.

articles.title: Mid-term outcomes of medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction using suture tape in paediatric and adolescent population: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suture tape medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction avoids tendon graft harvest, but outcomes in children are poorly reported. This study evaluated functional outcomes and complications in children and adolescents with recurrent patellar instability.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 56 patients (77 knees; 40 female; mean age 14.3 years, range 8.2-17.7) underwent isolated suture tape MPFL reconstruction for recurrent instability at a tertiary centre between 2020 and 2025. Minimum follow-up was 6 months. The primary outcome was the Paediatric International Knee Documentation Committee (Pedi-IKDC) score at ≥6 months (available for 58 knees). Secondary outcomes were recurrent instability, extensor lag and other complications.
RESULTS: The mean Pedi-IKDC score improved from 49.6 (SD 13.9) to 79.6 (SD 16.9), a mean gain of 30.0 points (p < 0.001). Recurrent instability occurred in 5 of 77 knees (6.5%), one following trauma, despite trochlear dysplasia (Dejour B-D) in 79% of knees. An extensor lag was recorded in 17 of 65 knees (26.2%): 16 of these were 5-10° and resolved with physiotherapy within 3-6 months; one of approximately 25° is awaiting revision. Steroid injection for medial patellar pain was required in four knees (5.2%). No physeal complications were observed.
CONCLUSION: Suture tape MPFL reconstruction improved the Pedi-IKDC score by 30.0 points, more than three times the minimal clinically important difference, with recurrent instability (6.5%) comparable to tendon graft reconstruction in children and no physeal complications. Extensor lag (26.2%) was common but resolved with physiotherapy in all but one knee. Suture tape is a reasonable graft-free option; comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: Altered quadriceps forces and patellofemoral joint loading during walking in adolescents with patellar instability.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Patellofemoral instability is a common and clinically important knee disorder in children and adolescents, but its functional biomechanics during walking remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to compare gait kinematics, quadriceps muscle forces, and patellofemoral joint contact forces during walking between adolescents with recurrent patellar instability (PFP) and typically developing (TD) controls. We hypothesized that the PFP group would exhibit altered gait kinematics together with reduced or redistributed quadriceps-force and patellofemoral contact-force patterns during gait.
METHODS: This study used an electromyography (EMG)-informed neuromusculoskeletal modeling framework to compare gait kinematics, quadriceps muscle forces, and patellofemoral joint contact-force waveforms during walking between adolescent participants with PFP and TD controls. Forty-eight adolescents were included, comprising 24 participants with PFP and 24 controls. Three-dimensional gait analysis, ground reaction forces, and surface EMG were collected during level walking. Between-group differences were evaluated using peak comparisons, statistical parametric mapping (SPM), and principal component analysis (PCA).
RESULTS: No significant between-group differences were detected in kinematic waveforms using SPM (all p > 0.05). In contrast, significant differences were identified in patellofemoral joint contact-force waveforms in the mediolateral (cluster-level p = 0.0497 and p < 0.001) and proximodistal (both cluster-level p < 0.001) directions. Peak comparisons further showed larger relative differences in quadriceps muscle forces and patellofemoral joint contact-force components than in most kinematic variables. The PCA identified additional between-group differences in selected frontal- and transverse-plane kinematic waveforms, patellofemoral joint contact-force waveforms, and quadriceps force waveforms, particularly for vastus lateralis and rectus femoris. The PFP group also showed broader dispersion of principal component scores, indicating greater between-subject variability.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that adolescent PFP during walking is characterized less by large overt differences in gross gait kinematics and more by altered quadriceps force and patellofemoral joint loading patterns. EMG-informed neuromusculoskeletal modeling may therefore provide clinically relevant biomechanical information that could support future patient-specific assessment and rehabilitation research beyond conventional gait analysis alone.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Risk factors that predict future onset of overvaluation of weight and shape in adolescent girls.
articles.abstract: Given that overvaluation of weight/shape has emerged as a potent transdiagnostic risk factor for a range of eating disorders, we investigated risk factors that predict future onset of this key prodromal symptom to advance understanding of etiologic processes, which has not been examined previously. We used data from a community sample of 496 adolescent female participants (M age = 13.02, SD = 0.73, age range = 11.0-15.0 years) who completed annual diagnostic interviews and surveys assessing putative risk factors over 8-year period. Overvaluation of weight/shape was not significantly correlated with thin-ideal internalization, but was positively correlated with pressure to be thin, body dissatisfaction, dietary restraint, and zBMI at baseline. In univariate logistic regressions, higher baseline perceived pressure to be thin, body dissatisfaction, dietary restraint, negative emotionality, and zBMI, as well as lower parent support and self-esteem, predicted future onset of clinically meaningful overvaluation of weight/shape over 8-year follow-up. Multivariate analyses revealed that only low self-esteem showed a unique effect when statistically controlling for the other risk factors. An exploratory classification tree analysis suggested that low self-esteem was the primary pathway to overvaluation of weight/shape, but that there was also evidence of qualitative distinct risk pathways through elevated dietary restraint and zBMI. Our results suggest that certain risk factors predict future onset of clinically significant overvaluation of weight/shape, and that reducing these risk factors in selective prevention programs may prove effective in reducing a broader range of eating disorders than extent prevention programs.

articles.title: Fever management and parental anxiety in a pediatric emergency department: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fever, often associated with considerable parental anxiety, is one of the most common reasons for pediatric emergency department visits. Parental anxiety could be related to how parents manage childhood fever. This study aims to describe parental fever management practices and state anxiety among parents presenting to a pediatric emergency department and investigate the relationship between these variables.
METHODS: This descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted between November 2025 and February 2026 in the pediatric emergency department of a state hospital. The sample consisted of 360 parents of children aged 0-6 years who presented with fever and met the inclusion criteria. Data were collected through the Personal Information Form, the Parent Fever Management Scale, and the State Anxiety Inventory (STAI). Group differences were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). The relationship between parental state anxiety and fever management scores were analyzed using Pearson's correlation and hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses.
RESULTS: While the Parent Fever Management Scale mean score was 31.37 ± 6.82, the State Anxiety Inventory mean score was 48.47 ± 16.36. A significant positive correlation was found between fever management scores and parental state anxiety (r = 0.471, p < .001). Hierarchical regression analysis showed that after adjustment for the variables was included in the model, state anxiety was positively associated with fever management scores (β = 0.315, p < .001).
CONCLUSION: Parental fever management practices were positively associated with state anxiety levels. Healthcare professionals should consider parental anxiety when providing education and counseling about childhood fever management. Further intervention studies are needed to determine whether interventions addressing parental anxiety can improve the appropriateness and evidence-based nature of fever management practices.

articles.title: Application of the ICF in the functioning assessment of children with suspected developmental coordination difficulties.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) is based on a biopsychosocial model that promotes a multidimensional approach in rehabilitation. The ICF has been recommended as a framework for clinical reasoning in several health conditions, including those characterized by motor difficulties such as Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD). We compared the functioning profile of children with motor challenges (at risk [r-DCD] and probable DCD [p-DCD]) with those with typical neurodevelopment (TND) using the ICF framework.
METHODS: Cross-sectional study involving children from Southern Brazil. ICF-informed instruments included: body functions (MABC-2, 6MWT, SDQ-Por); activities (DCDQ-Br, IPAQ-SF, SDQ-Por); participation (PEM-CY) and contextual factors (sex and age). Statistics included the chi-square test, Fisher's exact test, and the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn's post hoc test with p < 0.05.
RESULTS: 208 children (mean age 8.2 [1.3] years) classified as TND (n = 158), r-DCD (n = 25) and p-DCD (n = 25) were included. In the activities domain, except for the expected lower motor skills in the p-DCD group, no differences were found across groups. In participation, there were significant differences only for lower involvement in the community for p-DCD (p = 0.016).
CONCLUSION: The impact of motor challenges was found in activities and in participation. These findings underscore the role for physical therapy interventions targeting improved coordination and balance while encouraging social interactions. The study serves as an example of how to select and combine assessment instruments aligned with ICF domains to evaluate children with motor difficulties.

articles.title: Congenital ovine goitre in northwestern Argentina: Clinicopathological and immunohistochemical characterization in natural cases.
articles.abstract: Congenital goitre is an important cause of neonatal mortality and reproductive losses in sheep raised in iodine-deficient regions. However, integrative clinicopathological studies remain scarce, particularly in South America. This study characterized congenital ovine goitre in a flock from northwestern Argentina through endocrine, morphometric, histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. Serum total thyroxine (T4) concentrations were determined in 20 adult ewes and 22 neonatal lambs, and 14 lambs that died spontaneously underwent complete post-mortem examination with thyroid morphometry and tissue analysis. Serum T4 concentrations were significantly lower in lambs than in adult ewes (P <0.001), and thyroid enlargement showed a strong inverse correlation with circulating T4 concentrations (Spearman's ρ = -0.71, P <0.01). The thyroid weight:body weight ratio reached 21.14 g/kg, confirming marked thyroid enlargement. Histological examination identified both hyperplastic and colloidal goitre within the same flock. Hyperplastic goitres had a proliferating cell nuclear antigen index of 42.8% and a caspase-3 apoptotic area index of 2.6%, consistent with a predominance of follicular cell proliferation over apoptosis, whereas the colloidal goitre showed a contrasting profile compatible with an involutional stage. The combined findings strongly support iodine deficiency as the most likely cause of the outbreak and demonstrate that congenital ovine goitre may encompass different morphological and biological stages within the same flock. By integrating endocrine, morphometric, histopathological and immunohistochemical findings, this study provides a complementary characterization of naturally occurring ovine goitre in an endemic region and highlights the value of combining functional and tissue-based assessments for its diagnosis.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and blood pressure in childhood: A systematic review of prospective observational studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) may affect early-life cardiovascular programming, but epidemiological findings regarding blood pressure outcomes in children remain inconsistent. This systematic review synthesized evidence on associations between prenatal PFAS exposure and blood pressure or hypertension in children and adolescents.
METHODS: Following Cochrane recommendations and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE (EBSCO), and Embase were searched through 02 November 2026. The search strategy was developed with an information specialist. Prospective studies reporting prenatal PFAS exposure and offspring blood pressure outcomes were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Thirteen prospective cohort studies from North America, Europe, and Asia were included. Associations between individual PFAS and systolic or diastolic blood pressure were generally small and inconsistent across compounds, exposure windows, and ages at outcome assessment. Evidence regarding PFAS mixtures was similarly heterogeneous, with some studies reporting associations with systolic blood pressure or cardiometabolic outcomes, while others observed null or inverse associations. Heterogeneity in exposure assessment, mixture modeling approaches, and outcome definitions precluded quantitative synthesis.
LIMITATIONS OF EVIDENCE: The evidence was limited by heterogeneity across studies, potential residual confounding, differences in exposure assessment and outcome definitions, and varying risk of bias.
INTERPRETATION: Current evidence suggests that prenatal PFAS exposure may influence offspring BP, but findings remain inconsistent. Harmonized longitudinal studies with standardized exposure assessment and robust mixture methodologies are needed to clarify the role of early-life PFAS exposure in pediatric cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Psychotherapy in routine clinical practice in Chile with children who have been sexually abused: Factors associated with initial symptoms and trajectory of symptomatic change.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy of child sexual abuse treatment has been demonstrated. Nonetheless, a gap persists in understanding how different factors are associated with treatment outcomes. Furthermore, evidence in non-high-income countries and in routine clinical practice is scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the children's symptoms trajectories over the course of treatment for child sexual abuse, and whether child and caregiver characteristics, the nature of the abusive experience, and caregiver session attendance are associated with initial symptom severity and symptomatic change.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The sample comprised 78 children aged 4 to 9 (x̄ 6.6; SD 1.6) who were referred to specialized treatment centres for sexual abuse in Santiago, Chile.
METHODS: Children's primary caregivers and professionals leading their treatment completed questionnaires at the beginning, middle and end of treatment. Multilevel models were utilized to analyse changes in the child's symptomatology.
RESULTS: Internalizing, externalizing and post-traumatic stress symptoms decreased during treatment (p < .001). Children whose caregiver reported a history of child sexual abuse had higher initial scores across all three types of assessed symptoms (p < .05 or less), and those whose caregiver reported higher post-traumatic stress had higher initial internalizing and post-traumatic stress scores (p < .001). Caregiver session attendance was the only factor linked to change, with more sessions associated with a steeper reduction in post-traumatic symptoms (p < .01).
CONCLUSIONS: Children receiving treatment as usual in Chile showed symptom reduction over the course of the intervention, although the observational design precludes attributing this change to treatment. Caregiver-related factors were consistently associated with children's symptoms, with potential implications for clinical practice and for research using an intergenerational approach.

articles.title: Perfectionism and burnout among pediatric intensive care unit nurses: The mediation role of workaholism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) nurses work in high-acuity environments characterized by complex clinical demands, repeated exposure to critically ill children, parental distress, and pediatric death, placing them at increased risk of burnout. Perfectionistic tendencies may promote excessive and compulsive work patterns, or workaholism, that further deplete nurses' psychological resources. However, the pathways linking perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout remain insufficiently understood in pediatric critical care nursing.
AIM: This study examined the relationships among perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout among PICU nurses and investigated the mediating role of workaholism in the perfectionism-burnout relationship.
METHODS: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 431 PICU nurses recruited from eight hospitals across five Egyptian governorates. Data were collected using a web-based questionnaire including the Short Almost Perfect Scale, Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey, and Dutch Work Addiction Scale. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation, hierarchical multiple regression, and mediation path analysis.
RESULTS: Burnout was positively associated with workaholism (r = 0.218, p < 0.01) and perfectionism (r = 0.247, p < 0.01). A significant positive correlation was also observed between perfectionism and workaholism (r = 0.334, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect association between perfectionism and burnout through workaholism (standardized indirect effect = 0.051, bootstrap 95% CI [0.016, 0.089]), accounting for approximately 20.6% of the total association and supporting partial statistical mediation. Hierarchical regression analysis identified alternating shifts, perceived insufficient income, a nurse-to-patient ratio of 1:3, workaholism, and perfectionism as significant predictors of burnout.
CONCLUSION: Perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout were significantly interrelated among pediatric intensive care unit nurses. Workaholism showed a partial statistical mediating role in the association between perfectionism and burnout, suggesting that compulsive work behaviors may represent a relevant behavioral pathway linking these psychological characteristics. The findings highlight the importance of addressing both individual and organizational factors through strategies targeting maladaptive perfectionism, excessive work involvement, staffing adequacy, and psychological support. Longitudinal research is needed to establish temporal relationships and evaluate interventions aimed at reducing burnout.

articles.title: Maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccination: A systematic review and meta-analysis of determinants of vaccine acceptability and uptake.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination has potential to prevent infant respiratory morbidity. We identified sociodemographic factors influencing the acceptability and uptake of RSV vaccination among pregnant individuals.
METHODS: We carried out a systematic review and meta-analysis of sociodemographic factors associated with maternal RSV vaccination behavior. We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science for observational studies of RSV vaccination in pregnant women published before September 10, 2025. We included articles that examined how maternal race/ethnicity, education, employment, age, and marital status were related to RSV vaccine intention and uptake. We performed a meta-analysis using random effects models with inverse-variance weighting to estimate pooled odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the association between sociodemographic factors and RSV vaccination intention and uptake.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies comprising 15,275 individuals met inclusion criteria. Black race was the strongest determinant of vaccination behavior during pregnancy, followed by socioeconomic factors. In meta-analysis, Black race was associated with more than 50% lower odds of RSV vaccine uptake compared with White race (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.32-0.57; 6 studies). Low educational attainment (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.45-0.76; 8 studies) and unemployment (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56-0.96; 7 studies) were associated with >20% less intention to be vaccinated compared with higher education or employment. Maternal age and marital status were not associated with RSV vaccination intention.
CONCLUSION: Black patients and patients from low socioeconomic backgrounds should be a primary focus of obstetric RSV vaccination efforts.

articles.title: Adult-pretrained activity recognition across paediatric datasets: target adaptation and wheelchair activity coverage.
articles.abstract: Adult-pretrained models may support paediatric activity recognition, but their performance across datasets and activities remains uncertain. We evaluated harnet10 using thigh accelerometry from 46 typically developing children and 31 children and adolescents with mobility impairments. Training and testing involved separate participants. Source fine tuning achieved participant-equal macro-F1 of 0.904, compared with 0.842 for random initialisation. In the target dataset, five-seed logit ensembles achieved F1 of 0.373 for direct transfer and 0.678 for fine tuning. Fine tuning used five labelled windows per class selected from a fully annotated pool. Across 20 repetitions with independently sampled support sets in each fold, mean F1 was 0.594, compared with 0.372 for matched direct transfer. Each repetition averaged participant-normalised confusion matrices across three optimisation seeds, so the two analyses differed in both support sets and prediction aggregation. Adaptation improved F1 in every repetition and after excluding wheelchair-leading mixed windows. Among 18 participants with wheelchair activity, uncertainty ranking achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.801. The seven-class model predicted no wheelchair windows, giving zero wheelchair recall and F1. Adult pretraining and limited target supervision improved recognition of shared activities in these cohorts. The wheelchair findings highlight the need for activity-specific validation before clinical use.
