articles.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical activity, sleep, digital-media engagement, cognition, and emotional health become increasingly interconnected. However, reliance on retrospective self-report and low-frequency longitudinal designs limits understanding of how these domains relate within individuals and families in daily life. Few studies have integrated ecological momentary assessment (EMA), passive sensing, and wearable monitoring within mother-child dyads.
OBJECTIVE: Lion Tracks aims to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an integrated ambulatory monitoring protocol. Secondary exploratory aims are to characterize within-person, between-person, and dyadic temporal associations among health behaviors, physiological measures, cognition, and momentary anxiety.
METHODS: Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational, microlongitudinal feasibility study targeting 25 mother-child dyads (50 participants), with children aged 11-14 years. Participants complete baseline assessments, 4 weeks of ambulatory monitoring, and poststudy assessments. Garmin wearables monitor physical activity, sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability. MetricWire (MetricWire, Inc) collects passive smartphone screen-on duration and timing and delivers repeated EMA of momentary affect, anxiety, context, and behaviors. Digital-media engagement characteristics are self-reported through EMA. Brief mobile cognitive testing assesses cognitive performance. A hybrid EMA design combines fixed, pseudorandom, and behavior-contingent assessments to capture daily experiences while limiting participant burden. Primary outcomes include recruitment, retention, acceptability, participant burden, wearable compliance, EMA completion, and data completeness. Descriptive statistics and CIs will summarize feasibility outcomes. Exploratory multilevel mixed-effects models will examine within-person and between-person associations, while time-lagged and cross-lagged analyses will explore temporal relationships and behavioral synchrony within dyads.
RESULTS: The study received approval from The Pennsylvania State University Institutional Review Board (STUDY00027664). Recruitment is ongoing, with 7 mother-child dyads enrolled as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by June 1, 2027. Analyses will follow completion of data collection.
CONCLUSIONS: Lion Tracks represents Phase 1 of a larger research program designed to progressively optimize ambulatory monitoring and subsequently incorporate mobile electroencephalography to examine neural correlates of daily behaviors, cognition, and emotional functioning. Findings will inform protocol refinement and assess the feasibility of a scalable, multimodal platform for future family-centered behavioral health research.
INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/107879.

articles.title: Adolescent Substance Use and All-Cause Mortality Through Midlife in the US Nationally Representative Monitoring the Future Longitudinal Panel Study.
articles.abstract: Objectives. To examine whether adolescent substance use was associated with mortality. Methods. Mortality data on US nationally representative cohorts of high school classes surveyed in 1976 to 2019 were collected through 2026 in the Monitoring the Future Longitudinal Panel Study (n = 107 346). We estimated associations between age-18-years substance use (cigarettes, binge drinking, cannabis, other drugs) and all-cause mortality and time to death using logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models. Results. About 3.5% (n = 3773) were deceased by March 2026. Adolescent cigarette use, binge drinking, cannabis use, and other drug use were associated with likelihood of death and earlier age of death. With age-18-years covariates including sociodemographics and other substance use, use of cigarettes, cannabis, and other drugs remained statistically significantly associated with mortality; binge drinking was not statistically significantly associated with mortality when other substances were included. Conclusions. In a national study with data spanning 5 decades, substance use reported at age 18 years was associated with premature mortality. Public Health Implications. Adolescent substance use predicted mortality across decades of the life course. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print November 19, 2026:e1-e5. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308838).

articles.title: Examining the Effectiveness of a Dual Executive Function Training Package: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Executive function (EF) refers to the cognitive processes that enable goal-directed regulation of thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. Two interrelated domains are commonly distinguished: "cool" EF, which involves abstract cognitive processes, and "hot" EF, which involves regulation in emotionally or motivationally charged contexts. Children with special educational needs (SEN) frequently show difficulties across both domains, yet most interventions target one in isolation.
OBJECTIVE: The present study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a dual EF training package for 3 of the most prevalent SEN groups: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), specific learning difficulties (SpLD), and autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
METHODS: A total of 288 primary school students aged 6 to 12 years with a diagnosis of ADHD, ASD, or SpLD will be recruited. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an intervention or a waitlist control group, stratified by diagnosis. Each intervention group (n=48) will receive the dual EF training program. Participants in the waitlist control group will continue to receive usual educational and clinical support (standard care) during the study period and will be offered the dual EF program upon completion of the study. Preintervention and postintervention assessments will include neuropsychological tests of EF, teacher- and parent-reported behavioral ratings, and measures of disability impact, school satisfaction, and social participation. Changes in outcome measures will be examined using a mixed-design analysis, with diagnosis (ADHD, ASD, and SpLD) and group (experimental vs waitlist control) as between-participant factors and time (pretest vs posttest) as the within-participant factor. Baseline scores will be included as covariates where appropriate. The analysis will assess overall intervention effects and whether changes over time differ by intervention condition and diagnosis, with significant interactions followed by appropriate post hoc comparisons.
RESULTS: The study was funded by Advance Children Medical and Education Foundation Limited from September 2025 to December 2026 and received ethical approval. Recruitment commenced in early 2026, and 30 participants with ADHD, 30 with ASD, and 45 with SpLD had been enrolled by June 2026. Baseline assessments were completed for all participants. Further data collection and data analysis are scheduled for completion by early 2027, with the results to be submitted for publication thereafter.
CONCLUSIONS: This study will evaluate the effectiveness of a theme-based dual EF program that integrates hot and cool EF within a structured curriculum. Findings will provide evidence of the potential of this approach to support EF and related outcomes in children with SEN and may inform future research and inclusive educational practices.

articles.title: State of The Art of The da Silva's Cone Operation for Treatment of Ebstein's Anomaly.
articles.abstract: Ebstein's anomaly (EA) is a complex congenital heart disease caused by embryological failure of the tricuspid valve (TV) leaflet delamination, leading to displacement of the leaflets and right ventricular myopathy. In 1958, Hunter and Lillehei began developing surgical techniques for the repair of EA. Their technique was followed by many others. However, those techniques presented significant limitations due to the wide range of anatomical variations in the disease. The Da Silva Cone repair (CR) for EA emerged as the most anatomical repair technique for all forms of the disease, yielding the best results for most patients. Since CR can be performed with low mortality and morbidity, is effective and durable, and rarely requires TV replacement, it has been widely adopted. It allowed that surgical intervention can be indicated before the development of significant right ventricular dilatation or dysfunction. CR can be applied to any age, but it carries more risk in the neonate with critical EA. Therefore, neonates with critical EA may benefit from a staged approach, performing the Starnes procedure in the neonatal period and the CR later. The 2025 American Association for Thoracic Surgery expert consensus on managing EA covered preoperative evaluation, surgical indications, and contraindications in neonates, children, and adults. Additionally, the expert consensus discussed the approach to cardiac arrhythmias associated with EA and alternative procedures for select cases, including TV replacement and a bidirectional cavopulmonary shunt, depending on patient characteristics. They also agreed that the CR repair of the TV is beneficial when surgery is indicated.

articles.title: Knowledge, Practices, and Training Needs Related to Radiation Protection among Critical Care Staff Exposed to Portable Radiography: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portable radiography is frequently performed in critical care settings, where healthcare workers may be exposed to scattered ionizing radiation. Adequate knowledge and appropriate protective practices are important components of occupational radiation protection.
OBJECTIVE: To assess radiation protection knowledge, practices, and training needs among nurses and physicians working in critical care units during portable radiography in hospitals in Bethlehem and East Jerusalem, Palestine.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among nurses and physicians working in intensive care units, cardiac care units, and neonatal intensive care units in nine hospitals between November 2022 and March 2023. The questionnaire assessed demographic characteristics, objective radiation protection knowledge, reported radiation protection practices during portable radiography, personal protective equipment use, training history and needs, and self-rated knowledge.
RESULTS: A total of 142 critical care staff participated, including 104 nurses and 38 physicians. The mean objective radiation protection knowledge score was 8.30 ± 2.83 out of 14 (59.3%). Although 85.3% of participants rated their radiation protection knowledge as good or very good, objective assessment indicated that 68.3% had poor or fair knowledge. Regarding reported practice behaviors during portable radiography, leaving the unit during image acquisition was the most common response (37.3%), followed by maintaining maximum distance within the unit (23.2%), relocating to a break room (19.0%), remaining at the nursing station (12.0%), and standing behind shielding (8.5%). Use of personal protective equipment was limited, with 48.6% reporting that they never used lead aprons, 62.7% never using thyroid shields, 68.3% never using lead gloves, and 73.9% never using protective eyewear. Most participants (72.5%) had never attended formal radiation protection training, and 85.2% reported a need for additional education.
CONCLUSION: Critical care staff demonstrated a discrepancy between perceived and objectively assessed radiation protection knowledge and reported inconsistent use of protective measures during portable radiography. The findings support structured and continuing radiation protection education and institutional measures to reinforce appropriate occupational protection practices.

articles.title: Experiences of Families Receiving Regular Remote Review of CGM to Provide Targeted Supports: A mixed methods study evaluating a pilot model of care in children with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the experience of families of children (aged 7-14) with type 1 diabetes participating in a model of diabetes care that utilises regular remote review of CGM to prioritise contact and provide personalised and targeted support. This study focused on exploring the acceptability and impact of this model of care on participants and their families.
METHODS: This mixed-methods study used semi-structured interviews and a combined multiple-choice and free-text survey, completed by parents of children participating in a trial model of diabetes care. Qualitative data was analysed via reflexive content analysis to establish categories describing the experience and acceptability of the model of care. Quantitative data reflecting acceptability of the model of care were reported using frequency of response.
RESULTS: A sample of 15 surveys and 9 interviews were completed from 59 eligible participants who completed the model of care. The primary outcome, family experience of receiving contact, was most frequently referenced with 83% reporting positive personal impacts such as reassurance, support and validation, 46% reporting improved wellbeing and 70% reporting impacts on diabetes self-knowledge and management changes. Secondarily, the model was largely seen to be acceptable with 83% reporting convenient, positive and flexible communication and with potential to add-value to and reduce the requirement of traditional outpatient clinical care. Further, most participants reported a desire to continue the model of care. Participants also described potential revisions to improve the model and target specific populations who may benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggested acceptability and subjective benefit of regular review of CGM by the clinical team with targeted remote intervention in a group of children with T1D. It highlights the value that families place on support and communication, independent of glycaemic benefits. This insight may be used to guide clinical contacts and future trials.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury and death in severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria: An individual patient data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum or plasma concentrations of creatinine and urea are the usual laboratory parameters measured to assess acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients with suspected severe malaria. Creatinine is preferred for estimation of the glomerular filtration rate, but the current threshold for defining severe malaria (>265 μmol/L or a urea >20 mmol/L) is based on adult values and does not reflect the large difference between children and adults in normal values resulting from differences in muscle mass. We reevaluated these thresholds and their prognostic significance in severe malaria using individual patient data from large prospective studies.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: We pooled individual patient data from 22,663 patients recruited into 14 studies of severe malaria of whom 16,441 were included in the primary analysis population. Patients were included in the primary analysis population if their age (if missing, imputed from weight or height), coma status on admission, and either an admission serum or plasma creatinine or urea measurement (blood urea nitrogen, BUN), were all recorded. The primary outcome was mortality by day 28. The secondary outcome was the admission plasma Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (PfHRP2) concentration (a measure of parasite biomass). Bayesian penalised spline regression models were used to characterise the age-specific relationships (interaction with age) between the outcome and the absolute creatinine, the creatinine fold change relative to the age/weight predicted baseline, and the absolute urea. The models adjusted for coma status and calendar year, with nested random additive effects by study site and study. We estimated threshold plasma or serum creatinine and urea concentrations associated with >5% mortality with probability > 0.9. The majority (84%; 13,793/16,441) were children under 15 years of age. Current thresholds for AKI were associated with mortalities greater than 5%. An admission creatinine greater than three times the age/weight predicted baseline value was associated with >5% mortality. An admission urea >10 mmol/L had approximately similar prognostic value. A urea >10 mmol/L was 3.5 times more common in adults than children. In children <15 years of age, urea was a better prognostic indicator of death than creatinine and, unlike creatinine, correlated with the plasma PfHRP2 concentration. The main limitations of this analysis are the lack of metadata documenting laboratory methods and wide heterogeneity in eligibility criteria, such as creatinine or urea admission values for inclusion.
CONCLUSIONS: Admission serum or plasma creatinine >3 times the age/weight predicted baseline value (KDIGO AKI stage 3) can be used to define severe malaria AKI. In children, urea is a better predictor of the true infection biomass and a better prognostic indicator for death. We recommend the following as defining criteria for severe malaria: either a urea (BUN) threshold of 10 mmol/L for both children and adults, or simple age-based thresholds representing approximately >3 times fold change in creatinine from predicted baseline. These updated thresholds identify between 4 and 8 times more children with severe malaria AKI who are at a high risk of death.

articles.title: Long-term Risk of Neoplasms After Childhood Growth Hormone Therapy in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with Turner syndrome have a distinct pattern of neoplastic events occurrence, although their overall cancer risk does not appear to exceed that of the general population. Recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) therapy is widely used to improve adult height, but concerns remain regarding its long-term safety.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term risk of neoplastic events among patients with Turner syndrome treated with rhGH during childhood and to examine associations between rhGH treatment duration or dose.
DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including all Swedish patients with Turner syndrome treated with rhGH during childhood between 1983 and 2010 (n=583) and matched comparators (n=8745). Follow-up continued until the first neoplastic event, death, emigration or December 31, 2020.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 20.2 years (188445 person-years), patients with Turner syndrome had an increased hazard of overall neoplastic events (Hazard Ratio, HR, 2.0, 95% confidence interval, CI: 1.7-2.4), and of benign neoplasms (HR 2.5, 95% CI: 2.1-3.0), but not of malignant neoplasms (HR 0.7, 95% CI: 0.5-1.1). Hazards were increased for malignant neoplasms of the gastrointestinal tract and several benign neoplasms, while female genital malignancies were decreased. Neither rhGH treatment duration nor dose was associated with malignant or overall neoplastic risk.
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Patients with Turner syndrome treated with rhGH in childhood had an increased risk of overall neoplastic events driven primarily by benign neoplasms. No association was observed between rhGH treatment duration or dose and neoplastic risk in early to mid-adulthood, supporting its long-term safety.

articles.title: Metabolic Acidosis in Children with Glomerular Disease: Nephrotic Syndrome Study Network (NEPTUNE) and Cure Glomerulonephropathy (CureGN).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic acidosis is linked to faster kidney function decline in children with CKD, especially in those with glomerular CKD who are more likely to have untreated acidosis. Unlike prior cohorts limited to children with established CKD, our cohort consisted of 786 children with glomerular disease and largely preserved kidney function at enrollment. We studied the prevalence, factors associated with acidosis, and the impact of unresolved acidosis on eGFR decline.
METHODS: Children aged 1-17 years from NEPTUNE or CureGN were included. Acidosis was defined as serum bicarbonate <22 mEq/L. Unresolved acidosis was defined as acidosis at baseline that remained <22 mEq/L, and resolved acidosis was defined as baseline acidosis that reached ≥22 mEq/L on follow-up. Associations of acidosis with demographic and clinical characteristics were assessed. The primary outcome eGFR slope (ml/min/1.73m2/year) was analyzed using an adjusted linear mixed-effects model. Secondary analysis examined associations of acidosis with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA).
RESULTS: Mean baseline serum bicarbonate was 24.8±3.2 mEq/L and median eGFR was 97 ml/min/1.73m2 (IQR: 81, 117). The prevalence of acidosis was 12% (n=96), and only 4% of children with acidosis were receiving alkali therapy at baseline. Children with unresolved acidosis had a greater decline in eGFR compared to those with resolved acidosis, with a difference in eGFR slope of -4.05 ml/min/1.73m2/year (95%CI: -5.62, -2.47), independent of disease diagnosis and proteinuria. The degree of IFTA was not significantly associated with categories of serum bicarbonate (P = 0.61).
CONCLUSIONS: Unresolved metabolic acidosis was associated with a faster eGFR decline in children with glomerular disease. Acidosis was not associated with baseline IFTA, suggesting it may not simply reflect pre-existing fibrosis. Further studies are needed to clarify mechanisms linking metabolic acidosis with kidney disease progression and to identify patients who may benefit from targeted interventions.

articles.title: Gynecologic problems in adolescents and young adults: a 30-year referral cohort from a tertiary pediatric and adolescent gynecology clinic in Korea.
articles.abstract: Adolescent gynecologic practice relies largely on adult-derived evidence, as age-specific data remain limited. We compared the spectrum of gynecologic problems in Korean adolescents and young adults and, as a secondary analysis, examined whether the age at diagnosis of congenital causes of primary amenorrhea has changed over three decades. We retrospectively reviewed 6,350 patients (adolescents aged 10-19 years, n = 2,841; young adults aged 20-29 years, n = 3,509) who attended a pediatric and adolescent gynecology clinic between January 1995 and December 2024. Chief complaints, final diagnoses, and trends in age at diagnosis across three 10-year periods were analyzed. Menstrual disorders were the most frequent complaint in both groups but were more prevalent in adolescents (74.4% vs. 64.7%, p < 0.001). Endocrine disorders were the leading diagnosis, again more frequent in adolescents (36.4% vs. 28.2%, p < 0.001). Turner syndrome was the predominant cause of primary amenorrhea in adolescents (39.8%), and Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome in adults (62.0%). Polycystic ovary syndrome appeared more prevalent among adolescents with secondary amenorrhea (51.1% vs. 37.8%, p = 0.019), but this difference did not persist after applying adolescent-specific criteria (33.3% vs. 37.3%, p = 0.516). The median age at diagnosis of Turner syndrome decreased from 18 to 13 years (ρ =- 0.580, p < 0.001), whereas that of MRKH syndrome was unchanged (median 20 years; ρ =- 0.033, p = 0.731).Conclusion: Within the limits of a single-center referral cohort, the gynecologic disease spectrum is age-specific. Despite improved imaging access, diagnostic delay in MRKH syndrome showed no detectable improvement, supporting proactive pelvic imaging in adolescents with primary amenorrhea. What is Known • Adolescent gynecologic care is largely extrapolated from adult evidence, and long-term trends in the age at diagnosis of congenital causes of primary amenorrhea have not been characterized. What is New • Over 30 years, median age at Turner syndrome diagnosis fell from 18 to 13 years, whereas MRKH syndrome showed no detectable change from 20 years, indicating persistent diagnostic delay.

articles.title: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications after severe blunt liver trauma in children: a single-center retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-operative management is standard for hemodynamically stable pediatric blunt liver trauma, but the incidence and optimal surveillance for late intra-hepatic arterial complications remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To analyze late intra-hepatic arterial complications and their management in a cohort of children with severe blunt liver injury, to confirm a clinical protocol.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients younger than 18 years referred to a quaternary liver center for grade ≥3 blunt liver injury (American Pediatric Surgical Association grading). Demographic and clinical data, imaging findings, active arterial bleeding or pseudoaneurysm not suspected at presentation and/or not detected on initial computerized tomography, and surgical and interventional radiology procedures were collected.
RESULTS: Thirty-two patients (median age 14.9 years) with grade III (n=10), IV (n=5), and V (n=17) liver injuries were included. A total of 37 procedures were performed in 19 patients (59%), including peri-hepatic packing, early and delayed surgical explorations, angiography, and 12 embolizations in 11 patients. Overall survival was 100%. In 5 patients (16% of the cohort; all grade IV-V injuries), late intra-hepatic arterial complications were documented on elective follow-up computerized tomography at a median of 10 days after trauma (when patients were asymptomatic), and all were managed successfully by selective interventional radiology, without procedure-related complications. No deaths occurred in this series.
CONCLUSIONS: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications were not rare in children with grade IV-V liver injuries. These findings support considering computerized tomography in children with very severe hepatic trauma, around days 10-15 after trauma, to allow pre-emptive interventional radiology management.

articles.title: From Competence to Expertise in Congenital Cardiology: The LENS Model for Learning to See Problems Differently.
articles.abstract: Competency-based medical education has improved how paediatric and congenital cardiology defines readiness for independent practice. Competencies and entrustable professional activities describe what trainees should be able to do, and the degree of supervision they require. Competence is an essential threshold rather than the endpoint of professional development. The mechanisms through which a competent congenital cardiologist subsequently develops expertise remain incompletely understood. Research in medical education and cognitive psychology suggests that experts do not simply accumulate more knowledge or more clinical experience. Expertise involves changes in knowledge organisation, clinical problem representation, information selection, recognition of discordance, management of uncertainty, decision-making and adaptation when familiar solutions are insufficient. These concepts are particularly relevant to congenital cardiology, where clinicians integrate complex anatomy, physiology, imaging, haemodynamics, previous interventions and longitudinal trajectories while frequently making decisions despite incomplete evidence. We propose that the expert congenital cardiologist may be distinguished not simply by knowing more answers, but by seeing problems differently. We introduce the LENS model as a conceptual framework for this process: Link information into a coherent clinical representation; Extract the discriminating signal from noise; Notice discordance, uncertainty and possible failure of the initial pattern; and Shift reasoning strategy, seek distributed expertise or learn when the existing model is insufficient. The framework integrates literature on medical expertise, deliberate practice, adaptive expertise, uncertainty and congenital cardiac decision-making. It offers a vocabulary for teaching, faculty development and future empirical study while deliberately preserving the distinction between career stage, reputation and demonstrated expertise.

articles.title: Transpulmonary pressure monitoring in neonates and infants.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Transpulmonary pressure (PL) monitoring has been extensively studied in adult critical care, but evidence remains limited in neonates and infants despite their high vulnerability to lung and cardiac injury. This narrative review summarizes the physiological rationale, measurement techniques, and clinical evidence for PL monitoring in neonates and infants. PL is the distending pressure of the lungs. PL monitoring may help characterize lung stress and strain, assess respiratory effort, guide PEEP selection, and better understand cardiopulmonary interactions. Esophageal pressure monitoring remains the reference method for estimating PL, but its invasiveness and technical limitations restrict its use, particularly in extremely preterm neonates. Alternative approaches, including diaphragmatic electrical activity or airway occlusion maneuvers, may provide less invasive estimates, although most remain insufficiently validated in neonates. Current clinical evidence is scarce but suggests that excessive respiratory effort and elevated lung stress may occur in preterm infants, including during non-invasive respiratory support. PL monitoring may also help to optimize lung recruitment and cardiopulmonary interactions in infants with congenital heart disease or right ventricular failure.
CONCLUSIONS: PL monitoring offers a promising physiological approach to individualize respiratory support in neonates and young infants. Further studies are needed to validate minimally invasive or non-invasive surrogates of PL and to determine their clinical relevance in this population. Integration of automated occlusion maneuvers and other advanced monitoring tools into neonatal ventilators may facilitate the transition towards physiology-based, individualized respiratory and cardioprotective strategies.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Neonates' physiology may increase their vulnerability to ventilator-induced injuries. • Transpulmonary pressure (PL) reflects the true lung distending pressure, but neonatal evidence remains limited and esophageal pressure monitoring is challenging.
WHAT IS NEW: • Emerging alternatives (diaphragmatic electrical activity and airway occlusion maneuvers) could provide emerging approaches to estimate lung stress and respiratory effort. • PL-informed PEEP titration may help optimize lung recruitment to optimize hemodynamics in neonates with our without congenital heart disease.

articles.title: RSV and all-cause lower respiratory infection burden among infants residing in remote British Columbia: Retrospective population-based birth cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the population-based incidence of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection-related hospitalization in infancy by community remoteness.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of live births within an integrated health jurisdiction in British Columbia (BC, Canada) from April 2013 to March 2024, followed for 1 year, using routinely collected health administrative data. Main outcomes were hospitalizations for all-cause and RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI). Secondary outcomes were tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, length of stay, and air transport. Main exposures were community remoteness and social determinants of health. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated with Poisson generalized estimating equations accounting for clustering by community, with and without additional adjustment for sex, prematurity, and chronic conditions.
RESULTS: Among 472,623 infants, those living in remote communities (n = 3636) had higher hospitalization risk for all-cause (IRR 2.91, 95% CI 2.24-3.79) and RSV-LRTIs (IRR 1.60, 95% CI 1.17-2.19) compared to metropolitan areas. Length of stay and PICU admission rates were similar by region. Almost half (48.8%) of children from remote areas hospitalized for RSV-LRTIs required air evacuation. Infants from remote communities remained at higher risk for all-cause (aIRR 2.84, 95% CI 2.22-3.63) and RSV-LRTI (aIRR 1.56, 95% CI 1.15-2.12) hospitalizations after adjusting for covariates.
CONCLUSION: Infants in remote communities experienced a disproportionately high burden of RSV and all-cause LRTI hospitalization that is not fully explained by measured clinical or social determinants of health. These findings underscore the need for region-specific approaches and equitable implementation of prevention programs as jurisdictions move toward universal RSV immunization.

articles.title: Association between breakfast frequency, school commuting mode, and psychological symptoms: a cross-sectional study of Chinese adolescents.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Psychological symptoms among adolescents are a rising global public health concern. Irregular breakfast habits and passive commuting may be associated with these symptoms, but large-scale national evidence from China is scarce. We examined independent and joint associations using nationwide Chinese adolescent data. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to June 2025 among 52,035 adolescents aged 12-17 (26,104 boys, 25,931 girls) from 27 regions in China, using a multistage stratified cluster random sampling. Breakfast frequency and school commuting mode (active: walking or cycling; passive: motorized transport) were assessed via self-report questionnaires. Subclinical psychological symptoms were evaluated using the Multidimensional Subhealth Questionnaire for Adolescents (MSQA). Covariates included age, sex, monthly household income, sleep duration, body mass index, and grip strength. t-tests, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression are used to explore the associations. The proportions of adolescents breakfast frequency ≤ 1, 2-4, and > 4 times per week were 4.0%, 12.5%, and 83.4% and active and passive commuting accounted for 43.1% and 56.9%. The prevalence of emotional problems, behavioral problems, social adjustment difficulties, and subclinical psychological symptoms were 27.5%, 26.6%, 17.6%, and 20.8%. Fully adjusted models found independent associations of low breakfast frequency (≤ 1/week: OR 2.58, 95%CI 2.35-2.82) and passive commuting (OR 1.18, 95%CI 1.13-1.24) with symptoms; the combined category had the highest OR (OR 3.04, 95%CI 2.66-3.49, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Low breakfast frequency and passive commuting were associated with higher prevalence of subclinical psychological symptoms, with the highest OR in the combined category but no evidence of multiplicative interaction. Related interventions warrant evaluation.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Low breakfast frequency and passive school commuting are separately associated with adverse psychological outcomes in adolescents, but large nationwide evidence from China is limited.  • The joint association of these two modifiable daily behaviors with adolescent psychological symptoms remains unclear, including whether the association of one behavior varies according to the other.
WHAT IS NEW: • This large nationwide study found independent associations of low breakfast frequency and passive commuting with higher odds of subclinical psychological symptoms among Chinese adolescents. • Adolescents with infrequent breakfast consumption and passive commuting had the highest odds of psychological symptoms, with no statistical evidence of multiplicative interaction.

articles.title: Early-stage tendon stiffening precedes morphological thickening in pediatric type 1 diabetes: a quantitative shear wave elastography study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to comparatively evaluate Achilles tendon thickness and elastographic tissue stiffness in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) versus healthy controls, demonstrating the early radiological reflections of chronic hyperglycemia on pediatric tendon histomorphology. This prospective cross-sectional study included 60 pediatric T1DM patients and 60 age- and gender-matched healthy controls (mean age, 11.82 ± 4.02 years; range, 7-16 years). Glycemic control was evaluated using mean HbA1c levels. Anteroposterior Achilles tendon thickness was measured via B-mode ultrasonography. Quantitative tissue stiffness was assessed using Shear Wave Elastography (SWE), recording Young's modulus (kPa) and shear wave velocity (m/s) guided by motion stability and reliability indices. Bilateral Achilles tendon thickness did not differ significantly between the diabetic and control groups (p > 0.05). However, SWE revealed a highly significantly increased Young's modulus and shear wave velocity in the diabetic group compared to healthy controls (p < 0.001). Multiple linear regression identified diabetes duration as a significant independent predictor of increased tendon thickness (p < 0.05). Furthermore, left Achilles tendon velocity demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.940) in distinguishing diabetic tissue.
CONCLUSIONS: In children with T1DM, quantitative SWE detects a highly significant increase in Achilles tendon stiffness before macroscopic morphological thickening occurs on B-mode ultrasonography. While histopathological confirmation is lacking, this imaging-based observation of early-stage stiffening may serve as a non-invasive surrogate marker reflecting putative glycation-related microstructural alterations within the tendon matrix, presenting a biphasic biomechanical contrast to the chronic tendon softening typically reported in adult diabetic cohorts.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • In adult diabetic cohorts, chronic hyperglycemia leads to macroscopic Achilles tendon thickening and biomechanical softening due to long-term collagen degradation. • The subclinical effects of type 1 diabetes on connective tissue histomorphology in the early pediatric stage remain largely unexplored.
WHAT IS NEW: • Quantitative Shear Wave Elastography detects a highly significant increase in Achilles tendon stiffness in pediatric type 1 diabetes before any macroscopic morphological thickening occurs.  • This early-stage tissue stiffening reveals a biphasic biomechanical contrast to the chronic tendon softening typically observed in adult diabetic patients.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and acceptance of HPV vaccination in parents and patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection and a major cause of cervical and other anogenital cancers. Children with rheumatologic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy are at increased risk for persistent HPV infection, making vaccination a critical preventive strategy. The HPV vaccine is not included in Türkiye's National Immunization Program (NIP). This study aimed to assess HPV awareness, vaccine acceptance, and factors contributing to vaccine hesitancy among children with rheumatologic conditions and their parents. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 156 parent-child pairs attending the Pediatric Rheumatology Department at Dokuz Eylul University between August 2024 and August 2025. The survey was offered to 178 eligible parent-child pairs, of whom 156 agreed to participate (response rate, 88%). Inclusion criteria were ages 9-18 years, confirmed rheumatologic diagnosis, and current immunosuppressive therapy. Separate structured questionnaires were administered to parents and children to assess demographic characteristics, disease characteristics, immunization history, HPV knowledge, vaccine awareness, attitudes, and actual vaccination status. Median child age was 13 years; 81% of parents were female. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis was the most common diagnosis [87%]. HPV vaccine coverage was low [3% in both children and parents]. Among parents, 48% had heard of HPV and 47% were aware of the HPV vaccine. The most commonly reported barriers to HPV vaccination were insufficient knowledge [65% of children and 58% of parents], safety concerns [38% of children and 39% of parents], and lack of physician recommendation [63% of parents]. Logistic regression showed that female parent respondent status [OR = 7.3, 95% CI 2.2-24.6; p = 0.001] and university education compared with primary school education [OR = 12.9, 95% CI 1.8-90.4; p = 0.010] were associated with higher HPV awareness. Parents who had not previously obtained optional vaccines [not included in the NIP] for their children had lower odds of HPV awareness than those who had [OR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.06-0.69; p = 0.010]. Conclusions: HPV vaccination rates were very low among children with rheumatic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Higher parental HPV awareness was associated with female parent sex, higher parental education, and previous uptake of optional vaccines. The most commonly reported barriers to vaccination included insufficient knowledge, safety concerns, and lack of physician recommendation. These findings highlight the need for targeted educational interventions and stronger physician-family communication regarding HPV vaccination.

articles.title: Prevalence and pretreatment predictors of acetaminophen treatment failure for patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of acetaminophen-induced patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) closure failure and evaluate pretreatment predictors of non-response in preterm infants. This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261472267). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Epistemonikos, and ProQuest were searched from inception to August 2026. Randomized and observational studies reporting PDA closure outcomes following acetaminophen treatment were included. Random-effects models pooled study-defined failure prevalence and crude odds ratios (ORs). Subgroup analyses and exploratory univariable meta-regression examined heterogeneity. Analyses used R version 4.4.1 with the meta and metafor packages. Twenty-eight studies contributed 1559 evaluable infants. The pooled failure prevalence was 34% (95% CI, 28%-42%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 85.8%; τ2 = 0.5886). Crude analyses linked extreme prematurity (OR, 2.97; 95% CI, 1.44-6.13) and female sex (OR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.05-2.55) to higher failure odds. Treatment context, dose, and duration showed significant subgroup differences; administration route did not. Meta-regression identified study-level associations involving birth weight, gestational age, small-for-gestational-age status, 1-min Apgar score, preterm premature rupture of membranes, and antenatal corticosteroid exposure. Individual adjusted analyses identified greater ductal diameter and thrombocytopenia as potential predictors.  Conclusion: Overall, approximately one-third of treated preterm infants met study-defined criteria for acetaminophen treatment failure. Extreme prematurity, greater ductal severity, and thrombocytopenia warrant further evaluation as prognostic factors. Prospective studies should standardize outcome definitions and validate prediction models. What is Known: • Acetaminophen is used for PDA closure in preterm infants, particularly when cyclooxygenase inhibitors are contraindicated. • Treatment response varies substantially, but acetaminophen-specific predictors of failure remain poorly defined. What is New: • Across 28 studies involving 1559 infants, acetaminophen treatment failed in 34% (95% CI, 28%-42%). • Extreme prematurity showed higher failure odds, while greater ductal diameter and thrombocytopenia emerged as potential predictors requiring validation.

articles.title: Familial Mediterranean fever across the age spectrum: pediatric and adult-onset differences in phenotype, diagnosis, treatment response, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an auto-inflammatory disease caused by pathogenic variants in the MEFV gene, leading to dysregulated pyrin inflammasome activation and excessive IL-1β-mediated inflammation. FMF is characterized by recurrent fever, serositis, and musculoskeletal manifestations, with substantial interindividual variability. Although traditionally considered a pediatric disease, FMF is now recognized as a lifelong condition extending into adulthood, with age-related differences in clinical presentation, genetics, treatment response, and long-term outcomes. This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence comparing pediatric-onset disease, adult-onset FMF, and adults with childhood-onset disease across these domains. A structured narrative search of current evidence on FMF was conducted using different platforms, highlighting differences in clinical presentation, genotype-phenotype correlations, treatment response, and quality of life. Research indicates that pediatric-onset FMF is typically associated with earlier and more severe disease, higher attack frequency, and a stronger association with high-penetrance pathogenic variants, particularly M694V. In contrast, adult-onset FMF patients often exhibit milder and atypical manifestations, lower inflammatory burden, and a higher prevalence of heterozygous or low-penetrance variants, although diagnostic delays remain common in this population. Adults with childhood-onset FMF represent a distinct subgroup with cumulative inflammatory exposure and a higher risk of complications, including AA amyloidosis. Across all age groups, colchicine remains the cornerstone of therapy, although treatment challenges differ, with higher rates of colchicine resistance in children and greater intolerance and comorbidity-related constraints in adults.
CONCLUSION: Recognizing FMF as a disease continuum may enhance clinical awareness, facilitate earlier diagnosis, and support age-adapted, proactive management strategies aimed at reducing long-term complications and preserving quality of life.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • FMF is clinically and genetically heterogeneous, with established differences between pediatric- and adult-onset disease. Delayed diagnosis and persistent inflammation contribute to preventable disease burden and complications.
WHAT IS NEW: • This review directly compares pediatric-onset, adult-onset, and adult with childhood-onset FMF across multiple domains. This distinction highlights how age at onset and cumulative inflammatory exposure may lead to different disease trajectories in adulthood, linking phenotype, diagnostic recognition, genotype, treatment timing, and long-term outcomes within an age-continuum framework.

articles.title: Pornography use in adolescence: a gender perspective on co-occurring behavioural, psychosocial, and health outcomes.
articles.abstract: This study examined associations between pornography use and gender identity, sexual attraction, sexual behaviours, substance use, adverse social experiences, and health and wellbeing among secondary school students from a gender perspective. This cross-sectional study used data from the 2025 FRESC Health Survey on Adolescence in Barcelona, Spain (3,690 students aged 13-19 years). Occasional or regular pornography use was contrasted with no use or one-time use. Sex-stratified survey-weighted complex-samples logistic regression models accounted for sampling strata and classroom clustering and were adjusted for age, family socioeconomic status, and family structure. Pornography use was more frequent among boys than girls (55.6% vs. 13.8%). Associations with ever having had sexual intercourse, daily smoking, recent drunkenness, lifetime cannabis use, peer aggression, and hyperactivity/inattention were observed in both sexes. Among girls, associations were additionally observed with transgender/nonbinary gender identity, non-exclusively heterosexual attraction, poor family relationships, peer victimization, sexual harassment, poor self-reported health, and life dissatisfaction; body dissatisfaction was significant only before correction for multiple testing. Among boys, conduct problems were also associated with pornography use. Following Benjamini-Hochberg correction across 21 outcomes per sex, seven of eight initially significant associations in boys and 13 of 14 in girls remained significant. Overall, these findings suggest that pornography use should not be understood as an isolated behaviour but rather in relation to a broader range of behavioural, psychosocial, and health characteristics during adolescence, although the cross-sectional design does not permit causal or temporal conclusions.

articles.title: Maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy and child internalising and externalising problems over time.
articles.abstract: Adequate gestational thyroid function is important for offspring neurodevelopment, yet behavioural implications of variation within the normal range are unclear. We examined associations with externalising and internalising problems across repeated assessments in childhood and adolescence. 2,606 mother-child dyads from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) cohort with maternal free thyroxine (FT4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) measurements in the first half of pregnancy and at least one child SDQ assessment. Primary analysis excluded women with overt thyroid disease or thyroid medication use and children born < 32 weeks or < 1500 g. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) scores at 5-6, 11-12 and 15-16 years, via mother-, teacher-, and self-report. Secondary analyses included logistic regression for borderline SDQ cut-offs, sex interactions, and effect modification by TSH. FT4 showed a U-shaped association with teacher-reported externalising problems (quadratic β = 9.49, FDR-adjusted p = 0.03), with higher scores at both low and high FT4. Higher FT4 was associated with lower child-reported internalising problems (β = -0.17, FDR-adjusted p = 0.04). For both primary associations, there was no evidence of FT4-by-age interaction, suggesting differences in problem levels rather than thyroid-related differences in symptom change over time. At age 5-6, FT4 showed a non-linear association with teacher-reported hyperactivity/inattention above the threshold, with a negative linear term (OR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.97) and a positive quadratic term (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.02 to 1.20). At age 11-12, higher FT4 was associated with fewer self-reported peer problems (OR = 0.84, 95% CI:0.71-0.99). In exploratory analyses, curvature of the FT4-externalising association varied by maternal TSH; no sex modification was detected. Within a cohort free of overt thyroid disease, maternal thyroid function in the first half of pregnancy was associated with domain- and rater-specific differences in child internalising and externalising problems. We found no evidence that these associations changed across the available repeated assessments, suggesting differences in average problem scores rather than differences in how symptoms changed with age.

articles.title: Persistent bowel dysfunction and health-related quality of life after surgery for Hirschsprung disease: generic versus disease-specific outcomes and measurement heterogeneity in children and adolescents.
articles.abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a condition that can implant intestinal continuity surgically although technical success does not necessarily correlate with its age-specific bowel functionality. This critical narrative review addresses the association of persistent postoperative bowel dysfunction and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) with specific emphasis on discordance between generic and disease-specific measures, and on heterogeneity in the outcome measures. The literature review was updated: June 20 to July 15, 2026(PubMed), Web of science, Google Scholar, and NCBI Bookshelf. Twenty-five records were filtered and 19 sources published since 1998 constituted the main evidence base of outcomes; all sources were categorized according to evidence level and population and mixed HD/anorectal-malformation (ARM) evidence was classified as indirect. Reported constipation and fecal incontinence/soiling do not represent consistent reliable prevalence studies and vary greatly among the studies because of age, follow-up, operative method, definitions, questionnaire, type of respondent and bowel-management practice. The chronic obstructive symptoms need an assessment of mechanical or histopathologic errors that can be corrected prior to the intensification of bowel management. No statistically significant difference in generic HRQoL at the group level was shown between healthy comparison and available evidence, though results indicated a great degree of heterogeneity, precluding a general interpretation; disease-specific instruments and symptom-stratified analyses showed evidence of statistically important impairment in a sub-group with chronic dysfunction. Parent- proxy and child self-reports are not interchangeable but rather give complementary views. A standardized follow-up ought to thus combine effective bowel-function evaluation, generic and disease-specific HRQoL questionnaires, in addition to child plus parent reports.

articles.title: Association of differential growth and the incidence of respiratory distress in twins with birth weight discordance: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Birth weight is linked to neonatal lung morbidities, including respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). Studies in singletons are often limited by confounding factors. Birth weight discordant (BWD) twins eliminate these biases, providing a unique model to isolate the impact of differential growth. Our aim is to compare the risk of RDS in the smaller twin versus the larger twin within discordant pairs. PubMed and preprint servers (medRxiv and Research Square) were systematically searched using a Boolean phrase combining terms such as twin, birth weight discordance, respiratory distress, and RDS, retrieving all relevant articles from August 21st 2025 to July 30th, 2026, with no language, geographical, or time restrictions. All studies reporting on the correlation of birth weight and the incidence of RDS in BWD twins were included in our review. The systematic review and meta-analysis is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251135439). A total of 21 studies were included in our review. RDS incidence was found to be lower in the lighter twin compared to its heavier co-twin (11.44% vs 14.67% respectively, RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.63-0.95, p = 0.01) with lower need for surfactant administration, a result which was reversed in the analysis for BPD incidence where the lighter twin was at greater risk (5.71% vs 2.76% in the heavier twin, RR 2.04, 95% CI 1.11-3.72, p = 0.02). Although the individual studies had contradicting findings, our study revealed no difference in all-cause mortality and the NICU length of stay.
CONCLUSION: Birth weight is an important risk factor for neonatal morbidities. Our review revealed that the lighter twin in BWD pairs is at a significantly lower risk of RDS and need for surfactant. On the contrary, the smaller twin demonstrated a statistically significant higher prevalence of BPD.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • The impact of intrauterine growth restriction on neonatal lung maturation remains controversial, with singleton studies often limited by genetic, maternal, and environmental confounders. Birth weight discordance in twins offers a unique naturally controlled model to isolate the effect of growth restriction on respiratory outcomes.
WHAT IS NEW: • In birth weight discordant twins, the lighter co-twin faces a significantly lower risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and a lesser requirement for surfactant administration. Conversely, this risk profile reverses for chronic lung disease, where the smaller growth-restricted twin exhibits a significantly higher incidence of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD).

articles.title: Hydroxychloroquine as adjunctive therapy in steroid-dependent pediatric Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease with liver dysfunction: A case report.
articles.abstract: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease is usually self-limiting, but treatment of steroid-dependent disease in children remains uncertain. We report a 7-year-old girl with biopsy-confirmed Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease and severe liver dysfunction. She presented with intermittent fever and cervical lymphadenopathy, followed by rash and worsening liver dysfunction. Cervical lymph node biopsy revealed necrotizing lymphadenitis without evidence of malignancy. Antinuclear and U1 ribonucleoprotein antibodies were positive; liver-kidney microsomal type 1 antibodies were subsequently detected. Serologic tests for the viruses examined were negative, although hepatitis A testing was not performed. Retrospective assessment using the revised International Autoimmune Hepatitis Group scoring system did not reach the threshold for probable autoimmune hepatitis. Nevertheless, autoimmune hepatitis could not be excluded because liver histology was unavailable and the viral evaluation was incomplete. After relapse during prednisolone tapering, she received methylprednisolone pulse therapy followed by prednisolone and hydroxychloroquine. Remission was achieved, allowing gradual corticosteroid tapering. Prednisolone was discontinued at month 39 and hydroxychloroquine at month 50 after disease onset. No relapse occurred during the subsequent 8-month follow-up. No hydroxychloroquine-related adverse events, including retinopathy, were observed during 44 months of treatment or the subsequent follow-up. This case adds to the limited experience with prolonged hydroxychloroquine use in younger children with steroid-dependent Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease. Hydroxychloroquine may have contributed to corticosteroid tapering, although its independent efficacy cannot be established because it was initiated alongside intensified corticosteroid therapy.

articles.title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP.
articles.abstract: In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend:EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should:Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include:External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquetsAirway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empiric bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with:Injuries that are incompatible with life (e.g., decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (e.g., rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.Resuscitation attempts may be discontinued in pediatric TOHCA patients who:Have no return of spontaneous circulation after provision of at least 15 minutes of high-quality CPR in addition to performance of other lifesaving interventions directed at treating potentially reversible causes of pediatric TOHCA. Longer durations of CPR, up to 30 minutes, may be considered for patients with positive predictors of survival such as organized rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander CPR, or with proximate access to a trauma center.Have known predictors of very low probability of survival such as penetrating trauma without proximate access to a trauma center, asystole, unwitnessed arrest, or lack of bystander CPR.Protocols guiding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA benefit from oversight by EMS physicians in collaboration with pediatric experts and local or regional trauma system stakeholders. Implementation of such protocols for pediatric patients benefits from involvement of community stakeholders including family representatives, law enforcement, medical examiner, and child fatality review committees.Considerations for protocol implementation include local resource availability, EMS clinician and public safety, psychosocial support to surviving family members and emergency responders, and dignified handling of the deceased patient.Training needs for EMS clinicians include techniques to communicate with family members regarding the death of a child and understanding the clinician's own response to this low-frequency, high-emotion experience.

articles.title: Developmental dynamics of strength and gait asymmetries in hemiparetic cerebral palsy: Findings from a 2-year cohort with biannual assessments.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the longitudinal relationship between lower limb strength asymmetry and gait asymmetry in children with hemiparetic cerebral palsy (CP) over a 2-year period using biannual assessments.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 29 children with hemiparetic CP (mean age, 13.45 ± 3.15 years; Gross Motor Function Classification System levels I-II). Participants were assessed biannually for lower limb strength asymmetry indices (SAI) and Spatial/Temporal Gait Asymmetry Indices (GAI). Data were analyzed using Linear Mixed-Effects (LME) models, Repeated Measures Correlations, two-wave Cross-Lagged Panel Models (CLPM) (baseline to 24 months), and trajectory analysis.
RESULTS: LME models revealed significant positive associations between baseline SAIs and Spatial GAI for hip flexors (β = 0.625, p < .001), hip abductors (β = 0.470, p < .001), knee extensors (β = 0.216, p = .023), ankle dorsiflexors (β = 0.557, p < .001), and plantarflexors (β = 0.203, p = .016). Similar associations were found for Temporal GAI (β = 0.347-0.544, all p < .001). Repeated measures correlations showed strong associations for all muscle groups (r = 0.579-0.769, all p < .001), with the strongest for ankle plantarflexors (Spatial: r = 0.769; Temporal: r = 0.734). CLPMs demonstrated that baseline SAI significantly predicted future GAI for hip flexors (Spatial: β = 0.347; Temporal: β = 0.312), knee extensors (Spatial: β = 0.435; Temporal: β = 0.391), and ankle plantarflexors (Spatial: β = 0.408; Temporal: β = 0.382) (all p < .001), while reverse pathways were generally non-significant. Trajectory analysis confirmed a progressive decline in all asymmetry scores over 24 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Strength asymmetry significantly predicts the longitudinal course of gait asymmetry in children with hemiparetic CP, with muscle-specific temporal precedence. Targeted interventions addressing hip flexor, knee extensor, and ankle plantarflexor strength asymmetries may optimize gait outcomes.

articles.title: Redefining glucose thresholds for hypoglycaemia management in children and young adults with type 1 diabetes on automated insulin therapy: A cross-over clinical trial protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Current international guidelines for hypoglycaemia management in Type 1 diabetes recommend initiating treatment when glucose level falls below 3.9 mmol/L. However, these recommendations were developed before widespread use of diabetes technologies. This study aims to determine whether a revised hypoglycaemia treatment approach incorporating a lower treatment threshold is non-inferior to the standard threshold (<3.9 mmol/L) in children and young adults with Type 1 diabetes using automated insulin delivery (AID) systems. We hypothesise that the revised approach will be non-inferior to the current standard recommendations without increasing time in clinically significant hypoglycaemia.
METHODS: This single-centre, randomised, two-period, crossover, non-inferiority trial will recruit 45 participants aged 6-25 years with Type 1 diabetes, diagnosed for at least 12 months and using AID systems. Participants will complete two 4-week treatment periods in random order: standard hypoglycaemia treatment (<3.9 mmol/L) and revised hypoglycaemia treatment (≤3.6 mmol/L with consideration of CGM trends, active insulin, exercise and symptoms). Treatment periods will be separated by a 2-week washout period. The primary outcome is the percentage of time spent in clinically significant hypoglycaemia (<3.0 mmol/L), measured using CGM. Secondary outcomes are CGM metrics including time in range and time above range, along with participant acceptability of the revised treatment approach.
CONCLUSION: This study will provide prospective evidence on whether a revised hypoglycaemia treatment approach can safely reduce the glucose threshold for treatment in children and young adults using AID systems. Findings may inform future recommendations for hypoglycaemia management in the era of diabetes technologies.

articles.title: Serum Renin As a Prognostic Biomarker in Children With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) derangement contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI) and is associated with poor outcomes in critical illness. Serum renin, a clinically available biomarker of RAAS derangement, is associated with poor outcomes in critically ill adults and children. Renin has not been evaluated in children with sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI), either alone or in combination with other prognostic enrichment tools, including the recently derived pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) subphenotypes.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a multicenter, prospective, observational study of pediatric septic shock.
SETTING: Ten U.S. PICUs from January 2002 to February 2025.
PATIENTS: Patients 0-18 years old with early SA-AKI (serum creatinine-based Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 1-3 on days 1-2 of admission) with residual day 1 serum available for renin measurement.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Seven hundred eight patients were examined by renin tertiles. The highest renin tertile cohort (T3, > 247 pg/mL) had one fewer severe AKI-free day (4 [0-6] vs. 5 [1-7] T2 vs. 5 [2-7] T1; p < 0.001), higher day 7 severe AKI rates (47% vs. 32% vs. 27%; p < 0.001), fewer PICU-free days, and higher 28-day mortality rates. In multivariate analysis incorporating markers of illness severity, including age, T3 was independently associated with fewer severe AKI-free days (β = -0.5; se = 0.2; p = 0.01), fewer PICU-free days, and higher adjusted odds of day 7 severe AKI and 28-day mortality. Patients were assigned to either the pSAKI-1 or pSAKI-2 subphenotype to assess for additional enrichment. T3 patients had uniformly worse outcomes among the less severe pSAKI-1 subphenotype but not among pSAKI-2 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Worsening RAAS derangement, as evidenced by increasing renin concentrations, is associated with worse outcomes in children with SA-AKI. Serum renin may provide clinically useful prognostic enrichment in this population, both alone and in combination with the pSAKI subphenotypes.

articles.title: Residents' Ventilator Management Performance in an Online Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Case Scenario: Secondary Analysis of the Game-Based Education in Residency Study, 2015-2017.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate resident performance in an online pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) case scenario of mild/moderate severity, with the provision of individualized feedback.
DESIGN: A secondary analysis of the Game-based Education in Residency study.
SETTING: The dataset comprised residents in their first clinical rotation in any of 28 international PICUs, recruited between October 2015 and December 2017.
SUBJECTS: Residents who used the online mechanical ventilation (MV) simulator and completed PARDS tasks were included in the analysis.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The simulated MV parameters analyzed among 125 residents were positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), Fio2, tidal volume (Vt), peak inspiratory pressure (PIP), Pao2, and pH. Residents' MV selections in relation to recommended scoring goals were: median (interquartile range [IQR]) PEEP, below or in the lower range (8 cm H2O [IQR, 7-8 cm H2O]); median Fio2, above or in the higher range (60% [IQR, 51-60%]); and median Vt, within range (5.36 mL/kg [IQR, 4.98-5.73 mL/kg]). Residents had higher than recommended median Pao2 (93 mm Hg [IQR, 83-99 mm Hg]), pH (7.37 [IQR, 7.33-7.40]), and median PIP (30 cm H2O [IQR, 28-31 cm H2O]). Progress through the case scenario was associated with greater odds (odds ratio [OR] and 95% CI) of adherence to goals in PEEP, Fio2, and Vt: PEEP (OR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.65-4.34; p < 0.001); Fio2 (OR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.29-4.76; p = 0.007); and Vt (OR, 2.66; 95% CI, 1.11-6.38; p = 0.028).
CONCLUSIONS: In an international PICU residents' educational dataset from 2015 to 2017, we found that progression through the simulated PARDS case was associated with greater odds of adherence to PEEP, Fio2, and Vt goals, which suggests that repeated practice and individualized feedback were of benefit. However, residents did not wean Fio2 or MV parameters when Pao2 and pH were above goal. These results may help educators design contemporary MV teaching.

articles.title: Long-Term Neurologic Complication and Healthcare Burden in Infants Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate survival, neurologic complications, and healthcare burden in infant extracorporeal life support (ECLS) recipients using nationally representative administrative data from a single-payer healthcare system.
DESIGN: Retrospective, population-based cohort study.
SETTING: South Korea's National Health Insurance Service, covering 97% of the population.
PATIENTS: Infants under 1 year who received ECLS between 2009 and 2022.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 698 infants who underwent ECLS, 212 infants (30.4%) survived during follow-up (estimated 1-yr mortality: 67.1%). Among survivors, 128 (60.4%) developed neurologic injuries, including acute events such as ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI), as well as long-term sequelae such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, hearing loss, and developmental delay. Most acute neurologic injuries were diagnosed within the first year, whereas developmental delay showed prolonged diagnostic windows extending up to 12 years. Survivors with neurologic injury had significantly longer hospital stays (432.1 vs. 182.3 d; p < 0.001) and higher cumulative healthcare costs during long-term follow-up. Median index hospitalization costs were USD 36,000-37,000. The burden analysis showed distinct profiles across neurologic complications: developmental delay was the most prevalent sequela, whereas HIBI was associated with the highest cumulative healthcare cost despite lower prevalence.
CONCLUSIONS: Neurologic complications following ECLS in infants are common and impose substantial long-term healthcare burden. These findings highlight the need for early risk stratification, structured neurologic and neurodevelopmental monitoring, and sustained rehabilitation planning in this high-risk population. This study provides a foundation for international benchmarking and health policy planning in pediatric critical care.

articles.title: Clinical Factors Associated With Physical Restraint Use in Critically Ill Children: A Secondary Analysis of the PICU Up! Pilot Trial, 2019-2020.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify clinical factors associated with physical restraint use in critically ill children.
DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected observational daily data from the baseline (preintervention) phase of the PICU Up! multicenter stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial (NCT03860168). The analytic dataset represents a shared subset of the larger parent study population.
SETTING: Six PICUs in the United States, from May 2019 to March 2020.
PATIENTS: A total of 1153 patients younger than 18 years admitted to a PICU for 3 or more days.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Children younger than 18 years old admitted for 3 or more consecutive PICU days were included. Daily data on sedation level, medication exposure, device use, and restraint status were collected, and multivariable generalized estimating equation models were used to evaluate associated factors. Physical restraints were used in 216 patients (18.7%) and 1,043 of 11,491 patient-days (9.07%), with a median duration of 3 days (interquartile range, 2-5). In multivariable analysis, the strongest predictor of restraint use was previous-day restraint (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 22.79; 95% CI, 16.72-31.07). Other significant factors included age 3-17 years vs. 0-2 years (aOR, 2.46-2.69), mechanical ventilation (aOR, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.39-6.38), benzodiazepine use (aOR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.05-2.10), and opioid use (aOR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.42-2.78). Light sedation (State Behavioral Scale [SBS] -1) was associated with restraint use compared with calm/alert status (SBS 0; aOR, 1.72; 95% CI, 1.24-2.37), while agitation (SBS > 0) showed no association (SBS 1 [aOR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.52-1.80] and SBS 2 [aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.47-2.54]). Invasive devices were associated with increased restraint use (p < 0.001). Notably, 51 patients (12.5%) of 407 patients receiving neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA) remained restrained, and 30 patients were restrained on the day of ICU discharge.
CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to previous reports linking agitation to restraint use, agitation (SBS > 0) was not associated with restraint use; only light sedation (SBS -1) was associated with increased odds of being restrained. Previous-day restraint use was the strongest predictor of continued restraint, highlighting persistence of previous-day practices with limited reassessment. The presence of restraints during periods of NMBA administration and at discharge days further suggests the need for improved reevaluation practices.

articles.title: Utility of Renal Replacement Therapy for Infants With Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between renal replacement therapy (RRT) use and survival outcomes in infants with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) receiving extracorporeal life support (ECLS).
DESIGN: Multicenter retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization database (2011-2020). Propensity score (PS) matching was used to account for pre-ECLS disease severity.
SETTING: International multicenter ECLS centers.
PATIENTS: Infants with CDH requiring ECLS.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 2815 infants, 749 infants (26.6%) received RRT. Before matching, +RRT patients had significantly lower survival to discharge (35.5% vs. 60.2%; p < 0.0001). PS matching generated 413 pairs with balanced pre-ECLS characteristics. After matching, +RRT remained associated with significantly lower survival to discharge (36.3% vs. 57.4%; survival odds ratio, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32-0.56; p < 0.0001). +RRT patients also experienced longer median ECLS durations (15 vs. 9.4 d; p < 0.0001) and higher rates of severe on-ECLS AKI (10.9% vs. 3.6%; p < 0.0001). Stratified analysis showed that RRT was associated with significantly worse survival only in patients undergoing on-ECLS CDH repair.
CONCLUSIONS: In infants with CDH on ECLS, RRT use is strongly associated with increased ECLS duration and decreased survival to discharge. Although PS matching suggests this association persists regardless of baseline severity, RRT likely serves as a marker for significant clinical deterioration during the ECLS course.

articles.title: Physiological Impact of Chest Wall Closure in Infants Post-Cardiac Surgery. Implications for Mechanical Ventilation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effect of delayed sternal closure post-cardiac surgery on respiratory system mechanics and hemodynamics.
DESIGN: Prospective single-center physiologic study.
SETTING: Cardiac PICU.
PATIENTS: Infants (< 1 yr old) with delayed sternal closure post-cardiopulmonary bypass for correction or palliation of a congenital heart disease.
INTERVENTIONS: Four ventilation conditions were studied: 1) baseline: positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) 5 cm H2O and low tidal volume (Vt; 6-7 mL/kg); 2) PEEP 5, high Vt (9-10 mL/kg); 3) PEEP 3, low Vt; and 4) PEEP 8, low Vt. Respiratory rate was adjusted to end-tidal carbon dioxide. Measurements were repeated after sternal closure.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Esophageal pressure (Pes), transpulmonary pressure (PL), normalized respiratory system elastance (Ers) in cm H2O/(mL/kg), and hemodynamics, including transmural pressures, were obtained before and after sternal closure. The open-sternum model used assumes that the chest wall maintains a vertical pleural pressure gradient, with the most nondependent lung exposed to atmospheric pressure. A nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O was used as a marker of overdistention, and end-expiratory PL 0-2 cm H2O was considered to prevent collapse. Ten patients were included: median (interquartile range) age 32 days (18-50 d) and weight 3.1 kg (3.0-3.5 kg). Chest closure increased Pes in all conditions and Ers in most conditions, except for PEEP 8 low Vt.
