Chest closure reduced expiratory PL in all conditions, at baseline from -0.5 cm H2O (-1.2 to -0.1 cm H2O) to -2.5 cm H2O (-3.1 to -1.8 cm H2O). Sternal closure impacted nondependent inspiratory PL differently depending on the ventilator settings. High Vt was the condition more frequently associated with high nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O. Blood pressure was maintained with fluids or vasopressors. Central venous pressure increased after closure, but the transmural filling pressure remained unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: Infants with delayed sternal closure exhibited elevated Pes and Ers after chest wall closure. Under the model assumptions, during the open-chest phase, high Vt was more frequently associated with high nondependent PL, suggesting overdistention. Sternal closure made expiratory PL more negative. These findings suggest that individualized PEEP and Vt adjustments guided by Pes could be considered to help preserve expiratory PL and minimize the risk of overdistension before and after chest closure.

articles.title: Ryan House: Sharing 15 Years of Inpatient Pediatric Respite and Hospice Experience.
articles.abstract: BackgroundA 2021 UNICEF report estimates that nearly 240 million children live with disabilities globally, including children with medical complexity (CMC). In the United States, over 2 million children have complex medical needs requiring around-the-clock care, creating significant physical, emotional, and financial burdens for their families.ObjectiveTo describe the organizational structure, financial support, medical staffing model, and patient demographics of Ryan House, aiming to establish its framework as a global standard that can be adapted to support communities worldwide.Setting & InterventionRyan House is one of only 3 inpatient pediatric facilities in the United States offering dedicated respite and palliative hospice services for CMC. The facility provides a flexible, community-based care model designed to extend support from clinical settings into the home life of families.ResultsDuring its 15 years of operation, Ryan House has served over 1100 patients and families, delivering more than 24 000 days of care. The manuscript details the specific operational, staffing, and funding structures that enabled this level of service delivery.ConclusionRyan House represents a unique and critical resource for families caring for CMC. Its operational model offers a scalable and adaptable framework that can be implemented globally to alleviate caregiving burdens and improve quality of life for complex pediatric populations.

articles.title: Prevalence of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Associated with Congenital Heart Disease Following Defect Correction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Qual Care Clin Outcomes
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Understanding the disease burden of repaired pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease (PAH-CHD) is essential for guiding healthcare strategies, yet data are lacking in this area.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) following defect correction in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD).
DATA SOURCES: A systematic review and meta-analysis was performed using PubMed, Embase and Cochrane databases.
STUDY SELECTION: Longitudinal cohort published between 1970-2023 involving CHD patients who underwent defect correction and were subsequently diagnosed with PAH were reviewed. Eligible studies reporting the prevalence of repaired PAH-CHD at least 3 months post-repair was included. Study selection was conducted independently by two reviewers. The primary outcome was the prevalence of PAH in patients following CHD defect correction.
RESULTS: Across 58 studies (7,036 participants), the random-effects pooled prevalence of reported post-repair PAH/PH was 10.8% (95% CI 7.3-15.0, I2 = 95.6%; prediction interval 0-50.1%). Prevalence was 9.0% (95% CI 3.3-17) in studies using right heart catheterisation, 19.3% (CI 10.6-29.7) in studies using echocardiography and 16.1% (CI 8.6- 25.1%) in studies using both modalities (p=0.19). Prevalence was highest in the adult-only cohort (18.5%, 95%CI 11.8-26.2) and lower in paediatric only (7.6%, 95%CI 3-13.5) and mixed-age cohorts (7.5%,95%CI1.7-16.3), p=0.039. Preoperative pulmonary hypertension (PH) was the strongest predictor of post-repair PAH and remained predictive on adjusted meta-regression (p<0.01).
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: PAH following defect repair remains a significant clinical dilemma requiring standardised diagnostic criteria and robust risk stratification tools to guide management.

articles.title: Associations of Vaping and Smoking Expectancies and Subsequent E-cigarette Ever-Use among United States Adolescents: A Two-Year Longitudinal Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: E-cigarettes continue to be the most common tobacco/nicotine product among United States adolescents. Understanding the predictive value of vaping and smoking expectancies can help prevent youth e-cigarette use.
METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study analyzed the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study 6.0 data to examine vaping and smoking expectancies (15-item scales ranging 1-5) for adolescents aged 12-13 years (baseline) who had never used an e-cigarette. A dual vaping-smoking expectancy variable (low vaping/low smoking, low vaping/high smoking, high vaping/low smoking, high vaping/high smoking) was created, and multivariable regressions tested the association between vaping, smoking, and dual expectancies and e-cigarette use susceptibility as well as ever-use by age 14-15 (two-year follow-up).
RESULTS: Among 1,990 participants at baseline, the mean (interquartile range) vaping and smoking expectancies were 2.3(1.8-2.8) and 1.7(1.2-2.0). Both vaping expectancy and smoking expectancy at baseline were associated with e-cigarette use susceptibility at baseline (AOR[95%CI]=3.8[2.8-5.1],p<.001; 3.1[2.2-4.2],p<.001; respectively) and subsequent ever-use at two-year follow-up (3.0[1.9-4.8, p<.001); 2.5[1.6-3.9], p<.001; respectively). Dual vaping/smoking expectancy showed a dose-response relationship with susceptibility to e-cigarette use (high/high, 8.3[5.4-12.9]p<.001; high/low, 3.9[2.3-6.8],p<.001; low/high, 2.9[1.8-4.6],p<.001 vs. low vaping/low smoking) and ever-use (6.4[2.4-17.1], p<.001; 6.1[2.0-18.7],p=0.002; 3.9[1.4-10.9], p=0.01; vs. low/low). Adolescents with high vaping and high smoking expectancies tended to be older, female, and report lower parental monitoring and school environment scores(p<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Vaping, smoking, and dual expectancies were associated with risk of e-cigarette use susceptibility and ever-use within two years. Identifying adolescents with high vaping and smoking expectancies offers a crucial opportunity to implement targeted interventions aimed at preventing youth vaping.

articles.title: Clinical spectrum and morbidity of ocular parasitic infections among rural children in central India.
articles.abstract: Ocular parasitic infections are an under-recognised cause of ocular morbidity in low- and middle-income countries. We found Taenia solium (26.5%) was the most common parasite, followed by Toxocara canis/cati (19.4%), Toxoplasma gondii (17.3%) and Acanthamoeba spp. (11.2%). Reduced visual acuity (66.3%), retinitis/chorioretinitis (38.8%), uveitis (32.7%) and vitreous involvement (28.6%) were the predominant clinical manifestations. Poor nutritional status was significantly associated with infection. Frequent open defaecation, barefoot outdoor play and inadequate handwashing before meals were identified as significant behavioural risk factors for ocular parasitic infection.

articles.title: Virtual Reality-Based Rehabilitation for Pediatric Acquired Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundVirtual reality and augmented reality (VR/AR) rehabilitation shows promise after adult brain injury, but its efficacy in pediatric acquired brain injury remains unclear.ObjectiveTo synthesize within-person changes in cognitive, motor, and functional outcomes following VR/AR rehabilitation in pediatric acquired brain injury and explore moderators.MethodsSix databases were searched through March 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. Of 373 records, ten studies (nine VR, one AR) were included: four randomized trials and six uncontrolled studies. Standardized mean changes were pooled using three-level random-effects meta-analysis.ResultsAcross 72 effect sizes, VR/AR rehabilitation was associated with significant pre-post improvement (g = 0.62, 95% CI [0.15, 1.09], p = .01). Improvements were significant for motor and functional outcomes, but not cognitive outcomes. Outcome domain, developmental stage, study design, immersion, assessment method, and treatment dose were not significant moderators. Longer pre-post intervals predicted larger changes (β = 0.01, p = .004), potentially reflecting natural recovery. Overall improvements remained significant across assumed correlations and when restricting analyses to VR, excluding mixed diagnostic samples, or clustering by research team. Funnel plot asymmetry suggested possible publication bias.ConclusionsVR-based rehabilitation was associated with within-person improvement, but comparative efficacy remains uncertain because evidence is limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly uncontrolled. Larger controlled studies should evaluate efficacy, safety, mechanisms, durability, and functional transfer.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis of Standard- and High-Dose Rifampicin to Predict Safety, Completion, and Tolerability of Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy in the 2R2 Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rifampicin-based tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT) may shorten treatment duration, but substantial interindividual pharmacokinetic variability may lead to different safety and tolerability profiles at the same dose. We performed pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analyses of standard- and high-dose rifampicin to predict safety, completion, and tolerability.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 1,368 adults and adolescents enrolled in the 2R2 trial comparing two months of rifampicin at 20 or 30 mg/kg/day with four months at 10 mg/kg/day. A population pharmacokinetic model developed from 440 participants was used to predict rifampicin exposure for all participants. Missing exposure metrics were imputed using 1,000 simulated datasets. Exposure-response relationships were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression models fitted within imputed datasets, with coefficients and standard errors pooled across imputations.
RESULTS: A two-fold increase in total rifampicin exposure (AUC0-24) was associated with higher odds of protocol-defined adverse events (AEs) requiring permanent discontinuation (aOR 1.88, 95% CI 1.25-2.81), discontinuation unrelated to AEs (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.15-1.75), and tolerability symptoms potentially related to AEs without discontinuation (aOR 1.48, 95% CI 1.18-1.86); similar patterns were observed for peak concentration (Cmax). Higher AUC0-24 and Cmax were also associated with grade 1-2 and grade 3-4 AEs, rash/allergy/hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal intolerance, and early discontinuation, with no significant association for hepatotoxicity. Exposure-based models showed slightly better discriminatory performance than dose-based models in predicting safety.
CONCLUSION: Higher rifampicin exposure was associated with worse safety, completion, and tolerability in TPT. Larger efficacy trials are needed to determine the optimal dose to achieve sufficient exposure, alongside investigation of therapeutic drug monitoring to avoid excessive exposure.

articles.title: Adolescent loneliness and health-compromising behaviors: Relations with dieting, substance use, and sleep disturbances.
articles.abstract: Loneliness is a major public health risk, and understanding its impacts on physical health is crucial for preventative healthcare strategies. This study examined whether adolescent loneliness predicted health-compromising behaviors (i.e. sleep disturbances, weight control, substance use) 1 year later and whether gender moderated these associations. Data were drawn from a longitudinal study of adolescents in the Southwestern United States (N = 751). Greater loneliness in ninth grade was associated with more frequent sleep disturbances 1 year later (an association that was significantly stronger among girls than boys) and with larger increases in sleep disturbances over the same period. Loneliness was not associated with dieting or substance use. Findings highlight loneliness as a contributor to adolescent sleep disturbances, particularly among girls, and a potential target for intervention.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes of a standardised interdisciplinary protocol for implant-prosthetic rehabilitation in patients with severe oligodontia associated with ectodermal dysplasia: A retrospective case series with a follow-up period of up to 30 years.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Oral rehabilitation in patients with ectodermal dysplasia is complex due to severe oligodontia and extreme alveolar ridge atrophy. This retrospective case series aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of a standardised interdisciplinary protocol for the oral rehabilitation of patients with ectodermal dysplasia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 13 patients (8 men and 5 women; mean age 20.5 ± 1.9 years) with severe oligodontia (mean 18.4 ± 4.4 missing teeth) were included. The cohort included 12 cases of hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia and one case of Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome. The protocol consisted of orthodontic treatment until skeletal maturity, restoration of the vertical dimension of occlusion via fixed temporary restorations supported by natural teeth and/or interim implants, 3D bone reconstruction using autogenous bone (iliac crest or intraoral bone blocks) via the split bone block technique, and placement of dental implants followed by definitive prosthetic rehabilitation. Clinical and radiographic parameters were assessed over an observation period of 14.4 ± 7.0 years (median 13 years; range 5 to 30 years).
RESULTS: A total of 147 implants were placed (79 in the maxilla and 68 in the mandible). All patients were successfully rehabilitated with fixed implant-supported prosthetics. Three patients were lost to follow-up (non-attendance) after a mean observation period of 19.0 ± 3.6 years. The implant survival rate was 100% over the entire observation period. All grafts integrated successfully. Five patients required secondary free gingival grafts to manage soft tissue shrinkage. At the final follow-up, all sites were free of inflammation with stable marginal bone levels.
CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this small patient cohort, the described approach, consisting of orthodontic treatment, fixed provisionalisation, autogenous bone augmentation and implant placement at skeletal maturity, demonstrated high long-term predictability, even in patients with Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome.

articles.title: Autistic Adolescents and Associate Medical Conditions.
articles.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder is a neurological and developmental condition impacting 1 in 31 children. Children, identified on the autism spectrum, are typically diagnosed by the age of 8; however, research indicates that there could be as many as 25% of undiagnosed adolescents. Autistic adolescents have a significantly higher prevalence of mental-health and medical conditions than their neurotypical peers including gastrointestinal disorders (e.g., chronic constipation), seizure disorders, sleep disturbances, and nutritional disorders (e.g., overeating). Part-1, "Interventions for Adolescent Students with Autism and Co-Occurring Mental Health Disorders," of this three-part series discussed interventions for the mental health comorbidities often experienced by autistic adolescents. This second article will address common medical conditions experienced by autistic adolescents and how school nurses can help manage these conditions in school settings.

articles.title: Sustained Improvement in Time in Range After Automated Insulin Delivery Initiation in Adolescents and Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A 12-Month Prospective Observational Study From Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated insulin delivery (AID) improves glycemic outcomes in trials, but long-term real-world data on comprehensive continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics remain limited in the Middle East.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) initiating Control-IQ (CIQ) or MiniMed 780G (MMG) at King Fahad Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between December 2023 and November 2025. Participants were followed for 12 months. Continuous glucose monitoring outcomes included time in range (TIR: 70-180 mg/dL), time above range (TAR), time below range (TBR), glycemic management indicator (GMI), mean sensor glucose, and coefficient of variation (CV) and assessed at baseline and 6 post-initiation time points. Glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) was assessed using paired pre- and post-AID values.
RESULTS: A total of 132 adults were included: 76 using CIQ and 56 using MMG. Mean age was 27.2 ± 7.7 years, 68.9% were female, and mean diabetes duration was 14.5 ± 7.9 years. Time in range increased from 59.0 ± 15.4% at baseline to 72.3 ± 10.2% at 2 weeks and remained sustained at 12 months (73.5 ± 11.5%; +15.1 percentage points; P < .001). Time below range <70 mg/dL decreased from 5.3 ± 5.3 to 1.4 ± 1.2%. Glycated hemoglobin A1c decreased from 7.42 ± 1.13 to 6.52 ± 0.73% (P < .001; n = 106). Time in range ≥70% increased from 29.0% to 71.0%, and HbA1c <7% increased from 30.3% to 74.5%. Severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis rates were significantly reduced.
CONCLUSION: In a Saudi tertiary diabetes center, AID initiation was associated with rapid and sustained 12-month improvements in TIR, HbA1c, hypoglycemia exposure, and acute diabetes-related events.

articles.title: Specific associations of seven dimensions of sleep quality with suicide behaviours in Chinese adolescents: the partially moderating role of morning chronotype.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To quantify the associations between seven dimensions of sleep quality and suicide behaviours (suicide ideation [SI], suicide plan [SP] and suicide attempt [SA]), and to examine the moderating role of chronotype in these relationships.
METHODS: A total of 20,055 adolescents were recruited through a stratified cluster sampling across 5 representative provinces in mainland China. Confounding variables included demographic characteristics, depression and anxiety.
RESULTS: Among 20,055 adolescents, 2,099 had SI (10.5%), 1,596 had SP (7.9%) and 1,005 had SA (5.0%). In total, 4,276 were classified as morning-type (21.3%). Multinomial logistic regression analysis indicated that sleep duration and sleep disturbances were significantly associated with SI, SP and SA (all p < 0.05), whereas the relationship between subjective sleep quality and suicide behaviours was not significant (p > 0.05). Notably, hypnotic drug use is significantly associated only with SA (p < 0.05). Moreover, among morning-type adolescents, the relationships between the two dimensions of sleep quality (sleep disturbance and hypnotic drug use) and suicide behaviours became non-significant (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The seven dimensions of sleep quality exhibited unique associations with suicide behaviours in Chinese adolescents. Furthermore, morningness appears to partially moderate the associations between some sleep problems and suicide behaviours.

articles.title: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation in children and young adults with severe adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Left cardiac sympathetic denervation is established for selected high-risk inherited arrhythmia syndromes, but evidence for an intended bilateral strategy in children and young adults remains limited. We evaluated the rationale, feasibility, safety, follow-up ascertainment, and outcomes of intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation.
METHODS: Consecutive children and young adults undergoing intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation between January 2015 and November 2025 were reviewed. The operation targeted the lower stellate component and upper thoracic sympathetic chain bilaterally, usually through single-port thoracoscopic access. Outcomes were obtained from specialist cardiology follow-up, electrocardiography, Holter monitoring, exercise testing when available, inpatient telemetry, device interrogation, and medication records.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients were operated. Mean age was 12.4 years. Bilateral denervation was completed in 36 patients; 1 underwent left-sided denervation only owing to intraoperative haemodynamic instability. Single-port access was used in 30 patients. There were no intraoperative deaths, unplanned full thoracotomy conversions, intercostal injuries, reoperations for surgical complications, or denervation-related permanent pacing. Procedure-attributable morbidity comprised one mild Horner syndrome and one self-limited axillary wound complaint. Among 36 patients with post-discharge follow-up, 32 remained free from the primary malignant ventricular arrhythmic endpoint. Estimated malignant ventricular arrhythmia-free survival was 95.8 per cent at 1 year and 89.4 per cent at 3 years.
CONCLUSION: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation was feasible and had low procedure-attributable morbidity in selected young patients. It should be interpreted as an adjunct to multidisciplinary arrhythmia care, not as a replacement for medication, device surveillance, or follow-up.

articles.title: Echoes of Trauma: The Role of Self-Esteem Between Adverse Childhood Experiences and Intimate Partner Violence Victimization.
articles.abstract: The association between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and intimate partner violence victimization (IPVV) is well-documented. However, little is known about whether this association varies by self-esteem during emerging adulthood, a developmental period marked by increasing self-exploration and exposure to intimate relationships. This study examines whether self-esteem moderates the association between ACEs and IPVV in emerging adulthood. Data were drawn from South Korean emerging adults aged 18 to 29 with dating experience (N = 953). Negative binomial regression models were estimated, followed by average marginal effects and Johnson-Neyman style floodlight analysis. The results show that the association between physical ACEs and physical IPVV was significantly positive at lower levels of self-esteem. However, two disjoint crossover patterns were found between neglect and emotional IPVV (EIPVV). Neglect was negatively associated with EIPVV at a lower level of self-esteem but positively associated at a higher level. Findings highlight subtype-specific ACE-IPVV pathways and caution against treating self-esteem as a uniformly protective factor. The study contributes to trauma-informed IPVV prevention by emphasizing the need to consider both childhood adversity histories and the quality of self-esteem during emerging adulthood.

articles.title: Early TSH-FT4 discordance and subsequent biochemical TSH elevation in NICU-admitted neonates: An exploratory retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether relative thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)-free thyroxine (FT4) imbalance on postnatal day 2 was associated with subsequent TSH elevation in neonates admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).Study DesignThis single-center retrospective cohort included 154 NICU-admitted neonates with simultaneous serum TSH, free triiodothyronine, and FT4 measurements on postnatal day 2 and at least one subsequent serum TSH measurement. The primary predictor was the TSH-FT4 Δ score, defined as cohort-standardized TSH minus cohort-standardized FT4. The primary outcome was new threshold crossing or a further TSH increase after day 2 using an operational threshold of >15 mIU/L. Associations were evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for gestational age.ResultsEight infants met the primary outcome. Each 1-standard-deviation increase in the day-2 TSH-FT4 Δ score was associated with higher odds of subsequent TSH elevation (adjusted odds ratio, 2.47; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-5.91; p = 0.024). Day-2 TSH, day-2 FT4, and the TSH-FT4 average score showed no clear associations. A three-analyte score incorporating free triiodothyronine showed a similar association.ConclusionRelative TSH-FT4 discordance during early neonatal thyroid testing was associated with subsequent biochemical TSH elevation. These exploratory findings should not be interpreted as establishing a clinical predictive tool and require prospective external validation using standardized follow-up and clinically meaningful thyroid outcomes.

articles.title: Empathic Versus Informational Messaging and Expertise Cues in Search Ads for Suicide Prevention.
articles.abstract: Background: Search-based advertising is used as a digital outreach method to reach users searching for suicide-related terms. However, it remains unclear which ad message elements promote access to support information among users searching for terms related to life issues associated with suicide risk. Aims: We compared empathic and informational headlines and descriptions with and without expertise cues to examine ad message elements that promote access to support information among users searching for life issues. Method: Search-based advertising was displayed in Tokyo, Japan, to users searching for life-issue-related terms across six areas (perinatal women, domestic violence, addiction, depression, sexual minorities, and child abuse). Four ad types were created by combining headline type (empathic vs. informational) and description type (with vs. without an expertise cue). Outcomes were click rate and conversion rates for the three landing page actions (self-check, self-care, and consultation services). We fit mixed-effects binomial logistic regression models. Results: Empathic headlines were associated with higher odds of ad clicks and self-checks, while informational headlines were associated with higher odds of consultation services. Descriptions with expertise cues were associated with lower odds of self-care and consultation services. A headline × description interaction was observed for self-care with higher odds when an expertise cue was paired with an empathic headline. Limitations: As this study examined a limited set of ad elements in Tokyo and used Japanese-language ads and landing pages, conversion outcomes may have been influenced by the structure of the multifunctional landing page. Conclusion: Empathic headlines may promote ad clicks and self-check, whereas informational headlines may support access to consultation services. Expertise cues were not uniformly associated with greater engagement, and their associations varied by outcome and accompanying headline. These findings highlight the importance of tailoring ad messages to the behaviors they are intended to promote.

articles.title: FGF23 and Cardiac Remodeling in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Rapid Review and Exploratory Quantitative Synthesis.
articles.abstract: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), elevated left ventricular mass index (LVMI), diastolic dysfunction, heart failure, and cardiovascular mortality are common in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises early in CKD and is linked to cardiac remodeling, but consistency across studies is unclear. We conducted a rapid review of FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD, incorporating a reanalyzed unpublished single-center cohort, and pooled effect estimates where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics. A structured web-based search (August 2026) identified 11 candidate studies on FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD; 9 met eligibility, including 1 unpublished investigator-held cohort (n = 80) reanalyzed for this review. Pooling (inverse variance) was performed only where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics; all pooled estimates are exploratory, below the prespecified 3-study minimum. For FGF23 and LVH, using a derived LVH variable from the present cohort, a pooled log-FGF23 odds ratio (OR) across 2 adult-CKD studies (n = 242) was 1.33 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.92-1.93), I2 = 78%; a pediatric study (OR 2.53, n = 587) was consistent in direction but unpooled. For LVMI, correlations were not pooled; a Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort cohort showed higher LVMI only in the top quartile. For heart failure/cardiovascular mortality, a pooled hazard ratio across 2 studies (n = 374) was 2.37 (95% CI 1.47-3.84), I2 = 0%, with LVMI mediating only 7-22% in Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort. FGF23 was not significantly associated with diastolic dysfunction after adjustment (OR 1.51/standard deviation, 95% CI 0.92-2.47). The available evidence, though sparse and heterogeneous, is directionally consistent with a positive FGF23-cardiac remodeling association in CKD. Certainty is very low throughout; a full multi-database search is needed before a definitive conclusion.

articles.title: Physical activity in Swedish 3-year-old children: associations with lifestyle and behavioral factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) positively affects children's health and well-being. Despite numerous studies on factors that influence PA in adults and older school-children, limited information exists about lifestyle factors, behavior, and neurodevelopmental predictors of PA in preschool children. This study aimed to (i) quantify the time spent in various activity levels (vigorous, moderate, light, and sedentary) among 3-year-old Swedish children, and (ii) examine associations between actigraphy-measured PA and various lifestyle, behavioral factors, and health in this age group.
METHODS: PA levels were measured using wrist-worn movement sensors (MotionWatch 8) in 497 3-year-old children in the ongoing NorthPop Birth Cohort in Northern Sweden. Motion data were collected over 24 h per day for eight continuous days and were classified into sleep, sedentary behavior, and PA intensities according to an age-, epoch-, and position-validated method. Children's lifestyle, health, and demographic data were collected using register data and parental questionnaires. Neurodevelopment and behavior were assessed using the Ages & Stages Questionnaire (ASQ) and Strength and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), respectively.
RESULTS: Swedish 3-year-old children spent an average of 163 min on moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) per day. Boys spent significantly more time at MVPA levels than girls (p < 0.001). Children with better gross motor function, older siblings in the household, and spending more time playing outdoors demonstrated longer time spent at higher levels of PA over 24 h per day. Children with hyperactivity problems were more physically active, whereas those with peer problems had lower PA levels. Children who were exposed to more time playing on computer/phone spent less time being physically active.
CONCLUSIONS: Three-year-olds in Sweden are generally highly active, with nearly all (99%) meeting the WHO recommendation of at least 60 min of MVPA per day and all (100%) meeting the recommendation of at least 180 min of total daily physical activity. The explanatory factors associated with particular PA levels are multidimensional, but the results suggest that behaviors such as playing outdoors and spending less time playing on computers/phones are associated with higher PA levels in this age group.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Retrospectively registered at Researchweb 11 November 2024 (project number 279272).

articles.title: Neuro-adaptive predictive control for upper-limb rehabilitation using EMG and intention-aware assistance.
articles.abstract: Upper-limb motor impairments associated with neurological disorders such as cerebral palsy (CP) are characterized by abnormal muscle coordination, spasticity, fatigue, and highly variable electromyographic (EMG) patterns, posing significant challenges for rehabilitation exoskeleton control. While EMG-driven and adaptive controllers have shown promise, existing approaches often rely on fixed gains or address physiological state estimation, prediction, and decision-making in isolation, limiting robustness and clinical relevance-particularly in pediatric populations. This paper proposes a unified neuro-adaptive predictive control framework for upper-limb rehabilitation exoskeletons that integrates physiologically interpretable state estimation, task-aware assistance, predictive intelligence, and intention-aware supervisory control within a closed-loop architecture. The framework combines a Neuro-Motor Index (NMI) that fuses muscle co-contraction and joint tracking error, fuzzy EMG-based load estimation for task context awareness, hybrid support vector regression-long short-term memory (SVR-LSTM) trajectory prediction, and robust kernel-based motor intention decoding. NMI and task context are used to adapt admittance parameters at each simulation step, enabling assistance modulation that reflects the user's evolving neuromechanical condition. The learning-based modules were trained and evaluated using EMG recordings from pediatric populations, whereas closed-loop controller evaluation was performed exclusively in OpenSim using simulation-derived muscle excitation and activation variables, joint kinematics, and joint-level assistive torques. Clinically inspired perturbations, including fatigue-like degradation, spasticity-inspired activation bursts, EMG-like noise, and variable external loads, were introduced to assess controller robustness. Compared with no assistance and fixed-admittance control, the proposed controller reduced simulated muscular effort by 45-60% and co-contraction by up to 50%, while improving trajectory-tracking accuracy, movement smoothness, and robustness across the evaluated disturbance conditions. These results support the numerical feasibility of the integrated controller under the evaluated CP-inspired simulation conditions. They do not establish physiological benefit or clinical effectiveness in children with CP. Experimental validation and complete documentation of the clinical-data provenance and evaluation procedures are required before translation to rehabilitation exoskeletons.

articles.title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. Common neurological presentations included encephalopathy (50%), headache (45.8%), and seizures (20.8%). 37% met MIS-C criteria. Neuroimaging revealed lacunar infarctions, demyelinating white matter lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and cauda equina nerve root enhancement. Despite similar mortality rates, children with neurological involvement had a significantly higher rate of incomplete recovery, with more than a quarter experiencing persistent neurological sequelae (29.2% vs. 4.3%, p = 0.048).
CONCLUSION: Neurological manifestations of pediatric COVID-19 represent a clinically distinct pattern characterized by limited systemic inflammation but an increased risk of persistent neurological sequelae. Early neurological evaluation, appropriate neuroimaging, and structured long-term follow-up are warranted even in the absence of severe systemic illness.

articles.title: Vacuum-assisted elevation as a minimally invasive strategy for ping-pong skull fractures: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ping-pong skull fractures, although rare, represent a distinctive form of depressed skull fracture that primarily affects newborns and infants following traumatic brain injury, birth-related trauma, or compression during delivery. Due to the high malleability of the cranial vault at this age, the application of negative pressure over the depressed area has emerged as a minimally invasive therapeutic alternative capable of promoting bone elevation through local suction. The present study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this technique in the treatment of ping-pong skull fractures.
METHODS: A systematic search of publications was conducted in databases including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, covering studies published up to April 2026. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Series. Data analysis was performed using RStudio (version 2026.01.1).
RESULTS: Among the included studies, comprising a total of 81 patients, complete elevation of the ping-pong skull fracture was achieved in 86.52% of cases (95% CI 71.81-94.17; I2 = 25.0%). General complications were reported in 9.82% of patients (95% CI 4.84-18.90; I2 = 0%). The pooled rate of patients requiring a subsequent surgical approach after vacuum-assisted treatment was 10.58% (95% CI 3.95-25.40; I2 = 0%).
CONCLUSION: The vacuum-assisted elevation represents a therapeutic option for PPF, showing encouraging results across clinical, radiological and safety outcomes. However, more and larger studies are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Curcuma longa (turmeric) or its active ingredients for osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Osteoarthritis is a major cause of disability worldwide. Current treatments have limited efficacy. Curcuma longa (turmeric) contains curcuminoids with anti-inflammatory properties that may modulate osteoarthritis pathophysiology. However, the clinical benefits and safety of Curcuma longa in osteoarthritis remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of Curcuma longa extracts or сurcuminoids for osteoarthritis.
SEARCH METHODS: We used CENTRAL, MEDLINE, five other databases, and two trials registers, together with reference checking, to identify the studies included in the review. The latest search date was 7 November 2025. We applied no restrictions on language, publication date, or publication status.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing Curcuma longa extracts or curcuminoids to placebo, in people with osteoarthritis in any joint. Other comparators included no treatment, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), non-NSAID analgesics, or other active comparators. We focused on oral formulations of Curcuma longa, with or without bioavailability enhancers, and excluded combination products containing other active herbal compounds.
OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes included pain, function, quality of life, participant-reported global assessment of success, adverse events, withdrawals due to adverse events, and serious adverse events. The primary time point was up to three months.
RISK OF BIAS: We used Cochrane's RoB 2 tool to assess bias in the RCTs.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We used a random-effects model for meta-analysis. We assessed the trustworthiness of all trials eligible for inclusion using the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Trustworthiness Screening Tool.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We included nine RCTs involving 1245 participants with knee osteoarthritis. The mean age of participants ranged from 52 years to 62 years; 67% of participants were female. All trials were short (up to 90 days) and investigated different Curcuma longa formulations. One trial evaluated a bioavailability-enhanced Curcuma longa formulation, while others did not report the use of bio-enhancers. Two trials used Curcuma longa extract with essential oils. Four trials used standardised or rhizome extracts of Curcuma longa, with curcuminoid content varying from 23% to 88%. Four trials compared Curcuma longa with placebo (379 participants), four with NSAIDs (673 participants), and one with paracetamol (193 participants). Here, we limit reporting to the primary comparison, Curcuma longa versus placebo. We judged three (75%) placebo-controlled trials to be at low risk of bias for pain, function, and quality of life outcomes. Two trials (50%) were at low risk of bias for safety outcomes.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Low-certainty evidence downgraded for indirectness and publication bias showed that, compared with placebo, Curcuma longa may result in little to no difference in pain, function, or quality of life, and may improve participant-reported global assessment of success. We are very uncertain about the effect of Curcuma longa on adverse events, withdrawals due to adverse events, and serious adverse events due to very low-certainty evidence, downgraded for publication bias, imprecision, and indirectness. By three months, the mean change in pain (0 to 10 scale, 0 = no pain) was -1.57 points with placebo and 0.72 points lower (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.39 points lower to 0.06 points lower) with Curcuma longa (I² = 0%; 4 studies, 349 participants). The effect did not reach clinical significance of 1.5 points. By three months, the mean change in function (0 to 100, 0 = best function) was -5.42 points with placebo and 3.5 points lower with Curcuma longa (95% CI 7.29 points lower to 0.29 points higher; I² = 0%; 4 studies, 348 participants). By three months, the mean change in quality of life (0 to 100 scale, 100 = best quality of life) was 9.83 points with placebo and 2.19 points higher (95% CI 1.56 points lower to 5.94 points higher) with Curcuma longa (I² = 0%; 3 studies, 291 participants). By three months, 107 of 1000 participants receiving placebo reported treatment success, compared with 191 of 1000 receiving Curcuma longa (risk ratio (RR) 1.78, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.67; 2 studies, 170 participants). At the end of follow-up, 224 of 1000 participants in the placebo group reported adverse events compared with 226 of 1000 in the Curcuma longa group (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.51; I² = 0%; 4 studies, 379 participants). At the end of follow-up, 46 of 1000 participants in the placebo group withdrew due to adverse events compared with 66 of 1000 in the Curcuma longa group (RR 1.45, 95% CI 0.61 to 3.43; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 321 participants). Three trials reported no serious adverse events, while one trial reported two serious adverse events in the placebo group that were unrelated to the study.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Compared with placebo, Curcuma longa may result in little to no improvement in pain, function, or quality of life, and may improve participant-reported global assessment of success in people with knee osteoarthritis. We are very uncertain about the effect of Curcuma longa on adverse events, withdrawals due to adverse events, and serious adverse events. Future studies should last longer than three months; the maximum duration of the included studies was three months. The current evidence is limited to knee osteoarthritis, and future studies should include people with hand and hip osteoarthritis.
FUNDING: No external funding was received for this work.
REGISTRATION: Protocol (2021): 10.1002/14651858.CD014683.

articles.title: Hospitalized and Population Prevalence Over Time of Children With Medical Complexity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Children with medical complexity (CMC) experience disproportionately higher adverse health outcomes. Studies have reported their point prevalence and smaller-scale outpatient trends; however, hospitalized prevalence trends and larger-scale population prevalence trend estimates have not been done. As such, our objective was to report the prevalence trends of hospitalized CMC from 2006 to 2024 in the hospitalized and provincial population of Alberta, Canada.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, repeated, cross-sectional study of CMC prevalence, aged 0 to 18 years, in 2-year intervals from 2006 to 2024 using data from all residents of Alberta, Canada. We identified all children with at least 1 inpatient hospitalization associated with a complex chronic condition (CCC). We calculated prevalence both by dividing the absolute count of children hospitalized with a CCC in a time interval by the age-matched hospitalized population and the age-matched Alberta population for the same time interval.
RESULTS: The most recent adjusted overall hospitalized prevalence, from the 2022-2024 time interval, was 6301 per 100 000, and the adjusted provincial prevalence of hospitalized CMC was 784 per 100 000 population. The adjusted hospitalized prevalence increased by 3.9% per 2-year time interval from 2006 to 2018, followed by a decline of 3.1% per time interval in 2019-2024. The adjusted provincial prevalence of hospitalized CMC increased by 2.6% per time interval from 2006 to 2014, followed by a decline of 3.4% per time interval from 2015 until 2024.
CONCLUSIONS: A peak followed by a decline was seen in hospitalized CMC prevalence between 2014 and 2018 in the provincial and hospitalized population, which may be aligning with preliminary evidence from the literature.

articles.title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP.
articles.abstract: In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend: EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should: ○ Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.○ Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include: ▪ External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquets▪ Airway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.▪ Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empirical bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.▪ External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.▪ Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.○ Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with: ○ Injuries that are incompatible with life (eg, decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).○ Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (eg, rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).○ Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.

articles.title: Socioecological Influences on Food and Nutrition Security Among Publicly Insured Families.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding of the factors influencing food and nutrition security among households with children remains limited, particularly during pediatric hospitalization, a vulnerable period for food access. Caregivers' perspectives offer critical insights into the determinants of food-related decision-making and the strategies households use to obtain preferred, nutritious foods.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study using semistructured interviews with caregivers of publicly insured hospitalized children from an existing study cohort. We purposively sampled participants using maximal variation sampling to reflect a range of food and nutrition security statuses. Guided by a socioecological framework, interviews explored caregivers' perspectives on nutrition, food access and benefits, and community resources. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis with both inductive and deductive coding, informed by the same framework.
RESULTS: We interviewed 23 caregivers, predominantly from food-secure and nutrition-secure households. Six themes were identified, including (1) balancing nutritional ideals with everyday realities; (2) dynamics of food access across cycles of resource fluctuation and strain; (3) dignity, choice, and a hierarchy with food assistance programs; (4) food scarcity-driven sacrifice, emotional burden, and adaptive measures; (5) technology-enabled strategies to mitigate barriers to food access and nutrition information; and (6) skepticism toward the food system and a preference for natural foods.
CONCLUSION: Constrained choices, fluctuating resources, and system-level factors shaped perceptions of food and nutrition, influencing caregivers' sense of dignity, control, and adaptive strategies, such as using grocery-delivery services and online sources. These findings highlight the importance of autonomy and stability in supporting vulnerable families' access to preferred foods.

articles.title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and management in nursing practice.
articles.abstract: Asthma is one of the most common chronic respiratory conditions in the UK, affecting both children and adults. It is characterised by airway inflammation, variable symptoms, and reversible airflow limitation. This article provides a nursing-focused overview of asthma, exploring the definition, altered pathophysiology, diagnosis, and both pharmacological and non-pharmacological management. It highlights the importance of accurate assessment, early differentiation from other respiratory conditions, and the use of structured diagnostic tools within national guidance. Education, adherence support, and awareness of excessive reliever use are identified as key nursing priorities. By following national and local guidelines, promoting the use of combination and anti-inflammatory therapies, and providing holistic, person-centred education, nurses can improve symptom control, reduce preventable hospital admissions, and enhance quality of life for individuals and families living with asthma.

articles.title: The Role of Droperidol in the Management of Acute Agitation: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute behavioral disturbance accounts for ~1.7 million emergency department visits in the USA annually, with 83% involving an underlying serious mental illness. A 2001 FDA black box warning regarding QT prolongation reduced use of droperidol, a butyrophenone antipsychotic, but recent data challenge these concerns.
METHODS: We reviewed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and observational studies from 2000 to 2025 assessing droperidol's efficacy and safety.
RESULTS: Droperidol provides rapid, effective sedation, with onset within 3 to 10 minutes and median time to adequate sedation of 14 to 25 minutes. Sixty-four percent of patients achieved adequate sedation at 15 minutes with droperidol versus 25% to 35% with ziprasidone and 29% with lorazepam. QT prolongation occurred in 1.3% of 1009 patients, mostly those with pre-existing risk factors. Respiratory depression was less common with droperidol (12%) than with ziprasidone (36% to 39%) or lorazepam (48%). Droperidol-midazolam combinations achieved faster sedation and reduced need for rescue medications (41% vs. 62%). Droperidol-treated patients had shorter hospital stays. Large studies found negligible rates of torsades de pointes or extracardiac arrhythmias. Elderly and pediatric patients responded favorably to low-dose droperidol. The American College of Emergency Physicians now recommends droperidol as first-line treatment for severe agitation. Combined with benzodiazepines, droperidol shows synergistic effects and allows lower doses of both with fewer adverse effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Recent evidence contradicts earlier FDA concerns, supporting droperidol as a safe, effective treatment for acute agitation. Its rapid onset, efficacy, safety profile, and operational benefits, including shorter ED stay, support its return to routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Latent profiles of addictive-like behaviors: a person-centered analysis of risk and protective factors among adolescents.
articles.abstract: Addictive-like behaviors are common during adolescence and are associated with a broad range of emotional, behavioral, and social outcomes. Using a person-centered framework, the present study aimed to identify distinct profiles of adolescents based on the frequency and severity of addictive-like behaviors and to examine how these profiles differ in key risk and protective factors. A large community sample of 6,849 adolescents aged 12-18 completed self-report measures assessing alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, and cocaine use, gambling, shopping, gaming, disordered-eating, sexual-activity, and social-networking behaviors. Risk and protective-factor measures were available in a 6,031-participant study component and included impulsivity, reward deficiency syndrome (RDS), meaning in life (presence and search), psychological flexibility, eudaimonic well-being, perceived acceptance and rejection from teachers, and parent-adolescent communication. Latent profile analysis identified three distinct behavioral profiles: Normal Engagement (n = 6,164; 90.00%), Tobacco-Dominant (n = 511; 7.46%), and Substance and Gambling Vulnerability (n = 174; 2.54%). The profiles differed significantly across sociodemographic characteristics and across the examined risk and protective factors. A clear and consistent directional pattern emerged, with Normal Engagement generally showing higher protective and lower risk characteristics, Substance and Gambling Vulnerability generally showing the reverse pattern, and Tobacco-Dominant frequently falling between them. Omnibus effects were very small to small. Overall, the findings are consistent with transdiagnostic risk and protective processes across adolescent addictive-like behaviors, while the modest effect sizes indicate substantial overlap between profiles.

articles.title: Patient and Caregiver Education in Inborn Errors of Immunity: Short-Term Changes After a Structured Booklet-Based Intervention.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess baseline disease-related knowledge among patients with IEI and caregivers and to explore short-term changes 2 months after the distribution of a structured educational booklet.
METHODS: This exploratory, uncontrolled, single-center, pilot pre-post survey study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric immunology center. Eligible respondents were adult patients with IEI, literate adolescents aged 14-17 years, and caregivers of pediatric patients. Respondents completed a researcher-developed 30-item questionnaire covering general knowledge, warning signs/manifestations, treatment awareness, and protective/preventive measures at baseline and 2 months after booklet distribution. Paired scores were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
RESULTS: Fifty-one respondents completed both assessments: 33 patients with IEI and 18 caregivers. Mean respondent age was 34.55 ± 12.83 years, and 32 respondents were female. The median total score increased from 23 (interquartile range [IQR]: 19-25) to 25 (IQR: 20-27), with a median paired change of 1 point (IQR: 0-5, P <.001). Treatment awareness increased from 6 (IQR: 4-8) to 8 (IQR: 6-9, P <.001), and protective/preventive measures increased from 8 (IQR: 6-9) to 9 (IQR: 7-9, P = 0.009).
CONCLUSION: Questionnaire scores were higher 2 months after booklet distribution, mainly in treatment and prevention domains. These findings suggest that written educational materials may help identify and address selected knowledge gaps, particularly regarding immunoglobulin replacement therapy, home-based treatment, and preventive measures.

articles.title: Quality of life in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease over the past decade: A repeated cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Children with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), experience a significantly lower health-related quality of life (HRQoL) compared to healthy children. Over the past decade, advancements in IBD care may have influenced HRQoL. The aim of this study was to compare HRQoL between two independent pediatric IBD cohorts from distinct time periods.
METHODS: Two pediatric IBD cohorts, T1 cohort (2014-2015) and T2 cohort (2022-2024), completed the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory 4.0 (PedsQL) and the IBD-specific IMPACT-III questionnaire. Total and scale scores of both questionnaires were compared between the two cohorts. Moreover, the HRQoL of T2 was compared to the general population (GP).
RESULTS: In total, 117 (T1: 72, T2: 45) patients completed both questionnaires. The PedsQL total and scale scores did not differ between T1 and T2 for both patients with CD and UC. IMPACT-III total and subscale scores showed no differences for patients with CD and the total IBD-cohort. In UC, the IMPACT-III total score and its subdomain social functioning were higher in T2 (p = 0.049 and p = 0.013, respectively). Children with IBD in the T2 cohort scored lower in the physical (p = 0.001) and school (p = 0.001) functioning subscales when compared to the GP cohort.
CONCLUSION: This study shows no overall difference in HRQoL for pediatric patients with IBD over the past decade but indicates an improvement in HRQoL for children with UC.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Family Maltreatment After Military Parental Injury in a Matched Retrospective Cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric nurse practitioners may provide care for military families experiencing parental health conditions associated with injury. Parental injury or illness may contribute to stress, leading to increased risks of child maltreatment or family violence.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 6,253 spouses and 13,298 children of 9,157 injured service members who returned to duty. Records were followed for two years for child maltreatment, family violence, and well-child care. Chi-square, Wilcoxon rank sum tests, and logistic regression compared and calculated odds of outcomes.
RESULTS: Families with parents who experienced co-occurring mental health and physical injury were at significantly increased risk of child maltreatment, family violence, and decreased well-child care. Having a non-injured parent with a mental health diagnosis was associated with significantly higher odds of maltreatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric nurse practitioners should be aware of risk factors for maltreatment during periods of parental injury and provide avenues for early identification.

articles.title: Early-Life Movement Behaviour Patterns and Later Clinically Diagnosed Obesity: A Longitudinal Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the longitudinal association between early-life movement behaviour patterns and later clinically diagnosed obesity.
METHOD: In the population-based All Babies in Southeast Sweden (ABIS) cohort, 16 415 children were included after consent. A total of 542 participants had an obesity diagnosis recorded in the Swedish National Patient Register through 2023. Questionnaire-based movement behaviour data were collected at ages 3, 5, 8, 10-12 and 17-23 years. A Total Activity Score (TAS) combining physical activity and sedentary behaviours was used to classify participants as less active or highly active. Cox proportional hazards regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for maternal education and parental body mass index.
RESULTS: Higher TAS was associated with a lower hazard of clinically diagnosed obesity from age 5 onwards. Adjusted HRs for highly active versus less active participants were 0.85 (0.62-0.97, p = 0.003) at age 5, 0.66 (0.43-0.78, p = 0.002) at age 8, 0.54 (0.38-0.67, p = 0.001) at age 10-12 and 0.49 (0.23-0.59, p = 0.001) at age 17-23. Associations were observed in both sexes, without formal interaction testing.
CONCLUSION: Favourable childhood movement behaviour patterns were associated with a lower hazard of clinically diagnosed obesity.

articles.title: Atypical inflammatory bowel disease and multi-system inflammation expand the phenotype of inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B kinase subunit beta gain-of-function variants.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Gain-of-function (GoF) variants in the inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa-B kinase subunit beta (IKK2) protein, encoded by inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B kinase subunit beta (IKBKB), have previously been reported to cause autoinflammation with a progressive immunodeficiency. Genetic defects have not previously been described in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), although disruption of highly interacting proteins, such as IKBKG and RELA, are known causes of monogenic IBD.
METHODS: Using whole exome sequencing data, we screened a cohort of over 1250 adult and paediatric onset patients with IBD for deleterious variants (minor allele frequency < 0.0005, Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion [CADD] > 15) in IKBKB. We retrieved in-depth phenotypic data and performed peripheral blood mononuclear cell CD25/CD70 stimulation validation in patients with apparent IKBKB GoF variants.
RESULTS: We identified 11 patients with potentially pathogenic variants. Correlation with clinical and immunophenotypic data prioritised a rare, potential gain-of-function, variant in a patient and his affected parent, c.522T>G, p Asp174Glu. The proband had multi-system inflammation and severe atypical inflammatory bowel disease with rectal stricturing. We demonstrated impaired CD25/CD70 T- and B-cell responses in the patient, characteristic of the IKBKB defect, alongside hallmark immunological manifestations of reduced natural killer and B-cell numbers, and perturbed immunoglobulin titres. Treatment with a selective Janus kinase (JAK1)-inhibitor resulted in rapid clinical and biochemical improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: This study expands the phenotypic manifestation of IKBKB GoF variants to include IBD and demonstrates a biologically plausible targeted treatment. Further functional work is required to elucidate the precise mechanism of bowel inflammation and identify additional patients.

articles.title: Implementing intestinal ultrasound in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: Practical framework for program development: Perspectives from the Pediatric Committee of the Intestinal Ultrasound Group of the United States and Canada.
authors: Intestinal Ultrasound Group of the United States and Canada (iUSCAN)
articles.abstract: Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is a noninvasive, radiation-free tool that is well-tolerated and frequently preferred by children and families. Its ability to provide real-time assessments that facilitate timely decision-making is driving its adoption as an increasingly important monitoring standard in comprehensive pediatric inflammatory bowel disease care. IUS programs follow a common trajectory: begin by identifying and supporting a physician lead, then scale through additional trained physicians, a consultation service, and, where volume supports it, sonographer or hybrid models. Institutional planning should enable this growth while preserving the point-of-care delivery that defines IUS's clinical value. Sustainability requires institutional commitment to equipment, protected time, training (ideally embedded in fellowship), standardized documentation, and a reimbursement strategy. Equipment is attainable, not aspirational: a moderately priced cart-based system is sufficient and should be framed to leadership as essential infrastructure. Centers that adopt IUS with rigorous documentation and join collaborative registries from the outset will be positioned to generate the outcomes data needed to further advance the field.

articles.title: The impact of highly effective modulator therapy on gastrointestinal, hepatic, and nutritional outcomes in cystic fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a multisystemic disease that has implications throughout the gastrointestinal (GI) tract and is a significant cause of morbidity for people with CF (PwCF). The introduction of highly effective modulator therapy (HEMT) has led to major implications in the health and life expectancy of PwCF. However, the influence of HEMT on GI manifestations for PwCF is less clear and complex. This paper performs a review of the current literature assessing the impact of HEMT on GI manifestations related to CF. We review the implications of HEMT on the upper GI tract, pancreas, liver, lower GI tract, and nutrition. HEMT has a positive impact on overall weight and nutrition but may lead to greater than recommended weight gain. HEMT may also lead to improved pancreatic function when started at a young age, may improve meconium ileus in the neonatal period, and may improve intestinal inflammation. There is less clear evidence on the impact of HEMT on reflux, bloating, constipation, distal intestinal obstruction syndrome, and pancreatitis. There does not appear to be an improvement in CF hepatobiliary disease (CFHBI) with HEMT, and those taking it should be monitored for drug-induced injury (DILI). HEMT does show promising benefits for some GI manifestations of CF. However, there continues to be significant morbidity from GI manifestations in PwCF despite HEMT. Further research would benefit the understanding and implications of HEMT in this realm.

articles.title: BMI percentile trajectories and liver enzyme changes in children with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: A longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The incidence of pediatric obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are rapidly rising. However, the impact of dynamic body mass index (BMI) changes on liver chemistries remains understudied. We investigated the association between longitudinal changes in BMI percentile and changes in liver chemistries among children with MASLD.
METHODS: In this multicenter study, 1169 children with biopsy-confirmed MASLD enrolled in the Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network were followed for a mean of 4.0 years. BMI percentiles were calculated using the lambda-mu-sigma method with an extended metric to capture nuances at extreme values. Generalized linear mixed-effects models with random effects for patients and clinics were applied, and inverse probability treatment weighting adjusted for demographics and baseline histologic features. Sensitivity analyses stratified by sex and ethnicity assessed robustness.
RESULTS: Participants (mean age 13 years; 72% Hispanic) with higher BMI percentiles exhibited elevated blood pressures, increased insulin levels, and a lower frequency of the patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) GG variant. Each 5-unit increase in BMI percentile was independently associated with a 23% increase in alanine aminotransferase (1.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.17-1.30), a 13% increase in aspartate aminotransferase (1.13; 95% CI, 1.09-1.17), and a 12% increase in γ‑glutamyl transferase (1.12; 95% CI, 1.08-1.16).
CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal increases in BMI percentile are independently associated with worse liver chemistry in pediatric MASLD. Routine monitoring of BMI trajectories, alongside early weight management strategies, may be critical to mitigating disease progression. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01061684, NCT04454463.

articles.title: Design priorities for paediatric walkers in India: professional perspectives.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Independent mobility is essential for children's participation in education, community life, and social activities. In India, no paediatric walker is specifically designed for Indian children or the contexts in which they live. This study explored rehabilitation providers' perspectives on the limitations of existing paediatric walkers and identified features that may optimise walker design for Indian settings.
METHODS: A qualitative study using reflexive thematic analysis was conducted across four cities in India. Rehabilitation providers, orthotists and equipment vendors, involved in the assessment, prescription, and provision of paediatric mobility devices were recruited through convenience and snowball sampling. Data were collected through focus groups and individual interviews.
RESULTS: Fifty-eight participants shared their perspectives over nine focus groups and five individual interviews, in four different Indian cities. Six themes were identified (1): child-friendly design, emphasising attractive, engaging, safe, and easy-to-use walkers (2); customisation, including adjustability for age, diagnosis, growth, and terrain (3); durability, particularly for uneven rural environments and prolonged use (4); functional features, such as harnesses, splints, seating options, braking systems, and improved wheel designs (5); technology integration, including biofeedback, artificial intelligence, and GPS-enabled monitoring; and (6) lightweight construction, supporting portability, transportation, and everyday use.
CONCLUSIONS: Rehabilitation providers identified several design priorities for a paediatric walker tailored to Indian contexts. These findings provide foundational guidance for the development of paediatric mobility devices that better meet the needs of Indian children and their families.

articles.title: Functional Somatic Symptoms in Paediatric Patients With Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Aberrant stress-system activation or dysregulation affects the cardiovascular system through various pathways, including the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, autonomic nervous system, neuro-endocrine system, and a range of neurophysiological intermediaries. In children with congenital heart disease-who have high rates of adverse childhood experiences, comorbid medical conditions, and neurodevelopmental issues-this activation/dysregulation commonly results in functional cardiac symptoms such as orthostatic intolerance, (functional) chest pain, and syncope-like presentations. Despite the obvious need, research into stress-system responses in children with congenital heart disease is limited. This article reviews commonly encountered clinical scenarios with the goal of encouraging practitioners to recognise the interconnections between structural cardiac lesions in children, stress-system activation/dysregulation, and functional somatic symptoms. Children with congenital heart disease and comorbid functional symptoms require comprehensive management strategies. We propose a framework to help clinicians facilitate appropriate treatment.

articles.title: Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life Measure for Children/Adolescents With Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to adapt the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life for Adolescents with Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS) scale into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties. It also explored oral health status and quality of life among children with Down syndrome (DS).
METHODS: The study included 100 children with DS and their mothers. Sociodemographic and oral health data were collected through structured questionnaires. The OH-QOLADS, comprising child and family forms with two timeframes, was translated and culturally adapted following international guidelines. Internal consistency, CFA, and item-total correlations were conducted to assess psychometric validity.
RESULTS: The Turkish OH-QOLADS showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α and McDonald's ω > 0.94) across all forms and timeframes. CFA supported the original four-factor structure (symptoms/functioning, emotional well-being, social participation, and family impact) with strong model fit indices (CFI > 0.98; RMSEA < 0.05). Most participants reported poor oral health, low tooth brushing frequency, and minimal preventive care. Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) scores were significantly associated with comorbidities like thyroid disease, diabetes, and hearing impairments.
CONCLUSION: The Turkish OH-QOLADS is a valid, reliable tool for assessing OHRQoL in children with DS. The findings highlight the need for better access to preventive dental services and caregiver support.

articles.title: Latent Profile Analysis of Reproductive Concerns in Thyroid Cancer Survivors: Implications for Stratified Fertility Preservation Interventions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study applied latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify distinct phenotypes of reproductive concerns (RCs) and their influencing factors among young adult thyroid cancer (TC) patients in a Chinese tertiary hospital setting, providing preliminary evidence for stratified fertility preservation interventions.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 313 TC patients (aged 18-45 years) recruited from a tertiary hospital in China. RCs were assessed using the Reproductive Concerns After Cancer scale. LPA was employed to identify distinct subgroups, and multivariate logistic regression was performed to determine factors associated with profile membership.
RESULTS: Three latent profiles were identified: (1) Low Concern-Traditional (28.7%), characterized by minimal distress and family-oriented priorities; (2) Moderate Concern-Balanced (44.4%), characterized by intermediate distress and conflicted family and reproductive goals; and (3) High Concern-Comprehensive (26.8%), characterized by severe distress, particularly in partner disclosure and child's health. Multivariate logistic regression (with the 40-45 years age group as reference) indicated that patients aged 18-29 years (odds ratio [OR] = 0.184, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.055-0.609, p = 0.006) and 30-34 years (OR = 0.213, 95% CI: 0.073-0.624, p = 0.005) had significantly lower odds of high RC compared with those aged 40-45 years, suggesting that older age is independently associated with higher concern after adjustment for treatment-related covariates. Patients who underwent thyroidectomy (OR = 8.944, p = 0.016) or radioactive iodine therapy (OR = 2.131, p < 0.001) exhibited significantly elevated RCs compared to untreated patients. Sensitivity analyses restricted to female participants (n = 259) yielded class structures, proportions, and covariate effects virtually identical to the primary combined-sample analysis, supporting the robustness of our findings.
CONCLUSION: This study delineates three distinct RC profiles among young Chinese TC patients. Key correlates of greater RC include older age (40-45 years, independently associated after multivariate adjustment), radioactive iodine therapy (I131), and surgical treatment, while younger age was associated with greater concern at the univariate level. Tailored interventions are recommended to address the specific needs of each subgroup. Future longitudinal studies are warranted to validate these phenotypes and translate findings into clinical practice.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This is a cross-sectional observational study, which is not subject to clinical trial registration requirements.

articles.title: The efficacy of adding leg wrapping to prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of post-spinal hypotension in elective cesarean section: a prospective double-blinded randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Various pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods have been studied in the literature to reduce the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of adding bilateral lower-limb wrapping to a prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of hypotension in parturients receiving intrathecal anesthesia for cesarean delivery.
METHODS: This prospective randomized trial included parturients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Parturients were divided into the following: norepinephrine group (N) (n = 84), and norepinephrine and leg wrapping group (NW) (n = 84). The 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion continued until 5 min after fetal delivery. The primary outcome was the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of maternal severe hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, hypertension, nausea, vomiting, post-delivery hypotension, and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: The final analysis included 168 patients. The incidence of hypotension in the NW group was lower than in the N group (7/84 [8.3%], 18/84 [21.4%], respectively) with P = 0.017, RR = 0.39, and CI: (0.17-0.88). According to the Kaplan-Meier curve with the log-rank test, the time to post-spinal maternal hypotension differed significantly (P = 0.016), with a restricted mean time of 21.1 min in the NW group and 19.7 min in the N group (hazard ratio = 2.82 for the N group vs. NW, 95%CI: (1.18-6.76). Furthermore, a repeated-measures analysis revealed significant group-by-time interactions for both heart rate (P = 0.003) and systolic blood pressure (P = 0.028), demonstrating superior longitudinal hemodynamic stability in the NW group. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected for secondary maternal and neonatal outcomes.
