CONCLUSION: When added to a prophylactic 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion, leg wrapping decreased the incidence of postspinal maternal hypotension and enhanced hemodynamic stability over time during elective cesarean delivery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06496061; principal investigator: Mohamed Ahmed Hamed; date of registration: 11/07/2024; no protocol amendments or study changes after trial start).

articles.title: Usability of an artificial intelligence enabled Participation and Environment Measure prototype for family-centered goal setting support in pediatric rehabilitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family-centered care coordination (FC-CC) in pediatric rehabilitation benefits from tools that support caregivers in contributing to personalized service planning for their children. Participation and Environment Measure (PEM) is a digital application that is being further developed to support FC-CC in early intervention (EI). PEM is being further developed to include the Young Children's Participation and Environment Measure (YC-PEM) electronic patient-reported outcome and a companion PEM-Plus (PEM+) goal setting intervention. This study examined usability of the first artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled PEM prototype.
METHODS: Caregivers from an urban EI program met these eligibility criteria: (1) were at least 18 years old; (2) identified as the parent or legal guardian of a child enrolled in EI services; (3) read, wrote, and spoke English; (4) had internet and telephone access; and (5) had a child 0-3 years old who received EI services for 3 or more months. Participants completed the AI-enabled PEM application with access to a debiased prototypic conversational agent. PEM usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS), and chatbot usability was assessed along four BOT Usability Scale (BUS-11) domains: 1) accessibility of chatbot functions; 2) functional interactive conversation; 3) privacy and security; and 4) timely response. Univariate logistic regression models were used to examine associations between each of the four BUS-11 domains and PEM+ engagement.
RESULTS: Eleven female caregivers of children (mean age: 24.5 months) enrolled, 66.7% of whom interacted with the prototypic chatbot during one or more iterations of the PEM+ intervention. Overall PEM usability remained acceptable. While overall chatbot usability was very poor (Mdn = 53.4%, IQR = 50.0, 55.4), caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability were average for accessibility of chatbot functions (Mdn = 3.8, IQR = 3.0, 4.0) and good for privacy and security (M = 3.1, Range = 2.0-5.0). Higher caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability did not significantly increase odds of PEM+ intervention use.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings indicate that an AI-enabled PEM retains adequate usability. A chatbot integrated within the PEM+ intervention is accessible and secure, though its functional interactive conversation and timely responses could benefit from further development to increase odds of its use in an EI service context.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06458959 (Registration date: 2024-06-14).

articles.title: Patterns and Factors Associated With Coronary Artery Involvement in Kawasaki Disease: Experience From Southern Tunisia.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a paediatric vasculitis associated with coronary complications. We aimed to describe clinical and echocardiographic characteristics and factors associated with coronary involvement. This retrospective, single-centre study included 70 children over 18 years (2007-2024). Univariate analyses assessed clinical and laboratory associations. The mean age was 55.4 ± 32.8 months; 61.7% were younger than 5 years. Coronary involvement occurred in 32/70 (45.7%), including dilation in 25 (35.7%), wall thickening in 7 (10.0%) and aneurysms in 3 (4.3%). Lesions regressed in 27/32 (84.4%). Significant associations included cheilitis, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, cough, rhinorrhoea, leucocytosis, lymphocytosis, lower mean corpuscular volume, higher mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration, thrombocytosis and elevated alanine aminotransferase. These unadjusted associations do not establish independent predictors. Early diagnosis, intravenous immunoglobulin and aspirin remain essential. Systematic echocardiographic assessment, structured follow-up and larger multicentre studies are needed to improve coronary risk stratification and long-term outcomes in children with KD.

articles.title: Primary Care Continuity During the Transition to Adulthood and Its Association With Acute Healthcare Utilization Among Youth With Eating Disorders.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The transition from pediatric to adult care is a high-risk period for youth with eating disorders (EDs), often characterized by care disruptions and disengagement from adult services. This study examined whether patterns of primary care continuity during this transition are associated with acute healthcare utilization post-transition.
METHOD: A retrospective cohort study of 1106 youth discharged from a tertiary pediatric ED program in Ontario, Canada. Primary care continuity was categorized into five groups based on dominant general practitioner (GP) patterns before and after age 18. Outcomes included emergency department visits (EDVs) and hospitalizations within 2 years post-transition. Multivariate logistic regression models estimated associations, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors, and corresponding pre-transition acute healthcare utilization.
RESULTS: Compared with maintaining the same dominant GP before and after age 18 (Group 1), no dominant GP in either period (Group 5) was associated with lower odds of any EDV (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.32-0.73), any hospitalization (OR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.16-0.76), and MH-related hospitalization (OR: 0.30, 95% CI: 0.08-0.81). A dominant GP before but not after 18 (Group 4) was associated with lower odds of MH-related EDVs (OR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.29-0.95). Sensitivity analyses generally supported these findings.
DISCUSSION: Primary care continuity was not associated with acute healthcare utilization among youth with EDs, highlighting a complex relationship between GP continuity, healthcare needs, and healthcare use. Lower utilization among those without a dominant GP may not indicate lower need or better outcomes. Future research should clarify these patterns, while transition planning should continue to support timely and sustained primary care involvement for youth with EDs.

articles.title: Clinical and Radiographic Characteristics of Pneumococcal Pneumonia in Children: A Case Series.
articles.abstract: Given the decline in pneumococcal infections related to widespread childhood vaccinations in the United States, we evaluate the rate of Streptococcus pneumoniae and also report the demographic and radiographic characteristics of children with pneumococcal pneumonia in the post-pneumococcal conjugate vaccine era. We studied the prevalence of medical comorbidities, clinical presentations and outcomes, antibiotic susceptibility results, and radiographic findings among children aged less than 18 years presenting to a pediatric Emergency Department between 2010 and 2023 with a diagnosis of pneumonia and detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae in blood and/or pleural fluid. Of the 31 cases of pneumococcal pneumonia, over 50% occurred among children less than 5 years of age, and 71% of children had medical comorbidities. Eighty percent of children had radiographic pneumonia; the most common radiographic findings included opacities (71.0%), consolidation (29.0%), and pleural effusion (25.8%). Given high rates of antibiotic overtreatment, these findings may help clinicians to judiciously use antibiotics for children with pneumonia.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity and functional disability in middle-aged and older adults: a harmonized multicohort study.
articles.abstract: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is highly prevalent in aging populations, yet its association and underlying mechanisms with functional disability (FD) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate CMM-FD relationship, quantify the influencing mechanisms, and explore heterogeneity across different CMM patterns and population subgroups. A multicohort study was conducted by pooling harmonized longitudinal data from three international aging cohorts. CMM was defined as the co-occurrence of at least two cardiometabolic diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, heart diseases, and stroke. FD was measured through difficulty performing basic or instrumental activities of daily living. Logistic regression models were used to estimate associations and heterogeneities, and Kohler-Holm-Breen decomposition was used to quantify mediating contributions. CMM prevalence was 22.53%, and FD prevalence was 23.01%. CMM was strongly associated with higher odds of FD (OR = 2.940; p < 0.001), with consistent findings across all countries and FD subtypes. Respiratory, neuropsychiatric, and sensory conditions jointly explained 20.44% of the association, with psychological problems contributing the largest share. CMM patterns involving stroke generally showed high odds of FD, while the four-disease combination had the largest overall point estimate. Middle-aged, male, married, childless, non-retired, and smoking older adults exhibited a stronger CMM-associated elevation in odds of FD. Early identification of high-risk CMM patterns, routine screening for functional and psychological, cognitive, respiratory, and sensory symptoms, and targeted follow-up for individuals with stroke-containing or complex CMM patterns may reduce the risk of functional deterioration and support independent living in aging populations.

articles.title: KAWACALP study: the utility of serum calprotectin as a prognostic biomarker in Kawasaki disease.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To assess if serum calprotectin (sCP) can be used as a predictor of resistance to intravenous immunoglobulin treatment (IVIG) and coronary artery aneurysms (CAA) in Kawasaki disease (KD). A multicenter, observational, cohort study was conducted prospectively between September 2018 and February 2023. sCP was analyzed at four points in the evolution of KD in 74 patients from four Spanish hospitals. The sCP and other clinical and analytical values were compared between groups: IVIG responders or sensitive KD patients (SKD) versus IVIG nonresponders or refractory KD patients (RKD), and KD patients with CAA versus those without CAA. In refractory KD patients and in those who developed CAA, sCP was higher at the moment of diagnosis and remained elevated after treatment with IVIG, unlike what happened in sensitive KD patients and in those without CAA. A post-treatment sCP level ≥ 14.09 μg/ml predicted RKD with Sn 75% and Sp 72.97% (AUC 0.75). A pre-treatment sCP cutoff of ≥ 21.49 μg/ml predicted CAA with Sn:100% and Sp 71.05% (AUC 0.86). A post-treatment sCP value ≥ 14.76 μg/ml predicted CAA with S 71.43% and Sp 76.32% (AUC 0.74).
CONCLUSIONS: Serum CP at the time of diagnosis ≥ 21.49 μg/ml has a sensitivity of 100% to detect CAA. Therefore, if these results are confirmed in larger studies, sCP may be used as a prognostic biomarker in patients with Kawasaki disease, to detect early patients with a higher probability of CAA occurrence, guide treatment decisions and ultimately reduce cardiac complications.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • At present, no validated biomarkers allow early identification of IVIG resistance or predict coronary involvement in KD patients.
WHAT IS NEW: • High serum calprotectin level at the diagnosis of KD and persistently elevated levels after IVIG treatment may identify patients at risk for IVIG resistance and coronary complications.

articles.title: Impact of acute hyperglycaemia on cognitive function in people with diabetes: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: While the effect of short-term hypoglycaemia on cognitive function has been widely studied, the impact of acute hyperglycaemia on cognitive performance in people with diabetes is poorly understood. This systematic review summarised evidence on the effect of acute hyperglycaemia on cognitive functioning.
METHODS: Searches were conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO from conception to 5th March 2025. People with type 1 diabetes (T1D), type 2 diabetes (T2D) or control participants were included. Studies with the main outcome of dementia were excluded. A narrative synthesis was undertaken.
RESULTS: Eighteen studies were included, involving children and adults with T1D and T2D, using observational and experimental designs. Findings were synthesised by cognitive function domain: attention, processing speed, executive functioning, working memory and study design. Two studies measured driving performance. At blood glucose of 10-15 mmol/L the effects were mixed. At a blood glucose of 15-18 mmol/L impairment was more consistent. Driving performance in young adults with T1D was impaired at >16.7 mmol/L. At glucose ≥20 mmol/L, most studies reported widespread cognitive impairment in especially working memory, attention and processing speed.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute hyperglycaemia impairs cognitive functioning in people living with diabetes, with effects generally increasing at higher glucose levels. Whilst this pattern was not uniform across all blood glucose ranges and cognitive domains, impairment in cognitive function could impact on everyday activities for adults and children, including schoolwork, driving and work productivity. Future research should focus on crossover or clamp studies to clarify thresholds and evaluate real-world outcomes.

articles.title: Caregiving networks and children with neurologic impairment: A multicenter social network analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with neurologic impairment (NI) often require care from multiple paid and unpaid caregivers-a "caregiving network"-yet little is known about how caregiving networks influence child health. Understanding how networks influence health could support innovative intervention designs targeting groups of caregivers.
OBJECTIVES: This multicenter prospective cohort study will evaluate whether caregiving network characteristics are associated with serious health events and quality of life among children with NI.
METHODS: THRIvE (Teamwork and Healthy Relationships Improving Engagement in Caregiving) is a multicenter prospective cohort study enrolling children ages 2-16 years with NI and at least one hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visit in the prior 12 months, along with primary caregivers (PCGs) and secondary caregivers (SCGs), at five academic medical centers. Caregiving networks will be assessed at enrollment using egocentric social network analysis administered to PCGs and validated with SCG surveys. Exposures include network density, centralization, triadic closure, network size, and composition. Primary outcomes at 12 months are serious health events (death or hospitalization) and child quality of life. Secondary outcomes include clinical symptoms, missed school days, and ED visits. Associations will be examined using mixed-effects regression models accounting for site clustering, confounding, and multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: This study will provide novel prospective evidence about how caregiving network configurations are associated with health outcomes in children with NI.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings may identify modifiable social network features that can inform future family-centered, network-based interventions to improve child health and quality of life.

articles.title: Recompensation in autoimmune hepatitis.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is an immune-mediated liver disease in which persistent necroinflammation drives progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, and ultimately portal hypertension-related decompensation. Effective immunosuppression may halt hepatic inflammation, thereby inducing biochemical (and histological) remission, facilitating regeneration of hepatic function, clinical recompensation, and fibrosis regression. Studies indicate that approximately 19-54% of immunosuppressed patients achieve recompensation. Lower Child-Pugh score, lower immunoglobulin G levels, and a complete biochemical response are associated with higher recompensation rates, whereas advanced-grade hepatic encephalopathy and a higher Model for End-stage Liver Disease score are associated with lower recompensation rates. Recompensation improves prognosis and transplant-free survival compared with non-recompensated AIH patients. However, recompensation should not be equated with resolution of portal hypertension or a reduced risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, which may persist and continue to require surveillance and treatment. CONCLUSION: Recompensation in AIH is possible and confers better clinical outcomes. However, with the definition of aetiological control less well defined, data remain heterogeneous.

articles.title: Natural History of Prenatally Identified Children With 48,XXYY Syndrome in Infancy and Early Childhood.
articles.abstract: 48,XXYY syndrome is a rare sex chromosome aneuploidy (SCA) associated with a variable profile of neurodevelopmental and medical. The limited information available in the literature is almost exclusively limited to postnatally diagnosed cases. This study aims to describe the early medical and developmental features of prenatally identified 48,XXYY infants, The eXtraordinarY Babies Study prospectively follows children prenatally identified to be at high risk for SCA with annual medical and neurodevelopmental evaluations. Data presented herein include the prevalence of medical conditions, developmental milestones, developmental and adaptive functioning assessment scores, and therapy utilization in 15 participants confirmed to have 48,XXYY. Comparisons were made with 47,XYY and 47,XXY males also enrolled in the eXtraordinarY Babies Study, the general population and a 2008 cohort of individuals postnatally identified 48,XXYY. Infants and young chlidren with 48,XXYY exhibited a range of early medical features, including elevated rates of feeding and GI disorders (breastfeeding difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux, and eosinophilic esophagitis), allergic disorders (food allergies and environmental allergies), and hypotonia. Developmental and adaptive functioning scores identified variable delays in motor, communication, and social domains, with nearly all infants receiving speech therapy, physical and/or occupational therapy due to delays or proactive developmental care. Medical and developmental findings were more prevalent in 48,XXYY compared to the 47,XYY and 47,XXY cohorts, although considerable individual variability and overlap in developmental functioning were observed across groups. Compared to the 2008 postnatally identified 48,XXYY cohort, infants identified prenatally received earlier intervention services, and developmental outcomes in the first years of life were similar between the two groups. Prenatal identification of 48,XXYY provides opportunity for early developmental monitoring, anticipatory guidance, and proactive referrals for medical evaluations and intervention. These findings provide valuable insights for genetic counselors and healthcare providers, emphasizing the spectrum of medical and developmental findings and the importance of early and proactive care to support individual outcomes. Prospective study of this prenatally identified cohort will provide important data about the natural history and phenotypic variability in XXYY, as well as identification of predictors of health and developmental outcomes. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03396562.

articles.title: Design Thinking in Advance Care Planning for Emerging Adults: Enhancing Control and Customization to Support Engagement.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study examined how emerging adults with serious illness engage with advance care planning (ACP) through a design-informed lens.Background:ACP enables individuals to communicate their preferences and goals for medical care if they are unable to make decisions for themselves. Although ACP is widely recognized as critical for individuals with serious illness, engagement remains low among emerging adults (ages 18-29), a distinct developmental subgroup within the adolescent and young adult population. Traditional ACP approaches emphasize documentation and legal requirements, which may limit engagement among individuals navigating identity development, autonomy, and future-oriented life transitions.Methods: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from 39 emerging adults with oncology or hematology diagnoses who reviewed the ACP communication guide, Voicing My CHOiCES (VMC). Structured interviews assessed participant perspectives on usability, preferences, and emotional responses. Data were explored using thematic content analysis.Results:Two central themes emerged: (1) affording choice and control and (2) designing for customization and usability. Participants valued opportunities for personalization, structured guidance, and revisable formats. Design elements that supported autonomy, reduced cognitive burden, and facilitated reflection were associated with more positive experiences of engagement, while overly rigid features constrained expression.Discussion: Across themes, ACP engagement with emerging adults was closely tied to how the VMC tool structured interaction. Design features that enabled choice, reduced complexity, and allowed for iterative engagement were associated with more positive experiences. This suggests that designing ACP as a flexible, user-centered, developmentally tailored process may better support meaningful participation.

articles.title: Feasibility of implementing a digital peer-support intervention aimed at reducing HIV-related stigma among adolescents and young adults living with HIV in south Ethiopia.
articles.abstract: Adolescents and young adults living with HIV (AYLHIV) experience a high burden of HIV-related stigma, but there are limited data on the interventions needed to reduce stigma. We assessed the feasibility of a planned Telegram-based peer-support intervention to reduce HIV-related stigma among AYLHIV in south Ethiopia. Eighteen AYLHIV (15-22 years old) were recruited from three public hospitals. The nine-week intervention was delivered via Telegram Messenger following an initial digital skill orientation, irrespective of prior experience of using the mobile application. In a mixed-methods design, we collected data using semi-structured face-to-face interviews and focus group discussions and reported feasibility outcomes using Bowen et al.'s framework. Participants described the discussion platform as private, safe, and supportive, with a family-like atmosphere. Retention was high (94.4%) and the overall scheduled-session attendance rate was 67.6%. Participants exchanged 4,033 messages, with an average of 13 messages per participant per session. Contextual, operational, and technical barriers may have reduced engagement; participants also provided recommendations to improve future intervention. Overall, the Telegram Messenger-based digital peer-support intervention appears feasible and acceptable across key feasibility domains, supporting progression to an evaluation of intervention effectiveness.Abbreviations: AYLHIV: adolescents and young adults living with HIV; ART: antiretroviral therapy; ARV: antiretroviral; EAT: East Africa Time; GB: gigabyte(s); HIV: human immunodeficiency virus; IT: information technology; mHealth: mobile health; MRC: Medical Research Council; SD: standard deviation.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for the Diagnosis and Monitoring of Takayasu Arteritis in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Imaging evidence of vasculitis is mandatory for classification of Takayasu arteritis (TA) in children, yet the ability of a negative study to exclude the diagnosis has not been evaluated. We aimed to determine the negative predictive value (NPV) of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for excluding TA in children, to describe the imaging phenotype at diagnosis, and to characterise interval change on serial imaging.
METHODS: This retrospective study included all children who underwent CMR for suspected or established large vessel vasculitis at a single tertiary centre between May 2018 and November 2025. The protocol comprised contrast-enhanced angiography, 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) imaging, black-blood imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of vessel walls. TA was classified by the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES paediatric criteria. A true negative was defined as a negative baseline CMR with no emergence of TA over at least 6 months of documented follow-up. Interval change on serial CMR was classified per scan pair as improved, unchanged or worsened, recording wall findings (thickening, LGE) and luminal findings (stenosis, dilation) separately, by two readers.
RESULTS: 161 children underwent 222 CMR studies. Of 156 initial diagnostic studies, 10 (6%) showed TA and 146 were negative. No child with a negative baseline CMR developed TA during a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR 2.1 to 4.7), corresponding to an observed NPV of 100% (95% CI 97.5 to 100). Positive initial studies were characterised by aortic wall thickening and LGE in 7 of 10 children (70%), these were concordant in every child; extra-aortic involvement was present in 7 (70%). Fifteen children with TA underwent serial CMR (51 interval comparisons; inter-reader agreement 90%, weighted κ 0.86, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.96): 11 intervals (22%) showed improvement, 20 (39%) no change and 20 (39%) worsening. Two children had a previously undescribed imaging finding of focal 3D bSSFP signal abnormalities at sites of disease, consistent with a local susceptibility effect that improved or resolved with treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: In a tertiary referral population, no child with a negative CMR developed TA during follow-up. Serial CMR detected interval change with high agreement between readers. These findings support CMR as a reliable investigation for both the exclusion and longitudinal monitoring of TA in children.

articles.title: Drug Development in Pediatric Heart Failure: Current Landscape and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Pediatric heart failure (HF) remains an important area of unmet medical need. Pharmacological treatments primarily consist of adult drugs used off label in children. HF regulatory guidance specific to pediatric drug development is limited. The diversity in underlying pathophysiology necessitates a shift toward a mechanism-of-action driven approach. We examine the current landscape of pediatric HF, identify key challenges and opportunities for drug development, and discuss a paradigm shift to a new high-level HF phenotype classification system for pediatric HF. Pediatric extrapolation utilizing pharmacokinetics and bridging biomarkers, especially given the absence of validated surrogate endpoints, remains a promising strategy for subsets of pediatric HF physiology. Ongoing reorganization of pediatric regulatory frameworks presents a key opportunity to promote harmonization between pediatric requirements from regulatory agencies across jurisdictions. We describe innovation in pediatric HF treatment through use of extrapolation, bridging biomarkers, and adaptive trial design.

articles.title: Adverse childhood experiences, social isolation and loneliness across adulthood: A nationwide cross-sectional study of Chinese adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loneliness and social isolation are distinct risk factors for depression and other affective disorders but are often conflated. Whether adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) relate differently to the two, and whether this varies across adulthood, is unclear.
METHODS: We analysed 24,219 adults from the nationwide 2024 Psychology and Behaviour Investigation of Chinese Residents. Seven ACE domains were assessed with items adapted from the WHO ACE-IQ. Social isolation (three-item structural index, score ≥ 2) and loneliness (two-item functional index, score 2) were defined using indices adapted from the UK Biobank. Adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated by modified Poisson regression with city-clustered standard errors; a stacked model compared the two outcomes.
RESULTS: Social isolation (30.0%) and loneliness (11.0%) overlapped weakly (kappa 0.17). Each additional ACE was associated with higher prevalence of loneliness (PR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20-1.28) and, more weakly, isolation (PR 1.04, 1.01-1.08; ratio of PRs 1.19, 1.17-1.22). All seven domains were associated with loneliness; only emotional abuse, witnessed violence and, marginally, physical abuse were associated with isolation; sexual abuse, household substance use, household mental illness and parental incarceration were not. The association of ≥4 ACEs with loneliness strengthened with age (P for interaction <0.001; PR 2.71, 1.98-3.72, at ≥60 years).
LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design and retrospectively self-reported ACEs preclude causal inference.
CONCLUSIONS: ACEs were more strongly associated with loneliness than with social isolation, particularly in later life. Among adults with ACE histories, asking about loneliness may capture disconnection that structural indicators such as living arrangements or contact frequency miss.

articles.title: Automating the Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 in the Electronic Health Record: Automated Risk Scoring Using Structured Clinical Documentation.
articles.abstract: Background The Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 (PIM3) is a validated severity-of-illness score widely used for risk adjustment, benchmarking, quality improvement initiatives, and research in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs). Its use in electronic workflows is limited by required variables that rely on clinical judgement and are traditionally abstracted manually from narrative documentation. Objectives To design, implement, and evaluate an automated PIM3 calculation within the electronic health record (EHR) using structured clinical documentation to capture non-discrete variables, and to assess clinician adoption, documentation accuracy, and concordance with manual abstraction. Methods A structured documentation template with standardized response options was developed to capture non-discrete PIM3 variables, including ventilation status, elective admission status, procedural recovery, and diagnosis category. These clinician-entered data were mapped to discrete structured data elements and combined with physiologic and laboratory inputs for automated score calculation. Documentation completion and accuracy were evaluated over a 12-month period. Automated scores were validated against manually abstracted gold standard PIM3 scores in a convenience sample of 20 targeted encounters. Results Among 923 PICU encounters, clinician compliance with structured PIM3 documentation was 95% (n=877). Of the completed entries, 84% (n=773) contained no documentation errors. Identified errors were primarily related to binary clinical judgements rather than diagnostic clarification. Of the 20 encounter validation sample, automated PIM3 scores and associated probabilities of death demonstrated near-complete concordance with manually calculated gold standard values, with no clinically meaningful discrepancies. Conclusion Automated PIM3 calculation using structured clinical documentation within the EHR is feasible and reliable for supporting standardized data capture and timely availability of risk-adjustment information. This approach reduces reliance on manual abstraction and provides a scalable informatics framework for quality improvement, benchmarking, and research in pediatric critical care.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Alabama Perinatal Quality Collaborative Postpartum Bracelet Pilot.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of a pilot project implementing postpartum alert bracelets to support the timely identification and treatment of maternal complications.
DESIGN: Program evaluation.
SETTING/LOCAL PROBLEM: Seven urban, regional, and community hospitals in Alabama participating in the Alabama Perinatal Quality Collaborative. Inconsistent recognition of recent childbirth status in emergency settings and limited retention of discharge education can delay diagnosis and treatment.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients who recently gave birth (n = 1,237), Mother-baby unit (MBU) nurse leaders (n = 10), emergency department (ED) nurses (n = 35), and emergency medical technicians (EMTs; n = 79).
INTERVENTIONS/MEASUREMENTS: The intervention included distribution of silicone postpartum alert bracelets designed for continuous wear, standardized patient education, and staff awareness efforts. Surveys assessed patient acceptance and perceived safety and ED nurses' and EMTs' awareness and perceived utility. Semistructured interviews explored nurse leaders' implementation experiences.
RESULTS: Patient acceptance was high (81.3% would wear; 79.9% felt safer). Compared with non-Hispanic White respondents, non-Hispanic Black respondents (odds ratio [OR] = 2.05, 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.67, 2.43]) and Hispanic respondents (OR = 2.23, 95% CI [1.78, 2.68]) were more likely to report willingness to wear the bracelet and perceived safety benefits. Awareness was 100% among MBU nurse leaders, 40% among ED nurses, and 19% among EMTs. However, both ED nurses and EMTs agreed that the bracelets could support timely recognition of complications and potentially reduce maternal mortalities.
CONCLUSION: Postpartum alert bracelets are a promising, low-cost intervention highly accepted by patients. Statewide implementation requires standardized distribution and targeted education for patients, ED staff, and emergency medical services.

articles.title: Infant mortality due to congenital heart disease in Brazil: a nationwide study of regional inequality and diagnostic imprecision, 2010-2024.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of congenital anomaly-related deaths. In Brazil, a country marked by heterogeneous access to specialized care, mortality due to CHD may reflect disease severity and regional differences in diagnosis, screening, and treatment.
METHODS: The authors characterized temporal trends, regional and federative-unit patterns of CHD-related infant mortality in Brazil from 2010 to 2024 using data from the Mortality Information System (SIM) and Live Birth Information System (SINASC). The primary case definition was restricted to ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Temporal trends were evaluated via Prais-Winsten regression and linear regression with Newey-West standard errors to calculate the Annual Percent Change (APC) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, Brazil recorded 45,543 CHD deaths in children under one year (108.3 deaths per 100,000 live births). The Central-West and the Southeast had the highest and the lowest regional rates (125.70 and 104.38 per 100,000). National mortality notification increased (APC was 0.623%; 95% CI: 0.201 - 1.047; p = 0.012), with significant increases in the North (APC, 2.363%; p < 0.001) and Northeast (APC, 0.994%; p = 0.007), while other regions remained stationary. Over half of the deaths occurred in the neonatal period (52.8%).
CONCLUSION: Infant mortality notification due to CHD in Brazil increased from 2010 to 2024, showing marked regional inequalities. Rising trends in the North and Northeast and the high proportion of post-neonatal deaths suggest that delayed diagnosis, referral limitations, continuity-of-care gaps, and diagnostic imprecision in death certification influence preventable mortality.

articles.title: Postoperative Sleep Quality in Children: Development and Psychometric Evaluation of a Questionnaire.
articles.abstract: Sleep in the immediate postoperative period is influenced by multiple perioperative factors. A key limitation in current research and clinical practice is the lack of brief, psychometrically robust instruments specifically designed to assess postoperative sleep. The aim of this study is to evaluate the psychometric properties of a short questionnaire assessing postoperative sleep quality in children and adolescents. The questionnaire was developed based on a literature review and 48 semi-structured interviews. This is a retrospective analysis. Out of 685 postoperative paediatric patients included across three studies (Study 1: n = 120; age: 14.7 ± 1.9 years, female: 43%; Study 2: n = 249; age: median 5.5, IQR: 4.5-6.5, female: 44%; Study 3: n = 312; age: median 12.0, IQR: 9.3-14.0, female: 38%), 88.5% (n = 609) could be included in the final analysis. Item response theory analysis was used to analyse factorial structure, reliability and measurement invariance (differential item functioning-DIF). A two-factor structure was identified: F1: Pain related impaired sleep quality and F2: General sleep quality with three items loading high on each factor could be identified (RMSEA: 0.01, 90% CI: < 0.01 to 0.06; CFI: 0.997, TLI: 0.996). Reliability was good (< 0.8) for relevant sleep quality ranges. No relevant DIF was observed with respect to sex or response mode. The Post-operative Sleep Questionnaire for children (Po-S-C) is a new short questionnaire for assessing postoperative sleep quality in children and adolescents showing good reliability and no measurement invariance. Further studies are needed to replicate these results in other samples.

articles.title: "I hardly fall asleep because I keep thinking about my child": Psychosocial experiences of caregivers of children admitted to Mercy James Centre Paediatric Intensive Care Unit, Malawi.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Admission of a child to a paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) is highly distressing for caregivers, who face uncertainty about the child's outcome and disruption of normal caregiving roles. In low-resource settings such as Malawi, where psychosocial support is limited, little is known about caregivers' experiences during their child's PICU admission.
OBJECTIVES: This study explored psychosocial experiences, coping mechanisms and support needs of caregivers of children admitted to Mercy James PICU in Malawi.
METHODS: A qualitative exploratory-descriptive study was conducted between October and December 2024 at Mercy James PICU within Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, Blantyre. Eleven caregivers of children admitted for over 48 h were purposively sampled for in-depth, semi-structured interviews, which were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated and analysed thematically. The transactional theory of stress and coping guided interpretation of findings.
RESULTS: Four themes were identified: emotional and psychological distress, caregivers' perceptions of care delivery, coping mechanisms and perceived support needs. Caregivers experienced both immediate and ongoing distress associated with sudden PICU admission, uncertainty, separation from family and financial strain. Perceptions of care were shaped by interactions with staff and hospital environment. Caregivers used both problem-focused strategies, like information seeking, and emotion-focused strategies like reliance on God, social support and acceptance. They reported unmet needs for psychological support, compassionate care and access to food.
CONCLUSION: Caregivers of children in PICU experience significant psychosocial challenges shaped by admission context, environment and limited support. Strengthening communication and information-sharing practices, compassionate care, structured emotional support and addressing basic needs is essential.

articles.title: FcRn beyond IgG recycling in systemic lupus erythematosus.
articles.abstract: In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), in which autoantibody titers alone do not account for disease activity, the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) links their persistence in the circulation to the routing of immune complexes (ICs) and antigen presentation. The recycling of monomeric IgG maintains the pool available to form these complexes, whereas their multivalency engages FcRn in pathways that direct their degradation and the presentation of their autoantigens. It is not the functions themselves, but the cell type in which they operate, that shapes their consequences. This cell dependence results in distinct effects, from the placental transfer of anti-SSA/Ro antibodies to renal clearance or inflammatory functions. Extracellular signals and intracellular mechanisms can locally modulate FcRn expression. Early therapeutic data provide clinical proof of concept in SLE, but the inhibitors evaluated primarily target IgG recycling and transport, without directly elucidating the intracellular handling of ICs. Linking local FcRn expression to IC fate should clarify its contribution to lupus manifestations and the scope of its therapeutic blockade.

articles.title: The Effect of Care Team Composition on Healthcare Resource Use Among Rural Children Enrolled in Hospice.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the effect of care team composition on healthcare resource use among rural children enrolled in hospice during the last year of life.MethodsThe sample included 3131 children aged 20 years or younger who received concurrent hospice care, resided in rural communities in 28 Midwestern and Southern states, and were enrolled in Medicaid between 2011 and 2022. Analyses used multivariable logistic and Poisson regression models adjusted for demographic, health, and community characteristics and year of data collection.ResultsChildren had a mean age of 10.1 years (SD = 7.1); 42.1% received care from a medical subspecialist, 52.5% from a primary care provider, and the mean care team size was 9.1 providers (SD = 17.0). Multiple hospital admissions occurred in 80.3% of children, multiple ED visits in 40.4%, and children averaged 1.2 duplicate medications (SD = 0.90). Subspecialist involvement was associated with lower resource use: 69% lower odds of multiple admissions, 83% lower odds of multiple ED visits, and a 37% lower rate of duplicate medications. In contrast, primary care involvement and larger care team size were associated with significantly greater resource use, particularly ED visits and medication utilization.ConclusionCare team composition was significantly associated with healthcare use among rural children enrolled in hospice. Future research should examine the specific mechanisms through which care team composition influences healthcare use.

articles.title: Precannulation Risk Factors Associated With Hemorrhagic Events During Respiratory Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Children: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic complications are frequent and clinically significant during pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), yet associated precannulation factors remain poorly defined. We evaluated these factors in a multicenter retrospective cohort of children receiving respiratory ECMO at four Colombian centers during 2018-2022. A total of 106 children were included; 53 (50.0%) developed at least one hemorrhagic complication during ECMO support, and 83% of events occurred within the first 7 days after cannulation. Cannulation-site bleeding was most frequent (41.5%), followed by intracranial hemorrhage (22.6%) and pulmonary hemorrhage (17.0%). In bias-reduced adjusted analyses, higher precannulation lactate concentrations, lower bicarbonate levels, previous severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, adenovirus infection at admission, and longer mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support before ECMO remained associated with bleeding. Patients who developed hemorrhagic complications had higher 28 day mortality than those without bleeding (39.6% vs. 13.2%; p = 0.002). When bleeding was modeled as a time-dependent exposure, hemorrhagic events were associated with a higher subsequent hazard of 28 day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 4.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.09-11.64). Hemorrhagic complications affected half of children receiving respiratory ECMO, occurred predominantly during the first week, and were associated with increased mortality. Several precannulation characteristics remained associated with bleeding in bias-reduced adjusted analyses. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Rescue of glutaric aciduria type I by GalNAc-conjugated siRNA against aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase.
articles.abstract: Glutaric aciduria type I (GA-1) is a severe metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency of glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase (GCDH), leading to accumulation of organic acids in the brain and resulting in striatal injury and progressive movement disorders. Although early diagnosis and dietary management reduce risk, one-third of patients still develop debilitating neurological complications. We previously demonstrated that liver-specific deletion of aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase (AASS), an upstream enzyme in lysine degradation, is a promising therapeutic strategy. Here, we tested an N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated siRNA against Aass. Treatment of neonatal Gcdh-/- mice rescued lethality and improved the brain pathology while reducing toxic metabolites in the brain and other organs. Serum biomarkers, including glutaric acid, 3-hydroxyglutaric acid, and glutarylcarnitine, predicted neurological outcomes, supporting their use for therapeutic monitoring. Although systemic metabolite concentrations declined, their urinary excretion remained elevated, consistent with a renal washout phenomenon and preserved excretory capacity. These findings demonstrate the potential of liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapy as a treatment for GA-1.

articles.title: Hybrid Closed-Loop Use Mediates the Relationship Between Social Determinants of Health and Glycemic Outcomes in a Canadian Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Clinic.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sociodemographic disparities continue to impact people living with type 1 diabetes (T1D), despite advances like hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems, which improve glycemic outcomes and quality of life. This study evaluated whether HCL system use mediates the relationship between social determinants of health (SDH) and glycemic outcomes in children living with T1D (CLWT1D).
METHOD: A retrospective chart review included CLWT1D followed at the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario between May 2023 and May 2024. Demographics, management, and glycemic outcomes (hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and percent time in range (%TIR)) were collected. SDH were measured using the Canadian Index of Multiple Deprivation, which categorizes individuals into quintiles (Q1= least to Q5= most deprived) across four dimensions using postal codes. Regression models examined mediation effects.
RESULTS: Data from 581 children (mean age 13.4±3.8 years; 46.6% female; mean T1D duration 6.1±3.8 years; mean HbA1c 8.0±1.5%) were analyzed. Of these, 46% used HCL systems, while 54% used injections or stand-alone pumps. HbA1c was associated with situational vulnerability (p<0.001) and residential instability (p<0.001), with HCL system use significantly mediating differences in HbA1c between Q1-4 vs Q5. No mediation effect was found for economic dependency or ethnocultural composition. %TIR results were consistent with HbA1c findings.
CONCLUSION: HCL system use mediated the relationship between glycemic outcomes and residential instability and situational vulnerability, but not economic dependency or ethnocultural composition. Access to HCL systems may mitigate health inequities in CLWT1D; however, technology alone does not eliminate these disparities, and parallel interventions are needed to promote equitable care.

articles.title: Child abuse and mental health outcomes in Canada: A population-based study with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity: Violence faite aux enfants et résultats en matière de santé mentale au Canada : étude fondée sur la population axée sur le sexe à la naissance et l'identité sexuelle.
articles.abstract: BackgroundContemporary nationally representative Canadian statistics on child abuse and mental health outcomes with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity are essential in determining approaches to prevention and the need for services. The objectives of the current study were to examine the relationship between experiences of abuse during childhood (physical, sexual, exposure to intimate partner violence, and any) and past-year mental health conditions (depression, generalized anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder, social phobia, and suicidal ideation) among adult Canadians, and whether these relationships are moderated by sex at birth and sexual identity.MethodsData were obtained from the cross-sectional 2022 Statistics Canada Mental Health and Access to Care Survey (2022; n = 9,409; 18+ years).FindingsAny child abuse history and each individual child abuse type were associated with an increased likelihood of all poor mental health indicators in the sample after adjusting for sociodemographic covariates (Adjusted Odds Ratio ranging from 1.66 to 4.67). Generally, an increasing dose-response trend was noted for increasing counts of child abuse types (multitype abuse) experienced and increased odds of poor mental health indicators. Sex at birth and sexual identity moderated models for both child abuse and depression and child abuse and social phobia, with stronger associations for females compared to males and for some sexual identities other than heterosexual.InterpretationThe current study provides updated nationally representative data on child abuse history and mental health indicators among adults in Canada. The development and evaluation of child abuse prevention strategies must remain a priority in reducing violence against children and mental health problems among Canadians. Sex at birth and sexual identity differences highlight the need for policies and practices to address the unique needs of women and individuals identifying as lesbian/gay, bisexual, and other nonheterosexual identities.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate in Paediatric Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Assessed by Physicians and School Teachers: A Post-marketing Surveillance Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lisdexamfetamine dimesylate (LDX) is a long-acting prodrug approved for the treatment of paediatric attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in Japan. This multicentre, prospective, post-marketing surveillance study evaluated real-world safety and effectiveness of LDX in children and adolescents with ADHD in Japan.
METHODS: Patients aged 6 to < 18 years initiating LDX between April 2021 and September 2023 were enrolled across 24 medical institutions in Japan. Safety was assessed over 24 weeks by monitoring adverse drug reactions (ADRs), including dependence/abuse events. Effectiveness was evaluated by physicians and school teachers at baseline, and weeks 12 and 24 using the Japanese ADHD rating scale IV (ADHD-RS-IV) questionnaire.
RESULTS: Of the 88 enrolled patients, 73 were included in the safety analysis and 57 in the effectiveness analysis. The mean (standard deviation [SD]) age was 10.4 (2.6) years; 79.5% were male and 20.5% were female. Most patients (90.4%) had received prior ADHD treatment. LDX was initiated at a mean (SD) dose of 26.8 (4.7) mg, with 72.6% continuing treatment at week 24. ADRs occurred in 30.14% of patients; the most common (in ≥ 2 patients) were decreased appetite (17.81%), weight decrease (4.11%), and aggression, insomnia, irritability, middle insomnia, and abdominal pain (each 2.74%). One serious ADR (suicide attempt with methylphenidate overdose, also considered a dependence/abuse event) was reported; LDX was discontinued and the patient recovered the following day. No other dependence/abuse events were reported. Physician- and teacher-rated ADHD-RS-IV total scores improved significantly from baseline: mean (SD) changes were - 10.1 (8.0; p < 0.0001) at week 12 and - 9.7 (8.5; p < 0.0001) at week 24 for physician-rated scores, and - 4.9 (8.5; p < 0.001) at week 12 and - 5.1 (9.7; p < 0.01) at week 24 for teacher-rated scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings from this post-marketing surveillance study of LDX in paediatric patients with ADHD in Japan were consistent with its established safety profile. Patients' ADHD symptoms improved according to both physician and teacher assessments.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN) Clinical Trials Registry (identifier UMIN000046038).

articles.title: Adverse Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors in Pediatric Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Proportions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become a foundational therapy for adult heart failure across the entire spectrum of ejection fraction, but their safety profile in children with heart failure has not been quantitatively synthesized. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions to summarize the incidence of adverse events associated with SGLT2 inhibitors in pediatric heart failure.
STUDY DESIGN: In this systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions (PROSPERO CRD420261355711; PRISMA 2020), five databases were searched through June 2026 for studies of any design reporting adverse events among pediatric patients receiving an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart failure. Random-effects incidence estimates were pooled using logit-transformed proportions with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals; risk of bias and GRADE certainty were assessed.
RESULTS: Ten studies (573 unique children; 2023-2026) were included; eight studies (572 patients; maximum pooled denominator 474) were meta-analyzed, and one case report was summarized narratively. Dapagliflozin accounted for 94.1% of exposures. Study-level dapagliflozin doses ranged from 0.11 to 0.23 mg/kg/day, while the single cohort reporting empagliflozin used a median dose of 0.13 mg/kg/day. No regimen was derived from pediatric heart-failure pharmacokinetic data, and in the only cohort reporting a comparison, infants received a higher weight-normalized dose than older children (0.18 versus 0.16 mg/kg/day). Pooled incidences were: any adverse event 21.2% (95% CI 10.7-37.8%), acute kidney injury 10.7% (3.5-28.1%), urinary tract infection 7.8% (4.8-12.4%), treatment discontinuation 7.0% (4.5-10.6%), all-cause mortality 5.6% (2.4-12.5%), hypoglycemia 2.9% (0.9-9.3%), genital mycotic infection 2.7% (0.9-8.2%), and diabetic ketoacidosis 1.3% (0.4-3.9%). No deaths were attributed to therapy, and no cases of euglycemic ketoacidosis or Fournier gangrene occurred. Directional efficacy signals were consistently favorable, with left ventricular ejection fraction improving in five of six cohorts and natriuretic peptide levels declining across all seven in which they were assessed.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors had a tolerable safety profile in pediatric heart failure, mirroring the adult experience. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized adverse-event grading are needed.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420261355711.

articles.title: Urinary exosomal C5b-9 as a non-invasive biomarker for diagnosis and monitoring of pediatric IgA nephropathy: a single-center prospective study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This exploratory study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and predictive value of urinary exosomal C5b-9 in children with IgA nephropathy (IgAN). A total of 70 children with biopsy-proven IgAN, 43 with non-IgAN glomerulopathies, and 30 healthy controls were enrolled. Urinary exosomal C5b-9 levels were measured at baseline and at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after renal biopsy. The diagnostic performance of baseline C5b-9 was assessed using ROC curve analysis. Multivariate logistic regression models were constructed to evaluate its independent association with 12-week remission. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using a repeated-measures mixed-effects model, and the predictive value of the early decline rate was assessed by ROC analysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression were also performed. Baseline urinary exosomal C5b-9 levels were significantly higher in IgAN patients compared with non-IgAN patients and healthy controls (both p < 0.01). The area under the curve (AUC) for distinguishing IgAN from non-IgAN was 0.942, with an optimal cutoff of 227.36 ng/mL (sensitivity, 92.9%; specificity, 83.7%). The optimal cutoff for predicting 12-week non-remission was 287.90 ng/mL (AUC = 0.819; sensitivity, 75.7%; specificity, 71.9%). Low baseline C5b-9 (< 287.90 ng/mL) was associated with significantly higher cumulative remission rates (log-rank p < 0.01). Across three multivariate models, baseline C5b-9 remained independently associated with 12-week remission (OR range, 0.599-0.623, all p < 0.01). Longitudinal analysis revealed a significant time × group interaction (p = 0.002), indicating greater C5b-9 decline in remitted patients. The early decline rate (> 8.15% reduction by week 4) predicted remission with an AUC of 0.754 (sensitivity, 63.9%; specificity, 84.4%). Combination therapy showed a trend toward faster remission (HR = 1.856, p = 0.056).
CONCLUSION: Urinary exosomal C5b-9 may have potential as a non-invasive biomarker for diagnosing IgAN and predicting early treatment response in children. These exploratory findings suggest clinical utility and require external validation in larger cohorts.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • IgAN is the most common childhood glomerulonephritis; diagnosis needs invasive biopsy. Complement activation (C5b-9 deposition) is involved. • Whole-urine C5b-9 has given inconsistent results, limiting its clinical use.
WHAT IS NEW: • Urinary exosomal C5b-9 may offer a stable, kidney-specific option. This pediatric study explored its potential in IgAN. • Urinary exosomal C5b-9 helped distinguish IgAN from other glomerulopathies (AUC = 0.942). Levels were linked to 12-week remission. An early decline by week 4 predicted later remission with 84.4% specificity.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and diagnostic challenges of Kawasaki disease in infants younger than 3 months: a 21-year single-center retrospective study from China.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) in infants younger than 3 months is uncommon but poses substantial diagnostic challenges because classical clinical manifestations are frequently incomplete during the early phase of illness. Delayed diagnosis increases the risk of coronary artery abnormalities (CAA), yet the clinical characteristics and diagnostic evolution of this age group remain insufficiently understood. We retrospectively reviewed all infants younger than 3 months diagnosed with KD at Peking University First Hospital between January 2005 and January 2026. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, echocardiographic features, treatment, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed. Particular attention was paid to the temporal evolution of clinical manifestations and coronary artery abnormalities during the diagnostic process. Fifteen infants were included in the study. Incomplete KD accounted for 86.7% (13/15) of cases. Gastrointestinal manifestations (53.3%), bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) scar reactivation (60.0%), and respiratory symptoms (40.0%) were common and frequently resulted in an initial diagnosis of infection. Coronary artery abnormalities developed in ten patients during the disease course. Three infants had normal initial echocardiographic examinations but subsequently developed coronary artery abnormalities on repeat evaluation between fever days 7 and 10. Fourteen patients responded to initial intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment, whereas one patient was IVIG-resistant. Coronary artery abnormalities and other cardiac echocardiographic involvement resolved in all patients during follow-up.Conclusion: KD in infants younger than 3 months is characterized by an evolving clinical presentation in which classical clinical manifestations and echocardiographically detectable coronary artery abnormalities emerge sequentially rather than simultaneously. Recognition of this evolving diagnostic process may facilitate earlier diagnosis. Persistent clinical suspicion, together with longitudinal clinical reassessment and appropriately timed repeat echocardiography, may improve recognition before clinically significant coronary injury develops.

articles.title: Latent tuberculosis infection conversion and TST-IGRA agreement in BCG-vaccinated children with rheumatic diseases receiving biologic therapy: a 10-year single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To assess agreement between the tuberculin skin test (TST) and QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube (QFT-GIT) assay and describe latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) screening conversion during biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs). This 10-year retrospective cohort included children receiving bDMARDs. Baseline screening comprised TST and/or QFT-GIT and chest radiography, with follow-up testing as available. TST positivity was defined as ≥ 5-mm. Agreement and paired TST positivity were assessed using Cohen's kappa, and McNemar's test, respectively. Among 106 patients (49.1% female), median age at bDMARD initiation was 11.6 years. New LTBI screening positivity occurred in 14/87 (16.1%) with no positive baseline result. Overall, 31 (29.2%) received isoniazid, 19 before bDMARD and 12 during follow-up. TST-QFT-GIT agreement was moderate at baseline (n = 90; κ = 0.472) and fair at follow-up (n = 76; κ = 0.213). Paired TST positivity increased from 8.8% to 20.0% (n = 80; p = 0.012). New QFT-GIT positivity occurred in 6/74 patients (8.1%) with negative or indeterminate baseline results. Of 14 conversions, two were detected by both tests, eight by TST only, and four by QFT-GIT only. Conversion occurred with both tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors and non-TNF biologics, without significant between-group differences. No active tuberculosis developed during available follow-up.
CONCLUSION: New LTBI screening positivity occurred after initiation of both biologic classes in BCG-vaccinated children. Agreement between TST and QFT-GIT was moderate at baseline and fair at first follow-up. The clinical significance of isolated TST conversion remains uncertain and requires interpretation in the context of BCG vaccination, prior tuberculin testing and TB exposure risk.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children receiving biologic therapy require LTBI screening because of risk of active tuberculosis. • BCG vaccination, immunosuppression, and the absence of gold standard complicate interpretation of TST and IGRA results.
WHAT IS NEW: • Agreement between TST and QFT-GIT was moderate at baseline and fair at follow-up, the clinical significance of isolated TST conversion remains uncertain. • New LTBI screening positivity was documented during follow-up, after initiation of both anti-TNF and non-anti-TNF biologic agents.

articles.title: Image quality and procedural safety in neonatal brain MRI with and without sedation.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neontal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is susceptible to motion artefacts, whereas pharmacological sedation or anaesthesia may cause cardiorespiratory adverse events. We compared image quality and adverse events across three MRI strategies in newborns: natural sleep without sedation, pharmacological sedation, and imaging during mechanical ventilation. We retrospectively analysed 151 brain MRI examinations performed in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between August 2013 and August 2024. Examinations were classified as non-sedated using a feed-and-swaddle approach (n = 21), pharmacologically sedated without intubation (n = 67), or performed in intubated and mechanically ventilated infants (n = 63). Motion artefacts and documented adverse events were compared between groups. Motion artefacts were more frequent in non-sedated examinations than in sedated or intubated examinations (85.7% vs. 32.8% and 25.4%, respectively; p < 0.001). Moderate/severe artefacts occurred in 14.3%, 7.5%, and 0%, respectively. No adverse events were documented in the non-sedated group, compared with 8/67 (11.9%) in sedated and 7/63 (11.1%) in intubated infants; this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.275). Within the sedated cohort, artefacts were more frequent with chloral hydrate, whereas respiratory complications occurred predominantly with propofol-based sedation.
CONCLUSION: Neonatal MRI strategies involve a clinically relevant trade-off between image quality and procedural safety. Natural-sleep MRI avoids pharmacological exposure and was not associated with documented adverse events but resulted in more motion artefacts. MRI strategies should therefore be individualized according to clinical condition and required diagnostic image quality.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Motion artefacts may compromise neonatal MRI, and pharmacological sedation or anaesthesia is frequently used to improve image quality. • Feed-and-swaddle MRI can avoid drug exposure, while sedative and anaesthetic agents may cause respiratory and haemodynamic adverse events.
WHAT IS NEW: • Direct comparison of three real-world neonatal MRI strategies demonstrates a trade-off between image quality and procedural safety: sedation and controlled ventilation reduced motion artefacts, whereas no adverse events were documented during natural-sleep MRI. • Exploratory analyses suggest differences between sedation regimens, with more artefacts after chloral hydrate and respiratory events occurring predominantly with propofol-based sedation.

articles.title: Patients with Congenital Heart Disease have Inferior Intent-to-Treat Outcomes When Listed for Pediatric Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract: While the impact of patient characteristics on waitlist and post-transplant mortality in pediatric heart transplantation has been widely studied, these metrics are limited in their ability to provide a complete picture for patients and their families. In contrast, less prevalent in the literature is an intent-to-treat analysis approach, which provides a single data point that encompasses both of these measures. This retrospective study examines pediatric patients listed for heart transplantation in the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database between 2016 and 2025, evaluating the impact of transplant indication on intent-to-treat outcomes following the implementation of the 2016 allocation policy, which prioritizes children with congenital heart disease (CHD) on inotropic support. Kaplan-Meier analysis by transplant indication was performed across all pediatric patients listed during the study period, followed by Cox regression analyses using clinical and demographic covariates. In this initial analysis, CHD patients had poorer intent-to-treat outcomes. Risk and protective factors in this particularly high-risk population were then identified using univariable Cox regression. Significant factors (p < 0.05) were entered into a multivariable Cox regression, which was used to generate a predictive score for one-year intent-to-treat mortality (c-statistic = 0.74). Risk factors significant in the multivariable analysis were age 0-1 years, geographic region, public (rather than private) insurance, need for life support and/or hemodialysis, and low serum albumin level. Following external validation and study of transplant timing on outcomes, these findings may serve as an additional tool to identify and prioritize high-risk patients and target modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: Abbreviated brain magnetic resonance imaging protocol using fluid-attenuated inversion recovery and diffusion-weighted imaging in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocols may reduce radiation exposure and sedation requirements in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical adequacy of an abbreviated brain MRI (abMRI) protocol featuring fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included pediatric emergency department patients who underwent abMRI between July 2023 and July 2025. The protocol consisted of axial diffusion-weighted imaging and axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery obtained with motion-resistant radial filling, with an acquisition time of approximately 220 s. Technical success and clinical adequacy were evaluated using image quality, emergency observation, pediatric neurology follow-up, and full-protocol MRI when clinically indicated.
RESULTS: Among 971 attempted examinations, diagnostic-quality images were obtained in 951, yielding a technical success rate of 97.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 96.8-98.7%). The mean age was 7.61±5.46 years, and 480 patients (50.5%) were boys. Of the 951 diagnostic examinations, 649 underwent no further neuroimaging. Full-protocol MRI was performed in 302 patients. Eight false-negative cases were identified. The overall clinical adequacy rate was 99.2% (943/951; 95% CI 98.4-99.6%). Clinically inadequate examinations were more frequent in patients with suspected intracranial hypertension (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Diffusion-weighted imaging- and motion-resistant radial FLAIR-based abMRI appears feasible and clinically adequate as an initial imaging approach for selected pediatric emergency neuroimaging indications. Full-protocol MRI remains preferable when intracranial hypertension is suspected.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Mortality in Pediatric Medical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) using extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used in pediatric refractory cardiac arrest. This study investigated the association between ECPR and mortality in pediatric patients receiving venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) for medical indications. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 28 days to <18 years who received VA-ECMO at a tertiary referral children's hospital between January 2010 and May 2025. The primary outcome was pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) mortality. Among 73 patients (non-ECPR, n = 58; ECPR, n = 15), ECPR was associated with increased mortality in unadjusted analysis (odds ratio [OR], 5.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.47-18.53; p = 0.010). After adjustment for pre-ECMO physiologic variables, the association between ECPR and mortality was no longer significant (adjusted OR, 1.74; 95% CI, 0.37-8.08; p = 0.483). Lower pre-ECMO arterial pH remained associated with higher mortality (adjusted OR, 1.87 per 0.1 decrease; 95% CI, 1.20-2.92; p = 0.006). In a sensitivity analysis, underlying cardiac disease was associated with lower mortality than noncardiac disease (adjusted OR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.07-0.79; p = 0.020). These findings highlight the associations of pre-ECMO physiologic status and underlying disease category with PICU mortality.

articles.title: Kidney involvement is associated with glucose-insulin homeostasis in adolescents with newly diagnosed anorexia nervosa: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is associated with multisystem medical complications, although kidney involvement (KI) remains an underrecognized component of the medical burden of the disease, particularly in adolescents. We aimed to characterize the spectrum of KI in adolescents with newly diagnosed AN by assessing both glomerular and tubular function and exploring clinical and metabolic correlates of renal abnormalities, including glucose-insulin homeostasis alterations. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 125 adolescents with newly diagnosed AN that underwent clinical evaluation, biochemical testing, and abdominal ultrasonography. KI was defined by the presence of reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), calculated using the modified Schwartz equation, and/or albuminuria, and/or renal tubular dysfunction. Glucose-insulin homeostasis was assessed using the Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR). The cohort (75.2% female, mean age of 13.8 ± 2.3 years) showed KI in 31.2% of patients. Both urinary β2-microglobulin and eGFR were independently associated with HOMA-IR after adjustments (both p < 0.05). Renal parameters were not significantly associated with body mass index, heart rate, or FT3 concentrations (all p > 0.05). Urinary β2-microglobulin was positively associated with HOMA-IR (R2 = 0.12, p < 0.001), whereas eGFR was inversely associated with HOMA-IR (R2 = 0.06, p = 0.006). In adjusted analyses, both urinary β2-microglobulin and eGFR remained independently associated with HOMA-IR (both p < 0.05). Renal parameters were not significantly associated with body mass index, heart rate, or FT3 concentrations (all p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: KI was identified in nearly one-third of adolescents with newly diagnosed AN and involved both glomerular and tubular compartments. The association between renal parameters and HOMA-IR, together with the absence of associations with conventional markers of disease severity, suggests that renal abnormalities may coexist with alterations in glucose-insulin homeostasis at diagnosis. Comprehensive kidney assessment at diagnosis may improve the identification of KI and support individualized clinical monitoring in adolescents with AN.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Kidney involvement is an underrecognized complication of anorexia nervosa, although pediatric data remain limited, particularly regarding tubular abnormalities. • Creatinine-based assessment may not fully capture renal alterations in adolescents with anorexia nervosa.
WHAT IS NEW: • In adolescents with newly diagnosed anorexia nervosa, kidney involvement was detectable before nutritional rehabilitation and involved both glomerular and tubular compartments.  • Renal parameters were associated with glucose-insulin homeostasis alterations, suggesting coexistence of renal and metabolic abnormalities at diagnosis.

articles.title: Severe Fetal Anemia and Pancytopenia in Maternal Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Treated with Serial Intrauterine Transfusions and Intravenous Immunoglobulin: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Severe fetal anemia with hydrops and multilineage cytopenia is rarely reported in pregnancies complicated by maternal systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We report a 33-year-old woman with SLE and maternal thrombocytopenia whose fetus developed hydrops and an MCA-PSV of 1.823 MoM at 24+6 weeks. Fetal sampling before the first intrauterine transfusion (IUT) showed hemoglobin 3.3 g/dL, hematocrit 10.5%, WBC 0.28 × 10³/µL and platelets 17 × 10³/µL. The first IUT at 25+6 weeks corrected the anemia, although profound leukopenia and thrombocytopenia were documented immediately afterward. Repeat sampling immediately before a second IUT at 28+1 weeks showed hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, WBC 0.14 × 10³/µL and platelets 26 × 10³/µL. Serial IUTs corrected fetal anemia; maternal IVIG was given empirically because of concern for an additional immune contribution, without proof of immune-mediated cell destruction or an independent IVIG effect. Fetal growth restriction and abnormal Dopplers contributed to delivery at 33+6 weeks. The neonate had normal blood counts without postnatal transfusion. This case highlights the importance of targeted evaluation for fetal anemia when concerning sonographic findings arise in SLE pregnancies.

articles.title: Omalizumab Efficacy, Drug Survival and Clinical and Serological Biomarkers in Chronic Inducible Urticaria.
articles.abstract: Chronic inducible urticaria is treated with offlabel omalizumab in antihistamine-refractory cases, although real-world evidence on its long-term efficacy, drug survival and predictive biomarkers is limited. The aim was to evaluate the real-world efficacy and long-term drug survival of omalizumab in chronic inducible urticaria and to identify clinical and serological predictors of response and persistence. This retrospective, multicentre study included 144 patients with isolated chronic inducible urticaria treated with omalizumab. At 6 months, 73% of patients achieved complete or good disease control. Solar urticaria showed a higher rate of complete control (69%), with a significantly higher rate than symptomatic dermographism (32%; p=0.0246). Most patients were fast responders (83%) and 26% required updosing. Higher body mass index was associated with lower complete control [odds ratio (OR) 0.92; p=0.049] and a greater likelihood of dose escalation (OR 1.11; p=0.019). Overall drug survival was 95%, 87.5% and 72.4% at 1, 2 and 5 years, respectively. Discontinuation occurred in 33% of patients, primarily due to remission (50%). Exploratory analyses did not identify robust predictors of cause-specific discontinuation. In conclusion, omalizumab is effective and well tolerated in chronic inducible urticaria, providing sustained control and long-term drug survival; however, baseline clinical and serum biomarkers did not predict treatment response or drug survival.

articles.title: Opioid Prescribing Calibration, Consumption, and Disposal After Posterior Spinal Fusion for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: A 7-year Institutional Stewardship Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathways have reduced inpatient opioid exposure after posterior spinal fusion (PSF) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), yet the discharge prescription has received far less scrutiny. Temporal trends in prescription size, caregiver-reported consumption, and household disposal of unused medication remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 321 patients aged 10 to 20 years undergoing primary PSF for AIS from 2018 to 19 through 2024 to 25 at a single tertiary pediatric hospital. Prescribing among 275 patients discharged with tablets was modeled with multivariable linear regression. Caregiver-reported pill counts from a postoperative survey (consumption cohort, n=79; telephone era, n=36; text-message era, n=43) informed consumption and waste analyses; disposal and home pain-management items came from all respondents (n=91 to 115 per item). Sensitivity analyses addressed pathway timing, survey modality, response bias, and missing pill counts among families still taking opioids.
RESULTS: Median tablets prescribed declined 67%, from 55 to 18 (adjusted β=-4.91 tablets/year; 95% CI, -5.53 to -4.29; P<0.001), beginning before the most recent ERAS pathway. Reported consumption declined from a median of 30 to 7 tablets, but this decline could not be separated from the survey modality change (telephone era only, P=0.69). The median unused proportion rose from 10% to 40% (unadjusted β=+4.6 percentage points/year; P=0.004) but not significantly after adjustment (P=0.056) or when families still taking opioids were assumed to use their full prescription. Among families with leftover opioids, 22% reported disposal. Requests for additional pain medication (18%) and satisfaction (93%) did not differ between survey eras.
