CONCLUSIONS: Discharge opioid prescribing after PSF for AIS declined substantially over 7 years without an apparent change in home pain-management outcomes. Consumption and waste estimates are less certain because they rest on a small, survey-dependent cohort. A default prescription near 15 tablets is a hypothesis for prospective testing, and routine disposal kits at discharge warrant evaluation.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV-therapeutic study.

articles.title: Pediatric Frostbite and Cold-Weather Injuries in the United States: A Multi-Database Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pediatric cold-weather injuries (frostbite and hypothermia) are uncommon but can lead to substantial morbidity, including amputation and long-term functional loss. National data on incidence, management, and outcomes are limited, particularly for fatalities outside healthcare settings. We conducted a retrospective analysis using three complementary data sources: an institutional registry at an American Burn Association-verified burn center (2018-2026), the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Readmission Database (NRD 2016-2021), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Storm Events Database (NOAA 2016-2023). Our institutional cohort included 16 patients (ages 1-17 years; 68.8% >13 years); treatments included rapid rewarming (43.8%), perfusion imaging (56.3%), thrombolytic therapy (18.8%), and hyperbaric oxygen therapy (31.3%). Two patients required amputation; both presented with hemorrhagic blisters, had delayed care, and did not receive thrombolytics. No thrombolytic-related complications were observed. Nationally, 2,155 pediatric cold weather injuries occurred; a national estimated hospitalization rate of 1.62 per 100,000. 79 pediatric frostbite admissions were identified, including 15 admissions designated as severe injury. NOAA data captured 16 pediatric deaths and 49 injuries across 30 states. Pediatric cold-weather injuries result in morbidity and mortality across diverse U.S. regions. Early aggressive management may reduce amputation and broader adoption of standardized protocols and public health prevention strategies are needed. Limitations of public health data emphasize the need for integrating diverse data sources to better understand the full impact of cold-weather injuries in the U.S.

articles.title: Age-Related Differences in the Organ Donation Process Among Pediatric Brain-Dead Donors: A Nationwide Study in Japan.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the pediatric organ donation process and age-related differences among brain-dead donors in Japan and evaluate organ-specific transplantation rates and graft survival across age groups.
DESIGN: Nationwide retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: National donor records maintained by the Japan Organ Transplant Network.
PATIENTS: All pediatric (≤ 17 yr old) brain-dead organ donors in Japan between July 17, 2010, and March 31, 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENT AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 100 pediatric brain-dead organ donors were included. Donors were categorized into three age groups: younger than 6 years (n = 32), 6-14 years (n = 48), and 15-17 years (n = 20). The time intervals from hospital admission to organ procurement showed marked age-dependent prolongation, with median durations of 28, 19.5, and 13.5 days, respectively (p < 0.01). Younger donors were more frequently managed in children's hospitals and pediatric departments, whereas older donors were increasingly managed in emergency and critical care settings. Organ transplantation was achieved in 99% of donors. Organ-specific transplantation rates were consistently high for the heart, liver, and kidneys across all age groups, whereas lung and pancreas transplantation rates increased with donor age. During donor management, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic function were generally maintained or improved until procurement. No significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed for any organ type.
CONCLUSIONS: The pediatric organ donation process in Japan was substantially prolonged in an age-dependent manner, particularly among donors younger than 6 years. Despite prolonged donor management, transplantation rates remained high, and no significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed. These findings highlight the importance of sustained multidisciplinary and family support throughout the donation process and may provide insights for pediatric donation systems in low-volume settings.

articles.title: The Radiographic Lung Edema Score in Pediatric Acute Respiratory Failure: Associations With Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers and Multiple Organ Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although chest radiographs (CXR) are among the most used imaging modalities in critically ill patients, their interpretation and clinical significance remain incompletely leveraged. The Radiographic Lung Edema (RALE) score is a prognostic bedside tool widely applied in adults to quantify lung edema on CXR. However, this score has been infrequently studied in children, and its potential to reflect broader aspects of critical illness pathophysiology beyond the lungs is unknown. We sought to determine the reproducibility of the RALE score, and whether higher RALE scores were associated with circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers, multi-organ dysfunction, and worse clinical outcomes in pediatric acute respiratory failure (ARF).
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Multicenter PICUs.
PATIENTS: Critically ill children (2 wk to 17 yr old) receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ARF, enrolled in the CAF-PINT (Coagulation and Fibrinolysis in Pediatric Insulin Titration) study (2012-2016).
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A baseline RALE score was calculated for each patient from a single CXR obtained within 72 hours of IMV initiation. Among 212 patients, RALE scores demonstrated good inter-rater reliability (intra-class coefficient 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.87). After adjustment for ARF etiology and illness severity, higher RALE scores were associated with fewer 28-day ventilator-free days (sub-distribution hazard ratio per 1-sd increase, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Structural equation modeling demonstrated that this association was mediated through both pulmonary dysfunction, measured by the oxygenation index (β -0.14; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.22 to -0.06), and extrapulmonary organ dysfunction, measured by the Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction score (β -0.05; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.10 to -0.002). Similar associations were observed for 28-day PICU-free days. Finally, penalized regression selected soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1, intercellular adhesion molecule-1, and tumor necrosis factor receptor-1 as biomarkers associated with higher RALE scores.
CONCLUSIONS: We provide evidence that the RALE score is not solely a lung injury marker but also reflects broader systemic pathophysiology. These findings have important implications for the interpretation and clinical application of this bedside tool in pediatric ARF.

articles.title: Navigating discharge information during early oral antibiotic switch in children: a qualitative comparison of caregiver and clinician experiences.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early switch from intravenous (IV) to oral antibiotic therapy is clinically safe for hospitalized children and supports earlier discharge. Responsibility for ongoing care then shifts to caregivers, increasing reliance on effective communication during the hospital-to-home transition.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the information needs and preferences of caregivers during children's transition home on oral antibiotic therapy and examine clinician perceptions of these needs.
METHODS: This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with caregivers of children discharged home on oral antibiotics following IV therapy and clinicians involved in their care. Participants were recruited through a hospital participating in the HOMEFREE program and consumer networks. Interviews explored information needs, timing, delivery, understanding, and discharge readiness. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, followed by interpretation through Longo's Extended Model of Health Information Seeking Behaviour.
RESULTS: Fifteen caregivers and eight clinicians participated. Four interrelated themes were identified. Information was frequently delivered at clinically appropriate but challenging time points, limiting families' ability to absorb key messages. Clinicians relied primarily on verbal communication, whereas caregivers preferred written information that could be revisited after discharge. Confidence in oral antibiotic therapy developed through observing recovery at home rather than clinical explanation alone. Caregivers often compensated for information gaps through vigilance and self-advocacy, and clinicians recognised that this dynamic could advantage more confident families.
CONCLUSIONS: Although oral antibiotic switch is clinically safe, family confidence and preparedness may be influenced by how information is delivered and used. Timely, multimodal communication may support safer and more equitable discharge.

articles.title: Menarche in Young-Onset Type 1 Diabetes: Data from the Australasian Diabetes Data Network (ADDN) Registry.
articles.abstract: Aim Data on age at menarche in youth with type 1 diabetes (T1D) remain limited. We examined factors associated with age at menarche and longitudinal trajectories of insulin dose, glycaemia, and body mass index (BMI) before and after menarche in an Australasian cohort. Method Longitudinal sociodemographic and clinical data for females with T1D and a documented menarche date were extracted from the Australasian Diabetes Data Network (ADDN) registry. Generalised estimating equations were used to examine factors associated with age at menarche (< vs. ≥ cohort median age), including Index of Relative Socioeconomic Disadvantage score, T1D duration, total daily insulin dose/kg (TDD/kg), HbA1c, insulin pump use, and BMI standard deviation score (SDS). Trajectories of TDD/kg, HbA1c, and BMI SDS across nine clinically defined pre- and post-menarche time intervals were analysed using linear mixed models with time modelled as a categorical fixed effect, accounting for repeated measures and within-subject correlation. Results Overall, 601 females from nine centres were included. Median (IQR) age at menarche was 12.6 (12.0, 13.3) years. Later menarche was associated with longer T1D duration (B = 0.10; 95% CI 0.01-0.19; p = 0.04), lower TDD/kg (-1.20; -2.00 to -0.42; p = 0.003), higher HbA1c (0.21; 0.02-0.39; p = 0.03), and lower BMI SDS (-0.48; -0.79 to -0.17; p = 0.002). TDD/kg increased in the pre-menarcheal period, peaking around menarche then declining; BMI SDS increased progressively from pre- to post-menarche; and HbA1c rose over time from pre- to post-menarche (all p < 0.001), demonstrating distinct trajectories. Conclusions Increasing insulin requirements preceded menarche, while HbA1c and BMI SDS continued to rise during the post-menarcheal period. These findings suggest that metabolic changes associated with pubertal maturation extend beyond menarche itself and highlight the importance of considering pubertal progression in diabetes care and anticipatory management during adolescence.

articles.title: National Trends and Demographic Disparities in Self-Reported Cognitive Difficulty Among U.S. High School Students, 2015-2023.
articles.abstract: The National Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) asks students whether, because of a physical, mental, or emotional problem, they have serious difficulty concentrating, remembering, or making decisions. We analyzed nationally representative 2015-2023 YRBS data from 50,222 U.S. high school students using survey-weighted prevalence estimates and logistic regression. The prevalence of this self-reported cognitive difficulty increased from 29.9% (95% CI, 27.7%-32.1%) in 2015 to 45.0% (95% CI, 43.1%-47.0%) in 2023-approximately 3 in 10 students to nearly 1 in 2 (adjusted odds ratio per 2-year cycle, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.18-1.25)-while 2021 and 2023 estimates were similar. The increase was steeper among female than male students. In secondary models, insufficient sleep, excessive recreational screen use, frequent poor mental health, household basic needs not consistently met, and unstable housing were associated with cognitive difficulty. These findings identify a growing functional signal requiring surveillance, school-health assessment, referral pathways, and further study.

articles.title: Delayed Diagnosis of Coronary Sinus Ostial Atresia in a Single-Ventricle Patient.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: Coronary sinus ostial atresia is a rare congenital anomaly that is often clinically silent; however, hemodynamic compromise can occur if venous drainage is interrupted. We present a 4-month old infant with hypoplastic left heart syndrome who previously underwent palliation with a Norwood procedure. During bidirectional Glenn palliation, ligation of a 2-mm left superior vena cava resulted in coronary sinus dilation and myocardial edema, raising suspicion for coronary sinus ostial atresia. The coronary sinus was unroofed, and the child recovered well.

articles.title: Prevalence of Powassan Virus Infection in Children with Suspected Lyme Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both Lyme disease and Powassan virus (POWV) are transmitted by the bite of the Ixodes tick. While severe POWV encephalitis cases are uncommon in children, milder infections may be underdiagnosed.
METHODS: We performed a case-control study nested within a prospective cohort of children < 21 years evaluated for Lyme disease at one of eight Pedi Lyme Net emergency departments. We selected children with early or early-disseminated Lyme disease (n=305) with age, sex, center and symptom matched clinical mimics (n=295). Using biobanked research specimens, we performed POWV two-tier serology with confirmatory focus neutralization testing (FNT) and a reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test. We defined a POWV infection with a positive two-tier serology or RT-PCR test. We compared the prevalence of POWV between children with Lyme disease and matched mimics.
RESULTS: Of the 600 included children, the median age was 9 years (interquartile range 6-14 years) and 377 (63%) were male. POWV infection was more common in the children with Lyme disease (8.5%, 95% confidence interval (CI) 5.4-11.7%) compared to matched mimics (0.7%, 95% CI 0.1-2.4%; difference 7.9%, 95% CI 4.6-11.1; adjusted odds ratio 5.0, 95% CI 1.2-21.9). Of the 28 children with a positive POWV two-tier serology test, 11 (39%) had a positive FNT test. None of the RT-PCR tests were positive (0%, 95% CI 0-0.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: A substantial minority of children with Lyme disease had serologic evidence of POWV co-infection compared with matched clinical mimics. Clinically unrecognized POWV infections were more common than previously acknowledged.

articles.title: Psychological Assets and Cardiovascular Health in Adulthood: A Mixed Methods Investigation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological risk factors like depression increase risk for poor cardiovascular outcomes but psychological assets like purpose in life are protective and linked to reduced risk of cardiovascular events. However, most assets are investigated individually, and not all have been explored in relation to cardiovascular health (CVH). This study used mixed methods to assess multiple psychological assets and evaluate associations with CVH 12 years later.
METHODS: Data came from 2092 participants in the National Child Development Study. At age 50 years, participants wrote open-ended responses describing their futures. Two trained researchers qualitatively coded each response by rating them for 7 commonly assessed psychological assets (1=not at all; 7=very): optimism, purpose, satisfaction, personal growth, agency, enjoyment, and overall positivity. At age 62, CVH behavioral factors (exercise, smoking status, sleep) were self-reported; CVH clinical factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose, body weight) were measured during nurse visits. Following Life's Essential 8 guidelines, CVH components were combined into total CVH scores. Linear regressions examined associations between each age 50 asset and age 62 CVH scores, adjusting for age 50 confounders.
RESULTS: All age 50 assets were positively associated with better CVH scores 12 years later, accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and word counts (p≤0.05). Purpose (b=0.81 [95% CI, 0.33-1.29]) and personal growth (b=0.82 [95% CI, 0.34-1.20]) showed the strongest associations with CVH in fully adjusted models.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher levels of most midlife psychological assets were linked with better CVH over time, suggesting multiple paths to health protection. These findings highlight assets that could be prevention targets.

articles.title: First-hand Alcohol-Related Harms in Hong Kong University Dormitories: A Serial Cross-sectional Study Comparing the Normative, Social Unrest, and COVID-19 Pandemic Periods.
articles.abstract: Between September 2018 and June 2021, we conducted serial cross-sectional surveys of university dormitory residents in Hong Kong (n = 2659). Drinking behaviors and first-hand harms were examined across a normative period, time of protests, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Drinking levels remained steady between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic, and the proportions reporting drinking-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5%, respectively. Binge drinking was associated with high first-hand harms across 3 periods (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 3.46-5.76). Having a drinking roommate was also correlated with harms during the normative period (AOR = 1.66). During the protests, underage drinking history and university location were associated with high first-hand harms (AOR: 1.69 and 1.82). During the COVID-19 pandemic, weekend dormitory residence and low alcohol-related knowledge were significant factors (AOR: 2.78 and 2.85). The findings indicate the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories.

articles.title: Short- and median-term disease outcome after Clostridioides difficile infection in paediatric inflammatory bowel disease patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a recognised complication of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). In adults, CDI has been linked to increased long-term colectomy risk, but data on its impact in paediatric IBD remain scarce. We aimed to assess the medium-term course of IBD after CDI in children.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre, case-control study in the paediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition Department at Necker-Enfants Malades Hospital. All paediatric IBD (pIBD) patients hospitalised with CDI between January 2008 and December 2020 were included. Each case was matched 1:3 with IBD controls by sex, age, IBD subtype, disease location, and year of diagnosis. Outcomes at 12, 24 and 36 months included disease activity scores, number of exacerbations, hospitalisations, digestive surgeries, and treatment escalation.
RESULTS: Forty-five pIBD patients with CDI were enrolled and matched with 152 pIBD controls. Compared with controls, children with CDI experienced a more severe disease course, characterised by higher mean activity scores each year of follow-up, more flares requiring hospitalisation at 24 and 36 months, and greater need for therapeutic escalation over time (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In paediatric patients, CDI is associated with a significantly more severe medium-term course of IBD. Early recognition and targeted management of CDI are therefore crucial in this population.

articles.title: Natural history and disease burden of biliary atresia in the United States: A systematic literature review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Biliary atresia (BA) is a rare and potentially fatal cholangiopathy affecting infants. The primary treatment approach for BA is Kasai hepatoportoenterostomy (KP); however, even with KP, many patients still require liver transplantation (LT). The objective of this systematic literature review (SLR) was to describe epidemiology, natural history, and native liver survival (NLS), as well as the humanistic and economic burden, in patients with BA in the United States (US).
METHODS: Embase and MEDLINE searches were performed; US-based, English-language publications from 2014 to 2024 were included. Additional searches were conducted for non-peer-reviewed publications, including congress abstracts. The SLR was conducted per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines.
RESULTS: Across epidemiology, natural history, and NLS, 38/3485 records were included; for the humanistic and economic burden outcomes, 16/1471 records were included. Sample sizes ranged from 10 to 4306 patients, and BA prevalence was 6.5-6.8 per 100,000 live births. Complications of BA included various hepatic, cardiovascular, and renal abnormalities, among others. Post-transplant graft survival rates ranged from 86.0%-96.0% and 79.0%-97.0% at 1 and 5 years post-LT, respectively. BA was also associated with high healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and disease costs. Overall, sample heterogeneity and study design differences made comparisons across studies difficult.
CONCLUSIONS: Although there are limited data on BA outcomes in the US, and the published BA studies are heterogeneous, this SLR reveals a substantial burden due to BA-related care and complications. Additionally, data on HCRU and costs highlight the unmet need for additional management and research in BA.

articles.title: The impact of childhood obesity on the developing skeleton.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity is an increasingly prevalent global health concern associated with significant metabolic, endocrine, and skeletal consequences. During critical periods of growth and peak bone mineralisation, excessive adiposity may impair skeletal development by disrupting bone formation and remodeling. The effects of obesity on bone metabolism are complex and multifactorial, involving altered mechanical loading, hormonal dysregulation, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Key mediators, including insulin resistance, adipose tissue dysfunction, and disturbances in calcium-phosphate-magnesium-vitamin D homeostasis, contribute to impaired osteoblastic and osteoclastic activity. Additionally, gut microbiome dysbiosis and reduced nutrient absorption may exacerbate skeletal fragility and abnormal mineralisation. This review provides an integrative overview of current evidence regarding the impact of obesity on the developing skeleton. It discusses (I) methods of bone assessment in children with excess body weight and associated diagnostic challenges, (II) biomarkers relevant to bone metabolism and obesity-related skeletal alterations, (III) the role of dietary factors, nutrient intake, and physical activity in bone development, and (IV) future research directions aimed at reducing fracture risk and improving skeletal health outcomes in paediatric populations.

articles.title: Clinical Perspectives on Heart-Kidney-Brain Crosstalk.
articles.journal: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular, kidney, and neurological diseases are highly prevalent and frequently co-occur, reflecting an integrated heart-kidney-brain axis linked by shared hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and inflammatory pathways. This crosstalk maintains perfusion, blood volume, and metabolic homeostasis through coordinate signaling via the circulation, autonomic nervous system, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. When dysregulated, these same pathways perpetuate injury across organs, transforming adaptive responses into maladaptive cycles of dysfunction.This review synthesizes current understanding of the physiology and molecular mechanisms underlying heart-kidney-brain interactions, emphasizing hypoperfusion, neurohormonal activation, and convergent pathways of oxidative stress and inflammation as central drivers. Key amplifiers, including iron dysregulation, uremic toxin accumulation, and disordered mineral metabolism, extend injury systemically, contributing to cardiac remodeling, kidney disease, progression, and neurological disease. Clinically, this axis manifests as interconnected syndromes such as cardiorenal syndrome, cerebrovascular disease, and cognitive impairment. Emerging biomarkers and imaging modalities reveal overlapping signals across organs yet are rarely integrated in practice. Notably, neurological outcomes remain underrepresented in cardiovascular and kidney research despite their profound impact on quality of life, particularly in the pediatric population where disease affects lifelong development. We highlight gaps in mutli-organ diagnostic frameworks, biomarker standardization, and translational models, and propose future research directions in the heart-kidney-brain axis. Recognizing the heart, kidney, and brain as a unified system is essential to improving risk stratification, preventing multi-organ injury, and advancing patient-centered care.

articles.title: Photoacoustic imaging assessment of acute kidney injury associated with experimental necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract: Background: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating gastrointestinal condition increasingly recognized to cause systemic complications, including acute kidney injury (AKI). However, the underlying mechanisms and variations in renal impairment remain largely unknown, and there is a lack of non-invasive imaging methods for detecting early kidney injury. Methods: We evaluated kidney injury through a multimodal approach, using a neonatal rat model of experimental NEC. Plasma and renal tissue were analyzed for pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) by ELISA. Histological analysis and immunofluorescence staining were used to identify renal abnormalities and expressions of KIM-1 and NGAL. Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) was used to assess renal oxygenation and total hemoglobin as functional imaging biomarkers of kidney injury. Results: NEC pups showed significant elevations of systemic and renal cytokines, as well as increased expression of KIM-1, NGAL and CD31 in proximal tubules of the kidney. Histological examination further confirms renal injury in the NEC cohort. PAI demonstrated reduction in renal oxygen saturation, offering non-invasive assessment of physiological kidney damage. Conclusion: This study characterizes AKI associated with NEC as an inflammatory and hypoxic response in the neonatal rat NEC model and introduces PAI as a promising imaging modality for non-invasive evaluation of renal injury in NEC.

articles.title: Hypophosphatemia in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Incidence, Determinants, and Clinical Impact in a Tertiary Emergency and Intensive Care Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Serum phosphate levels commonly decline during treatment of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), but the determinants and clinical implications of hypophosphatemia remain incompletely defined. We aimed to determine its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact during pediatric DKA.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 116 DKA episodes managed in a tertiary pediatric emergency department and intensive care unit between January 2022 and June 2025 were analyzed. Demographic characteristics, admission biochemical parameters, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Hypophosphatemia was defined according to age-specific reference ranges. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of hypophosphatemia, while length of hospital stay was assessed using multivariable linear regression of log-transformed values.
RESULTS: Hypophosphatemia occurred in 72/116 episodes (62.1%). Compared with those without hypophosphatemia, affected patients had lower admission pH (7.03±0.13 vs. 7.12±0.17; P=0.002), bicarbonate (7.8±2.4 vs. 9.8±3.3 mEq/L; P<0.001), and potassium levels (4.43±0.96 vs. 4.81±0.66 mEq/L; P=0.024). Hyponatremia and hypokalemia were more frequent, whereas hyperkalemia was less common (all P<0.05). Lower admission pH (OR: 0.008, 95% CI: 0.000-0.219; P=0.004) and lower baseline phosphate concentration (OR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; P=0.031) independently predicted hypophosphatemia. Although hospitalization was longer in the hypophosphatemia group (85.3±75.2 vs. 56.2±36.4 h; P=0.018), hypophosphatemia was not independently associated with length of stay. Higher admission pH independently predicted shorter hospitalization (β=-0.957, P=0.026). Baseline phosphate positively correlated with nadir phosphate during treatment (r=0.303, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Hypophosphatemia is common during pediatric DKA and is closely associated with the severity of metabolic acidosis at presentation. However, it does not independently affect hospitalization duration, suggesting that it primarily reflects disease severity rather than independently determining short-term outcomes.

articles.title: From broad suppression to precision targeting: the new era of antigen-specific immunotherapy for type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the selective destruction of pancreatic β-cells driven by autoreactive immune responses. In recent decades, the global incidence of T1D has risen markedly, with the most rapid increase observed among children and adolescents, imposing a substantial burden on healthcare systems worldwide. Conventional treatment primarily relies on exogenous insulin administration, which manages hyperglycemia but does not address the underlying autoimmune pathology or restore endogenous insulin production. Antigen-specific immunotherapy (ASI) has emerged as a promising strategy that may restore antigen-specific immune tolerance via multiple mechanisms, including clonal deletion/ anergy, immune deviation, induction of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and type 1 regulatory T (Tr1) cells, and tolerogenic antigen presentation. ASI may help preserve residual β-cell function and potentially modify disease progression. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in ASI for T1D, with a focus on the biological features of key T1D autoantigens, optimization of antigen delivery strategies, and prospects for clinical translation.

articles.title: PDE4B inhibition attenuates intestinal inflammation with reducing glycolysis in macrophages.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence underscores that PDE4B expression is significantly upregulated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, its therapeutic potential and the underlying molecular mechanisms in pediatric IBD remain poorly defined. In this study, multiple public datasets were analyzed to characterize PDE4B expression in pediatric IBD. This was followed by therapeutic evaluation in mice colitis models to validate the efficacy of PDE4B inhibition in vivo. Analysis of public datasets revealed a marked elevation of PDE4B in pediatric IBD cohorts. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that a PDE4B inhibitor effectively suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory responses in primary blood samples from pediatric patients. In murine models, pharmacological inhibition of PDE4B significantly attenuated intestinal inflammation in both DSS- and LPS-induced colitis models. Furthermore, treatment with the PDE4B inhibitor successfully alleviated established chronic mucosal injury and preserved goblet cell integrity in spontaneous Il10-/- mice. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrated that PDE4B inhibition was associated with a partial restoration of gut microbiota diversity and a reduction in specific bacterial dysbiosis. At the molecular level, the inhibitor promoted the activation of the anti-inflammatory mediator p-CREB while concurrently abrogating pro-inflammatory p-STAT3 signaling. Notably, the suppression of pathological glycolysis by the inhibitor was closely accompanied by the metabolic reprogramming and enhanced anti-inflammatory function. In conclusion, these findings suggest that targeting PDE4B represents a potential therapeutic approach for pediatric IBD by modulating macrophage immunometabolism and restoring intestinal homeostasis.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Cytomegalovirus Infection in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, epidemiology, and outcomes of children with active cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in a pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and to identify risk factors associated with mortality.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, medical records of patients admitted to a tertiary-level PICU between January 2015 and January 2023 were reviewed. Patients aged 1 month to 18 years with laboratory-confirmed CMV infection during PICU stay were included. Demographic, clinical, and outcome data were collected. Disease severity was assessed using pediatric risk of mortality (PRISM) and pediatric logistic organ dysfunction (PELOD) scores. Risk factors for mortality were analyzed using regression models, and the predictive value of CMV viral load was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: During the study period, a total of 3320 patients were admitted to the PICU, of whom 79 (2.38%; 95% CI, 1.9-2.9) had laboratory-confirmed CMV infection. Nearly half of the patients (n = 36, 45.6%) were immunocompromised. Overall mortality was 25.3% (n = 20). The main cause of death was septic shock (85%, n = 17). In most non-survivors (80%, n = 16), CMV polymerase chain reaction remained positive prior to death. A PELOD score ≥ 3 independently predicted mortality (crude RR 3.42; 95% CI, 2.98-7.78). Each 1-point increase in PRISM score was independently associated with mortality (crude RR 1.12; 95% CI, 1.05-1.20). Cytomegalovirus viral load demonstrated poor discriminative performance for mortality prediction ( Area Under the Curve-AUC 0.57; 95% CI, 0.47-0.63).
CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of CMV infection in critically ill children was low but associated with high mortality. Organ dysfunction severity, particularly elevated PELOD scores, was a significant predictor of mortality. Pediatric risk of mortality score was statistically associated with mortality despite limited discriminative performance, whereas CMV viral load was not associated with mortality. These findings suggest that CMV infection in PICU patients likely reflects disease severity rather than being a direct determinant of outcome.

articles.title: Factors associated with post-tonsillectomy secondary hemorrhage: A retrospective study of 3289 patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To determine the epidemiological characteristics of post-tonsillectomy secondary hemorrhage (PTSH) across different age groups and to explore factors associated with PTSH in a large Asian cohort.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted on 3289 consecutive patients who underwent tonsillectomy from March 2015 to March 2025. PTSH was defined as bleeding occurring ≥24 h postoperatively requiring medical intervention. Only univariable analyses (chi-square or Fisher's exact test) were performed; therefore, all findings are reported as associations rather than independent effects.
RESULTS: The overall PTSH incidence was 1.73% (57/3289). Age was associated with PTSH (P < 0.001), with the highest bleeding rates in adolescents (13-17 years, 3.82%) and young adults (18-44 years, 3.38%). Surgeon volume was associated with PTSH (P < 0.001): the low-volume group (≤50 cases) had a 3.18% bleeding rate versus 0.83% in the high-volume group (>200 cases). Infectious-hypertrophic lesions had the highest bleeding rate (3.73%, P = 0.007). In adults (≥18 years, n = 1067), high BMI, smoking, hypertension, and diabetes were each associated with higher bleeding rates (all P < 0.05). Two cases of pseudoaneurysm were successfully managed via interventional embolization.
CONCLUSION: Low surgeon volume, infectious-hypertrophic lesions, high BMI, smoking, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus were factors associated with PTSH in univariable analysis. Adolescent and young adult males may warrant closer perioperative attention; this subgroup analysis was exploratory. Clinically, perioperative risk assessment should be strengthened, surgical training standardized, and vigilance maintained for serious complications such as pseudoaneurysm.

articles.title: Association of vitamin therapy with acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus and neurological outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus (AEFCSE) has a poor prognosis, but no definitive treatment. We aimed to evaluate whether early combination vitamin therapy (VT) (vitamin B1, B6, and l-carnitine) could prevent AEFCSE onset and improve neurological outcomes of pediatric febrile status epilepticus (FSE).
METHODS: The present, single-center, retrospective observational study enrolled patients admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit during 2017-2019 and 2022-2024 with FSE lasting ≥30 min. The patients were categorized into a VT group, who received vitamins within 72 h of the initial seizure onset, and a non-VT group. The primary outcome was the AEFCSE incidence. The secondary outcome was AEFCSE-related, poor neurological prognosis as defined by the Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category score. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on propensity scores was used to adjust for confounding factors.
RESULTS: Of 109 included patients with FSE, 40 (37%) and 69 (63%) were in the VT and the non-VT group, respectively. AEFCSE occurred in eight (20%) and 11 (16%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, VT was associated with lower but non-significant odds of AEFCSE (odds ratio [OR]: 0.60; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.21-1.73). AEFCSE-related, poor neurological outcomes occurred in five (13%) and eight (12%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, the odds were lower but non-significant (OR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.16-1.90).
CONCLUSIONS: Early combination VT demonstrated an exploratory association with lower AEFCSE incidence and improved neurological outcomes in children with FSE albeit the findings were inconclusive.

articles.title: The association between binge eating and the metabolic profile of adolescents with obesity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Binge eating (BE) might further deteriorate the inflammatory and metabolic profile of individuals with obesity, but data in adolescents are limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to compare the metabolic and inflammatory parameters of adolescents with and without BE and to investigate the relationship between BE and metabolic syndrome.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 82 adolescents (12-18 years) with overweight or obesity were evaluated for the presence of BE through the Munich Eating and Nutritional Disorders Questionnaire. Waist circumference, BMI z-score, systolic and diastolic blood pressure measurements, a range of biomarkers including fasting and postprandial glucose and insulin, lipid profile, liver enzymes, thyroid function, and inflammatory markers were measured. BE episodes were reported by 47.6% of participants and were more prevalent in females (p = 0.041). Elevated blood pressure was more common in the BE group (p = 0.021). No significant differences were found in anthropometric measures, laboratory findings, or overall metabolic syndrome prevalence between the BE and non-BE groups. In univariable logistic regression analysis, BE was associated with elevated blood pressure (OR = 4.59, 95% CI: 1.61-18.20, p = 0.030). In the multivariable model, only waist circumference remained significant (OR = 1.14, 95% CI: 1.04-1.25, p = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: While univariable analysis suggested a potential relationship between BE and elevated blood pressure, this association was attenuated after accounting for adiposity-related factors. Larger longitudinal follow-up studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between BE and cardiometabolic risk factors and assess whether BE predicts future development of metabolic syndrome.

articles.title: Tailoring practices identified in pediatric serious illness communication tools: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serious illness communication tools have been designed to ensure safe and standardized care. Effective person-centered communication requires clinicians not only to identify each patient's needs, but also to adapt their communication approach and interaction behaviors accordingly. Tailoring is a responsive and adaptive communication approach that has been defined in adult healthcare literature but not in pediatric literature.
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review sought to identify tools used to guide serious illness communication in pediatric settings and map tool constructs against the communication approach 'tailoring' to consider the potential transferability of this approach to the pediatric healthcare context.
METHODS: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews. Articles were eligible for inclusion if they were English-language, peer-reviewed publications that proposed or synthesized an original communication tool for health professionals conducting serious illness conversations in pediatric healthcare. The Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) was used to guide reporting.
RESULTS: A total of 3788 articles were identified for screening and 19 were retained for data extraction. Variation existed in the derivation of pediatric serious illness communication tools with most being informed by expert opinion. Tailoring practices were identified in all pediatric serious illness communication tools, but to varying extents. They could be utilized both prior to and during serious illness conversations and the majority of tailoring practices focused on what to discuss as opposed to how to communicate. Practices that could guide clinicians to address key pediatric considerations such as neurodevelopment and language abilities were underrepresented.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric serious illness communication tools incorporated tailoring practices, albeit to varying degrees. Further empirical research is needed to examine how tailoring practices could be integrated into these tools, particularly to support clinicians in monitoring children's non-verbal cues, emotions, and neurodevelopmental capacities during serious illness conversations.

articles.title: Epidemiology, risk factors, and antimicrobial susceptibility of nasopharyngeal bacterial colonization in children: A prospective study using culture and PCR.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSES: To investigate bacterial carriage among Taiwanese children, focusing on colonization patterns, risk factors, and antibiotic susceptibility.
METHODS: In this prospective hospital-based study, children aged 1 month to <13 years were recruited from well-child/vaccination clinics, general pediatric outpatient clinics, and pediatric inpatient wards from March to November 2025. Nasopharyngeal specimens were analyzed using culture and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed for cultured isolates. Risk factors for carriage were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 346 children, carriage of Moraxella catarrhalis (59%) was most prevalent, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae (35.8%), Haemophilus influenzae (23.1%), and Staphylococcus aureus (15.6%), as determined by combined culture and qPCR results. PCR increased detection and identified frequent co-colonization (42.5%). S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae carriage peaked at 1-2 years, whereas S. aureus showed a U-shaped distribution. Daycare attendance (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 7.761, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.396-17.738), recent upper respiratory tract infection (aOR = 4.704, 95% CI: 2.626-8.428), allergic diseases (aOR = 3.441, 95% CI: 1.857-6.379), and prior otitis media (aOR = 2.385, 95% CI: 1.151-4.943) were independently associated with carriage. Penicillin resistance in S. pneumoniae was low (5.3%, non-meningitis breakpoints). Ampicillin resistance was common in H. influenzae (63.8%) and M. catarrhalis (54.3%), but both remained susceptible to amoxicillin-clavulanate (93.6% and 100%).
CONCLUSIONS: Nasopharyngeal carriage in children is common, often polymicrobial, and age-dependent. PCR improves detection over culture. Local carriage surveillance may complement clinical isolate data and help monitor antimicrobial resistance trends.

articles.title: Distinct predictors of sleep timing and sleep problems in infants and young toddlers: The role of parental chronotype, sleep quality, and psychological distress.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child sleep timing and perceived sleep problems may have different family-level correlates. We examined associations of maternal and paternal chronotype, sleep quality, psychological distress, maternal sleep-related cognitions, and paternal involvement in infant care with infant and young toddler sleep timing and perceived sleep-problem severity.
METHODS: This single-center cross-sectional study included 107 mother-father-child triads aged 6-18 months. Child sleep was evaluated using the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire-Revised. Sleep midpoint was calculated as a measure of child sleep timing, and perceived sleep-problem severity was assessed on a 1-5 ordinal scale. Both parents completed measures of chronotype, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), anxiety, and depressive symptoms; maternal sleep-related cognitions and paternal involvement were also assessed. Multiple linear and ordinal logistic regression models evaluated associations with the two outcomes.
RESULTS: Greater maternal morningness was independently associated with an earlier child sleep midpoint, including after adjustment for child age (B = -0.051, 95% CI -0.075 to -0.026; p < 0.001). In the combined ordinal model, poorer maternal sleep quality was the only factor independently associated with greater perceived sleep-problem severity (aOR = 1.28 per PSQI point, 95% CI 1.12-1.46; p < 0.001). No paternal variable was independently associated with either outcome in the adjusted models. Child sleep midpoint was not associated with sleep-problem severity (Spearman's ρ = -0.088, p = 0.369).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal chronotype was associated with infant and young child sleep timing, whereas maternal sleep quality was associated with perceived child sleep-problem severity. These findings suggest that child sleep timing and sleep problems may represent distinct dimensions of sleep in infants and young toddlers.

articles.title: Through tired eyes: Self-reported sleepiness and sleep patterns of children with and without ADHD.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/AIM: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is common among children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) but is frequently under-recognised, with most paediatric sleep research relying on parent-report or objective measures that cannot capture the child's subjective experience of sleepiness. This study examined self-reported EDS and sleep patterns in Australian primary school-aged children with and without ADHD and examined whether the inattentive (ADHD-I) and combined (ADHD-C) presentations show distinct sleep profiles.
METHODS: Two hundred and seventy-three children aged 7-12 years (typically developing [TD], n = 131; ADHD-I, n = 57; ADHD-C, n = 85) completed the Children's Report of Sleep Patterns-Sleepiness Scale and a modified Children's Report of Sleep Patterns self-reported deriving measures of daytime sleepiness and sleep habits, with group differences examined.
RESULTS: Children with ADHD-C took significantly longer to fall asleep and were more likely to use nighttime medication than TD children and woke more frequently overnight than children with ADHD-I. Children with ADHD-C also reported increased amount of sleepiness than TD children, an effect that approached significance. Children with ADHD-I reported significantly higher sleepiness at school than TD children and rated themselves less positively as sleepers than TD children, despite no significant differences in other self-reported sleep variables.
CONCLUSION: Children with ADHD-C and ADHD-I did not differ significantly in overall sleepiness, but differences emerged in specific domains, including longer sleep onset latency and increased nighttime medication use in ADHD-C as well as increased sleepiness at school for children with ADHD-I. A trend also emerged toward poorer self-rated sleeper status in children with ADHD-I without corresponding differences in other self-reported sleep variables. These findings support routine sleep screening in ADHD and the clinical value of asking children directly about their own sleep experience.

articles.title: Consensus Statements on the Clinical Practice for Patients With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: The Fontan procedure has been transformative for patients with univentricular physiology. By using a single ventricle as the systemic pump and relying on passive venous return to drive pulmonary circulation, Fontan circulation alleviates cyanosis and heart failure, allowing children to engage in normal activities during school and adolescence. Nevertheless, Fontan circulation is characterized by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, which leads to systemic venous congestion and long-term multiorgan effects. Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) is now recognized as a major long-term complication. Approximately 50% of patients develop hepatic abnormalities within 10-20 years after surgery, and some progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite this risk, strategies to identify individuals at high risk for early HCC and to provide better prognostic information remain limited. This article compiles knowledge from congenital heart disease specialists and hepatologists on FALD, including areas where evidence is limited. By facilitating early diagnosis, structured follow-up, and multidisciplinary management of FALD, this initiative aims to improve outcomes, build a nationwide clinical experience, and ultimately support the development of formal, evidence-based guidelines for FALD management.

articles.title: Expert consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of recurrent wheezing in preschool children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wheezing is a very common symptom in preschool children. Compared with that of older children with wheezing or asthma, the morbidity and health care utilization of preschool are disproportionately high, imposing a heavy economic burden on the health care system and society. Furthermore, severe and frequent wheezing in early life is associated with a trajectory of poor lung function, which is associated with respiratory and non-respiratory health outcomes in later adulthood, including high-risk chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and high-risk cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in middle age. However, recurrent preschool wheezing, which is defined as two or more wheezing episodes in children younger than 6 years, excluding bronchiolitis, is highly heterogeneous in etiology and prognosis and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges for pediatricians.
METHODS: Thirty Chinese experts majoring in pediatric pulmonology and epidemiology were invited to write this practical consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of recurrent wheezing in preschool children on the basis of evidence collection and experience. Elucidation and reviews were conducted using electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang databases. We used variations in terms for "wheezing", "asthma", "wheezing bronchitis", "preschool", "children", and "pediatric".
RESULTS: The etiology, evaluation, management of acute wheezing exacerbation, and strategy of long-term anti-inflammatory therapy in recurrent preschool wheezing are highlighted. The most common causes of preschool wheezing are virus-induced wheezing and asthma (typical wheezing), some of which require long-term anti-inflammatory therapy. Some other children had identifiable underlying diseases (atypical wheezing). On the basis of the confirmation of wheezing, the underlying diseases and phenotypes of typical wheezing should be carefully investigated. For acute wheezing, inhaled short-acting β₂-agonists are the first-line agents, and systemic corticosteroids should be reserved only for severe cases. Routine use of azithromycin is not recommended in acute wheezing. The decision to initiate long-term anti-inflammatory therapy for recurrent preschool wheezing should be based on a comprehensive evaluation of clinical risk indicators and treatable traits such as type 2 inflammation. Immunomodulators such as bacterial lysates may be considered for use in trials in preschool children with recurrent virus-induced wheezing.
CONCLUSIONS: This symptom-based, phenotype-oriented consensus provides practical guidance for the individualized management of heterogeneous recurrent wheezing in preschool children. Further studies are needed to identify clinical risk factors and biomarkers for persistent wheezing and asthma. More appropriate long-term treatment regimens should also be explored.

articles.title: Candidemia in patients with intestinal failure: Diagnostic utility of fungal blood cultures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatric patients with intestinal failure (IF) receiving parenteral nutrition are at increased risk for candidemia. Evaluation of central line-associated bloodstream infection often includes aerobic, anaerobic, and fungal blood cultures, but the diagnostic yield of dedicated fungal cultures is uncertain. We evaluated fungal blood cultures compared with aerobic cultures for detecting candidemia.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients with IF and central venous catheters admitted to Children's National Hospital from 2010 through 2020 was conducted. Candidemia episodes were identified through microbiology records. Primary analysis included episodes with both aerobic and fungal blood cultures obtained on the first day of fungemia. Time to positivity (TTP) was compared between paired cultures.
RESULTS: Among 121 hospitalizations, 20 candidemia episodes occurred in 17 patients; 14 had paired aerobic and fungal cultures and were included in the primary analysis. Median age was 3.3 years (interquartile range [IQR] 1.0-8.7), and median length of stay was 25.5 days (IQR 17.0-36.3). Candida parapsilosis and Candida guilliermondii were most common (13/20 episodes). Ninety percent were receiving parenteral nutrition, and 90% had antimicrobial exposure within 6 months. In all paired cases, Candida grew in both cultures. Aerobic cultures had faster TTP than fungal cultures (23.8 ± 8.5 vs. 67.2 ± 18.0 h; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Aerobic cultures detected all candidemia identified by fungal cultures and had faster TTP. Dedicated fungal cultures provided no observed incremental diagnostic yield, although sample size limits precision. Larger studies should determine whether selective rather than routine fungal cultures are appropriate in pediatric IF.

articles.title: Improving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in hospitalized pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Youth hospitalized with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin is routine in adults hospitalized with IBD, but standardized pediatric protocols are rare. Using quality improvement methods, we aimed to increase the rate of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst select hospitalized patients with IBD by reaching 90% algorithm adherence by June 2023 and sustaining.
METHODS: Current evidence, external institutional algorithms, and multidisciplinary collaboration (hematology, pharmacy, surgery) were used to create an algorithm for providing pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin. The algorithm was implemented in February 2023 for all patients admitted with active IBD to a large, tertiary care children's hospital. Rates of algorithm adherence and rates of enoxaparin receipt during the project period were compared to baseline rates. Patient and provider education, electronic data tracking, and regular data auditing and review with providers were used to improve algorithm adherence. Reasons for non-adherence to the algorithm and rates of VTE, bleeding complications, and medication side effects during hospitalization were tracked.
RESULTS: The proportion of patients who appropriately followed the algorithm reached 94%, increased from 50% when the algorithm was retrospectively applied to the pre-project period (p < 0.001). The total proportion of hospitalized patients who received pharmacologic prophylaxis increased from 1% to 31% (p < 0.001). Following algorithm introduction, there were no VTEs or reported complications from enoxaparin during hospitalization.
CONCLUSIONS: The introduction of a standardized algorithm was associated with significantly increased rates of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst children hospitalized with IBD with no recorded adverse in-hospital events.

articles.title: Novel pathogenic variant in haploinsufficiency of A20 with severe gastrointestinal effects and fulminant hepatic failure: A pediatric case series.
articles.abstract: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a rare autoinflammatory disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in tumor necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3), encoding a negative regulator of nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NFκB) signaling. We report two pediatric patients with a previously unreported novel pathogenic variant (p. Glu409*) in the zinc finger (ZnF) 1 domain, exhibiting markedly divergent phenotypes. Case 1 presented with very-early-onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO-IBD) and autoimmune thyroiditis, requiring aggressive infliximab dose escalation. Case 2 developed fulminant hepatic failure requiring liver transplantation, followed by post-transplant complications including refractory rejection, recurrent infections, and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder. This represents the first known case of HA20 in solid organ transplantation. These cases underscore the importance of early genetic diagnosis in unexplained pediatric inflammatory disease and transplant rejection, as HA20 recognition may alter immunosuppressive strategies and guide therapies including cytokine blockade or Janus kinase (JAK) inhibition.

articles.title: Eosinophilic esophagitis and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome: A case series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RTS) is a rare disorder characterized by intellectual disability, poor growth, distinctive facial features, and gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms. While dysphagia and feeding difficulties are well recognized in RTS, the prevalence and clinical significance of eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) in this population remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series at a single pediatric tertiary care center (2012-2022) collecting demographic, genetic, clinical, endoscopic, and histopathological data.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients with RTS were identified; 15 (56%) had an identifiable genetic variant (12 with CREBBP and 3 with EP300). Seventeen patients (63%) had GI symptoms and 8 (30%) underwent endoscopy. Four patients (15%) were diagnosed with EoE, with one patient also having eosinophilic gastritis and eosinophilic duodenitis. Age at diagnosis ranged from 8 months to 23 years. Presenting symptoms included food impaction, vomiting, dysphagia, and poor weight gain. Three of the 4 patients had RTS type 1 (CREBBP variant gene). Treatments included proton pump inhibitors, swallowed steroids, and dietary elimination with variable responses. Compared with the general population, the odds of EoE in our RTS cohort were 121-fold higher (odds ratio = 121.6, 95% confidence interval: 13.1-1131.0, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: There is a markedly increased prevalence of EoE in patients with RTS. Early recognition and evaluation of GI symptoms with endoscopic assessment is important to enable timely diagnosis, optimize management, and reduce the risk of EoE-related complications. Further research is needed to understand the underlying genetic and immunologic mechanisms linking RTS and EoE.

articles.title: Parent perceptions of disease monitoring in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: The influence of intestinal ultrasound exposure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Monitoring pediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) typically requires invasive or resource-intensive testing. Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is a noninvasive, radiation-free, point-of-care modality increasingly used in pediatric IBD. Whether IUS exposure influences parent preferences for disease-monitoring strategies remains unknown.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of parents of children with IBD at a tertiary center. Parents, recruited from a prospective IBD biobank with linked clinical data, were stratified by prior IUS exposure based on clinical records/imaging history. The survey assessed parent preferences, perceived discomfort, and perceived usefulness for five monitoring modalities (IUS, colonoscopy, cross-sectional imaging [magnetic resonance imaging/computed tomography], blood tests, and stool studies), as well as parent activation (parent-patient activation measure), medication adherence (parent-adapted Morisky Medication Adherence Scale), and visit impact.
RESULTS: Sixty-two parents completed the survey (31 IUS-experienced, 31 IUS-naïve). Compared with IUS-naïve parents, IUS-experienced parents were more likely to report definite preference for IUS (83% vs. 36%, p = 0.003), rate IUS as completely useful (67% vs. 27%, p = 0.002), and report no perceived discomfort with IUS (90% vs. 68%, p = 0.01); conversely, they were more likely to report great discomfort with cross-sectional imaging (37% vs. 12%, p = 0.04). Trends toward greater perceived visit benefit included higher trust in physician recommendations (97% vs. 81%, p = 0.07) and greater sense of control over their child's IBD (90% vs. 71%, p = 0.08). Parent activation and adherence were high across groups. Qualitative responses highlighted reassurance, speed, and noninvasiveness of IUS.
CONCLUSIONS: Parents report strong acceptance of IUS, with prior exposure associated with greater preference, perceived usefulness, and lower perceived burden.

articles.title: Pediatric methemoglobinemia in the emergency department: etiology, treatment patterns, and short-term outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to characterize the clinical and etiological features of pediatric methemoglobinemia presenting to a pediatric emergency department, with particular attention to procedure-related local anesthetic exposure, and to explore short-term treatment responses to methylene blue and intravenous ascorbic acid.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients presenting between November 1, 2022 1 November 2022 1 November 2022, and November 1, 2025 1 November 2025 1 November 2025, with methemoglobin levels ≥ 5% measured by co-oximetry. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, G6PD, genetic, and disposition data were collected. Baseline characteristics and early treatment responses were compared between patients receiving methylene blue and intravenous ascorbic acid.
RESULTS: Twenty-four patients were included; the median age was 4 months (IQR, 2-5), and 21 (87.5%) were male. Median initial SpO2 was 88% (IQR, 85%-90%), initial methemoglobin was 25.5% (IQR, 21.4%-30.6%), and post-treatment methemoglobin was 5.8% (IQR, 2.6%-8.3%). Drug exposure accounted for 19 cases (79.2%), most commonly lidocaine (n = 10) and prilocaine (n = 7). Among the five patients without documented oxidant exposure, two had pathogenic CYB5R3 variants and two had likely pathogenic CYB5R3 variants. Eleven patients received methylene blue and 13 received intravenous ascorbic acid. Post-treatment methemoglobin was lower with methylene blue (2.6% vs. 7.8%; p = 0.024), whereas relative reduction did not differ significantly (88.8% vs. 72.8%; p = 0.118).
CONCLUSION: Methemoglobinemia predominantly affected young infants and was most often associated with procedure-related local anesthetic exposure, particularly in the context of circumcision. Topical oropharyngeal anesthetic exposure before intubation should also be recognized as a potential source of oxidant exposure. Treatment comparisons were exploratory, and underlying enzymatic or genetic susceptibility should be considered even when an acquired oxidant exposure is identified.

articles.title: Transabdominal ultrasound as a radiation-free tool for objective assessment of faecal burden in children with constipation and colorectal disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the utility of transabdominal ultrasound in children with colorectal pathology (anorectal malformation, functional constipation and Hirschsprung's disease) to assess the outcome of bowel management. Collect data to calculate age-dependent cut-offs of the transrectal diameter (TRD) in children with faecal load.
METHODS: Prospective cohort study with subgrouping for a-/symptomatic patients and a healthy control group. Derived control group for adjusting sex-ratio in patients with Hirschsprung's disease (4:1 ratio for male to female). 380 patients during a 31-month period were included. The transrectal diameter was measured routinely during the bowel management program after 1/3/6 months. Treatment options were oral laxatives, transanal irrigation or combination of both. For calculation of an age-dependent TRD cut-off, receiver operating characteristic, linear regression and locally estimated scatterplot smoothing were determined. The cut-off value was chosen based on a positive likelihood ratio > 10. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated by the area under the curve, sensitivity and specificity.
RESULTS: In the symptomatic subgroups of all cohorts the median values of TRD were significantly elevated compared to asymptomatic subgroups or control groups (p < 0.001). Successful bowel management had a large to very large effect on the TRD (Cohen's d = 1.05 - 1.81) and mean values were significantly lower (p = 0.015 - 0.001). TRD and age showed a minor association with a non-linear positive trend without significant influence after age stratification. Receiver operating characteristics determined a collective cut-off for all cohorts of 2.985 cm in children ≥ 1 year old (positive likelihood ratio = 36.09; sensitivity = 81.92 %; specificity = 97.73 %; area under the curve = 0.91 (95%-CI 0.87 - 0.94); accuracy = 88.67 %).
CONCLUSIONS: Measuring the TRD is a radiation-free alternative method to assess faecal loading and monitoring response to bowel management in patients with colorectal pathology. TRD was consistently increased in symptomatic patients and decreased following successful treatment. Diagnostic thresholds were close to 3 cm across all cohorts, with good diagnostic performance. This study extends patient cohorts for transabdominal ultrasound and supports further multicentre validation of a standardized ultrasound protocol.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: An appraisal of the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition clinical practice guidelines.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinical practice guidelines produced by the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (NASPGHAN) guide clinical decision-making across pediatric gastroenterology in North America, yet their methodological quality has not been systematically evaluated. We aimed to assess the quality of NASPGHAN clinical practice guidelines using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation II (AGREE-II) instrument.
METHODS: We identified 11 NASPGHAN clinical practice guidelines published between 2005 and 2024. Each guideline was independently appraised by ≥4 reviewers using the AGREE-II tool, which evaluates six domains across 23 items on a 1-7 scale. Scaled domain scores were calculated according to the AGREE-II rubric. To assess reproducibility, domain-specific and pooled intraclass correlation coefficients were estimated using linear mixed-effects models with crossed random effects for raters and items.
RESULTS: Domain scores varied substantially across guidelines. Scope and Purpose (mean 83.8%, SD 7.6) and Clarity of Presentation (mean 80.4%, SD 9.9) received the highest ratings, reflecting clear objectives, defined target populations, and well-structured recommendations. Stakeholder Involvement (mean 58.1%, SD 7.8) and Applicability (mean 53.6%, SD 5.1) scored lowest, indicating limited reporting of patient or caregiver engagement, implementation tools, barriers, or resource implications. Inter-rater reliability ranged from poor to moderate across AGREE-II domains, consistent with the subjectivity inherent in AGREE II scoring and variability in guideline reporting detail.
CONCLUSIONS: NASPGHAN guidelines demonstrate strengths in defining scope and presenting recommendations clearly. Opportunities for improvement include greater stakeholder involvement, enhanced transparency in guideline development methodology and conflict-of-interest reporting, and clearer guidance on implementation and resource considerations.

articles.title: Evolution of the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across three COVID-19 waves in Central Kerala: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical profile, laboratory findings, cardiac manifestations, treatment patterns and outcomes of children diagnosed with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves of the COVID-19 pandemic.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study.
SETTING: A tertiary care teaching hospital in Central Kerala, India.
PARTICIPANTS: 95 children fulfilling established diagnostic criteria for MIS-C admitted between November 2020 and December 2022 were included. Patients were categorised into three groups according to the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant wave: Alpha (wave 1), Delta (wave 2) and Omicron (wave 3).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, echocardiographic findings, treatment modalities and markers of disease severity, including duration of hospitalisation, intensive care stay, oxygen requirement, inotropic support and ventilator support.
RESULTS: Gastrointestinal symptoms remained the predominant presentation across all three waves, whereas respiratory symptoms increased during the later waves. Mucocutaneous manifestations varied significantly across waves (p=0.02). The duration of hospital stay (p=0.004), duration of fever (p=0.009) and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (p=0.003) decreased significantly over successive waves, suggesting reduced overall disease severity. Pericardial effusion also decreased significantly (p=0.002), while the prevalence of left ventricular dysfunction showed a declining trend. In contrast, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave (p<0.0001). Oxygen requirement declined significantly in the third wave (p=0.02), whereas intensive care stay, inotropic support and ventilator support did not differ significantly between waves.
CONCLUSIONS: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement. The marked increase in coronary artery dilatation during the Omicron wave highlights the importance of continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up, even during clinically milder phases of the pandemic.

articles.title: Fathers' role conflicts and identity reconstruction in paediatric palliative care: A qualitative systematic review and meta-synthesis of qualitative studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although family-centred care is the guiding model in paediatric palliative care, mothers are frequently assumed to be the primary caregivers, while fathers' role experiences and unique needs have long been neglected-rendering them "forgotten caregivers".
OBJECTIVE: To systematically synthesize qualitative studies on fathers' role experiences in paediatric palliative care and to gain an in-depth understanding of the challenges they face, coping strategies, and psychological growth trajectories.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted across six databases. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) approach for qualitative synthesis was used for quality appraisal and data synthesis.
RESULTS: Eight studies were included. Four synthesized themes were identified: (1) Masculinity and the maternal-centric medical system intertwine, obscuring fathers' unique needs; (2) torn between economic provision expectations and caregiving desire, fathers fall into a deep role predicament; (3) confronted with structural exclusion, fathers adjust by seeking informational control and partnering with the mother; and (4) adversity catalyses transformation, leading to the reconstruction of fatherhood identity and meaning.
CONCLUSION: Fathers are systematically marginalized in paediatric palliative care, which conceals both their needs and vulnerabilities. Fathers possess caregiving willingness but develop instrumental coping pathways due to structural exclusion, ultimately transforming their identity.
IMPACT: Clinically, the default "mother-as-primary-carer" communication model should be disrupted, and father-friendly, skill-oriented, peer-supported services should be developed. At the policy level, fathers need to be recognized as core members of the care team, thereby advancing palliative care from "mother-centred" to truly family-centred care.

articles.title: Enhancing Rural and Indigenous Pediatric Dermatology: A Scoping Review and Practical Algorithm for Primary Care.
articles.abstract: Children living in rural and remote Canadian communities, including many First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities, face substantial barriers to timely dermatologic care. We conducted a scoping review of common pediatric skin conditions in these settings and used the findings, supplemented by established clinical guidance and expert input, to develop a practical diagnostic and management algorithm for front-line clinicians. The review focuses on inflammatory, infectious, and environmental conditions commonly encountered in primary care and highlights contextual factors that may influence presentation, treatment, and outcomes, including geographic isolation, limited specialist access, crowded housing, water insecurity, and extreme weather exposure. The proposed algorithm is intended to support initial assessment, treatment, and referral while identifying persistent evidence gaps and the need for culturally safe, community-informed models of care.

articles.title: Personal and environmental factors associated with allergic disorders among adolescents in Lusaka, Zambia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between wheezing, allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema and selected environmental, lifestyle and personal factors among school-going adolescents aged 13–14 years.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional study.
SETTING: Participants were enrolled from schools in Lusaka, Zambia.
PARTICIPANTS: Adolescents aged 13–14 years attending urban schools.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOMES: Three primary outcomes including symptoms of asthma (wheeze), rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema were determined using the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood–Global Asthma Network questionnaire. Multivariate mixed effect logistic regression models were used to assess the association between selected exposure variables and each outcome. The study was reviewed and approved by the Levy Mwanawasa Medical University Research Ethics Committee (ref: LMMU-REC 00003/21) and the Zambian National Health Research Authority (ref: NHRA 0000001/23/03/2022). The Ministry of Education, headquarters in Lusaka, gave permission to access the schools (ref: MOE/101/1/45). All participants assented while their guardians consented.
RESULTS: The prevalence of symptoms of asthma (current wheeze), allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema was 13.6%, 11.8% and 6.5%, respectively. In mixed-effect multivariable analysis, exposure to environmental pollutants including smoke from cigarettes, vehicle emissions, use of charcoal and pet exposure as well as lifestyle factors such as physical activity and frequent paracetamol intake were significantly associated with all the outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates a significant burden of allergic diseases among adolescents in this population. Additionally, the study reveals an association between these symptoms and modifiable environmental, lifestyle and personal factors. Although further studies are needed to elucidate the observed associations, the findings highlight the potential benefit of reduced exposure to indoor and outdoor air pollutants, promotion of healthier lifestyle choices among adolescents and encouraging cautious use of paracetamol

articles.title: An observational study protocol characterising pain trajectories, opioid use and predictors of chronic postsurgical pain in children with cerebral palsy undergoing orthopaedic surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Children with cerebral palsy (CP) are likely at greater risk for developing chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) due to their high prevalence of pre-existing pain and frequency of orthopaedic procedures. However, little is known about the prevalence, trajectories and risk factors of CPSP or persistent opioid use among children with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Understanding CPSP and patterns of postoperative opioid use in this population is crucial to optimise perioperative pain management, inform opioid stewardship practices, improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare use and costs.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This multi-site, prospective, longitudinal study aims to recruit 450 children aged 5–17 years with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Participants will complete study assessments from 1 month before surgery to 12 months postoperatively. Study measures include preoperative quantitative sensory testing; caregiver-reported and child-reported (for participants ≥8 years who are cognitively able) assessments of pain and psychosocial factors at five time points; real-time postoperative text message assessments of pain and opioid use; and postoperative gait laboratory measures of functional outcomes. Demographic and surgical, and clinical data, including medical history, inpatient postoperative pain scores and analgesic medication use, will be extracted from the electronic medical record.
