Analysis will (1) characterise the postoperative pain and opioid use trajectories, (2) identify predictors of CPSP and persistent opioid use and (3) examine relationships between perioperative pain severity and the functional mobility outcomes achieved via orthopaedic surgery.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Central and local Institutional Review Boards at each site have approved the study. Study results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journal publications and presentations at scientific conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05764681.

articles.title: Associations of academic time burden with depressive and anxiety symptoms in adolescents: A prospective multi-analytical study based on the Guangzhou Children and Adolescents Cohort.
articles.abstract: Academic pressure is a pervasive source of stress among secondary school students, and has been linked to higher risks of depression and anxiety. However, the association of academic time burden with depressive and anxiety symptoms, and the behavioral and symptom-level patterns involved, remain insufficiently understood. Using data from the Guangzhou Children and Adolescents Cohort, this study aimed to investigate whether self-reported academic time was longitudinally associated with elevated depressive and anxiety symptoms among adolescents. We curated the homework time, tutoring time, health-related behaviors, and depressive (CES-D-20) and anxiety (GAD-7) symptoms reported by participants, yielding depression (n = 9671, 44.7% girls) and anxiety (n = 4680, 41.1% girls) cohorts. Mixed-effects regression showed that longer homework time was significantly associated with both elevated depressive (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.03-1.15 per hour increase) and anxiety symptoms (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.02-1.19), with similar patterns for tutoring time (depressive: OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.08; anxiety: OR = 1.15, 95% CI: 1.10-1.21). Sleep duration mediated 20.4% and 26.9% of the associations of homework time with depressive and anxiety symptoms, respectively. The corresponding proportions for tutoring time were 9.5% and 2.1%, with the latter being non-significant. Network analysis revealed that baseline academic time was associated with somatic symptoms and uncontrollable worry during follow-up, and that anxiety and depressive symptoms were reciprocally associated over time. These findings add to the rationale for policies that regulate academic time and highlight sleep protection as a promising target for adolescent mental health.

articles.title: Relationship Between Timing of Surgery and Procedure-Specific Outcomes in Neonates and Infants for Congenital Heart Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Determining the right timing for neonatal heart surgery remains difficult. In a large multicenter cohort, we studied the relationship between birthweight, timing of surgery, and outcomes to identify optimal surgical timing.
METHODS: Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database from 2010-2022, we retrospectively reviewed infants who underwent surgery within 90 days of birth. Procedures analyzed included coarctation of aorta (CoA), ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair, atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) repair, tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, Norwood procedure, and arterial switch operation (ASO). Birthweight, prematurity, and genetic syndromes were analyzed as predictors of operative mortality using categorical and continuous models, including nonlinear spline analysis. Patients were divided into five birthweight categories for risk comparison.
RESULTS: The cohort included 35,315 patients: 26,367(74.7%) neonates and 8,948(25.3%) infants. Low birthweight (<2500g) was present in 15.8% of neonates and 59.9% of infants. Operative mortality was highest in the 0-1kg group (9%, p<0.001). Continuous birthweight was a predictor of mortality (OR=0.45 per 100g increase; 95% CI: 0.40-0.51; p<0.0001). Neonatal age at surgery, prematurity, and genetic syndromes were independently associated with increased mortality. For Norwood procedures, mortality increased below 1.8kg and before 5 days of age; for ASOs, lowest risk occurred between 1.8-3.5kg and after 5 days of age. In AVSD, VSD, and CoA, neither birthweight nor timing significantly affected mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Except for Norwood and ASO procedures, weight and timing had limited impact on mortality, supporting individualized surgical decision-making rather than reliance on historical weight thresholds.

articles.title: Vitamin C Status in Children and Young Adults with Epidermolysis Bullosa.
articles.abstract: Recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB) predisposes to malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies. In a retrospective cohort from a multidisciplinary EB clinic, 7 of 24 (29.2%) patients with RDEB had ascorbic acid concentrations consistent with deficiency. We recommend empiric vitamin C for all patients 4 years and older with RDEB.

articles.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Based Dietary Advice: A Scoping Review of Nutritional Accuracy, Safety, and Eating-Related Risks.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This scoping review aimed to synthesize current evidence on generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based dietary advice, with particular attention to nutritional accuracy, safety, weight-management guidance, eating-related harm, and professional safeguards.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, refined by Levac et al., and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Embase were searched up to 30 June 2026. Original empirical studies evaluating generative AI or large language models for dietary advice, meal planning, nutritional information, weight management, or eating-disorder-related guidance were eligible. Study selection, data charting, and synthesis were performed independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus or third-reviewer assessment.
RESULTS: Nine studies published between 2023 and 2026 were included. In this small and emerging evidence base, one study reported 84.38% accuracy on an objective nutrition-literacy assessment, and another found overall Diet Quality Index-International scores above 70 for chatbot-generated weight-loss plans. However, important limitations were identified in caloric accuracy, portion sizing, macronutrient and micronutrient balance, reproducibility, personalization, and management of food allergies and multimorbidity. Potential safety concerns were identified in adolescent and eating-disorder scenarios, where chatbot responses sometimes combined appropriate healthy-eating advice with restrictive or weight-focused recommendations; these studies did not establish resulting clinical or behavioral harm. Although some systems encouraged consultation with healthcare professionals, safety warnings and referral to regulated resources were inconsistent.
CONCLUSION: Evidence from the nine included studies remains preliminary, heterogeneous, and largely simulation-based. Generative AI may have a supplementary role in nutrition education and preliminary dietary guidance, but the available evidence is insufficient to support autonomous use in place of dietitians. Current findings indicate potential safety risks in high-risk or clinically complex scenarios rather than demonstrated long-term harm. Longitudinal and real-world studies are needed to establish the clinical and behavioral effects of AI-generated dietary advice.

articles.title: Survival after neonatal chest compressions at birth: Temporal trends and prognostic factors in a population-based cohort, Queensland, Australia.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine temporal trends and prognostic factors for 28-day survival among infants receiving chest compressions (CC) in Queensland, Australia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using the Queensland Perinatal Data Collection (2008-2024), including all liveborn CC recipients at birth. Temporal trends in crude 28-day survival were examined overall and by gestational age (GA) groups. Multivariable generalised estimating equations were used to identify factors independently associated with survival while accounting for clustering within birthing locations.
RESULTS: Among 3,077 CC recipients, 70.5% established regular spontaneous breathing within 60 minutes of birth, and 89.0% survived to 28 days. Crude 28-day survival improved from 82% in 2008 to 89% in 2024 and was consistently higher in term (GA ≥37+0 weeks) than preterm infants. Compared with term infants, adjusted odds of survival declined with decreasing GA: 32+0 to 36+6 weeks (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.77), 28+0 to 31+6 weeks (aOR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.54), and <28+0 weeks (aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.12-0.23). However, after adjusting for cord pH or epinephrine administration, survival in infants born at 32+0 to 36+6 weeks did not differ significantly from term infants.
CONCLUSION: Survival to 28 days among CC recipients was high and increased over time. Lower gestational age was the strongest independent prognostic factor for mortality, although the survival difference between term and moderate-to-late preterm infants was attenuated after adjustment for cord pH or epinephrine administration. Prospective studies assessing CC indications and measures of resuscitation quality are needed to optimise neonatal resuscitation and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Neisseria meningitidis carriage in university students following a group B invasive meningococcal disease outbreak in Kent, England.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In March 2026, an invasive meningococcal disease outbreak in South-East England included 21 cases in young adults. In May 2026, we aimed to investigate carriage of meningococci in nearby universities, including the outbreak strain group B (MenB) ST-485 subtype P1·12-1,16-183.
METHODS: Students aged ≥18 years attending three university campuses completed a risk factor questionnaire an oropharyngeal swab for culture. Meningococcal isolates underwent serogrouping and whole genome sequencing. Carriage prevalences were estimated using the Clopper-Pearson exact binomial method. Associations between demographic or behavioural characteristics and carriage were assessed using modified Poisson regression.
RESULTS: Among 1,991 participants, 76 meningococcal isolates were identified, including 18 (23·7%) genogroup B. Three isolates (3·9%) were ciprofloxacin resistant. The outbreak strain was not detected. Overall meningococcal carriage was 4·8% (95% CI 3·6-6·1%) among 1,242 non-prophylaxed participants and 2·3% (1·3-3·6%) among 747 participants who received ciprofloxacin prophylaxis 6-9 weeks earlier. Higher carriage was associated with residence in shared accommodation (prevalence ratio 2·21, 95% CI 1·19-4·41) compared to a family home and combined smoking/vaping (1·90, 1·10-3·25), while chemoprophylaxis (0·27, 0·15-0·46) and Asian (0·44, 0·22-0·85) or Black (0·17, 0·05-0·42) compared to White ethnicity were associated with lower carriage.
CONCLUSION: Lack of outbreak strain carriage may reflect a highly virulent strain and the impact of outbreak control measures. The low overall carriage rate continues a decline in carriage among adolescents and young adults over the past 25 years. Meningococcal carriage was lower in chemoprophylaxed students but rapid recolonisation suggests short-lived protection in semi-closed populations with ongoing mixing.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy for severe dengue with multiorgan failure: a case report and focused review.
authors: Medauar Reis de Andrade Moreira F
articles.abstract: Severe dengue can progress to acute liver failure, haemolysis, encephalopathy, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction, but the role of therapeutic plasma exchange in treatment remains uncertain. We report a 17-year-old adolescent with NS1-positive dengue managed with continuous renal replacement therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange, and comprehensive intensive care, and provide a focused narrative review of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue. The patient developed abrupt massive intravascular haemolysis, profound anaemia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, encephalopathy requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, oliguric acute kidney injury, shock, and acute liver failure. She also met five of eight HLH-2004 criteria for secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated before three therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, beginning with an exchange of 1·5 estimated plasma volumes using fresh frozen plasma. Haemodynamic, hepatic, renal, and coagulation parameters subsequently improved. Secondary infection and haemothorax requiring video-assisted thoracoscopic drainage complicated recovery; she was discharged 38 days after admission. Published evidence on the use of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue consists mainly of case reports, small series, and observational cohorts. Therapeutic plasma exchange can be considered an adjunctive rescue therapy in selected refractory cases, particularly acute liver failure or thrombotic microangiopathy phenotypes, but its independent benefit, optimal timing, prescription, and target population remain undefined.

articles.title: A phase 2, open-label, single-arm clinical trial of the safety and efficacy of the JAK1/3 inhibitor tofacitinib in Down syndrome.
articles.abstract: Down syndrome (DS) is characterized by strong immune dysregulation and hyperactive interferon/JAK/STAT signaling. We report a phase 2, open-label, single-arm clinical trial testing the JAK1/3 inhibitor tofacitinib in persons with DS and immune skin conditions. Participants received treatment for up to 9 months with extensive safety monitoring and assessments of biomarkers, skin pathology, and neuropsychological measures. The primary safety endpoint was met, with tofacitinib showing a safety profile similar to that observed in the general population. Tofacitinib decreases interferon scores, cytokine scores, and neurotoxic immunometabolites without overt immune suppression. Participants experienced benefits for immunodermatological conditions, most prominently hidradenitis suppurativa and alopecia areata, and improvements in multiple neuropsychological assessments. Multi-omics analyses reveal specific inflammatory pathways modulated by tofacitinib in DS. Given the lack of a placebo control arm, efficacy findings remain exploratory. These results support JAK inhibition as a safe strategy to attenuate immune dysregulation in DS. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04246372).

articles.title: Development and psychometric properties of the scale of perceived safe care among hospitalized children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a child-reported scale for assessing perceived safe care among hospitalized children aged 7-12 years and to examine its psychometric properties.
METHODS: This methodological scale-development study was conducted between 15 March and 15 June 2026 with 410 hospitalized children in pediatric clinics in three provinces. A 32-item pool underwent expert content review and pilot testing; the resulting 20-item draft was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 205) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 205) in non-overlapping analytic datasets.
RESULTS: EFA yielded a 13-item, two-factor structure. In the final Principal Axis Factoring solution, the two extracted factors accounted for 50.833% of the variance after extraction (43.812% and 7.020%, respectively); the first two initial eigenvalues were 6.182 and 1.385, whereas the third was 0.841. The correlation matrix was suitable for factor analysis (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin [KMO] = 0.895; Bartlett's χ2 = 1279.755, df = 78, p < 0.001). CFA supported an acceptable-to-good fit (χ2 = 126.505, df = 60, χ2/df = 2.108, root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) = 0.074, 90% confidence interval (CI) 0.056-0.092, comparative fit index (CFI) = 0.951, incremental fit index (IFI) = 0.952, Tucker-Lewis index (TLI) = 0.937, standardized root mean square residual (SRMR) = 0.061). The two factors were named Perceived Safety and Protection and Information and Supportive Care. Internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = 0.904; McDonald's ω = 0.903). The total score correlated positively with the Assessment of Care Quality Through Children's Eyes Scale (r = 0.709, 95% CI 0.657-0.754, p < 0.001) and negatively with the Perceived Stress Scale for Kids (r = -0.514, 95% CI -0.582 to -0.439, p < 0.001). Two of the three prespecified hypotheses were fully supported; the structural hypothesis received qualified support because the two-factor representation was supported, although evidence for factor distinctness was mixed.
CONCLUSION: The scale provided preliminary evidence of content validity, structural validity, hypothesis-based construct validity, and internal consistency for assessing hospitalized children's perceptions of safe care. Further testing of temporal stability, measurement invariance, responsiveness, and external validity in independent and diverse samples is warranted.
PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: The scale may be used as a child-reported measure to describe perceived safe care and to support pediatric nursing research and quality-improvement activities; it should not be interpreted as a substitute for objective patient-safety indicators.

articles.title: The effect of web-based education and therapeutic play methods provided to children undergoing elective surgery on preoperative anxiety and fear, and postoperative pain and sleep: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of combining web-based education provided at home with therapeutic play implemented in the hospital on preoperative anxiety and fear, as well as postoperative pain and sleep, in children aged 7-12 years undergoing elective surgery.
DESIGN: Randomized controlled experimental study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study included 78 children aged 7-12 years who underwent elective surgery. The children were randomly assigned to two groups: intervention (n = 37) and control (n = 41). Children in the intervention group received web-based education about the surgical process at home and information through therapeutic play at the hospital, whereas the control group received standard preoperative nursing care. Data were collected using the Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale-Short Form (mYPAS-SF), Child Fear Scale (CFS), Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale (WBFPS), and Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC).
RESULTS: The preoperative mYPAS-SF and CFS scores, as well as the postoperative WBFPS scores, were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (p < 0.05), with effect sizes indicating large clinical significance. No significant difference was found between the groups in terms of post-discharge SDSC scores (p > 0.05), and the effect size was clinically small.
CONCLUSION: Providing preoperative preparation education using a combination of web-based education and therapeutic play was effective in reducing preoperative anxiety and fear and postoperative pain in children undergoing elective surgery; however, it did not affect improving sleep.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Pediatric nurses can help reduce children's preoperative anxiety, fear, and postoperative pain in children scheduled for surgery by using effective, practical, web-based educational and therapeutic play methods tailored to the children's age and developmental characteristics in pediatric surgery clinics.

articles.title: Configurations of family and socioeconomic circumstances and registered outcomes among children investigated by child welfare services in Sweden: A latent class analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children investigated by child welfare services (CWS) are often exposed to multiple, co-occurring family and socioeconomic difficulties. Less is known about how such circumstances cluster within this population and whether different configurations are associated with different outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To identify profiles of family and socioeconomic circumstances among children investigated by CWS and examine their associations with criminal justice involvement, mental health-related medication use, and school performance.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The source cohort comprised 1764 children aged 7-12 years investigated by CWS in Stockholm, Sweden, in 2019 following concerns of maltreatment. The latent class analytic sample included 1660 children with complete data on six class indicators.
METHODS: Latent class analysis was conducted using indicators of foreign background, single-parent household, large household size, low income, persistent parental unemployment, and parental criminal conviction. Associations with distal outcomes were estimated using two-step maximum-likelihood models that retained uncertainty in latent class membership and adjusted for age or birth cohort and sex, as appropriate. Confidence intervals were obtained using 600 nonparametric bootstrap replications.
RESULTS: Three partly overlapping profiles were identified: Multiple adversity (38.3%), Low income and foreign background (21.1%), and Lower adversity (40.6%). In outcome-specific analyses, the Multiple adversity profile had higher odds of antidepressant medication use (OR = 1.79, 95% CI [1.27, 2.69]) and ADHD medication use (OR = 1.53, 95% CI [1.07, 2.45]) than the Lower adversity profile. The Low income and foreign background profile had higher odds of low school performance (OR = 1.96, 95% CI [1.09, 3.12]) than the Lower adversity profile. Associations with criminal justice outcomes were imprecise. None of the 15 pairwise outcome-profile contrasts remained statistically significant after Holm correction for multiple testing.
CONCLUSIONS: Children investigated by CWS showed heterogeneous and partly overlapping configurations of family and socioeconomic circumstances. Outcome-specific patterns suggest that different configurations may be associated with different domains of functioning, but the findings should be considered exploratory given the multiple-testing results. Replication with longer follow-up and richer measures of family processes and child functioning is needed.

articles.title: Extreme temperatures and child neglect: A nationwide case-crossover study of Brazilian children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neglect is the most frequently reported but least studied form of child maltreatment. Because it arises in part from the conditions under which care is provided, neglect may be sensitive to environmental stressors associated with a warming climate. As an act of omission, it may also respond to heat through pathways distinct from those implicated in abusive behavior. However, population-level evidence on this association remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between heat and child neglect in a middle-income setting and examine heterogeneity across child and case characteristics.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: 150,163 notifications of neglect or abandonment involving children aged 0 to 9, recorded in Brazil's national violence notification system across 3428 municipalities, 2012 to 2019.
METHODS: Time-stratified case-crossover analysis with conditional logistic regression. Each child served as their own control, matched on municipality, calendar month, year, and day of week. Exposure was municipal daily maximum temperature, categorized with 27 to 30 °C as reference.
RESULTS: Odds of child neglect increase with temperature. On days of 33 °C or above, odds were 6.0% higher than at 27 to 30 °C (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09). Below 24 °C, they were 6.0% lower (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.96). Findings were robust to alternative event dates, reference categories, and municipality exclusions. No variation appeared by sex or race. Exploratory age comparison suggested a larger association among children aged 5 to 9 than among those aged 0 to 4 (ratio of odds ratios 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.18, p = 0.017), although the difference did not meet the Bonferroni-adjusted threshold.
CONCLUSIONS: Heat is measurably associated with child neglect. Exploratory analyses suggest that these associations are larger in older children, though this effect does not persist after correction for multiple comparisons. Child welfare research and practice should consider environmental conditions as a potentially relevant and modifiable context.

articles.title: Parents' Perspectives on the Use and Development of Predictive AI in Neonatology: Focus Group Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predictive AI models, such as AI-generated early warning systems for detecting critical conditions, are being praised as promising applications in neonatology. Despite technological advancements in predictive AI, the integration of AI at the bedside remains challenging, and few AI technologies are currently integrated into routine neonatal care. A better understanding of the wishes and barriers of patients and, in the case of neonatal patients, their parents, is essential to bridge this gap. Yet, parental perspectives on the use of AI remain underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: This study explored the perspectives of parents whose child had previously been admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit about the development and use of predictive AI in neonatal clinical settings.
METHODS: We conducted 3 focus groups with 18 Dutch parents of children admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit to explore their views on AI in neonatal care. Participants were purposively recruited via a neonatology parent and patient organization. Discussions focused on predictive AI in acute settings and on AI to predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in later life. A reflexive thematic analysis of the focus group data was performed.
RESULTS: Parents generally welcomed predictive AI as a supportive tool for the medical team, anticipating improvements in patient outcomes. AI for short-term predictions was especially appreciated, whereas longer-term predictions were received with some reservations. Overarching concerns regarding predictive AI systems included AI undermining parental intuition, overreliance on AI in decision-making, and undesirable ethical and psychological implications of long-term health predictions. Interestingly, in addition to predictive AI systems that support medical judgment, parents also hoped that other AI tools could be developed to better involve parental input in the decision-making process. Specifically, they envisioned applications that extend beyond clinical decision support to provide parents with information, emotional support, and tailored guidance on the right course of action.
CONCLUSIONS: Parental perspectives highlight both opportunities and challenges for predictive AI integration in neonatal care. Engaging parents in the design and implementation of AI informs the development of family-centered, ethically responsible AI solutions and may identify opportunities for developing parent-centered AI tools alongside systems designed to support clinicians.

articles.title: Cranial Injuries due to Misuse of Infant Carriers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Infant carriers (car seats, bouncy chairs) can cause injuries when used for other than their intended purpose.
METHODS: We studied children aged 0-24 months with carrier related injuries reported to the Pennsylvania Trauma Outcome Study (PTOS) dataset (2001-2022 inclusive).
RESULTS: There were 562 injured children, averaging 23 injuries per year. Mean age was 3.3 months; 54.3% were male. Most (82.7%) fell from an elevated surface; 88.7% fell an estimated 2-5 feet. Head injuries (intracranial injury/hemorrhage and/or skull fracture) were present in 85.6%. Admission Glasgow Coma Scores were most commonly 15 (79.1%); 7 had GCS <12. Average Injury Severity Score was 9.3 (range 1-30). Average length of stay was 1.4 days; 30% spent >1 day in the intensive care unit. Two children underwent cranial operations. There were no deaths, and 82.9% were discharged home.
CONCLUSION: Falls in, or from, infant carriers are a significant public health concern. Education, advocacy, and changes in carrier design may help reduce the frequency of these injuries.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States.
articles.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates. We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating "late-small" and "early-large" epidemics. When the best-fit model including the RSV-associated term was used to predict the potential impact of RSV interventions on HMPV transmission, we found that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV. Our work unravels the spatiotemporal dynamics of HMPV and its interaction with RSV, informing future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV.

articles.title: Medical adhesive-related skin injuries and medical device-related pressure injuries in newborns: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (flexible). The objectives are as follows: To map information on the incidence, characteristics, risk factors, and preventive strategies for MDRPI and MARSI in newborns. Based on the findings, we hope to identify knowledge gaps and to guide future research, improve treatments, and reduce injuries.

articles.title: Pediatric forensic cases during the COVID 19 lockdown and reopening periods: a retrospective cohort study from a tertiary care pediatric emergency department.
articles.abstract: The COVID‑19 lockdown disrupted daily life, altering children's exposure to risks and reshaping emergency department utilisation. Understanding how these changes influenced pediatric forensic epidemiology is essential for prevention and policy development. All forensic cases involving children aged 1 month-18 years were included. Two periods were analysed: the COVID-19 lockdown period (March 2020-June 2021) and the post-lockdown period (June 2021-March 2024). Data on demographics, causes, outcomes and costs were extracted from medical and forensic records. During the COVID‑19 lockdown period, the incidence of forensic cases was 25.8 per 1000 PED visits per month, whereas during the reopening period this rate decreased to 12.7 per 1000 PED visits per month (p < 0.001). Exposure to chemical substances and assault were more frequent during the lockdown period (p = 0.01 and p = 0.001, respectively), whereas food poisoning was more common during the reopening period (p = 0.004). Forensic cases were predominant among female adolescents (p = 0.004). Male sex was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of forensic cases (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.05-1.49, p = 0.011). Furthermore, the COVID-19 lockdown period was independently associated with an increased odds of forensic cases (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.65-2.56, p < 0.001). The median outpatient and total bills per PED visit were lower in forensic cases (48.7 vs. 68.1 TRY, p < 0.001 and 57.8 vs. 90.2 TRY, p < 0.001, respectively). Different COVID‑19 periods were associated with significant differences in the incidence, causes, and patterns of pediatric forensic cases. Male sex and the lockdown period were identified as independent risk factors for forensic presentations, highlighting the complex interaction between demographic and temporal factors in forensic epidemiology.

articles.title: Longitudinal trends in early childhood sleep and napping behaviors.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Although most children discontinue daytime napping by six years of age, longitudinal evidence describing how napping changes over time remains limited. We examined 6-month changes in nap duration, frequency, timing, spontaneity, and proportion of daytime sleep in preschool-aged children.
METHODS: At baseline, 702 parents representative of the Canadian population completed surveys about their children aged 1 to 6 years, inclusive. Six months later, 162 parents reported on their child's napping (duration, frequency, timing, spontaneity, and proportion of daytime sleep) and nighttime sleep (duration and sleep problems). Children were categorized at baseline into nap profiles-regular, intermittent, spontaneous, or non-nappers-and changes were examined overall and within profiles.
RESULTS: Among children napping at baseline, 25.2% had ceased napping at follow-up, whereas 11% of baseline non-nappers resumed napping. Among children napping at both time points, nap duration and proportion of daytime sleep significantly decreased over 6 months. The largest reductions in nap duration were observed among regular nappers. Nap timing and spontaneity remained relatively stable. Nighttime sleep duration did not significantly change; however, nighttime sleep problems decreased over time.
CONCLUSION: Preschool nap behaviors are dynamic and vary by nap profile. Regular nappers exhibited the most pronounced reductions, while some non-nappers resumed napping. These findings support flexible, developmentally sensitive definitions of nap cessation and highlight the importance of individualized approaches to supporting sleep during early childhood.
CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Most research on preschool napping has focused on single sleep measures and has provided limited longitudinal evidence on how multiple nap behaviors change over time. This study examined 6-month changes in several dimensions of napping among children classified into distinct nap behavior profiles.
STUDY IMPACT: Preschool nap behaviors changed differently across nap profiles, with regular nappers showing the largest reductions in daytime sleep and some non-nappers resuming napping. These findings suggest that nap cessation is a dynamic process and support flexible, individualized approaches to defining and managing daytime sleep in early childhood.

articles.title: National survey of the clinical profile and management of patients with hereditary angioedema due to C1-inhibitor deficiency in Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare, often misdiagnosed disorder. Epidemiological data on this condition are scarce in Latin America, particularly in Colombia. This study aimed to describe the demographics, clinical features, and treatment of Colombian HAE patients in order to address data gaps.
METHODS: A web-based survey (Sept, 2021-Mar, 2023) of Colombian physicians managing HAE patients collected anonymous data on demographics, clinical features, and treatments. Statistical analyses compared patients receiving long-term prophylaxis (LTP) versus those who did not.
RESULTS: The survey included 42 physicians from 19 Colombian provinces, covering 274 HAE patients. Median age at symptom onset was 13 years, with a diagnostic delay of 8 years. Most patients were female (59.85%) and had a family history of HAE (83.58%). Attacks mainly affected peripheral, abdominal, and facial areas; common triggers included stress, trauma, and menstruation. Hospitalization was reported by 46.24% of patients, with 23.77% hospitalized in the preceding year and 4.96% requiring intubation. All received on-demand therapy, mainly icatibant (91.41%). Long-term prophylaxis was prescribed in 52.14% of cases, with danazol (66.67%), tranexamic acid (31.21%), and lanadelumab (17.02%). These patients had longer diagnostic delays and higher hospitalization rates compared to those not receiving prophylaxis (p < 0.01 and p = 0.01, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: This study shows significant diagnostic delays and treatment challenges for HAE in Colombia. Underreporting and geographic disparities suggest an underestimated prevalence. The findings underscore the urgent need for greater awareness, equitable access to therapies, and robust patient registries in order to address unmet needs and reduce the burden of HAE for affected individuals.

articles.title: Functional outcomes in pediatric colorectal surgery: a predictor-based analysis of Hirschsprung disease and anorectal malformation in a resource-limited setting.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Long-term fecal continence and bowel habit outcomes remain a significant challenge in pediatric colorectal surgery. This study evaluated long-term functional bowel outcomes in patients treated for Hirschsprung disease (HD) and Anorectal Malformations (ARM) using the standardized Rintala Bowel Function Score, identifying key clinical predictors of favorable outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at St. Paul's Hospital Millennium Medical College, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, among children who underwent definitive surgical repair for HD and ARM between January 2018 and December 2022. Functional bowel outcomes were evaluated using the Rintala Bowel Function Score (0-20 scale), with a score ≥ 17 defined as a clinically favorable outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to assess predictive factors.
RESULTS: A total of 136 patients were included: 94 with HD and 42 with ARM. In the HD cohort, the presence of associated congenital anomalies and colonic excision proximal to the splenic flexure were major negative predictors of bowel function, reducing the probability of a favorable outcome from 66 to 22% (p = 0.007) and from 75 to 28% (p = 0.008), respectively. In the ARM cohort, 100% of patients with low-severity malformations achieved favorable outcomes compared with 54.5% of those with high/intermediate-severity malformations (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: While anatomical severity appears to be an important factor influencing bowel function outcomes in ARM, associated systemic anomalies and the extent of colonic excision were also associated with poorer bowel function in children with HD. These findings highlight the potential importance of structured, long-term postoperative follow-up, with particular attention to children at higher risk of functional bowel problems.

articles.title: Nutrition in the Era of Incretin-Based Therapies: Clinical Strategies for Optimizing Care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review current evidence and practical nutrition strategies for patients receiving incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists, with a focus on nutritional adequacy, body composition, gastrointestinal tolerance, and long-term adherence.
RECENT FINDINGS: Incretin-based therapies have transformed obesity treatment by producing substantial weight loss and cardiometabolic improvement. However, these therapies are also associated with reduced oral intake, gastrointestinal adverse effects, lean mass loss, and potential micronutrient inadequacy, highlighting the need for comprehensive nutritional management. Emerging evidence supports individualized dietary strategies to improve tolerance and maintain nutritional status, including targeted approaches for constipation, diarrhea, nausea, and reflux, as well as considerations for special populations such as pati​ents with inflammatory bowel disease, short bowel syndrome, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and pediatric obesity. Nutrition care is a critical component of treatment with incretin-based therapies. Individualized dietary strategies may help preserve lean body mass, optimize nutrient intake, reduce gastrointestinal side effects, and support long-term adherence and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Pediatric total thyroidectomy and lobectomy; an analysis of surgeon specialty and outcomes for same-day discharge.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Our study aimed to evaluate differences in patient outcomes overall and by specialty for same-day discharge (SDD) following pediatric total thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy.
METHODS: Data from the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric (NSQIP-P) was used to evaluate thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy patients (2017-2021). For each operation, patients were categorized into SDD and those discharged 1-2 days post-operation (non-SDD). Postoperative outcomes were both analyzed overall and by surgeon specialty (pediatric and adult general surgery, pediatric and adult ENT).
RESULTS: NSQIP-P identified 2,622 patients. Rates of SDD increased from 2017 to 2021 for thyroidectomy (5.2% to 10.9%) and thyroid lobectomy (23.1% to 34.6%). The SDD rate was lower for pediatric general surgeons than for adult general or ENT surgeons for both operations (p < 0.001), without outcome differences. Regression demonstrated steroid use as a risk for readmission (OR 4.42, p = 0.026) and reoperation (OR 5.99, p = 0.047) following thyroidectomy.
CONCLUSION: SDD for pediatric patients undergoing thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy has increased without worsening outcomes. Some surgical specialties have increased rates of SDD without outcome differences. In carefully selected non-steroid using patients meeting specific criteria to optimize communication and minimize complication risks, SDD following pediatric thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy may be a safe option.

articles.title: Dysregulated serotonin reuptake impairs intestinal serotonin availability in human necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating gastrointestinal disease in preterm infants associated with impaired gut motility. We previously demonstrated that delayed gastric emptying correlates with intestinal injury severity in experimental NEC. Serotonin (5-HT) from enterochromaffin (EC) cells regulates intestinal motility and gastric emptying. We hypothesized that dysregulated 5-HT signaling contributes to NEC-associated dysmotility.
METHODS: Distal ileal tissues from NEC and non-NEC patients were analyzed by immunofluorescence for EC cells (CHGA), 5-HT, synthesis (TPH1), release (TRPA1), metabolism (MAO-A), and reuptake proteins (SERT, VMAT1). EC cell-enriched human intestinal organoids were generated, and forskolin-induced 5-HT release was assessed following SERT or VMAT1 inhibition.
RESULTS: EC cell number and expression of TPH1, TRPA1, and MAOA were unchanged in NEC ileum. In contrast, SERT and VMAT1 expression were increased in NEC tissues and patient-derived EC cell-enriched organoids. Reduced extracellular 5-HT levels in NEC organoids were restored following SERT or VMAT1 inhibition.
CONCLUSION: NEC is associated with increased 5-HT reuptake despite an unchanged EC cell population, resulting in reduced extracellular 5-HT availability. Dysregulated serotonin signaling may contribute to impaired gastric emptying and gut dysmotility in NEC, identifying serotonin reuptake as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Outcome After Late Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract: The optimal timing of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and severe pulmonary regurgitation remains controversial. Current recommendations rely largely on right ventricular volumetric thresholds derived from cohorts undergoing intervention during adolescence or early adulthood, although their prognostic value remains debated. To identify predictors of postoperative morbidity and mortality after PVR in patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF, with a specific focus on invasive preoperative hemodynamic parameters. We conducted a retrospective single-center study including patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF who underwent surgical PVR between 2009 and 2018. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint including supraventricular arrhythmia, cardiovascular rehospitalization, or all-cause death during follow-up. Clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Forty-eight patients (mean age at PVR 41 ± 9.8 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 52 months. The primary outcome occurred in 23 patients (48%). Preoperative signs of advanced disease, including right heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, and a history of syncope or ventricular tachycardia, were associated with adverse outcomes. Although right ventricular end-diastolic volumes were markedly increased in both groups, they were not associated with the primary outcome. Conversely, right ventricular end-systolic volume and, particularly, right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) showed stronger prognostic value. In multivariable analysis, RVEDP remained the only independent predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.01-3.40; p = 0.04). In adults aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF undergoing PVR, elevated RVEDP is a key predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality, whereas right ventricular end diastolic volumes on MRI are not. Invasive hemodynamic assessment may help refine the timing of PVR in this "senior" population.

articles.title: Schwannomas Visible on the Skin: Clinicopathological Characteristics and Treatment.
articles.abstract: Clinical information on schwannomas that are visible on the skin as (sub)cutaneous lesions is very limited. In this article, we provide clinicopathological information about cutaneous schwannomas and (deeper located) visible noncutaneous schwannomas including diagnostic methods, treatments, surgical complications and follow-up. This retrospective observational study includes data from 191 cases obtained from electronic healthcare records within a large teaching hospital with regional neurosurgical expertise. We show that 114 cutaneous and 77 visible noncutaneous schwannomas were painful (83%), slow-growing (68%), skin-coloured (48%) nodules (83%) on the head/neck and upper extremities (58%). Common features included pain after local pressure (72%), radiating pain (45%), tingling after percussion (63%) and mobility (88%). Imaging was performed in 63% (mainly ultrasound and MRI); pretreatment histologic examination in 9%. Excision was performed in 64%, intracapsular microenucleation in 31%. Complications occurred in 15% (8% in cutaneous schwannomas and 23% in visible noncutaenous schwannomas), most commonly sensory nerve deficits (12%). In conclusion, this study shows that visible schwannomas primarily present as painful, skin-coloured, mobile nodules on the head/neck and arms. Invasive treatment by excision and intracapsular microenucleation resulted in complications in 15% of patients, most commonly sensory nerve deficits. These occurred more often in deeply located visible noncutaneous schwannomas.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes After Dupilumab Initiation for Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether dupilumab initiation is associated with reduced short-term flare burden, healthcare utilization, and surgical escalation in pediatric patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP).
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: TriNetX United States Collaborative Network.
METHODS: Patients aged ≤18 years with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps were identified between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Dupilumab-treated patients were indexed at treatment initiation and propensity score-matched 1:1 to nondupilumab controls indexed at a systemic corticosteroid burst based on asthma, atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and prior endoscopic sinus surgery. Outcomes within 12 months were compared using risk ratios.
RESULTS: In 442 matched patients (221 per cohort), dupilumab-treated patients had lower rates of acute sinusitis (12/221 [5.4%] vs 31/221 [14.0%]; risk ratio [RR] 0.39; 95% CI: 0.20-0.73; P = .002), systemic corticosteroid bursts (80/221 [36.2%] vs 101/221 [45.7%]; RR 0.79; 95% CI: 0.63-0.99; P = .042), and functional endoscopic sinus surgery (19/221 [8.6%] vs 38/221 [17.2%]; RR 0.50; 95% CI: 0.30-0.84; P = .007). Nasal polyp diagnoses were more frequently documented in the dupilumab-treated cohort (148/221 [67.0%] vs 95/221 [43.0%]; P < .0001), while emergency department visits (16/221 [7.2%] vs 27/221 [12.2%]; P = .078) and inpatient admissions (12/221 [5.4%] vs 16/221 [7.2%]; P = .435) were similar between cohorts.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that dupilumab may be a steroid-sparing and surgery-sparing option in pediatric CRSwNP.

articles.title: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias.
OBSERVATIONS: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing health inequities; reducing stigma and bias; modernizing obesity care delivery; expanding access to lifestyle, healthy food, medication, and surgical interventions; and supporting long-term treatment adherence and maintenance. Proposed actions include new government policies on food production, labeling, marketing, and school nutrition; modernization of drug evaluation; payment reform to support comprehensive obesity treatment; development of multidisciplinary care models; incentives to promote cross-sector partnerships; and research to advance personalized prevention and treatment strategies.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The emergence of effective obesity management medications offers a significant opportunity to curb the prevalence of obesity. However, no single intervention will be enough. Sustained improvement will require addressing the underlying structural and environmental drivers of obesity, along with person-centered, multilevel strategies that simultaneously improve prevention, reduce stigma, and expand equitable access to evidence-based treatment. Coordinated action across government, health care systems, clinicians, payers, industry, schools, communities, and researchers will be essential to achieving long-term improvement.

articles.title: Brief Report: Short-Term Outcomes of Child-Child Sexual Interactions.
articles.abstract: There is much controversy over the potential effects of sexual interactions between similar-aged children, although little empirical data relevant to the question has been offered. Exploratory, non-violent, and non-coercive play is at times conflated with abusive interactions, with both lay and professional authors fearing that sexual exploration of any kind may lead to adverse outcomes. Problems with conflation of these two experiences emerge frequently in legal contexts, where experts are requested to comment on the potential consequences of child-child sexual encounters based on very little empirical information. To investigate such interactions, 25 children seen in forensic or clinical settings were examined utilizing the Trauma Symptom Checklist for Children (TSCC). Results showed limited potential negative outcomes, with no child meeting criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). One child did receive a borderline positive result and several were elevated on specific subscales, most commonly Sexual Concerns and Anxiety. In general, results suggest that child-child sexual interactions are not universally harmful, although specific reactions will vary due to family and cultural context.

articles.title: Serum serotonin levels in children with functional constipation: A prospective case-control study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Functional constipation is a common pediatric functional gastrointestinal disorder, but data on circulating serotonin are limited. This study compared fasting serum serotonin levels between children with functional constipation and healthy controls and examined associations with clinical characteristics.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, case-control study included children aged 4-18 years with Rome IV-defined functional constipation and healthy controls. Fasting serum serotonin was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Clinical characteristics, including fecal incontinence, body mass index categories, and treatment response, were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed discriminatory performance.
RESULTS: Seventy-four children were included: 37 with functional constipation and 37 controls. Age and sex distribution were similar. Serum serotonin levels were higher in children with functional constipation (174.1 ng/mL [interquartile range, IQR, 161.1-188.3] versus 160.5 ng/mL [IQR, 149.5-181.9]; p = 0.048). Children with fecal incontinence had higher serum serotonin levels in the unadjusted analysis (p = 0.031), but this finding did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. After excluding children with fecal incontinence, the between-group difference was no longer significant (p = 0.134). Levels were numerically higher in children with obesity, but differences across body mass index categories were not significant. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.628 (95% confidence interval, 0.496-0.759; p = 0.062).
CONCLUSIONS: Serum serotonin was modestly higher in children with functional constipation, but diagnostic utility was limited. These exploratory findings do not support its use as a diagnostic marker. Further studies are needed to clarify serotonin-related pathways in pediatric functional constipation.

articles.title: Genetic testing strategies for neonatal cholestasis in the neonatal intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cholestasis in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) has a broad differential diagnosis, including genetic diseases. Advances in next generation sequencing (NGS) have expanded the ability to identify genetic etiologies. Studies evaluating testing strategies, diagnostic yield, and clinical characteristics of those undergoing genetic testing for cholestasis in the NICU are limited.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied patients at a single-center Level IV NICU with cholestasis, genetic testing and Hepatology consultation between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Microarray, targeted gene panel and exome or genome sequencing (ES/GS) results and clinical characteristics of those tested were reviewed. Diagnostic yield was defined as identification of pathogenic variants determined to be causative of cholestasis. Categorical variables were compared using Chi-squared test or Fisher's exact as appropriate. Continuous variables were compared using Wilcoxon rank sum tests or Kruskal-Wallis tests as appropriate.
RESULTS: A total of 174 patients were included for analysis. Patients with three modalities of testing had higher peak direct bilirubin and alanine aminotransferase. Diagnostic yield increased by comprehensiveness: microarray 5% (3/54), targeted gene panel 10% (12/125) and ES/GS 33% (23/70). Seven patients with non-diagnostic targeted panels had diagnostic ES/GS. Those with diagnostic ES/GS were younger at Hepatology consultation, had higher peak direct bilirubin and were less likely to have sepsis compared to those with diagnostic targeted panels.
CONCLUSIONS: ES/GS demonstrated greater diagnostic yield for cholestasis in the NICU than other modalities. Confounding by year of testing is possible, but differences in yield support preferential use of ES/GS for neonatal cholestasis evaluation.

articles.title: Implementation of the PaliEnf Digital Technology Based on Standardized Nursing Languages to Improve Nursing Documentation in Pediatric Oncology Palliative Care.
articles.abstract: AimTo evaluate the effect of the PaliEnf application on the quality of nursing process documentation in pediatric oncology palliative care.MethodsThis quasi-experimental study compared pre- and post-intervention periods and was conducted in accordance with the Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Nonrandomized Designs (TREND) guidelines in a Pediatric Oncology Intensive Care Unit at a Brazilian national cancer referral center. The intervention consisted of implementing the PaliEnf application, a digital technology structured according to the NANDA International (NANDA-I), Nursing Interventions Classification (NIC), and Nursing Outcomes Classification (NOC) systems. Ten nurses were trained to use the application. The quality of nursing process documentation was assessed before and after the intervention using the Quality of Diagnoses, Interventions and Outcomes (Q-DIO) instrument. Comparisons between periods were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, adopting a significance level of 5%.ResultsA total of 40 medical records were analyzed, including 20 from the pre-intervention period and 20 from the post-intervention period. Significant improvement in nursing process documentation was observed following implementation of the PaliEnf application, with increased scores across all Q-DIO dimensions (p < 0.001). The overall Q-DIO score increased from a median of 16.5 (IQR: 15.75-19.75) to 43.5 (IQR: 41.00-44.25). The greatest improvements were identified in items related to diagnostic structuring, coherence among nursing diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes, and documentation of patients' clinical progress.ConclusionImplementation of the PaliEnf application was associated with significant improvement in the quality of nursing process documentation in pediatric oncology palliative care. The findings suggest that digital technologies grounded in standardized nursing languages may support structured documentation and improve the internal coherence of the nursing process in complex clinical settings. Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (REBEC): UTN U1111-1297-9546.

articles.title: Learning and memory profile in pediatric craniopharyngioma with and without associated sleep disturbance.
articles.abstract: Children and adolescents with craniopharyngioma are at increased risk for visual field cuts, endocrinopathies, associated sleep disturbances, and cognitive challenges. While general intellectual functioning tends to remain intact within this population, the sellar/suprasellar location of craniopharyngiomas can disrupt important neural pathways essential for learning and memory. This study examines rote verbal learning and memory profiles - including nuances in learning approaches and slopes - in a clinical sample of pediatric patients treated for craniopharyngioma. Furthermore, the role of sleep disturbance on these outcomes is also explored. Retrospective data were collected for 17 pediatric patients with craniopharyngioma and associated endocrinopathies who underwent neurosurgical resection and irradiation (for all but one). As hypothesized, specific deficits related to rote verbal learning and memory were noted for the sample despite average estimated intellectual and adaptive functioning, while more pronounced learning and memory deficits were observed in the subset with reported sleep disturbances. Learning slope stagnation and/or decline across trials was observed in 75% of the patients, while post-hoc analyses revealed heightened susceptibility to recency effects (with poorer recall from the middle of the list) and a non-statistically significant trend toward increased intrusion errors, despite preserved semantic clustering. Findings underscore the importance of targeted memory assessment and multidisciplinary sleep management in this population.

articles.title: The relationship of physical activity and exercise to the initiation and use of nicotine and cocaine.
articles.abstract: Each year, the USA federal government spends hundreds of billions of dollars addressing the ramifications of substance use; however, limited and ineffective treatment strategies exist to mitigate these challenges. Continued targeting of the adolescent population contributes to the growing number of substance-dependent individuals because of an enhanced susceptibility to substance use. Many studies have suggested that exercise may be a suitable adjunct or nonpharmacological therapy because of its rewarding potential and ability to reduce stress and other drug-related risk factors. This review aims to assess the clinical associations of physical activity and preclinical evidence of exercise as protection against the development of nicotine and cocaine use disorders. This will build on previous work by using a substance-use-cycle-specific lens, focusing on substance initiation and use, while clarifying and addressing concerns about the timing of exercise exposure relative to the substance-use experience and its impact on exercise intervention efficacy. Together, this work identifies clinical observations associated with lower instances of nicotine initiation and use, in addition to preclinical behavioral and molecular interventions associated with reductions in cocaine initiation and use, providing support for the protective effect of physical activity and exercise.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Propofol Induction for Sedated Radiologic Procedures in Patients With Trisomy 21.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with Trisomy 21 (T21) are more susceptible to sedation-related adverse events (AEs). Few studies address the risk of propofol or compare natural airway sedation regimens in this population. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is less likely than propofol to result in AEs as it promotes a more natural sleep and less airway muscle relaxation.
METHODS: This study is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data. We queried the Pediatric Sedation Research Consortium (PSRC) Database from the years 2020 to 2025. The demographic characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. The incidence of sedation-related AEs and sedation failures were described by induction drug (DEX vs. propofol). Any medication used other than DEX or propofol were excluded. We performed a propensity score analysis comparing the DEX cohort to the propofol cohort. All the statistical work was performed using SAS 9.4.
RESULTS: A total of 337 patients met inclusion criteria. The average age was 7 years. Forty-four percent of AEs were partial airway obstruction. For the bivariate analyses, the AE outcome variable is statistically significant with the medication variable (χ2df=1=33.249, P<0.001). Induction with propofol had a 5 times higher odds of an AE (OR=5.069, 95% CI: 2.829-9.082). After propensity score matching, there are a total of 216 matched observations.
CONCLUSION: In patients with T21 undergoing radiologic procedures, the odds of having any AE are higher with induction using propofol compared with DEX. Greater consideration should be given for use of DEX induction for patients with T21 undergoing sedated radiologic procedures.

articles.title: The hidden burden of insomnia in late pregnancy: prevalence and risk factors among Egyptian women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep condition that has a harmful impact on one's quality of life and presents considerable health hazards, especially for pregnant women in their third trimester. It can lead to stress, postpartum depression and negative fetal outcomes. The prevalence and contributing variables of insomnia among pregnant women in Egypt have not been adequately studied. This study evaluated the prevalence of insomnia among third trimester pregnant women in Egypt and analyzed the associated risk factors.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This is a cross-sectional study of pregnant women in the third trimester at Menoufia University Hospital. The study included 390 participants. The study employed a pre-structured questionnaire that includes questions about sociodemographic and lifestyle attributes, accompanied by the ISI questionnaire used to diagnose and assess insomnia severity.
RESULTS: A total of 390 pregnant women in the third trimester completed the questionnaire. The prevalence of insomnia was 75.4% (n = 294), with 33.1% categorized as sub-threshold, 26.2% as moderate, and 16.2% as severe. Multivariate logistic regression identified maternal age 25-35 years (AOR = 4.57, 95% CI: 2.50-8.36) and age > 35 years (AOR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.01-9.70) as significant risk factors. Conversely, university education (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.11-0.61), overweight BMI (AOR = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.16-0.62), and rural residence (AOR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.30-0.95) were significant protective factors. Linear regression further confirmed that higher insomnia severity scores were predicted by increased maternal age, while overweight BMI (B = -3.10), rural residence (B = -1.98), and nulliparity (B = -3.69) were significant negative predictors of severity (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Insomnia is highly prevalent among pregnant women, particularly in the third trimester. Advanced maternal age and urban residence were associated with a higher risk and severity of insomnia, while higher education and nulliparity appear protective. Further research is needed to develop strategies to improve maternal well-being and reduce adverse outcomes for mothers and infants.

articles.title: Changes in Childhood Food Allergy Following Implementation of Infant Feeding Guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Since 2016, Australian infant feeding guidelines recommend introducing allergenic foods into the diet in the first year of life to prevent food allergy. Here, we evaluated whether the prevalence of food allergy in 6-year-old children changed following implementation of these guidelines.
METHODS: We conducted 2 population-based studies using the same methodology in Melbourne, Australia, before and after the guideline changes, recruiting 5276 12-month-old infants in 2007 to 2011 and 1933 infants in 2018 to 2019. Both studies followed up with children at age 6 years (2012-2016 and 2024-2025 respectively) with questionnaires, optional skin prick tests, and oral food challenges. Direct regression standardization compared prevalence estimates between cohorts, adjusting for demographic differences between the samples. Multiple imputation was used to handle missing data.
RESULTS: Participation at age 6 years in 2012 to 2016 was 84% and in 2024 to 2025 was 83%. After adjusting for temporal changes in food allergy risk factors, and applying multiple imputation, the prevalence of food allergy decreased: absolute reduction -2.0% (95% CI -3.4% to -0.6%, P = .005; n = 7209) and relative reduction -31% (95% CI -50% to -11%, P = .002). Findings were similar using complete cases (absolute reduction -2.9%, 95% CI -4.5% to -1.2%, P < .001; relative reduction -37%, 95% CI -57% to -18%, P < 0.001; n = 4173). This reduction was primarily driven by changes in cashew and peanut allergy; prevalence of milk and egg allergy did not change substantially in this age group.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide evidence that infant feeding guidelines recommending earlier allergen introduction may translate to measurable reductions in childhood food allergy at the population level.

articles.title: Treated and untreated maternal asthma and early pregnancy outcomes: a retrospective cohort study of 324,238 infants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continued use of asthma medication during pregnancy is recommended, because asthma exacerbations often increase during pregnancy, and poor control may adversely affect maternal and foetal health. However, evidence on whether adverse outcomes arise from the treatment itself or just the underlying disease remains inconsistent. This study examined the relationship between maternal asthma, and its medication, and early pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective birth cohort was constructed using population-wide linked Welsh health records of 324,238 infants born between 2009 and 2022. Logistic regression was used to investigate associations between maternal asthma (treated, untreated, and medication exposure) and pregnancy outcomes: stillbirth, iatrogenic and spontaneous preterm delivery, small/very small for gestational age (SGA/VSGA), and low Apgar score.
RESULTS: Of the 324,238 infants, 39,040 (12.0%) had mothers with asthma: 20,840 (6.4%) had treated asthma, 8,230 (2.5%) had untreated asthma, and 9,970 (3.1%) were prescribed asthma medications without recorded asthma diagnoses. Compared to offspring of mothers with no maternal asthma (reference group), those whose mothers had treated asthma had higher odds of SGA (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.07-1.19), VSGA (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.26), Apgar score < 7 (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.01-1.29), and iatrogenic preterm delivery (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26). Associations were observed across multiple classes of asthma medication with stronger associations among the offspring of mothers prescribed more than one medication class and those with add-on therapies including long-acting muscarinic antagonists, short-acting muscarinic antagonists, leukotrienes antagonist and theophylline, consistent with more severe, or poorly controlled, asthma rather than medication effects. Untreated asthma was associated with higher risk of iatrogenic preterm delivery, and treated asthma was associated with lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery (aOR 0.81, 95% CI 0.73-0.89). No associations were observed with stillbirth.
CONCLUSIONS: The non-specific associations observed across different classes of asthma medication and dose-relationships with polytherapy suggested confounding by indication and severity. The findings for iatrogenic preterm delivery further supported an effect of the underlying disease rather than its treatment. These findings, together with the lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery among treated mothers, support guideline recommendations to continue asthma treatment during pregnancy.

articles.title: Identity-based bullying and maladaptive weight control behaviors among sexual and gender minority youth: Does bullying subtype and format matter?
articles.abstract: Little is known about how bullying an individual because of their weight may be differentially associated with eating disorder risk compared to bullying for other identity components (e.g., gender, sexual orientation) among sexual and gender minority (SGM) youth. It is also unclear how bullying that occurs in-person versus online may impact maladaptive weight control behaviors. The present study quantified experiences of identity-based bullying and examined their differential associations with maladaptive weight control behaviors by subtype and setting (i.e., in school or online) of bullying. 12,868 adolescent participants who identified as SGM completed measures that assessed engagement in maladaptive weight control behaviors, and experiences of bullying in-school and online across domains of identity including weight, gender, race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, disability, immigration status, and gender expression. High rates of bullying were documented across settings with it occurring more often in-person than online, t(12,152)=19.60, p<.001, d=.18. Experiencing bullying in either setting was associated with maladaptive weight control behaviors: bullying experiences in school, F(29, 10,240)=59.09, p<.001, R 2=.14 and bullying experiences online, F(29, 10,150)=50.25, p<.001, R 2=.13. There were slightly stronger associations between being bullied for visible components of identity (weight, gender expression, gender identity) and maladaptive weight control behaviors (βs=.23-.31 versus βs=.10-.25), though all types of bullying victimization across both settings were associated with greater engagement in these behaviors (p<.001 for all). These findings suggest that more resources are needed to combat bullying across locations and to facilitate coping for adolescents at increased risk of identity-based bullying.

articles.title: Exploring the potential therapeutic significance of secukinumab for annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
articles.abstract: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis (AEI), also known as KRT1/KRT10-nEDD-annular, is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by recurrent annular erythema on the trunk and proximal extremities. Currently, the treatment of AEI is limited to the use of emollients, keratolytics, and oral retinoids, which remains insufficient. To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of secukinumab in patients with AEI. Two patients with AEI were enrolled for secukinumab therapy following a laboratory assessment that excluded contraindications. Disease severity was assessed using the Ichthyosis Area and Severity Index (IASI), the Children's Dermatology Life Quality Index (cDLQI) and the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), and the 5-D itch scale. Immunological profiling was performed by measuring biomarker levels in both serum and lesional skin tissue. Significant differences in treatment efficacy were observed between the paediatric and adult patient receiving secukinumab, with the paediatric patient demonstrating marked outcomes and improvements in both subjective symptoms and skin lesions. Notably, despite showing no pre-treatment elevation in serum IL-17A levels, the paediatric patient exhibited increased IL-17A expression in lesional skin. Limitations: Small sample group. Although our findings are based on a small sample size, they provide novel therapeutic perspectives for the management of AEI and offer preliminary therapeutic clues for future clinical management.

articles.title: Association Between Cancer Stage and Parenting Self-Efficacy in Breast Cancer Survivors: A Survey of a Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Community.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer substantially affects women's health and survivorship, with an increasing number of survivors. However, research on social reintegration into family and work roles after cancer remains limited. This study aimed to examine the association between breast cancer-related clinical indicators and parenting self-efficacy among survivors who were working mothers before diagnosis, thereby enhancing understanding of post-cancer social reintegration into parenting.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 357 women who completed their last treatment between 2018 and 2022 and had at least one dependent child aged 12 years or younger. Participants were recruited from an online patient community in Republic of Korea (= South Korea) in October 2023, which predominantly consisted of survivors of triple-negative breast cancer. Parenting self-efficacy was the primary outcome. Clinical characteristics, return-to-work-related factors, and sociodemographic variables were included as independent variables and covariates. Multivariate linear regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Higher breast cancer stages were associated with lower parenting self-efficacy compared with Stage 0. Undergoing breast-conserving surgery and longer time since the completion of the last treatment were positively associated with parenting self-efficacy. Overall patterns were similar in the total sample and among participants who had returned to work (n = 229), although some associations varied in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Advanced cancer stages may be associated with lower parenting self-efficacy among breast cancer survivor mothers. However, this association appears sensitive to stage grouping and warrants cautious interpretation. These findings may provide preliminary insights into post-cancer parenting experiences, although the specific study population and cross-sectional design limit generalizability. Greater attention may be needed for social reintegration into parenting for young women with breast cancer, who play critical roles in both the workforce and childcare.

articles.title: Polypharmacy and use of prescription medication in children and adolescents with life-limiting conditions-a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Children and adolescents (CA) with life-limiting conditions (LLC) are living longer thanks to better treatment but face substantial medication burden. We investigated polypharmacy and use of prescription medication in CAs with LLC compared to a comparison population of CAs with no LLC up to 25 years after diagnosis. This retrospective nationwide cohort study included all patients aged 0-21 years born in Denmark and diagnosed with an LLC between January 1, 1996, and December 31, 2021. Sociodemographic and prescription data were obtained from national registries. We assessed polypharmacy and the mean cumulative number of prescriptions at 1, 5, 10 and 25 years after diagnosis. We assessed concurrent polypharmacy (≥ 5 different prescriptions within 120 days before a follow-up time) and sequential polypharmacy (≥ 4 regularly dispensed prescriptions, defined as at least three prescriptions within 12 months before a follow-up time). We identified 98,508 CAs with LLC and 492,540 CAs with no LLC matched 1:5 on sex and age at diagnosis. Median follow-up was 9.4 years (interquartile range 4.8, 15.5) with 3608 deaths.
