One year after diagnosis, 4.53% of CAs with LLC were using ≥ 5 unique medications compared to 1.57% of population controls, while 2.1% of CAs with LLC were using ≥ 4 medications regularly compared to only 0.1% of population controls. CAs with a neurological or neuromuscular diagnosis and from families with lower education levels had the highest medication use.
CONCLUSIONS: Healthcare providers of CAs with LLCs must be aware of the impact of long-term polypharmacy and balance symptom control with the complexity of medication regiments, especially in children from families with lower educational levels.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children and adolescents (CA) with life-limiting conditions (LLC) are living longer and often receive multiple medications for long-term symptom management. • However, the prevalence of polypharmacy and patterns of prescription medication use over time across diagnostic groups and sociodemograpic factors in this population compared to the general pediatric population are unknown.
WHAT IS NEW: • The prevalence of polypharmacy was almost threefold higher among CAs with LLC compared to the general pediatric population at one year after diagnosis, with smaller yet elevated differences up to 25 years after diagnosis. • Anti-infectives, anti-epileptics, respiratory drugs, and anxiolytics/sedatives were most prescribed, and the highest overall medication use was observed among CAs with a neurological or neuromuscular diagnosis and those from families with lower parental educational attainment.

articles.title: Child Sexual Abuse, Sexual Function, and Sexual Distress in Couples Coping with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder: A Dyadic Longitudinal Study.
articles.abstract: Sexual interest/arousal disorder (SIAD), characterized by low sexual desire and high sexual distress, is the most common sexual dysfunction among women. Although current theoretical models support interpersonal conceptualizations of sexual desire, distal interpersonal factors that may underlie the sexual well-being of couples coping with SIAD, such as child sexual abuse (CSA), have not been thoroughly documented. Yet, difficulties with sexual desire and arousal are among the most frequently reported sexual dysfunctions among CSA survivors. Using a one-year longitudinal design among couples with SIAD, this study examined the associations between both partners' CSA and their sexual function and distress. Individuals with SIAD (N = 263; Mage = 34.16) and their partners (N = 263; Mage = 35.71) completed validated questionnaires at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Dyadic latent growth curve analyses were conducted within a structural equation model. Results showed that greater CSA among individuals with SIAD was associated with their own higher initial levels of sexual distress. Moreover, higher levels of non-SIAD partners' CSA were unexpectedly associated with lower initial levels of sexual function difficulties for individuals with SIAD. However, non-SIAD partners' CSA predicted greater increases in sexual function difficulties over time for individuals with SIAD. No other significant associations were found. Findings highlight the role of CSA in the sexual function and distress of couples coping with SIAD and point towards the value of couple-based interventions that acknowledge both partners' histories and their impact on mutual sexual experiences.

articles.title: Evaluation of pediatric patients diagnosed with food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Food Protein-Induced Enterocolitis Syndrome (FPIES) is a non-IgE-mediated food allergy typically presenting in infancy with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. The absence of specific biomarkers complicates diagnosis and management. This study aimed to evaluate demographic characteristics, trigger food distribution, clinical phenotypes, and tolerance development in pediatric patients diagnosed with FPIES. This cross-sectional study included pediatric patients diagnosed with FPIES and followed at Ankara Etlik City Hospital between October 2022 and December 2025. Patients were re-evaluated for demographic data, trigger foods, phenotypic features, oral food challenge (OFC) outcomes, and tolerance development. A total of 63 patients were included (63.5% male), with a median age of 26 months (IQR 16-37). A total of 134 reactions were documented, with a median age at first reaction of 7 months (IQR 6-8). During first acute episodes, 19 patients required emergency care; three were hospitalized, and two required intensive care unit admission. Egg yolk was the most common trigger (51.5%), followed by cow's milk (21.2%), fish (18.1%), egg white (6%), and red meat (3%). Multiple trigger foods were identified in three patients. Phenotypic analysis revealed atypical FPIES in 10 patients and chronic FPIES in one patient. A total of 34 OFCs were performed for diagnostic confirmation and tolerance assessment. Reactions occurred in 11 tests, and eight required medical treatment. During follow-up, tolerance developed in 47.6% (n = 30) of patients, with a median tolerance age of 18 months (IQR 14-26). Tolerance was confirmed by OFC in 18 patients and by successful home reintroduction in 12.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort, egg yolk was the predominant trigger food. Nearly half of the patients achieved early tolerance. Given the heterogeneous phenotypic spectrum of FPIES, increased clinical awareness and standardized management approaches are essential for optimal follow-up and prognosis assessment.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • FPIES shows geographic variation in trigger foods and clinical presentation, and tolerance acquisition may differ according to the culprit food.
WHAT IS NEW: • Egg yolk was the predominant trigger in this cohort, while fish-induced FPIES showed significantly later tolerance acquisition, supporting food-specific timing of follow-up and re-evaluation.

articles.title: Paediatric clinicians' knowledge and experiences of e-bike and e-scooter harms in children and young people: a UK national service evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: E-bike and e-scooter use is increasing, with growing concern about harms in children and young people (CYP). We assessed paediatric clinicians’ legislative knowledge, clinical experiences and prevention opportunities.
METHODS: This UK national service evaluation comprised a narrative literature review, clinician survey, structured local needs-assessment discussions and contextual mortality data from England. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; free-text responses and discussion notes underwent descriptive thematic synthesis.
RESULTS: 484 clinicians contributed: 353 completed the survey, 217 participated in structured local discussions and 86 contributed to both components. Legislative knowledge was limited: 11% correctly identified the minimum age for rental e-bike use, 22% for private e-bike use and 25% knew that a driving licence is required for rental e-scooter use. Of 303 clinicians, 142 (47%) reported encountering e-bike or e-scooter-related injuries or discussing micromobility use with CYP in the past year. Reported harms included head injury, fractures and polytrauma, with dual riding, lack of helmet use and motor-vehicle collisions commonly reported. National mortality data identified 17 child deaths in England between April 2019 and December 2025 related to e-bike or e-scooter use; numbers were small, and 2025 data were incomplete, but the distribution over time raises concern that deaths may be increasing. Clinicians reported inconsistent advice provision, barriers to discussion and support for coordinated prevention strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: E-bike and e-scooter-related harm is an emerging paediatric public health concern. Improved education about additional risks, integration into routine risk assessment, improved injury surveillance and coordinated policy responses, including legislative review, are needed to reduce preventable harm.

articles.title: Study of 34 prospective pregnancies in women receiving IL-1 inhibitors for autoinflammatory diseases and comparison to unexposed pregnancies (GR2 study).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibitors are widely used in autoinflammatory diseases (AID) such as Still’s disease and monogenic inflammasomopathies, including cryopyrinopathies (CAPS) and familial Mediterranean fever. As these conditions frequently affect women of reproductive age and data are limited, concerns remain regarding anti-IL-1 therapy safety during pregnancy. We aimed to evaluate maternal and neonatal outcomes in women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception and pregnancy.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included pregnant women from the Groupe de recherche sur la Grossesse et les Maladies Rares (GR2) prospective cohort, spanning 76 French centres before September 2024. Women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception or pregnancy were selected. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes were compared with a 1:1 matched control group of unexposed women with similar conditions and with the nationwide 2021 French National Perinatal Survey.
RESULTS: Thirty-four pregnancies (three twin pregnancies) in 31 women were exposed to anakinra (n=30) and/or canakinumab (n=5) for Still’s disease (n=15), familial Mediterranean fever (n=15), CAPS (n=3), undifferentiated systemic AID (n=2), tumour necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome and recurrent pericarditis (n=1 each). Reported outcomes included infections (n=6), intrahepatic cholestasis (n=3), gestational diabetes (n=2), gestational hypertension (n=1) and intrauterine growth restriction (n=1). Median gestational age was 39 weeks with five preterm births between 32 and 37. One baby was diagnosed with laryngomalacia but did not require surgery. Paediatric follow-up (33 babies to 6 months, 30 thereafter for a median of 14.5 months (13–24)) confirmed normal infant development. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes did not differ between treated with anti-IL-1 and untreated with anti-IL-1 patients with AID.
CONCLUSION: Anti-IL-1 therapy, particularly anakinra, appears safe during pregnancy in women with systemic AID.

articles.title: Mapping research on suicide bereavement in older adults: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Suicide bereavement may impact individuals from different age groups in varying ways. Existing research has mainly focused on suicide bereavement in adolescents and adults. This review aims to understand suicide bereavement amongst older adults and identify existing evidence gaps.
METHOD: The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and adhered to the PRISMA-ScR. Peer-reviewed articles were retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO (Ovid), Medline (Ovid), and Embase (Ovid). Grey literature was identified through Google Scholar and ProQuest Thesis and Dissertations. Protocol registration OSF: https://osf.io/ub524/.
RESULTS: The review identified 11 relevant publications, five of which originated from the United States. Suicide-bereaved older adults face diverse challenges, including concerns about rebuilding their lives as time and resources become increasingly limited, as well as prioritising others' needs while suppressing personal grief. The impacts of their loss included an increased risk of suicidal behaviour and psychosocial problems, and diminished social support and help-seeking.
CONCLUSIONS: Further studies are urgently needed to explore the experiences and interventions of suicide bereavement in older adults, with consideration of various context, such as non-western and low-and-middle-income countries.

articles.title: Stress Fracture Recovery and Return to Sports in Youth with Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare stress fracture recovery times in children with and without juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), and to evaluate JIA-related factors associated with recovery.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective case-control study included children with JIA <19 years old with a first stress fracture treated at a single center from 2004-2024. Cases were matched 1:3 to children without JIA by age, gender, and fracture location. Recovery time was defined from imaging confirmation of a stress fracture to medical clearance to return to sports. We used a generalized estimating equations method to compare recovery times and evaluate associations with JIA-related factors, including JIA subtype, glucocorticoid and arthritis-directed therapy exposure, and proximity of arthritis to fracture location.
RESULTS: The cohort included 260 children (65 cases, 195 controls; 53.8% female; median age 14.3 years [IQR 12.6, 16.2]). Pars interarticularis fractures accounted for 30.8% of injuries, followed by metatarsal (23.1%), and tibial fractures (14.2%). Among children with JIA who sustained pars fractures, 75.0% had an enthesitis-related arthritis (ERA) phenotype. Median recovery times were 10.6 (IQR 7.0, 19.4) weeks for children with JIA and 10.6 (IQR 7.1, 14.6) weeks for controls (P=0.197), with no significant differences for lower-extremity fractures. In contrast, children with JIA who sustained pars fractures had longer recovery times than controls (ratio of geometric means: 1.44, 95% CI 1.01, 2.05; P=0.045). Among children with active sacroiliitis, fractures occurred more frequently in the proximate pars or pelvis than at non-proximate sites (P<0.001). Recovery time was not associated with JIA subtype (all p>0.150), glucocorticoid exposure (P=0.365), or biologic therapy (P=0.625).
CONCLUSIONS: Overall recovery times did not differ significantly between children with and without JIA. However, children with JIA and pars fractures had longer recovery times, and associations with ERA and sacroiliitis warrant further investigation. Additional research on spondylolysis recovery in young athletes with JIA may help inform individualized return-to-sports recommendations.

articles.title: Tailored Dosing Recommendations for Amikacin in Severely Ill Children: A Population Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Evaluation using Cmax/MIC and AUC/MIC-based Indices.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Optimal amikacin dosing in severely ill patients remains challenging due to maturational and pathophysiological alterations affecting the pharmacokinetics (PK). This study aimed to develop a population PK model for amikacin, evaluate pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) indices, and propose personalised dosing recommendations for this patient population.
METHODS: A prospective PK study was conducted in 38 severely ill children receiving intravenous 20 mg/kg amikacin every 24h. PK parameters were determined using nonlinear mixed-effects modelling (Monolix 2024R1). Probability of target attainment (PTA) was simulated for the minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 2 mg/L and 8 mg/L for Enterobacterales. Evaluated PK/PD targets were a peak concentration (Cmax)/MIC ≥ 8 and a 24h area under the concentration-time curve (AUC0-24h)/MIC ≥ 62.5h, in combination with a trough concentration (Ctrough) ≤ 5 mg/L toxicity threshold.
RESULTS: A two-compartment model with a priori allometric weight scaling on the PK parameters best described the data. Clearance was predicted using the Bouvet estimated glomerular filtration (eGFR) formula, combining creatinine and cystatin C. The central volume of distribution was 41% lower in oncology patients compared with intensive care patients. The population parameters for clearance and the total volume of distribution were 7.4 L/h/70 kg and 39.0 L/70 kg, respectively. AUC0-24h/MIC, as PK/PD index, was less frequently attained than the Cmax/MIC index. For a MIC of 2 mg/L, a dose of 20 mg/kg every 18h achieved a 100% PTA for the targets Cmax/MIC ≥ 8, AUC0-24h/MIC ≥ 62.5h, and Ctrough ≤ 5 mg/L in typical patients with a 120-150 mL/min/1.73 m2 eGFR, compared with ≤76% for the current regimen. For a MIC of 8 mg/L, ≥80% PTA could not be achieved.
CONCLUSIONS: Current amikacin dosing regimens may result in subtherapeutic exposure, particularly in intensive care patients with high eGFR or when targeting higher MIC values or AUC/MIC targets. Optimised dosing regimens were proposed.

articles.title: Early food introduction and skin intervention in the prevention of food allergy in young children (PreventADALL): 7-year follow-up of a factorial, multicentre, cluster-randomised trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In our previous study, early food introduction prevented food allergy, whereas skin intervention alone did not prevent atopic dermatitis at age 3 years. In this follow-up study, we aimed to determine the effect of food and skin interventions on food allergy, allergic sensitisation, atopic dermatitis, food avoidance diets, and BMI at age 7 years.
METHODS: We conducted a 7-year follow-up study of 2394 children from Norway and Sweden antenatally included (between Dec 9, 2014, and Oct 31, 2016) in the ongoing, general-population-based Preventing Atopic Dermatitis and ALLergies in children (PreventADALL) study. Children were randomly assigned at study site hospitals at birth (1:1:1:1) into the 2×2 factorially designed cluster-randomised controlled trial to no intervention (n=597), skin intervention (n=575; oil baths and facial cream from age 2 weeks to 9 months a minimum of four times weekly), food intervention (n=642; tastes of peanut, cow's milk, wheat, and egg a minimum of four times weekly from ages 3-6 months), or both interventions combined (n=583). The primary outcome at the 7-year follow-up was allergy to any of the interventional foods, as diagnosed by an expert panel following international guidelines. Secondary outcomes were allergy to the individual interventional foods, allergy to non-interventional foods, allergic sensitisation by skin prick test and serum-IgE, atopic dermatitis by validated diagnostic criteria, food avoidance diets through interview, and BMI. Study personnel performing clinical assessments and all researchers involved in data analysis were masked to group allocation, except for the data manager for some parts of the analysis. Mixed logistic regression with best case imputation (of no atopic disease) was used to estimate risk differences. The trial is registered on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT02449850) and is closed for recruitment.
FINDINGS: At the 7-year follow-up, the risk of food allergy to interventional foods (38 [1·6%] of 2394) was similar in the no food intervention (21 [1·8%] of 1170) versus food intervention groups (17 [1·4%] of 1224; risk difference -0·4% [95% CI -1·4 to 0·6]). Any food allergy was diagnosed in 76 (3·2%) of 2394 children, similar across the intervention groups. Allergic sensitisation to interventional foods at 7 years was lower in the food intervention (67 [9·9%] of 680) versus no food intervention groups (95 [15·6%] of 610; -5·7% [-9·3 to -2·1]). Atopic dermatitis was less frequent in the combined intervention group (17·3%) than in the controls (25·2%; -7·8% [-12·5 to -3·2]). Food avoidance diets and BMI were similar across the intervention groups.
INTERPRETATION: Early short-term food intervention was insufficient for sustained food allergy prevention by age 7 years, despite reduced allergic sensitisation, suggesting that continued allergen exposure might be needed for long-term prevention. Combined food and skin interventions reduced atopic dermatitis at 7 years.
FUNDING: For a full list of funders, see Acknowledgments.

articles.title: Exercise Test Findings in the Long-Term Outcomes After Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MUSIC) Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) commonly presents with cardiovascular involvement, but the frequency of exercise-related arrhythmias and exercise capacity are poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe exercise stress testing (EST) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) after MIS-C.
METHODS: We summarized EST and CPET results from the MUSIC (Long-terM OUtcomes after the Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome In Children) study (1,204 participants, 32 North American sites). Demographics and details of hospitalization from participants undergoing clinical EST were compared to participants ≥5 years who did not undergo EST. Site reported results of EST and CPET were described.
RESULTS: EST was performed in 22% (208/932) at a mean of 150 ± 110 days after hospitalization. Compared with those who did not undergo EST (n = 724), the EST cohort was older (12.2 vs 10.5 years) and had higher rates of intensive care unit admission (77.4% vs 63.8%), vasoactive infusions (57.2% vs 46.1%), troponin elevation (64.4% vs 51.0%), and coronary artery aneurysm (22.7% vs 0.4%) (all P ≤ 0.01). During EST, only 1% (2/208; 95% CI: 0.1%-3.4%) exhibited premature ventricular contractions and no sustained ectopy. Among 160 participants undergoing CPET, 75.6% (121/160; 95% CI: 68.2%-82.1%) achieved oxygen consumption/kg ≥ 80% predicted, and 83.8% (134/160; 95% CI: 77.1%-89.1%) achieved an oxygen pulse ≥80% predicted.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing exercise testing after MIS-C, most had normal exercise capacity, no sustained arrhythmias occurred, and premature ventricular contractions were rare.

articles.title: The apelin-APJ axis in infantile hemangioma: Emerging evidence and potential links to propranolol response.
articles.abstract: Propranolol is the standard first-line systemic therapy for infantile hemangioma (IH), but its antiangiogenic mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Emerging evidence implicates the apelin-APJ system in IH endothelial biology. APJ is enriched in hemangioma-derived endothelial cells (HemECs), and pharmacological inhibition suppresses proliferation, migration and angiogenic behavior, with genetic experiments supporting an APJ-dependent component. Separately, propranolol reduces APLN transcription in IH-derived models, and circulating apelin declines during treatment. These findings motivate investigation of an indirect link through ligand regulation, but do not establish APJ-dependent mediation of propranolol efficacy. This review distinguishes ligand transcription, ligand abundance, receptor expression and receptor-dependent function, integrating IH observations with mechanistic evidence from other vascular and disease models. We examine endothelial cell states, HIF-1α-dependent transcription, and the distinct SOX18-mevalonate mechanism of R(+)-propranolol. Cross-disease intervention studies provide a rationale for investigating treatment responsiveness. Priorities include defining functional ligand sources and recipient cells, testing receptor-dependent effects on drug response, validating circulating biomarkers, and establishing developmental safety before therapeutic translation.

articles.title: "It is worth seeing this, and it is never too late": Survivors' expectations of significant others during intrafamilial child sexual abuse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research on child sexual abuse has largely examined children's needs and expectations after disclosure. Less is known about how survivors retrospectively understand their expectations of significant others who were present during intrafamilial child sexual abuse (IFCSA), before disclosure became possible.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined what adult survivors of IFCSA expected from significant others during and after the abuse, and how these expectations were shaped by others' relational roles, authority, and capacity to intervene.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The study included 18 adult survivors of intrafamilial child sexual abuse (IFCSA) who reported the presence of significant others during abusive incidents. Participants were recruited through online support groups for adults with histories of childhood abuse.
METHODS: Guided by Denzin's interpretive paradigm and reflexive thematic analysis, the study draws on semi-structured, in-depth interviews to examine survivors' expectations of significant others and the meanings attributed to their presence.
RESULTS: Participants' expectations clustered around three relational demands: to be witnessed, to be protected, and to be stood with. Expectations differed according to relational role and capacity, with mothers, adults, siblings, and professionals each assigned distinct forms of responsibility.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings show that the presence of others may shape survivors' traumatic meaning-making before, during, and long after the disclosure. Practice and policy should support earlier recognition, protective action, and long-term acknowledgment.

articles.title: A Social Media Mining and Questionnaire Survey Hybrid Approach to Characterizing Caregiver Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices on House Dust Mite Control: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: House dust mite (HDM) sensitization commonly begins in early life and contributes to persistent allergic airway inflammation and asthma chronicity. Primary prevention via early-life environmental control is a potential pathway to reduce HDM sensitization and asthma risk.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to characterize child caregivers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding pediatric HDM control using a hybrid literature/expert-driven and social media-driven approach and to examine associations between KAP levels, child age, and caregiver HDM-related online engagement.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study comprised two interconnected components: (1) mining of content published between August 2023 and July 2025 from 5 major Chinese social media platforms, analyzed via latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), and (2) a social media-enhanced web-based KAP survey administered in November 2025 to child caregivers in Chongqing, China. In total, 132,341 social media documents and 2275 caregivers of children younger than 18 years were included in the analysis. The main outcomes included social media discourse patterns and domain-specific KAP levels across 5 dimensions: foundational knowledge (K1), recommended control knowledge (K2), attitude toward social media topics (A1), attitude toward recommended methods (A2), and control practices (P). Stratified analysis was conducted by 2 exposure variables: child age (≤3 years vs >3 years) and caregiver HDM-related online engagement (engaged vs nonengaged).
RESULTS: LDA topic modeling identified 5 distinct topic clusters in the social media content. Commercial, emotional, and misleading content collectively dominated the information landscape, accounting for 83.3% (n=110,254) of the included documents (65.8% of the tokens), with commercial content often systematically conflating the concepts of "disinfection" and "mite elimination." Only 16.7% (n=22,087) of the documents (34.1% of the tokens) were classified as health educational content focusing on HDM allergy prevention, reflecting that this valid educational content is substantially longer and more information-dense than other social media posts. The average KAP levels of K1, K2, A1, A2, and P domains were 62.9%, 84.7%, 57.0%, 37.8%, and 25.8%, respectively. Social media emerged as the primary knowledge source (80.7%, n=1836), with methodological knowledge gaps (47.5%) being the top implementation barrier. Caregivers of children ≤3 years had significantly lower self-rated knowledge (23.5% vs 28.3%; P=.01), stronger endorsement of recommended methods, but also greater information overload (odds ratio [OR] 1.39, 95% CI 1.15-1.67; P<.001) and efficacy uncertainty (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.01-1.52; P=.04). Caregivers with HDM-related online engagement showed better performance across multiple items in 5 domains, but also increased traditional practice with uncertain evidence (ultraviolet irradiation: OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.35-2.53; P<.001) and misconception acceptance (allergy impact exaggeration: OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.04-1.87; P=.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Complex and suboptimal KAP levels exist, particularly among caregivers of young children (≤3 years). HDM-related online engagement is associated with both enhanced implementation of control practices and elevated misconception endorsement. These findings reveal critical educational gaps and the necessity of social media intervention.

articles.title: Consensus Statements on the Clinical Practice for Patients With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: The Fontan procedure has been transformative for patients with univentricular physiology. By using a single ventricle as the systemic pump and relying on passive venous return to drive pulmonary circulation, Fontan circulation alleviates cyanosis and heart failure, allowing children to engage in normal activities during school and adolescence. Nevertheless, Fontan circulation is characterized by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, which leads to systemic venous congestion and long-term multiorgan effects. Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) is now recognized as a major long-term complication. Approximately 50% of patients develop hepatic abnormalities within 10-20 years after surgery, and some progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite this risk, strategies to identify individuals at high risk for early HCC and to provide better prognostic information remain limited. This article compiles knowledge from congenital heart disease specialists and hepatologists on FALD, including areas where evidence is limited. By facilitating early diagnosis, structured follow-up, and multidisciplinary management of FALD, this initiative aims to improve outcomes, build a nationwide clinical experience, and ultimately support the development of formal, evidence-based guidelines for FALD management.

articles.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening condition and often diagnosed late, with many patients presenting in advanced heart failure. This study aimed to examine the demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and maternal and neonatal outcomes METHODS AND RESULTS: This meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 4,341 records up to May 2025, were identified and 122 eligible studies reporting PPCM clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes were included. Heterogeneity was explored through meta-regression analyses assessing demographic, clinical, and study-level variables. An aggregate of 66,908 PPCM patients were reported across the included studies, with a pooled mean age of 30.1 years. Black or African women accounted for a disproportionately large proportion of the reported population compared with other racial groups. Approximately 62% of women presented with advanced heart failure (NYHA class III/IV). Pre-existing diabetes mellitus (OR 5.09) and hypertensive disorders, including pre-existing hypertension (OR 10.07), gestational hypertension (OR 7.75), and pre-eclampsia (OR 9.27), were associated with higher odds of PPCM. The pooled mean LVEF at diagnosis was 29.98%, which subsequently improved to 46.47% at 6 months and 49.12% at 12 months. Despite over half of PPCM patients achieving LVEF recovery (55%), maternal mortality remained high at 6% and neonatal mortality at 4%. Pharmacological treatments for PPCM varied widely, with high heterogeneity suggesting substantial differences in prescribing practices across studies.
CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

articles.title: Fluzoparib combined with docetaxel followed by epirubicin and cyclophosphamide as neoadjuvant therapy in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a single-arm phase II study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most prevalent molecular subtype of breast cancer, yet overall pathological complete response (pCR) rates after neoadjuvant chemotherapy remain low. BRCA mutations and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) may sensitize tumors to PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality. We investigated the efficacy and safety of fluzoparib combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with HRD-positive and/or germline BRCA (gBRCA)-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center, prospective, open-label, single-arm phase II trial (NCT07162051) enrolled women aged 18-70 years with newly diagnosed HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer. Patients received fluzoparib combined with docetaxel during cycles 1-4, followed by epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide during cycles 5-8. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving residual cancer burden (RCB) grade 0/I. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), pathological complete response (pCR) rate, and safety.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients were enrolled between March 2023 and October 2025. Four patients (14.3%; 95% CI 4.0%-32.7%) achieved RCB 0/I, two patients (7.1%; 95% CI 0.9%-23.5%) achieved total pCR (tpCR), and six patients (21.4%; 95% CI 8.3%-41.0%) achieved breast pCR (bpCR). The ORR was 82.1%. Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in four patients (14.3%). No treatment discontinuations, dose reductions, treatment delays, or treatment-related deaths were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: The addition of fluzoparib to standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not improve RCB 0/I rates in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer, although the regimen was well tolerated. Future studies should focus on gBRCA-mutated or higher-risk populations and explore optimized combination strategies, including anti-angiogenic agents. REGISTRATION CENTER, TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER, AND REGISTRATION DATE: This is a prospective, open label, single arm phase II clinical trial. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov; Trial registration number: NCT07162051; Registration date:2023-02-21.

articles.title: Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Septic shock is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the pediatric population worldwide, and evidence comparing balanced crystalloids with normal saline (NS) for resuscitation remains inconclusive.
OBJECTIVE: To compare balanced crystalloids with NS for fluid resuscitation in children with septic shock, incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to May 2026, without language restrictions.
STUDY SELECTION: RCTs comparing balanced crystalloids with NS in patients aged 0 to 18 years with sepsis or septic shock were eligible.
DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; leave-one-out and post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the largest trial were performed.
RESULTS: Six RCTs comprising 10,308 participants were included. RRs are reported with NS as the reference. Pooled mortality showed no statistical significance between groups (3.8% with balanced crystalloids vs. 4.0% with NS; RR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.67-1.27; P = 0.63). Acute kidney injury incidence also did not differ significantly between groups (19.7% vs. 29.6%; RR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.46-1.27; P = 0.29). The need for renal replacement therapy (RRT) was lower with balanced crystalloids (1.3% vs. 1.9%; RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.92; P = 0.01). Hyperchloremia incidence was lower with balanced crystalloids (32.3% vs. 49.9%; RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; P < 0.00001). After excluding the largest trial (PRoMPT BOLUS), mortality remained nonsignificant (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.45-1.50), and the reductions in RRT (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.87) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82) persisted.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with NS, balanced crystalloids reduced the need for RRT and the incidence of hyperchloremia, without significantly affecting mortality or acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Pharmacologic Management of Pediatric Paroxysmal Sympathetic Hyperactivity in North America.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe pharmacological management approaches to pediatric paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH) among North American pediatric attending physicians.
PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Cross-sectional web-based survey of pediatric attending physicians conducted from March to August 2023. The questionnaire examined PSH medication utilization and preferences, subspecialty responsibilities for managing PSH, and the influence of patient age on medication selection. Descriptive statistics summarize PSH medication utilization and rank-order preferences. Chi-square analyses examined relationships between physician specialty and medication selection.
RESULTS: Among 295 respondents (33% palliative care, 23% neurology, 18% complex care, 17% physiatry), considerable heterogeneity in PSH pharmacotherapy approaches was observed. The most used abortive PSH medications were gamma-aminobutyric acid A (GABA-A) agonists (86%), alpha-2 agonists (79%), and opioids (49%). Leading preventive PSH medications included alpha-2 agonists (90%), gabapentinoids (89%), and beta-blockers (66%). Top-ranked medications for abortive management were alpha-2 agonists, GABA-A agonists, and non-opioid analgesics; and gabapentinoids, alpha-2 agonists, and beta-blockers for preventive management. While physiatrists and neurologists were most frequently identified as primary managers of PSH at participants' home institutions, several other specialties (including multidisciplinary models) were reported as well. We observed significant differences in utilization of alpha-2 agonists, opioids, dopamine agonists, and beta-blockers across subspecialties (all P < .05). Patient age influenced medication selection among 41% of our sample.
CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic management of pediatric PSH currently lacks clinical consensus and varies significantly based on physician subspecialty. Our findings underscore the need for focused research efforts to identify optimal treatment strategies and develop standardized and evidence-based management guidelines.

articles.title: Deciphering mitochondrial dysfunction and circadian rhythm-related pathogenic patterns for the pathogenesis of Kawasaki Disease and corresponding nursing therapeutic enrichment: Evidence from machine learning-driven multi-omics and clinical validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki Disease (KD) is an acute, self-limited vasculitis of childhood, with its etiopathogenesis intricately tied to systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Disruption of circadian rhythms and mitochondrial transport, 2 fundamental homeostatic systems, are increasingly recognized as independent contributors to vascular pathology. However, their integrated molecular crosstalk in KD remains completely uncharted.
OBJECTIVE: The primary objective was to identify and validate a mitochondrial transport andcircadian rhythm (MRC)-related molecular signature in KD. The secondary objectives were to resolve MRC-defined molecular subtypes, to nominate and characterize a candidate hub gene, to define its cellular distribution, and to prioritize candidate therapeutic compounds.
METHODS: First, Peripheral blood bulk transcriptomic datasets of KD patients were analyzed. GSE68004 was interrogated via Limma, GSVA, and WGCNA to isolate MRC-associated shared DEGs. Second, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) and 3 machine learning algorithms (RF, Lasso and SVM-RFE) were deployed in GSE63881 for molecular subtype identification and diagnostic model construction, with independent diagnostic validation in integrated GSE73463 and GSE73462. Next, leveraging single-cell transcriptomic data from peripheral blood samples of KD patients (GSE24757), we resolved the spatiotemporal dissemination and functional evolution of the hub gene. In addition, deep learning-driven drug screening (DrugReflector) and molecular docking nominated a candidate compound in GSE18606. Finally, differential expression of the hub gene was validated using q-RT-PCR in clinical samples from KD patients.
RESULTS: The integrated MRC-related signature robustly stratified KD patients into 2 distinct molecular subgroups. FNDC5 was identified as an NK-distributed and MRC-related pathogenic factor in KD. BRD-K10482608 was nominated as a computationally predicted candidate targeting FNDC5 for KD.
CONCLUSION: This study provides the first pathway-anchored MRC-related signature in KD together with a validated framework for molecular stratification. FNDC5 is put forward as a prioritized, hypothesis-generating candidate of KD vasculopathy, and BRD-K10482608 as a computationally nominated starting point for future functional and nursing pharmacological testing.

articles.title: Adjuvant capecitabine-based oral chemotherapy plus trastuzumab as adjuvant therapy in patients with HER2-positive, node-negative breast tumors measuring 1 cm or smaller (ORCHID study).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant treatment decisions for patients with small (T ≤ 1 cm), node-negative, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast tumors remain challenging, particularly regarding whether oral chemotherapy is comparable to intravenous regimens. We therefore conducted a phase II trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of an oral chemotherapy plus trastuzumab regimen in this population.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients received either single-agent capecitabine (1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 every 3 weeks) or vinorelbine capsules (60 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 3 weeks) plus trastuzumab, followed by trastuzumab monotherapy for a total of 12 months of therapy. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS). The secondary end points were distant disease-free survival (DDFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04296162).
RESULTS: The analysis population included 182 patients, of whom 81% had tumors measuring ≤ 0.5 cm and 74% had hormone receptor (HR)-negative disease. Of the 181 treated patients, 176 (97.2%) received capecitabine and 5 (2.8%) vinorelbine, with agent selection at the physician's discretion. After a median follow-up of 5.7 years (range, 1.0-6.2 years), the 5-year DFS rate was 97.3% (90% Confidence interval [CI], 94.4-98.7). The lower bound of the 90% CI exceeded the prespecified threshold of 92%, meeting the primary endpoint. Among the 6 observed invasive disease events, 2 involved distant metastasis, 3 involved local or regional recurrence, and 1 involved contralateral breast cancer. Among the secondary endpoints, the 5-year DDFS rate was 97.2%, with a 5-year OS rate of 100% (no deaths) during follow-up. Among the 176 patients treated with capecitabine, the most common capecitabine-related adverse event (AE) was hand-foot syndrome, which occurred in 66.5% of patients, with 8.0% of patients experiencing a grade 3 event.
CONCLUSIONS: Among women with HER2-positive, node-negative breast tumors measuring ≤ 1 cm, capecitabine-based oral chemotherapy plus 1 year of trastuzumab was associated with a low risk of cancer recurrence and favorable toxicity in this single-arm cohort, supporting further prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Predictors of Parental Strain in Pediatric Atopic Dermatitis: Findings From the US National Survey of Children's Health.
articles.abstract: Caring for a child with atopic dermatitis (AD) places strain on parents, but it remains unclear whether additional atopic comorbidities or psychosocial context compounds this burden. Data from the 2007-2008 National Survey of Children's Health among 6913 children aged 6-17 years was analyzed using survey-weighted multivariable regression to examine associations between a 5-item parental strain scale and parent-reported AD severity, comorbid asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy, along with family, social, and healthcare access factors. Increased parental strain was associated with AD severity and with delayed or forgone care. Decreased parental strain was associated with better maternal mental health and with the female sex of the child. Atopic comorbidities were not associated with strain. Parental strain was more strongly associated with psychosocial factors and the severity of AD than the presence of additional atopic comorbidities.

articles.title: Lao PDR's achievements in family planning: a mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The use of modern contraceptives and family planning (FP) services has increased globally; however, progress varies across countries and regions. The current research aims to examine the key socioecological determinants driving the demand for and utilisation of modern contraceptive methods in the Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), providing insights into the factors that facilitate contraceptive uptake.
METHODOLOGY: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach including: (1) a systematic literature review to synthesise existing evidence, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data to identify demographic and behavioural trends, (3) a desk review of relevant policies and programmes to evaluate the policy landscape and (4) community-based qualitative design to explore sociocultural and contextual factors supporting FP uptake.
RESULTS: Modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR) rose steadily from 38.6% in 2005 to 56.3% in 2017, associated with education, household wealth, contraceptive knowledge and age at first sex, alongside marked geographic and ethnic disparities that persisted throughout. Policy analysis identified three programmatic phases: foundation-building (1988–2005), scale-up aligned with the Millennium Development Goals (2005–2015) and an equity-focused phase emphasising adolescent health (2015–present). Qualitative findings revealed five interconnected themes driving FP progress in Lao PDR: political commitment, financing sustainability, health systems strengthening, community-driven demand generation and women’s reproductive agency. While strong policy commitment and expanded service delivery have improved access, donor dependency, geographic barriers for rural and ethnic minority populations and persistent gender-based decision-making constraints continue to limit equitable contraceptive use.
CONCLUSION: Lao PDR’s FP success reflects the simultaneous alignment of political will, financing structures, service delivery and shifting social norms. Sustaining and extending these gains will require a structured domestic financing transition, strengthened commodity supply and workforce systems, expansion of youth-friendly services into rural and ethnic minority areas and continued investment in gender-transformative community engagement to translate increased spousal communication into genuine shared decision-making.

articles.title: How Bolivia became a positive outlier in family planning: an in-depth mixed-methods case study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bolivia made remarkable progress in increasing modern contraceptive use among all women of reproductive age, achieving an exponential annual growth rate exceeding 5% between 1989 and 2016—from 8% to 32.4%. Based on a systematic, criteria-based country selection process implemented by the Exemplars in Global Health coalition, Bolivia was identified as a case for in-depth analysis of progress in family planning. In this study, we aimed to identify the socioeconomic, demographic, political, programmatic and health system factors that have contributed to Bolivia’s success in family planning.
METHODS: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach, incorporating results from: (1) a systematic literature review, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data, (3) a desk review of policies and programmes and (4) qualitative analysis of primary data. This study summarises the findings from these four analyses.
RESULTS: Bolivia’s progress in family planning outcomes is the result of a multifaceted approach emphasising political commitment, community engagement, health system strengthening and innovative service delivery mechanisms. Key initiatives such as the Universal Maternal and Child Health Insurance and the Revolving Fund for Contraceptives were instrumental in improving the accessibility of family planning services. These efforts ensured a steady supply of contraceptives and reduced financial barriers for marginalised populations particularly in rural and underserved areas.
CONCLUSION: Bolivia’s success in family planning since 1989 has been driven by strong political commitment and policy reforms that created a supportive sexual and reproductive health policy landscape. This, combined with the contributions of non-governmental organisations, has improved access to family planning services. Despite these advancements, service gaps persist for adolescents and marginalised groups, highlighting the need for continued investment in education and healthcare. This study provides valuable insights for enhancing contraceptive use and meeting family planning needs in similar global contexts.

articles.title: Predicting adolescent physical activity beyond recent behavior: domain-level incremental prediction from motivation measures in two windows.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: An indicator can appear prominent in a fitted model without its wider domain adding distinct predictive information. We examined both repeated indicator prominence and domain-level incremental prediction of later adolescent physical activity beyond recent participation.
METHODS: Four assessments from 3755 Grade 7-8 adolescents at nine schools supported two approximately 3-month prediction windows: June-September (across summer vacation) and September-December. Participant-blocked rolling validation kept each adolescent in one fold and used earlier transitions to predict later activity. Elastic net and XGBoost compared 12 candidate characteristics in five domains with recent-activity-plus-sex baselines.
RESULTS: The recent-activity-plus-sex linear comparator explained 55.4% and 64.9% of held-out variance. Adding all characteristics increased elastic-net R² to.588 and.665 (absolute gains.034, 95% CI [.025,.043], and.017 [.008,.026]). Removing the motivation domain reduced R² across the two windows by.037 and.024 for elastic net and.039 and.026 for XGBoost (2.4-3.9 %age-point losses). Intentions, beliefs about capabilities, and affective appraisal were recurrent prominent indicators; removing the wider affective domain changed R² by approximately zero.
CONCLUSION: Motivation-related measures contributed domain-level predictive information in both windows, whereas prominent affective appraisal did not imply a comparable contribution from its wider domain. Independent school-based replication should assess generalisability, calibration, assessment burden, and decision utility.

articles.title: Longitudinal association between baseline brain entropy and gray matter volume changes in Shidu parents: A five-year multimodal MRI study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People who have lost their only child (Shidu parents) may experience prolonged bereavement-related psychological trauma. Although structural brain alterations have been reported, whether baseline functional complexity is associated with subsequent gray matter volume (GMV) changes remains unclear.
METHODS: This study included 66 Shidu parents and 33 healthy controls. Five-year longitudinal structural MRI was used to assess GMV changes in Shidu parents, and baseline brain entropy (BEN) was derived from resting-state fMRI. Linear mixed-effects models identified regions with significant GMV changes. We then examined associations between baseline BEN and the annualized percent change in GMV (GMV-APC) within these regions, the incremental explanatory value of BEN, and whether these associations differed by GMV change direction.
RESULTS: During the five-year follow-up, 35 brain regions showed significant GMV changes within the Shidu parent group, including GMV decreases in 27 regions and GMV increases in 8 regions. Further analyses showed that baseline BEN was significantly associated with GMV-APC in 6 regions showing GMV decreases and 2 regions showing GMV increases. Overall, these associations were predominantly observed in regions showing GMV decreases, and baseline BEN provided additional explanatory information related to subsequent GMV changes beyond that explained by baseline GMV.
CONCLUSION: A five-year longitudinal follow-up showed that baseline BEN was associated with subsequent GMV changes, providing neuroimaging evidence for the relationship between brain functional complexity and gray matter structural changes in the context of long-term trauma associated with the loss of an only child.

articles.title: Effects of Helium on Carbon Dioxide Elimination and Regional Airway Pressure During High-Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation in a Three-Dimensional Lung Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate regional airway pressures and CO₂ elimination during conventional mechanical ventilation (CMV) and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV), with and without helium, using a reductionist three-dimensional airway model.
METHODS: An infant CT-derived tracheobronchial replica was placed in a 5-L airtight chamber with continuous CO₂ insufflation. Circuit CO₂ partial pressure (PCO₂,circuit) and pressure at proximal (P1), intermediate (P2), and distal (P3) sites were recorded during CMV and HFOV.
RESULTS: Helium reduced PCO₂,circuit during HFOV but increased it during CMV. During HFOV, helium reduced oscillatory pressure amplitude at P1 and P2. At P3, no statistically significant difference was detected (mean difference, 0.08 cmH₂O; 95% CI, -0.02 to 0.18; p = 0.104).
CONCLUSIONS: Helium was associated with enhanced CO₂ elimination during HFOV under the tested settings. The distal pressure result alone does not establish equivalence or a pressure-independent mechanism; regional flow, delivered tidal volume, and specific transport processes require direct investigation.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE OR PURPOSE: To identify patient characteristics associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: Children ≤18 years of age seen at a tertiary care children's hospital between 2009 and 2025 who were prescribed any type of steroid and had a documented intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Children with any IOP measurement >21 mmHg recorded prior to or on the day of steroid initiation were excluded.
METHODS: Steroid type, route of administration, and patient characteristics, including comorbidities, were extracted from the electronic medical record. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ocular hypertension among children who underwent IOP measurement after steroid initiation, defined as IOP >21 mmHg measured within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation.
RESULTS: Of 5,687 children included (mean age at steroid initiation 8.8 years; 54.4% male), 1,034 (18.2%) developed ocular hypertension. The most frequently prescribed steroid was fluticasone (20.0%), and the most common route of administration was inhaled/intranasal (24.8%). In multivariable analysis, glaucoma conferred the highest odds of ocular hypertension after steroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.77; 95% CI, 5.21-8.79), followed by prednisone relative to dexamethasone (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.30-4.93), juvenile arthritis (aOR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.09-2.24), and uveitis (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.16-1.99). Compared with topical administration, ocular (aOR, 3.57; 95% CI, 2.39-5.33) and intravenous (aOR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.78-3.89) routes each independently conferred higher odds of ocular hypertension. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, diabetes, and asthma were not independently associated with ocular hypertension.
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly 1 in 5 children with an IOP measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation developed ocular hypertension. Glaucoma, uveitis, juvenile arthritis, and non-topical routes of administration-particularly ocular and intravenous-were the strongest risk factors, highlighting the importance of ophthalmic monitoring in children receiving glucocorticoid therapy.

articles.title: Physiological and clinical comparison of two high-frequency oscillatory ventilation with volume guarantee strategies in preterm infants with respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the physiological performance and clinical outcomes of two high-frequency oscillatory ventilation with volume guarantee (HFOV-VG) strategies in preterm infants born at less than 30 weeks of gestation.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 88 preterm infants born at less than 30 weeks of gestation received either a low-VThf/high-frequency strategy (oscillatory frequency 15-17 Hz; measured VThf/kg 1.5-1.9 mL/kg; n=61) or a high-VThf/standard-frequency strategy (oscillatory frequency 10-12 Hz; measured VThf/kg 2.0-3.0 mL/kg; n=27). Minute-level ventilator and paired arterial blood gas data were analysed. Clinical outcomes included moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), mortality, and duration of invasive mechanical ventilation.
RESULTS: A total of 267,786 ventilator observations and 825 paired blood gas observations were analysed. PaCO₂ was comparable between strategies (50 [44-56] vs 49 [43-57] mmHg; p=0.67). The low-VThf/high-frequency strategy was associated with lower FiO₂ requirements, reduced oscillatory pressure variability, and shorter invasive mechanical ventilation (10 [6-21] vs 24 [12-39] days; p=0.0005). After adjustment for gestational age, antenatal corticosteroid exposure, and baseline oxygenation index, the high-VThf/standard-frequency strategy remained independently associated with longer invasive mechanical ventilation (duration ratio 1.65, 95% CI 1.13-2.41; p=0.009), but not moderate-to-severe BPD.
CONCLUSIONS: In preterm infants born at less than 30 weeks of gestation, a low-VThf/high-frequency HFOV-VG strategy maintained comparable arterial PaCO₂ control while reducing respiratory support requirements, supporting its use as a physiologically favourable ventilation strategy.

articles.title: Psychological care of children, adolescents and young adults with diabetes.
articles.abstract: The 2026 International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes (ISPAD) Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines on psychological care provide updated, evidence-informed recommendations to support the psychological well-being and quality of life of children, adolescents, and young adults living with diabetes. This update adopts a broader biopsychosocial-spiritual and social ecological framework, recognizing the influence of individual, family, cultural, socioeconomic, and environmental factors on psychological health and diabetes outcomes. A major addition is the consideration of psychological aspects of type 1 diabetes screening, early detection, and staging, including parental anxiety, decision-making, and psychological support during ongoing monitoring. The guidelines also expand their coverage of psychological comorbidities, disordered eating behaviors and eating disorders, neurodevelopmental conditions, parental mental health, transition to adult care, and the broader social impact of diabetes, with particular attention to stigma and health equity. Updated recommendations emphasize the integration of routine psychosocial monitoring and screening into diabetes care, including the use of person-reported outcome measures, caregiver assessment, and stepped-care pathways for identifying and addressing psychological difficulties. The guidelines further highlight the importance of developmentally appropriate, person-centered, culturally sensitive, and multidisciplinary approaches to psychological care. By integrating psychological assessment and support into routine diabetes management, these recommendations aim to promote psychological well-being, strengthen family support, and improve the quality of care for young people living with diabetes across diverse healthcare settings.

articles.title: Children in contact with security units in Türkiye: a nationwide forensic analysis of victimization and delinquency patterns.
articles.abstract: Children's interaction with security units reflects both victimization and delinquency, representing a critical forensic medicine and public health concern. Concurrent national analyses addressing both dimensions remain scarce in Türkiye. This study aimed to evaluate children in contact with security units in Türkiye using national data, focusing on admission reasons, demographic characteristics, victimization types, and offense patterns. This descriptive study used publicly available TÜİK data on "Children Brought to Security Units, 2024," covering 2020-2024. Variables included admission reason, sex, age group, victimization types, and alleged offenses. Results were presented as numbers and percentages. In 2024, a total of 612,651 registered contacts/cases involving children were recorded at security units; 66.6% were male and 33.4% female. Victimization was the leading admission reason (45.6%), followed by delinquency-related contacts (33.1%). Most cases involved the 15-17 age group. Delinquency-related contacts were markedly higher among boys, while girls were more represented in certain victimization types. Injury, sexual crimes, and migrant smuggling were the most prevalent victimization categories, with sexual crimes disproportionately affecting girls. Among alleged delinquent contacts, injury (40.4%) and theft (16.6%) were leading offenses. Substance-related offenses were notable among boys. Registered delinquency-related contacts increased by 80.8% between 2020 and 2024, a trend that may partly reflect changes in reporting, registration, or enforcement practices. Children's contact with security units is shaped by victimization and delinquency, with clear age and sex variations. Forensic medicine specialists play a critical role in medicolegal evaluation and prevention. Gender-sensitive, age-specific, and multidisciplinary strategies are urgently needed.

articles.title: Adverse reactions associated with henna-based cosmetic products: a twenty-two-year pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA adverse event reporting system.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Henna-based cosmetic products, particularly those adulterated with para-phenylenediamine (PPD), are an increasingly recognized cause of adverse skin reactions. Despite widespread consumer use, population-level pharmacovigilance data from US regulatory sources remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical, demographic, and temporal patterns of henna-associated adverse events reported to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and to identify factors associated with case seriousness.
METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of henna-related adverse event reports extracted from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System Cosmetic Public Dashboard, excluding products unrelated to henna (Lawsonia inermis) such as Jagua-based formulations. Statistical analyses included chi-square, Spearman's rank correlation, and Proportional Reporting Ratio disproportionality analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 110 cases were identified (female: 65.5%; pediatric cases <18 years). Black Henna products (classified by product name) represented the largest product category (n = 47, 42.7%). The most frequently reported reactions were pruritus (39.3%), hypersensitivity (32.1%). Serious cases 50.0% of the dataset. No statistically significant association was found between gender and seriousness (χ2=0.133, p = 0.715). hypersensitivity (PRR = 1.54, 95% CI: 0.81-2.92, χ2=1.74, p = 0.187) and urticaria (PRR = 2.26, 95% CI: 0.82-6.18, χ2=2.51, p = 0.113) showed elevated PRR values; however, neither met the predefined signal threshold (PRR ≥ 2.0, χ2≥4.0, n ≥ 3), and no formal disproportionality signal was identified.
CONCLUSIONS: Henna-associated adverse events affect predominantly young females and pediatric patients. These findings support enhanced regulatory scrutiny under the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA), mandatory product labeling, and targeted consumer safety communication.

articles.title: Association Between Weight Percentile and Non-Accidental Trauma in Pediatric Burn Patients Aged 0-4 Years: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early recognition of non-accidental trauma (NAT) in pediatric burn patients remains challenging because no single clinical feature reliably distinguishes abusive from accidental injuries. Although poor growth has been associated with maltreatment, its relationship with NAT in pediatric burn patients is unclear. This study evaluated whether weight percentile is associated with NAT.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the burn registry of a single burn center. Children aged 0-4 years admitted with burn injuries between 2010 and 2021 were included if NAT status and admission weight percentile were available. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between weight percentile and NAT after adjustment for age, sex, race, and total body surface area (TBSA) burned. Sensitivity analyses examined weight percentile thresholds (<5th, <10th, and <25th percentile).
RESULTS: Among 830 patients, 69 (8.3%) had documented NAT. Children with NAT had lower median weight percentiles (46.6 vs. 64.5; p<0.001) and larger burns (median TBSA, 5.0% vs. 3.0%; p<0.001). After adjustment, each 10-percentile decrease in weight percentile was associated with increased odds of NAT (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-1.26; p<0.001). Weight percentile <10th (aOR, 4.10; 95% CI, 1.93-8.69; p<0.001) and <25th percentile (aOR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.17-3.75; p=0.013) were also independently associated with NAT. Model discrimination was modest (AUC=0.674).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower weight percentile was independently associated with NAT in pediatric burn patients aged 0-4 years. Although insufficient as a standalone screening tool, weight percentile is an objective, readily available clinical characteristic that may complement evaluation of suspected maltreatment.

articles.title: Evidence-based expert consensus on long-acting injectable antipsychotics for bipolar disorder: Recommendations from the TSBPN.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop evidence-based expert consensus recommendations from the Taiwanese Society of Biological Psychiatry and Neuropsychopharmacology (TSBPN) on the use of long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics in bipolar disorder.
METHODS: An eight-member working group and 12-member scientific committee formed a 20-member expert panel. A narrative review of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and EMBASE from inception through February 2026 prioritized bipolar-specific evidence and incorporated relevant indirect evidence when necessary. Fourteen statements were graded using the World Federation of Societies of Biological Psychiatry framework for level of evidence (LoE) and acceptability. After expert review and revision, 18 panelists completed anonymous voting to determine the Taiwan recommendation grade (RG-T) and level of agreement.
RESULTS: The 14 statements covered LAI selection, clinical role, timing of initiation, special populations, and safety monitoring. Strong RG-T 1 recommendations supported prioritizing locally approved agents, individualized shared decision-making, use during mania as part of an acute-to-maintenance strategy, maintenance monotherapy or combination treatment, management of suspected nonadherence, earlier use in recurrent illness, use in patients with frequent manic episodes or comorbid substance use disorder, prevention of manic-spectrum recurrence, and combination with established bipolar-depression treatments when clinically indicated. RG-T 2 recommendations addressed older adults, children and adolescents, pregnancy, breastfeeding, and metabolic monitoring. Agreement ranged from 72.2% to 100%. Evidence was strongest for maintenance and manic-spectrum recurrence, but more limited for bipolar depression and several special populations.
CONCLUSION: This TSBPN consensus integrates available evidence with expert judgment to support individualized LAI use across bipolar-disorder treatment settings while highlighting areas requiring further research.

articles.title: Transition Readiness in Adolescents With Chronic Orthopedic Conditions: A Cross-Sectional Study Using the TRAQ Instrument in Mexico.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transition from pediatric to adult care is a high-risk period for adolescents with chronic conditions. Data from Latin American orthopedic populations are lacking.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at a Mexican tertiary hospital. Patients aged 16-26 years with childhood‑onset orthopedic conditions completed the Transition Readiness Assessment Questionnaire (TRAQ) by telephone or in person. TRAQ scores (1-5, higher = better readiness) were compared across sex, age, and diagnosis (physical limitation vs. cognitive impairment).
RESULTS: Of 456 eligible patients, 30 completed the questionnaire (6.6%). Mean age was 19.6 years; 73% were male. Mean global TRAQ score was 2.98. Patients with physical limitations scored higher than those with cognitive impairment (3.39 vs. 2.28, p = .001). Males scored higher than females (3.12 vs. 2.48, p = .041). No patient reached the maintenance stage (score 5).
CONCLUSIONS: Transition readiness is poor, particularly among females and cognitively impaired patients. The 6.6% contact rate indicates profound loss to follow‑up. Structured transition programs are urgently needed.

articles.title: Differential factors associated with adolescent suicide ideation, plans, and attempts in South Korea: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few studies have examined factors differing between adjacent levels of suicidality or between hospital-treated and non-hospital-treated suicide attempts. We examined factors associated with levels of suicidality among South Korean adolescents.
METHODS: We used data from the 2020 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Web-based Survey (N = 54,809). Suicidality was categorised into mutually exclusive groups (i.e., no suicidality, suicide ideation, plans, and attempts, with attempts classified as non-hospital-treated or hospital-treated). We compared the sex-specific prevalence of seven mental health and well-being factors (e.g., depressive symptoms and anxiety), five risk behaviours (e.g., substance use), and four adverse life circumstances (e.g., experience of violence) across suicidality levels. Multivariable logistic regression was used to compare adjacent levels of suicidality.
RESULTS: Overall, 7.2% of adolescents reported suicide ideation, 2.3% plans, and 2.0% attempts (1.7% non-hospital-treated and 0.3% hospital-treated), with higher prevalence among girls. Most risk factors, particularly depressive symptoms (odds ratio [OR]: 4.08, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.74, 4.46), were associated with suicide ideation compared with no suicidality, whereas few factors (e.g., anxiety) differentiated suicide plans from ideation. Compared with suicide plans, suicide attempts were associated with most risk behaviours, including substance use (OR: 2.06, 95% CI: 1.16, 3.66), and with depressive symptoms (OR: 1.48, 95% CI: 1.16, 1.90), experience of violence (OR: 2.00, 95% CI: 1.32, 3.02), and perceived poor academic performance. Among adolescents reporting suicide attempts, anxiety, substance use, and experience of violence were associated with hospital-treated attempts.
CONCLUSION: Population-level mental health promotion may help reduce suicidality, while risk behaviours and violence may be targets for preventing suicide attempts.

articles.title: Psychosocial interventions for adolescent substance use and related outcomes: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review synthesized evidence on the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions for reducing adolescent substance use and improving related psychiatric and psychosocial outcomes.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261284775) on January 14, 2026. The review was conducted between November 13, 2025, and February 14, 2026, and searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science for randomized controlled trials published between January 2015 and December 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool.
RESULTS: Thirty-four RCTs were included. Cognitive-behavioral and motivational approaches were the most frequently investigated interventions (29.41 % and 32.35 % of studies, respectively), although their comparative superiority could not be established. Selected trials reported favorable effects on substance use outcomes, including reduced odds of substance use disorder following a personality-targeted cognitive-behavioral intervention (OR = 0.66, 95 % CI: 0.46-0.92) and reduced smoking initiation following a school-based intervention (OR = 0.65, 95 % CI: 0.44-0.97). However, findings were mixed: a digital intervention showed no significant effect on smoking (OR = 1.01, 95 % CI: 0.62-1.66), and a mindfulness-based intervention showed no advantage over usual treatment in reducing cannabis use (d = 0.02, p = 0.930). Other interventions showed benefits restricted to specific outcomes, subgroups, or follow-up periods. Risk-of-bias assessments identified some concerns in 20 studies (58.82 %) and high risk in 14 (41.18 %).
CONCLUSIONS: Psychosocial interventions may improve selected adolescent substance use outcomes, but findings are heterogeneous and frequently include non-significant or time-limited effects. Methodological limitations, variability in outcome measures, and the absence of a pooled quantitative synthesis prevent firm conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness and clinical significance.

articles.title: Imaging in young ischemic stroke: a pictorial review.
articles.abstract: Young ischemic stroke encompasses a group of cerebrovascular disorders occurring in patients younger than 45 years, with pediatric stroke generally defined as stroke occurring between 28 days and 18 years of age. The incidence of stroke in the pediatric and young adult population is increasing and is emerging as a major public health issue. Diagnosis of young stroke is often challenging because of non-specific clinical presentations, etiologies that differ from those in older adults, and the wide range of stroke mimics. Imaging plays a critical role in the prompt and accurate diagnosis of young stroke by characterizing stroke subtypes, identifying underlying causes, assessing vascular abnormalities, and guiding management decisions. This pictorial review highlights the current imaging workup for diagnosing young stroke describing the advantages and limitations of various imaging modalities. We present a pictorial review of stroke in the young based on their imaging features, differentiating them from common stroke mimics. Using a multimodality case-based approach, we illustrate the characteristic imaging findings and classic signs of a broad spectrum of young ischemic stroke etiologies. They range from common causes like cardioembolism and dissection to less common infectious, metabolic and genetic causes like Borrelia vasculitis, Fabry disease and Adenosine deaminase 2 deficiency (DADA2). This review aims to equip radiologists and trainees with a structured and practical approach to the diagnosis and management of young stroke through classic imaging patterns and illustrative cases, ultimately facilitating improved patient outcome.

articles.title: Two international Delphi surveys on labels and descriptors to inform the new classification criteria for juvenile idiopathic arthritides.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Developing an evidence-based classification of the group of juvenile idiopathic arthritides (JIA) is a topic of high relevance. A two-round international Delphi survey was conducted among paediatric rheumatologists to identify the most appropriate names (labels) and the most relevant descriptors used by physicians to define JIA categories.
METHODS: In Delphi 1, participants reported with open-ended responses the descriptors they used to identify JIA categories, and whether and how, these categories should be re-labelled. In Delphi 2, respondents ranked the top three disease labels and the top 10 disease descriptors that emerged from Delphi 1 from best to worst for each JIA category; a weighted score was calculated multiplying the sum of ranks for the selection frequency.
RESULTS: Overall, 330 and 470 physicians responded to Delphi 1 and Delphi 2, respectively. The highest-ranking labels and descriptors were: 'juvenile-onset Still's disease' and response to IL-1 inhibitors for systemic arthritis, 'RF or ACPAs positive JIA' and RF/ACPA positivity for RF-positive polyarthritis; 'polyarticular JIA' and age at onset <18 years for RF-negative polyarthritis; 'juvenile PsA' and dactylitis for psoriatic arthritis (PsA); 'early-onset spondyloarthritis' and HLA-B27 positivity for enthesitis-related arthritis, 'oligoarticular JIA' and ANA positivity for oligoarthritis, 'early-onset ANA-positive arthritis' and ANA positivity with RF negativity for early-onset ANA-positive arthritis; and 'undifferentiated JIA' and arthritis fitting more than one category for undifferentiated arthritis.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the category labels and descriptors to be prioritized in the future development of the new JIA classification criteria.

articles.title: Recurrent Pediatric Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans of the Abdominal Wall: A Rare Case Report With Diagnostic and Surgical Challenges.
articles.abstract: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a rare, locally aggressive sarcoma usually seen in adults. We report a recurrent epigastric DFSP in an 11-year-old boy, initially misdiagnosed on incisional biopsy. Accurate diagnosis and successful treatment required wide excision, careful surgical planning, and multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Clinically Suspected Fulminant Myocarditis Following PCR-Confirmed Pertussis in an Infant: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Cardiac involvement following pertussis infection is uncommon but may be associated with severe clinical deterioration in infants.
