We report the case of a 3-month-old girl who developed shock, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe biventricular systolic dysfunction approximately 2 weeks after PCR-confirmed Bordetella pertussis infection. Echocardiography demonstrated marked left ventricular dilatation, global hypokinesia, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%. Troponin I was markedly elevated. The clinical presentation was consistent with suspected fulminant myocarditis, although definitive myocardial confirmation was unavailable. The infant received intensive supportive care, inotropic treatment, heart failure medications, antiarrhythmic therapy, and intravenous immunoglobulin, with subsequent clinical and echocardiographic improvement. She was discharged in a stable condition but died unexpectedly approximately 2 months later. The immediate cause of death remained undetermined. This case emphasizes the importance of early cardiac assessment and structured post-discharge surveillance in infants with severe cardiac dysfunction following pertussis infection.

articles.title: Novel Breath Segmentation and Predictive Quality Classification Model for Pediatric Bag-Mask Ventilation Using Capnography Waveforms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bag-mask ventilation (BMV) is a critical phase of pediatric airway management, yet objective feedback remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a two-stage, CO2-only framework for pediatric BMV assessment comprising automated breath segmentation and machine learning classification of breaths according to predefined low-quality criteria for insufficient ventilation. We hypothesized that our model would achieve area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) greater than or equal to 0.75 and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) greater than or equal to 0.75.
DERIVATION COHORT: We retrospectively analyzed capnography waveforms from 85 critically ill children receiving peri-intubation BMV in a quaternary-care PICU. Flow and pressure data established reference-standard low-quality criteria: expiratory tidal volume (VTE) less than 4 mL/kg of ideal body weight, mask leak greater than 40%, or upper airway obstruction (VTE < 4 mL/kg with peak inspiratory pressure > 30 cm H2O and leak > 80%).
VALIDATION COHORT: CO2-based segmentation was validated in 10 randomly selected patients comprising 605 manually adjudicated breaths. Classification performance was internally validated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation within the derivation cohort; no independent validation cohort was used.
PREDICTION MODEL: A rule-based algorithm segmented continuous CO2 waveforms into breaths. Deep learning architectures then used CO2 waveforms alone to classify breaths according to whether they met predefined low-quality criteria.
RESULTS: The CO2-only algorithm identified 6942 breaths (median, 66 per patient [interquartile range, 47-100 per patient]); 49.5% met at least one low-quality criterion. Segmentation achieved positive predictive value 0.95 (95% CI, 0.93-0.96) and sensitivity 0.86 (95% CI, 0.83-0.89). Twenty-seven breaths were adjudicated as false-positive detections (0.05; 95% CI, 0.036-0.074). CO2-only segmentation may miss ventilatory attempts with minimal or absent exhaled CO2. The best-performing classification model achieved AUROC 0.79 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89) and AUPRC 0.75 (95% CI, 0.57-0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: A CO2-only framework showed proof-of-concept feasibility for breath segmentation and quality classification during pediatric BMV, supporting further development of objective bedside feedback systems.

articles.title: Effects of L-Carnitine Supplementation on Clinical Outcomes, Metabolic Profile, and Organ Function in Critically Ill Children: A Triple-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Critically ill children often develop relative l-carnitine deficiency due to hypermetabolism, which can impair mitochondrial energy production and exacerbate organ dysfunction. While adult data suggest that l-carnitine supplementation improves metabolic and clinical outcomes, robust randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in the pediatric intensive care population are lacking.
METHODS: This double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). Critically ill children aged 1 month to 12 years were randomly assigned to receive enteral l-carnitine (50-100 mg/kg/day, maximum 2000 mg/day) or placebo for seven consecutive days. The primary outcome was change in serum total protein. Secondary and exploratory outcomes included changes in glycemic profile, lipid profile, liver function tests, renal function tests, coagulation parameters, blood gas parameters, and clinical outcomes including 28-day mortality and Glasgow Coma Scale.
RESULTS: The l-carnitine group showed between-group improvements in liver and tissue injury markers compared to placebo, with reductions in ALT (p = 0.01) and LDH (p = 0.002). While serum albumin improved in both groups, between-group differences were non-significant. Within-group increases were observed for HDL (p < 0.001) and TG (p = 0.03) in the l-carnitine arm. No significant between-group differences were observed for blood sugar, renal function, or coagulation parameters. Notably, the l-carnitine group showed less favorable median shifts in PCO2 and pH (p = 0.01 and p = 0.03, respectively). 28-day mortality was numerically lower in the l-carnitine group than in the placebo group; however, this difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: Enteral l-carnitine supplementation for 7 days was associated with exploratory reductions in biomarkers of tissue and hepatocellular injury (LDH and ALT). However, it did not improve lipid profiles, clinical outcomes, or mortality, and was associated with less favorable acid-base alterations. Larger randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these exploratory findings and clarify the clinical relevance of these effects in critically ill children.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT: IRCT20221206056734N3).

articles.title: Preoperative Serum Biomarkers Improve Prediction of Poor Postoperative Outcome After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Compared With Clinical Variables in Neonates.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Neonates undergoing surgery for congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk for poor postoperative outcomes after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), including death, prolonged ICU stay, and ICU readmission. Current prognostic models rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical factors.
OBJECTIVES: To utilize machine learning methods to compare the predictive utility of preoperative blood biomarkers vs. clinical features alone for ICU-30, a validated composite outcome after neonatal CPB that includes postoperative 30-day morbidity and mortality.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prospective observational single-center cohort study of consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days undergoing CPB for CHD.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Plasma and clinical data were collected from consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days immediately before CPB. Thirty-seven biomarkers were measured by individual or multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and tested for association with ICU-30, defined as 1) mortality within 30 days of CPB, 2) ICU stay longer than 30 days, or 3) ICU readmission within 30 days. Predictive performance of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and random forest (RF) models was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). For XGBoost, the top 20 features were identified based on model importance (gain).
RESULTS: Biomarkers were available for 144 neonates. Most were male (51%), White (64%), and non-Hispanic (75%). Most operations were Society of Thoracic Surgeons-European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery (STAT) category 3 (32%) or STAT category 5 (29%). ICU-30 occurred in 29 neonates (20%). Using combined clinical and biomarker data, XGBoost demonstrated moderate discrimination for ICU-30 (AUROC, 0.74), outperformed RF (AUROC, 0.72), and LASSO (AUROC, 0.70). Biomarkers alone performed better (AUROC, 0.72) than clinical data alone (AUROC, 0.67) with XGBoost. The top two features in the combined XGBoost model were neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and trefoil factor 3 (TFF3). Using Shapley additive explanation to assess both predictive impact and directionality, the most influential features were NGAL, a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13 (ADAMTS13), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among neonates with CHD requiring CPB, multibiomarker models improved prediction of poor postoperative outcome compared with clinical variables alone. The most informative model features included markers of renal injury/perfusion and gastrointestinal epithelial injury (NGAL and TFF3), as well as vascular injury and inflammation (ADAMTS13 and Ang-2). These findings support further investigation of biomarker-informed risk stratification and may provide insight into pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying adverse postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: A Gap on Judgment of Fertility and the Need for Contraception Between Physicians and Patients With Rheumatic Diseases: A Multicenter Questionnaire Survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Effective contraception is essential for women of reproductive age with rheumatic disease (RD), specifically those receiving teratogenic drugs, and physicians should recognize that these women may wish to conceive or control their fertility. This study aimed to evaluate the status of preconception care and contraception use, awareness, and counseling among women with RD in Japan.
METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire survey included Japanese women with RD (age: 18-45 years) and their attending physicians, conducted between September 2023 and May 2024 at 14 medical institutions. Patient and physician responses were linked and analyzed.
RESULTS: In total, 157 patients completed the survey. Of these, 35% of patients wished to conceive in the future and 38% were aware of their current need for contraception. The results revealed a gap between physicians' and patients' judgment of fertility and the need for contraception. Most patients used less effective contraceptive methods (condoms: 67.1%; withdrawal: 20.5%). Although patients were aware of the need for contraception, only 12% had received specific contraception instructions from their healthcare providers, whereas 39% had never received contraception counseling. Most of the patients decided on contraceptive methods themselves or together with their partners. One patient who tested positive for antiphospholipid antibodies used contraindicated estrogen-containing contraceptives.
CONCLUSION: Significant deficiencies exist in contraception counseling and awareness among women with RD. Proactive and system-building approaches are urgently required to improve preconception care and reproductive safety in this population.

articles.title: From Autoantigens to GlycoRNAs: The Prehistory of RNA at the Cell Surface.
articles.abstract: The discovery of glycoRNAs in 2021 transformed the study of cell-surface biology, but it did not emerge from a vacuum. A substantial, though heterogeneous, body of evidence accumulated over four decades, suggesting that several nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) can access the outer plasma membrane under defined biological conditions. This historical perspective traces that development from the earliest hints in 1981, through the founding observations of 1989-1990 when La/SSB, nucleolin, and Ku70 were independently detected at the cell surface, to the consolidation period of 1990-1995 that connected surface-expressed RNP autoantigens to neonatal lupus and photosensitive cutaneous lupus, and finally to the glycoRNA era beginning in 2021. Throughout, early researchers working with limited tools identified the key phenomenon: surface-expressed nuclear RBPs as potential autoimmune triggers. They articulated the core hypothesis that modern glycoRNA biology is now positioned to test.

articles.title: Transformations in play. Dyadic work inspired by psychoanalytic infant observation.
articles.abstract: The article explores the psychoanalytic foundations of Watch Me Play! (WMP), an applied approach first developed to promote understanding of the needs of babies and young children in care, now more widely used to support parent-child relationships and child development. Watch Me Play! is derived from psychoanalytic infant observation and underpinned by key concepts in child development research such as mind-mindedness, joint attention and contingent responsiveness. The relevance of the central psychoanalytic concepts of attention and time in the thinking of Freud, Bion and Birksted-Breen is illustrated in clinical examples from work with the group for whom the approach was first developed: infants and young children who have experienced abuse, neglect and disrupted attachments, together with their foster carers or adoptive parents.

articles.title: Internalizing and externalizing symptoms and social problem-solving difficulties in adolescents in residential care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents in residential care frequently present mental health and psychosocial adjustment difficulties. However, within this population, research comparing adolescents with documented maltreatment histories and those placed due to other documented inadequate-care or protection-related situations remains scarce. This study aimed to analyze emotional and behavioral problems and social problem-solving difficulties among adolescents in residential care and to examine, among those with maltreatment histories, their association with sociocognitive processes.
METHODS: This observational cross-sectional study included 84 adolescents aged 12-17 years in residential care, divided into a group with a documented history of maltreatment (n = 59) and a group placed due to other documented inadequate-care or protection-related situations (n = 25). The Child and Adolescent Assessment System (SENA) and the Social Cognitive Attitudes and Strategies Questionnaire (AECS) were used. Group differences were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U tests. Within the maltreatment group, partial Spearman correlations and linear regression models were performed, controlling for age, sex, polyvictimization, and length of stay in residential care. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied for multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: Adolescents with documented maltreatment histories showed higher scores in anxiety, posttraumatic symptomatology, attention problems, and global behavioral problems, with small to small-to-moderate effect sizes (all adjusted p = 0.032), whereas no group differences were found in social problem-solving difficulties. Within the maltreatment group, significant partial correlations showed that anxiety and social anxiety were associated with greater social problem-solving difficulties. Behavioral symptoms, particularly attention problems and antisocial behavior, showed significant associations with social problem-solving difficulties. The Emotional Index × Behavioral Index interaction was associated with difficulty obtaining information and difficulty generating solutions after adjustment for covariates and multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.048 for both). This association was strongest at low Emotional Index levels and weakened as the Emotional Index increased.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide a better understanding of the psychological vulnerability and sociocognitive functioning of adolescents in residential care with documented maltreatment histories. They suggest a differentiated pattern linking behavioral and anxiety-related symptoms, particularly social anxiety, to social problem-solving difficulties. Future studies should evaluate integrated interventions combining emotional regulation, behavioral regulation, and social problem-solving in residential care settings.

articles.title: Uveitic glaucoma in a multi-ethnic Malaysian cohort: demography, risk factors and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between uveitis and secondary glaucoma has been established, but the specific factors associated with progression to uveitic glaucoma remain poorly defined. This study aims to identify the prevalence and factors associated with uveitic glaucoma, and their clinical outcomes in a Malaysian cohort.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study reviewing the clinical records of patients who attended the uveitis clinics at tertiary eye centres in Kuala Lumpur and Sarawak, Malaysia.
RESULTS: A total of 257 eyes from 163 patients were included. Mean age at uveitis onset was 37.3 ± 16.2 years with a slight female predominance. The prevalence of uveitic ocular hypertension and uveitic glaucoma was 26.1% and 30.0% respectively. Multiple logistic regression identified age of onset (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.023; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.003-1.044, p = 0.023), male gender (aOR 1.970; 95% CI 1.046-3.709, p = 0.036), presence of posterior synechiae (PS) (aOR 3.326; 95% CI 1.092-10.133, p = 0.034), peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS) (aOR 4.606; 95% CI 2.065-10.272, p < 0.001) and intraocular pressure (IOP) at presentation (aOR 1.077; 95% CI 1.039-1.117, p < 0.001) as significant factors for uveitic glaucoma. Steroid responsiveness occurred in 74 (29.2%) corticosteroid-treated eyes. Fifty-three eyes (36.80%) required at least one glaucoma incisional surgery. Chronic uveitis (p = 0.004) and PAS (p < 0.001) were associated with a higher percentage of glaucoma surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Older age of onset, male gender, presence of PS or PAS, and elevated presenting IOP were significant factors associated with uveitic glaucoma. Additionally, chronic uveitis and PAS were factors associated with a higher percentage of glaucoma surgery. Early identification of these factors can prevent onset of uveitic glaucoma, which is a potential blinding complication of uveitis.

articles.title: Exploring parents' experiences of palliative care in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU): a meta-synthesis of qualitative research.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: When the goals of care for a critically ill child in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) shift from curative treatment toward palliative care, parents' experiences are often complex and multifaceted. This review aimed primarily to synthesize qualitative evidence on parents' experiences and, secondarily, to examine the interpretive relevance and boundaries of Weick's sensemaking framework after the data-driven synthesis had been completed.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative systematic review using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) meta-aggregation approach. PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and ProQuest were searched from inception to 2 February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted author-generated analytical findings and supporting participant illustrations, and appraised methodological quality. Findings were synthesized inductively; the 15 resulting subdomains were subsequently mapped to Weick's seven properties of sensemaking.
RESULTS: Ten studies were included. Meta-aggregation generated five interrelated synthesized findings: (1) confronting and understanding the end-of-life reality; (2) finding recognition and support through relational networks; (3) maintaining the parental role; (4) safeguarding comfort, dignity, and farewell; and (5) continuing care and connection after the child's death.
CONCLUSIONS: Parents' experiences encompassed efforts to understand a changing clinical situation, rely on relationships with clinicians and others, remain involved as parents, protect the child's comfort and dignity, and sustain connection after death. Weick's framework helped interpret how parents used clinical cues, relationships, identity, and caregiving actions to construct a workable understanding of events, but gave less attention to grief-related emotions, surrogate decision-making burden, cultural and spiritual meaning, organizational constraints, and continuing bonds. The findings may inform family-centered communication, parental-role support, individualized end-of-life care, and bereavement services in the PICU.

articles.title: Emotional childhood trauma, attachment dimensions, and depression severity in women with major depressive disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood trauma is a well-established risk factor for depression in adulthood. However, its clinical correlates may differ according to trauma subtype and patient population. In women with major depressive disorder, attachment-related interpersonal patterns may be relevant to understanding variation in depressive symptom severity. This study examined childhood trauma subtypes, attachment anxiety, attachment avoidance, and depression severity in adult women with major depressive disorder.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 120 adult women with major depressive disorder who had not yet initiated pharmacological or psychotherapeutic treatment for the current depressive episode. Participants completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-33, the Experiences in Close Relationships Scale-Short Form, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Spearman correlation analyses were used to examine bivariate relationships among study variables. Exploratory cross-sectional indirect association models with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were estimated to examine whether attachment dimensions statistically accounted for the associations between childhood trauma subtypes and depression severity.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 35.85 years (SD = 12.53), and the mean PHQ-9 score was 16.48 (SD = 5.03). Overall childhood trauma was correlated with PHQ-9 scores (ρ = 0.246, p < 0.01). Among trauma subtypes, emotional abuse (ρ = 0.203, p < 0.05), physical abuse (ρ = 0.246, p < 0.01), and emotional neglect (ρ = 0.236, p < 0.01) were correlated with PHQ-9 scores. In exploratory indirect association models, attachment anxiety showed indirect estimates with confidence intervals excluding zero for emotional abuse (B = 0.042, 95% CI [0.003, 0.111]) and emotional neglect (B = 0.037, 95% CI [0.004, 0.101]). Attachment avoidance showed indirect estimates with confidence intervals excluding zero for emotional abuse (B = 0.037, 95% CI [0.001, 0.112]), physical abuse (B = 0.061, 95% CI [0.001, 0.177]), sexual abuse (B = 0.092, 95% CI [0.009, 0.228]), and emotional neglect (B = 0.030, 95% CI [0.001, 0.091]).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that attachment-related interpersonal processes may be relevant to the association between childhood trauma and depression severity in women with major depressive disorder. However, given the cross-sectional design and the exploratory nature of the indirect association analyses, the results should be interpreted cautiously and require replication in larger longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Parental experience of end-of-life care for their infant or child in the United Kingdom.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence confirms that provision of end-of-life care for infants, children and young people varies across the United Kingdom, however it is not clear how this variation impacts children and their families.
METHODS: This study aimed to assess parental outcomes and experiences of their infant, child or young person receiving end-of-life care in the United Kingdom through a cross-sectional mixed-methods survey. Bereaved parents were sent a survey, after their infant or child had died and had received end-of-life care in a neonatal or paediatric intensive care unit. The survey yielded qualitative and quantitative data, which were analysed using qualitative content analysis and graphical summaries of quantitative results. Data were integrated using joint display matrices.
RESULTS: One hundred sixty nine bereaved parents completed the survey, of which 60% were White British mothers of infants. Overall experiences were positive, however there were some differences between care settings and a minority reported mostly negative experiences. Key components of end-of-life care were not always available and choices over place of care were limited. Experiences of care as death approached were more positive. However, experiences of after death care, such as the use of cooling facilities, were highly variable with some parents expressing regret at not having the chance to have extended time with their child.
CONCLUSIONS: Parental experiences of end-of-life care varied widely, with key components often not available. Ensuring consistently high-quality care across all settings is essential to support parents' enduring wellbeing.

articles.title: Clinicopathological characteristics and short-term follow-up outcomes of IgA vasculitis nephritis in pediatric and adult patients: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare the clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, renal pathological features, immune complex deposition patterns, and short-term follow-up outcomes between pediatric and adult patients with IgA vasculitis nephritis (IgAVN).
METHODS: A retrospective review of 441 biopsy-confirmed IgAVN patients was conducted. Patients were divided into pediatric (age < 18 years, n = 305) and adult (age ≥ 18 years, n = 136) groups. General demographic data, clinical classification, laboratory parameters, pathological grades (glomerular and tubulointerstitial), immune complex deposition patterns, and short-term follow-up outcomes were collected and compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Significant differences were found in sex distribution, time from IgAVN to kidney biopsy, and clinical classification. The adult group had higher levels of urea (BUN), creatinine (Cr), uric acid (UA), fibrinogen (FIB), IgG, IgA, C3, and C4, whereas the pediatric group had higher prothrombin time (PT), thrombin time (TT), D-dimer (DD), and fibrin degradation product (FDPs) levels. The degree of glomerular pathological injury and chronic tubulointerstitial injury were significantly more severe in the adult group than in the pediatric group, whereas no statistically significant difference was observed in the overall distribution of acute tubulointerstitial injury or immune complex deposition patterns. Prognosis was worse in the adult group.
CONCLUSION: Adult patients showed a greater burden of chronic histopathological lesions and a less favorable distribution of short-term outcome categories than pediatric patients. These differences were associated with age group but may also reflect differences in biopsy timing, baseline kidney function, and treatment exposure.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Attitudes of registered nurses toward palliative and end-of-life care in Macao: a cross-sectional study in an east-meets-west context.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurses' attitudes toward palliative and end-of-life care may affect communication with patients and families, symptom support, and willingness to provide care for dying patients. Evidence from Macao remains limited despite its ageing population and healthcare context shaped by Chinese cultural traditions and Western medical practice.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to August 2021 in the main public hospital in Macao. Registered nurses completed an anonymous online questionnaire containing demographic/professional items and the Chinese version of the Frommelt Attitude Toward Care of the Dying scale. Negatively worded FATCOD items were reverse-coded before total scores were calculated. Welch tests, Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons, effect sizes, and multivariable linear regression with robust standard errors were used.
RESULTS: A total of 282 nurses completed the survey. Most were female (88.3%), held a bachelor's degree (75.5%), and had no palliative care training (61.0%). The mean FATCOD score was 110.45 (SD = 8.22), and internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach's alpha = 0.804). In adjusted analysis, prior palliative care experience was associated with higher FATCOD scores (B = 4.22, robust SE = 1.22, p < .001). Work unit also remained associated with scores; compared with Surgery, Pediatrics, Internal Medicine, and Orthopedics/Rehabilitation had higher adjusted scores. The model explained 22.6% of the variance.
CONCLUSIONS: Registered nurses in Macao reported moderately favorable attitudes toward palliative and end-of-life care. Training and experience should be strengthened, but cultural explanations should be interpreted cautiously because cultural beliefs were not directly measured.

articles.title: Associations between adverse childhood experiences and later-life multiple functional limitation in older adults across four cohorts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study is to evaluate the association between Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and multiple functional limitation in older adults across various international settings.
METHODS: We used longitudinal data from 78,417 adults aged 50 years or older in four ageing cohorts: the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), and the Health and Retirement Study (HRS). Six ACE indicators were assessed retrospectively (physical abuse, emotional neglect, parental death, foster care placement, financial hardship, and parental unemployment) and analyzed in two ways: as the cumulative number of ACEs (categorized as 0, 1, 2, or ≥ 3), and as four ACE types (physical abuse, emotional neglect, adverse family environment, and economic adversity). At each survey wave, multiple functional limitation was measured as the number of impairments across six domains (hearing, vision, physical functioning, mobility, mental health, and cognition), giving a score from 0 to 6. Within each cohort, we used survey-weighted generalized estimating equations with a Poisson distribution to estimate associations with functional limitation, adjusting for age, sex, and survey wave. Cohort-specific risk ratios (RRs) were then combined using random-effects meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Across all cohorts, the proportion reporting at least one ACE ranged from 32.6% in ELSA to 66.9% in CHARLS. Compared with those reporting no ACE, the RRs (95% CI) for functional limitations were 1.17 (1.09-1.26) for one ACE, 1.29 (1.17-1.43) for two ACEs, and 1.39 (1.20-1.61) for three or more ACEs. Among the four ACE types, physical abuse (RR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.08-1.29), economic adversity (RR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.10-1.23), and emotional neglect (RR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.20) were each associated with higher functional limitation. Increased risks were observed across all six domains, with the strongest associations for mental disorders among individuals with three or more ACEs (RR, 1.82). The findings were consistent across cohorts and robust in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: ACEs were consistently associated with a greater risk of experiencing multiple functional limitations in later life, emphasizing the importance of mitigating childhood adversity to promote healthier ageing.

articles.title: Associations between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying among adolescents: a three-wave longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Negative bystander behaviors significantly shape the trajectory of cyberbullying incidents. Previous research has established a link between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying. However, little is known about the longitudinal mechanisms underlying this relationship. To address this gap, the current study investigated the mediating role of callous‑unemotional traits and the moderating role of perceived social support in the longitudinal association between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying.
METHODS: A total of 1531 Chinese adolescents (49.8% female) with an average age of 16.12 years (SD = 0.34) participated in a three-wave longitudinal study with 6-month intervals. Validated self-report measures were used to assess childhood emotional maltreatment, callous‑unemotional traits, perceived social support, and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying. A moderated mediation model was tested using path analysis with bootstrapping (5000 resamples), after confirming the measurement model via confirmatory factor analysis.
RESULTS: The results revealed that childhood emotional maltreatment was positively associated with negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying 12 months later, and this association was mediated by callous‑unemotional traits. Perceived social support buffered the association between childhood emotional maltreatment and callous‑unemotional traits and mitigated the link between callous‑unemotional traits and negative bystander behavior. Further findings revealed that the indirect pathway of callous‑unemotional traits was more pronounced when levels of perceived social support were low, and higher levels of perceived social support could disrupt the mediating pathway of callous‑unemotional traits between childhood emotional maltreatment and negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying.
CONCLUSIONS: This study enhances understanding of the longitudinal mechanisms linking childhood emotional maltreatment to negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying through callous‑unemotional traits. The findings highlight the importance of promoting perceived social support as a buffer that can disrupt this mediating pathway, providing empirical evidence for interventions aimed at reducing negative bystander behavior in cyberbullying among adolescents.

articles.title: Environmental risk factors in Juvenile dermatomyositis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is a rare autoimmune vasculopathy of childhood. Alongside genetic predisposition, environmental exposures are thought to influence when the disease begins and how it progresses. Despite many reports, the evidence base is fragmented, with few studies able to draw firm conclusions.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review according to PRISMA 2020 standards, searching six major databases and conference proceedings (2005-2025). Eligible studies investigated environmental, infectious, chemical, physical, lifestyle, or psychosocial exposures in children with JDM. Two reviewers independently screened articles, extracted data, and assessed study quality using NIH and ROBINS-E tools. Results were summarized by exposure type.
RESULTS: One hundred forty-eight studies were included. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation was the most consistently reported factor, with recent sun exposure often preceding onset or chronic disease, particularly in defined autoantibody subgroups. Infections, especially viral and respiratory, were frequently described as triggers of onset or relapse. Air pollutants and maternal exposures during pregnancy also emerged as significant risks. Psychosocial stress, including early adversity and pandemic-related distress, was linked to flares. By contrast, structured exercise, particularly aquatic therapy, improved fitness and fatigue without worsening disease.
CONCLUSIONS: Multiple modifiable environmental influences appear relevant in JDM. Strategies such as UV protection, minimizing pollutant exposure, and tailored exercise may benefit patients. Well-designed, prospective studies are urgently needed to clarify causal pathways and inform prevention.
PROSPERO: Registration number: CRD42024595442PROSPERO.

articles.title: Expression and mechanism exploration of miR-483-5p in children with IgA vasculitis with nephritis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: IgA vasculitis with nephritis (IgAVN) represents the most serious renal complication in pediatric patients with IgA vasculitis (IgAV).
AIMS: To characterize miR‑483‑5p expression in pediatric IgAVN patients, evaluate its potential as a diagnostic biomarker, and elucidate underlying molecular mechanisms.
METHODS: A total of 150 children with IgAV (55 with IgAVN, 95 with non‑IgAVN) and 60 age‑ and gender‑matched healthy controls were enrolled in this retrospective clinical study. RT-qPCR was used to detect miR-483-5p and HDAC4 mRNA expression. ROC curve analysis was conducted to assess its tentative auxiliary screening capacity for IgAV-associated renal injury. Pearson correlation analysis was used to analyze the correlation between miR-483-5p expression and clinical indicators. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify factors independently associated IgAVN. Human glomerular mesangial cells (HGMCs) were treated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to construct cell model.
RESULTS: miR-483-5p was markedly downregulated in the serum and renal tissues of children with IgAVN, and serum miR-483-5p exhibited significant discriminative capacity to distinguish children with concurrent IgAVN from IgAV patients without renal involvement in this retrospective cohort. MiR-483-5p expression was negatively correlated with renal function indicators, serum IgA and inflammatory factors, and its low expression was an independently associated factor for IgAVN. In vitro, LPS downregulated miR-483-5p, promoted HGMC proliferation and inflammatory response. MiR-483-5p directly targeted and negatively regulated HDAC4. Overexpression of miR-483-5p inhibited LPS-induced HGMC proliferation and inflammatory factor secretion, while HDAC4 overexpression reversed these effects.
CONCLUSIONS: miR‑483‑5p is downregulated in children with IgAVN and may serve as a potential non‑invasive auxiliary indicator for pediatric IgAVN. miR‑483‑5p attenuates LPS‑induced HGMC proliferation and inflammation by targeting HDAC4 in vitro; however, the in vivo mechanistic relevance and clinical utility remain preliminary and require further validation.

articles.title: Bereaved mothers' and nurses' experiences of neonatal palliative and bereavement care in Iran: a qualitative content analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The death of a newborn in a neonatal intensive care unit is a profound experience for parents and nurses. Understanding how bereaved mothers and nurses experience communication, parental participation, farewell practices and continuing support can inform care that is responsive to families' individual and cultural preferences. This study explored bereaved mothers' and neonatal intensive care unit nurses' experiences of neonatal palliative and bereavement care in Iran and examined similarities and differences between their accounts.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study using conventional content analysis was conducted in the neonatal intensive care units of two tertiary university hospitals in Iran. Participants were selected through purposive sampling with maximum variation. Individual, semi structured, face to face interviews were conducted with mothers who had experienced the death of a newborn during the previous 12 months and nurses with experience caring for newborns and families during end-of-life care. Data were collected from March 2024 to January 2025. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed verbatim, anonymized and analyzed inductively using MAXQDA Analytics Pro 2020. Credibility, dependability, confirmability and transferability were supported through transcript review, independent coding, participant feedback, research team discussions, reflexive memo writing and maintenance of an audit trail.
RESULTS: Fifteen bereaved mothers and 18 neonatal intensive care unit nurses participated. Analysis generated three themes: losing and reclaiming maternal agency during neonatal end of life care, nurses' emotional labor in sustaining compassionate bereavement care and building a culturally responsive continuum of neonatal palliative and bereavement care. Mothers described receiving fragmented or indirect information, having restricted opportunities for presence and participation and seeking meaningful ways to acknowledge and remember their newborn. Nurses described providing emotional support while managing their own responses, professional responsibilities, educational preparation and organizational conditions. The accounts of both groups emphasized compassionate communication, respectful recognition of the newborn, individualized memory making, spiritual sensitivity and continuing support. Differences between their accounts concerned family mediated disclosure, maternal participation, opportunities for presence and touch, professional emotional expression and responsibility for follow up care.
CONCLUSIONS: Participants' accounts suggest that neonatal palliative and bereavement care may be strengthened by directly assessing each mother's preferences for communication and participation, sensitively offering individualized opportunities for farewell and memory making, and establishing clearly coordinated follow-up care. Education, reflective support and supportive organizational processes may assist nurses in providing compassionate care to newborns and bereaved families.

articles.title: The effect of educational intervention using a multimedia package in the prevention of sexual abuse in preschool children on knowledge and attitude of mothers: a quasi-experimental study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preschool children are particularly vulnerable to child sexual abuse. Mothers, as primary caregivers, play a key role in protecting children from sexual abuse through appropriate knowledge and preventive practices. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a multimedia educational intervention on mothers' knowledge and attitudes regarding the prevention of CSA among preschool children.
METHODS: This quasi-experimental educational study included 84 mothers of preschool children who were recruited through multistage cluster sampling from five comprehensive health service centers in Rasht, Iran. Participants were allocated to intervention and control groups. Data were collected at baseline, two weeks after the intervention, and four weeks after the intervention. Mothers in the intervention group received a six-week multimedia educational program delivered via DVD and reinforced through weekly educational reminders sent via social media, whereas the control group received routine care only during the study period. Mothers completed researcher-developed knowledge and attitude questionnaires at all three assessment points.
RESULTS: At baseline, there were no significant differences between the intervention and control groups in knowledge (P = 0.157) or attitude (P = 0.444). Following the intervention, the mean knowledge score in the intervention group increased from 26.19 ± 3.47 at baseline to 32.07 ± 2.18 at two weeks and remained significantly higher (30.83 ± 2.58) at four weeks. The mean attitude score also increased from 125.62 ± 10.81 at baseline to 135.88 ± 10.20 at two weeks and 132.45 ± 10.75 at four weeks. Compared with the control group, knowledge scores were significantly higher at two weeks (P < 0.001) and four weeks (P < 0.001). Likewise, attitude scores were significantly higher at two weeks (P < 0.001) and four weeks (P = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: The multimedia educational intervention significantly improved mothers' knowledge and attitudes regarding the prevention of child sexual abuse among preschool children. These findings suggest that culturally adapted multimedia education may provide an effective and accessible approach for strengthening parental education and supporting community-based child sexual abuse prevention programs.

articles.title: Evaluation of spirituality among primary caregivers in a perinatal palliative care program in Mexico.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perinatal palliative care seeks to maximize quality of life through physical, social, psychological, and spiritual care, supporting families from diagnosis through bereavement. Spirituality (the search for meaning and connection, and religiousness, a system of beliefs and rituals linked to the divine) shape the experience of illness and death, yet are often sidelined in medical care. Evaluating spirituality is essential but complex, as it requires translating an abstract concept into a socio-clinical measure and is limited by health professionals' lack of training. Tools such as FICA (Faith, Importance, Community, and Address in care) can facilitate this process.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the spiritual dimensions and needs of caregivers of newborns in palliative care, using the FICA tool as an evaluation guide.
METHODOLOGY: Semi-structured interviews with primary caregivers, guided by the FICA dimensions, were recorded and transcribed for thematic narrative analysis. Participants provided informed consent.
RESULTS: Caregivers of nine newborns were invited; seven caregivers of five newborns accepted. Ages ranged from 18 to 53 years; most belonged to extended nuclear families, lived in urban areas, and were traditionally Catholic. Most recognized their spiritual beliefs and needs and the importance of spirituality in their lives; six of seven belonged to informal spiritual communities. The affective dimension predominated, and anguish and abandonment emerged as spiritual symptoms.
CONCLUSION: FICA helps identify caregivers' spiritual dimensions, their community support, and how prayer, ritual, and family support provide comfort. Routine spiritual evaluation could help detect spiritual suffering and guide better support strategies from health professionals in perinatal palliative care.

articles.title: Evaluating the evidence of health consequences of celiac disease: an umbrella review of meta-analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Celiac disease (CeD) extends beyond the gastrointestinal tract and may affect multiple organ systems. However, the credibility of reported extra-intestinal associations remains uncertain.
METHODS: We searched PubMed and Scopus until August 2024 for systematic reviews and meta-analyses of observational studies evaluating associations between CeD and any health-related outcome. Each meta-analytic association was appraised using established credibility criteria.
RESULTS: Thirteen publications met eligibility, reporting 26 meta-analytic associations, 17 of which were nominally statistically significant (P < 0.05). One association achieved strong evidence: CeD and higher risk of thyroid disease evaluated across all ages (odds ratio [OR] = 3.09, 95% CI: 2.33-4.09, nstudies = 12, I2 = 40%). Three associations reached highly suggestive evidence: CeD and higher risk of pneumococcal infection at all ages (OR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.43-1.92, nstudies = 3, I2 = 0%) and among children/adolescents, lower bone mineral content (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.65, 95% Cl: -0.83 to -0.48, nstudies = 15, I2 = 67%), and lower areal bone mineral density (SMD = -0.80, 95% Cl: -1.03 to -0.56, nstudies=15, I2 = 72%). Most meta-analyses were based on case-control or cross-sectional studies, while all studies contributing to pneumococcal infection had a cohort design. Suggestive evidence supported five associations, namely CeD and higher risk of any fracture and psoriasis (all ages), insomnia (children, adults), and lower height and body weight (children/adolescents). Eight associations showed weak evidence, and the remaining were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Four meta-analytic associations between CeD and higher risk of thyroid disease, pneumococcal infection, and lower bone mass and density reached high credibility, highlighting the potential systemic nature of CeD. Prospective studies are needed to strengthen this evidence. This synthesis may inform the future research agenda in this understudied field and prevention strategies aimed at mitigating CeD-related morbidity.

articles.title: Cigarette smoking in Canadian adolescents: A cross-sectional examination of psychosocial determinants.
articles.abstract: Tobacco cigarette smoking is often initiated during adolescence. Although rates of cigarette smoking have declined in the past decades, some Canadian adolescents still engage in this behaviour despite its widely known health risks. It is important to understand the predictors of cigarette smoking in a contemporary context. Psychosocial factors associated with cigarette smoking behaviours among Canadian adolescents are examined. # Methods This study used a population-based dataset of 23,732 Canadian adolescents in grades 6-10 who completed the 2022 cycle of the Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) Survey. Bivariate analysis and sequential multiple logistic regression models were utilized to assess adolescents' odds of having ever smoked cigarettes in relation to a range of psychosocial predictor variables. # Results Among the participants, 7.5% reported having ever smoked cigarettes. The fully specified models showed significant associations between cigarette smoking and other substance use (vaping: Odds Ratio=26.3, alcohol: Odds Ratio = 4.7) and higher friend support (Odds Ratio = 1.1), indicating that these were predictors of cigarette smoking, when holding other factors constant. Higher relative family affluence (Odds Ratio = 0.6), having higher family support (Odds Ratio=0.9), and higher teacher support (Odds Ratio = 0.8) were significantly associated with reduced odds of cigarette smoking. # Conclusion Other substance use was a significant predictor for increased odds of smoking. Some factors that were associated with reduced odds were identified, including family and teacher support. These findings can inform future research that seeks to examine the mechanisms underlying these associations.

articles.title: Ritlecitinib for Alopecia Areata in Patients Under 18 Years of Age: A Single-Center Retrospective Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Alopecia areata (AA) in pediatric and adolescent patients can be severe and difficult to manage, and real-world data on targeted therapies in this population remain limited. Ritlecitinib, a selective JAK3/TEC inhibitor, has demonstrated efficacy in adults with AA, but evidence in patients under 18 years of age is scarce. The purpose of this study is to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of ritlecitinib in pediatric and adolescent patients with alopecia areata.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective real-world study included patients aged <18 years with AA treated with ritlecitinib 50 mg once daily. Treatment response was assessed using changes in Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) scores and achievement of SALT50/75/90 at the last on-treatment observation. Safety outcomes were evaluated based on clinical records.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients were included, with a median age of 9.3 years (IQR, 6.0-14.6), including patients younger than 12 years who received off-label treatment. The median baseline SALT score was 50. The median SALT score decreased to 0 at the last observation (p < 0.001). SALT50, SALT75, and SALT90 were achieved by 96.3%, 77.8%, and 55.6% of patients, respectively, and 51.9% achieved complete scalp regrowth. Treatment responses were observed in both patchy AA and AT/AU subgroups; however, interpretation of subgroup differences is limited by the small sample sizes. No serious adverse events or treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were documented in the available medical records.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, ritlecitinib treatment was associated with substantial improvement in SALT scores and no documented serious adverse events during the observation period. These preliminary findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies, particularly in children younger than 12 years receiving off-label treatment.

articles.title: Improving Rates of Screening for Health-related Social Needs in a Pediatric Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In September 2024, our hospital implemented health-related social needs (HRSN) screening in the pediatric emergency department (PED). We aimed to increase rates of completed HRSN screens from a baseline of 18% in October 2024 to greater than 50% by December 2025.
METHODS: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, we implemented a new workflow that shifted from verbal to paper screening, posted screening posters in the PED, and provided stakeholders with education and weekly updates on screening rates. The primary outcome measure was the percentage of eligible patient encounters with a completed HRSN screen. The secondary outcome measure was the percentage of patients with a completed HRSN screen who requested to be connected with resources. We created statistical process control charts and performed chi-square tests or Fisher's exact tests to assess the associations between demographics and HRSN screen completion status.
RESULTS: The mean screening rate increased from 18% to 40% during the course of 14 months. The mean rate of patients/caregivers requesting connection to resources on HRSN screens increased from 16% to 29%. Patients aged younger than 18 years, Black non-Hispanic patients, Hispanic patients, patients with public insurance, and patients who preferred the Haitian Creole language were less likely to have a completed HRSN screen.
CONCLUSIONS: Through our quality improvement initiative, we improved HRSN screening rates in our PED. We observed an increase in the rate of patients/caregivers requesting connections to resources. We could increase these rates in future studies through targeted interventions to engage patient groups that were less likely to complete screening and by improving stakeholder buy-in.

articles.title: Increasing Resident Involvement in Medical Resuscitations in the Pediatric Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Primary care and general emergency providers must recognize critically ill children and initiate life-sustaining interventions, yet trainees report limited experience and low confidence in this domain. The pediatric emergency department (PED) offers an optimal setting to improve resident exposure to pediatric medical resuscitations (MRs). We aimed to increase resident involvement in PED MRs from 45% to 70% during a 6-month period and evaluate the effect on resident confidence in managing critically ill children.
METHODS: We implemented a disruptive alarm-based alert system and assigned 1 resident per shift to a defined MR-response role. The process measure was alert-system use per 25 MRs; the outcome measure was the percentage of MRs with resident involvement, defined by resident completion of the encounter note per 25 MRs. We assessed change over time using standard rules for special-cause variation. Residents voluntarily completed pre- and postintervention surveys.
RESULTS: Resident involvement in MRs in the PED increased from 45% to 64%. Use of the disruptive alarm increased from 0% to 33%. Residents initially indicated increased confidence in responding to MRs, but this confidence waned over time.
CONCLUSIONS: A standardized disruptive alert system paired with designated MR roles increased resident involvement in MRs in the PED and may influence resident confidence in managing critically ill children.

articles.title: Perinatal outcomes of minimally invasive fetal procedures for the treatment of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sacrococcygeal teratomas are the most common fetal teratoma. When ultrasonographic parameters deteriorate at early gestational ages at which preterm delivery is not feasible, intrauterine treatment methods have been indicated. This study aimed to assess the perinatal outcomes of minimally invasive fetal procedures for the treatment of sacrococcygeal teratoma.
METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251238039). We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL for studies published from January 2000 through November 2025, with four or more participants reporting minimally invasive intrauterine interventions for sacrococcygeal teratoma. The primary outcome was fetal death; secondary outcomes included perinatal mortality and preterm birth. Risk of bias was assessed using Downs and Black.
RESULTS: Five studies met inclusion criteria (three retrospective cohorts and two case series; n=4-22 participants) across six countries. Procedures included radiofrequency ablation, percutaneous and fetoscopic laser ablation, cyst aspiration, and shunting. Fetal hydrops and cardiac compromise were the main indications for intervention. Among studies with a comparator group, survival ranged from 40.0-75.0 % in intervention groups vs. 12.5-100 % in expectant management. Neonatal mortality reached 50.0 % in two studies, and preterm birth before 32 weeks occurred in 25.0-100 % of intervention cases across the five studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive fetal procedures are a feasible option for fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma complicated by hydrops or cardiac compromise, but the available evidence is limited to small retrospective studies subject to severity-based selection bias and does not allow conclusions regarding their effect on survival. Preterm birth was frequent after intervention.

articles.title: Common household foods fail to mitigate button battery esophageal injury in infants: an ex vivo dynamic model study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Button battery (BB) ingestion is a life-threatening pediatric emergency, particularly in infants at high risk of severe esophageal injury. This study evaluated whether readily available household food could mitigate BB-induced esophageal injury in infants.
METHODS: A dynamic ex vivo porcine esophageal model simulating peristalsis, salivary flow, and body temperature was used. After insertion of a CR2032 lithium BB, 5 mL of agave syrup, soy drink, orange juice, ketchup, or honey was administered at 5, 15, and 25 min, then every 30 min for 2, 4, or 6 hours. Outcomes included macroscopic ulcer grade, histologic injury depth, esophageal pH, and residual battery voltage.
RESULTS: In this dynamic model, agave syrup, soy drink, and orange juice did not reduce ulcer severity or histologic injury compared with untreated controls (p>0.05). Ketchup markedly worsened injury, increasing ulcer grades and voltage loss at all time points (p<0.05). Protective effects suggested in static models for agave syrup and soy drink were not reproduced under dynamic conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: Common household foods do not protect against BB-induced esophageal injury in a ex vivo experimental model. Dynamic testing is essential before recommending food-based prehospital therapies.

articles.title: Very Early-Onset Schizophrenia in a 9-Year-Old With X-Linked Ichthyosis: Case Report.
articles.abstract: Very early-onset schizophrenia (VEOS) is a rare childhood psychiatric disorder with a poor prognosis that is characterized by varying degrees of positive and negative symptoms. The disorder is challenging to diagnose at a young age due to overlap with other developmental and behavioral disorders. Treatment and management are complicated by the rarity of VEOS and the poor prognosis seen in prior patients. This case follows BB, a 9-year-old boy who has VEOS with a multifactorial etiology from biological, psychological, and social influences. BB's case demonstrates the complexities of evaluation along the developmental trajectory as symptom presentation and environmental influences evolve over time. A unique point of interest is the co-occurrence of X-linked Ichthyosis, which has been documented in a prior case report of childhood schizophrenia and severe attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This piece contributes to the limited literature on VEOS, especially in the setting of other developmental issues such as comorbid medical illness and attachment disorders.

articles.title: Heritability estimation of subcortical volumes in a multi-ancestry multi-site cohort study.
articles.abstract: Heritability of regional subcortical brain volumes (rSBVs) quantifies the contribution of genetic variation to individual differences in subcortical brain morphology during neurodevelopment. rSBVs are highly heritable in adults but are not well characterized in adolescents. The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study (ABCD), collected across 21 US sites, provides data to characterize the heritability of subcortical structures in adolescence. However, in a multi-site multi-ancestry study, such as ABCD, site-specific effects may co-occur with genetic effects, which can bias heritability estimates. Existing methods that adjust for site effects require additional steps and can lead to inconsistent estimates. We propose a random-effect model-based MOM approach to estimate heritability that is a single-step asymptotically consistent estimator even when ancestries are differentially distributed across sites. Our approach performed well under a wide range of simulations. The proposed approach yielded heritability estimates similar to previous results derived from single-site studies and studies on different age groups, with the cerebellar cortex and hippocampus showing the highest estimated heritability (>50%).

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Thrombosis in a Growth Faltering Infant With Acinetobacter Sepsis-A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary artery thrombosis is a rare finding in infant patients. Contributors to infant hypercoagulability include inherited thrombophilias, immature anticoagulation systems, and systemic insults such as septic shock and liver disease.
CASE PRESENTATION: We present the case of a 7-week-old girl with perinatal HIV exposure diagnosed with a pulmonary artery thrombus. The patient was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) for sepsis due to Acinetobacter nosocomialis bacteremia. During a workup for growth faltering and an S3 gallop, echocardiogram revealed a mass in the main pulmonary artery. Days later, after failing to achieve therapeutic anticoagulation, infant developed hypoxia and echocardiogram demonstrated worsening luminal obstruction by the thrombus, prompting urgent treatment with thrombectomy. We hypothesize that septic shock, with associated coagulopathy and severe dehydration, predisposed to thrombus formation in this critically ill patient.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the rapid, multidisciplinary approach to diagnosing a pulmonary artery thrombus and the underlying factors contributing to hypercoagulability in an infant. This case is novel for the patient's risk factor of perinatal HIV exposure, which may have predisposed her to opportunistic infection as well as thrombosis. Hypoxia and hemodynamic instability presented later in her course, prompting invasive management. Early recognition and timely intervention are essential for optimizing patient outcomes.

articles.title: Achalasia Cardia Unmasking 4A Syndrome in an Adolescent.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achalasia cardia is an esophageal motility disorder characterized by impaired relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) and absent peristalsis, leading to progressive dysphagia and weight loss. Often isolated, achalasia can occur as part of rare syndromes such as 4A Syndrome, which includes achalasia, Addison's disease (adrenocorticotropic hormone [ACTH]-resistant adrenal insufficiency), alacrima, and autonomic dysfunction.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 15-year-old male presented with 1.5 years of progressive dysphagia, initially affecting liquids and later solids, along with retrosternal chest pain, regurgitation, and 6 kg weight loss. He had a history of recurrent dry eyes since birth and symptoms of fatigue, dizziness, and skin darkening over the past 2 years. Examination revealed diffuse hyperpigmentation, dry eyes, hyperemic conjunctivae, and bilateral weakness of ankle dorsiflexion with diminished ankle jerk. His BMI was 17.53 kg/m2, indicating undernutrition.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) raised clinical suspicion of achalasia cardia, demonstrating a dilated esophagus and a tight gastroesophageal junction; high-resolution manometry (HRM) confirmed the diagnosis. Corticosteroid and ACTH tests indicated ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease). Schirmer's test confirmed alacrima. Genetic testing revealed mutations in the AAAS gene, confirming 4A Syndrome. Nerve conduction studies showed motor axonal neuropathy.
TREATMENT AND OUTCOME: Pneumatic dilation with 30 and 35 mm balloons resulted in a reduction of the Eckardt score from 7 to 2. Hydrocortisone therapy (10 mg morning, 5 mg evening) improved skin manifestations and weakness. The patient gained 3 kg in weight over 6 months, indicating clinical improvement.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the rare co-occurrence of achalasia cardia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, alacrimia, and peripheral neuropathy in 4A Syndrome. Early diagnosis and a multidisciplinary treatment approach led to significant improvement, making this the first reported case of 4A Syndrome in India.

articles.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic, 2018-2019.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women.
METHODS: Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18-76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR detection.
RESULTS: Overall, 114 of 1268 women with evaluable samples (9.0%) had abnormal cytology and three (0.2%) had cervical cancer. AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit detected 256 positives among 1184 participants (21.6%), with types 52, 58 and 16 being the most prevalent HR genotypes (20.4%, 12.8% and 11.7%, respectively). Multivariable analysis showed that participants aged ≥ 40 years (OR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.1-2.4, p = 0.015) and those living in Luangprabang province (OR: 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1-3.2, p = 0.02) had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology compared to younger women and those residing in Huaphan. Single/divorced/widow women had a higher probability of HPV detection compared to married women (OR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.5-3.7, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: HPV 52, 58 and 16 were the most prevalent high-risk genotypes, clearly advocating for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. Periodic screening of women too old to benefit from the recently introduced vaccine should be considered.

articles.title: Prevalence and factors associated with post-tuberculosis lung disease among children and adolescents in Kenya: A multi-centre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most patients survive tuberculosis (TB) with treatment. However, emerging evidence reveals occurrence of a post-TB sequelae termed post TB lung disease (PTLD) that affects survivor's long term lung health. Evidence on PTLD in children and adolescents is limited. We evaluated the prevalence and factors associated with PTLD in children and adolescents completing treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi, Kenya.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study done on participants<20 years at the end of treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi. After obtaining informed consent and assent, we interviewed and examined participants, reviewed their medical records, and conducted a six-minute walk test (6MWT) for children >5 years. Post-TB sequelae was defined as persistent respiratory symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs after TB treatment. Descriptive statistics were computed for prevalence of post-TB symptoms and signs, and logistic regression analysis performed to evaluate factors associated with post-TB sequelae.
RESULTS: We enrolled 107 participants, of median age 6.3 years; 59% were female and 12% had Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. Persistent respiratory symptoms were present in 29%; commonest being cough (21.5%). Abnormal respiratory signs were present in 51%; commonest being tachypnea (27%). Of 56 participants who did the 6MWT, 58% walked <70% of their expected distance. Overall, 57.0% (95% CI 47.1-66.5) had at least one while 33.6% (95% CI 23.8-41.6%) had two or more persistent symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs. Hospitalization at diagnosis (aOR 10.26 (1.76-59.79) and older age (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26) were independent predictors of PTLD.
CONCLUSION: A significant number of children and adolescents have persisting respiratory disease post-TB and it is more common among older children, and those with severe disease at TB diagnosis. There is need to institute routine assessment of children and adolescents at the end of TB treatment to identify those with sequelae, and provide post-TB care.

articles.title: High blood pressure among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus in Uganda: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coexistence of diabetes mellitus (DM) and hypertension (HTN) worsens the clinical outcomes of children with diabetes concerning both microvascular and macrovascular disease. It increases mortality risk by 5 times, with a higher risk of death in developing countries. Therefore, comprehensive care for patients with diabetes, including hypertension screening, must be provided.
METHODS: This multicenter health facility-based cross-sectional study included 150 children and adolescents aged from 6 months to 18 years with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) who were treated at Jinja Regional Referral Hospital (JRRH), Mbale Regional Referral Hospital (MRRH) and Lira Regional Referral Hospital (LRRH). Interviewer-administered questionnaires were used to obtain data, which were then analyzed according to the study objectives using STATA® version 18. High blood pressure diagnosis was based on blood pressure (BP) above or equal to the 90th percentile for <13 years and either systolic BP ≥ 120 mmHg or Diastolic BP ≥ 80mmhg for 13 years and older for age, sex and height. The prevalence of high BP was determined as a percentage, whereas associated factors were analyzed at both bivariate and multivariable logistic regression. The significance of associations was set at a p-value <0.05 and a 95% confidence interval.
RESULTS: Of the 150 participants, 115 (76.7%) were above 12 years of age, and the median age was 15 years (IQR 13-17). There were more females [81/150 (54%)] than males. The majority were attending school [130/150 (86.7%)], with a few attending boarding school [26/130 (20%)]. Sixty-one participants (40.7%, 95% C.I 33%-49%) had high BP, and 53 (86.9%) of these patients had poor glycemic control. The factors associated with high BP among T1DM participants included having diabetes for 4-8 years (aOR= 2.23 [95% CI: 1.05-4.75]; p = 0.037), and 9-12 years (aOR= 4.545 [95% CI: 1.075-19.221]; p = 0.040) respectively compared to those less than 4 years. Additionally, having Poor glycemic control (HBA1C ≥ 7%) increased odds for high BP by 2.905 [95% CI: 1.149-7.342]; p = 0.024) times compared to their counterparts with good glycemic control.
CONCLUSION: There was a high prevalence of high blood pressure among children with type 1 diabetes. Factors associated with high blood pressure included disease duration of more than 4 years and poor glycemic control.

articles.title: Co-developing a women-centered HIV prevention intervention to reduce stigma, increase HIV self-testing, and improve pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake in Ghana (WISE WOMAN): A study protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young women in Ghana (18-35 years) remain disproportionately affected by HIV due to intersecting structural and social challenges, including stigma, gendered power dynamics, and limited access to women-centered prevention services. Although HIV self-testing (HIVST) and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) are effective biomedical prevention strategies, uptake among young Ghanaian women remains low. Barriers include limited awareness, persistent stigma, and a lack of culturally relevant, youth-responsive prevention approaches. The WISE WOMAN study aims to address these gaps by developing and piloting a women-centered HIV prevention intervention co-created with young women in Ghana.
METHODS: This protocol describes a pilot implementation study of a women-centered HIV prevention intervention that will be delivered via WhatsApp. The intervention is informed by community-based participatory research and human-centered design approaches to enhance cultural relevance and responsiveness to young women's lived experiences. The study will enroll 50 young women aged 18-35 years who will participate in a four-week WhatsApp-based intervention designed to increase HIV prevention knowledge, reduce stigma, and support engagement with HIVST and PrEP. Implementation outcomes, including feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness, will be assessed using mixed methods. Quantitative data will be collected through baseline and post-intervention surveys, including the PIERS-22 engagement scale, and will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired comparisons. Qualitative data from group interactions and post-intervention interviews will be analyzed using thematic analysis. The study has received ethical approval from the University at Buffalo Institutional Review Board (STUDY00009328) and the Ensign Global College Ethics Committee (IRB/EL/AF-02/2025) and is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07003789).
DISCUSSION: This protocol outlines the design and methods for a digitally delivered, women-centered HIV prevention intervention grounded in participatory approaches. The planned pilot study will generate critical implementation evidence on the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of a WhatsApp-based, co-designed intervention, informing future adaptation, scale-up, and integration of culturally grounded HIV prevention strategies for young women in Ghana and similar settings.

articles.title: Visuo-spatial perception deficit in ophthalmological disorders: Visual field extent matters.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Persons with Visual Impairment (VI) are more at risk to be without academic qualification. This is classically attributed to limited access to visual information, considered difficult due to reduced visual acuity. However, in some cases, visual acuity is preserved but visual field is reduced. Given the importance of visuo-spatial skills in learning, we assessed the accuracy of perceptual visuo-spatial judgements relative to visual field extent and visual acuity to question their respective contribution to the functional repercussions in VI.
METHODS: 97 patients were administered the elementary visuo-spatial perception (EVSP) test during their clinical assessment. We put a focus on two diseases of our sample: Retinitis Pigmentosa (N = 19) and Albinism (N = 18), with mainly restriction of visual field extent in the former, and visual acuity loss in the latter. In addition, we investigated the correlation between the visuo-spatial performance and these two distinctive factors of VI in the whole sample.
RESULTS: The results indicated higher prevalence of visuo-spatial perception deficit in the whole sample of VI compared to typically developing individuals. Even if most pathologies affect both peripheral and central vision, which makes it complicated to fully disentangle between these two factors, the focus on the Retinitis Pigmentosa and the Albinism groups suggested that visuo-spatial perception is less impacted by a low visual acuity than by peripheral visual field restriction. Additionally, we found that visuospatial perception performance was significantly correlated with visual field extent and not with visual acuity in the whole sample.
CONCLUSIONS: Visual field extent matters for visuo-spatial processing and probably for academic achievement. Further investigations are needed to understand how impaired visuo-spatial perceptual skills may explain academic difficulties in VI.

articles.title: Responsiveness of the CPCHILD Questionnaire to Monitor Changes in HRQoL for Nonambulatory Children With Cerebral Palsy After Hip and Spine Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caregiver Priorities and Child Health Index of Life with Disabilities (CPCHILD) is a health-related quality-of-life questionnaire designed for children with cerebral palsy (CP). It is valid, reliable, and universally adopted; however, studies evaluating its longitudinal validity are lacking. The aim of this study was to evaluate the CPCHILD's responsiveness to change after orthopaedic hip and spine surgery in nonambulatory children with CP.
METHODS: This longitudinal observational responsiveness study used distribution-based methods to evaluate the CPCHILD questionnaire. Caregivers of nonambulatory children with CP completed the questionnaire before and 6-, 12-, 24 months after hip and spine surgery. Responsiveness was quantified using effect size (ES) and standardized response mean with 95% confidence intervals (CI), and measurement precision was assessed using standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change at the 90% confidence level (MDC90).
RESULTS: One hundred forty-one children (mean age 11 years) with CP underwent surgery (95 hip reconstruction surgery/46 spinal fusion surgery). Six months after hip reconstruction, the Personal, Positioning, and Health domains, as well as the Total score demonstrated small or moderate responsiveness (ES, range 0.25-0.57), with up to half of patients exceeding the MDC90 threshold for measurement error. After spinal fusion surgery, the Total score and all domains showed small or moderate responsiveness (ES, range 0.22-0.77), with a larger proportion of patients exceeding the MDC90 compared with hip reconstruction.
CONCLUSIONS: CPCHILD captured meaningful responsiveness in the Personal and Positioning domains, as well as the Total score following hip and spine surgery, while other domains (Comfort and QoL) showed minimal or no detectable change. This suggests that CPCHILD can capture improvements in functional domains, while changes for Comfort and QoL were smaller than expected, and other domains (Communication and Health) not expected to be influenced with surgery, remained stable. Healthcare providers using the CPCHILD to evaluate the effect of surgical procedures on health-related quality of life should be aware of these findings.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

articles.title: A Rare Case of Fulminant Guillain-Barre Syndrome as the Cardinal Presenting Feature of New Onset Pediatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Here we present a complex case of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presenting initially as fulminant Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS). This particular manifestation of neuropsychiatric lupus is uncommon but can be severe and even life threatening.
