Increasing providers' awareness of the overlap between lupus and GBS will improve diagnostic accuracy and timing as well as expedite appropriate therapies, which may differ from typical GBS treatment.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 12-year-old previously healthy Hispanic female presented with subacute onset vision changes and imbalance with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and hyporeflexia. Given her classic clinical triad and suspicion for GBS variant Miller Fischer syndrome (MFS), neuroaxis imaging was obtained. MRI showed cranial nerve and ventral nerve root enhancement, and cytoalbuminologic dissociation seen on cerebrospinal fluid analysis also supported this diagnosis. Weakness including the facial and bulbar muscles and the extremities progressed rapidly and threatened respiratory functions, so the patient was intubated. Typical treatments for GBS including intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and plasma exchange (PLEX) were insufficient to manage symptoms, and additional evaluations supported a diagnosis of SLE with nephritis. Coordinated care between neuroimmunology and rheumatology enabled rapid escalation of therapy to include high-dose intravenous steroid pulses, cyclophosphamide, and rituximab. Together, these therapies eventually stabilized the patient, and with support from neuropsychology, psychiatry, and rehabilitation medicine, she was able to discharge from the hospital after 115 days of admission. She has remained in remission on maintenance immunosuppression including mycophenolate mofetil as well as hydroxychloroquine.
CONCLUSIONS: Neuropsychiatric lupus can be difficult to diagnose and manage, but its severity necessitates vigilance and aggressive management. In the current case, the isolated neurological symptoms at presentation consistent with GBS could have delayed diagnosis, but neuroimmunology and rheumatology were consulted early, and appropriate diagnostic testing was performed. The patient's multidisciplinary team worked closely together to appropriately escalate her treatment beyond what is typical for GBS, ultimately leading to remission of her neuropsychiatric symptoms and recovery of her baseline neurological status. This case highlights the complex nature of neuropsychiatric lupus, suggests that SLE should be on the differential in atypical or difficult-to-treat cases of GBS, and underscores the need for coordinated interdisciplinary care to achieve best outcomes for these patients.

articles.title: Gut microbiome and fecal metabolome dysregulation in pediatric atopic eczema: a multi-omics correlation study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic eczema (AE) is a highly prevalent inflammatory skin disorder in children, with growing evidence underscoring the role of gut microbiota dysbiosis in its pathogenesis. However, the specific mechanisms by which gut microbes and their metabolic products contribute to AE development remain poorly understood.
METHODS: This study employed an integrated multi-omics approach to investigate the gut ecosystem in pediatric AE. Fecal samples from affected children and matched controls were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing to profile the gut microbiota and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based metabolomics to characterize the fecal metabolome.
RESULTS: Significant gut microbial dysbiosis was observed in children with AE, marked by reduced species diversity and altered community structure. Specifically, the relative abundances of key genera such as Streptococcus, Enterococcus, and Bifidobacterium were significantly diminished. Correlation network analysis revealed the metabolite Fruleuile as a central hub in the microbe-metabolite interaction network, demonstrating significant associations with several bacterial genera, including Mycobacterium. Our findings confirm significant gut microbiota dysbiosis in pediatric AE and identify distinct microbial and metabolic signatures associated with the condition. The metabolite Fruleuile emerges as a potential key mediator in the gut-skin axis, highlighting the importance of host-microbiota metabolic interactions in the pathophysiology of AE patients.

articles.title: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia: a descriptive single-centre case series from a resource-limited setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia (JMML) is a rare myeloproliferative neoplasm of early childhood driven by RAS-MAPK pathway activation, for which allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is the only established cure. Data from low- and middle-income countries, where donor access, drug availability and monitoring capacity differ from the settings that generate most published evidence, are scarce.
METHODS: We reviewed all consecutive children with JMML who underwent allogeneic HSCT at a single tertiary centre in northern India between January 2019 and August 2025. Engraftment, graft failure, poor graft function and transplant complications were classified by pre-specified consensus criteria. The analysis is descriptive: proportions are reported with exact 95% confidence intervals (CI) and survival as Kaplan-Meier estimates, without hypothesis testing.
RESULTS: Eight children (seven boys; median age 19.5 months) received myeloablative fludarabine-busulfan-melphalan conditioning and fresh peripheral blood stem cells from four HLA-matched siblings and four haploidentical parents. Initial neutrophil engraftment occurred in six (75%; 95% CI 34.9-96.8) at a median of 17.5 days, and sustained engraftment in five (62.5%; 95% CI 24.5-91.5). Primary graft failure, secondary graft failure and poor graft function occurred in one patient each, all haploidentical recipients; all four matched-sibling recipients engrafted durably. Cytokine release syndrome (grade 1-2) occurred in three haploidentical recipients and skin-limited grade I-II acute graft-versus-host disease in two patients. Three children died without relapse: two after graft failure (days +28 and +41) and one of a COVID-19/MIS-C-like illness 28 months after transplantation. No relapse occurred. At a median follow-up of 35 months among survivors, five of eight children were alive (62.5%; 95% CI 24.5-91.5); Kaplan-Meier overall and event-free survival at 36 months were 60% (95% CI 19.5-85.2) and 46.9% (95% CI 12.0-76.3), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Allogeneic HSCT for JMML, including haploidentical transplantation with post-transplant cyclophosphamide, was feasible in a resource-limited setting, and no patient relapsed. However, graft failure or poor graft function affected three of four haploidentical recipients, and this cohort is far too small to support any comparison between donor types. Donor-specific antibodies, HLA disparity, splenic disease burden, conditioning exposure and graft composition warrant systematic attention in alternative-donor transplantation for JMML in similar settings.

articles.title: Regional variation in adolescent births and associations with adverse perinatal outcomes in Georgia: A birth registry-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Georgia, approximately 2,700 (5.8%) adolescents give birth every year. Adolescent births are a public health concern due to an increased risk of various adverse maternal and newborn outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the regional variation of adolescent births and also the associations between maternal age and preterm birth (PB), neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and perinatal death (PD) in Georgia.
METHODS: The study population included all childbirths in women aged <30 years between 2017 and 2022, comprising 173,238 women and their 175,213 newborns. We used three age groups: adolescents aged <18, and 18-19 years, and adults aged 20-29 years (reference group). Logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the associations between maternal age and PB, NICU admission, and PD. Population attributable fractions and absolute numbers of the selected adverse outcomes attributable to adolescent births were estimated.
RESULTS: The adolescent birth rate (ABR) was 22.2 per 1000 adolescents in Georgia in 2022. Most of the adolescents aged <20 years lived in the regions of Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti with an ABR of 70.3 per 1000, 35.3 per 1000, and 26.4 per 1000, respectively. Newborns born to adolescents aged <18 (PB adjusted odds ratio [aOR]= 1.25, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.11-1.41; NICU aOR= 1.19, 95% CI: 1.06-1.33; PD aOR= 1.33, 95% CI: 0.99-1.80) and 18-19 years (PB aOR= 1.04, 95% CI: 0.98-1.11; NICU aOR= 1.08, 95% CI: 1.01-1.16; PD aOR= 1.17, 95% CI: 0.98-1.40) had higher odds for almost all the selected perinatal outcomes than newborns born to the reference group of 20-29-year-old women. If adolescents <20 years had postponed childbirth until they were between 20 and 29 years old, approximately 14 cases of singleton preterm birth (1%), 16 NICU admissions (1%), and 4 perinatal deaths (2%) occurring between 2017 and 2022 could have been prevented.
CONCLUSION: Our findings revealed large geographical differences in adolescent births across Georgia, with the highest rates in Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti. Adolescent childbirth, particularly among those <18 years, was linked to higher risks of PB, NICU admission, and PD compared to adults aged 20-29 years. Targeted interventions, such as improved access to reproductive health education and family planning, are needed, especially in high-burden regions.

articles.title: Untargeted plasma metabolomics reveals metabolite alterations and pathway perturbations in gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is defined as glucose intolerance first detected during pregnancy and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Metabolomics provides a system-level approach to characterize metabolic alterations associated with gestational insulin resistance. This study aimed to identify plasma metabolite differences between women with GDM and normal glucose tolerance (NGT) and to evaluate the discriminatory performance of a metabolite-based panel.
METHODS: Plasma samples from 270 pregnant women (169 GDM and 101 NGT) were analyzed using an untargeted 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR)-based metabolomics approach. Differential metabolites were identified using univariate, followed by multivariate modeling and regression adjustment for maternal age and pre-pregnancy body mass index. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using Random Forest (RF), Partial Least Squares-Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA), and Linear Support Vector Machine (Linear-SVM) models with Receiver Operating Characteristic curve analysis. Pathway enrichment analyses were performed using KEGG and SMPDB, and disease-based enrichment was assessed using HMDB.
RESULTS: Among 31 identified metabolites, 14 differed significantly between GDM and NGT. Integration of univariate and multivariate analyses prioritized nine metabolites-acetone, citrate, glucose, succinate, glycine, 3-hydroxybutyrate, leucine, phenylalanine, and the CH = CH bond of unsaturated lipids-that remained independently associated with GDM after covariate adjustment. All nine metabolites were elevated in the GDM group. A nine-metabolite panel achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.70-0.81) using the RF model. Pathway enrichment identified valine, leucine, and isoleucine biosynthesis and ketone body metabolism as significantly enriched pathways. HMDB-based disease enrichment showed overlap with preeclampsia-related metabolic signatures.
CONCLUSION: Untargeted 1H NMR metabolomics, combined enrichment analyses, identified coordinated metabolic disturbances in GDM involving amino acid and ketone body metabolism. A nine-metabolite panel demonstrated moderate discriminative performance and provides mechanistic insight into GDM-associated metabolic adaptations, supporting their potential utility for future biomarker validation and translational studies.

articles.title: Clinical features, first aid practices, and hospital management of snakebites in Northern Uganda: A multi-facility cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Snakebite envenoming is a neglected tropical disease with a disproportionate burden in sub-Saharan Africa, where weak surveillance, limited antivenom availability, and reliance on traditional remedies compound morbidity and mortality. Evidence on how snakebite cases are clinically managed in routine practice in Uganda remains scarce. We conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study with retrospective abstraction of records from four purposively selected health facilities in Gulu and Arua Districts of Northern Uganda. Snakebite case records from outpatient, inpatient, paediatric, and intensive-care service points covering the period 2017-2021 were reviewed using a standardised abstraction tool. Descriptive statistics were computed in Stata version 14, with frequencies and proportions for categorical variables and medians with interquartile ranges (IQR) for continuous variables, both of which were right-skewed. All analyses were complete-case, and the denominator is reported wherever it differs from the full sample. We analysed 227 snakebite case records. Of these, 58.6% were female and the median age was 21 years (IQR 13-38); students or pupils accounted for 26.6% of the 192 records in which occupation was described. Most bites involved the lower limb (85.9%) and occurred in the second and third quarters of the year (59.9%). Snake species was undocumented in 76.2% of records. No pre-hospital first aid was recorded in 59.1% of cases; where first aid was documented it was usually harmful, most often a tourniquet (29.3%) or a herbal remedy (8.9%). The dominant clinical manifestations were pain (60.8%), swelling or blisters at the bite site (68.7%), and fang marks (26.9%). One or more features suggestive of systemic envenoming were documented in 18.5% of cases, of whom 33.3% received antivenom. Overall, only 15.0% of cases received antivenom, while supportive care predominated (intravenous fluids 68.1%, analgesics 64.2%, antibiotics 53.1%). Coagulation testing was rare (20-minute whole blood clotting test 17.3%; INR 12.0%). Overall, 93.4% of patients recovered, 3.1% died, 0.9% were referred to other healthcare facilities, and the rest (2.6%) had missing information on the outcomes. Snakebite management in Northern Uganda is largely symptomatic, with critical gaps in species identification, syndromic assessment, coagulation testing, antivenom utilisation, and pre-hospital first aid practices. Strengthening health-worker training, improving documentation and surveillance, and community education on appropriate first aid are urgently needed to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Sensorimotor representation in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis compared with healthy controls: Proprioception, tactile acuity, left-right judgment, and motor imagery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is increasingly recognized as involving central sensorimotor alterations beyond structural spinal deformity, yet multiple sensorimotor domains have not been assessed comprehensively within a single AIS sample. This study aimed to compare tactile acuity, proprioception, left/right judgment, and motor imagery between adolescents with AIS and healthy controls, and to explore the associations of these sensorimotor domains with postural, body image, and health-related quality-of-life outcomes.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional case-control study, 41 adolescents with AIS and 42 healthy controls were assessed for tactile acuity, proprioception, left/right judgment, motor imagery, and pressure pain threshold, alongside body image, perceived spinal appearance, and quality of life.
RESULTS: Adolescents with AIS showed elevated paraspinal two-point discrimination thresholds at right T10, right L4, and left L4 (all adjusted p ≤ 0.040), but not at left T10, greater spinal repositioning errors in all four tested directions (all adjusted p ≤ 0.005), and poorer external visual motor imagery (adjusted p = 0.023). No between-group differences were found for left/right judgment or pressure pain threshold (all adjusted p > 0.05). Proprioceptive measures showed the strongest discriminative ability (lumbar right lateral flexion and lumbar flexion repositioning errors: AUC = 0.802 and 0.794, both p < 0.001), and a three-variable exploratory model correctly classified 82.9% of participants in the original sample and 81.7% after leave-one-out cross-validation. Body image disturbance and perceived spinal appearance were also worse in the AIS group, as were SRS-22 function, self-image, and subtotal scores (all adjusted p ≤ 0.012).
CONCLUSION: Adolescents with AIS showed impairments in tactile acuity, proprioception, and external visual motor imagery relative to healthy controls. These cross-sectional findings suggest that sensorimotor alterations may be relevant when designing rehabilitation strategies for this population, but they should be interpreted cautiously and do not establish causality. Larger longitudinal and neuroimaging-based studies are needed to clarify these relationships.

articles.title: Developing a syndromic case definition for timely surveillance of severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) based on financial claim codes in the Netherlands.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To improve pandemic preparedness, a sustainable and timely surveillance system for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) is crucial. We developed and evaluated a proxy for syndromic SARI-surveillance using financial claim codes (DTC-codes).
METHODS: With data from 2016-2020 we compared DTC-codes with primary discharge diagnosis classified by ICD-10 codes (J0-J22, U07) as comparative benchmark for SARI, distinguishing between paediatric and adult populations, and pre- and during COVID-19-pandemic periods. To establish DTC-based proxies for SARI, accuracy metrics of individual and combinations of DTC-codes, and temporal trends were assessed. We retrospectively assessed its ability to detect COVID-19 epidemic patterns and its relationship with outcomes of existing respiratory surveillance systems.
RESULTS: For adults, DTC-codes for pneumonia and unspecified respiratory and viral infections served as proxy for SARI. In the paediatric population, codes for laryngitis subglottica, RSV bronchiolitis and respiratory tract infection were used. While trends in DTC-based SARI proxies correlate with trends in ICD-10-coded SARI, the accuracy relative to this benchmark was moderate. The adult DTC-based SARI proxy reflected peaks in COVID-19 hospitalisations during the pandemic and aligned with influenza and RSV laboratory detections in the pre-pandemic period. The paediatric DTC-based SARI proxy aligned with RSV laboratory detections.
CONCLUSION: We established DTC-based proxies for syndromic SARI-surveillance that appeared suitable to monitor SARI-trends. However, on the patient level the accuracy for ICD-10-coded SARI appeared moderate. Accuracy of the DTC-based SARI proxy and its ability to detect relevant epidemic signals, should be assessed prospectively with real-time data.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in Pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia: An Emerging Mechanistic Framework, Candidate Biomarkers and Their Limitations, and Translational Priorities.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) is among the most common causes of community-acquired pneumonia in children. Against a background of widespread macrolide-resistant M. pneumoniae (MRMP) in East Asia, severe (SMPP) and refractory (RMPP) MP pneumonia have become pressing clinical problems, and a subset of children develop long-term sequelae including bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchiectasis, and organizing pneumonia. The mechanisms driving MPP severity remain incompletely understood, and tools for the early identification of high-risk children are limited. Ferroptosis-an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by uncontrolled accumulation of lipid peroxides-contributes to several forms of infectious lung injury; extrapolating from this cross-pathogen evidence, we propose here that it may also participate in MP-related alveolar epithelial damage and inflammatory amplification, a hypothesis that has not previously been articulated specifically for pediatric MPP. In this narrative review of an emerging area, we summarize the molecular regulation of ferroptosis, appraise the current-and still limited-evidence linking it to pediatric MPP (explicitly separating direct MP data from cross-pathogen extrapolation), and critically evaluate the clinical applicability of ferroptosis-related biomarkers. Because direct evidence in pediatric MPP is sparse, the mechanistic model presented here is explicitly hypothesis-generating rather than a claim of established causation. We give particular attention to serum ferritin, whose pragmatic value for SMPP/RMPP risk stratification is well supported but is better understood as reflecting combined iron metabolism and systemic inflammation than as evidence of ferroptosis specifically; markedly elevated values should prompt evaluation for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis/macrophage activation syndrome. We argue that ferroptosis offers a biologically plausible, complementary framework to the cytokine-storm paradigm for understanding MPP severity, and we outline priority research directions for a field that remains in its infancy.

articles.title: X-Linked Agammaglobulinemia Diagnosed in Adolescence Complicated by Invasive Aspergillosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA) is a primary humoral immunodeficiency that is typically recognized in early childhood. We report a 16-year-old male with recurrent respiratory tract infections (RTIs) since childhood who presented with severe pulmonary infection and focal neurological deficits. Immunologic evaluation showed profound hypogammaglobulinemia, with serum IgG of 0.24 g/L and both IgA and IgM < 0.10 g/L, together with virtually absent peripheral CD19+ B cells (0.00%). Genetic testing identified a hemizygous Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) c.1039G > C (p.Ala347Pro) variant. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) detected the Aspergillus flavus/oryzae complex. Serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) galactomannan (GM) tests were positive, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed multiple ring-enhancing lesions. Taken together, these findings supported invasive pulmonary aspergillosis with possible central nervous system (CNS) Aspergillus involvement. This case illustrates the clinical heterogeneity of XLA, including delayed recognition until adolescence, and underscores the importance of integrating immunologic, microbiological, mycological, imaging, and longitudinal clinical evidence when interpreting multiple pathogen-detection results in complex infections.

articles.title: Multidimensional analysis of the pathological mechanisms of infantile hemangioma: metabolic reprogramming, immune remodeling, and programmed cell death.
articles.abstract: Infantile hemangioma (IH) is a common benign vascular tumor of infancy. Its self-limiting course, which progresses from proliferation to involution, involves aberrant angiogenesis, altered cell fate, and remodeling of the lesional microenvironment. Hypoxia/HIF-VEGF, PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, and Notch signaling pathways contribute to vascular formation and cellular differentiation. During the proliferative phase, hemangioma endothelial cells (HemECs) undergo metabolic reprogramming characterized by enhanced glycolysis and altered amino acid metabolism, including pathways involving glutamine, arginine, glycine, and serine. Macrophages, mast cells, T cells, and their associated cytokines also shape a proangiogenic immune microenvironment. During the involuting phase, the transition of hemangioma stem cells (HemSCs) toward an adipogenic fate, together with changes in lesional cell composition, contributes to fibrofatty tissue remodeling. At the same time, the immune microenvironment undergoes stage-dependent remodeling, and processes related to programmed cell death, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, and autophagy, change accordingly. However, the strength of evidence supporting these processes in IH varies. Current studies have identified specific links among metabolism, immunity, and cell death, but they have not established a fixed, sequential causal cascade; PANoptosis remains an unverified mechanistic hypothesis in IH. Although propranolol is the first-line treatment, variable treatment responses, rebound growth after treatment withdrawal, and refractory lesions remain clinical challenges. Focusing on the transition from proliferation to involution, this review integrates current evidence and potential mechanistic connections to inform research on spontaneous involution and the development of interventions tailored to specific disease stages and cell types.

articles.title: Mental health outcomes following COVID-19- associated caregiver loss in children and adolescents: a six-year evidence gap.
articles.abstract: By May 2022, an estimated 10.5 million children worldwide had lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19. We found only two cohorts with quantitative mental-health data: one in Iran and the South African Orphanhood and Caregiver Loss Among Adolescents and Youth study. Both reported more psychiatric and psychosocial difficulties among bereaved children than controls. In Iran, internalizing symptoms, post-traumatic stress, and suicidal ideation increased during follow-up, and no participant received mental-health care. In South Africa, likely mental disorder declined in both groups but remained more common among bereaved participants; suicidal ideation or attempts rose slightly in the bereaved group while falling among controls. Social support, food insecurity, and domestic violence were associated with outcomes. These children were bereaved during school closures, social isolation, disrupted mourning, and financial strain, when usual sources of support were often reduced. Yet few were identified and followed over time. Research funding priorities and fragmented health, education, mortality, and child-protection systems may have contributed to this gap. Many children bereaved in the first pandemic waves are now adolescents or young adults, but their longer-term mental-health course remains largely unknown. They should be identified, followed, and offered support according to clinical and family need.

articles.title: Persistent left ventricular systolic dysfunction at ≥6 months after SARS-CoV-2-associated MIS-C: a systematic review and rare-event meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with SARS-CoV-2 frequently involves acute myocardial dysfunction. However, the prevalence of persistent left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction at longer-term follow-up remains uncertain. We therefore performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the prevalence of persistent LV systolic dysfunction at ≥6 months after MIS-C.
METHODS: We included observational cohort studies reporting longitudinal echocardiographic follow-up in children and adolescents aged <21 years with SARS-CoV-2-associated MIS-C. The prespecified primary outcome was persistent LV systolic dysfunction, defined as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 55% at ≥6 months. Study-level events and denominators were extracted and harmonized using the number of children who underwent ≥6-month echocardiography as the endpoint-specific denominator. Pooled prevalence was estimated using an intercept-only binomial logistic-normal generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) fitted directly to study-level event counts and denominators without continuity correction. The originally prespecified random-effects logit model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals, together with alternative continuity corrections and transformation-based approaches, was retained as sensitivity analysis under sparse-event conditions.
RESULTS: Ten cohorts met the inclusion criteria and contributed to quantitative synthesis, comprising 432 children with echocardiography at ≥6 months. Persistent LV systolic dysfunction occurred in 3 children, corresponding to a crude observed proportion of 0.69% (3/432). In the revised primary continuity-correction-free binomial logistic-normal GLMM, the pooled prevalence was 0.69% (95% CI, 0.22%-2.13%). Given that only three events were observed, this model-based estimate should not be interpreted as a precise estimate of the underlying population prevalence. Continuity-corrected sensitivity models yielded pooled estimates from 1.62% to 2.23%, further demonstrating numerical sensitivity to the treatment of zero-event cohorts.
CONCLUSION: Persistent LV systolic dysfunction was infrequently observed among children with MIS-C reassessed by echocardiography at ≥6 months. However, only three events were identified, so the available evidence is insufficient to determine the exact population prevalence with precision. Inference is further limited by heterogeneous follow-up and potential selection bias from nonuniform late imaging. Larger prospective cohorts with standardized long-term surveillance are needed.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of Jordanian mothers regarding acute gastroenteritis in children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices of mothers living in Jordan regarding childhood acute gastroenteritis and to identify factors associated with poor knowledge, poor practice, lack of oral rehydration solution (ORS) awareness, and antibiotic use without medical consultation.
METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 730 mothers living in Jordan using a structured Arabic-language questionnaire. Participants were recruited through paediatric hospital settings and social media using convenience sampling. Composite knowledge and practice scores were calculated, and four multivariable binary logistic-regression models were fitted to examine factors associated with the prespecified outcomes.
RESULTS: The mean composite knowledge score was 15.73 ± 6.83 out of 28, corresponding to 56.18% of the maximum score, and 31.37% of participants were categorized as having poor knowledge. The mean composite practice score was 4.58 ± 1.71 out of 10, corresponding to 45.84% of the maximum score, and 61.23% were categorized as having poor practice. Overall, 54.52% identified three or fewer of the eight dehydration signs assessed, 59.59% were aware of ORS, and 3.15% selected ORS as their intended first action. Compared with residence in Central Jordan, residence in North Jordan was associated with higher adjusted odds of poor knowledge (aOR 2.18, 95% CI 1.38-3.45), poor practice (aOR 1.74, 95% CI 1.19-2.55), lack of ORS awareness (aOR 1.52, 95% CI 1.01-2.28), and antibiotic use without medical consultation (aOR 1.81, 95% CI 1.12-2.91). University-level education was associated with lower odds of poor knowledge and poor practice, while healthcare employment was associated with lower odds of poor practice and lack of ORS awareness.
CONCLUSION: Important gaps were identified in dehydration-sign recognition, ORS-related intended practices, and overall reported home-management practices. These findings support the development and evaluation of targeted caregiver-education initiatives emphasizing dehydration recognition, appropriate ORS use, safe medication practices, and timely care-seeking. Regional and educational differences may help identify groups requiring additional support; however, the observed associations should not be interpreted causally because of the cross-sectional design.

articles.title: Regional Left Ventricular Myocardial Strain Alterations in Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy and Correlation with Electrocardiographic and Motor Function Alterations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is characterized by progressive degradation of muscle function. Myocardial dysfunction is a major cause of mortality; however, its correlation with skeletal motor function remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess myocardial function and to correlate it with motor function in patients with DMD.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional observational study of patients with DMD. Evaluations included the Motor Function Measurement (MFM) scale, electrocardiogram (ECG), and echocardiography (Echo) with speckle-tracking (STE) imaging of the left ventricle (LV). The level of significance adopted in the statistical analysis was 5%.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients with a mean age of 14.30 ± 4.09 years. The average MFM score was 52.30 ± 16.32%. Electrocardiographic abnormalities were observed in 75% of patients. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was preserved (57.80 ± 9.62%). Global longitudinal strain (GLS) was reduced in 70% of the patients (-15.06 ± 2.46%; normal ≤ -18%), global circumferential strain (GCS) was decreased in 76% (-12.99 ± 2.89; normal ≤ -18%), and global radial strain (GRS) was reduced in 80% (20.52 ± 15.72; normal ≥ 40%). Hypokinesia and a significant reduction in regional myocardial strain (REGLSi) were also observed in the inferior and inferolateral segments of the LV. No significant correlation was found between MFM and ECHO variables.
CONCLUSION: Patients with DMD exhibit early compromise in STE parameters (GLS, GRS and GCS) and in REGLSi, particularly in the inferior and inferolateral LV regions, even with preserved LVEF (Central Figure). No significant correlation was observed between motor and cardiac function parameters.

articles.title: Dermatological conditions in endurance athletes: prevalence and associated factors in a cross-sectional online survey.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the prevalence of dermatological conditions among endurance athletes and investigate associations with demographic and sports-related variables.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 400 Brazilian adult endurance athletes, defined as individuals regularly training ≥10 h/week and/or participating in long-distance endurance events. Participants completed a structured questionnaire including demographic data, sports-related variables, sun exposure, photoprotection habits, and self-reported dermatological conditions. Associations between sports modalities and dermatological outcomes were assessed using logistic regression, with effect sizes expressed as odds ratios and 95%CIs.
RESULTS: Dermatological conditions were highly prevalent, with mechanically induced lesions representing the most frequent group. The most common conditions were foot blisters (73.8%), excoriations (59.0%), calluses (56.3%), abrasions (54.8%), and traumatic onycholysis (53.8%). First-degree sunburn (40.8%) and insect stings (36.3%) were the most frequent inflammatory/environmental conditions. Running was independently associated with foot blisters (OR 5.0; 95%CI 2.2-11.7) and traumatic onycholysis (OR 3.2; 95%CI 1.4-7.6), whereas cycling was associated with bacterial folliculitis (OR 2.7; 95%CI 1.0-7.5). Most athletes reported sun exposure exceeding 1 h per training session, while regular sunscreen use remained incomplete (56.4%). Self-reported skin neoplasms were uncommon but included seven melanoma cases, all among runners.
CONCLUSION: Endurance athletes exhibit a substantial burden of dermatological conditions related to repetitive mechanical stress, ultraviolet exposure, and sport-specific practices. Educational and preventive strategies focused on friction reduction, photoprotection, and early recognition of suspicious skin lesions may reduce short- and long-term morbidity.

articles.title: Operating room extubation: experience from a public Brazilian pediatric cardiovascular center.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence and success of intentional postoperative operating room extubation after elective congenital cardiac surgery at a Brazilian federal referral center and identify factors associated with non-extubation and extubation failure.
METHODS: This historical cohort study was conducted in a pediatric and neonatal cardiac intensive care unit over five years. Patients aged 0-18 years with congenital heart disease who underwent elective corrective or palliative cardiac surgery without preoperative mechanical ventilation were included. The primary outcome was operating room extubation, and the secondary outcome was extubation success, defined as no reintubation within 48 postoperative hours. Multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance identified factors independently associated with nonextubation and extubation failure (p<0.05).
RESULTS: Among 637 patients, 37% were extubated in the operating room, with a 98% success rate. They were older, had higher body weight, shorter noninvasive ventilation duration, shorter intensive care unit stays, and lower mortality. Increasing age reduced the risk of non-extubation. The need for noninvasive ventilation and longer intensive care unit stay were independently associated with non-extubation and extubation failure, although only four failures occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Operating room extubation was feasible in a substantial proportion of pediatric patients and achieved a high success rate, supporting its safety in selected cases. Greater surgical complexity, need for noninvasive ventilation, and longer intensive care unit stay increased the risk of non-extubation, whereas increasing age reduced this risk.

articles.title: Epidemiology and Associated Risk Factors of Malaria Infection in Loka Abaya District, Sidama Region, Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite continuous efforts to manage malaria, it remains a deadly disease, particularly common in low-lying areas of Ethiopia. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence, trends, and risk factors associated with malaria infection in Loka Abaya district, Sidama region, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out using house-to-house visits from April to June 2023. A total of 186 febrile patients were chosen using systematic random sampling. Those above the age of 18 were included in the study. Five health facilities and one primary hospital in the district provided retrospective data. A systematic questionnaire and microscopic analysis of blood films were used to gather data. The blood samples were evaluated in Hantate primary hospital. Univariate and multivariate binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the associated factors of malaria infection. Variables with p value less than 5% were considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Of 34,613 suspected patients tested for malaria over the previous 5 years, 26.2% were positive. The lowest rate recorded at 20.3% in 2018, whereas 2020 was the highest rate at 30.1%. Among them, 47.4% and 52.6% were females and males, respectively. Age groups from 5 to 14 covered up 21.6%, adults aged over 15 take up to 57.2%, and children under age 5 were 21.2%. The infection distribution was 58.8% for Plasmodium falciparum, 38.8% for Plasmodium vivax, and 2.4% mixed infections. The highest rate of infection was recorded during September to November. Cross-sectional parasitological survey showed that 18.3% of individuals were infected. The identified risk of contracting malaria was significant for individuals who were closer to mosquito breeding sites (AOR, 13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), did not use a mosquito net while sleeping (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), did not use indoor residual spraying in the previous 12 months (AOR,13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), used a window without a screen (AOR, 2.78.3, 95% CI, 1.03-13.86, p < 0.02), used a thatched roof (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), and did not know how malaria is transmitted (AOR, 4.3, 95% CI, 2.36-22.6, p < 0.04).
CONCLUSION: The study indicated that malaria remains a health issue in the Loko Abaya district. Several factors, including low income, wall openings, proximity to mosquito breeding sites, lack of indoor residual spraying, and lack of bed net use, were important predictors of malaria.

articles.title: Nutritional Therapy in Malnourished Children With Cancer: Response Among Hospitalized Children in Northern Tanzania.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malnutrition significantly compromises treatment tolerance and outcomes in children with cancer. Although nutritional therapy has been incorporated into pediatric oncology care, its effectiveness remains unevaluated. This study assessed the effectiveness of nutritional therapy and predictors of poor response among malnourished children diagnosed with cancer in Northern Tanzania.
METHODOLOGY: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among children aged 6 months to 18 years diagnosed with cancer from January 2023 to December 2024 at a zonal referral hospital in Northern Tanzania. Children receiving palliative care were excluded. Nutritional therapy was initiated among children with acute malnutrition. At 6 months, nutritional response was determined by comparing changes in mean WHO z-scores and by assessing differences across cancer types using the independent t-test. A good response to therapy was defined as a WHO z-score > -2 SD at six months, while a poor response was defined as a WHO z-score ≤ -2 SD.
RESULTS: Of 190 children diagnosed with cancer, 117 had acute malnutrition. Among these, 77 completed six months of follow-up, 37 died, and 3 were referred out. Nutritional therapy significantly improved mean WHO z-scores by 2.347 (p<0.001). Predictors of poor response included age below five years (AHR: 1.99, 95% CI: 1.05-5.46), combined chemotherapy and surgery (AHR: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.09-1.99), and neuroblastoma diagnosis (AHR: 1.47, 95% CI: 1.10-2.43).
CONCLUSION: Nutritional therapy significantly improved the nutritional status of malnourished children with cancer. Better response was observed among children older than five years, while poor response was associated with solid tumors and combined chemotherapy with surgery.

articles.title: De-identification of child protection intake reports using relationship-based replacement (DI-REBAR).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child protection contacts are documented in the form of child protection intake reports detailing the child(ren) suspected to be at risk of harm, the notifier's concerns, the alleged person responsible, and other details. These narrative reports remain untapped for statistical reporting and research purposes due to being text-based as well as containing extremely sensitive content. Applying a contextual de-identification approach to child protection narratives opens up the possibility of large-scale automated analysis by external researchers while preserving data privacy and relational meaning.
DATA: 10,000 randomly selected South Australian Department for Child Protection intake reports were provided for this study. A total of 300 (200 development, 100 evaluation) were randomly selected, manually reviewed and annotated.
METHODS: We designed and implemented a context-preserving de-identification pipeline called De-Identification via Relationship-Based Replacement (DI-REBAR) on 10,000 reports while preserving the noted relationships between named individuals. A total of seven indirect identifiers (date, time, school, early learning centre, hospital, prison, sensitive reference numbers) and three direct identifiers (name, address, phone number) were selected for de-identification. A relationship table was temporarily created to map individuals and their relationship to the child of interest, with direct identifiers replaced. Indirect identifiers were replaced by list-based replacement and regular expressions.
RESULTS: DI-REBAR evaluation showed promising results in macro precision (>0.98), recall (>0.88), and F1-Score (>0.92) across nine out of the ten identifier classes (prison excluded). Each identifier had a range of precision (0.74-1.00), recall (0.61-1.00), and F1-Score (0.66-1.00). Address, phone number, and date have the best performances (>0.98) across precision, recall, and F1-Score.
CONCLUSION: This is the first Australian study to automatically de-identify sensitive child protection data whilst preserving relationship information, allowing large-scale text analysis by external researchers in a data custodian's controlled environment. This approach can be applied to other areas that rely on unstructured data such as court documents and police reports. However, human reviewers are still needed to ensure identifiable information is not disclosed.

articles.title: India's rising palliative care needs and the policy response: A review of state palliative care policies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The need for palliative care is increasing in India. As health is primarily a state responsibility, state governments play a key role in translating national priorities into policies. This study examined how national and state palliative care policies address these challenges.
METHODS: A documentary analysis of palliative care policies in India was conducted. Documents were identified through Google search, government website searches and expert consultation. Documents were reviewed against a framework based on the World Health Organisation public health model for palliative care development. Additional domains included paediatric palliative care, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, governance, financing, and cross-sectoral interventions.
RESULTS: The analysis included the National Programme for Palliative Care (NPPC) and policies from Kerala, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Goa. All policies supported institution and home-based care, emphasised opioid availability, promoted health-system integration, and included workforce training and community engagement. Kerala and Tamil Nadu provided the most comprehensive approaches to health-system integration, community participation, and implementation planning, while Kerala demonstrated the strongest commitment to research and diversified financing. Considerable variation existed in implementation readiness, monitoring and evaluation frameworks, governance arrangements, and financing mechanisms. Most policies incorporated monitoring structures, although only some specified indicators, targets, or review processes. Paediatric palliative care was inconsistently addressed, with most policies lacking actionable implementation strategies. Despite increasing needs associated with population ageing and chronic disease, only Goa explicitly identified older adults as a vulnerable population, and no policy addressed advance care planning. Cross-sectoral approaches were limited; only Kerala and Tamil Nadu included explicit mechanisms linking palliative care with social welfare and community support systems.
CONCLUSIONS: Indian palliative care policies align with core palliative care development domains but remain insufficiently responsive to demographic and epidemiological transitions. Strengthening age-responsive planning, paediatric palliative care, financing, and intersectoral social support could improve preparedness for future palliative care needs.

articles.title: Chest Pain in Children and Adolescents in the Emergency Department: A State-of-the-Art Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Risk Stratification, and Evidence-Based Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest pain accounts for approximately 0.5%-1% of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits and is a frequent source of anxiety for families and clinicians. Although concern for cardiac disease often drives evaluation, true cardiac etiologies are rare, typically representing only 1%-2.5% of cases. The challenge in pediatric emergency care lies in distinguishing the small subset of patients with potentially life-threatening conditions from the large majority with benign causes, while avoiding unnecessary testing and radiation exposure.
METHODS: We conducted a state-of-the-art narrative review synthesizing contemporary literature on the epidemiology, differential diagnosis, cardiac risk stratification, diagnostic testing, and emerging technologies relevant to pediatric chest pain evaluation in the ED. Emphasis was placed on structured clinical assessment and evidence-based use of diagnostic modalities.
RESULTS: Most pediatric chest pain is noncardiac, with musculoskeletal causes predominating, followed by psychogenic, pulmonary, and gastrointestinal etiologies. Cardiac causes remain uncommon but require systematic identification through careful history, focused physical examination, and electrocardiography. High-risk features include exertional pain, syncope, abnormal examination findings, concerning family history, and abnormal ECG results. Standardized clinical pathways reduce unnecessary imaging and cardiac testing without compromising diagnostic safety. Chest radiography and troponin testing have limited utility when used indiscriminately, whereas point-of-care ultrasound offers a radiation-free adjunct in selected cases. Emerging tools such as teletriage and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics show promise but require further validation in pediatric populations.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric chest pain is usually benign but necessitates structured, risk-stratified evaluation to safely exclude serious disease. Judicious testing guided by clinical assessment improves efficiency, minimizes radiation exposure, and supports high-value, patient-centered emergency care.

articles.title: Increased rate of C-section in women with rheumatic diseases-indications under the magnifying glass: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and inflammatory joint diseases (IJD) show higher obstetric risk and cesarean delivery (CD) rates than healthy women. CD is associated with increased maternal and neonatal morbidity and healthcare costs; however, data on indications for CD in women with rheumatic diseases are limited. This study aimed to investigate the reasons for increased CD rates in women with SLE and IJD using the Robson classification and a detailed analysis of CD indications.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, CD rates and indications in women with SLE and IJD were compared with healthy controls (HC) as part of the RhePro Study, which prospectively collected data from patients with rheumatic diseases before, during, and after pregnancy to investigate reproductive health in this specific cohort. The study population was classified according to the Robson system, the mode of delivery was assessed, and CD indications were categorized as absolute obstetric, relative composite, or rheumatic disease-related.
RESULTS: A total of 185 women were included (119 HC, 40 SLE, 26 IJD). Women with IJD had significantly fewer vaginal deliveries (23.1% vs. 54.6% in HC, p = 0.009) and higher CD rates (65.4% vs. 37.8% in HC, p = 0.038) compared with healthy controls. CD and vaginal delivery rates did not differ significantly between IJD and SLE. SLE patients had the highest proportion of absolute obstetric CD indications (78.95%), compared with HC (55.56%) and IJD (23.53%). In contrast, 64.7% of CDs in IJD patients were performed for composite indications. The most common indication for CD was one previous CD (25.93%).
CONCLUSION: High CD rates in IJD patients, despite few absolute obstetric indications, suggest potentially modifiable clinical decision-making. In IJD, CDs were largely driven by composite indications. Neither SLE nor IJD alone necessitate cesarean delivery, and cesarean deliveries should be reduced in rheumatic patients without absolute indications, in line with WHO recommendations.

articles.title: Pediatric palliative care research participation: do adolescent and adult patients and caregivers find it acceptable?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Palliative care has matured as a life-span field with an increasing research base. Advancing the field means understanding why patients and caregivers participate in palliative care research, and participation's benefits and burdens. This study extended previous work to include greater diversity of clinical sampling and study design.
METHODS: Prospective, multi-methods study examined reported benefits, burdens, and motivations associated with participation in pediatric palliative care research. Study pParticipants included patients, caregivers, and family members who enrolled in pediatric palliative care research, as well as individuals declining participation, within a single quaternary pediatric hospital system. Structured questionnaires were administered at enrollment and study completion; qualitative responses were analyzed thematically.
RESULTS: 57 participants completed the questionnaires. Altruism and personal benefit were the most frequently cited motivations for enrollment at baseline and study completion. Emotional expression and the opportunity to help others were commonly identified as positive aspects of participation. The majority reported no discomfort and indicated willingness to participate in future research. The most frequent reasons given for declining participation were feeling overwhelmed, lack of interest, or study-specific aversion, rather than distress associated with palliative care research iPPC involvement.
DISCUSSION: Participants consistently reported greater benefit than burden, suggesting that pediatric palliative care research participation is acceptable and often meaningful. Given the pre/post design, the findings suggest eligible participants are able to determine if actual study participation is likely beneficial for them or not. Supporting families as they consider research participation promotes ethical, sensitive, and inclusive research design. Identified patterns may guide research design for future investigators to continue to advance the science of pediatric palliative care across the lifespanresearch.

articles.title: Latent profiles of parental discipline in Singapore: Intergenerational patterns and links to adjustment in young adulthood.
articles.abstract: Using a person-centered approach, this paper examined parental discipline profiles in Singapore from parents' and young adults' perspectives, and how these were linked to young adults' adjustment. Two quantitative studies were conducted to explore parents' experiences of disciplining their children (Study 1) and young adults' experiences of receiving discipline (Study 2). Study 1 utilized the self-reported ISPCAN Child Abuse Screening Tool for Parents (ICAST-P) to document the frequency of use of 36 discipline methods. The ICAST-P was reworded for Study 2 to assess young adults' experiences of being disciplined. Latent class analysis identified three groups of disciplinarians in each study. Study 1 (N = 747 parents; 80.7% mothers) showed that 14.6% of participants were harsh disciplinarians (high psychological-physical/violent discipline), 54.5% were high psychological-low physical/violent disciplinarians, and 30.8% were low psychological-physical/violent disciplinarians. Parents who endorsed physical discipline and had been physically punished during childhood were more likely to be harsh disciplinarians. Study 2 (N = 667; 74.3% females; age 18-25) showed three similar groups: harsh disciplinarians (4.0% mothers; 6.1% fathers), the high psychological-moderate physical/violent discipline group (34.0% mothers; 37.7% fathers), and the moderate psychological-low physical/violent discipline group (62.0% mothers; 56.1% fathers). Young adults whose parents used moderate psychological and low levels of physical/violent discipline had the least emotion dysregulation, the best parent-child relationship, and the highest self-esteem. The potential long-term impact of harsh discipline and intergenerational transmission of harsh discipline are discussed.

articles.title: Beyond generalizations: Understanding adolescent social networks in American Indian communities.
articles.abstract: American Indian (AI) adolescents experience disproportionately high rates of substance use, yet the role of substance use and other individual characteristics in friendship network formation within AI-majority reservation schools remains understudied. Most existing research on adolescent networks derives from racially heterogeneous school settings, where substance use is often linked to friendship formation and popularity. This study examines the structural and relational foundations of friendship networks among AI adolescents in their unique cultural context. Using social network data from 9th and 10th-grade students (N = 247) across three schools on a Northern Plains reservation, we employed exponential random graph models (ERGMs) to analyze factors shaping friendship ties. Models assessed endogenous structural processes (reciprocity, transitivity, degree effects) and actor-level characteristics, including demographic factors, substance use (alcohol, tobacco, marijuana), depression, and AI identity. Results indicated that universal structural mechanisms (reciprocity, transitivity) and demographic homophily (gender, grade, sexual orientation) were primary drivers of friendship. However, unlike what is often observed in studies of other adolescent populations, substance use showed no consistent association with sending ties or receiving ties. Similarly, depression and AI identity were not substantively associated with friendship formation. These findings reveal a distinct relational ecology within AI-majority reservation schools, where peer ties are organized around structural and demographic commonalities rather than risky behaviors. These findings challenge assumptions underpinning many network-based prevention programs and underscore the critical need for theories and interventions that are culturally and contextually grounded in the lived experiences of AI youth.

articles.title: Age as a determinant of trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries in pediatric emergency department visits: A NEISS analysis.
articles.abstract: Over the last decade trampoline use has increased. Many injuries occur that require emergency department (ED) care. The purpose of this research is to examine the role of age in trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries that require ED care. Data from the 2024 National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) was used. Trampoline-related injuries were extracted from the data set. Oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries were compared with other types of trampoline-related injuries by age groups (0 to <6 years, 6 to <12 years, and 12 to ≤18 years) in Chi-Square analyses and logistic regression analyses. There were 3548 NEISS-reported trampoline-associated injuries for children, ages 0 to ≤18 years, in 2024. This corresponded to an estimated 101,474 trampoline injuries in the United States in 2024. Of these, 21.7% were oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries (weighted estimate of 22,033 injuries). Of all the trampoline-related injuries in children ages 0 to ≤18 years, children ages 0 to <6 years had 33.0% of the injuries; children ages 6 to <12 years had 51.9%; and, children ages 12 to ≤18 years had 15.1%. Children ages 0 to <6 years had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.66 [95% CI: 1.11, 2.50; p = 0.0155] compared with children ages 12 to ≤18 years for oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries as compared with other injuries from trampolines. Younger children have significantly higher odds of trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries requiring emergency department care compared with adolescents, supporting age as an important host factor within the Haddon Matrix framework. These findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and anticipatory guidance for younger children.

articles.title: Perceptions and Barriers to the Use of Modern Contraceptive Methods and HIV Prevention Among Youth Aged 16-20 in Rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study explored young people's perceptions of modern contraceptive methods and HIV prevention, alongside the socioeconomic and cultural barriers they encounter three years post-implementation of Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) in rural Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Evaluating this curriculum exposes critical implementation gaps.
METHODS: A qualitative cross-sectional study using semi-structured, face-to-face in-depth individual interviews was conducted in January 2025 among 64 students aged 16-20 across four secondary schools (two public, two faith-based) in South Kivu. A purposive stratified sampling strategy enabled intra-sample comparative analysis across genders and institutional models. Transcribed data underwent inductive thematic open coding with double independent coding to ensure inter-rater reliability.
RESULTS: Our findings expose a significant public health paradox. On one hand, an absolute semantic disconnect exists where 100% of interviewed youth were unfamiliar with the term "contraception", coexisting with a low rate of consistent condom use (17.7%) among sexually active participants, despite comprehensive theoretical mastery of HIV transmission pathways. On the other hand, constrained by community taboos and the fear of parental or religious sanctions, these adolescents underutilize formal youth-friendly healthcare channels. Instead, they engage in alternative risk behaviors, specifically the post-coital utilization of high-dose quinine and aspirin (reported by 40.9% of sexually active girls) as makeshift emergency contraceptives, inducing clinical side effects. Conservative religious leaders and parents with low formal education levels constituted the primary socio-cultural barriers, whereas schoolteachers were supportive.
CONCLUSION: Rural youth remain vulnerable to unintended pregnancies and HIV due to community-enforced silence and institutional linguistic barriers. Effective interventions must transcend classroom education to engage religious and parental gatekeepers, de-stigmatize family planning services, and adapt formal medical terminologies to local daily vernacular languages to align theoretical knowledge with behavioral change.

articles.title: Network analysis of hope, medical coping, and self-deficiency in patients with port-wine stain.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Port-wine stain (PWS) is a chronic congenital vascular malformation that often causes substantial psychosocial burden due to visible skin lesions. However, the complex interrelationships among hope, medical coping, and self-deficiency in patients with PWS remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the network structure of hope, medical coping styles, and self-deficiency in patients with PWS, identify core and bridge psychological nodes, and examine subgroup differences by socioeconomic status (SES), gender, and treatment experience.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 227 patients with PWS. Hope was assessed using the Herth Hope Index (HHI), coping styles using the Medical Coping Modes Questionnaire (MCMQ), and self-deficiency using the Feeling of Inadequacy Scale (FIS). Network analysis was performed to estimate the psychological interaction structure, evaluate centrality and bridge centrality, identify community structures, and assess network stability. Subgroup network comparisons were further conducted based on gender, SES, and treatment experience.
RESULTS: The network analysis identified learning ability as the most central node and the most important bridge node. Confrontation and appearance also showed high centrality. The strongest edge was observed between learning ability and confrontation, suggesting a close interaction between perceived competence and active coping. Bridge centrality analysis further highlighted social confidence as an important connector across psychological domains. Community detection identified three interconnected psychological subsystems. Subgroup analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: males showed stronger associations between hope and self-deficiency, females demonstrated tighter connections among self-esteem, appearance, and social confidence, and patients without treatment experience exhibited denser psychological networks. In addition, low-SES patients had significantly higher network density than high-SES patients, indicating stronger mutual reinforcement among psychological factors.
CONCLUSION: The psychological adaptation of patients with PWS exhibits a complex network structure, with learning ability, confrontation, and social confidence serving as key intervention targets. Patients with lower SES may be more psychologically vulnerable due to denser network connectivity. These findings provide a theoretical basis for precision psychological interventions in PWS from a network perspective. Notably, patients with low SES exhibited denser network connectivity, suggesting heightened psychological vulnerability, so future public health strategies should prioritize both node-specific interventions and resources for disadvantaged populations.

articles.title: Perinatal bereavement care skills, training needs, and workplace support in an Italian descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perinatal bereavement is a complex clinical and emotional experience that affects not only parents but also healthcare professionals working in maternal and child healthcare. Despite growing international attention to bereavement care, many healthcare professionals report inadequate preparation, limited organizational support, and insufficient confidence in caring for families following a perinatal death.
OBJECTIVE: To describe self-reported bereavement-care skills, attitudes toward training, awareness of learning needs, and workplace support among healthcare professionals and near-graduation students.
METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in Italy between January and April 2026 among healthcare professionals and near-graduation students in maternal and child healthcare. The sample comprised 126 participants. Participants completed an Italian adaptation of the Perinatal Bereavement Care Confidence Scale (PBCCS). Descriptive statistics, internal consistency analysis, and non-parametric inferential tests were performed. Open-ended responses were examined using exploratory thematic content analysis with T-LAB Plus.
RESULTS: The descriptive mean of the 44 adapted questionnaire items was 2.23 (SD = 0.263; possible range 1-3; α = 0.86). Block means were 2.51 for knowledge, 2.22 for skills, 2.55 for self-awareness, and 1.68 for organizational support. These summaries do not constitute validated measures of overall professional confidence. Exploratory omnibus comparisons were significant across professional groups (p = 0.009); the years-of-service comparison was not statistically significant (p = 0.210). The principal reported needs concerned organizational support, training, and emotional coping.
CONCLUSION: The item and block descriptions highlight needs for structured training, reflective and emotional support, and multidisciplinary protocols. The 44-item mean is a descriptive summary of heterogeneous questionnaire content, not a validated measure of overall professional confidence. The cross-sectional study does not establish effects on confidence, quality of care, or staff well-being.

articles.title: Cohort profile: Assessment of factors impacting on foetal and infant immunity, growth, and neurodevelopment in HIV and antiretroviral drug exposed uninfected children: The Siyakhula Study.
articles.abstract: This cohort profile paper describes the Siyakhula cohort, a prospective longitudinal study of mother-child dyads during the ante- and postpartum period. The cohort was established to investigate how in-utero and early postnatal environments altered by maternal HIV status influence infants' growth trajectories, cognitive development, immune development and function, irrespective of the infant's HIV status. Pregnant women aged ≥18 years with singleton pregnancies at <22 weeks' gestation (as per best obstetric estimate, including ultrasound), regardless of HIV status, were recruited from January 2018 to January 2021 and followed throughout pregnancy. After delivery, women were approached for continued enrolment in the postpartum arm, which followed the dyads for 24 months. A total of 315 pregnant women (152 living with HIV and 163 without HIV) were recruited. Routine (pregnancy-related clinical data, HIV status, anthropometry) and research-specific (socio-demographic information, body composition analysis, diet, vaginal swabs, bloods) were collected antepartum. Cord blood and placental samples were collected intrapartum, while breast milk, stool samples, and blood were collected postpartum. Infants had anthropometric measurements performed at 6, 10 and 14 weeks, as well as 6, 12 and 24 months. Neurodevelopmental assessments were conducted during later follow-up visits. Extensive clinical, immunological, metabolomic, nutritional, and developmental data, together with a large biorepository of maternal and infant biospecimens, have been established. This paper provides an overview of the cohort design, participant characteristics, available data and biospecimens, completed analyses, and future research opportunities. Future plans include developing immunometabolic signatures associated with optimal and suboptimal growth and neurodevelopment of infants in the first two years of life.

articles.title: Depressive symptoms among adult patients with systemic lupus erythematosus in the Jazan Region, Saudi Arabia: An analytical cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Mental disorders, including depression, are common among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Depressive symptoms can significantly impair quality of life and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Studies investigating depressive symptoms and their associated factors in individuals with SLE have yielded inconsistent findings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms among patients with SLE and to identify the associated factors in patients from the Jazan Region of Saudi Arabia. An analytical cross-sectional study of 112 patients with SLE in Jazan, Saudi Arabia was conducted in 2023. A convenience sampling technique was used to recruit all eligible adult patients with SLE who attended rheumatology clinics and day-care units at the referral hospitals in the region. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Chi-square tests and binary logistic regression analyses were used to examine associations and identify factors associated with depressive symptoms. The majority of participants were female (104 [92.9%]), with ages ranging from 18 to 59 years. Depressive symptoms were present in 80% of participants, with patients experiencing mild depression 25 (22%), moderate depression 28 (25%), moderate-to-severe depression 22 (20%), and severe depression 15 (13%).In the multivariable analysis, although physical activity as a categorical variable did not reach overall statistical significance (global p = 0.067), participants engaging in less than 150 minutes of physical activity per week were significantly less likely to experience depressive symptoms compared with those performing no physical activity (OR = 0.28; 95% CI 0.10-0.82; P = 0.020).In conclusion, depressive symptoms were highly prevalent among patients with SLE in the Jazan Region, and physical activity level was identified as a significant modifiable associated factor in this population. Routine screening could facilitate early detection and intervention in patients with SLE in similar settings, resulting in improved clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Co-creating death and grief literacies with young people: A case-based example of youth engagement in research in Canada.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Death literacy refers to the knowledge and skills that make it possible to understand, gain access to, and act upon end-of-life and death care options. Grief literacy focuses on the capacity to access, process, and use knowledge related to experiences of loss. Despite growing attention to death and grief literacies in public health research, theory, and practice, young people are rarely involved as active contributors to their development, and often remain passive recipients of education about death, dying, and grief.
OBJECTIVE: Grounded in Childhood Ethics scholarship, this project aimed to explore: (a) how a multigenerational research team involving youth researchers and non-youth researchers experienced conducting a study on youth engagement in palliative and end-of-life care; and (b) the ways in which the research process could support the co-creation of knowledge on death and grief literacies.
DESIGN: A case-based approach was used to explore the experiences of multigenerational research team members involved in a national study on pediatric palliative and end-of-life care in Canada.
METHODS: Reflexive accounts from youth researchers (n = 2) and non-youth researchers (n = 4) were gathered during multiple reflexive team conversations.
RESULTS: Analysis of team member accounts identified five themes regarding the co-creation of death and grief literacies within a multigenerational research team, including: (1) challenging societal silences around death, dying, and grief among young people; (2) expanding death and grief literacies into social networks; (3) fostering trust and intellectual humility; (4) legitimizing youth researcher contributions; and (5) engaging in reciprocal learning.
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that engaging young people in research on palliative and end-of-life care can function as a way of reflecting upon, expanding, and advancing death and grief literacies. We propose that death and grief literacies may be understood as participatory, relational, and multigenerational practices, and suggest implications for public health, palliative care, and youth engagement research and practice.

articles.title: Acute and Early HIV Infection Among Key Populations in Rwanda: A Multisite Cross-Sectional Study to Inform Targeted Testing and Case-Finding, 2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute HIV infection is highly transmissible yet often missed by antibody-only rapid tests. Rwanda adopted fourth-generation antigen/antibody (Ag/Ab) tests in 2016, but routine p24 antigen documentation remains limited, limiting acute/early infection estimates. This study characterized acute/early HIV infection among key populations, including female sex workers (FSW), men who have sex with men (MSM), and people who inject drugs (PWID), to inform targeted testing and prevention interventions.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study in 2025 across 25 health facilities in 12 Rwandan districts. Individuals aged ≥ 15 years with unknown HIV status from FSW, MSM, PWID, and adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) were recruited via snowball sampling. Structured RedCap questionnaires captured socio-demographic, behavioral, and HIV testing history data. HIV testing followed the national serial algorithm using fourth-generation Determine HIV Early Detect rapid tests; acute/early infection required p24 antigen positivity regardless of antibody status.
RESULTS: Among 1341 participants (median age 25 years, interquartile range [IQR]: 21-30), 864 (64%) were FSW, 177 (13%) were MSM, 58 (4.3%) were PWID, and 242 (18%) were AGYW; 66% had only primary education and 55% resided in rural areas. In the prior 4 weeks, 52% reported multiple sexual partners and 35.5% reported consistent condom use. One-third (416, 32.8%) were aware of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and 34.7% (141/406) had ever used it. Overall HIV positivity was 5.0% (67/1341); acute/early HIV infection yield was 0.45% (6/1341), with two-thirds of cases (4/6) among MSM, all from Kigali City. Half (3/6) of acute/early cases reported inconsistent condom use and none reported PrEP use.
CONCLUSION: Acute and early HIV infections appear more common among MSM in Kigali, potentially associated with ongoing risk behaviors and low PrEP uptake, although this observation is based on a small number of cases. Priorities include strengthened acute HIV surveillance via fourth-generation and self-testing, rapid antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation, and scaled-up tailored prevention, especially PrEP.

articles.title: Lessons Learned from Kawasaki Disease: Current Understanding, Cardiac Inflammation and Relationship to Systemic Childhood Inflammatory Disorders.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki Disease (KD) is now recognized as the global leading cause of acquired heart disease in children. The purpose of this review is to provide an overview of what is known about KD etiology, its management strategies and sequelae, and to discuss the inflammatory pathophysiology, specifically cardiac inflammation and development of coronary artery aneurysms (CAA) in KD and how this compares with other childhood inflammatory disorders. While the presentation of KD and its cardiovascular sequelae is unique, there is overlap in the pathophysiology of other pediatric inflammatory vasculopathies. As we understand and learn more about KD, there is opportunity for further discovery of effective treatments which may have implications in other pediatric inflammatory conditions.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Lebrikizumab versus Dupilumab for Patients with Severe Atopic Dermatitis in Austria.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with significant economic burden. This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of lebrikizumab compared to dupilumab for adults and adolescents with severe AD from an Austrian healthcare payer's perspective.
METHODS: A cost-effectiveness analysis, based on the NICE assessment's TA986 model, was conducted, comprising a decision tree for the first year and a Markov model for long-term outcomes. The analysis adopted a healthcare system perspective, discount rate (3%) and applied Austrian-specific data, costs and quality of life measures. Two scenarios assessed the robustness of the base case analysis.
RESULTS: The base case analysis showed lebrikizumab was associated with lower total costs (€128,961 vs €133,870) and slightly lower QALYs (16.53 vs 16.56) compared to dupilumab over a lifetime horizon. The primary driver of cost savings was lower drug acquisition costs for lebrikizumab (-€5,349). Scenario analyses with different economic and clinical data demonstrated cost-effectiveness for lebrikizumab.
DISCUSSION: This economic evaluation suggests lebrikizumab is a potential cost-saving alternative to dupilumab based on the base case analysis of this health economic model for severe AD treatment in Austria, with comparable clinical efficacy. Consequently, lebrikizumab has been reimbursed in Austria since January 2025 as the second biological therapeutic option alongside dupilumab, following national pricing and reimbursement rules.

articles.title: Developing smart-helper content to support home-based care for technology-dependent children with chronic complex conditions: An application of the double diamond design process.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Technology-dependent children with chronic complex conditions often require intensive home-based care, which places substantial physical, emotional, and logistical burdens on family caregivers. Although digital-health technologies such as socially assistive robots show promise, few have been developed using systematic, user-centered methods grounded in the realities of everyday caregiving.
OBJECTIVE: To identify the needs of families caring for technology-dependent children with chronic complex conditions at home and to develop user-centered content concepts for a "smart-helper" robot.
METHODS: Guided by the Double Diamond service-design framework, we conducted interviews with clinicians and caregivers of technology-dependent children with chronic complex conditions, developed personas and journey maps, and convened a multidisciplinary expert workshop to design actionable smart-helper features.
RESULTS: Caregivers emphasized four core value domains for a smart helper: reducing routine workload, providing continuous and reliable monitoring, offering emotional reassurance, and delivering clinically informed guidance. Thirteen content concepts were developed, including automated daily documentation, nighttime vigilance support, context-aware emergency guidance, child state interpretation, personalized sensory engagement, caregiver emotional support, and tools to support family communication and peer connection.
CONCLUSIONS: This service-design process generated a comprehensive, user-centered blueprint for a smart-helper robot that may enhance caregiver capacity, child comfort, and continuity of care. Future work should advance technical development and evaluate prototypes in real home environments to ensure usability, safety, and equitable implementation.
